e.en: The magazine is famous for its {satiric} cartoons of politicians.
e.zh: 这家杂志以讽刺政客的漫画而闻名。

e.en: Her {satiric} tone made the audience uncomfortable but thoughtful.
e.zh: 她讽刺的语气让观众不太舒服却引人深思。

e.en: The Onion publishes {satirical} news stories that mimic real headlines.
e.zh: 洋葱新闻发布模仿真新闻标题的讽刺报道。

e.en: His {satirical} novel skewers Silicon Valley startup culture.
e.zh: 他的讽刺小说狠狠调侃了硅谷创业文化。

e.en: She {satirically} described her boss as a misunderstood genius.
e.zh: 她讽刺地把老板形容成一个被误解的天才。

e.en: The article {satirically} praises billionaires for their humble lifestyles.
e.zh: 这篇文章讽刺地赞美亿万富翁的朴素生活。

satirise.t: v. 讽刺，挖苦（英式拼写）

e.en: Comedians love to {satirise} the awkwardness of online dating.
e.zh: 喜剧演员爱拿网恋的尴尬开涮。

e.en: The play {satirises} the absurdity of modern corporate meetings.
e.zh: 这部剧讽刺了现代公司会议的荒诞。

e.en: Jonathan Swift remains one of history's greatest English {satirists}.
e.zh: 乔纳森·斯威夫特至今仍是英国历史上最伟大的讽刺作家之一。

e.en: The {satirist} mocked tech billionaires in his weekly column.
e.zh: 这位讽刺作家在每周专栏里嘲讽科技亿万富翁。

e.en: SNL loves to {satirize} politicians during election season.
e.zh: 《周六夜现场》喜欢在选举季讽刺政客。

e.en: The film cleverly {satirizes} influencer culture and social media obsession.
e.zh: 这部电影巧妙地讽刺了网红文化和社交媒体痴迷。

e.en: She felt deep {satisfaction} after finishing the marathon.
e.zh: 跑完马拉松后,她感到深深的满足。

e.en: Customer {satisfaction} scores improved after the redesign.
e.zh: 重新设计后,客户满意度评分有所提升。

e.en: Teaching offers small daily {satisfactions} that office work cannot.
e.zh: 教学带来的日常小满足是办公室工作无法给予的。

e.en: Among life's quiet {satisfactions}, gardening ranks high for me.
e.zh: 在生活中那些静谧的满足里,园艺对我来说排得很靠前。

e.en: The plumber resolved the leak {satisfactorily} within an hour.
e.zh: 水管工在一小时内令人满意地解决了漏水问题。

e.en: She answered every interview question {satisfactorily}.
e.zh: 她令人满意地回答了每一个面试问题。

satisfactory.t: adj. 令人满意的；合格的

e.en: The hotel room was clean and {satisfactory} for one night.
e.zh: 这间酒店房间干净,住一晚是令人满意的。

e.en: His explanation wasn't entirely {satisfactory} to the manager.
e.zh: 他的解释并未让经理完全满意。

satisfied.t:
adj. 满意的
v. satisfy 的过去式

e.en: I'm completely {satisfied} with my new noise-canceling headphones.
e.zh: 我对新买的降噪耳机非常满意。

e.en: She looked {satisfied} after closing the big sales deal.
e.zh: 谈成那笔大单后,她看上去十分满足。

satisfies.t: v. 满足；使满意（satisfy 第三人称单数）

e.en: This recipe {satisfies} both vegetarians and meat lovers alike.
e.zh: 这道菜素食者和肉食爱好者都会满意。

e.en: Nothing {satisfies} a craving like a slice of pizza.
e.zh: 没什么能像一块披萨那样满足嘴馋。

e.en: A glass of cold water can {satisfy} your thirst quickly.
e.zh: 一杯冷水能很快解渴。

e.en: The new policy fails to {satisfy} either side of the debate.
e.zh: 新政策让辩论的双方都不满意。

satisfying.t: adj. 令人满足的；称心的

e.en: There's nothing more {satisfying} than crossing tasks off a list.
e.zh: 没有什么比把待办事项一一划掉更让人满足的了。

e.en: The movie's ending was emotionally {satisfying} and well-earned.
e.zh: 这部电影的结局在情感上令人满足,水到渠成。

e.en: The puzzle pieces clicked together {satisfyingly} on the final try.
e.zh: 最后一次尝试时,拼图碎片令人愉悦地咔哒拼合。

e.en: Her plan came together {satisfyingly} after weeks of work.
e.zh: 经过几周的努力,她的计划令人满意地落实了。

sativa.t: n. 苜蓿型大麻（植物学用语）

e.en: Cannabis {sativa} strains are known for their energizing effects.
e.zh: 大麻苜蓿类品系以其提神效果而著称。

e.en: He prefers {sativa} over indica for daytime focus.
e.zh: 白天集中精力时,他更喜欢苜蓿型而非印度型大麻。

e.en: The monk experienced {satori} after years of meditation.
e.zh: 那位僧人在多年禅修后达到了顿悟。

e.en: Zen students seek {satori} through quiet contemplation.
e.zh: 禅宗弟子通过静思来追求顿悟。

satrap.t: n. 古波斯总督；地方权贵

e.en: The local {satrap} ruled the province with absolute authority.
e.zh: 当地的总督以绝对权威统治着这个省份。

e.en: Critics called the governor a corporate {satrap} serving wealthy donors.
e.zh: 批评者称这位州长是为富有捐助者效劳的傀儡。

e.en: I peeled a sweet {satsuma} for an afternoon snack.
e.zh: 我剥了一个甜蜜橘当下午茶点心。

e.en: The market sells {satsuma} oranges by the crate in winter.
e.zh: 市场冬天按箱出售蜜橘。

e.en: Heavy rain will {saturate} the soil within minutes.
e.zh: 大雨几分钟内就会让土壤完全饱和。

e.en: Advertisers {saturate} social media with holiday promotions.
e.zh: 广告商让节日促销充斥整个社交媒体。

e.en: The sponge was completely {saturated} with soapy water.
e.zh: 海绵已经完全被肥皂水浸透了。

e.en: Try to limit your intake of {saturated} fats.
e.zh: 尽量限制饱和脂肪的摄入量。

e.en: Bump up the {saturation} to make the colors pop.
e.zh: 把饱和度调高一点让颜色更鲜艳。

e.en: The streaming market has reached near total {saturation}.
e.zh: 流媒体市场已接近完全饱和。

e.en: We're hosting a barbecue this {Saturday} afternoon.
e.zh: 我们这周六下午要办烧烤聚会。

e.en: The library is closed every {Saturday} during summer.
e.zh: 夏季期间图书馆每个星期六都闭馆。

saturdays.t: n. 每逢周六；星期六（复数）

e.en: She teaches yoga on {Saturdays} at the community center.
e.zh: 她每周六在社区中心教瑜伽。

e.en: Most {Saturdays} we drive out to the countryside.
e.zh: 大多数周六我们都开车去乡下。

saturn.t: n. 土星；农神（罗马神话）

e.en: Through the telescope you can clearly see {Saturn}'s rings.
e.zh: 透过望远镜可以清楚看到土星的光环。

e.en: The probe sent back stunning images of {Saturn}.
e.zh: 探测器传回了土星的惊人图像。

saturnalia.t: n. 纵情狂欢；古罗马农神节

e.en: The festival turned into a wild {saturnalia} of music and dance.
e.zh: 这个节日变成了音乐与舞蹈的狂欢盛宴。

e.en: Ancient Romans celebrated {Saturnalia} in mid-December.
e.zh: 古罗马人在十二月中旬庆祝农神节。

e.en: Astronomers detailed the {Saturnian} moons in their report.
e.zh: 天文学家在报告中详细描述了土星的卫星。

e.en: The novel imagines a peaceful {Saturnian} golden age.
e.zh: 这本小说设想了一个宁静的农神黄金时代。

e.en: His {saturnine} expression discouraged casual conversation.
e.zh: 他阴郁的表情让人不敢随便搭话。

e.en: The detective had a famously {saturnine} personality.
e.zh: 那位侦探以阴沉的性格而闻名。

satyr.t: n. 半人半羊的森林之神；好色之徒

e.en: The painting depicts a {satyr} dancing in the woods.
e.zh: 这幅画描绘了一个森林之神在树林中起舞。

e.en: Greek myths often feature a mischievous {satyr} chasing nymphs.
e.zh: 希腊神话中常有调皮的萨提尔追逐仙女。

e.en: This pasta {sauce} tastes amazing with fresh basil.
e.zh: 这个意面酱配上新鲜罗勒非常好吃。

e.en: Don't forget to pour hot {sauce} on the tacos.
e.zh: 别忘了在玉米卷上淋点辣酱。

e.en: Heat the milk gently in a small {saucepan}.
e.zh: 用小炖锅慢慢加热牛奶。

e.en: The {saucepan} boiled over while I was distracted.
e.zh: 我分神的时候炖锅里的水溢出来了。

e.en: She stacked the clean {saucepans} neatly under the counter.
e.zh: 她把洗干净的炖锅整齐地叠放在台子下面。

e.en: Copper {saucepans} conduct heat much more evenly.
e.zh: 铜质炖锅导热要均匀得多。

e.en: Simmer the stew in a heavy {saucepot} for hours.
e.zh: 用厚重的炖锅把肉汤慢炖几个小时。

e.en: Grandma's old {saucepot} still makes the best soup.
e.zh: 奶奶那口旧炖锅还是能煮出最好喝的汤。

e.en: She balanced her teacup on a chipped {saucer}.
e.zh: 她把茶杯搁在一只缺了口的茶碟上。

e.en: Witnesses claimed they saw a flying {saucer} that night.
e.zh: 目击者声称那天晚上看到了飞碟。

e.en: His eyes went wide as {saucers} when he heard the news.
e.zh: 听到这个消息他眼睛瞪得像茶碟那么大。

e.en: The cafe served espresso with tiny porcelain {saucers}.
e.zh: 咖啡馆用小巧的瓷碟盛着浓缩咖啡端上来。

sauces.t:
n. 酱汁（复数）
v. 加调味汁

e.en: The chef makes all his {sauces} from scratch.
e.zh: 这位主厨所有的酱汁都是亲手现做的。

e.en: Asian cuisine features many fermented {sauces} and pastes.
e.zh: 亚洲菜系有许多发酵酱料和酱膏。

e.en: She gave him a {saucy} wink across the room.
e.zh: 她从房间另一头俏皮地朝他眨了眨眼。

e.en: The comedian's {saucy} jokes had everyone laughing.
e.zh: 那位喜剧演员调皮的笑话把大家逗笑了。

saudi.t:
adj. 沙特阿拉伯的
n. 沙特人

e.en: The {Saudi} delegation arrived for trade negotiations yesterday.
e.zh: 沙特代表团昨天抵达进行贸易谈判。

e.en: He spent five years working as an engineer in {Saudi} Arabia.
e.zh: 他在沙特阿拉伯当了五年工程师。

e.en: German bratwurst is best served with tangy {sauerkraut}.
e.zh: 德国香肠最适合配上酸爽的德国酸菜。

e.en: She fermented homemade {sauerkraut} in a glass jar.
e.zh: 她用玻璃罐自己发酵了酸菜。

e.en: After the workout, I relaxed in the hotel {sauna}.
e.zh: 健身完后我在酒店桑拿房里放松了一下。

e.en: This summer heatwave makes the city feel like a {sauna}.
e.zh: 夏天这波热浪让整座城市像桑拿房一样。

e.en: Finnish homes traditionally have private wood-burning {saunas}.
e.zh: 芬兰家庭传统上都有私人柴火桑拿房。

e.en: The spa offers infrared {saunas} for deep relaxation.
e.zh: 这家水疗中心提供红外线桑拿房供深度放松。

saunter.t:
v. 闲逛；漫步
n. 散步

e.en: We {saunter} along the riverbank every Sunday morning.
e.zh: 我们每个周日早上都沿着河岸悠闲散步。

e.en: He'd often {saunter} into meetings ten minutes late.
e.zh: 他经常优哉游哉地迟到十分钟才进会议室。

saurian.t:
adj. 蜥蜴类的
n. 蜥蜴类动物

e.en: Paleontologists uncovered fossils of an enormous {saurian} creature.
e.zh: 古生物学家发掘出了一只巨大蜥形类生物的化石。

e.en: The film features a terrifying {saurian} monster.
e.zh: 这部电影里有一只可怕的蜥形怪物。

e.en: The {sauropod} was the largest land animal ever to exist.
e.zh: 蜥脚类恐龙是地球上有史以来最大的陆地动物。

e.en: Children gazed up at the towering {sauropod} skeleton.
e.zh: 孩子们仰望着高耸的蜥脚类恐龙骨架。

e.en: I had a spicy {sausage} sandwich for breakfast.
e.zh: 我早餐吃了一份香辣香肠三明治。

e.en: The butcher makes his own {sausage} every morning.
e.zh: 那位肉贩每天早上都自己灌香肠。

e.en: He grilled a few {sausages} on the backyard barbecue.
e.zh: 他在后院烧烤架上烤了几根香肠。

e.en: German {sausages} come in countless regional varieties.
e.zh: 德国香肠有无数种地方风味。

e.en: The recipe says to {saut} the onions until golden.
e.zh: 食谱说要把洋葱煎炒到金黄色。

e.en: Quickly {saut} the garlic before adding the tomatoes.
e.zh: 先快速煎香大蒜再加入番茄。

saute.t:
v. 嫩煎；快炒
n. 炒菜

e.en: {Saute} the mushrooms in butter for about five minutes.
e.zh: 用黄油把蘑菇煎炒大约五分钟。

e.en: This pan is perfect to {saute} vegetables quickly.
e.zh: 这口锅非常适合快速煎炒蔬菜。

sauted.t:
adj. 嫩煎过的
v. sauté 的过去式

e.en: She {sauted} the spinach with garlic and olive oil.
e.zh: 她用大蒜和橄榄油煎炒了菠菜。

e.en: The dish came with lightly {sauted} bell peppers.
e.zh: 这道菜配着轻微煎炒过的彩椒。

sauvignon.t: n. 长相思（葡萄/葡萄酒品种）

e.en: A crisp {sauvignon} blanc pairs perfectly with seafood.
e.zh: 清爽的长相思白葡萄酒搭海鲜简直完美。

e.en: She ordered a glass of cabernet {sauvignon} with dinner.
e.zh: 她晚餐点了一杯赤霞珠葡萄酒。

savage.t:
adj. 凶猛的；野蛮的
v. 猛烈抨击

e.en: The critic wrote a {savage} review of the new film.
e.zh: 那位影评人对新片写了一篇毒辣的评论。

e.en: A {savage} storm tore through the coastal town overnight.
e.zh: 一场猛烈的风暴一夜之间席卷了沿海小镇。

e.en: The article {savagely} mocked the candidate's debate performance.
e.zh: 那篇文章狠狠嘲讽了候选人的辩论表现。

e.en: Wolves attacked the herd {savagely} during the night.
e.zh: 狼群在夜里凶猛地袭击了畜群。

e.en: The documentary exposes the {savagery} of the civil war.
e.zh: 这部纪录片揭露了内战的残暴。

e.en: Online debates often descend into shocking {savagery}.
e.zh: 网络辩论常常沦为令人震惊的恶毒攻击。

e.en: Lions roam freely across the African {savanna}.
e.zh: 狮子在非洲大草原上自由地游荡。

e.en: The {savanna} stretches endlessly toward the horizon.
e.zh: 大草原一直绵延到地平线。

savannah.t: n. 热带草原（savanna 异体）

e.en: Elephants migrate across the dry {savannah} each year.
e.zh: 大象每年都会穿越干旱的稀树草原迁徙。

e.en: We took a sunrise safari across the {savannah}.
e.zh: 我们在日出时分穿越稀树草原参加了野生动物游。

scab.t:
n. 伤口结的痂
n. 破坏罢工者

e.en: Don't pick at the {scab} or it will scar.
e.zh: 别去抠结痂,不然会留疤。

e.en: Striking workers shouted insults at the {scab} crossing the line.
e.zh: 罢工工人对越过警戒线的工贼大声辱骂。

e.en: The knight slid his sword back into its leather {scabbard}.
e.zh: 骑士把剑插回皮制的剑鞘里。

e.en: An ornate {scabbard} hung from the general's belt.
e.zh: 将军腰间挂着一个华丽的剑鞘。

e.en: The stray dog had a {scabby} patch on its back.
e.zh: 那只流浪狗背上有一块结痂的皮肤。

e.en: His knees were {scabby} from falling off the skateboard.
e.zh: 他从滑板上摔下来后膝盖结满了痂。

e.en: The clinic treated several students for {scabies} last week.
e.zh: 诊所上周治疗了几名患疥疮的学生。

e.en: {Scabies} spreads quickly in crowded living conditions.
e.zh: 疥疮在拥挤的居住环境中传播得很快。

scabious.t:
n. 山萝卜（植物）
adj. 有疮痂的

e.en: Bees love the purple {scabious} flowers in our garden.
e.zh: 蜜蜂很喜欢我们花园里紫色的山萝卜花。

e.en: The wound left a {scabious} mark on his arm.
e.zh: 那道伤口在他手臂上留下了一块结痂的痕迹。

e.en: The novel is famous for its {scabrous} humor and biting satire.
e.zh: 那部小说以粗俗的幽默和辛辣的讽刺著称。

e.en: He ran his hand over the {scabrous} bark of the oak.
e.zh: 他抚摸着橡树粗糙不平的树皮。

e.en: Fishermen pulled in a single silver {scad} at dawn.
e.zh: 渔民们在黎明时捞上一条银色的竹荚鱼。

e.en: Grilled {scad} is a popular street food in Manila.
e.zh: 烤竹荚鱼是马尼拉很受欢迎的街头小吃。

e.en: She has {scads} of unread emails in her inbox.
e.zh: 她收件箱里有一大堆未读邮件。

e.en: The festival drew {scads} of tourists from across Europe.
e.zh: 那场节日吸引了来自欧洲各地的大批游客。

scaffold.t:
n. 脚手架；绞刑架
v. 搭建支架

e.en: Workers climbed the {scaffold} to repaint the building's facade.
e.zh: 工人们爬上脚手架重新粉刷大楼外墙。

e.en: Good lesson plans {scaffold} learning from simple to complex.
e.zh: 好的教案能让学习从简到难循序渐进。

scaffolded.t: v. 搭建脚手架（过去式）

e.en: The teacher carefully {scaffolded} the lesson for new readers.
e.zh: 老师精心为初学阅读的学生搭建了学习支架。

e.en: Crews {scaffolded} the cathedral before starting the restoration.
e.zh: 施工队在开始修复前为大教堂搭起了脚手架。

scaffolding.t: n. 脚手架；（学习／代码）支架结构

e.en: The {scaffolding} around the tower will come down next week.
e.zh: 塔楼周围的脚手架下周就会拆除。

e.en: The framework provides useful {scaffolding} for new developers.
e.zh: 这个框架为新开发者提供了有用的入门支架。

scala.t:
n. Scala 编程语言
n. (解剖) 耳蜗阶

e.en: Many big-data tools at our company are written in {Scala}.
e.zh: 我们公司很多大数据工具都是用 Scala 写的。

e.en: She debuted at La {Scala} with a stunning soprano performance.
e.zh: 她在斯卡拉歌剧院以一场惊艳的女高音演出登台。

scalability.t: n. 可扩展性；可伸缩性

e.en: Cloud architecture greatly improves the {scalability} of our service.
e.zh: 云端架构大大提升了我们服务的可扩展性。

e.en: Investors questioned the startup's long-term {scalability}.
e.zh: 投资人对这家初创公司的长期扩展能力提出质疑。

scalable.t: adj. 可扩展的；可伸缩的

e.en: We need a {scalable} solution that handles millions of users.
e.zh: 我们需要一个能支撑数百万用户的可扩展方案。

e.en: The new database is more {scalable} than the old one.
e.zh: 新数据库比旧的更具可扩展性。

scalar.t:
n. 标量
adj. 数量的，纯量的

e.en: In the formula, mass is treated as a {scalar} value.
e.zh: 在这个公式里,质量被当作一个标量。

e.en: This function returns a single {scalar} rather than a vector.
e.zh: 这个函数返回的是单个标量,而不是向量。

scald.t:
v. 烫伤；把(奶)烫煮
n. 烫伤

e.en: Be careful not to {scald} yourself with the hot soup.
e.zh: 小心别被热汤烫伤。

e.en: {Scald} the milk before adding it to the dough.
e.zh: 把牛奶烫一下再加入面团里。

scalded.t: v. 被开水烫伤（过去式）

e.en: He {scalded} his hand on the steam from the kettle.
e.zh: 他被水壶冒出的蒸汽烫伤了手。

e.en: The recipe calls for {scalded} cream cooled to room temperature.
e.zh: 这道食谱需要烫过后冷却至室温的奶油。

e.en: She poured a cup of {scalding} tea and burned her tongue.
e.zh: 她倒了一杯滚烫的茶,把舌头烫伤了。

e.en: The review delivered a {scalding} critique of the film.
e.zh: 那篇评论对这部电影进行了严厉的抨击。

scale.t:
n. 规模；比例；刻度
v. 攀登；缩放

e.en: Step on the {scale} to check your weight.
e.zh: 站到秤上量一下你的体重。

e.en: The startup struggled to {scale} beyond its first city.
e.zh: 这家初创公司难以扩张到第一个城市之外。

scaled.t:
v. 按比例缩放（过去式）
adj. 有鳞的

e.en: The startup quickly {scaled} from ten users to ten million.
e.zh: 这家初创公司迅速从十个用户扩展到了一千万。

e.en: They {scaled} the cliff face using ropes and harnesses.
e.zh: 他们用绳索和安全带攀上了那面峭壁。

scales.t:
n. 秤；鳞片
v. scale 的三单

e.en: The bathroom {scales} say I gained two pounds over the holidays.
e.zh: 浴室体重秤显示我假期里胖了两磅。

e.en: A goldfish has shimmering {scales} that catch the light beautifully.
e.zh: 金鱼身上闪亮的鳞片在光下美丽夺目。

scaling.t:
n. 缩放；扩容
v. 攀登；缩放（进行时）

e.en: We're {scaling} the platform to handle holiday traffic spikes.
e.zh: 我们正在扩展平台以应对节假日的流量高峰。

e.en: {Scaling} a frozen waterfall requires specialized ice climbing gear.
e.zh: 攀登冰瀑需要专业的攀冰装备。

e.en: Sprinkle chopped {scallions} on top of the noodle soup.
e.zh: 在面汤上撒些切碎的小葱。

e.en: I always keep fresh {scallions} in the fridge for stir-fries.
e.zh: 我总在冰箱里备着新鲜的小葱用来炒菜。

e.en: We grilled fresh {scallop} with garlic butter for dinner.
e.zh: 我们用蒜蓉黄油烤了新鲜的扇贝当晚餐。

e.en: The dress had a delicate {scallop} pattern along the hem.
e.zh: 这条裙子的下摆有精致的扇形花边。

scalloped.t: adj. 带扇形边的；焗烤的

e.en: She wore a blouse with {scalloped} edges to the party.
e.zh: 她穿了一件荷叶边领口的衬衫去派对。

e.en: The recipe calls for {scalloped} potatoes baked with cream.
e.zh: 这道菜需要用奶油烤制的奶汁千层土豆。

e.en: That little {scallywag} stole cookies from the jar again.
e.zh: 那个小调皮鬼又从罐子里偷饼干了。

e.en: My grandfather called us {scallywag} whenever we played pranks.
e.zh: 我们恶作剧时,爷爷总叫我们小淘气。

scalp.t:
n. 头皮
v. 倒卖（票）牟利

e.en: This shampoo soothes a dry, itchy {scalp}.
e.zh: 这款洗发水能舒缓干燥发痒的头皮。

e.en: Resellers {scalp} concert tickets and resell them at huge markups.
e.zh: 黄牛抢购演唱会门票后高价转卖。

e.en: The surgeon picked up a {scalpel} and made a careful incision.
e.zh: 外科医生拿起手术刀,小心地切开了一道口子。

e.en: Use a hobby {scalpel} to cut these tiny model parts.
e.zh: 用爱好者用的手术刀来切这些细小的模型零件。

e.en: A {scalper} was selling tickets outside the stadium for triple price.
e.zh: 一个黄牛在球场外以三倍价格倒卖门票。

e.en: The website blocks any {scalper} trying to bulk-buy tickets.
e.zh: 该网站会拦截试图批量抢票的黄牛。

scaly.t: adj. 有鳞的；片状剥落的

e.en: The lizard's {scaly} skin glittered in the sunlight.
e.zh: 蜥蜴布满鳞片的皮肤在阳光下闪闪发光。

e.en: Cold weather makes my hands dry and {scaly}.
e.zh: 天气一冷,我的手就变得干燥脱皮。

scam.t:
n. 骗局；诈骗
v. 行骗

e.en: Don't click that link — it's an obvious phishing {scam}.
e.zh: 别点那个链接,明显是钓鱼骗局。

e.en: Scammers {scam} elderly people out of their savings every day.
e.zh: 骗子每天都在骗走老年人的积蓄。

e.en: A {scammer} called pretending to be from the bank.
e.zh: 一个骗子打电话来,假装是银行的工作人员。

e.en: Report any {scammer} you spot to the platform immediately.
e.zh: 发现骗子请立即向平台举报。

e.en: That little {scamp} hid my keys as a joke.
e.zh: 那个小淘气把我的钥匙藏起来当作恶作剧。

e.en: My nephew is a lovable {scamp} who always makes us laugh.
e.zh: 我侄子是个可爱的小调皮,总能逗我们开心。

scamper.t:
v. 蹦蹦跳跳地跑
n. 欢快的奔跑

e.en: The squirrels {scamper} across the lawn chasing each other.
e.zh: 松鼠们在草坪上互相追逐着蹦跳。

e.en: The kids {scamper} upstairs when they hear the ice cream truck.
e.zh: 孩子们一听到冰淇淋车就飞奔上楼。

e.en: I ordered shrimp {scampi} with linguine for lunch.
e.zh: 我午餐点了蒜香大虾配扁面条。

e.en: Her signature dish is buttery garlic {scampi}.
e.zh: 她的招牌菜是黄油蒜香大虾。

scan.t:
v. 扫描；浏览
n. 扫描（图像）

e.en: Please {scan} the QR code to join the meeting.
e.zh: 请扫描二维码加入会议。

e.en: The doctor ordered a brain {scan} to check for damage.
e.zh: 医生安排了一次脑部扫描以检查是否有损伤。

e.en: The corruption {scandal} forced the minister to resign.
e.zh: 这起腐败丑闻迫使部长辞职。

e.en: Her affair became the biggest {scandal} in Hollywood that year.
e.zh: 她的绯闻成了那年好莱坞最大的丑闻。

scandalise.t: v. 使愤慨；使反感（英式拼写）

e.en: Her revealing outfit will {scandalise} the conservative guests.
e.zh: 她暴露的着装会让保守的宾客感到震惊。

e.en: The leaked emails {scandalise} the entire industry overnight.
e.zh: 泄露的邮件一夜之间震惊了整个行业。

e.en: Grandma was {scandalised} by the language used on TV.
e.zh: 奶奶被电视上使用的粗话震惊到了。

e.en: The community felt {scandalised} when the truth finally came out.
e.zh: 真相大白后,整个社区都感到震惊不已。

e.en: His tweets continue to {scandalize} long-time fans.
e.zh: 他的推文不断让老粉丝们感到震惊。

e.en: The affair would {scandalize} the small religious town.
e.zh: 这桩婚外情会让这个保守的小镇为之哗然。

scandalized.t: adj. 感到愤慨的；震惊的

e.en: Viewers were {scandalized} by the host's racist remarks.
e.zh: 观众对主持人的种族歧视言论感到震惊。

e.en: She looked {scandalized} when he proposed splitting the bill.
e.zh: 他提议AA制时,她一脸震惊。

scandalous.t: adj. 骇人听闻的；不光彩的

e.en: The tabloid published {scandalous} photos of the celebrity.
e.zh: 这家小报发表了那位名人的丑闻照片。

e.en: It's {scandalous} how much CEOs earn compared to workers.
e.zh: 高管和员工的收入差距大得令人愤慨。

scandalously.t: adv. 骇人听闻地；丢人地

e.en: The hotel charged {scandalously} high prices during the holiday.
e.zh: 假期期间这家酒店收费高得离谱。

e.en: She dressed {scandalously} for the formal church service.
e.zh: 她穿得太过暴露,不适合正式的教堂礼拜。

e.en: A series of corruption {scandals} rocked the government this year.
e.zh: 今年一连串的腐败丑闻震动了政府。

e.en: The magazine thrives on celebrity {scandals} and gossip.
e.zh: 这本杂志靠名人丑闻和八卦发家。

scandinavia.t: n. 斯堪的纳维亚（北欧地区）

e.en: We're planning a summer trip to {Scandinavia} next year.
e.zh: 我们计划明年夏天去北欧旅行。

e.en: {Scandinavia} is famous for its minimalist design and cold winters.
e.zh: 北欧以极简设计和寒冷的冬天闻名。

scandinavian.t:
adj. 斯堪的纳维亚的
n. 北欧人

e.en: I love the clean lines of {Scandinavian} furniture design.
e.zh: 我喜欢北欧家具设计的简洁线条。

e.en: Many {Scandinavian} countries rank highest in global happiness surveys.
e.zh: 许多北欧国家在全球幸福感排名中名列前茅。

e.en: Aerospace engineers add {scandium} to aluminum to strengthen alloys.
e.zh: 航空工程师在铝中加入钪以增强合金强度。

e.en: {Scandium} is a rare earth element with atomic number 21.
e.zh: 钪是一种稀土元素,原子序数为21。

scania.t: n. 斯堪尼亚（瑞典卡车品牌／地区）

e.en: {Scania} trucks are common on European highways.
e.zh: 斯堪尼亚卡车在欧洲高速公路上很常见。

e.en: Malmö is the largest city in {Scania}, southern Sweden.
e.zh: 马尔默是瑞典南部斯科讷地区最大的城市。

scanned.t: v. 扫描（scan 的过去式）

e.en: I {scanned} the document and emailed it to the lawyer.
e.zh: 我扫描了文件并通过邮件发给了律师。

e.en: She quickly {scanned} the headlines before her morning coffee.
e.zh: 她在喝晨间咖啡前快速浏览了头条新闻。

e.en: The office printer doubles as a high-resolution {scanner}.
e.zh: 办公室的打印机也兼作高分辨率扫描仪。

e.en: Airport security uses a body {scanner} to check passengers.
e.zh: 机场安检用人体扫描仪检查乘客。

scanning.t:
v. 正在扫描
n. 扫描

e.en: She kept {scanning} the crowd, looking for her brother.
e.zh: 她不停地扫视人群,寻找她的弟弟。

e.en: {Scanning} old photos preserves them before they fade further.
e.zh: 扫描旧照片可以在它们继续褪色前保存下来。

scans.t:
v. 扫描（第三人称单数）
n. 扫描结果

e.en: The MRI {scans} revealed no signs of a tumor.
e.zh: 核磁共振扫描显示没有肿瘤的迹象。

e.en: This app {scans} receipts and tracks your spending automatically.
e.zh: 这个应用会扫描收据并自动记录你的开支。

e.en: The professor demonstrated the {scansion} of a Shakespearean sonnet.
e.zh: 教授示范了如何分析莎士比亚十四行诗的格律。

e.en: Mastering {scansion} helps you read poetry aloud with proper rhythm.
e.zh: 掌握韵律分析能帮你以正确的节奏朗读诗歌。

e.en: There is {scant} evidence to support that conspiracy theory.
e.zh: 几乎没有证据支持那个阴谋论。

e.en: The report paid {scant} attention to environmental concerns.
e.zh: 这份报告对环境问题几乎没有给予关注。

e.en: The tourists were {scantily} dressed despite the cold wind.
e.zh: 尽管寒风凛冽,游客们仍穿得很单薄。

e.en: His résumé was {scantily} detailed and lacked specifics.
e.zh: 他的简历内容寥寥,缺乏具体细节。

e.en: The hikers survived on {scanty} rations for three days.
e.zh: 徒步者靠着稀少的口粮坚持了三天。

e.en: Her bikini was so {scanty} it caused a stir.
e.zh: 她的比基尼太过暴露,引起了轩然大波。

scapa.t: n. 斯卡帕（地名，英国海军基地）

e.en: The German fleet was scuttled at {Scapa} Flow in 1919.
e.zh: 德国舰队于1919年在斯卡帕湾自沉。

e.en: {Scapa} Flow remains a famous diving site for wreck enthusiasts.
e.zh: 斯卡帕湾至今仍是沉船爱好者著名的潜水胜地。

e.en: The garlic {scape} adds a mild oniony flavor to stir-fries.
e.zh: 蒜薹能为炒菜增添淡淡的葱蒜香味。

e.en: Photographers love capturing the urban {scape} at golden hour.
e.zh: 摄影师喜欢在黄金时刻捕捉城市风景。

scapegoat.t:
n. 替罪羊
v. 使…成为替罪羊

e.en: They made the intern a {scapegoat} for the project's failure.
e.zh: 他们把项目失败的责任推给了实习生。

e.en: Politicians often {scapegoat} immigrants for economic problems.
e.zh: 政客常把经济问题归咎于移民。

scapegoating.t: n. 把责任推给他人；替罪羊行为

e.en: {Scapegoating} junior staff for management's mistakes is unfair.
e.zh: 把管理层的错误推给基层员工是不公平的。

e.en: The media has been {scapegoating} video games for years.
e.zh: 媒体多年来一直把电子游戏当作替罪羊。

e.en: She injured her left {scapula} during the rock climbing fall.
e.zh: 她在攀岩摔倒时伤到了左肩胛骨。

e.en: The {scapula} connects the upper arm to the collarbone.
e.zh: 肩胛骨连接着上臂和锁骨。

scapular.t:
adj. 肩胛骨的
n. 圣衣（天主教）

e.en: The physiotherapist focused on {scapular} stability exercises.
e.zh: 物理治疗师重点训练肩胛骨稳定性。

e.en: Many Catholics wear a {scapular} as a sign of devotion.
e.zh: 许多天主教徒佩戴圣衣以表虔诚。

scar.t:
n. 伤疤；心理创伤
v. 留下疤痕

e.en: He still has a {scar} from the bike accident as a kid.
e.zh: 他身上还留着小时候骑车摔的疤痕。

e.en: The war left a deep emotional {scar} on the survivors.
e.zh: 战争给幸存者留下了深深的心理创伤。

scarab.t: n. 圣甲虫；甲虫形饰物

e.en: Ancient Egyptians believed the {scarab} beetle symbolized rebirth.
e.zh: 古埃及人认为圣甲虫象征着重生。

e.en: She bought a turquoise {scarab} pendant from the museum shop.
e.zh: 她在博物馆商店买了一个绿松石圣甲虫吊坠。

e.en: We spent the weekend at the seaside in {Scarborough}.
e.zh: 我们在斯卡伯勒海边度过了周末。

e.en: {Scarborough} Fair is a traditional English folk song.
e.zh: 《斯卡伯勒集市》是一首传统的英国民谣。

e.en: Clean drinking water is becoming {scarce} in many regions.
e.zh: 在许多地区,清洁饮用水正变得越来越稀缺。

e.en: Good entry-level jobs are {scarce} in this economy.
e.zh: 在当前经济形势下,好的入门级工作机会很少。

e.en: I had {scarcely} sat down when the phone rang again.
e.zh: 我刚坐下,电话又响了。

e.en: She could {scarcely} believe she had won the lottery.
e.zh: 她简直不敢相信自己中了彩票。

e.en: The drought caused a serious {scarcity} of fresh produce.
e.zh: 干旱导致新鲜农产品严重短缺。

e.en: Marketing often creates artificial {scarcity} to drive up demand.
e.zh: 营销常常制造人为的稀缺感来推高需求。

scare.t:
v. 惊吓；使害怕
n. 惊恐；恐慌

e.en: That horror movie really gave me a {scare} last night.
e.zh: 那部恐怖片昨晚真的把我吓到了。

e.en: Don't {scare} the cat — she just calmed down.
e.zh: 别吓猫,它好不容易才平静下来。

e.en: A tattered {scarecrow} stood in the middle of the field.
e.zh: 一个破烂的稻草人立在田中央。

e.en: The crows ignored the homemade {scarecrow} entirely.
e.zh: 乌鸦完全无视那个自制的稻草人。

e.en: I'm a little {scared} to fly through the storm.
e.zh: 我有点害怕在暴风雨中飞行。

e.en: The thunder {scared} the dog under the bed.
e.zh: 雷声把狗吓得钻到床底下。

scaremonger.t: n. 散布恐慌谣言的人

e.en: Don't listen to that {scaremonger} on the news.
e.zh: 别听新闻里那个散播恐慌的人。

e.en: Critics called him a {scaremonger} during the campaign.
e.zh: 批评者在竞选期间称他为散布恐慌者。

scares.t:
v. 惊吓（第三人称单数）
n. 惊恐事件

e.en: The thought of public speaking still {scares} him.
e.zh: 一想到要当众演讲他还是会害怕。

e.en: There have been several health {scares} this year.
e.zh: 今年出现了几起健康恐慌事件。

e.en: She wrapped a wool {scarf} around her neck.
e.zh: 她在脖子上围了一条羊毛围巾。

e.en: The kids {scarf} down pizza after soccer practice.
e.zh: 孩子们足球训练后狼吞虎咽地吃披萨。

e.en: Gardeners {scarify} the lawn to remove dead moss.
e.zh: 园丁会给草坪疏耙以清除枯苔。

e.en: You can {scarify} hard seeds to help them sprout.
e.zh: 可以划破硬种子的外壳以促进发芽。

scarily.t: adv. 吓人地；令人害怕地

e.en: The new AI is {scarily} good at writing code.
e.zh: 这个新人工智能写代码厉害得吓人。

e.en: She looks {scarily} similar to her grandmother.
e.zh: 她长得和奶奶像得吓人。

e.en: The film's {scariness} comes from its eerie silence.
e.zh: 这部电影的恐怖来自其诡异的寂静。

e.en: Reviewers praised the game for its sheer {scariness}.
e.zh: 评论员盛赞这款游戏的惊悚程度。

scaring.t:
v. 正在吓唬
adj. 吓人的

e.en: Stop {scaring} your little brother with ghost stories.
e.zh: 别再用鬼故事吓你弟弟了。

e.en: The loud fireworks were {scaring} the neighborhood dogs.
e.zh: 巨响的烟花把附近的狗都吓到了。

scarlatti.t: n. 斯卡拉蒂（意大利作曲家姓氏）

e.en: She practiced a {Scarlatti} sonata for the recital.
e.zh: 她为独奏会练习了一首斯卡拉蒂奏鸣曲。

e.en: {Scarlatti} wrote hundreds of keyboard sonatas.
e.zh: 斯卡拉蒂创作了数百首键盘奏鸣曲。

scarlet.t:
n. 猩红色
adj. 鲜红的

e.en: She wore a stunning {scarlet} dress to the gala.
e.zh: 她穿着一袭惊艳的猩红色礼服出席晚宴。

e.en: The maple leaves turned bright {scarlet} in October.
e.zh: 枫叶在十月变成了鲜艳的猩红色。

e.en: The garden bloomed with deep {scarlets} and golden yellows.
e.zh: 花园里盛开着深红与金黄。

e.en: She painted the sunset using several {scarlets} and oranges.
e.zh: 她用几种猩红和橙色画出了日落。

e.en: The hikers climbed cautiously up the rocky {scarp}.
e.zh: 徒步者小心翼翼地爬上陡峭的岩坡。

e.en: A steep {scarp} marked the edge of the plateau.
e.zh: 一道陡峭的悬崖标示着高原的边缘。

scarper.t: v. 逃跑；溜走（英式俚语）

e.en: The thieves tried to {scarper} before the police arrived.
e.zh: 小偷想在警察赶到前溜走。

e.en: Let's {scarper} before the boss notices we left early.
e.zh: 趁老板没发现,我们赶紧开溜吧。

scarred.t: adj. 有疤痕的；受过创伤的

e.en: His left cheek was {scarred} from the old accident.
e.zh: 他的左脸颊还留着旧事故的疤痕。

e.en: The war had deeply {scarred} the small village.
e.zh: 战争给这个小村庄留下了深深的创伤。

scarring.t:
n. 瘢痕形成
v. 留下疤痕

e.en: The burn left permanent {scarring} on her arm.
e.zh: 那次烧伤在她手臂上留下了永久的疤痕。

e.en: Losing the championship was a {scarring} experience for him.
e.zh: 输掉冠军赛对他是一段刻骨铭心的经历。

scars.t:
n. 伤疤（复数）
v. 留下疤痕

e.en: The old soldier still bore {scars} from the war.
e.zh: 那位老兵身上仍带着战争的伤疤。

e.en: Childhood bullying left emotional {scars} that lasted years.
e.zh: 童年的霸凌留下了多年难以抚平的心理创伤。

e.en: She knits colorful {scarves} for her family every winter.
e.zh: 她每年冬天都为家人织彩色围巾。

e.en: The shop sells silk {scarves} at half price today.
e.zh: 那家店今天的丝巾半价出售。

e.en: That horror movie was way too {scary} for kids.
e.zh: 那部恐怖片对孩子来说太吓人了。

e.en: Public speaking can be {scary} the first few times.
e.zh: 头几次公开演讲可能会很吓人。

scat.t:
n. 爵士拟声唱法
v. 快走开

e.en: The singer improvised a lively {scat} solo on stage.
e.zh: 歌手在台上即兴来了一段活泼的拟声爵士。

e.en: She yelled "{scat}!" to chase the cat off the table.
e.zh: 她大喊一声"走开!"把猫从桌上赶下去。

e.en: The critic did not {scathe} the young author's debut novel.
e.zh: 评论家并没有严厉抨击这位年轻作者的处女作。

e.en: Few politicians escape unscathed when reporters {scathe} their records.
e.zh: 很少有政客能在记者抨击其履历时全身而退。

scathing.t: adj. 尖刻的；严厉批评的

e.en: The review was {scathing} about the restaurant's slow service.
e.zh: 那篇评论对餐厅的缓慢服务大加抨击。

e.en: She wrote a {scathing} reply to the misleading article.
e.zh: 她写了一篇措辞犀利的回应来反驳那篇误导性文章。

e.en: He spoke {scathingly} about the company's broken promises.
e.zh: 他尖刻地批评了公司未兑现的承诺。

e.en: The judge {scathingly} dismissed the lawyer's weak arguments.
e.zh: 法官严厉地驳回了律师那些站不住脚的论点。

e.en: His comedy relied too heavily on {scatological} humor.
e.zh: 他的喜剧过于依赖粗俗的厕所笑话。

e.en: The book was banned for its {scatological} language.
e.zh: 这本书因粗俗污秽的语言被禁。

scatter.t:
v. 散开；撒
n. 散布；零星

e.en: Please don't {scatter} your toys all over the floor.
e.zh: 请不要把玩具丢得满地都是。

e.en: The pigeons {scatter} whenever a child runs by.
e.zh: 每当有小孩跑过,鸽子就四散飞开。

scatterbrained.t: adj. 注意力不集中的；丢三落四的

e.en: He's so {scatterbrained} that he forgot his own birthday.
e.zh: 他丢三落四到连自己的生日都忘了。

e.en: Sorry for the {scatterbrained} email — I was rushing.
e.zh: 抱歉邮件写得乱七八糟,我当时太赶了。

e.en: Papers were {scattered} across the desk after the meeting.
e.zh: 会议结束后桌上散落着各种文件。

e.en: The weather forecast predicts {scattered} showers this afternoon.
e.zh: 天气预报今天下午有零星阵雨。

scattering.t:
n. 散射；少量
v. 散开

e.en: A {scattering} of stars appeared as the clouds cleared.
e.zh: 云开之后,几颗星星零星地出现在天空。

e.en: Light {scattering} explains why the sky looks blue.
e.zh: 光的散射解释了天空为何是蓝色。

e.en: The farmer {scatters} seeds across the freshly tilled field.
e.zh: 农夫把种子撒在刚翻好的田里。

e.en: Sunlight {scatters} through the leaves onto the path.
e.zh: 阳光透过树叶散落在小径上。

scatty.t: adj. 糊里糊涂的；心不在焉的

e.en: My grandmother gets a bit {scatty} when she's tired.
e.zh: 我奶奶累的时候会有点丢三落四。

e.en: He's a {scatty} but lovable colleague who means well.
e.zh: 他是个迷糊但可爱的同事,本意都是好的。

e.en: A flock of {scaup} drifted across the icy lake.
e.zh: 一群斑背潜鸭漂浮在结冰的湖面上。

e.en: Birdwatchers spotted a rare {scaup} near the marsh.
e.zh: 观鸟者在沼泽附近发现了一只罕见的潜鸭。

e.en: Raccoons {scavenge} for food in the city's trash bins.
e.zh: 浣熊会在城市的垃圾桶里翻找食物。

e.en: He had to {scavenge} parts to repair the old bike.
e.zh: 他只能东拼西凑找零件来修这辆旧自行车。

e.en: The vulture is nature's most efficient {scavenger}.
e.zh: 秃鹫是自然界最高效的食腐动物。

e.en: We organized a {scavenger} hunt for the kids' party.
e.zh: 我们为孩子的派对组织了一场寻宝游戏。

scavengers.t: n. 拾荒者；食腐动物（复数）

e.en: Hyenas and vultures are common African {scavengers}.
e.zh: 鬣狗和秃鹫是非洲常见的食腐动物。

e.en: After the festival, {scavengers} collected discarded cans for recycling.
e.zh: 节日过后,拾荒者收集被丢弃的罐子去回收。

e.en: Stray dogs were {scavenging} through the alley garbage.
e.zh: 流浪狗在巷子里翻找垃圾。

e.en: The bears resorted to {scavenging} when prey grew scarce.
e.zh: 猎物稀少时,熊只能靠捡食腐肉为生。

scc.t: n. SCC 缩写（如鳞状细胞癌等）

e.en: In the worst-case {scenario}, the server crashes completely.
e.zh: 在最糟的情况下,服务器会彻底崩溃。

e.en: The team rehearsed every possible {scenario} before launch.
e.zh: 团队在发布前演练了每一种可能的情景。

e.en: Some writers misspell "scenarios" as {scenarioes} in their drafts.
e.zh: 有些作者在草稿里把"scenarios"误拼成"scenarioes"。

e.en: Spell-check flagged {scenarioes} as an incorrect plural form.
e.zh: 拼写检查把"scenarioes"标为错误的复数形式。

e.en: The opening {scene} of the film was absolutely stunning.
e.zh: 这部电影的开场镜头美得令人震撼。

e.en: Police arrived at the {scene} within five minutes.
e.zh: 警察在五分钟内赶到了现场。

e.en: The mountain {scenery} along the train route was breathtaking.
e.zh: 火车沿途的山地风光令人叹为观止。

e.en: I need a vacation just to change my {scenery}.
e.zh: 我需要度个假来换换环境。

e.en: Several deleted {scenes} were included on the Blu-ray release.
e.zh: 蓝光版收录了几个被删减的镜头。

e.en: A lot happens behind the {scenes} at a startup.
e.zh: 创业公司幕后其实发生着很多事。

e.en: We took the {scenic} route along the coast home.
e.zh: 我们沿着海岸线走了风景优美的那条路回家。

e.en: The hotel offers a {scenic} view of the lake.
e.zh: 这家酒店可以欣赏到湖景。

e.en: The village is {scenically} located between two green hills.
e.zh: 这个村庄坐落在两座青山之间,风景优美。

e.en: Their cabin sits {scenically} on the edge of a cliff.
e.zh: 他们的小屋风景如画地坐落在悬崖边。

scenographic.t: adj. 舞台布景的；透视画法的

e.en: The play used bold {scenographic} effects to set the mood.
e.zh: 这部戏剧用大胆的舞台设计效果来营造氛围。

e.en: She studied {scenographic} design at a famous theater school.
e.zh: 她在一所著名戏剧学院学习舞台美术设计。

scent.t:
n. 香味；气味
v. 嗅到

e.en: The {scent} of fresh coffee filled the small kitchen.
e.zh: 新鲜咖啡的香气弥漫在小厨房里。

e.en: The dog quickly picked up the rabbit's {scent}.
e.zh: 狗很快嗅到了兔子的气味。

e.en: She lit a vanilla-{scented} candle to relax after work.
e.zh: 她点了一支香草味的蜡烛,下班后放松一下。

e.en: The garden was {scented} with jasmine in the evening.
e.zh: 傍晚的花园弥漫着茉莉花香。

e.en: These artificial flowers look real but are completely {scentless}.
e.zh: 这些假花看着像真的,但完全没有香味。

e.en: He prefers {scentless} laundry detergent because of his allergies.
e.zh: 因为过敏,他更喜欢无香型的洗衣液。

e.en: The bakery {scents} drifted out into the busy street.
e.zh: 面包店的香味飘到了繁忙的街道上。

e.en: She collects perfume {scents} from around the world.
e.zh: 她收集来自世界各地的香水香型。

e.en: The king raised his golden {scepter} before the crowd.
e.zh: 国王在人群面前举起了金色的权杖。

e.en: The {scepter} is displayed in a museum in London.
e.zh: 这把权杖陈列在伦敦的一家博物馆里。

e.en: Even the biggest {sceptic} was convinced by the demo.
e.zh: 就连最大的怀疑论者也被这次演示说服了。

e.en: He's a climate {sceptic} despite mounting scientific evidence.
e.zh: 尽管科学证据越来越多,他仍是个气候怀疑论者。

e.en: I'm {sceptical} of any diet that promises miraculous results.
e.zh: 我对任何承诺奇效的减肥法都持怀疑态度。

e.en: Investors remained {sceptical} about the startup's bold projections.
e.zh: 投资者对这家创业公司大胆的预测仍持怀疑态度。

e.en: She raised an eyebrow {sceptically} at his excuse.
e.zh: 她怀疑地挑了挑眉,听着他的借口。

e.en: The committee listened {sceptically} to the consultant's grand proposal.
e.zh: 委员会怀疑地听着顾问那宏大的提案。

e.en: His grand promises were met with widespread {scepticism}.
e.zh: 他那些宏大的承诺遭到了广泛的怀疑。

e.en: A healthy dose of {scepticism} protects you from online scams.
e.zh: 适度的怀疑能保护你免受网络骗局。

e.en: The queen held a golden {sceptre} during the coronation.
e.zh: 加冕礼上,女王手持一柄金色权杖。

e.en: A jeweled {sceptre} sat beside the crown on display.
e.zh: 一柄镶宝石的权杖摆放在王冠旁展出。

e.en: I felt a guilty {schadenfreude} when my rival's project failed.
e.zh: 对手的项目失败时,我有种愧疚的幸灾乐祸感。

e.en: There's something universally human about quiet {schadenfreude}.
e.zh: 那种暗暗幸灾乐祸的心理,似乎是人类共通的。

sched.t: n. schedule 的缩写，日程表

e.en: What's on your {sched} for tomorrow afternoon?
e.zh: 你明天下午的日程安排是什么?

e.en: I'll check my {sched} and get back to you tonight.
e.zh: 我看一下日程,今晚再回复你。

schedule.t:
n. 日程；时间表
v. 安排；预定

e.en: My {schedule} is packed with meetings all day Tuesday.
e.zh: 我周二一整天的日程都被会议排满了。

e.en: You can {schedule} a haircut through the salon's app.
e.zh: 你可以通过这家沙龙的应用预约理发。

e.en: The flight is {scheduled} to depart at 6:45 AM.
e.zh: 航班预定于早上6点45分起飞。

e.en: I {scheduled} a dentist appointment for next Thursday.
e.zh: 我预约了下周四的牙医。

e.en: The task {scheduler} runs backup scripts every night at midnight.
e.zh: 任务调度器每晚午夜运行备份脚本。

e.en: She uses an AI {scheduler} to coordinate meetings across time zones.
e.zh: 她用一款AI日程助手来协调跨时区的会议。

schedules.t:
n. 日程表
v. 安排（第三人称）

e.en: The app {schedules} reminders based on your daily routine.
e.zh: 这款应用会根据你的日常作息安排提醒。

e.en: Train {schedules} are posted on the station's main board.
e.zh: 火车时刻表张贴在车站的主告示板上。

e.en: I'm {scheduling} a meeting with the design team tomorrow.
e.zh: 我正在安排明天和设计团队的会议。

e.en: Smart {scheduling} software helps doctors avoid double bookings.
e.zh: 智能排班软件帮助医生避免重复预约。

e.en: The database {schema} defines how user data is stored.
e.zh: 该数据库模式定义了用户数据的存储方式。

e.en: Update the JSON {schema} before deploying the new API.
e.zh: 部署新接口之前请更新 JSON 模式。

schematic.t:
adj. 示意的
n. 原理图

e.en: The engineer drew a {schematic} of the circuit board.
e.zh: 工程师画出了电路板的原理图。

e.en: This map gives a {schematic} view of the subway lines.
e.zh: 这张地图给出了地铁线路的示意图。

e.en: The textbook explains the engine {schematically} with arrows and labels.
e.zh: 教材用箭头和标注示意性地讲解了引擎结构。

e.en: He sketched the layout {schematically} on a napkin.
e.zh: 他在餐巾纸上简略地画出了布局图。

schematics.t: n. 原理图；示意图（复数）

e.en: The hacker stole the {schematics} of the new drone.
e.zh: 黑客盗走了新型无人机的设计图纸。

e.en: Engineers reviewed the {schematics} before assembling the prototype.
e.zh: 工程师们在组装原型前审阅了原理图。

schematize.t: v. 以图示化；使系统化

e.en: Researchers often {schematize} complex processes into simple flowcharts.
e.zh: 研究人员常把复杂流程简化成流程图。

e.en: The author tries to {schematize} human emotions too neatly.
e.zh: 作者试图把人类情感过于工整地图式化。

scheme.t:
n. 方案；计划；诡计
v. 谋划

e.en: The government launched a new pension {scheme} this year.
e.zh: 政府今年推出了一项新的养老金计划。

e.en: Police uncovered a {scheme} to defraud elderly investors.
e.zh: 警方破获了一起诈骗老年投资者的阴谋。

e.en: That clever {schemer} always finds a loophole in the rules.
e.zh: 那个精明的算计者总能在规则里找到漏洞。

e.en: Office gossip painted her as a ruthless {schemer}.
e.zh: 办公室流言把她描绘成一个无情的阴谋家。

e.en: Pyramid {schemes} promise quick riches but rarely deliver.
e.zh: 传销骗局承诺快速致富,实际却很少兑现。

e.en: The city {schemes} new bike lanes for next year.
e.zh: 市政府计划明年新建几条自行车道。

scheming.t:
adj. 爱耍阴谋的
n. 谋划

e.en: Stop {scheming} behind your colleagues' backs at work.
e.zh: 别在同事背后耍心机了。

e.en: The {scheming} villain finally got caught in the season finale.
e.zh: 那个诡计多端的反派在季终集终于被抓住了。

e.en: {Schering} was once a major German pharmaceutical company.
e.zh: 先灵公司曾是一家大型德国制药企业。

e.en: My grandfather worked at {Schering} for over thirty years.
e.zh: 我祖父在先灵公司工作了三十多年。

e.en: The pianist played a lively {scherzo} as an encore.
e.zh: 钢琴家以一首轻快的谐谑曲作为返场。

e.en: Beethoven's {scherzo} feels both playful and intense.
e.zh: 贝多芬的谐谑曲既俏皮又激烈。

schilling.t: n. 先令（奥地利旧货币单位）

e.en: Austria used the {schilling} before adopting the euro in 2002.
e.zh: 奥地利在2002年改用欧元之前使用先令。

e.en: My grandmother still keeps a few old {schilling} coins.
e.zh: 我奶奶还留着几枚旧先令硬币。

e.en: A deep {schism} divided the political party last year.
e.zh: 去年一次深刻的分裂撕开了这个政党。

e.en: The 1054 {schism} split Christianity into east and west.
e.zh: 1054年的大分裂把基督教分成了东西两派。

schismatic.t:
adj. 分裂的
n. 分裂派者

e.en: The {schismatic} group broke away to form a new church.
e.zh: 那个分裂派系脱离出去成立了新教会。

e.en: His {schismatic} views angered the senior leadership.
e.zh: 他那些分裂性的观点激怒了高层领导。

e.en: The cliff is made of shiny grey {schist}.
e.zh: 那座悬崖由闪亮的灰色片岩构成。

e.en: Geologists found mica flakes embedded in the {schist}.
e.zh: 地质学家在片岩中发现了云母碎片。

e.en: {Schistosomiasis} still infects millions in tropical regions every year.
e.zh: 血吸虫病每年仍在热带地区感染数百万人。

e.en: Clean water access greatly reduces the risk of {schistosomiasis}.
e.zh: 获得清洁用水可大大降低感染血吸虫病的风险。

schizoid.t:
adj. 精神分裂型的
n. 分裂型人格者

e.en: The character shows clearly {schizoid} tendencies in the novel.
e.zh: 小说里那个角色表现出明显的类分裂样倾向。

e.en: He prefers solitude, which his therapist called {schizoid}.
e.zh: 他喜欢独处,治疗师称之为类分裂样人格。

e.en: Modern medication helps many people manage {schizophrenia} effectively.
e.zh: 现代药物帮助许多人有效控制精神分裂症。

e.en: Researchers are still searching for the genetic causes of {schizophrenia}.
e.zh: 研究人员仍在寻找精神分裂症的遗传成因。

schizophrenic.t:
adj. 精神分裂症的
n. 精神分裂症患者

e.en: The film portrays a {schizophrenic} artist with great sensitivity.
e.zh: 这部电影细腻地刻画了一位精神分裂症画家。

e.en: The company's strategy feels almost {schizophrenic} this quarter.
e.zh: 公司这季度的战略简直像分裂了一样自相矛盾。

schlemiel.t: n. 倒霉蛋；笨手笨脚的人

e.en: Poor Dave is the office {schlemiel} who spills every coffee.
e.zh: 可怜的戴夫是办公室里那个总打翻咖啡的倒霉蛋。

e.en: Don't be such a {schlemiel}—double-check your work.
e.zh: 别这么笨手笨脚的,工作要再三检查。

schlep.t:
v. 吃力地搬运
n. 苦差事

e.en: I had to {schlep} my luggage across the entire airport.
e.zh: 我不得不拖着行李横穿整个机场。

e.en: Driving two hours for groceries is a real {schlep}.
e.zh: 开两小时车去买菜真是一段苦差事。

e.en: The gift shop sells nothing but tourist {schlock}.
e.zh: 那家礼品店只卖些粗制滥造的旅游纪念品。

e.en: Critics dismissed the movie as sentimental {schlock}.
e.zh: 影评人把这部电影斥为煽情的烂俗之作。

e.en: The hotel lobby was decorated in a {schlocky} retro style.
e.zh: 酒店大堂装修成了一种俗气的复古风格。

e.en: He loves watching {schlocky} horror films on weekends.
e.zh: 他周末喜欢看那种粗制滥造的恐怖片。

e.en: We toured a beautiful Bavarian {schloss} overlooking the lake.
e.zh: 我们参观了一座俯瞰湖面的巴伐利亚城堡。

e.en: The {schloss} hosts classical concerts every summer.
e.zh: 这座城堡每年夏天举办古典音乐会。

schlumberger.t: n. 斯伦贝谢（油服公司/姓氏）

e.en: {Schlumberger} is a leading oilfield services company worldwide.
e.zh: 斯伦贝谢是全球领先的油田服务公司。

e.en: My cousin landed an engineering job at {Schlumberger} last month.
e.zh: 我表哥上个月在斯伦贝谢找到了一份工程师工作。

e.en: The wedding speech was full of cheesy {schmaltz}.
e.zh: 那段婚礼致辞充满了肉麻的煽情。

e.en: Grandma fries onions in chicken {schmaltz} for extra flavor.
e.zh: 奶奶用鸡油煎洋葱以增添风味。

schmaltzy.t: adj. 过度煽情的；滥情的

e.en: That ballad is way too {schmaltzy} for my taste.
e.zh: 那首民谣太煽情了,不合我的口味。

e.en: The Christmas movie was predictable and {schmaltzy}.
e.zh: 那部圣诞电影老套又煽情。

e.en: Some {schmo} parked his car right across the driveway.
e.zh: 某个傻瓜把车正好停在了车道上。

e.en: I'm just an ordinary {schmo} trying to pay rent.
e.zh: 我只是一个想付得起房租的普通人。

schmooze.t: v. 闲聊套近乎；拉关系

e.en: Sales reps {schmooze} clients at industry conferences every year.
e.zh: 销售代表每年都在行业会议上和客户套近乎。

e.en: He's great at networking events—he loves to {schmooze}.
e.zh: 他很擅长社交活动,特别喜欢攀谈拉关系。

e.en: That talented {schmoozer} can charm anyone in the room.
e.zh: 那位八面玲珑的人能让全场所有人为之倾倒。

e.en: As a natural {schmoozer}, she dominates every networking event.
e.zh: 作为天生的社交高手,她在每场社交活动里都很出彩。

e.en: Don't be a {schmuck}—apologize to your sister already.
e.zh: 别犯傻了,赶紧向你妹妹道个歉。

e.en: Some {schmuck} cut me off in traffic this morning.
e.zh: 今早有个浑蛋开车强行变道挡了我。

schnapps.t: n. 施纳普斯酒（德式烈酒）

e.en: We toasted with peach {schnapps} at the New Year's party.
e.zh: 我们在新年派对上用桃子烈酒举杯祝酒。

e.en: German {schnapps} is much stronger than most American liqueurs.
e.zh: 德国烈酒比大多数美国利口酒劲大得多。

e.en: Our miniature {schnauzer} barks at every passing squirrel.
e.zh: 我家的迷你雪纳瑞见到每只松鼠路过都要叫。

e.en: The {schnauzer} won first prize at the local dog show.
e.zh: 那只雪纳瑞在本地犬展上获得了一等奖。

e.en: We ordered crispy pork {schnitzel} with a side of potatoes.
e.zh: 我们点了酥脆的炸猪排配土豆作配菜。

e.en: Vienna is famous for its enormous veal {schnitzel}.
e.zh: 维也纳以其超大份的小牛肉炸排闻名。

schoenberg.t: n. 勋伯格（奥地利作曲家）

e.en: {Schoenberg} pioneered the twelve-tone technique in modern classical music.
e.zh: 勋伯格在现代古典音乐中开创了十二音体系。

e.en: My professor devoted an entire lecture to {Schoenberg}'s atonal works.
e.zh: 我的教授用整整一节课讲解勋伯格的无调性作品。

scholar.t: n. 学者；奖学金获得者

e.en: She is a leading {scholar} in medieval literature.
e.zh: 她是中世纪文学领域的领军学者。

e.en: The young {scholar} won a fellowship to study at Oxford.
e.zh: 这位年轻学者获得了去牛津学习的奖学金。

scholarly.t: adj. 学术的；治学严谨的

e.en: His {scholarly} article was published in a top journal.
e.zh: 他那篇学术论文发表在了一本顶级期刊上。

e.en: She has a quiet, {scholarly} manner that students admire.
e.zh: 她有一种安静博学的气质,深受学生敬佩。

e.en: {Scholars} have debated this question for over a century.
e.zh: 学者们就这个问题已经争论了一个多世纪。

e.en: Several visiting {scholars} joined our research lab this semester.
e.zh: 本学期有几位访问学者加入了我们的研究室。

e.en: She earned a full {scholarship} to study computer science.
e.zh: 她获得了攻读计算机科学的全额奖学金。

e.en: His {scholarship} on ancient Rome is widely respected.
e.zh: 他在古罗马研究方面的学术造诣广受尊敬。

e.en: The university offers many {scholarships} to international students.
e.zh: 这所大学为国际学生提供众多奖学金。

e.en: Athletic {scholarships} cover tuition for talented college players.
e.zh: 体育奖学金为有才华的大学运动员支付学费。

e.en: Her {scholastic} record earned her a spot at Harvard.
e.zh: 她优异的学业成绩为她争取到了哈佛的入学资格。

e.en: The school holds an annual {scholastic} achievement awards ceremony.
e.zh: 这所学校每年举办一次学业成就颁奖典礼。

e.en: Medieval {scholasticism} sought to reconcile faith with reason.
e.zh: 中世纪的经院哲学力图调和信仰与理性。

e.en: Aquinas remains the most influential figure in {scholasticism}.
e.zh: 阿奎那至今仍是经院哲学中最具影响力的人物。

e.en: The book compares various {scholasticisms} across different religious traditions.
e.zh: 这本书比较了不同宗教传统中的各种经院哲学体系。

e.en: Modern philosophers often criticize older {scholasticisms} as overly rigid.
e.zh: 现代哲学家常批评旧式经院哲学过于僵化。

scholastics.t: n. 经院派学者；经院哲学

e.en: The medieval {scholastics} dominated European universities for centuries.
e.zh: 中世纪的经院学者主宰欧洲大学长达数个世纪。

e.en: Top {scholastics} from each high school competed in the finals.
e.zh: 各高中的顶尖学子在决赛中一较高下。

school.t:
n. 学校；学派
v. 训练；教育

e.en: My daughter walks to {school} every morning with friends.
e.zh: 我女儿每天早上和朋友一起走路去上学。

e.en: A {school} of fish darted past the diver.
e.zh: 一群鱼从潜水员身旁飞快游过。

e.en: He forgot his {schoolbag} on the bus this morning.
e.zh: 他今早把书包落在公交车上了。

e.en: Her pink {schoolbag} is decorated with cartoon stickers.
e.zh: 她那个粉色书包上贴满了卡通贴纸。

e.en: Open your {schoolbook} to page forty-two, please.
e.zh: 请把课本翻到第四十二页。

e.en: He doodled in the margins of his math {schoolbook}.
e.zh: 他在数学课本的页边随手涂鸦。

e.en: He blushed like a nervous {schoolboy} at the interview.
e.zh: 他在面试时像个紧张的小学生一样脸红了。

e.en: The {schoolboy} raised his hand to answer the question.
e.zh: 那个男生举起手来回答问题。

e.en: Every {schoolchild} in the country learns this song.
e.zh: 全国每个学童都会学唱这首歌。

e.en: He behaved like a nervous {schoolchild} on his first day.
e.zh: 他第一天像个紧张的小学生一样。

schoolchildren.t: n. 学童们（schoolchild 的复数）

e.en: Crowds of {schoolchildren} waited at the bus stop.
e.zh: 一群学童在公交站等车。

e.en: The museum offers free tours for {schoolchildren}.
e.zh: 博物馆为学童提供免费导览。

e.en: Her favorite {schoolday} memory is the annual sports meet.
e.zh: 她最喜欢的校园记忆是每年的运动会。

e.en: A typical {schoolday} starts at eight in the morning.
e.zh: 普通的上学日早上八点开始。

schooled.t:
adj. 受过训练的
v. 教育、训练（school 的过去式）

e.en: She was {schooled} at home until she was twelve.
e.zh: 她十二岁前一直在家接受教育。

e.en: The rookie got {schooled} by the veteran player.
e.zh: 新人被老将上了一课。

e.en: I had lunch with an old {schoolfriend} yesterday.
e.zh: 我昨天和一位老同学一起吃了午饭。

e.en: My closest {schoolfriend} now lives in Canada.
e.zh: 我最要好的同学现在住在加拿大。

e.en: The {schoolgirl} carried a heavy backpack on the train.
e.zh: 那个女学生在火车上背着沉重的书包。

e.en: She blushed with a {schoolgirl} grin at his joke.
e.zh: 她对他的玩笑露出小女生般的笑容。

schoolgirls.t: n. 女学生们（schoolgirl 的复数）

e.en: A group of {schoolgirls} giggled near the vending machine.
e.zh: 一群女学生在自动售货机旁咯咯地笑。

e.en: The {schoolgirls} wore matching navy uniforms.
e.zh: 女学生们穿着统一的深蓝制服。

schoolhouse.t: n. 校舍（尤指乡村小学）

e.en: The old wooden {schoolhouse} still stands by the river.
e.zh: 那座老木校舍仍立在河边。

e.en: Their village had a one-room {schoolhouse} for decades.
e.zh: 他们村里几十年来都只有一间教室的小学校。

schooling.t: n. 学校教育；受教育经历

e.en: Her {schooling} was interrupted by the family's frequent moves.
e.zh: 她的学业因家里频繁搬家而中断。

e.en: Good {schooling} opens up many career options.
e.zh: 良好的教育能带来许多职业选择。

schoolmarm.t: n. 女教师（旧式、略带贬义）

e.en: The new boss has a strict {schoolmarm} energy.
e.zh: 新老板有种严厉女教师的气场。

e.en: Don't be such a {schoolmarm} about grammar mistakes.
e.zh: 别像个老学究似的纠结语法错误。

schoolmaster.t: n. 男教师；校长（旧用法）

e.en: The strict {schoolmaster} ran the village academy for years.
e.zh: 那位严厉的校长执掌村里的学堂多年。

e.en: His grandfather was the local {schoolmaster} in 1950.
e.zh: 他祖父在一九五零年是当地的男教师。

e.en: I bumped into an old {schoolmate} at the airport.
e.zh: 我在机场偶遇了一位老同学。

e.en: My childhood {schoolmate} became a famous chef.
e.zh: 我童年的同学后来成了著名厨师。

schoolmates.t: n. 同学们（schoolmate 的复数）

e.en: He keeps in touch with his old {schoolmates} online.
e.zh: 他在网上和老同学们保持联系。

e.en: Her former {schoolmates} threw her a surprise party.
e.zh: 她以前的同学给她办了一场惊喜派对。

schoolmistress.t: n. 女教师；女校长（旧用法）

e.en: The kindly {schoolmistress} knew every child by name.
e.zh: 那位和蔼的女校长能叫出每个孩子的名字。

e.en: Miss Hill served as {schoolmistress} for thirty years.
e.zh: 希尔小姐担任女校长三十年。

e.en: The {schoolroom} smelled of chalk and old books.
e.zh: 教室里弥漫着粉笔和旧书的味道。

e.en: Sunlight streamed through the {schoolroom} windows.
e.zh: 阳光从教室的窗户洒进来。

schools.t:
n. 学校（school 的复数）
v. 教导（school 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Public {schools} reopen next Monday after the holiday.
e.zh: 公立学校将于下周一假期后复课。

e.en: A teacher {schools} students in basic algebra.
e.zh: 一位老师教学生基础代数。

e.en: My aunt is a {schoolteacher} in a small town.
e.zh: 我姑妈在一个小镇当老师。

e.en: He left coding to become a {schoolteacher}.
e.zh: 他放弃编程,转行做了中小学老师。

schoolteachers.t: n. 中小学教师们（schoolteacher 的复数）

e.en: Many {schoolteachers} struggle with low pay.
e.zh: 许多中小学老师为低薪所困。

e.en: The conference brought together {schoolteachers} from across the state.
e.zh: 这次会议汇集了全州的中小学教师。

e.en: Finish your {schoolwork} before opening the game.
e.zh: 先做完作业再打开游戏。

e.en: His {schoolwork} has improved a lot this term.
e.zh: 他这学期的功课进步了很多。

e.en: She piles all her {schoolworks} on the kitchen table.
e.zh: 她把所有作业都堆在厨房桌上。

e.en: The teacher collected the {schoolworks} at the end of class.
e.zh: 老师在下课前收齐了作业。

e.en: Kids played tag in the {schoolyard} during recess.
e.zh: 孩子们课间在操场上玩追逐游戏。

e.en: The argument felt like a silly {schoolyard} fight.
e.zh: 那场争吵像幼稚的校园打闹。

schooner.t:
n. 纵帆船
n. 大啤酒杯

e.en: A two-masted {schooner} sailed past the harbor entrance.
e.zh: 一艘双桅纵帆船驶过港口入口。

e.en: He ordered a {schooner} of pale ale at the pub.
e.zh: 他在酒馆点了一大杯淡色艾尔啤酒。

schopenhauer.t: n. 叔本华（德国哲学家）

e.en: She quoted {Schopenhauer} during the philosophy seminar.
e.zh: 她在哲学讨论课上引用了叔本华。

e.en: {Schopenhauer} viewed the world as driven by blind will.
e.zh: 叔本华认为世界由盲目的意志驱动。

schtick.t: n. 招牌段子；个人特色表演

e.en: Sarcasm is basically his entire {schtick} online.
e.zh: 讽刺基本上就是他网上的全部套路。

e.en: The comedian's {schtick} is getting old fast.
e.zh: 那位喜剧演员的老梗已经过时了。

schubert.t: n. 舒伯特（奥地利作曲家）

e.en: The pianist played a {Schubert} sonata beautifully.
e.zh: 钢琴家美妙地演奏了一首舒伯特奏鸣曲。

e.en: {Schubert} composed hundreds of art songs.
e.zh: 舒伯特创作了数百首艺术歌曲。

schwarzkopf.t: n. 施瓦茨科普夫（姓氏）

e.en: General {Schwarzkopf} led coalition forces in the Gulf War.
e.zh: 施瓦茨科普夫将军在海湾战争中指挥联军。

e.en: She bought {Schwarzkopf} shampoo at the drugstore.
e.zh: 她在药妆店买了施华蔻洗发水。

e.en: He mixed gin with {Schweppes} tonic water.
e.zh: 他用怡泉汤力水调了杯金酒。

e.en: The bar only stocks {Schweppes} ginger ale.
e.zh: 这家酒吧只供应怡泉姜汁汽水。

sciatic.t: adj. 坐骨的；坐骨神经的

e.en: The injury pinched her {sciatic} nerve badly.
e.zh: 那次受伤严重压迫了她的坐骨神经。

e.en: Stretching can ease {sciatic} pain in the leg.
e.zh: 拉伸可以缓解腿部坐骨神经疼痛。

e.en: His {sciatica} flares up after long flights.
e.zh: 长途飞行后他的坐骨神经痛就会发作。

e.en: Yoga helped her manage chronic {sciatica}.
e.zh: 瑜伽帮她缓解了慢性坐骨神经痛。

e.en: Modern {science} has transformed how we treat disease.
e.zh: 现代科学改变了我们治疗疾病的方式。

e.en: My daughter loves her {science} class at school.
e.zh: 我女儿很喜欢学校的科学课。

sciences.t: n. 各门科学；理科（science 的复数）

e.en: She majored in the natural {sciences} at university.
e.zh: 她在大学主修自然科学。

e.en: The social {sciences} study human behavior and society.
e.zh: 社会科学研究人类行为与社会。

e.en: The claim has no real {scientific} evidence behind it.
e.zh: 这个说法背后没有真正的科学依据。

e.en: Her approach to cooking is almost {scientific}.
e.zh: 她对烹饪的方式几乎是科学化的。

scientifically.t: adv. 科学地；从科学角度

e.en: The product is not {scientifically} proven to work.
e.zh: 该产品并未经过科学验证有效。

e.en: He explained the result {scientifically} and clearly.
e.zh: 他用科学的方式清晰地解释了结果。

e.en: Critics questioned the {scientificity} of the new study.
e.zh: 批评者质疑这项新研究的科学性。

e.en: His paper lacks rigor and {scientificity}.
e.zh: 他的论文缺乏严谨性和科学性。

savant.t: n. 博学之士；专家（尤指某领域天才）

e.en: The young pianist is considered a true musical {savant}.
e.zh: 这位年轻钢琴家被视为真正的音乐天才。

e.en: He's an autistic {savant} with extraordinary memory skills.
e.zh: 他是一位拥有非凡记忆力的自闭症学者天才。

save.t:
v. 保存；拯救；节省
n. 救球

e.en: Remember to {save} your document before closing the app.
e.zh: 关闭应用前记得保存你的文档。

e.en: I'm trying to {save} money for a new laptop.
e.zh: 我正在攒钱买一台新笔记本电脑。

saved.t:
adj. 已保存的
v. save 的过去式

e.en: The lifeguard {saved} a child from drowning yesterday.
e.zh: 昨天救生员救起了一个溺水的孩子。

e.en: I {saved} all my photos to the cloud automatically.
e.zh: 我把所有照片都自动保存到云端了。

saver.t: n. 节省者；储蓄者；省XX的东西

e.en: This app is a real time {saver} for busy parents.
e.zh: 这个应用对忙碌的家长来说真是省时神器。

e.en: He's always been a careful {saver} rather than a spender.
e.zh: 他一向是个谨慎的存钱者,而不是花钱的人。

saves.t:
v. save 的第三人称单数
n. 救球（复数）

e.en: The goalkeeper made several spectacular {saves} in the final.
e.zh: 门将在决赛中做出了好几次精彩扑救。

e.en: Working from home {saves} me two hours of commuting daily.
e.zh: 在家办公每天为我节省了两个小时通勤时间。

savin.t: n. 沙地柏（一种桧属植物）

e.en: Old gardens often included a {savin} for medicinal use.
e.zh: 旧时的花园里常常种着一棵叉子圆柏入药。

e.en: The {savin} bush is toxic to grazing livestock.
e.zh: 叉子圆柏对放牧的牲畜有毒。

saving.t:
v. 保存；节省
n. 节约；存款

e.en: She's {saving} every dollar for her trip to Japan.
e.zh: 她正在攒每一块钱去日本旅行。

e.en: The new policy is {saving} the company millions annually.
e.zh: 新政策每年为公司节省了数百万元。

e.en: He emptied his {savings} account to buy the car.
e.zh: 他把储蓄账户清空买下了那辆车。

e.en: The sale offers huge {savings} on winter coats.
e.zh: 这次促销冬季外套优惠力度很大。

e.en: Coffee was my {savior} during exam week.
e.zh: 考试周咖啡简直是我的救星。

e.en: The new manager became the team's {savior} after the crisis.
e.zh: 新经理在危机过后成了团队的救星。

saviour.t: n. 救世主（savior 英式拼写）

e.en: That handyman was a real {saviour} when our pipes burst.
e.zh: 水管爆裂时那位维修工真是我们的救星。

e.en: Many regard the doctor as a {saviour} of the village.
e.zh: 许多人把这位医生视为村庄的救星。

savor.t:
v. 品味；享受
n. 风味

e.en: Take time to {savor} every bite of this meal.
e.zh: 花点时间细细品味这顿饭的每一口。

e.en: I want to {savor} this victory for a moment.
e.zh: 我想好好享受一下这次胜利的喜悦。

savory.t: adj. 咸香的；美味可口的

e.en: I prefer {savory} breakfasts like eggs and bacon over sweet ones.
e.zh: 比起甜食,我早餐更喜欢吃鸡蛋培根这类咸味的。

e.en: The chef created a {savory} pie with mushrooms and cheese.
e.zh: 厨师做了一款蘑菇芝士的咸味派。

savour.t: v. 品味；享受（savor 英式拼写）

e.en: Take time to {savour} every bite of this meal.
e.zh: 慢慢品尝这顿饭的每一口吧。

e.en: She wanted to {savour} the moment of victory.
e.zh: 她想细细品味这胜利的时刻。

savoury.t: adj. 咸香的（savory 英式拼写）

e.en: I'd rather have something {savoury} than a sweet dessert.
e.zh: 比起甜点,我更想吃点咸口的东西。

e.en: The bakery sells both sweet pastries and {savoury} pies.
e.zh: 这家面包店既卖甜点也卖咸味派。

savoy.t: n. 皱叶甘蓝；萨伏伊（地名）

e.en: This recipe uses {savoy} cabbage instead of regular green cabbage.
e.zh: 这道菜用的是皱叶甘蓝,而不是普通的绿甘蓝。

e.en: They celebrated their anniversary with dinner at the {Savoy}.
e.zh: 他们在萨伏伊酒店共进晚餐庆祝结婚纪念日。

savvier.t: adj. savvy 的比较级，更懂行的

e.en: The new intern is much {savvier} about social media trends.
e.zh: 这位新实习生对社交媒体趋势更为精通。

e.en: Older shoppers have grown {savvier} at spotting online scams.
e.zh: 年长的购物者越来越善于识别网络骗局。

savvy.t:
adj. 精明的；懂行的
n. 悟性

e.en: She is a {savvy} investor who avoids risky startups.
e.zh: 她是个精明的投资者,会避开高风险的初创公司。

e.en: You need tech {savvy} to set up this router.
e.zh: 你需要一些技术常识才能配置这台路由器。

saw.t:
n. 锯子
v. 锯；see 的过去式

e.en: The old western called the town doctor a {sawbones}.
e.zh: 那部老西部片把镇上的医生戏称为江湖郎中。

e.en: Get the {sawbones}—the captain has been shot in the leg.
e.zh: 快去叫军医来——船长腿上中弹了。

sawbuck.t: n. 锯木架；十美元钞票（俚）

e.en: He pulled a crumpled {sawbuck} from his back pocket.
e.zh: 他从后口袋里掏出一张皱巴巴的十美元钞票。

e.en: Lend me a {sawbuck} until payday, please.
e.zh: 借我十块钱,等发工资再还你。

e.en: The workshop floor was covered in fragrant pine {sawdust}.
e.zh: 车间地板上铺满了散发松香的锯末。

e.en: Sweep up the {sawdust} before the customers arrive.
e.zh: 在顾客到来之前把锯末清扫干净。

sawed.t: v. saw 的过去式/过去分词（锯）

e.en: He {sawed} the plank in half for the bookshelf.
e.zh: 他把木板锯成两半来做书架。

e.en: The carpenter {sawed} through the beam in minutes.
e.zh: 那位木匠几分钟就把梁锯断了。

e.en: Alligators glide silently through the Everglades {sawgrass}.
e.zh: 鳄鱼在大沼泽地的锯草丛中悄然游动。

e.en: The {sawgrass} cut his ankles as he waded ashore.
e.zh: 他涉水上岸时,锯草划伤了他的脚踝。

e.en: He balanced the long board across two wooden {sawhorse} stands.
e.zh: 他把长木板架在两个木制锯木架上。

e.en: The {sawhorse} folded flat for easy storage.
e.zh: 这个锯木架可以折叠平放以便收纳。

sawing.t: v. 锯（saw 的现在分词）

e.en: The neighbors complained about the {sawing} noise all morning.
e.zh: 邻居们抱怨了一上午的锯木声。

e.en: He spent the afternoon {sawing} firewood for winter.
e.zh: 他花了一下午锯柴准备过冬。

e.en: Logs are trucked to the {sawmill} every morning.
e.zh: 原木每天早上被卡车运到锯木厂。

e.en: Her grandfather worked at the local {sawmill} for decades.
e.zh: 她祖父在当地的锯木厂工作了几十年。

sawn.t: v. saw 的过去分词（锯开的）

e.en: The {sawn} planks were stacked neatly behind the barn.
e.zh: 锯好的木板整齐地堆在谷仓后面。

e.en: He carried a piece of freshly {sawn} oak inside.
e.zh: 他把一块刚锯好的橡木搬进屋里。

saws.t:
n. 锯子（复数）
v. 锯（第三人称单数）

e.en: The carpenter keeps his {saws} sharp and well oiled.
e.zh: 那位木匠把锯子保养得锋利又润滑。

e.en: Power {saws} make cutting hardwood much faster.
e.zh: 电锯能让切割硬木快得多。

sawtooth.t:
n. 锯齿
adj. 锯齿状的

e.en: The chart showed a {sawtooth} pattern of daily traffic.
e.zh: 图表显示出每日流量呈锯齿状的波动。

e.en: Hikers admired the jagged {sawtooth} ridge at sunset.
e.zh: 徒步者在日落时欣赏那座参差的锯齿状山脊。

e.en: The {sawyer} measured each log before cutting it.
e.zh: 那位锯木工人每根原木下锯前都先测量。

e.en: His grandfather earned a living as a village {sawyer}.
e.zh: 他祖父靠在村里当锯木工谋生。

sax.t: n. 萨克斯管（saxophone 的缩写）

e.en: Tiny pink {saxifrage} flowers bloomed between the rocks.
e.zh: 粉色的小虎耳草花在岩石缝间绽放。

e.en: Alpine {saxifrage} thrives in cold, rocky soil.
e.zh: 高山虎耳草在寒冷多石的土壤中长得茂盛。

saxon.t:
n. 撒克逊人
adj. 撒克逊的

e.en: The museum displayed weapons from the {Saxon} period.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了撒克逊时期的武器。

e.en: Many English place names have {Saxon} origins.
e.zh: 许多英格兰地名都源自撒克逊语。

saxony.t: n. 萨克森（德国地区）；萨克森毛呢

e.en: Dresden is the cultural capital of {Saxony}, in Germany.
e.zh: 德累斯顿是德国萨克森州的文化中心。

e.en: She bought a fine {Saxony} wool sweater for winter.
e.zh: 她买了一件优质萨克森羊毛衫过冬。

e.en: He played a smooth jazz solo on his {saxophone}.
e.zh: 他用萨克斯风演奏了一段流畅的爵士独奏。

e.en: She is learning to play the {saxophone} after work.
e.zh: 她下班后在学吹萨克斯风。

e.en: The {saxophonist} stole the show with a soulful solo.
e.zh: 那位萨克斯手以一段动人的独奏抢尽风头。

e.en: She dreams of becoming a professional jazz {saxophonist}.
e.zh: 她梦想成为一名职业爵士萨克斯演奏家。

say.t:
v. 说；表达
n. 发言权

e.en: He's a doer, not just a {sayer} of bold things.
e.zh: 他是个实干家,而不只是说大话的人。

e.en: The naysayer in the group is rarely the truth-{sayer}.
e.zh: 团队里唱反调的人未必就是说真话的人。

saying.t:
n. 谚语；格言
v. say 的现在分词

e.en: There's an old {saying} that practice makes perfect.
e.zh: 有句老话说,熟能生巧。

e.en: What were you {saying} before the call dropped?
e.zh: 电话断之前你刚才在说什么?

sayonara.t: int. 再见（源自日语 さようなら）

e.en: He waved and shouted {sayonara} as the train pulled away.
e.zh: 火车开动时他挥手喊了一声再见。

e.en: One bad review and it's {sayonara} to your reputation.
e.zh: 一条差评,你的名声就拜拜了。

says.t: v. say 的第三人称单数

e.en: The forecast {says} it will rain all weekend.
e.zh: 天气预报说整个周末都会下雨。

e.en: She {says} hello whenever we pass in the hallway.
e.zh: 我们在走廊擦肩而过时她总会打招呼。

sbu.t: n. 战略业务单元（Strategic Business Unit 缩写）

scientism.t: n. 科学主义（过度推崇科学的观点）

e.en: He warned against the {scientism} that ignores ethics.
e.zh: 他警告人们提防那种忽视伦理的科学主义。

e.en: Critics accused the author of crude {scientism}.
e.zh: 批评者指责作者持有粗糙的科学主义。

e.en: The {scientist} published her findings in Nature.
e.zh: 那位科学家在《自然》杂志发表了研究成果。

e.en: He dreamed of becoming a climate {scientist}.
e.zh: 他梦想成为一名气候科学家。

e.en: Her tone was overly {scientistic} for a humanities essay.
e.zh: 她的语气对人文论文来说过于科学主义化了。

e.en: The book criticizes {scientistic} explanations of love.
e.zh: 这本书批判了对爱情的科学主义式解释。

e.en: {Scientists} are racing to develop a new vaccine.
e.zh: 科学家们正在加紧研发新疫苗。

e.en: A team of {scientists} discovered the rare fossil.
e.zh: 一支科学家团队发现了这块罕见的化石。

scientology.t: n. 山达基教（科学教派）

e.en: The documentary explores controversies surrounding {Scientology}.
e.zh: 这部纪录片探讨了围绕山达基教的争议。

e.en: Several celebrities are well-known members of {Scientology}.
e.zh: 几位名人是知名的山达基教信徒。

scilly.t: n. 锡利群岛（英国地名）

e.en: We sailed to the {Scilly} Isles for a quiet holiday.
e.zh: 我们坐船去锡利群岛度过了一个宁静的假期。

e.en: The {Scilly} Islands lie off the southwest tip of England.
e.zh: 锡利群岛位于英格兰西南端外海。

scimitar.t: n. 弯刀（阿拉伯式短弯刀）

e.en: The warrior carried a curved {scimitar} at his side.
e.zh: 武士腰间挎着一把弯刀。

e.en: A jeweled {scimitar} hung above the fireplace.
e.zh: 壁炉上方挂着一把镶满宝石的弯刀。

e.en: There isn't a {scintilla} of evidence to support that claim.
e.zh: 没有一丝证据能支持这种说法。

e.en: She showed not a {scintilla} of doubt during the interview.
e.zh: 面试时她没流露出一丁点的怀疑。

e.en: Diamonds {scintillate} beautifully under the bright gallery lights.
e.zh: 钻石在明亮的画廊灯光下闪闪发光。

e.en: Her witty comments {scintillate} throughout every dinner party.
e.zh: 她机智的妙语让每场晚宴都熠熠生辉。

scintillating.t: adj. 才华横溢的；妙趣横生的

e.en: The two professors had a {scintillating} debate about ethics.
e.zh: 两位教授就伦理问题展开了一场精彩的辩论。

e.en: Her {scintillating} dress caught everyone's attention at the gala.
e.zh: 她那件闪闪发光的礼服在晚会上吸引了所有人的目光。

e.en: Stars show a beautiful {scintillation} when viewed from Earth.
e.zh: 从地球上看,星星会呈现出美丽的闪烁。

e.en: Detectors measure the {scintillation} produced by radioactive particles.
e.zh: 探测器测量放射性粒子产生的闪烁信号。

scion.t:
n. 名门之后
n. 接穗（嫁接用枝条）

e.en: He is the {scion} of a wealthy banking family.
e.zh: 他是一个富有银行世家的后裔。

e.en: The young {scion} took over the company last year.
e.zh: 那位年轻的家族继承人去年接管了公司。

scipio.t: n. 西庇阿（古罗马将领）

e.en: {Scipio} defeated Hannibal at the famous battle of Zama.
e.zh: 西庇阿在著名的扎马战役中击败了汉尼拔。

e.en: Roman general {Scipio} is studied in many history classes.
e.zh: 罗马将军西庇阿在许多历史课上都会被讲到。

e.en: The chemical reaction caused {scission} of the polymer chain.
e.zh: 这种化学反应导致聚合物链发生断裂。

e.en: DNA {scission} is a key step in genetic editing.
e.zh: DNA 断裂是基因编辑中的关键步骤。

scissor.t:
v. 剪开
n. 剪刀（单数形式）

e.en: Tailors {scissor} fabric carefully to avoid uneven edges.
e.zh: 裁缝小心地剪布,以免边缘不齐。

e.en: The gymnast performed a perfect {scissor} kick on the beam.
e.zh: 体操运动员在平衡木上完成了一个漂亮的剪式踢腿。

e.en: Please pass me the {scissors} on the kitchen counter.
e.zh: 请把厨房台面上的剪刀递给我。

e.en: These kid-safe {scissors} have rounded plastic tips.
e.zh: 这些儿童安全剪刀的刀尖是圆头塑料的。

sclerite.t: n. 骨片；硬皮（昆虫外壳）

e.en: Each {sclerite} on the beetle's body provides extra armor.
e.zh: 甲虫身上的每块硬片都提供了额外的护甲。

e.en: Entomologists examined the insect's {sclerite} under a microscope.
e.zh: 昆虫学家用显微镜观察了这只昆虫的骨片。

e.en: Patients with {scleroderma} often experience tightening of the skin.
e.zh: 硬皮病患者常常会出现皮肤变紧的症状。

e.en: Her doctor diagnosed early-stage {scleroderma} after several tests.
e.zh: 经过几次检查后,医生诊断她为早期硬皮病。

e.en: Untreated arteries can {sclerose} and harden over time.
e.zh: 未经治疗的动脉会随时间硬化。

e.en: Doctors warn that the tissues may {sclerose} after repeated injury.
e.zh: 医生警告反复损伤后组织可能硬化。

e.en: The patient was diagnosed with a rare {sclerosing} liver disease.
e.zh: 该患者被诊断出患有罕见的硬化性肝病。

e.en: Doctors used a {sclerosing} agent to close the swollen vein.
e.zh: 医生使用硬化剂封闭了曲张的静脉。

sclerosis.t: n. 硬化症（如多发性硬化）

e.en: Multiple {sclerosis} affects nerve signals throughout the body.
e.zh: 多发性硬化症会影响全身的神经信号传导。

e.en: Early diagnosis of {sclerosis} can slow its progression.
e.zh: 硬化症的早期诊断可以延缓病情发展。

sclerotherapy.t: n. 硬化剂疗法（治静脉曲张）

e.en: She booked {sclerotherapy} to treat the visible spider veins.
e.zh: 她预约了硬化剂治疗来处理明显的蜘蛛状静脉。

e.en: {Sclerotherapy} is a common minimally invasive vein procedure.
e.zh: 硬化剂注射疗法是一种常见的微创静脉治疗。

e.en: Critics called the bureaucracy {sclerotic} and resistant to change.
e.zh: 批评人士称这套官僚体系僵化且抗拒改变。

e.en: The scan revealed {sclerotic} patches on the patient's bones.
e.zh: 扫描显示患者骨骼上有硬化斑块。

scm.t: n. 源代码管理（Source Code Management）

sco.t: n. SCO（SCO 公司或圣克鲁兹操作系统）

e.en: Don't {scoff} at ideas before you've actually tested them.
e.zh: 还没真正试过之前别嘲笑那些想法。

e.en: Investors {scoff} at startups with no clear revenue model.
e.zh: 投资人会嘲笑没有清晰盈利模式的初创公司。

e.en: He {scoffed} at the idea of working from a beach.
e.zh: 他嘲笑在海滩上办公这种想法。

e.en: Critics {scoffed} when the tiny startup announced its plans.
e.zh: 那家小公司公布计划时,评论者纷纷嗤之以鼻。

e.en: Every {scoffer} eventually downloaded the app and loved it.
e.zh: 每个嘲讽者最终都下载了这款应用,而且爱上了它。

e.en: He's a known {scoffer} when it comes to crypto trends.
e.zh: 一谈到加密货币趋势,他就是出了名的爱嘲笑人。

e.en: Stop {scoffing} and give the new feature a fair try.
e.zh: 别再冷嘲热讽了,公平地试试这个新功能。

e.en: The audience kept {scoffing} throughout the politician's vague speech.
e.zh: 政客发表空洞演讲时,观众一直在嗤笑。

e.en: The city cracked down on every parking {scofflaw} this month.
e.zh: 市政府本月严打每一个无视停车法规的违规者。

e.en: He's a notorious {scofflaw} who ignores traffic cameras entirely.
e.zh: 他是个臭名昭著的违法者,完全无视交通摄像头。

scoffs.t: v. 嘲笑（第三人称单数）

e.en: She {scoffs} at anyone who pays full price online.
e.zh: 她嘲笑任何在网上买东西付原价的人。

e.en: He {scoffs} whenever someone mentions a four-hour workweek.
e.zh: 每当有人提起每周只工作四小时,他就嗤之以鼻。

e.en: Try not to {scold} the kids over small mistakes.
e.zh: 尽量不要因为小错误就责骂孩子。

e.en: My manager will {scold} anyone who skips the safety briefing.
e.zh: 我经理会责骂任何跳过安全简报的人。

e.en: The teacher {scolded} him for using his phone in class.
e.zh: 老师因为他在课堂上玩手机而训斥了他。

e.en: She {scolded} herself for forgetting the meeting again.
e.zh: 她又一次忘记开会,为此责备自己。

scolding.t:
n. 一顿训斥
v. 责骂（进行时）

e.en: He got a serious {scolding} for missing the project deadline.
e.zh: 他因为错过项目截止日期被狠狠训了一顿。

e.en: Stop {scolding} the dog and try positive reinforcement instead.
e.zh: 别再骂狗了,试试用正向激励吧。

scolds.t: v. 责骂（第三人称单数）

e.en: My mom always {scolds} me for skipping breakfast on workdays.
e.zh: 我妈总因为我工作日不吃早餐而念叨我。

e.en: The coach {scolds} players who arrive late to practice.
e.zh: 教练会斥责训练迟到的球员。

e.en: She wears a brace at night to manage her {scoliosis}.
e.zh: 她晚上戴支具来控制脊柱侧弯。

e.en: Early screening for {scoliosis} can prevent more serious problems.
e.zh: 及早筛查脊柱侧弯可以预防更严重的问题。

e.en: They installed a brass {sconce} beside the bathroom mirror.
e.zh: 他们在浴室镜子旁装了一盏黄铜壁灯。

e.en: Each hallway {sconce} casts a soft, warm glow.
e.zh: 走廊里每盏壁灯都投出柔和温暖的光。

scone.t: n. 司康饼（英式小圆饼）

e.en: I ordered a blueberry {scone} with my morning coffee.
e.zh: 我点了一杯早咖啡,配一个蓝莓司康饼。

e.en: This bakery's cranberry {scone} is famous across the neighborhood.
e.zh: 这家烘焙店的蔓越莓司康在整个街区都很有名。

scoop.t:
n. 勺子；独家新闻
v. 舀起

e.en: Reporters raced to publish the {scoop} before competitors did.
e.zh: 记者们争相在对手之前发布这条独家新闻。

e.en: Can I get one {scoop} of vanilla in a cone?
e.zh: 能给我装一个香草冰淇淋甜筒吗?

scooped.t: v. 舀起；抢先报道（过去式）

e.en: The newspaper {scooped} every rival on the merger story.
e.zh: 那家报纸在并购报道上抢先所有对手发布。

e.en: She {scooped} ice cream into the kids' colorful bowls.
e.zh: 她把冰淇淋舀进孩子们五彩的碗里。

e.en: Use the metal {scooper} to portion the cookie dough evenly.
e.zh: 用金属勺将曲奇面团均匀分量。

e.en: Every dog owner should carry a {scooper} on walks.
e.zh: 每位养狗的人遛狗时都应随身带便便铲。

e.en: Could you {scoot} over so I can sit down?
e.zh: 你能挪一下让我坐下吗?

e.en: I need to {scoot} home before the rain starts.
e.zh: 我得在下雨前赶紧回家。

e.en: He rented an electric {scooter} to get across campus quickly.
e.zh: 他租了辆电动滑板车快速穿过校园。

e.en: My kid begged for a kick {scooter} for his birthday.
e.zh: 我家孩子吵着生日要一辆踏板车。

e.en: Shared {scooters} are scattered along every sidewalk downtown.
e.zh: 市中心每条人行道上都散落着共享滑板车。

e.en: The city banned {scooters} from busy pedestrian zones.
e.zh: 市政府禁止滑板车进入繁忙的步行区。

e.en: The project's {scope} expanded well beyond the original plan.
e.zh: 项目的范围远远超出了最初的计划。

e.en: Variables declared inside a function have local {scope}.
e.zh: 在函数内部声明的变量具有局部作用域。

scoped.t:
adj. 限定作用域的
v. 审视（过去式）

e.en: We {scoped} the feature down to ship before the deadline.
e.zh: 我们缩小了功能范围,以便在截止日期前上线。

e.en: This CSS rule is {scoped} to the dashboard component only.
e.zh: 这条 CSS 规则的作用域仅限于仪表板组件。

e.en: The OAuth token requested too many permission {scopes}.
e.zh: 该 OAuth 令牌请求的权限范围过多。

e.en: Hunters compared rifle {scopes} before the camping trip.
e.zh: 猎人们在露营前比较各自的步枪瞄准镜。

e.en: The film explores the {scopic} pleasure of watching strangers.
e.zh: 这部电影探讨了观看陌生人时的视觉快感。

e.en: Critics analyze the {scopic} regime of modern social media.
e.zh: 评论家分析现代社交媒体中的视觉机制。

e.en: Don't let the iron {scorch} the silk blouse.
e.zh: 别让熨斗烫焦那件丝绸衬衫。

e.en: Wildfires continue to {scorch} acres of dry forest.
e.zh: 野火持续烧焦大片干燥的森林。

e.en: The summer sun {scorched} the grass in our backyard.
e.zh: 夏日的太阳把我们后院的草地都晒焦了。

e.en: She accidentally {scorched} the pancakes while checking her phone.
e.zh: 她看手机时不小心把煎饼煎糊了。

scorcher.t: n. 酷热的一天；极热的东西

e.en: Today's forecast calls for a real {scorcher} downtown.
e.zh: 今天的天气预报说市中心会非常酷热。

e.en: That final episode was a {scorcher} — totally unforgettable.
e.zh: 那集大结局太精彩了,令人难忘。

scorching.t:
adj. 灼热的；猛烈的
adv. 非常（热）

e.en: We hiked early to avoid the {scorching} afternoon heat.
e.zh: 我们一早就去徒步,避开下午的酷热。

e.en: The review gave a {scorching} critique of the new app.
e.zh: 那篇评论对这款新应用进行了猛烈抨击。

score.t:
n. 分数；比分
v. 得分；评分

e.en: Did you check the final {score} of last night's game?
e.zh: 你看昨晚比赛的最终比分了吗?

e.en: Her credit {score} jumped after she paid off the loan.
e.zh: 她还清贷款后信用分数大幅上升。

e.en: Fans cheered when the {scoreboard} flashed the winning goal.
e.zh: 当记分牌显示制胜进球时,球迷欢呼起来。

e.en: The giant {scoreboard} replays every key moment in slow motion.
e.zh: 巨型记分牌以慢动作回放每一个关键时刻。

e.en: Investors review the company's quarterly {scorecard} for key metrics.
e.zh: 投资者通过季度报告卡查看公司的关键指标。

e.en: He filled out the golf {scorecard} after every hole.
e.zh: 他每打完一洞就填一次高尔夫记分卡。

scored.t: v. 得分（score 的过去式）

e.en: She {scored} the winning goal in the final minute.
e.zh: 她在最后一分钟攻入了制胜球。

e.en: I {scored} two free tickets to the concert tonight.
e.zh: 我搞到了今晚演唱会的两张免费票。

e.en: The {scorekeeper} updates the bracket after every match.
e.zh: 记分员在每场比赛后更新对阵表。

e.en: My uncle volunteers as the {scorekeeper} for Little League games.
e.zh: 我叔叔自愿担任少年棒球联赛的记分员。

scoreless.t: adj. 未得分的；零比零的

e.en: The match remained {scoreless} after a tense first half.
e.zh: 上半场紧张激烈,但比分仍然为零。

e.en: Both teams left the field after a {scoreless} draw.
e.zh: 两队以零比零的平局结束了比赛。

e.en: The final {scoreline} flattered the losing side considerably.
e.zh: 最终的比分对输球的一方相当客气。

e.en: A 4-0 {scoreline} stunned fans of the home team.
e.zh: 4比0的比分让主队球迷大为震惊。

e.en: He's the league's top {scorer} for the third straight season.
e.zh: 他连续第三个赛季成为联赛头号射手。

e.en: Every {scorer} on the team contributed to last night's win.
e.zh: 球队每位得分手都为昨晚的胜利做出了贡献。

scores.t:
n. 分数（复数）
det. 许多；大量

e.en: Test {scores} have improved across every grade level this year.
e.zh: 今年各年级的考试分数都有所提高。

e.en: {Scores} of fans lined up outside the stadium overnight.
e.zh: 成群的球迷彻夜在体育场外排队。

e.en: The referee handed the {scoresheet} to the league official.
e.zh: 裁判把记分表交给了联赛官员。

e.en: Players signed the {scoresheet} immediately after the chess match.
e.zh: 棋手在国际象棋比赛结束后立即在记分表上签字。

scoring.t:
n. 得分；计分
v. 得分（进行时）

e.en: His {scoring} ability has dramatically improved since last season.
e.zh: 自上赛季以来,他的得分能力显著提高。

e.en: The model uses a custom {scoring} system to rank candidates.
e.zh: 该模型使用自定义评分系统对候选人进行排名。

scorn.t:
n. 蔑视；嘲笑
v. 鄙视

e.en: She poured {scorn} on the half-baked marketing proposal.
e.zh: 她对那份不成熟的营销方案极尽嘲讽。

e.en: Public {scorn} forced the company to reverse its decision.
e.zh: 公众的鄙视迫使公司收回了决定。

scorned.t: v. 鄙视（scorn 的过去式）

e.en: He was {scorned} by colleagues for cutting corners on safety.
e.zh: 他因在安全上偷工减料而被同事鄙视。

e.en: The proposal was openly {scorned} during the town hall meeting.
e.zh: 该提案在市政厅会议上遭到公开蔑视。

e.en: She gave him a {scornful} look and walked away silently.
e.zh: 她轻蔑地瞥了他一眼,默默走开了。

e.en: His {scornful} tone made the whole team uncomfortable.
e.zh: 他轻蔑的语气让整个团队都很不舒服。

e.en: He laughed {scornfully} when asked about his rival's success.
e.zh: 被问起对手的成就时,他轻蔑地大笑起来。

e.en: She {scornfully} dismissed the idea as completely unrealistic.
e.zh: 她轻蔑地把这个想法斥为完全不切实际。

scorns.t: v. 鄙视（scorn 的第三人称单数）

e.en: He openly {scorns} anyone who relies on horoscopes for decisions.
e.zh: 他公开鄙视那些靠星座做决定的人。

e.en: My grandmother {scorns} every modern cooking shortcut on principle.
e.zh: 我奶奶在原则上鄙视一切现代烹饪的偷懒方法。

e.en: As a {Scorpio}, she claims to be intensely loyal.
e.zh: 作为天蝎座,她说自己极度忠诚。

e.en: My best friend is a typical {Scorpio} — passionate and private.
e.zh: 我最好的朋友是典型的天蝎座——热烈又私密。

e.en: A small {scorpion} crawled out from under the desert rock.
e.zh: 一只小蝎子从沙漠石头下爬了出来。

e.en: The hiker checked his boots for any hidden {scorpion}.
e.zh: 徒步者检查了靴子里是否藏有蝎子。

e.en: He walked away {scot}-free despite breaking the rules.
e.zh: 尽管违规，他却毫发无损地脱身了。

e.en: The judge let the witness go {scot}-free.
e.zh: 法官让那名证人安然无事地离开了。

scotch.t:
n. 苏格兰威士忌
v. 制止；粉碎

e.en: The CEO moved quickly to {scotch} the merger rumors.
e.zh: 首席执行官迅速出面平息合并的传闻。

e.en: He poured a glass of single malt {scotch} after dinner.
e.zh: 晚餐后他倒了一杯单一麦芽苏格兰威士忌。

scotia.t: n. 斯科舍（苏格兰的古称）

e.en: Nova {Scotia} is famous for its rugged Atlantic coastline.
e.zh: 新斯科舍省以其崎岖的大西洋海岸线闻名。

e.en: We flew to Halifax in Nova {Scotia} last summer.
e.zh: 去年夏天我们飞往新斯科舍省的哈利法克斯。

e.en: We hiked through the highlands of {Scotland} last August.
e.zh: 去年八月我们徒步穿越了苏格兰高地。

e.en: {Scotland} is known for its whisky, kilts, and bagpipes.
e.zh: 苏格兰以威士忌、苏格兰短裙和风笛闻名。

e.en: The patient described a dark {scotoma} in her left eye.
e.zh: 病人描述左眼中有一片暗暗的盲点。

e.en: Migraines often produce a shimmering {scotoma} before the pain.
e.zh: 偏头痛发作前常出现闪烁的视野盲点。

scots.t:
adj. 苏格兰的
n. 苏格兰语

e.en: Many {Scots} celebrate Burns Night every January.
e.zh: 许多苏格兰人每年一月都会庆祝彭斯之夜。

e.en: The novel includes phrases written in broad {Scots}.
e.zh: 这本小说里有用浓厚苏格兰方言写的句子。

e.en: The {Scotsman} proudly wore his family tartan to the wedding.
e.zh: 那位苏格兰人自豪地穿着家族花格呢去参加婚礼。

e.en: A friendly {Scotsman} gave us directions to the castle.
e.zh: 一位友善的苏格兰人给我们指了去城堡的路。

e.en: Three {Scotsmen} played bagpipes at the opening ceremony.
e.zh: 三位苏格兰人在开幕式上演奏风笛。

e.en: The pub was crowded with cheerful {Scotsmen} after the match.
e.zh: 比赛结束后酒吧里挤满了兴高采烈的苏格兰人。

scottie.t: n. 苏格兰梗犬；昵称斯科蒂

e.en: Her black {Scottie} trotted happily beside the stroller.
e.zh: 她那只黑色苏格兰梗欢快地小跑在婴儿车旁。

e.en: The president famously kept a {Scottie} named Barney.
e.zh: 那位总统养了一只名叫巴尼的苏格兰梗，广为人知。

scottish.t: adj. 苏格兰的；苏格兰人的

e.en: She speaks with a soft {Scottish} accent.
e.zh: 她说话带着柔和的苏格兰口音。

e.en: We tried haggis at a traditional {Scottish} restaurant.
e.zh: 我们在一家传统苏格兰餐厅尝了哈吉斯。

e.en: That {scoundrel} tricked elderly people out of their savings.
e.zh: 那个恶棍骗走了老人们的积蓄。

e.en: In the novel, the {scoundrel} eventually gets his comeuppance.
e.zh: 小说里，那个无赖最终自食其果。

e.en: I had to {scour} the pan to remove the burnt sauce.
e.zh: 我不得不使劲擦洗锅子，把烧焦的酱汁去掉。

e.en: Detectives {scour} social media for clues about the suspect.
e.zh: 侦探们在社交媒体上仔细搜寻嫌疑人的线索。

scoured.t: v. 擦洗/搜遍（scour 的过去式）

e.en: She {scoured} every shop in town for the rare book.
e.zh: 她跑遍城里每家书店寻找那本珍本。

e.en: He {scoured} the bathtub until it gleamed.
e.zh: 他把浴缸刷得锃亮。

e.en: Use a metal {scourer} to clean the burnt grill.
e.zh: 用金属钢丝球来清洁烧焦的烤架。

e.en: The {scourer} wore through after weeks of heavy use.
e.zh: 那块钢丝球用了几周后就磨破了。

scourge.t:
n. 祸害；灾难
v. 折磨

e.en: Plastic pollution has become a {scourge} of modern oceans.
e.zh: 塑料污染已成为现代海洋的一大祸患。

e.en: Antibiotics greatly reduced the {scourge} of bacterial infections.
e.zh: 抗生素大大减轻了细菌感染这一灾祸。

scouring.t:
n. 擦洗；彻底搜寻
v. 擦洗（进行时）

e.en: Investigators are {scouring} the area for missing evidence.
e.zh: 调查人员正在该地区仔细搜寻丢失的证据。

e.en: She spent the morning {scouring} the kitchen tiles.
e.zh: 她花了一上午擦洗厨房的瓷砖。

scouse.t: n. 利物浦口音；利物浦人

e.en: His thick {Scouse} accent gave away his Liverpool roots.
e.zh: 他浓重的利物浦口音暴露了他的家乡。

e.en: We had a hearty bowl of {scouse} stew for lunch.
e.zh: 午餐我们吃了一大碗丰盛的利物浦炖肉。

e.en: The proud {Scouser} cheered loudly for Liverpool FC.
e.zh: 那位自豪的利物浦人为利物浦足球俱乐部大声欢呼。

e.en: Every {Scouser} I met was warm and quick-witted.
e.zh: 我遇到的每个利物浦人都热情又机智。

scout.t:
n. 侦察员；童子军
v. 侦察；物色

e.en: A talent {scout} spotted her at the school play.
e.zh: 一位星探在学校话剧表演中发现了她。

e.en: Let me {scout} ahead to see if the trail is clear.
e.zh: 让我先去前面探探路看看小道是否畅通。

e.en: NBA teams are {scouting} promising European players this season.
e.zh: NBA球队本赛季正在物色有潜力的欧洲球员。

e.en: He learned camping skills through {scouting} as a child.
e.zh: 他小时候通过童子军活动学到了野营技能。

e.en: The {scoutmaster} taught the boys how to tie knots.
e.zh: 童子军团长教孩子们如何打绳结。

e.en: Our {scoutmaster} led a weekend hike through the forest.
e.zh: 我们的童子军团长带队周末穿越森林徒步。

e.en: A flat-bottomed {scow} hauled gravel across the harbor.
e.zh: 一艘平底驳船把砾石运过港口。

e.en: The old {scow} creaked as workers loaded it with timber.
e.zh: 工人们往那艘旧驳船上装木材时它吱嘎作响。

scowl.t:
v. 怒视；皱眉
n. 怒容

e.en: She gave him a fierce {scowl} when he interrupted.
e.zh: 他打断她的话时，她狠狠地瞪了他一眼。

e.en: Don't {scowl} at me—I'm just trying to help.
e.zh: 别对我板着脸，我只是想帮忙。

e.en: The boss sat {scowling} at his computer all morning.
e.zh: 老板整个上午都板着脸盯着电脑。

e.en: A {scowling} guard waved us through the gate.
e.zh: 一个面色阴沉的守卫挥手让我们通过大门。

scr.t: n. 可控硅（Silicon Controlled Rectifier 缩写）

scrabble.t:
v. 乱抓；扒找
n. 拼字游戏

e.en: We played {Scrabble} on the porch all evening.
e.zh: 我们在门廊上玩了整晚拼字游戏。

e.en: Mice {scrabble} in the attic every night.
e.zh: 老鼠每晚都在阁楼里乱抓乱挠。

scrabbling.t: v. 乱抓、扒找（scrabble 的进行时）

e.en: The kitten was {scrabbling} at the door to get in.
e.zh: 小猫正用爪子抓门想要进来。

e.en: He kept {scrabbling} through his bag for the keys.
e.zh: 他一直在包里乱翻找钥匙。

scrag.t:
n. 瘦弱的人或动物颈部
v. 掐脖子

e.en: The butcher trimmed the {scrag} end for stew.
e.zh: 屠夫修整了用来炖菜的羊颈肉。

e.en: She bought a cheap {scrag} of mutton at the market.
e.zh: 她在市场上买了便宜的羊颈肉。

scraggly.t: adj. 参差不齐的；乱蓬蓬的

e.en: He stroked his {scraggly} beard while thinking.
e.zh: 他一边思考一边摸着稀疏凌乱的胡子。

e.en: A few {scraggly} pines clung to the cliff edge.
e.zh: 几棵稀疏凌乱的松树紧贴在悬崖边。

scraggy.t: adj. 瘦骨嶙峋的；粗糙不齐的

e.en: The stray cat was thin and {scraggy}.
e.zh: 那只流浪猫瘦得皮包骨。

e.en: He had a {scraggy} neck poking out of his oversized shirt.
e.zh: 他瘦削的脖子从过大的衬衫里伸出来。

e.en: The shopkeeper yelled at the kids to {scram}.
e.zh: 店主朝孩子们大喊让他们快滚。

e.en: You'd better {scram} before security catches you.
e.zh: 你最好在保安抓到你之前赶紧溜。

scramble.t:
v. 争抢；攀爬；扰乱（信号）
n. 混乱争夺

e.en: Engineers had to {scramble} to fix the outage overnight.
e.zh: 工程师们不得不连夜赶工修复故障。

e.en: I'll {scramble} some eggs for breakfast.
e.zh: 我做点炒蛋当早餐。

scrambled.t:
adj. 炒的（蛋）；被打乱的
v. scramble 的过去式

e.en: She ordered {scrambled} eggs with toast and bacon.
e.zh: 她点了炒蛋配吐司和培根。

e.en: The hikers {scrambled} up the rocky slope at dawn.
e.zh: 登山者们在黎明时分手脚并用攀上岩坡。

e.en: He bought a lightweight {scrambler} bike for off-road trails.
e.zh: 他买了一辆轻便的越野摩托车用于山道。

e.en: The signal {scrambler} prevented eavesdroppers from listening in.
e.zh: 信号干扰器防止了窃听者偷听。

scrambles.t: v. 争抢；攀爬（scramble 的三单）

e.en: The dog {scrambles} onto the couch whenever I sit down.
e.zh: 我一坐下，狗就立刻爬上沙发。

e.en: She {scrambles} four eggs every morning before work.
e.zh: 她每天上班前都炒四个鸡蛋。

scrambling.t: v. 攀爬；争抢（scramble 的进行时）

e.en: The team was {scrambling} to fix the bug before launch.
e.zh: 团队正手忙脚乱地在上线前修复这个 bug。

e.en: Hikers were {scrambling} up the rocky slope at dawn.
e.zh: 徒步者们在黎明时分攀爬岩石斜坡。

e.en: The {scramjet} can theoretically reach speeds above Mach 6.
e.zh: 超燃冲压发动机理论上能达到 6 马赫以上的速度。

e.en: Engineers tested a new {scramjet} engine over the desert.
e.zh: 工程师们在沙漠上空测试了一款新型超燃冲压发动机。

scrap.t:
n. 碎片；废料
v. 废弃；作废

e.en: He jotted the number on a {scrap} of paper.
e.zh: 他把电话号码记在一小片纸上。

e.en: The team decided to {scrap} the old design entirely.
e.zh: 团队决定彻底放弃旧设计。

e.en: She keeps a {scrapbook} of all her travel mementos.
e.zh: 她用一本剪贴簿收藏所有旅行纪念物。

e.en: Grandma showed me her wedding {scrapbook} from 1962.
e.zh: 奶奶给我看了她 1962 年的婚礼剪贴簿。

scrape.t:
v. 刮；擦；勉强凑够
n. 擦伤；困境

e.en: Be careful not to {scrape} your knee on the rock.
e.zh: 小心别在岩石上擦破膝盖。

e.en: I wrote a script to {scrape} prices from the website.
e.zh: 我写了个脚本从那个网站抓取价格。

scraped.t: v. 刮、擦（scrape 的过去式）

e.en: He {scraped} the ice off his windshield before driving.
e.zh: 他开车前把挡风玻璃上的冰刮掉了。

e.en: She just barely {scraped} through the final exam.
e.zh: 她勉强通过了期末考试。

scraper.t: n. 刮刀；爬虫程序（抓取工具）

e.en: I built a web {scraper} to collect job listings.
e.zh: 我做了一个网页抓取工具来收集招聘信息。

e.en: Use the plastic {scraper} to clean the dough off the counter.
e.zh: 用塑料刮板把面团从台面上刮下来。

e.en: The old project was tossed onto the {scrapheap} after layoffs.
e.zh: 裁员之后,那个老项目就被扔进了废料堆。

e.en: He felt thrown on the {scrapheap} after losing his job.
e.zh: 失业之后,他觉得自己像被扔进了垃圾堆。

scrapie.t: n. 羊瘙痒病（一种羊脑病）

e.en: {Scrapie} is a fatal brain disease that affects sheep.
e.zh: 羊瘙痒病是一种致命的绵羊脑部疾病。

e.en: Farmers must report any suspected case of {scrapie} immediately.
e.zh: 农户必须立即上报任何疑似羊瘙痒病的病例。

scraping.t:
v. 刮擦；数据抓取
n. 刮下的碎屑

e.en: Web {scraping} is how many price comparison sites get data.
e.zh: 许多比价网站都是通过网页抓取来获取数据的。

e.en: I heard a {scraping} sound coming from under the car.
e.zh: 我听到车底下传来刮擦的声音。

scrapped.t: v. 报废；废弃（scrap 的过去式）

e.en: The company {scrapped} the project after poor user feedback.
e.zh: 由于用户反馈不佳,公司放弃了这个项目。

e.en: They {scrapped} the old factory equipment for parts.
e.zh: 他们把旧工厂设备拆解卖零件了。

scrapper.t: n. 爱打架的人；拆解工

e.en: That little dog is a real {scrapper} despite his size.
e.zh: 那只小狗虽然个头小,却是个真正的小斗士。

e.en: She's a {scrapper} who never backs down from a challenge.
e.zh: 她是个不服输的人,从不在挑战面前退缩。

scrapping.t: v. 废弃；争吵（scrap 的进行时）

e.en: The government is {scrapping} the unpopular tax next year.
e.zh: 政府明年将废除这项不受欢迎的税收。

e.en: Two cats were {scrapping} loudly in the alley.
e.zh: 两只猫在巷子里大声打架。

scrapple.t: n. 肉糜糕（美式早餐食品）

e.en: Pennsylvania diners often serve {scrapple} with breakfast eggs.
e.zh: 宾夕法尼亚的小餐馆常把猪杂糕和早餐鸡蛋一起端上桌。

e.en: My grandfather fried {scrapple} every Sunday morning.
e.zh: 我祖父每个周日早上都会煎猪杂糕。

scrappy.t: adj. 好斗的；零碎拼凑的

e.en: The {scrappy} startup beat much larger competitors to market.
e.zh: 这家拼劲十足的初创公司抢在大公司之前进入了市场。

e.en: Their {scrappy} underdog team made it to the finals.
e.zh: 他们那支充满斗志的弱旅闯进了决赛。

e.en: He bought spare car parts from the local {scrapyard}.
