e.zh: 她给我看了新 logo 的草图。

e.en: He carries a {sketchbook} everywhere he travels.
e.zh: 他无论去哪儿旅行都带着速写本。

e.en: Her {sketchbook} is full of café scenes from Paris.
e.zh: 她的速写本里满是巴黎的咖啡馆速写。

e.en: Stacks of old {sketchbooks} filled the artist's studio.
e.zh: 画家的工作室里堆满了旧速写本。

e.en: The store sells {sketchbooks} in every size imaginable.
e.zh: 这家店出售各种尺寸的速写本。

sketched.t: v. 勾勒；画草图（过去式）

e.en: He {sketched} her portrait in under ten minutes.
e.zh: 他不到十分钟就画好了她的肖像。

e.en: The CEO {sketched} out the plan during the meeting.
e.zh: CEO 在会上简要勾勒了这个计划。

sketches.t:
n. 草图（复数）
v. 勾勒（第三人称）

e.en: Her notebook is filled with {sketches} of strangers on trains.
e.zh: 她的本子里画满了火车上陌生人的速写。

e.en: The comedy show featured several short {sketches} about office life.
e.zh: 那档喜剧节目演了几段关于职场的小品。

e.en: He described the suspect only {sketchily} to the police.
e.zh: 他向警方对嫌疑人的描述只是粗略带过。

e.en: The map was drawn {sketchily} but still useful.
e.zh: 地图画得很粗糙,但还算管用。

sketching.t: v. 画速写；勾勒（现在分词）

e.en: I love {sketching} in the park on Sunday mornings.
e.zh: 我喜欢周日早上在公园里画速写。

e.en: The architect is {sketching} ideas for the new library.
e.zh: 建筑师正在为新图书馆勾勒设计草图。

e.en: She opened her digital {sketchpad} and started doodling.
e.zh: 她打开数字画板,开始随手涂鸦。

e.en: The kid carries a small {sketchpad} in his backpack.
e.zh: 那孩子书包里总放着一个小画板。

sketchy.t:
adj. 粗略的；不详尽的
adj. 可疑的；靠不住的

e.en: That email looks {sketchy} — don't click the link.
e.zh: 那封邮件看起来很可疑,别点里面的链接。

e.en: My memory of last night is a bit {sketchy}.
e.zh: 我对昨晚的记忆有点模糊。

skew.t:
v. 使偏斜；扭曲
adj. 歪的；不对称的

e.en: Outliers can really {skew} the average score.
e.zh: 异常值会严重拉偏平均分。

e.en: The poll results {skew} younger than the general population.
e.zh: 民调结果偏向比总体人口更年轻的群体。

e.en: The data was {skewed} by a few extreme values.
e.zh: 数据被几个极端值严重拉偏了。

e.en: His view of the issue is heavily {skewed} by personal experience.
e.zh: 他对这件事的看法受个人经历严重影响。

skewer.t:
n. 烤肉签
v. 串起

e.en: Thread the chicken onto a {skewer} before grilling.
e.zh: 烤之前先把鸡肉串到扦子上。

e.en: The reviewer didn't hesitate to {skewer} the new film.
e.zh: 那位影评人毫不留情地痛批了这部新片。

e.en: She {skewered} the shrimp and brushed them with sauce.
e.zh: 她把虾穿成串,刷上了酱汁。

e.en: The columnist {skewered} the politician's empty promises.
e.zh: 专栏作家狠狠抨击了这位政客的空头支票。

e.en: Survey responses are {skewing} the results toward older users.
e.zh: 调查回复正使结果偏向年长用户。

e.en: Heavy advertising is {skewing} public perception of the product.
e.zh: 大量广告正在扭曲公众对该产品的看法。

e.en: The dataset shows clear positive {skewness} in income.
e.zh: 该数据集在收入分布上呈现明显的正偏态。

e.en: Analysts measured the {skewness} of the return distribution.
e.zh: 分析师测算了收益率分布的偏度。

e.en: Our user base {skews} heavily toward college students.
e.zh: 我们的用户群体明显偏向大学生。

e.en: Including weekends {skews} the daily traffic numbers.
e.zh: 算上周末会让每日流量数据失真。

ski.t:
v. 滑雪
n. 滑雪板

skid.t:
v. 打滑；侧滑
n. 打滑；垫木

e.en: The car began to {skid} on the icy road.
e.zh: 汽车在结冰的路面上开始打滑。

e.en: He left a long black {skid} mark on the pavement.
e.zh: 他在路面上留下了一道长长的刹车痕。

e.en: The truck went {skidding} across two lanes of traffic.
e.zh: 卡车横滑着冲过了两条车道。

e.en: My bike kept {skidding} on the wet leaves.
e.zh: 我的自行车在湿叶子上不停打滑。

e.en: We {skied} down the slope just before sunset.
e.zh: 我们赶在日落前从坡上滑了下来。

e.en: She has {skied} in the Alps every winter for a decade.
e.zh: 她十年来每个冬天都去阿尔卑斯山滑雪。

e.en: The {skier} carved a perfect arc down the mountain.
e.zh: 那位滑雪者沿着山坡划出了一道完美的弧线。

e.en: As a beginner {skier}, she stuck to the bunny slopes.
e.zh: 作为滑雪新手,她只在初级雪道上练习。

e.en: Clear blue {skies} stretched all the way to the horizon.
e.zh: 晴朗的蓝天一直延伸到地平线。

e.en: Stormy {skies} forced the airline to cancel the flight.
e.zh: 恶劣天气迫使航空公司取消了航班。

e.en: He rowed the small wooden {skiff} out to the buoy.
e.zh: 他划着那条小木舟出去到浮标处。

e.en: A fishing {skiff} bobbed gently near the dock.
e.zh: 一艘小渔船在码头边轻轻摇晃。

skiffle.t: n. 斯基福音乐（爵士民谣）

e.en: His grandfather played in a {skiffle} band in the fifties.
e.zh: 他爷爷五十年代在一个噼啪乐队里演奏过。

e.en: The pub hosts a {skiffle} night every Thursday.
e.zh: 那家酒吧每周四举办噼啪音乐之夜。

skiing.t:
n. 滑雪运动
v. 滑雪（现在分词）

e.en: We're going {skiing} in Hokkaido over New Year's.
e.zh: 新年我们要去北海道滑雪。

e.en: Cross-country {skiing} is great cardio in the winter.
e.zh: 越野滑雪是冬天很棒的有氧运动。

e.en: His weekend {skiings} in Vermont became a beloved ritual.
e.zh: 他在佛蒙特周末滑雪渐渐成了一个珍贵的习惯。

e.en: She compared the alpine and cross-country {skiings} she had tried.
e.zh: 她比较了自己尝试过的高山滑雪和越野滑雪。

skilful.t: adj. 熟练的；技巧娴熟的

e.en: She is a {skilful} negotiator who rarely loses a deal.
e.zh: 她是个谈判高手,很少谈崩生意。

e.en: His {skilful} handling of the crisis impressed everyone.
e.zh: 他对危机的娴熟处理给所有人留下了深刻印象。

e.en: The chef {skilfully} deboned the fish in seconds.
e.zh: 厨师几秒钟就熟练地把鱼骨剔了出来。

e.en: She {skilfully} steered the conversation away from politics.
e.zh: 她巧妙地把话题从政治上引开了。

e.en: Public speaking is a {skill} you can definitely learn.
e.zh: 演讲是一种完全可以学会的技能。

e.en: It takes real {skill} to debug code that's not yours.
e.zh: 调别人写的代码确实需要真本事。

e.en: We're hiring {skilled} engineers for the platform team.
e.zh: 我们正在为平台团队招聘有经验的工程师。

e.en: She is highly {skilled} at calming difficult customers.
e.zh: 她非常擅长安抚难缠的客户。

e.en: Heat the {skillet} until a drop of water sizzles.
e.zh: 把平底锅加热到滴水会嘶嘶响为止。

e.en: He cracked two eggs into the cast iron {skillet}.
e.zh: 他往铸铁平底锅里磕了两个鸡蛋。

skillful.t: adj. 熟练的；技艺高超的

e.en: She gave a {skillful} presentation that won over the board.
e.zh: 她做了一场出色的演示,赢得了董事会的支持。

e.en: The surgeon is known for her {skillful} hands.
e.zh: 那位外科医生以技艺娴熟的双手闻名。

e.en: He {skillfully} edited the footage into a polished short film.
e.zh: 他熟练地把素材剪成了一部精致的短片。

e.en: The host {skillfully} kept the conversation flowing all evening.
e.zh: 主持人整晚都巧妙地让对话保持流畅。

e.en: Coding {skills} are essential for tech industry careers today.
e.zh: 在当今科技行业，编程技能是必不可少的。

e.en: She {skills} the ball past the goalkeeper effortlessly.
e.zh: 她轻松地将球巧妙绕过守门员。

skim.t:
v. 浏览；略读
v. 撇去（浮沫）

e.en: I usually {skim} the news headlines during breakfast.
e.zh: 我通常在吃早餐时浏览新闻标题。

e.en: Please {skim} the foam off the soup before serving.
e.zh: 上汤前请把表面的浮沫撇掉。

skimmed.t:
adj. 脱脂的
v. 略读（过去式）

e.en: She {skimmed} the report quickly before the meeting.
e.zh: 开会前她快速浏览了一遍报告。

e.en: I prefer {skimmed} milk in my morning coffee.
e.zh: 早晨咖啡里我更喜欢加脱脂牛奶。

e.en: Use a {skimmer} to remove the fat from the broth.
e.zh: 用漏勺把汤里的油脂撇掉。

e.en: A card {skimmer} was found attached to the ATM.
e.zh: 取款机上发现了一个银行卡盗刷器。

skimming.t: v. 浏览；撇去（现在分词）

e.en: He's just {skimming} the article, not reading carefully.
e.zh: 他只是在略读文章，并没有细看。

e.en: The boat was {skimming} across the lake at sunset.
e.zh: 夕阳下小船轻快地掠过湖面。

e.en: Don't {skimp} on safety equipment for your team.
e.zh: 不要在团队的安全装备上省钱。

e.en: You shouldn't {skimp} on sleep before a big exam.
e.zh: 重要考试前可不能少睡觉。

skimpy.t: adj. 不足的；不够的；暴露的

e.en: The hotel served a rather {skimpy} breakfast buffet.
e.zh: 酒店的自助早餐相当寒酸简陋。

e.en: She wore a {skimpy} dress to the beach party.
e.zh: 她穿着一条暴露的短裙去海滩派对。

e.en: He {skims} every email before deciding to reply.
e.zh: 他每封邮件都先快速浏览再决定是否回复。

e.en: The hawk {skims} low over the open field.
e.zh: 那只鹰贴着开阔的田野低空掠过。

skin.t:
n. 皮肤；外皮
n. 皮肤（游戏外观）

e.en: Sunscreen helps protect your {skin} from harmful UV rays.
e.zh: 防晒霜能保护皮肤免受紫外线伤害。

e.en: The game lets players buy a new character {skin}.
e.zh: 游戏允许玩家购买新的角色皮肤。

e.en: Her {skincare} routine takes about twenty minutes each night.
e.zh: 她每晚的护肤流程大约要二十分钟。

e.en: Korean {skincare} products are popular around the world.
e.zh: 韩国护肤品在全球都很受欢迎。

e.en: My uncle is a {skinflint} who reuses tea bags.
e.zh: 我叔叔是个连茶包都重复用的吝啬鬼。

e.en: Don't be such a {skinflint} — leave a proper tip.
e.zh: 别这么小气——给点像样的小费吧。

skinful.t: n. 喝得酩酊大醉的量

e.en: He came home with a {skinful} of beer last night.
e.zh: 他昨晚喝得酩酊大醉才回家。

e.en: After a {skinful}, he could barely walk straight.
e.zh: 喝得烂醉之后，他几乎走不成直线。

skinhead.t: n. 光头党；剃光头的人

e.en: The documentary explored {skinhead} subculture in 1980s Britain.
e.zh: 这部纪录片探讨了八十年代英国的光头党亚文化。

e.en: He shaved his head and looked like a {skinhead}.
e.zh: 他剃了光头，看起来像个光头党。

e.en: A small {skink} darted across the warm patio stones.
e.zh: 一只小石龙子飞快地窜过温热的露台石板。

e.en: The blue-tongued {skink} is a popular pet lizard.
e.zh: 蓝舌石龙子是很受欢迎的宠物蜥蜴。

e.en: Use {skinless} chicken breast for a healthier salad.
e.zh: 用去皮鸡胸肉做沙拉更健康。

e.en: The recipe calls for {skinless} salmon fillets.
e.zh: 这道食谱需要去皮的三文鱼柳。

skinned.t:
adj. 去皮的
v. 剥皮（skin 的过去式）

e.en: She {skinned} her knee falling off the bike.
e.zh: 她从自行车上摔下来，把膝盖擦破了。

e.en: The chef carefully {skinned} the fish before grilling.
e.zh: 厨师在烤鱼前仔细去掉了鱼皮。

e.en: The {skinner} prepared the hides for the leather workshop.
e.zh: 剥皮工人为皮革作坊处理好了兽皮。

e.en: Professor {Skinner} pioneered behaviorist psychology in the twentieth century.
e.zh: 斯金纳教授在二十世纪开创了行为主义心理学。

e.en: The hunter spent the afternoon {skinning} the deer carefully.
e.zh: 猎人花了一下午仔细给鹿剥皮。

e.en: Mod developers enjoy {skinning} the game with custom art.
e.zh: 模组开发者喜欢用自制美术给游戏换皮。

skinny.t:
adj. 瘦削的；紧身的
n. 内幕消息

e.en: He's too {skinny} and needs to eat more protein.
e.zh: 他太瘦了，需要多吃点蛋白质。

e.en: She prefers {skinny} jeans over loose-fitting trousers.
e.zh: 比起宽松裤，她更喜欢紧身牛仔裤。

skins.t: n. 皮肤；外皮；皮肤（游戏中的角色外观）

e.en: Players can unlock new character {skins} by completing missions.
e.zh: 玩家完成任务可以解锁新的角色皮肤。

e.en: Banana {skins} should go into the compost bin.
e.zh: 香蕉皮应该扔到堆肥桶里。

skint.t: adj. 身无分文的（英式口语）

e.en: I'm completely {skint} until payday next week.
e.zh: 在下周发工资之前，我完全身无分文。

e.en: We're a bit {skint} this month, so no dinners out.
e.zh: 这个月我们有点拮据，不出去吃饭了。

e.en: She wore a {skintight} dress to the awards ceremony.
e.zh: 她穿着一条紧身连衣裙出席了颁奖典礼。

e.en: Cyclists often wear {skintight} suits to reduce drag.
e.zh: 自行车手常穿紧身骑行服来减少阻力。

skip.t:
v. 跳过；略过
n. 跳跃

e.en: You can {skip} the intro by pressing the spacebar.
e.zh: 按空格键就可以跳过片头。

e.en: Never {skip} breakfast if you have a busy morning.
e.zh: 如果早上很忙，千万别不吃早餐。

e.en: Most canned tuna is actually {skipjack}, not bluefin.
e.zh: 大多数罐头金枪鱼其实是鲣鱼，不是蓝鳍。

e.en: The fishermen hauled in a huge catch of {skipjack}.
e.zh: 渔民们捕获了一大批鲣鱼。

skipped.t: v. 跳过；略过（skip 的过去式）

e.en: I {skipped} lunch because the meeting ran long.
e.zh: 会议拖得太久，我午饭都没吃。

e.en: The little girl {skipped} happily down the garden path.
e.zh: 小女孩沿着花园小径欢快地蹦跳着。

e.en: The {skipper} steered the yacht safely back to harbor.
e.zh: 船长稳稳地把游艇驶回了港口。

e.en: Our team {skipper} gave a motivating pre-match speech.
e.zh: 我们队长在赛前做了激励士气的讲话。

skipping.t:
n. 跳绳
v. 跳过；略过

e.en: Children were {skipping} rope in the school playground.
e.zh: 孩子们在学校操场上跳绳。

e.en: He's been {skipping} class to play video games.
e.zh: 他一直在逃课打电子游戏。

skips.t: v. 跳过；略过（skip 的三单）

e.en: She always {skips} the boring parts of movies.
e.zh: 她总是跳过电影里无聊的部分。

e.en: My old laptop {skips} frames during video calls.
e.zh: 我的旧笔记本在视频通话时会卡帧。

skipton.t: n. 斯基普顿（英国地名）

e.en: {Skipton} is a charming market town in Yorkshire.
e.zh: 斯基普顿是约克郡一座迷人的集镇。

e.en: We visited the medieval castle in {Skipton} last summer.
e.zh: 去年夏天我们参观了斯基普顿的中世纪城堡。

skirl.t:
n. 风笛尖锐声
v. 发出尖锐声

e.en: The {skirl} of bagpipes echoed through the highland valley.
e.zh: 风笛的尖鸣回荡在高地山谷间。

e.en: You could hear the {skirl} of pipes from miles away.
e.zh: 几英里外都能听到风笛的尖锐声。

skirmish.t:
n. 小规模冲突；小争论
v. 发生小冲突

e.en: A brief {skirmish} broke out between the two patrols.
e.zh: 两支巡逻队之间爆发了一场短暂的小规模冲突。

e.en: The candidates had a verbal {skirmish} during the debate.
e.zh: 两位候选人在辩论中发生了一场口角交锋。

skirmisher.t: n. 散兵；小规模冲突者

e.en: A lone {skirmisher} signaled the enemy's position to headquarters.
e.zh: 一名散兵向总部报告了敌军的位置。

e.en: Each {skirmisher} carried light gear for quick movement.
e.zh: 每名散兵都只带轻装以便快速行动。

skirmishing.t:
n. 小规模交战
v. 小规模冲突

e.en: The two armies were {skirmishing} along the river border.
e.zh: 两军在河岸边境一带小规模交火。

e.en: Lawyers spent weeks {skirmishing} over procedural details.
e.zh: 律师们花了数周时间在程序细节上交锋。

skirt.t:
n. 裙子
v. 绕过；回避

e.en: She bought a long denim {skirt} for the summer.
e.zh: 她买了条夏天穿的长款牛仔裙。

e.en: The hiking trail {skirts} the edge of the lake.
e.zh: 这条徒步小径沿着湖边蜿蜒前行。

skirted.t:
adj. 穿裙子的
v. 绕过（skirt 的过去式）

e.en: The driver carefully {skirted} the pothole in the road.
e.zh: 司机小心翼翼地绕开了路上的坑洼。

e.en: The politician {skirted} the question about tax increases.
e.zh: 那位政客回避了关于加税的问题。

skirting.t:
n. 踢脚板；裙料
v. 绕过

e.en: The path runs {skirting} along the cliff's edge.
e.zh: 这条路沿着悬崖边缘蜿蜒而过。

e.en: We need to repaint the {skirting} board in the hallway.
e.zh: 我们需要重新粉刷走廊的踢脚线。

e.en: Long {skirts} are trending again this fall season.
e.zh: 今年秋季长裙又开始流行起来了。

e.en: The new highway {skirts} the southern edge of town.
e.zh: 新建的高速公路绕过城镇南缘。

e.en: She rented a pair of {skis} for the weekend trip.
e.zh: 她为周末旅行租了一副滑雪板。

e.en: The expert {skis} down the steepest slope effortlessly.
e.zh: 那位高手轻松地从最陡的雪坡上滑下。

skit.t: n. 幽默短剧；讽刺小品

e.en: The students performed a hilarious {skit} at the talent show.
e.zh: 学生们在才艺表演中演了一段超搞笑的小品。

e.en: He wrote a comedy {skit} mocking office meetings.
e.zh: 他写了一个讽刺办公室会议的喜剧短剧。

skitter.t: v. 急速掠过；轻掠水面

e.en: Mice {skitter} across the kitchen floor at night.
e.zh: 老鼠夜里在厨房地板上窸窣乱窜。

e.en: Dry leaves {skitter} along the pavement in the wind.
e.zh: 枯叶在风中沿着人行道沙沙滚动。

e.en: The horse became {skittish} during the loud thunderstorm.
e.zh: 那匹马在雷雨大作时变得惊慌不安。

e.en: Investors are {skittish} about the volatile stock market.
e.zh: 投资者对动荡的股市感到惴惴不安。

e.en: The deer glanced {skittishly} before darting into the woods.
e.zh: 那只鹿惊恐地看了一眼便窜进了树林。

e.en: She laughed {skittishly} when he asked her out.
e.zh: 他约她出去时，她紧张地笑了起来。

e.en: The cat's {skittishness} faded after a few weeks.
e.zh: 几周后，那只猫的惊慌劲儿才慢慢消退。

e.en: Market {skittishness} grew amid the trade war rumors.
e.zh: 在贸易战传闻中，市场的不安情绪日益加剧。

skittle.t: n. 九柱戏（类似保龄球）

e.en: He knocked down the last {skittle} with a perfect throw.
e.zh: 他完美一掷击倒了最后一根木瓶。

e.en: The kids set up a {skittle} game in the backyard.
e.zh: 孩子们在后院摆起了一组九柱戏。

skive.t: v. 逃避工作；偷懒（英式口语）

e.en: He likes to {skive} off work on sunny Friday afternoons.
e.zh: 晴朗的周五下午他总爱翘班。

e.en: Don't {skive} class just to play video games.
e.zh: 别为了打游戏就翘课。

skivvy.t:
n. 打杂女仆
v. 干杂活

e.en: I'm not your personal {skivvy}—clean up your own mess.
e.zh: 我不是你的私人佣人,自己的烂摊子自己收拾。

e.en: He felt like a {skivvy} doing all the office chores.
e.zh: 他觉得自己像个杂役,包办了所有办公室杂务。

e.en: The shop sells high-end {skiwear} from European brands.
e.zh: 这家店出售欧洲品牌的高端滑雪服。

e.en: Good {skiwear} keeps you warm and dry on the slopes.
e.zh: 好的滑雪服能让你在雪坡上保持温暖干爽。

e.en: He drives a red {Skoda} hatchback to work every day.
e.zh: 他每天开一辆红色斯柯达两厢车上班。

e.en: {Skoda} has become one of Volkswagen's most successful brands.
e.zh: 斯柯达已成为大众汽车旗下最成功的品牌之一。

e.en: They raised their glasses and shouted {skol} together.
e.zh: 他们举起酒杯一起喊干杯。

e.en: In Sweden, you say {skol} before drinking with friends.
e.zh: 在瑞典,和朋友喝酒前要说一声“干杯”。

e.en: A {skua} swooped down and stole the penguin's egg.
e.zh: 一只贼鸥俯冲下来偷走了企鹅的蛋。

e.en: The {skua} is known for aggressively chasing other seabirds.
e.zh: 贼鸥以凶猛追击其他海鸟而闻名。

skulduggery.t: n. 欺诈行为；不法勾当

e.en: The election was marred by political {skulduggery} and bribery.
e.zh: 这次选举被政治阴谋和贿赂玷污了。

e.en: Detectives uncovered the {skulduggery} behind the bank's collapse.
e.zh: 侦探揭开了银行倒闭背后的勾当。

skulk.t: v. 潜伏；鬼鬼祟祟行动

e.en: Stray cats {skulk} in the alley after dark.
e.zh: 流浪猫天黑后在巷子里偷偷出没。

e.en: Don't {skulk} around the office; just ask for help.
e.zh: 别在办公室里鬼鬼祟祟,直接求助就行。

e.en: The museum displayed a dinosaur {skull} behind glass.
e.zh: 博物馆在玻璃后面展出一具恐龙头骨。

e.en: He fractured his {skull} in the cycling accident.
e.zh: 他在那次自行车事故中颅骨骨折。

e.en: The rabbi wore a black silk {skullcap} during prayers.
e.zh: 拉比祈祷时戴着一顶黑色丝质小圆帽。

e.en: She knitted a warm {skullcap} for winter mornings.
e.zh: 她织了一顶暖和的小帽用于冬天的早晨。

e.en: Corporate {skullduggery} cost shareholders millions of dollars.
e.zh: 公司的暗箱操作让股东损失了数百万美元。

e.en: The novel is full of pirates and high-seas {skullduggery}.
e.zh: 这部小说充满了海盗和海上的尔虞我诈。

e.en: Ancient {skulls} were unearthed at the archaeological site.
e.zh: 在考古遗址出土了一些古代头骨。

e.en: His jacket is covered in embroidered {skulls} and roses.
e.zh: 他的夹克上绣满了骷髅和玫瑰图案。

skunk.t:
n. 臭鼬
v. 惨败对手

e.en: A {skunk} sprayed our dog in the backyard last night.
e.zh: 昨晚一只臭鼬在后院喷了我家的狗。

e.en: The underdog team {skunked} the champions in the final.
e.zh: 决赛中那支弱旅把冠军队打得一分未得。

skybox.t: n. 天空盒（游戏场景背景）；包厢

e.en: We watched the game from a luxury {skybox} above the field.
e.zh: 我们从球场上方的豪华包厢观看了比赛。

e.en: Corporate clients booked the {skybox} for the championship.
e.zh: 企业客户预订了那间包厢观看冠军赛。

e.en: The {skycap} loaded our suitcases onto a cart at the curb.
e.zh: 机场行李员在路边把我们的箱子装上推车。

e.en: Tip the {skycap} a few dollars for handling heavy bags.
e.zh: 给机场搬运员几美元小费以感谢搬重行李。

skydive.t:
v. 跳伞；高空跳伞
n. 跳伞运动

e.en: She wants to {skydive} from a plane on her birthday.
e.zh: 她想在生日那天从飞机上跳伞。

e.en: You can {skydive} tandem with an instructor your first time.
e.zh: 第一次跳伞可以和教练一起双人跳。

e.en: The {skydiver} opened her parachute at three thousand feet.
e.zh: 那位跳伞员在三千英尺高度打开了降落伞。

e.en: An experienced {skydiver} jumps hundreds of times each year.
e.zh: 一位经验丰富的跳伞员每年跳数百次。

e.en: {Skydiving} was the most thrilling experience of my life.
e.zh: 跳伞是我一生中最刺激的经历。

e.en: He went {skydiving} in New Zealand last summer.
e.zh: 去年夏天他在新西兰玩了跳伞。

e.en: We hiked across the misty Isle of {Skye} last autumn.
e.zh: 去年秋天我们徒步穿越了雾蒙蒙的斯凯岛。

e.en: The Isle of {Skye} is famous for its dramatic landscapes.
e.zh: 斯凯岛以壮丽的风景而闻名。

skyhook.t: n. 空中吊钩；高空气球

e.en: Kareem's signature {skyhook} was almost impossible to block.
e.zh: 贾巴尔的招牌天勾几乎无法被盖帽。

e.en: The crane lowered cargo onto the platform using a {skyhook}.
e.zh: 起重机用空中吊钩把货物降到平台上。

skylark.t:
n. 云雀
v. 嬉戏打闹

e.en: A {skylark} sang high above the wheat field at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时分一只云雀在麦田上空高声歌唱。

e.en: The boys would {skylark} for hours after school.
e.zh: 那些男孩放学后会嬉闹好几个小时。

skylarks.t:
n. 云雀（复数）
v. 嬉戏打闹

e.en: {Skylarks} hover and sing during their courtship flights.
e.zh: 云雀在求偶飞行时悬停并鸣唱。

e.en: She watched the {skylarks} rise above the meadow.
e.zh: 她看着云雀飞越草地上空。

e.en: Sunlight streamed through the kitchen {skylight} all afternoon.
e.zh: 整个下午阳光从厨房的天窗倾泻而下。

e.en: They installed a {skylight} to brighten the dim hallway.
e.zh: 他们安装了一扇天窗来照亮昏暗的走廊。

e.en: The Manhattan {skyline} glowed orange at sunset.
e.zh: 曼哈顿的天际线在日落时泛着橙色光芒。

e.en: New towers are reshaping the city's {skyline} every year.
e.zh: 新建的高楼每年都在改变城市的天际线。

e.en: We ate brunch in a sunny, {skylit} atrium.
e.zh: 我们在阳光透过天窗洒落的中庭吃了早午餐。

e.en: Her {skylit} studio is perfect for painting on cloudy days.
e.zh: 她那间带天窗的工作室在阴天画画再合适不过。

skyrocket.t:
v. (价格等) 暴涨
n. 冲天烟火

e.en: Housing prices {skyrocket} whenever interest rates drop.
e.zh: 利率一下降房价就会飙升。

e.en: A viral video can make follower counts {skyrocket} overnight.
e.zh: 一段爆红视频可以让粉丝数一夜暴涨。

skyrocketing.t:
adj. 飞涨的
v. 暴涨（进行时）

e.en: {Skyrocketing} rents are pushing families out of the city.
e.zh: 飙升的租金正把许多家庭挤出城市。

e.en: Demand for AI engineers is {skyrocketing} this year.
e.zh: 今年对人工智能工程师的需求正在飞速增长。

e.en: The painter captured a stunning {skyscape} at twilight.
e.zh: 画家捕捉到了暮光中令人惊叹的天空景象。

e.en: Drone photos reveal a vast desert {skyscape} above the dunes.
e.zh: 无人机照片展现了沙丘上空辽阔的天空景观。

e.en: The new {skyscraper} dominates the downtown skyline.
e.zh: 那栋新摩天大楼主宰着市中心的天际线。

e.en: From the {skyscraper}'s top floor, cars looked like ants.
e.zh: 从摩天大楼的顶层看下去,汽车小得像蚂蚁。

e.en: Shanghai's {skyscrapers} light up brilliantly every evening.
e.zh: 上海的摩天大楼每晚都灯火辉煌。

e.en: Glass {skyscrapers} reflected the morning sun blindingly.
e.zh: 玻璃幕墙摩天楼把晨光反射得令人睁不开眼。

e.en: A glass {skywalk} connects the two shopping malls downtown.
e.zh: 一条玻璃天桥连接着市中心的两座购物中心。

e.en: Tourists nervously crossed the canyon {skywalk}.
e.zh: 游客们紧张地走过那条峡谷天桥。

skyward.t:
adv. 向天空
adj. 朝天的

e.en: The rocket roared {skyward} in a column of flame.
e.zh: 火箭在一柱火焰中咆哮着冲向天空。

e.en: She gazed {skyward}, watching the kite dance.
e.zh: 她仰望天空,看着风筝翩翩起舞。

e.en: The balloon drifted gently {skywards} over the meadow.
e.zh: 气球轻柔地飘向草地上空。

e.en: Stock prices climbed {skywards} after the earnings report.
e.zh: 财报发布后股价一路向上攀升。

e.en: The enclosed {skyway} keeps commuters warm in winter.
e.zh: 封闭式空中走廊让通勤者在冬天也很暖和。

e.en: Minneapolis is famous for its downtown {skyway} system.
e.zh: 明尼阿波利斯以其市中心的空中走廊系统闻名。

e.en: He carried a heavy {slab} of concrete across the yard.
e.zh: 他把一块沉重的水泥板搬过院子。

e.en: She bought a thick {slab} of dark chocolate from the bakery.
e.zh: 她从面包店买了一大块厚厚的黑巧克力。

e.en: Workers laid stone {slabs} along the garden path.
e.zh: 工人沿着花园小径铺设石板。

e.en: The butcher cut huge {slabs} of beef for the barbecue.
e.zh: 肉店老板切了几大块牛肉用于烧烤。

slack.t:
adj. 松的；懈怠的
n. 淡季；余量

e.en: Pull the rope tight; there's too much {slack}.
e.zh: 把绳子拉紧,松得太多了。

e.en: Business has been {slack} since the holidays ended.
e.zh: 假期结束后生意一直很清淡。

e.en: He {slacked} off during the final week of the project.
e.zh: 在项目的最后一周他偷懒了。

e.en: The wind {slacked} as the storm finally moved offshore.
e.zh: 风暴最终移向海上,风也变小了。

e.en: Demand will likely {slacken} after the holiday rush.
e.zh: 假日抢购过后需求很可能减弱。

e.en: {Slacken} the reins so the horse can lower its head.
e.zh: 放松缰绳让马把头低下来。

e.en: The pace of construction {slackened} as winter approached.
e.zh: 随着冬天临近,施工的节奏放缓了。

e.en: She {slackened} her grip on the steering wheel.
e.zh: 她松开了握着方向盘的手。

slackening.t:
v. 放松；减缓（进行时）
n. 松弛

e.en: Economists worry about {slackening} consumer spending.
e.zh: 经济学家对消费者支出放缓感到担忧。

e.en: The runner felt his energy {slackening} near the finish.
e.zh: 跑步者在接近终点时感到体力在下降。

e.en: His teammates accused him of being a total {slacker}.
e.zh: 他的队友指责他是个十足的懒鬼。

e.en: Don't be such a {slacker}; finish your homework first.
e.zh: 别这么懒散,先把作业做完。

e.en: The manager warned employees about {slacking} on deadlines.
e.zh: 经理警告员工不要在截止日期前偷懒。

e.en: You've been {slacking} at the gym for weeks now.
e.zh: 你已经好几周没好好去健身了。

e.en: The flag hung {slackly} from the pole on a windless day.
e.zh: 在无风的日子里,旗帜松松地垂在旗杆上。

e.en: He held the leash {slackly} as the dog wandered ahead.
e.zh: 狗在前面闲逛,他松松地牵着狗绳。

e.en: The auditor criticized the {slackness} of internal controls.
e.zh: 审计员批评了内部控制的松懈。

e.en: There was visible {slackness} in the suspension cable.
e.zh: 悬索上明显有松弛的部分。

e.en: He wore gray wool {slacks} and a navy blazer to the interview.
e.zh: 他穿着灰色羊毛西裤和藏青西装外套去面试。

e.en: These linen {slacks} are perfect for hot summer days.
e.zh: 这条亚麻长裤非常适合炎热的夏日。

slag.t:
n. 炉渣；矿渣
v. 猛烈批评

e.en: The steel mill dumped piles of {slag} near the river.
e.zh: 钢厂把成堆的炉渣倾倒在河边。

e.en: British teens often {slag} each other off as a joke.
e.zh: 英国青少年常开玩笑地互相挖苦。

slain.t: v. 杀死（slay 的过去分词）

e.en: A monument honors the soldiers {slain} in the battle.
e.zh: 一座纪念碑缅怀在战役中阵亡的士兵。

e.en: Police are still searching for the {slain} man's killer.
e.zh: 警方仍在搜寻杀害遇害者的凶手。

e.en: A cold lemonade can {slake} your thirst on a hot day.
e.zh: 一杯冰柠檬水能在炎热的日子里解渴。

e.en: Nothing could {slake} her curiosity about the old letters.
e.zh: 什么也无法满足她对那些旧信件的好奇心。

e.en: She won gold in the women's giant {slalom} yesterday.
e.zh: 她昨天在女子大回转项目中夺得金牌。

e.en: The skier had to {slalom} between tightly spaced gates.
e.zh: 滑雪者必须在密集的旗门之间回转滑行。

slam.t:
v. 猛关；猛击
n. 砰的一声

e.en: Please don't {slam} the door when you leave.
e.zh: 你出去时请不要把门摔上。

e.en: Critics {slam} the new movie as boring and overlong.
e.zh: 评论家抨击这部新电影沉闷又冗长。

e.en: She {slammed} her laptop shut and stormed out of the room.
e.zh: 她啪地合上笔记本电脑,怒气冲冲地走出房间。

e.en: Reviewers {slammed} the restaurant for poor hygiene.
e.zh: 评论员们因卫生差猛烈抨击了那家餐厅。

e.en: He spent five years in the {slammer} for armed robbery.
e.zh: 他因持械抢劫在监狱里待了五年。

e.en: One more offense and you'll end up in the {slammer}.
e.zh: 再犯一次你就要进监狱了。

e.en: Stop {slamming} the cabinet doors when you're upset.
e.zh: 心情不好时别再砰砰地摔橱柜门了。

e.en: Pundits are {slamming} the proposal as unrealistic.
e.zh: 评论员们正抨击该提案不切实际。

slams.t:
v. 猛摔（第三人称单数）
n. 砰声

e.en: He {slams} his fist on the desk whenever he's frustrated.
e.zh: 他一受挫就用拳头砸桌子。

e.en: The senator {slams} the bill in a fiery speech.
e.zh: 那位参议员在激烈的演讲中猛烈抨击这项法案。

slander.t:
n. 诽谤
v. 诋毁

e.en: She sued the tabloid for {slander} after the false report.
e.zh: 那篇虚假报道之后,她以诽谤罪起诉了那家小报。

e.en: Don't {slander} a coworker just because you disagree.
e.zh: 不要因为意见不合就诋毁同事。

e.en: The tabloid printed {slanderous} claims about the singer's private life.
e.zh: 这家小报刊登了关于这位歌手私生活的诽谤性言论。

e.en: He sued the blogger for posting {slanderous} comments online.
e.zh: 他起诉那位博主在网上发布诽谤性评论。

e.en: Teenagers often use {slang} that adults struggle to understand.
e.zh: 青少年经常使用大人难以理解的俚语。

e.en: The dictionary added several new internet {slang} terms this year.
e.zh: 今年这本词典新增了几个网络俚语词条。

e.en: The two politicians ended up {slanging} each other on live TV.
e.zh: 两位政客最后在直播中互相辱骂起来。

e.en: Fans started {slanging} the referee after the controversial call.
e.zh: 那次有争议的判罚后,球迷开始大骂裁判。

e.en: Every generation invents its own {slangs} to feel unique.
e.zh: 每一代人都会创造自己的俚语来彰显独特。

e.en: The textbook lists common {slangs} used in American sitcoms.
e.zh: 这本教材列出了美国情景喜剧中常用的俚语。

e.en: His writing style is too {slangy} for a formal report.
e.zh: 他的文风太过口语化,不适合正式报告。

e.en: She gave a {slangy} reply that made everyone laugh.
e.zh: 她用一句俚语味十足的回答把大家逗笑了。

slant.t:
n. 倾斜；观点
v. 使倾斜

e.en: The article had a clear political {slant}.
e.zh: 这篇文章有明显的政治倾向。

e.en: Rain began to {slant} sideways in the strong wind.
e.zh: 雨在强风中开始斜着下。

e.en: Critics said the news coverage was heavily {slanted}.
e.zh: 批评人士认为这则新闻报道带有严重偏见。

e.en: Sunlight streamed through the {slanted} attic window.
e.zh: 阳光透过倾斜的阁楼窗户洒进来。

slanting.t:
adj. 倾斜的
v. 倾斜（进行时）

e.en: A {slanting} ray of light fell across the wooden floor.
e.zh: 一缕斜光洒在木地板上。

e.en: She wrote her notes in neat {slanting} handwriting.
e.zh: 她用工整的斜体字记笔记。

slantwise.t:
adv. 倾斜地
adj. 倾斜的

e.en: He glanced at her {slantwise}, trying not to be obvious.
e.zh: 他斜眼看了她一下,尽量不显山露水。

e.en: The shelves were mounted {slantwise} to display the books better.
e.zh: 书架被斜着安装,以便更好地展示书籍。

slap.t:
v. 掌掴；拍打
n. 耳光

e.en: She gave him a hard {slap} on the cheek.
e.zh: 她重重地扇了他一耳光。

e.en: The new tax feels like a {slap} in the face.
e.zh: 这项新税就像狠狠打了一记耳光。

slapdash.t:
adj. 草率的；马虎的
adv. 仓促地

e.en: His {slapdash} approach to homework worried his teacher.
e.zh: 他做作业马虎潦草,让老师很担心。

e.en: The repair was so {slapdash} that the leak returned within days.
e.zh: 这次维修太草率,几天后又开始漏水了。

slapped.t: v. slap 的过去式，掴、拍打

e.en: The company {slapped} a hefty fine on the violator.
e.zh: 公司对违规者处以重罚。

e.en: She {slapped} sunscreen on her face before heading to the beach.
e.zh: 去海滩前她往脸上抹了防晒霜。

slapping.t: v. slap 的现在分词，掴、拍打

e.en: Waves were {slapping} loudly against the side of the boat.
e.zh: 海浪啪啪地拍打着船身。

e.en: Stop {slapping} stickers all over your laptop.
e.zh: 别再把贴纸到处贴在你的笔记本电脑上了。

slaps.t:
v. slap 的第三人称单数
n. 耳光（复数）

e.en: This new song absolutely {slaps} on a good speaker.
e.zh: 这首新歌用好音箱听简直炸裂。

e.en: The comedian's punchline always lands like a series of {slaps}.
e.zh: 这位喜剧演员的笑点总是像一连串巴掌一样命中。

slapstick.t: n. 打闹喜剧；滑稽闹剧

e.en: Old silent films relied heavily on {slapstick} comedy.
e.zh: 老默片很大程度上依赖于闹剧式的肢体喜剧。

e.en: The kids burst out laughing at the {slapstick} chase scene.
e.zh: 孩子们看到那场闹剧式追逐戏笑得前仰后合。

slash.t:
n. 斜杠（/）
v. 砍；大幅削减

e.en: The store decided to {slash} prices before the holiday.
e.zh: 这家商店决定在节日前大幅降价。

e.en: Type a forward {slash} to separate the folder names.
e.zh: 输入一个正斜杠来分隔文件夹名。

slashed.t: v. slash 的过去式，砍、大幅削减

e.en: The company {slashed} its workforce by twenty percent.
e.zh: 公司将员工人数削减了百分之二十。

e.en: Vandals had {slashed} the tires of every car on the street.
e.zh: 破坏者把街上每辆车的轮胎都划破了。

slasher.t: n. 砍杀类恐怖片；砍人者

e.en: She refuses to watch any {slasher} film alone at night.
e.zh: 她绝不肯在夜里独自看血腥恐怖片。

e.en: The eighties produced countless classic {slasher} movies.
e.zh: 八十年代诞生了无数经典的砍杀片。

slashes.t:
n. 斜杠（复数）
v. 砍、削减（第三人称单数）

e.en: The URL contains two forward {slashes} after the protocol.
e.zh: 网址里协议后面有两个正斜杠。

e.en: He {slashes} through tall grass with his machete.
e.zh: 他用砍刀劈开高高的杂草。

slashing.t:
v. slash 的现在分词
adj. 猛烈的

e.en: The startup is {slashing} its cloud costs by switching providers.
e.zh: 这家创业公司通过更换云服务商来大幅削减成本。

e.en: Cold rain came {slashing} down on the campers' tent.
e.zh: 冰冷的雨倾盆砸在露营者的帐篷上。

e.en: One {slat} on the wooden blind had cracked.
e.zh: 木百叶窗上有一根板条裂了。

e.en: He replaced the broken {slat} in the bed frame.
e.zh: 他换掉了床架上断裂的那根板条。

slate.t:
n. 石板；候选名单
v. 安排；抨击

e.en: The studio announced an exciting {slate} of films for next year.
e.zh: 电影公司公布了明年一份激动人心的影片片单。

e.en: The roof is covered with traditional gray {slate} tiles.
e.zh: 屋顶铺着传统的灰色石板瓦。

slated.t:
adj. 预定的；计划中的
v. slate 的过去式

e.en: The new feature is {slated} for release next month.
e.zh: 新功能预计将于下个月发布。

e.en: She is {slated} to give the keynote at the conference.
e.zh: 她预定将在大会上发表主题演讲。

slater.t: n. 盖石板屋顶的工人

e.en: The {slater} climbed the ladder to fix the leaking roof.
e.zh: 瓦工爬上梯子去修补漏水的屋顶。

e.en: My grandfather worked as a {slater} for forty years.
e.zh: 我祖父做了四十年的石板瓦工。

e.en: Don't forget to {slather} sunscreen on your shoulders.
e.zh: 别忘了在肩膀上厚厚地抹一层防晒霜。

e.en: She likes to {slather} butter on warm bread.
e.zh: 她喜欢在热面包上厚厚地涂黄油。

slatted.t: adj. 板条制的；带板条的

e.en: Sunlight filtered through the {slatted} wooden shutters.
e.zh: 阳光透过百叶式的木百叶窗洒进来。

e.en: The garden bench had a {slatted} seat for drainage.
e.zh: 花园长凳的座面是板条式的,便于排水。

e.en: In the old novel, the landlady was described as a {slattern}.
e.zh: 在那部老小说里,女房东被描写成一个邋遢的女人。

e.en: He found the word {slattern} oddly old-fashioned and harsh.
e.zh: 他觉得 slattern 这个词既过时又刺耳。

slaty.t: adj. 石板色的；似石板的

e.en: The lake reflected a cold, {slaty} sky.
e.zh: 湖面映出一片冷冷的石板灰色天空。

e.en: Her eyes were a striking {slaty} blue.
e.zh: 她的眼睛是一种引人注目的青灰色。

slaughter.t:
v. 屠杀；宰杀
n. 大屠杀

e.en: The home team won by such a margin it was a {slaughter}.
e.zh: 主队赢得分差悬殊,简直是屠杀式的胜利。

e.en: New laws aim to prevent the {slaughter} of endangered animals.
e.zh: 新法律旨在阻止对濒危动物的屠杀。

slaughtered.t: v. slaughter 的过去式，屠杀、宰杀

e.en: Our team got absolutely {slaughtered} in the finals.
e.zh: 我们队在决赛中被打得落花流水。

e.en: Thousands of cattle were {slaughtered} during the disease outbreak.
e.zh: 疫情爆发期间,数千头牛被宰杀。

e.en: The {slaughterer} followed strict humane procedures at the plant.
e.zh: 屠宰工在工厂里严格遵循人道屠宰程序。

e.en: Becoming a skilled {slaughterer} requires years of training.
e.zh: 成为一名熟练的屠宰工需要多年的训练。

e.en: Activists protested outside the {slaughterhouse} for weeks.
e.zh: 活动人士在屠宰场外抗议了数周。

e.en: Strict hygiene rules apply inside every modern {slaughterhouse}.
e.zh: 每一家现代屠宰场内都执行严格的卫生规定。

slaughtering.t: v. slaughter 的现在分词，屠杀、宰杀

e.en: The startup is {slaughtering} its competitors in user growth.
e.zh: 这家创业公司在用户增长上把对手碾压得粉碎。

e.en: New regulations control the {slaughtering} of livestock.
e.zh: 新规对牲畜屠宰过程进行了规范。

slaughters.t: v. slaughter 的第三人称单数

e.en: That goalkeeper consistently {slaughters} opposing strikers' confidence.
e.zh: 那位门将总能彻底击垮对方前锋的信心。

e.en: The company {slaughters} its smaller rivals every quarter.
e.zh: 这家公司每个季度都把规模较小的对手打得溃不成军。

e.en: Her grandmother is a proud {Slav} from a small village.
e.zh: 她祖母是一位来自小村庄的、引以为豪的斯拉夫人。

e.en: The festival celebrated music from various {Slav} traditions.
e.zh: 这个节日展示了多种斯拉夫民族传统的音乐。

slave.t:
n. 奴隶
v. 苦干；(设备) 作从属端

e.en: He refuses to be a {slave} to his phone notifications.
e.zh: 他拒绝做手机通知的奴隶。

e.en: The museum documents the lives of those forced into {slave} labor.
e.zh: 这家博物馆记录了被迫从事奴隶劳动者的生活。

e.en: The historian uncovered letters written by a wealthy {slaveholder}.
e.zh: 这位历史学家发现了一位富有奴隶主写的信件。

e.en: Many founding fathers were also {slaveholder} themselves.
e.zh: 许多开国元勋本身也是奴隶主。

slaver.t:
v. 流口水
n. 贩奴者

e.en: The hungry dog began to {slaver} as dinner was served.
e.zh: 开饭时,饥饿的狗开始流口水。

e.en: Investors {slaver} over any startup mentioning artificial intelligence.
e.zh: 投资者一听到提及人工智能的创业公司就垂涎三尺。

slaveries.t: n. slavery 的复数，奴役、奴隶制

e.en: Modern {slaveries} take many disguised forms around the world.
e.zh: 现代奴役在世界各地以多种隐蔽形式存在。

e.en: The book compares ancient and contemporary {slaveries}.
e.zh: 这本书对比了古代和当代的各种奴役制度。

slavering.t: v. slaver 的现在分词，流口水

e.en: A pack of {slavering} dogs guarded the abandoned warehouse.
e.zh: 一群口水直流的恶犬看守着那座废弃仓库。

e.en: Reporters stood {slavering} for any quote from the celebrity.
e.zh: 记者们急切地等着名人吐出任何一句话。

e.en: The country abolished {slavery} in the nineteenth century.
e.zh: 这个国家在十九世纪废除了奴隶制。

e.en: Working three jobs feels like wage {slavery} to him.
e.zh: 对他来说,身兼三份工作就像工资奴役。

slaves.t:
n. 奴隶（复数）
v. slave 的第三人称单数

e.en: Many people are {slaves} to social media validation.
e.zh: 许多人都是社交媒体认可感的奴隶。

e.en: The ancient empire depended on the labor of {slaves}.
e.zh: 这个古代帝国依赖奴隶的劳动维持运转。

slavic.t:
adj. 斯拉夫的
n. 斯拉夫语

e.en: She studies {Slavic} languages at university.
e.zh: 她在大学里学习斯拉夫语言。

e.en: The choir performed traditional {Slavic} folk songs.
e.zh: 合唱团演唱了传统的斯拉夫民歌。

slavish.t: adj. 盲从的；毫无独创的

e.en: His {slavish} devotion to the brand surprised even his friends.
e.zh: 他对那个品牌的盲目崇拜连朋友都感到惊讶。

e.en: The remake is a {slavish} copy of the original film.
e.zh: 这部翻拍版是对原作毫无创意的照搬。

e.en: The film {slavishly} follows the original novel's plot.
e.zh: 这部电影一字不差地照搬了原著的情节。

e.en: He {slavishly} copied his mentor's writing style.
e.zh: 他亦步亦趋地模仿导师的写作风格。

slavonic.t: adj. 斯拉夫的；斯拉夫语的

e.en: She studies {Slavonic} languages at the university.
e.zh: 她在大学里研究斯拉夫语系。

e.en: The choir performed an old {Slavonic} folk song beautifully.
e.zh: 合唱团优美地演唱了一首古老的斯拉夫民歌。

e.en: The barbecue came with a side of creamy {slaw}.
e.zh: 烧烤配了一份奶香味的凉拌卷心菜。

e.en: I added apple slices to my homemade {slaw}.
e.zh: 我在自制的凉拌卷心菜里加了些苹果片。

slay.t: v. 杀死；(俚) 让人惊艳

e.en: Her outfit at the party absolutely {slay} tonight.
e.zh: 她今晚派对上的造型实在太惊艳了。

e.en: In the legend, the knight must {slay} the dragon.
e.zh: 在传说中，那位骑士必须杀死巨龙。

e.en: The video game features a vampire {slayer} as protagonist.
e.zh: 这款游戏的主角是一位吸血鬼猎人。

e.en: She's a total {slayer} on the dance floor tonight.
e.zh: 她今晚在舞池里简直惊艳全场。

slaying.t:
n. 凶杀
v. slay 的现在分词

e.en: Her new album is absolutely {slaying} the charts this week.
e.zh: 她的新专辑这周在排行榜上大杀四方。

e.en: The knight was famous for {slaying} the dragon single-handedly.
e.zh: 那位骑士因独自屠龙而闻名。

sleaze.t: n. 低俗行为；肮脏堕落

e.en: The tabloid is full of political {sleaze} and scandal.
e.zh: 那份小报充斥着政治丑闻和卑劣行径。

e.en: Voters are fed up with the {sleaze} in city hall.
e.zh: 选民们对市政府的腐败行为深感厌倦。

sleazy.t: adj. 低俗的；廉价肮脏的

e.en: He gave me a {sleazy} smile that made me uncomfortable.
e.zh: 他冲我露出一个令人不适的猥琐笑容。

e.en: They met in a {sleazy} bar near the docks.
e.zh: 他们在码头附近一家肮脏的酒吧碰头。

sled.t:
n. 雪橇
v. 乘雪橇

e.en: The kids dragged their {sled} up the snowy hill.
e.zh: 孩子们把雪橇拖上了白雪覆盖的山坡。

e.en: He built a wooden {sled} for his daughter's birthday.
e.zh: 他为女儿的生日做了一个木制雪橇。

e.en: We went {sledding} all afternoon after the snowstorm.
e.zh: 暴风雪过后我们滑了一下午雪橇。

e.en: Finishing this project won't be easy {sledding}.
e.zh: 完成这个项目可不会一帆风顺。

sledge.t:
n. 雪橇
v. 乘雪橇

e.en: They loaded supplies onto the {sledge} for the expedition.
e.zh: 他们把补给装上雪橇准备远征。

e.en: The dogs pulled the heavy {sledge} across the frozen lake.
e.zh: 狗群拉着沉重的雪橇穿过结冰的湖面。

e.en: He smashed the old wall with a {sledgehammer}.
e.zh: 他用大锤把旧墙砸了个稀烂。

e.en: Don't use a {sledgehammer} to crack a nut.
e.zh: 别用大锤砸核桃,小题大做。

sleek.t: adj. 光滑的；造型流畅的

e.en: The new phone has a {sleek} aluminum design.
e.zh: 这款新手机采用了流线型铝合金设计。

e.en: The cat's fur was {sleek} and shiny after grooming.
e.zh: 梳理过后,这只猫的毛光滑发亮。

e.en: The car turned {sleekly} around the corner at speed.
e.zh: 那辆车流畅地高速转过弯道。

e.en: Her hair was {sleekly} pulled back into a bun.
e.zh: 她的头发整齐光滑地束成了一个发髻。

e.en: The {sleekness} of the new MacBook impressed everyone.
e.zh: 新款MacBook的流畅外形让所有人惊艳。

e.en: I admired the {sleekness} of the dolphin's body.
e.zh: 我赞叹海豚身体的流线之美。

sleep.t:
v. 睡觉
n. 睡眠

e.en: I didn't get enough {sleep} before the big meeting.
e.zh: 重要会议前我没睡够。

e.en: Babies usually {sleep} sixteen hours a day.
e.zh: 婴儿一天通常要睡十六个小时。

sleeper.t: n. 睡觉的人；卧铺；爆冷作品

e.en: This indie film became the {sleeper} hit of the summer.
e.zh: 这部独立电影成了今夏的黑马。

e.en: My brother is a heavy {sleeper} who never hears alarms.
e.zh: 我哥睡得很沉,从来听不见闹钟。

sleepily.t: adv. 困倦地；昏昏欲睡地

e.en: She {sleepily} reached for her phone on the nightstand.
e.zh: 她睡眼惺忪地伸手去拿床头柜上的手机。

e.en: The toddler {sleepily} rubbed his eyes.
e.zh: 那个小孩困倦地揉着眼睛。

e.en: Coffee helps me fight the afternoon {sleepiness}.
e.zh: 咖啡能帮我抵抗下午的困意。

e.en: Her {sleepiness} made it hard to focus on the lecture.
e.zh: 她困得无法集中精力听讲座。

sleeping.t:
adj. 睡着的
n. 睡眠

e.en: Please be quiet—the baby is {sleeping}.
e.zh: 请安静,宝宝正在睡觉。

e.en: He bought a new {sleeping} bag for the camping trip.
e.zh: 他为这次露营买了一个新睡袋。

e.en: After three {sleepless} nights, she could barely function.
e.zh: 连续三个不眠之夜后,她几乎无法正常工作。

e.en: Worry about the exam left him {sleepless}.
e.zh: 对考试的担忧让他彻夜难眠。

e.en: Chronic {sleeplessness} can lead to serious health problems.
e.zh: 长期失眠会导致严重的健康问题。

e.en: Stress at work caused her {sleeplessness}.
e.zh: 工作压力导致了她的失眠。

sleepover.t: n. 在朋友家过夜（聚会）

e.en: My daughter is having a {sleepover} with three friends tonight.
e.zh: 我女儿今晚要和三个朋友一起过夜玩。

e.en: Kids love bringing snacks and movies to a {sleepover}.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢带零食和电影去过夜聚会。

sleeps.t: v. 睡觉（第三人称单数）

e.en: This tent comfortably {sleeps} four adults.
e.zh: 这顶帐篷可以舒适地容纳四个成年人睡觉。

e.en: My cat {sleeps} on top of my keyboard every morning.
e.zh: 我的猫每天早上都睡在我的键盘上。

e.en: As a child, I used to {sleepwalk} into the kitchen.
e.zh: 小时候我常常梦游走进厨房。

e.en: The team can't {sleepwalk} through the second half.
e.zh: 球队下半场不能心不在焉地应付。

e.en: Don't startle a {sleepwalker}—just gently guide them back.
e.zh: 别惊吓梦游者,只需轻轻把他们带回床上。

e.en: My roommate is a {sleepwalker} who once made breakfast asleep.
e.zh: 我室友会梦游,有次还在睡梦中做了早餐。

sleepwalking.t:
n. 梦游
adj. 梦游的

e.en: Doctors say {sleepwalking} usually stops by adolescence.
e.zh: 医生说梦游通常到青春期就会停止。

e.en: The CEO accused the company of {sleepwalking} into disaster.
e.zh: 那位首席执行官指责公司浑浑噩噩地走向灾难。

e.en: This brand makes soft cotton {sleepwear} for kids.
e.zh: 这个品牌生产柔软的儿童棉质睡衣。

e.en: She packed her {sleepwear} at the top of the suitcase.
e.zh: 她把睡衣放在行李箱最上层。

sleepy.t: adj. 困倦的；昏昏欲睡的

e.en: I always feel {sleepy} after a heavy lunch.
e.zh: 我吃完丰盛的午餐后总是犯困。

e.en: They retired to a {sleepy} village in Tuscany.
e.zh: 他们退居到托斯卡纳一个宁静的小村庄。

sleepyhead.t: n. 瞌睡虫；爱睡觉的人

e.en: Wake up, {sleepyhead}—breakfast is ready!
e.zh: 醒醒啦,小懒虫,早餐做好了!

e.en: My little {sleepyhead} can sleep through any thunderstorm.
e.zh: 我家的小瞌睡虫连打雷都吵不醒。

sleet.t:
n. 雨夹雪
v. 下雨夹雪

e.en: Driving through {sleet} made the highway dangerously slippery.
e.zh: 在雨夹雪中开车让高速公路变得非常滑。

e.en: It started to {sleet} just as we left home.
e.zh: 我们刚出门就开始下起了雨夹雪。

e.en: He rolled up his {sleeve} to show the tattoo.
e.zh: 他卷起袖子展示纹身。

e.en: She always has another trick up her {sleeve}.
e.zh: 她总是另有妙招暗藏在身。

e.en: I prefer long-{sleeved} shirts in the autumn.
e.zh: 秋天我更喜欢穿长袖衬衫。

e.en: She wore a beautifully {sleeved} dress to the gala.
e.zh: 她穿了一件袖子设计精美的礼服去参加晚会。

e.en: She wore a {sleeveless} dress to the summer wedding.
e.zh: 她穿了一件无袖连衣裙参加夏季婚礼。

e.en: This {sleeveless} top is perfect for hot weather.
e.zh: 这件无袖上衣很适合炎热的天气。

e.en: He rolled up his {sleeves} and got to work.
e.zh: 他卷起袖子开始干活。

e.en: The jacket has leather patches on the {sleeves}.
e.zh: 这件夹克的袖子上有皮革补丁。

e.en: Santa's {sleigh} is pulled by nine reindeer.
e.zh: 圣诞老人的雪橇由九只驯鹿拉着。

e.en: They took a horse-drawn {sleigh} ride through the forest.
e.zh: 他们乘坐马拉雪橇穿过森林。

sleight.t: n. 手法；戏法（常用 sleight of hand）

e.en: The magician's {sleight} of hand fooled everyone in the audience.
e.zh: 魔术师的手法骗过了所有观众。

e.en: He won the bet through pure {sleight} of hand.
e.zh: 他完全靠手上的小把戏赢得了赌注。

slender.t: adj. 苗条的；细长的；微薄的

e.en: She has a tall, {slender} build perfect for modeling.
e.zh: 她身材高挑纤细,非常适合做模特。

e.en: Our team has only a {slender} chance of winning.
e.zh: 我们队赢的机会非常渺茫。

e.en: The {slenderness} of the bridge's design is remarkable.
e.zh: 这座桥设计的纤细程度令人称奇。

e.en: Her {slenderness} comes from years of ballet training.
e.zh: 她的苗条身材源于多年的芭蕾训练。

slept.t: v. sleep 的过去式/过去分词

e.en: I {slept} like a baby after the long flight.
e.zh: 长途飞行之后我睡得像个婴儿一样香。

e.en: We {slept} in tents during the camping trip.
e.zh: 露营时我们睡在帐篷里。

sleuth.t:
n. 侦探
v. 侦查

e.en: The amateur {sleuth} solved the case before the police.
e.zh: 那位业余侦探在警察之前破了案。

e.en: Fans tried to {sleuth} out the singer's secret identity.
e.zh: 粉丝们试图侦查出那位歌手的真实身份。

e.en: A bit of online {sleuthing} revealed the scammer's real address.
e.zh: 一番网上侦查揭露了骗子的真实地址。

e.en: She enjoys {sleuthing} through old archives for clues.
e.zh: 她喜欢翻查旧档案寻找线索。

slew.t:
n. 大量
v. 扭转；slay 的过去式

e.en: The startup faces a whole {slew} of new regulations.
e.zh: 这家初创公司面临一大堆新法规。

e.en: The car {slew} sideways on the icy road.
e.zh: 汽车在结冰的路面上侧滑了出去。

slice.t:
n. 一片
v. 切片

e.en: Could I have another {slice} of pizza, please?
e.zh: 我能再来一片披萨吗?

e.en: Be careful when you {slice} the tomatoes.
e.zh: 切番茄的时候要小心。

e.en: He {sliced} the bread into thin, even pieces.
e.zh: 他把面包切成又薄又均匀的片。

e.en: This is the best thing since {sliced} bread.
e.zh: 这是有史以来最棒的发明。

e.en: The deli uses an electric {slicer} for the ham.
e.zh: 熟食店用电动切片机来切火腿。

e.en: I bought a manual vegetable {slicer} for the kitchen.
e.zh: 我给厨房买了一个手动蔬菜切片器。

slices.t:
n. 片（复数）
v. 切（第三人称单数）

e.en: She cut the cake into eight equal {slices}.
e.zh: 她把蛋糕切成八块相等的片。

e.en: The chef {slices} the salmon paper-thin.
e.zh: 厨师把三文鱼切得薄如纸。

slicing.t:
n. 切片
v. 切（进行时）

e.en: He cut his finger while {slicing} onions.
e.zh: 他在切洋葱时割破了手指。

e.en: The new feature is great for {slicing} the data by region.
e.zh: 新功能非常适合按地区切分数据。

slick.t: adj. 光滑的；圆滑的；漂亮利落的

e.en: The app has a {slick} interface that's easy to navigate.
e.zh: 这个应用界面流畅,操作起来很顺手。

e.en: Watch out—the road is {slick} after the rain.
e.zh: 小心点,雨后路面很滑。

slicked.t: adj. 梳得油亮的；抹平的

e.en: His hair was {slicked} back with gel.
e.zh: 他用发胶把头发向后梳得油光锃亮。

e.en: The model walked out with {slicked}-down hair.
e.zh: 那位模特顶着服帖光滑的头发走了出来。

slicker.t:
n. 雨衣
adj. 更圆滑的

e.en: The new app feels much {slicker} than the old version.
e.zh: 这款新应用感觉比旧版本流畅顺手得多。

e.en: He pulled on a yellow {slicker} before walking into the rain.
e.zh: 他在走进雨中前套上了一件黄色雨衣。

slickly.t: adv. 圆滑地；漂亮利落地

e.en: The presentation was {slickly} produced and very persuasive.
e.zh: 这场演示制作精良,极具说服力。

e.en: She {slickly} dodged every difficult question from reporters.
e.zh: 她圆滑地避开了记者每一个棘手的问题。

e.en: The {slickness} of the marketing made customers suspicious.
e.zh: 营销过于光鲜油滑,反而让顾客起了疑心。

e.en: Drivers were warned about the {slickness} of the icy roads.
e.zh: 驾驶员被警告注意结冰路面的湿滑。

slid.t: v. slide 的过去式/过去分词

e.en: She quietly {slid} the note across the table to him.
e.zh: 她悄悄地把纸条从桌上推给他。

e.en: The stock price {slid} sharply after the earnings report.
e.zh: 财报发布后,股价大幅下跌。

slide.t:
v. 滑动
n. 滑梯；幻灯片

e.en: Please advance to the next {slide} in the deck.
e.zh: 请翻到演示文稿的下一张幻灯片。

e.en: The kids love to {slide} down the snowy hill.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢从雪坡上滑下来。

e.en: Drag the {slider} to adjust the screen brightness.
e.zh: 拖动滑块来调节屏幕亮度。

e.en: He ordered three cheeseburger {slider} at the diner.
e.zh: 他在餐馆点了三个迷你芝士汉堡。

slides.t:
n. 幻灯片（复数）
v. 滑动（第三人称单数）

e.en: She {slides} her phone into her back pocket.
e.zh: 她把手机滑进后裤袋里。

e.en: The presentation has thirty {slides} with detailed charts.
e.zh: 这份演示文稿有三十张幻灯片，附详细图表。

slideshow.t: n. 幻灯片放映；图片轮播

e.en: He made a birthday {slideshow} of old family photos.
e.zh: 他用家庭老照片做了个生日幻灯片。

e.en: The app turns your gallery into an automatic {slideshow}.
e.zh: 这个应用能把相册自动变成幻灯片。

sliding.t:
adj. 滑动的
n. 滑动

e.en: The bedroom has a {sliding} glass door to the garden.
e.zh: 卧室有一扇通往花园的滑动玻璃门。

e.en: Stock prices have been {sliding} for three weeks straight.
e.zh: 股价已连续下滑了三周。

slight.t:
adj. 轻微的
v. 轻视
n. 怠慢

e.en: There was a {slight} delay due to heavy traffic.
e.zh: 由于交通拥堵，出现了轻微的延误。

e.en: She felt a {slight} chill and grabbed a sweater.
e.zh: 她感到一丝凉意，便拿起了毛衣。

slighted.t: adj. 被怠慢的；受冷落的

e.en: He felt {slighted} when nobody invited him to lunch.
e.zh: 没人邀请他吃午饭，他感到被冷落了。

e.en: She {slighted} her old friend by ignoring her message.
e.zh: 她不回老朋友的消息，怠慢了对方。

e.en: The new model is {slightly} faster than last year's.
e.zh: 新款比去年的型号稍快一些。

e.en: Turn the screw {slightly} to the right to tighten it.
e.zh: 把螺丝稍微向右拧一下就能拧紧。

slights.t:
n. 怠慢（复数）
v. 轻视（第三人称单数）

e.en: He brushed off the small {slights} from his coworkers.
e.zh: 他没把同事的小怠慢放在心上。

e.en: The article {slights} her contributions to the project.
e.zh: 这篇文章贬低了她对项目的贡献。

sligo.t: n. 斯莱戈（爱尔兰地名）

e.en: We spent the weekend surfing in {Sligo} on the west coast.
e.zh: 我们周末在西海岸的斯莱戈冲浪。

e.en: The poet Yeats is closely associated with {Sligo}, Ireland.
e.zh: 诗人叶芝与爱尔兰的斯莱戈关系密切。

slim.t:
adj. 苗条的，纤细的
v. 减肥

e.en: The new laptop is incredibly {slim} and light.
e.zh: 这款新笔记本电脑非常轻薄。

e.en: Our chances of winning are pretty {slim} now.
e.zh: 我们获胜的机会现在相当渺茫。

e.en: Kids love mixing glue and borax to make {slime}.
e.zh: 小孩子们喜欢用胶水和硼砂调出史莱姆玩。

e.en: Green {slime} covered the rocks at the pond's edge.
e.zh: 池塘边的石头上覆盖着一层绿色黏液。

e.en: That {slimeball} lied to everyone in the office.
e.zh: 那个卑鄙的家伙对办公室里每个人都撒了谎。

e.en: Don't trust him — he's a total {slimeball}.
e.zh: 别相信他，他就是个十足的小人。

slimline.t: adj. 超薄的，纤细外形的

e.en: I prefer the {slimline} version of the phone case.
e.zh: 我更喜欢这款手机壳的超薄版本。

e.en: She ordered a {slimline} tonic with her gin.
e.zh: 她点了杜松子酒配低糖汤力水。

slimmer.t:
n. 减肥的人
adj. 更苗条的

e.en: This jacket makes you look much {slimmer}.
e.zh: 这件外套让你看起来苗条多了。

e.en: The new phone is {slimmer} than its predecessor.
e.zh: 这款新手机比上一代更轻薄。

slimming.t:
n. 减肥
adj. 显瘦的

e.en: Black is famously {slimming} in photographs.
e.zh: 众所周知，黑色在照片里显瘦。

e.en: She joined a {slimming} club to lose some weight.
e.zh: 她加入了一个减肥俱乐部想瘦一点。

e.en: The phone's {slimness} makes it easy to slip into any pocket.
e.zh: 这款手机的轻薄让它能轻松装进任何口袋。

e.en: She's proud of the {slimness} she achieved through running.
e.zh: 她为通过跑步保持的苗条身材感到自豪。

slimy.t: adj. 黏滑的；令人厌恶的

e.en: The fish felt cold and {slimy} in my hands.
e.zh: 那条鱼在我手里冰凉黏滑。

e.en: He gave me a {slimy} smile that made me uneasy.
e.zh: 他冲我露出一个让人不安的虚伪笑容。

sling.t:
n. 吊带，绷带
v. 投掷，悬挂

e.en: She wore her arm in a {sling} after the fall.
e.zh: 摔倒后她用吊带把胳膊吊了起来。

e.en: He'll {sling} the backpack over his shoulder and go.
e.zh: 他会把背包往肩上一甩就走。

e.en: She paired the dress with elegant black {slingback} heels.
e.zh: 她用优雅的黑色露跟高跟鞋搭配那条裙子。

e.en: These {slingback} sandals are perfect for summer evenings.
e.zh: 这双露跟凉鞋很适合夏夜穿。

e.en: The boy made a {slingshot} from a forked branch.
e.zh: 那男孩用一根分叉的树枝做了个弹弓。

e.en: Earth's gravity acted like a {slingshot} for the spacecraft.
e.zh: 地球引力对那艘飞船起到了弹弓加速的作用。

e.en: He tried to {slink} out of the meeting unnoticed.
e.zh: 他想悄悄溜出会议而不被察觉。

e.en: Cats love to {slink} along the garden fence at night.
e.zh: 猫咪喜欢夜里沿着花园篱笆悄悄潜行。

e.en: She wore a {slinky} black dress to the gala.
e.zh: 她穿了一件贴身的黑色礼服参加晚宴。

e.en: As a kid I loved watching a {slinky} walk down stairs.
e.zh: 小时候我最喜欢看彩虹圈一阶阶滑下楼梯。

slip.t:
v. 滑倒；溜走
n. 小纸条；失误

e.en: Be careful not to {slip} on the wet floor.
e.zh: 小心别在湿地板上滑倒。

e.en: She handed me a {slip} of paper with her number.
e.zh: 她递给我一张写着电话号码的小纸条。

e.en: A washable {slipcover} keeps the sofa looking new.
e.zh: 可水洗的沙发套能让沙发一直看起来很新。

e.en: We bought a beige {slipcover} to hide the old stains.
e.zh: 我们买了米色沙发套来盖住旧污渍。

e.en: The living room has two {slipcovered} armchairs by the window.
e.zh: 客厅窗边摆着两把套着布罩的扶手椅。

e.en: She prefers {slipcovered} sofas because they're easy to clean.
e.zh: 她喜欢带布套的沙发，因为容易清洗。

slipknot.t: n. 活结（可拉紧的绳结）

e.en: Start every crochet project with a simple {slipknot}.
e.zh: 每个钩针作品都要从一个简单的活结开始。

e.en: He tied a {slipknot} so the rope could tighten easily.
e.zh: 他打了个活结，这样绳子能轻松收紧。

e.en: There's been some {slippage} in the project deadline.
e.zh: 项目截止日期出现了一些拖延。

e.en: Crypto traders worry about {slippage} during volatile markets.
e.zh: 加密货币交易者担心市场剧烈波动时的滑点。

slipped.t: v. 滑倒，溜走（slip 过去式）

e.en: She {slipped} on the icy steps and bruised her elbow.
e.zh: 她在结冰的台阶上滑倒，胳膊肘磕青了。

e.en: He quietly {slipped} the note into her bag.
e.zh: 他悄悄把字条塞进她的包里。

e.en: He lost one fluffy {slipper} under the bed again.
e.zh: 他又把一只毛绒拖鞋丢到床底下了。

e.en: She kicked off a {slipper} and curled up on the couch.
e.zh: 她踢掉一只拖鞋，蜷缩在沙发上。

e.en: Grandpa shuffled into the kitchen on {slippered} feet.
e.zh: 爷爷穿着拖鞋慢悠悠地走进厨房。

e.en: Her {slippered} feet made no sound on the wooden floor.
e.zh: 她穿着拖鞋的脚在木地板上毫无声响。

e.en: The {slipperiness} of the road caused several accidents.
e.zh: 路面的湿滑导致了几起事故。

e.en: I hate the {slipperiness} of okra when it's cooked.
e.zh: 我讨厌秋葵煮过之后那种黏滑的感觉。

e.en: The marble floor gets really {slippery} when it's wet.
e.zh: 大理石地板一湿就会变得很滑。

e.en: That politician is a {slippery} character — never gives straight answers.
e.zh: 那位政客是个滑头，从不正面回答问题。

slipping.t: v. 滑落，下滑（slip 现在分词）

e.en: My grades are {slipping} since I started working nights.
e.zh: 自从开始上夜班，我的成绩一直在下滑。

e.en: She kept {slipping} on the muddy trail up the hill.
e.zh: 她在上山的泥泞小路上不停打滑。

e.en: Watch out — the bathroom tiles are really {slippy} when wet.
e.zh: 小心，浴室瓷砖一湿就特别滑。

e.en: These shoes feel a bit {slippy} on polished floors.
e.zh: 这双鞋在抛光地板上感觉有点打滑。

e.en: She handed out paper {slips} for everyone to vote on.
e.zh: 她发下小纸条让大家投票。

e.en: He often {slips} away from parties without saying goodbye.
e.zh: 他经常不打招呼就从派对上溜走。

e.en: The report was rejected because of its {slipshod} research.
e.zh: 这份报告因调查粗制滥造而被驳回。

e.en: I won't tolerate {slipshod} work on such an important project.
e.zh: 这么重要的项目我不会容忍马虎应付的工作。

e.en: Cyclists save energy by riding in another rider's {slipstream}.
e.zh: 骑手通过跟在别人尾流后骑行来节省体力。

e.en: Smaller startups often ride the {slipstream} of tech giants.
e.zh: 小型初创公司常常借着科技巨头的尾流前行。

e.en: The new yacht was launched down the {slipway} this morning.
e.zh: 这艘新游艇今早从船台上下水了。

e.en: Fishing boats lined the old wooden {slipway} at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时分，渔船排列在旧木制船坡上。

slit.t:
n. 狭缝，切口
v. 切开，割裂

e.en: She wore a black dress with a high {slit}.
e.zh: 她穿了一条开高衩的黑色连衣裙。

e.en: He carefully {slit} open the envelope with a knife.
e.zh: 他用刀小心地划开了信封。

e.en: Snakes {slither} silently through the tall grass.
e.zh: 蛇悄无声息地在高草丛中蜿蜒游动。

e.en: He watched the eel {slither} back into the water.
e.zh: 他看着那条鳗鱼蜿蜒滑回水中。

slithered.t: v. 蜿蜒滑行（slither 过去式）

e.en: A small lizard {slithered} across the warm patio stones.
e.zh: 一只小蜥蜴从温热的庭院石板上溜过。

e.en: The snake {slithered} under a rock and disappeared.
e.zh: 那条蛇蜿蜒钻进石头底下不见了。

e.en: I saw something {slithering} through the leaves near the path.
e.zh: 我看见有东西在小路旁的落叶里蜿蜒爬行。

e.en: The python kept {slithering} toward the warm sunny corner.
e.zh: 那条蟒蛇不停地朝阳光温暖的角落蜿蜒爬去。

slithers.t: v. 蜿蜒滑行（第三人称单数）

e.en: The garden snake {slithers} away whenever someone approaches.
e.zh: 只要有人靠近，那条园蛇就蜿蜒爬走。

e.en: A trail of small {slithers} marked the sand by the dunes.
e.zh: 沙丘旁的沙地上留下一道道蜿蜒的爬行痕迹。

e.en: The wet seaweed felt cold and {slithery} underfoot.
e.zh: 湿漉漉的海藻踩上去又凉又滑。

e.en: She didn't like the {slithery} texture of raw oysters.
e.zh: 她不喜欢生蚝那种黏滑的口感。

e.en: The cat watched me through {slitted} green eyes.
e.zh: 那只猫眯着绿色的眼睛盯着我。

e.en: He wore a helmet with a narrow {slitted} visor.
e.zh: 他戴着一顶有窄缝面甲的头盔。

e.en: There's only a {sliver} of cake left in the fridge.
e.zh: 冰箱里只剩下薄薄一片蛋糕了。

e.en: A {sliver} of moon hung above the rooftops.
e.zh: 一弯细细的月牙挂在屋顶上方。

e.en: Sprinkle {slivered} almonds on top of the salad.
e.zh: 在沙拉上撒一些杏仁片。

e.en: She added {slivered} ginger to the simmering broth.
e.zh: 她在炖煮的高汤里加了些姜丝。

e.en: Be careful — there are glass {slivers} all over the floor.
e.zh: 小心，地上到处都是玻璃碎片。

e.en: Thin {slivers} of sunlight came through the blinds.
e.zh: 细细的阳光从百叶窗缝里透进来。

e.en: My roommate is such a {slob} — dishes everywhere.
e.zh: 我室友真是个邋遢鬼，到处都是脏盘子。

e.en: Don't be a {slob}; pick up your clothes off the floor.
e.zh: 别那么邋遢，把地上的衣服捡起来。

e.en: The big dog left {slobber} all over my new shirt.
e.zh: 那只大狗在我新衬衫上流了一堆口水。

e.en: Puppies tend to {slobber} when they get really excited.
e.zh: 小狗一兴奋就容易流口水。

e.en: A huge {slobbering} bulldog greeted us at the door.
e.zh: 一只流着口水的大斗牛犬在门口迎接我们。

e.en: Stop {slobbering} on the couch cushions, please.
e.zh: 求你别再把口水流到沙发垫上了。

slobbery.t: adj. 口水淋漓的，湿漉漉的

e.en: The puppy gave me a {slobbery} kiss on the cheek.
e.zh: 小狗在我脸颊上湿漉漉地亲了一口。

e.en: He wiped the {slobbery} tennis ball before throwing it again.
e.zh: 他擦了擦那颗满是口水的网球才再次扔出去。

e.en: My roommates are total {slobs} who never clean up.
e.zh: 我的室友都是从不收拾的邋遢鬼。

e.en: Don't be {slobs}—put your dishes in the sink.
e.zh: 别那么邋遢,把碗放进水槽里。

e.en: She poured a glass of {sloe} gin after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后她倒了一杯黑刺李金酒。

e.en: The hedge was full of dark, bitter {sloe} berries.
e.zh: 树篱上结满了深色苦涩的黑刺李果。

slog.t:
v. 埋头苦干；艰难跋涉
n. 苦差事

e.en: Writing the final chapter was a real {slog}.
e.zh: 写最后一章真是个苦差事。

e.en: We had to {slog} through mud for two hours.
e.zh: 我们不得不在泥地里艰难跋涉两个小时。

e.en: Their new ad {slogan} caught on instantly online.
e.zh: 他们的新广告标语在网上瞬间走红。

e.en: Protesters chanted a {slogan} outside city hall.
e.zh: 抗议者在市政厅外高喊着一句口号。

sloganeer.t:
n. 爱喊口号的人
v. 空喊口号

e.en: The candidate is more of a {sloganeer} than a thinker.
e.zh: 这位候选人更像个口号制造者,而不是思想家。

e.en: Critics accused him of being a shallow {sloganeer}.
e.zh: 批评者指责他是个空喊口号的人。

sloganeering.t: n. 空喊口号；标语式宣传

e.en: Voters are tired of empty {sloganeering} from politicians.
e.zh: 选民们厌倦了政客们空洞的口号宣传。

e.en: The campaign relied on {sloganeering} instead of real policy.
e.zh: 这场竞选靠的是喊口号,而不是真正的政策。

e.en: The walls were covered in protest {slogans}.
e.zh: 墙上贴满了抗议标语。

e.en: Catchy {slogans} can make or break an ad campaign.
e.zh: 朗朗上口的口号能决定一场广告活动的成败。

e.en: They sailed a small {sloop} around the bay.
e.zh: 他们驾着一艘小单桅帆船绕海湾航行。

e.en: The {sloop} was anchored just off the harbor.
e.zh: 那艘单桅帆船就停泊在港口外。

slop.t:
n. 泔水；溅出的液体
v. 溅出；洒落

e.en: Don't {slop} coffee on the keyboard again.
e.zh: 别再把咖啡洒在键盘上了。

e.en: The pigs eagerly ate the kitchen {slop}.
e.zh: 猪儿急切地吃着厨房剩下的泔水。

slope.t:
n. 斜坡；坡度
v. 倾斜

e.en: We hiked up a steep {slope} to the summit.
e.zh: 我们沿着陡峭的山坡爬到了山顶。

e.en: The roof has a gentle {slope} for drainage.
e.zh: 屋顶有一个利于排水的缓坡。

sloped.t:
adj. 倾斜的
v. 倾斜（过去式）

e.en: The garden {sloped} gently down toward the lake.
e.zh: 花园缓缓向湖边倾斜下去。

e.en: He {sloped} off home before anyone noticed.
e.zh: 他没等人察觉就溜回家了。

slopes.t:
n. 斜坡（复数）
v. 倾斜

e.en: Skiers crowded the {slopes} all weekend.
e.zh: 整个周末滑雪者挤满了雪道。

e.en: Vineyards cover the sunny {slopes} of the valley.
e.zh: 葡萄园覆盖着山谷向阳的山坡。

e.en: The cottage sits on a gently {sloping} lawn.
e.zh: 小屋坐落在一片缓缓倾斜的草坪上。

e.en: She built shelves into the {sloping} attic ceiling.
e.zh: 她在倾斜的阁楼天花板里嵌入了书架。

e.en: The report was {sloppily} written and full of typos.
e.zh: 这份报告写得潦草,充满错别字。

e.en: He {sloppily} threw his clothes onto the chair.
e.zh: 他随手把衣服胡乱扔在椅子上。

e.en: The manager warned the team about coding {sloppiness}.
e.zh: 经理警告团队不要在代码上马虎。

e.en: Her {sloppiness} cost the project an entire week.
e.zh: 她的草率让这个项目损失了整整一周。

sloppy.t: adj. 马虎的；邋遢的；湿哒哒的

e.en: His handwriting is too {sloppy} to read.
e.zh: 他的字写得太潦草,根本看不清。

e.en: That's a {sloppy} bug fix—please rewrite it.
e.zh: 这个修复太草率了,请重写一下。

e.en: Coffee began to {slosh} out of the mug.
e.zh: 咖啡开始从杯子里晃出来。

e.en: We had to {slosh} through ankle-deep water.
e.zh: 我们不得不在没到脚踝的水里走过去。

sloshed.t:
adj. 喝醉的
v. 晃荡（过去式）

e.en: Water {sloshed} around in the bucket as I walked.
e.zh: 我走路时桶里的水来回晃动。

e.en: He came home completely {sloshed} after the party.
e.zh: 他派对后回家时已经醉得不行。

sloshing.t: v. 晃荡；泼溅（现在分词）

e.en: I could hear the soup {sloshing} in the thermos.
e.zh: 我能听见保温瓶里的汤晃来晃去的声音。

e.en: Kids were {sloshing} through puddles after the rain.
e.zh: 雨后孩子们在水坑里啪嗒啪嗒地踩水。

slot.t:
n. 插槽；时段；位置
v. 插入

e.en: Insert your card into the {slot} above the screen.
e.zh: 把卡片插入屏幕上方的卡槽。

e.en: I booked a 3 p.m. {slot} for the meeting.
e.zh: 我预约了下午三点的会议时段。

e.en: A {sloth} hung lazily from the rainforest branch.
e.zh: 一只树懒懒洋洋地挂在雨林的树枝上。

e.en: His weekend {sloth} drove his roommate crazy.
e.zh: 他周末的懒散让室友抓狂。

e.en: After lunch I felt warm and {slothful}.
e.zh: 午饭后我感到暖洋洋的、懒洋洋的。

e.en: The boss criticized his {slothful} attitude at work.
e.zh: 老板批评了他工作上懒散的态度。

e.en: All the parking {slots} downtown were already taken.
e.zh: 市中心所有停车位都已经被占了。

e.en: She lost fifty bucks playing the {slots} in Vegas.
e.zh: 她在拉斯维加斯玩老虎机输了五十块。

slouch.t:
v. 无精打采地站/坐
n. 懒散的姿势

e.en: Try not to {slouch} when you're at your desk.
e.zh: 坐在桌前时尽量别弯腰驼背。

e.en: He's no {slouch} when it comes to coding.
e.zh: 说到编程,他可不是个庸才。

slouched.t: v. 弯腰驼背地坐/站（过去式）

e.en: She {slouched} into the chair, exhausted from work.
e.zh: 她精疲力尽地瘫坐进椅子里。

e.en: He {slouched} against the wall, scrolling on his phone.
e.zh: 他靠在墙上,弓着背刷手机。

slouching.t: v. 无精打采地站/坐（现在分词）

e.en: Stop {slouching}—it's bad for your back.
e.zh: 别再驼背了,对你的背不好。

e.en: The teen sat {slouching} at the back of the classroom.
e.zh: 那个少年驼着背坐在教室后排。

slouchy.t: adj. 宽松随意的；懒散的

e.en: She wore a {slouchy} sweater and jeans to brunch.
e.zh: 她穿着宽松的毛衣和牛仔裤去吃早午餐。

e.en: Designers love {slouchy} silhouettes this season.
e.zh: 本季设计师们偏爱宽松慵懒的廓形。

slough.t:
n. 泥沼；困境
v. 蜕皮；抛弃

e.en: Snakes {slough} their skin several times a year.
e.zh: 蛇一年要蜕几次皮。

e.en: It took months to {slough} off the bad memories.
e.zh: 她花了几个月才把那些不愉快的记忆抛开。

slovak.t:
adj. 斯洛伐克的
n. 斯洛伐克人/语

e.en: He's learning {Slovak} for his job in Bratislava.
e.zh: 他正在学斯洛伐克语,为了去布拉迪斯拉发工作。

e.en: The menu featured several traditional {Slovak} dishes.
e.zh: 菜单上有几道传统的斯洛伐克菜。

e.en: We spent a weekend hiking in northern {Slovakia}.
e.zh: 我们在斯洛伐克北部徒步度过了一个周末。

e.en: {Slovakia} joined the European Union back in 2004.
e.zh: 斯洛伐克早在2004年就加入了欧盟。

slovakian.t:
adj. 斯洛伐克的
n. 斯洛伐克人

e.en: My new coworker is {Slovakian} and speaks four languages.
e.zh: 我的新同事是斯洛伐克人,会说四种语言。

e.en: She brought back a bottle of {Slovakian} wine.
e.zh: 她带回了一瓶斯洛伐克葡萄酒。

e.en: His desk looks like a {sloven} has been working there.
e.zh: 他的办公桌看起来像个邋遢鬼在那儿工作。

e.en: Don't be such a {sloven}—change those clothes.
e.zh: 别这么邋遢,把这些衣服换掉。

slovene.t:
adj. 斯洛文尼亚的
n. 斯洛文尼亚人/语

e.en: She speaks {Slovene} fluently after living in Ljubljana.
e.zh: 在卢布尔雅那住过之后她说一口流利的斯洛文尼亚语。

e.en: The novel was originally written in {Slovene}.
e.zh: 这部小说最初是用斯洛文尼亚语写成的。

e.en: {Slovenia} is famous for its stunning Lake Bled.
e.zh: 斯洛文尼亚以美丽的布莱德湖而闻名。

e.en: We drove from {Slovenia} into Croatia in two hours.
e.zh: 我们用两个小时从斯洛文尼亚开车到了克罗地亚。

slovenian.t:
adj. 斯洛文尼亚的
n. 斯洛文尼亚人

e.en: The chef prepared a hearty {Slovenian} stew.
e.zh: 厨师做了一道丰盛的斯洛文尼亚炖菜。

e.en: He's the only {Slovenian} player on the team.
e.zh: 他是队里唯一的斯洛文尼亚球员。

e.en: Her {slovenliness} made the kitchen unbearable to use.
e.zh: 她的邋遢让厨房根本没法用。

e.en: The inspector noted the general {slovenliness} of the warehouse.
e.zh: 督察员指出仓库整体上一片狼藉。

e.en: He has a rather {slovenly} appearance most mornings.
e.zh: 他大多数早上看起来都挺邋遢的。

e.en: The report was rejected for its {slovenly} formatting.
e.zh: 报告因排版马虎而被退回。

slow.t:
adj. 慢的；迟钝的
v. 放慢

e.en: My laptop has gotten really {slow} this week.
e.zh: 我的笔记本这周变得超级慢。

e.en: Please {slow} down—I can't understand you.
e.zh: 请慢一点,我听不清你说的话。

e.en: Investors worry about a global economic {slowdown}.
e.zh: 投资者担心全球经济会放缓。

e.en: There's a major traffic {slowdown} on the highway.
e.zh: 高速公路上严重堵车,车速大幅下降。

slowed.t: v. 变慢；使放慢（过去式）

e.en: The rain {slowed} traffic across the entire city.
e.zh: 大雨让全城的交通都慢了下来。

e.en: Sales have {slowed} since the holiday season ended.
e.zh: 假日季结束以来销售已经放缓。

slower.t: adj. 更慢的（slow 的比较级）

e.en: The new update made the app feel {slower}.
e.zh: 新更新让这款应用感觉更慢了。

e.en: Could you walk a bit {slower}, please?
e.zh: 你能不能走慢一点?

slowing.t: v. 变慢；使放慢（现在分词）

e.en: Job growth has been {slowing} for three quarters.
e.zh: 就业增长已经连续三个季度放缓。

e.en: The car was {slowing} down as it approached the light.
e.zh: 汽车接近红灯时正在减速。

e.en: She {slowly} opened the door to the dark room.
e.zh: 她慢慢地打开了那间黑屋子的门。

e.en: His Chinese is {slowly} getting better.
e.zh: 他的中文正在慢慢进步。

e.en: The {slowness} of the website is driving customers away quickly.
e.zh: 网站的缓慢正在迅速赶走客户。

e.en: His {slowness} to respond to emails frustrates the entire team.
e.zh: 他回复邮件的迟缓让整个团队感到沮丧。

slowpoke.t: n. 动作慢的人；慢性子

e.en: Hurry up, {slowpoke} — we're going to miss the movie!
e.zh: 快点,慢吞吞的家伙,我们要错过电影了!

e.en: My little brother is such a {slowpoke} when getting dressed.
e.zh: 我弟弟穿衣服时真是个慢性子。

slows.t: v. 变慢；使放慢（第三人称单数）

e.en: Heavy traffic always {slows} my morning commute considerably.
e.zh: 严重的交通拥堵总是让我早上的通勤大幅减慢。

e.en: The new update {slows} down older phones noticeably.
e.zh: 新的更新明显让旧手机变慢了。

slr.t: n. 单镜头反光相机（single-lens reflex）

e.en: Industrial {sludge} from the factory polluted the nearby river badly.
e.zh: 工厂排出的工业污泥严重污染了附近的河流。

e.en: The melted snow turned into brown {sludge} on the streets.
e.zh: 融化的雪在街道上变成了棕色的烂泥。

e.en: The coffee was cold and {sludgy} at the bottom of the cup.
e.zh: 咖啡又冷又稠地沉在杯底。

e.en: After the rain, the trail became {sludgy} and hard to walk.
e.zh: 雨后小径变得泥泞难行。

e.en: The truck began to {slue} sideways on the icy road.
e.zh: 卡车在结冰的路面上开始侧向打滑。

e.en: He had to {slue} the camera around to catch the action.
e.zh: 他不得不转动摄像机以捕捉动作。

slug.t:
n. 鼻涕虫；子弹；一口烈酒
v. 猛击

e.en: A {slug} left a silvery trail across the garden path.
e.zh: 一只鼻涕虫在花园小径上留下了银色的痕迹。

e.en: He took a long {slug} of water after the workout.
e.zh: 锻炼后他大口地灌了一口水。

e.en: The boxing match turned into a brutal twelve-round {slugfest}.
e.zh: 那场拳击比赛变成了残酷的十二回合互殴。

e.en: Last night's baseball game was a high-scoring {slugfest}.
e.zh: 昨晚的棒球比赛是一场高分对轰大战。

e.en: Don't be a {sluggard} — get up and finish your homework!
e.zh: 别当懒虫了,起来把作业做完!

e.en: The old fable warns against becoming a lazy {sluggard}.
e.zh: 那则古老的寓言警告人们不要变成懒惰之人。

slugger.t: n. 强打者（棒球）；猛击者

e.en: The {slugger} hit three home runs in last night's game.
e.zh: 那位强打者在昨晚的比赛中打出了三支全垒打。

e.en: Coaches recruited the young {slugger} straight out of high school.
e.zh: 教练们直接从高中招募了那位年轻的强打者。

slugging.t:
v. 猛击
n. 棒球长打

e.en: His {slugging} percentage leads the entire league this season.
e.zh: 他的长打率本赛季在整个联盟中名列第一。

e.en: The boys were {slugging} each other in the schoolyard.
e.zh: 男孩们在操场上互相挥拳打闹。

e.en: My laptop has been really {sluggish} since the last update.
e.zh: 自从上次更新后我的笔记本电脑一直很卡。

e.en: Sales remained {sluggish} throughout the rainy summer months.
e.zh: 在多雨的夏季销售一直萎靡不振。

e.en: Traffic moved {sluggishly} through the flooded intersection.
e.zh: 车流缓慢地穿过被水淹的路口。

e.en: The app loads {sluggishly} on older Android phones.
e.zh: 这款应用在旧款安卓手机上加载得很慢。

e.en: Users complained about the {sluggishness} of the new website.
e.zh: 用户抱怨新网站的运行迟缓。

e.en: A heavy lunch often causes afternoon {sluggishness} at work.
e.zh: 丰盛的午餐常常导致下午工作时犯困乏力。

sluice.t:
n. 水闸
v. 冲洗

e.en: Workers opened the {sluice} to drain the flooded field.
e.zh: 工人们打开水闸排干被淹的田地。

e.en: Miners {sluice} gravel to separate tiny flakes of gold.
e.zh: 矿工们用水冲洗砂砾以分离出细小的金片。

e.en: The charity builds clean water systems in the city {slum}.
e.zh: 该慈善机构在城市贫民窟修建清洁供水系统。

e.en: He grew up in a {slum} but became a doctor.
e.zh: 他在贫民窟长大,后来成为了一名医生。

slumber.t:
n. 睡眠
v. 安睡

e.en: The baby fell into a deep {slumber} after her bath.
e.zh: 宝宝洗完澡后陷入了深沉的睡眠。

e.en: Don't disturb grandpa during his afternoon {slumber}.
e.zh: 爷爷午睡的时候别打扰他。

e.en: She tiptoed past the {slumbering} dog in the hallway.
e.zh: 她踮着脚尖走过走廊里熟睡的狗。

e.en: The volcano had been {slumbering} for over two centuries.
e.zh: 那座火山已经沉睡了两个多世纪。

slumlord.t: n. 出租贫民窟的黑心房东

e.en: Tenants sued the {slumlord} for refusing to fix the heating.
e.zh: 租户们起诉那个黑心房东拒绝修暖气。

e.en: The city finally cracked down on the notorious {slumlord}.
e.zh: 市政府终于严惩了那个臭名昭著的贫民窟房东。

slump.t:
v. 暴跌；瘫倒
n. 萧条

e.en: Tech stocks took a sharp {slump} last quarter.
e.zh: 科技股在上个季度大幅下跌。

e.en: He tends to {slump} in his chair while gaming.
e.zh: 他打游戏时总爱瘫坐在椅子上。

e.en: Sales have been {slumping} since the new competitor launched.
e.zh: 自从新竞争对手出现后销售一直在下滑。

e.en: She found him {slumping} forward asleep at his desk.
e.zh: 她发现他趴在桌子上睡着了。

slunk.t: v. slink 的过去式；偷偷溜走

e.en: The cat {slunk} away after knocking over the vase.
e.zh: 那只猫打翻花瓶后偷偷溜走了。

e.en: He {slunk} into the meeting twenty minutes late.
e.zh: 他迟到二十分钟才悄悄溜进会议室。

slur.t:
v. 含糊地说
n. 诋毁

e.en: The politician sued the newspaper for the racist {slur}.
e.zh: 那位政客就这一种族歧视言论起诉了报社。

e.en: After two drinks his words began to {slur}.
e.zh: 喝了两杯之后他说话开始含糊不清。

slurp.t:
v. 出声地吸食
n. 吸食声

e.en: In Japan it's polite to {slurp} your noodles loudly.
e.zh: 在日本大声吸溜面条是有礼貌的表现。

e.en: The toddler took a noisy {slurp} of his juice.
e.zh: 小宝宝大声地嘬了一口果汁。

slurpee.t: n. 思乐冰（冰沙饮料品牌）

e.en: Kids ran to 7-Eleven for a cherry {slurpee} after school.
e.zh: 孩子们放学后跑到7-Eleven去买樱桃味思乐冰。

e.en: Nothing beats a cold {slurpee} on a hot summer day.
e.zh: 炎热的夏日里没什么比一杯冰凉的思乐冰更爽了。

e.en: Stop {slurping} your soup; it's annoying everyone.
e.zh: 别再吸溜着喝汤了,大家都很烦。

e.en: The dog was happily {slurping} water from the bowl.
e.zh: 那只狗正开心地从碗里吧嗒吧嗒喝水。

e.en: His {slurred} speech made the officer suspect drunk driving.
e.zh: 他含混的口齿让警官怀疑他酒驾。

e.en: She {slurred} her words after the dental anesthesia.
e.zh: 打了牙科麻醉后她说话变得含糊不清。

e.en: He kept {slurring} his words during the late-night podcast.
e.zh: 他在深夜播客里一直说话含糊不清。

e.en: {Slurring} can be an early sign of a stroke.
e.zh: 言语含糊可能是中风的早期征兆。

e.en: Workers poured cement {slurry} into the foundation trenches.
e.zh: 工人们把水泥浆倒进地基沟里。

e.en: Whisk cornstarch with water to make a smooth {slurry}.
e.zh: 把玉米淀粉和水搅拌成顺滑的芡汁。

e.en: My boots got soaked walking through the gray {slush}.
e.zh: 走在灰乎乎的雪泥里我的靴子湿透了。

e.en: The kids loved the blue raspberry {slush} at the carnival.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢嘉年华上那杯蓝莓味的冰沙。

e.en: The streets turned {slushy} after the snow began to melt.
e.zh: 雪开始融化后街道变得泥泞不堪。

e.en: She ordered a strawberry {slushy} from the food truck.
e.zh: 她在餐车上点了一杯草莓冰沙。

e.en: Calling someone a {slut} online counts as harassment here.
e.zh: 在网上骂别人荡妇在这里算骚扰行为。

e.en: The film criticizes how society labels women as a {slut}.
e.zh: 这部电影批评了社会如何给女性贴上荡妇的标签。

slutty.t: adj. 风骚的；轻浮的（贬义）

e.en: She refused to wear what her friends called a {slutty} costume.
e.zh: 她拒绝穿朋友们口中那种暴露的服装。

e.en: The article challenges what makes clothing seem {slutty}.
e.zh: 这篇文章质疑了什么样的衣着会显得风骚。

e.en: He {slyly} slipped the note into her textbook.
e.zh: 他偷偷地把纸条塞进了她的课本里。

e.en: She {slyly} smiled when nobody guessed her secret.
e.zh: 没人猜出她的秘密时她狡黠地笑了笑。

e.en: His {slyness} helped him win every game of poker.
e.zh: 他的狡猾让他在每一局扑克中都能取胜。

e.en: The fox is famous in folktales for its {slyness}.
e.zh: 狐狸在民间故事中以狡猾闻名。

smack.t:
v. 拍打；用力打
n. 响亮一击

e.en: Mom gave him a gentle {smack} on the wrist.
e.zh: 妈妈轻轻拍了一下他的手腕。

e.en: The restaurant sits {smack} in the middle of downtown.
e.zh: 那家餐厅就坐落在市中心正中央。

smacker.t: n. 响亮的吻；（俚）一块钱

e.en: Grandma gave the baby a big {smacker} on the cheek.
e.zh: 奶奶在宝宝脸蛋上响亮地亲了一口。

e.en: That used car cost me twenty thousand {smacker}s.
e.zh: 那辆二手车花了我两万大洋。

smacking.t:
v. 拍打
adj. 强劲的

e.en: Many countries have banned {smacking} children as discipline.
e.zh: 许多国家已禁止用打屁股的方式管教孩子。

e.en: He kept {smacking} his lips while eating the ribs.
e.zh: 他啃排骨时不停地咂嘴。

e.en: We rented a {small} cabin near the lake last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末我们在湖边租了一间小木屋。

e.en: Don't sweat the {small} stuff; focus on what matters.
e.zh: 别为小事烦恼,专注于重要的事情。

smallholder.t: n. 小土地持有者；小农

e.en: Most coffee in Ethiopia is grown by a {smallholder} farmer.
e.zh: 埃塞俄比亚大部分咖啡都由小农户种植。

e.en: The program offers loans to every registered {smallholder}.
e.zh: 该项目为每一位登记在册的小农户提供贷款。

e.en: They retired and bought a {smallholding} in rural Wales.
e.zh: 他们退休后在威尔士乡下买了一块小农场。

e.en: Her {smallholding} produces eggs, honey, and seasonal vegetables.
e.zh: 她的小农场出产鸡蛋、蜂蜜和时令蔬菜。

e.en: We rented a {smallish} apartment near the subway station.
e.zh: 我们在地铁站附近租了一间不算大的公寓。

e.en: The cafe has a {smallish} menu but everything is delicious.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆菜单不算多,但样样都很好吃。

e.en: He caught a five-pound {smallmouth} bass on Lake Erie.
e.zh: 他在伊利湖钓到一条五磅重的小口鲈鱼。

e.en: {Smallmouth} bass prefer cooler, rocky lake waters.
e.zh: 小口鲈鱼喜欢生活在较凉、多岩石的湖水中。

e.en: The {smallness} of the apartment surprised the new tenants.
e.zh: 这套公寓之小让新租户感到吃惊。

e.en: Standing on the mountain, she felt her own {smallness}.
e.zh: 站在山顶,她感到了自己的渺小。

e.en: Vaccination programs eradicated {smallpox} from the world by 1980.
e.zh: 疫苗接种项目在1980年前从世界上根除了天花。

e.en: Historians blame {smallpox} for devastating Indigenous American populations.
e.zh: 史学家认为天花对美洲原住民人口造成了毁灭性打击。

smarmy.t: adj. 油腔滑调的；谄媚的

e.en: The {smarmy} salesman kept calling me his best friend.
e.zh: 那个油腔滑调的推销员一直叫我他最好的朋友。

e.en: I can't stand his {smarmy} compliments at every meeting.
e.zh: 我受不了他每次开会都那种谄媚的恭维。

smart.t:
adj. 聪明的；智能的
v. 刺痛

e.en: Buying that index fund was a really {smart} move.
e.zh: 买那只指数基金是个非常明智的决定。

e.en: My new {smart} watch tracks sleep and heart rate automatically.
e.zh: 我新买的智能手表能自动监测睡眠和心率。

e.en: You should {smarten} up before the job interview.
e.zh: 面试前你该把自己收拾精神点。

e.en: A fresh coat of paint will {smarten} the room.
e.zh: 刷一层新漆会让房间显得更精致。

e.en: He was dressed {smartly} for the client meeting.
e.zh: 他为见客户穿得很得体精神。

e.en: She {smartly} negotiated a higher salary on day one.
e.zh: 她第一天就机智地谈下了更高的薪水。

e.en: I admire the {smartness} of her design choices.
e.zh: 我很欣赏她设计选择中的那份巧思。

e.en: The suit gave him an air of {smartness}.
e.zh: 那套西装让他显得很精明利落。

e.en: My {smartphone} battery dies by mid-afternoon.
e.zh: 我的智能手机电池下午就没电了。

e.en: She bought her first {smartphone} at age sixty.
e.zh: 她六十岁才买了第一部智能手机。

e.en: Most teenagers check their {smartphones} hundreds of times daily.
e.zh: 大多数青少年每天看手机几百次。

e.en: Modern {smartphones} can replace cameras and wallets entirely.
e.zh: 现代智能手机已能完全取代相机和钱包。

e.en: It takes real {smarts} to negotiate a deal like that.
e.zh: 谈成那样的交易需要真本事。

e.en: Street {smarts} matter more than grades in this job.
e.zh: 在这份工作里,街头智慧比成绩更重要。

e.en: Okay, {smarty}, you tell me how to fix it.
e.zh: 行啊,小聪明,那你说怎么修。

e.en: Don't be such a {smarty} in front of guests.
e.zh: 在客人面前别这么自作聪明。

smash.t:
v. 打碎；猛击
n. 重击；轰动之作

e.en: Be careful not to {smash} the glass vase.
e.zh: 小心别把玻璃花瓶砸碎了。

e.en: The new song became an instant {smash} on TikTok.
e.zh: 这首新歌在TikTok上瞬间爆红。

e.en: He {smashed} the window with a hammer by accident.
e.zh: 他不小心用锤子把窗户砸碎了。

e.en: Our team {smashed} the previous sales record last quarter.
e.zh: 我们团队上季度打破了之前的销售记录。

smasher.t: n. 粉碎者；了不起的人或物

e.en: That new song is a real {smasher} on the charts.
e.zh: 那首新歌在排行榜上大获成功。

e.en: He bought a tile {smasher} for the renovation project.
e.zh: 他为装修项目买了一把碎砖锤。

smashes.t: v. 打碎（smash 的第三人称单数）

e.en: She always {smashes} her serve in the final set.
e.zh: 她在决胜盘里总能扣杀发球。

e.en: The film {smashes} box office records every weekend.
e.zh: 这部电影每个周末都打破票房纪录。

smashing.t:
adj. 极好的；了不起的
v. 打碎（smash 的 ing）

e.en: You look absolutely {smashing} in that new dress.
e.zh: 你穿那件新裙子真是美极了。

e.en: The kids kept {smashing} their toys against the wall.
e.zh: 孩子们不停地把玩具往墙上砸。

e.en: She speaks a {smattering} of Japanese from her travels.
e.zh: 她会一点点日语,是旅行时学的。

e.en: Only a {smattering} of fans showed up for the rainy game.
e.zh: 雨天只有零星几个球迷来看比赛。

smatterings.t: n. 略知；些许（smattering 的复数）

e.en: He picked up {smatterings} of French and Spanish abroad.
e.zh: 他在国外学到一点法语和西班牙语皮毛。

e.en: The report contains {smatterings} of useful data hidden inside.
e.zh: 报告里夹杂着一些零星的有用数据。

smear.t:
v. 涂抹；玷污
n. 污迹；诽谤

e.en: There's a {smear} of jam on your shirt.
e.zh: 你衬衫上有一抹果酱印。

e.en: The article was a clear {smear} against the candidate.
e.zh: 那篇文章明显是对候选人的抹黑。

smeared.t: adj. 被涂抹的；被玷污的

e.en: The toddler {smeared} chocolate all over the couch.
e.zh: 小孩把巧克力涂得沙发到处都是。

e.en: Critics {smeared} the author with baseless accusations online.
e.zh: 批评者在网上用毫无根据的指控诋毁作者。

smearing.t: v. 涂抹；诋毁（smear 的 ing）

e.en: Stop {smearing} sunscreen on the screen of your phone.
e.zh: 别再把防晒霜涂到手机屏幕上了。

e.en: The campaign was accused of {smearing} its rivals.
e.zh: 该竞选团队被指控抹黑对手。

e.en: The window was {smeary} after the rain dried.
e.zh: 雨干之后窗户上留下一道道污痕。

e.en: Her glasses looked {smeary} from constant fingerprint smudges.
e.zh: 她的眼镜因指纹污渍看起来油糊糊的。

smell.t:
n. 气味；嗅觉
v. 闻；散发气味

e.en: I can {smell} fresh coffee from the kitchen.
e.zh: 我能闻到厨房飘来的新鲜咖啡香。

e.en: There's a strange {smell} coming from the fridge.
e.zh: 冰箱里传出一股奇怪的味道。

smelling.t: v. 闻（smell 的 ing 形式）

e.en: The dog kept {smelling} the suspicious package on the porch.
e.zh: 狗一直在闻门廊上那个可疑的包裹。

e.en: The bakery was {smelling} amazing on Sunday morning.
e.zh: 周日早晨面包店里香气四溢。

smells.t:
n. 气味（复数）
v. 闻（第三人称单数）

e.en: This soap {smells} like fresh lavender.
e.zh: 这块肥皂闻起来像新鲜的薰衣草。

e.en: The kitchen {smells} wonderful when she bakes bread.
e.zh: 她烤面包时厨房闻起来特别香。

e.en: Take off those {smelly} socks before coming inside.
e.zh: 进屋前先把那双臭袜子脱掉。

e.en: The gym locker room gets really {smelly} by evening.
e.zh: 健身房更衣室到傍晚就变得很臭。

smelt.t:
v. 熔炼（金属）
n. 胡瓜鱼

e.en: The factory used to {smelt} iron ore here.
e.zh: 这家工厂以前在这里冶炼铁矿石。

e.en: We caught a bucket of {smelt} at the lake.
e.zh: 我们在湖边钓到一桶胡瓜鱼。

e.en: The old copper {smelter} closed down last year.
e.zh: 那家旧铜冶炼厂去年关闭了。

e.en: Workers at the {smelter} wear heavy protective gear.
e.zh: 冶炼厂的工人都穿着厚重的防护装备。

e.en: Aluminum {smelting} requires enormous amounts of electricity.
e.zh: 铝的冶炼需要消耗巨大的电力。

e.en: The town's economy depended on {smelting} for decades.
e.zh: 这座城镇的经济几十年来都依赖冶炼业。

smetana.t: n. 斯美塔那（捷克作曲家）

e.en: Add a spoonful of {smetana} to the borscht before serving.
e.zh: 上桌前往罗宋汤里加一勺酸奶油。

e.en: Russian dumplings taste better with cold {smetana} on top.
e.zh: 俄式饺子上面浇点冰酸奶油更好吃。

smethwick.t: n. 斯梅西克（英国地名）

e.en: She grew up in {Smethwick}, near Birmingham.
e.zh: 她在伯明翰附近的斯梅西克长大。

e.en: The train stops at {Smethwick} on its way north.
e.zh: 这趟火车北上途中会停靠斯梅西克。

e.en: Add just a {smidgen} of salt to the sauce.
e.zh: 酱料里只需加一丁点盐。

e.en: There's not even a {smidgen} of evidence to support that claim.
e.zh: 没有一丁点证据能支持这个说法。

smile.t:
v. 微笑
n. 微笑

e.en: Her warm {smile} made everyone feel welcome.
e.zh: 她温暖的微笑让每个人都感到亲切。

e.en: Try to {smile} for the camera, please.
e.zh: 请对着镜头笑一下。

smiled.t: v. 微笑（smile 的过去式）

e.en: She {smiled} when she saw the surprise gift.
e.zh: 她看到惊喜礼物时露出了微笑。

e.en: The teacher {smiled} kindly at the nervous student.
e.zh: 老师对紧张的学生友善地笑了笑。

e.en: He's a natural {smiler}, always cheerful at meetings.
e.zh: 他天生爱笑,开会时总是很开朗。

e.en: The baby is a real {smiler} around strangers.
e.zh: 这宝宝见到陌生人也总是笑眯眯的。

smiles.t:
n. 微笑（复数）
v. 微笑（第三人称单数）

e.en: She {smiles} every time her dog runs to greet her.
e.zh: 每次狗跑来迎接她,她都会微笑。

e.en: His genuine {smiles} brighten up the whole office.
e.zh: 他真诚的笑容照亮了整个办公室。

smiley.t:
n. 笑脸符号
adj. 笑嘻嘻的

e.en: She added a {smiley} to the end of her text.
e.zh: 她在短信末尾加了个笑脸表情。

e.en: The waiter was a {smiley}, friendly young man.
e.zh: 那位服务员是个爱笑、友善的年轻人。

smiling.t:
adj. 微笑的
v. 微笑（smile 的 ing）

e.en: The {smiling} child waved at the strangers.
e.zh: 那个笑着的孩子向陌生人挥了挥手。

e.en: She kept {smiling} throughout the long ceremony.
e.zh: 整个漫长的典礼中她都一直微笑着。

e.en: He {smilingly} accepted the award from the mayor.
e.zh: 他微笑着从市长手中接过了奖项。

e.en: She {smilingly} declined the third helping of dessert.
e.zh: 她笑着婉拒了第三份甜点。

smirch.t:
v. 弄脏；玷污
n. 污点

e.en: The scandal left a {smirch} on his career.
e.zh: 这桩丑闻给他的职业生涯留下了污点。

e.en: Don't let one mistake {smirch} your good reputation.
e.zh: 别让一个错误玷污了你的好名声。

smirk.t:
v. 得意地笑；傻笑
n. 假笑

e.en: He had a smug {smirk} after winning the bet.
e.zh: 赢了赌注后他露出一脸得意的坏笑。

e.en: Wipe that {smirk} off your face right now.
e.zh: 立刻把脸上那种得意的笑收起来。

smirking.t: v. 得意笑；假笑（smirk 的 ing）

e.en: Stop {smirking} and tell me what you did.
e.zh: 别在那儿坏笑了,告诉我你做了什么。

e.en: The {smirking} villain finally got what he deserved.
e.zh: 那个奸笑的反派终于得到了应有的惩罚。

e.en: His {smirky} comment annoyed everyone in the meeting.
e.zh: 他那带着坏笑的评论惹恼了会上所有人。

e.en: She gave him a {smirky} look across the room.
e.zh: 她隔着房间对他露出一个揶揄的笑。

e.en: The hero swore to {smite} the dragon in battle.
e.zh: 那位英雄发誓要在战斗中击败巨龙。

e.en: Ancient legends say the gods would {smite} the wicked.
e.zh: 古老传说称众神会惩罚邪恶之人。

e.en: The village {smith} forged horseshoes by the river.
e.zh: 村里的铁匠在河边打制马蹄铁。

e.en: Her grandfather worked as a {smith} for forty years.
e.zh: 她外祖父当了四十年的铁匠。

smithereen.t: n. 碎片（多用复数 smithereens）

e.en: Not a single {smithereen} of the vase was left.
e.zh: 花瓶碎得连一小块儿都没剩下。

e.en: He couldn't find one {smithereen} of evidence at the scene.
e.zh: 他在现场连一丁点儿证据都找不到。

smiths.t: n. 铁匠（复数）；史密斯一家

e.en: The village had three {smiths} working in the same forge.
e.zh: 村里有三位铁匠在同一家铁匠铺工作。

e.en: Modern {smiths} mostly create custom knives and decorative ironwork.
e.zh: 现代铁匠主要打造定制刀具和装饰铁艺。

e.en: We spent the whole day at the {Smithsonian} museums.
e.zh: 我们在史密森尼博物馆群里逛了一整天。

e.en: The artifact was donated to the {Smithsonian} last spring.
e.zh: 那件文物去年春天捐赠给了史密森尼学会。

e.en: Sparks flew from the old {smithy} at the village edge.
e.zh: 村边那间老铁匠铺里火花四溅。

e.en: He learned the trade in his father's small {smithy}.
e.zh: 他在父亲的小铁匠铺里学到了这门手艺。

smock.t: n. 工作罩衫；宽松外衣

e.en: The artist wore a paint-stained {smock} in the studio.
e.zh: 那位艺术家在工作室里穿着沾满颜料的罩衫。

e.en: Each child was given a colorful {smock} for art class.
e.zh: 每个孩子上美术课时都领到一件彩色罩衫。

e.en: Thick {smog} blanketed the city for days.
e.zh: 浓厚的雾霾笼罩了这座城市好几天。

e.en: The {smog} alert warned residents to stay indoors.
e.zh: 雾霾警报提醒居民待在室内。

e.en: It was too {smoggy} to see the mountains today.
e.zh: 今天雾霾太重,看不到山脉了。

e.en: Beijing winters used to be famously {smoggy}.
e.zh: 北京的冬天曾以雾霾严重而闻名。

smoke.t:
n. 烟；烟雾
v. 抽烟；冒烟

e.en: Thick {smoke} poured out of the burning building.
e.zh: 燃烧的大楼里冒出滚滚浓烟。

e.en: My doctor told me to stop {smoke} immediately.
e.zh: 医生让我立刻戒烟。

smoked.t:
adj. 熏制的
v. 抽烟（过去式）

e.en: I ordered a bagel with {smoked} salmon and cream cheese.
e.zh: 我点了一个加熏三文鱼和奶油芝士的贝果。

e.en: He {smoked} cigarettes for twenty years before quitting.
e.zh: 他抽了二十年烟才戒掉。

e.en: Grandpa cured bacon in his backyard {smokehouse}.
e.zh: 爷爷在后院的熏肉房里腌制培根。

e.en: The {smokehouse} fills the air with hickory aroma.
e.zh: 那间熏制房让空气中弥漫着山核桃木的香气。

e.en: She trained for two years to become a {smokejumper}.
e.zh: 她训练了两年才成为一名空降消防员。

e.en: A {smokejumper} parachuted into the burning forest at dawn.
e.zh: 一名空降消防员黎明时跳伞进入燃烧的森林。

e.en: The new grill burns clean and is virtually {smokeless}.
e.zh: 这款新烤炉燃烧干净,几乎无烟。

e.en: Many cities promote {smokeless} fuel for home heating.
e.zh: 许多城市推广无烟燃料用于家庭取暖。

e.en: He was a heavy {smoker} for over twenty years.
e.zh: 他是个有二十多年烟瘾的老烟民。

e.en: I bought a backyard {smoker} to make brisket.
e.zh: 我买了个后院烟熏炉来做牛胸肉。

e.en: {Smokers} must use the designated area outside.
e.zh: 吸烟者必须使用外面指定的区域。

e.en: Insurance premiums are higher for {smokers}.
e.zh: 吸烟者的保险费会更高。

smokes.t:
v. 抽烟（第三人称单数）
n. 香烟（复数）

e.en: He {smokes} a pack of cigarettes a day.
e.zh: 他每天抽一包烟。

e.en: The chimney {smokes} whenever the wind shifts.
e.zh: 风一变向,那个烟囱就冒烟。

e.en: The press release was just a {smokescreen} for layoffs.
e.zh: 那份新闻稿不过是裁员的烟幕弹。

e.en: Tanks released a {smokescreen} to cover their retreat.
e.zh: 坦克释放烟幕掩护撤退。

e.en: A tall {smokestack} towered over the old factory.
e.zh: 一根高大的烟囱矗立在旧工厂上方。

e.en: The {smokestack} belched gray smoke all morning.
e.zh: 那烟囱整个上午都在冒着灰烟。

e.en: Rusting {smokestacks} marked the abandoned steel mill.
e.zh: 锈迹斑斑的烟囱标示着废弃的钢铁厂。

e.en: The city banned coal {smokestacks} in residential zones.
e.zh: 该市禁止住宅区内设置燃煤烟囱。

e.en: The bar had a warm, {smokey} atmosphere.
e.zh: 那家酒吧有种温暖的烟熏气氛。

e.en: She loves whisky with a {smokey} finish.
e.zh: 她喜欢带烟熏尾韵的威士忌。

e.en: The {smokiness} of the barbecue filled the yard.
e.zh: 烧烤的烟熏味弥漫了整个院子。

e.en: I love the {smokiness} this scotch has.
e.zh: 我喜欢这款苏格兰威士忌的烟熏气息。

smoking.t:
n. 吸烟
adj. 冒烟的

e.en: {Smoking} is banned in all indoor restaurants here.
e.zh: 这里所有室内餐厅都禁止吸烟。

e.en: A {smoking} pan filled the kitchen with haze.
e.zh: 冒烟的平底锅让厨房充满烟雾。

smoky.t: adj. 烟雾弥漫的；有烟熏味的

e.en: Her voice has a low, {smoky} quality.
e.zh: 她的嗓音低沉而带着烟熏感。

e.en: The cabin was {smoky} from the wood stove.
e.zh: 小屋因柴炉而烟雾弥漫。

e.en: Embers continued to {smolder} long after the fire died.
e.zh: 火熄灭后余烬仍在闷烧很久。

e.en: Resentment began to {smolder} between the two coworkers.
e.zh: 两位同事之间开始暗暗滋生怨恨。

e.en: Firefighters watched the {smoldering} ruins until dawn.
e.zh: 消防员一直守着闷烧的废墟到天亮。

e.en: She gave him a {smoldering} look across the room.
e.zh: 她隔着房间给了他一个炽热的眼神。

smolensk.t: n. 斯摩棱斯克（俄罗斯城市）

e.en: He grew up in {Smolensk}, a city in western Russia.
e.zh: 他在俄罗斯西部的斯摩棱斯克长大。

e.en: The train from Moscow to {Smolensk} took six hours.
e.zh: 从莫斯科到斯摩棱斯克的火车走了六个小时。

e.en: Each {smolt} swims downstream toward the open sea.
e.zh: 每条银鳞鲑都顺流游向开阔的大海。

e.en: Researchers tagged the young {smolt} before release.
e.zh: 研究人员在放流前给幼鲑做了标记。

e.en: He gave his grandma a quick {smooch} on the cheek.
e.zh: 他在奶奶脸颊上飞快地亲了一下。

e.en: The couple stopped to {smooch} under the streetlight.
e.zh: 那对情侣在路灯下停下来亲热了一会儿。

e.en: The movie got a bit too {smoochy} for the kids.
e.zh: 那部电影对孩子来说有点太腻歪了。

e.en: They sent {smoochy} texts to each other all day.
e.zh: 他们一整天互相发着甜腻的短信。

smooth.t:
adj. 平滑的；顺畅的
v. 使光滑

e.en: This lotion makes my skin feel really {smooth}.
e.zh: 这款乳液让我的皮肤摸起来非常光滑。
