e.en: The transition to the new system was surprisingly {smooth}.
e.zh: 切换到新系统的过程出乎意料地顺利。

e.en: Tank crews reload the {smoothbore} cannon in seconds.
e.zh: 坦克兵能在几秒内为滑膛炮重新装弹。

e.en: He collects antique {smoothbore} muskets from the 1700s.
e.zh: 他收藏十八世纪的古董滑膛火枪。

smoothed.t: v. 使光滑；理顺（过去式）

e.en: She {smoothed} the wrinkles out of her dress.
e.zh: 她把裙子上的皱褶抚平。

e.en: The mediator {smoothed} tensions between the two teams.
e.zh: 调解人化解了两队之间的紧张关系。

e.en: I blend a banana {smoothie} every morning before work.
e.zh: 我每天上班前都打一杯香蕉奶昔。

e.en: This cafe sells the best mango {smoothie} in town.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆卖全城最好喝的芒果思慕雪。

smoothing.t:
n. 平滑；抚平
v. 使光滑（现分）

e.en: The chart applies {smoothing} to reduce daily noise.
e.zh: 该图表使用平滑处理来降低日波动噪声。

e.en: He kept {smoothing} his tie before the interview.
e.zh: 面试前他不停地抚平自己的领带。

e.en: The meeting ran {smoothly} from start to finish.
e.zh: 会议从头到尾都进行得很顺利。

e.en: The car shifts gears {smoothly} at any speed.
e.zh: 这辆车在任何速度下换挡都很平顺。

e.en: I was impressed by the {smoothness} of the deployment.
e.zh: 我对这次部署的顺畅程度印象深刻。

e.en: She admired the {smoothness} of the marble countertop.
e.zh: 她欣赏那张大理石台面的光滑质感。

e.en: Don't trust that {smoothy} — he flatters everyone.
e.zh: 别信那个圆滑的家伙,他对谁都甜言蜜语。

e.en: The salesman was a real {smoothy} on the phone.
e.zh: 那个推销员在电话里真是个油嘴滑舌的家伙。

smorgasbord.t: n. 瑞典式自助餐；大杂烩

e.en: The festival offered a {smorgasbord} of street food.
e.zh: 那个节日提供了琳琅满目的街头美食。

e.en: Netflix has a {smorgasbord} of holiday romance films.
e.zh: Netflix上有一大堆节日爱情片任你挑选。

e.en: Don't {smother} the kids with too many rules.
e.zh: 别用太多规矩把孩子管得喘不过气。

e.en: Use a wet blanket to {smother} a small grease fire.
e.zh: 用湿毯子可以扑灭小型油锅起火。

smothered.t: v. 使窒息；压制（过去式）

e.en: She {smothered} her pancakes in maple syrup.
e.zh: 她在松饼上浇满了枫糖浆。

e.en: The fire was {smothered} before it spread.
e.zh: 那场火在蔓延之前就被扑灭了。

smothering.t: adj. 令人窒息的；压抑的

e.en: His {smothering} attention started to push her away.
e.zh: 他那种令人窒息的关心开始把她推远。

e.en: A {smothering} blanket of fog covered the valley.
e.zh: 一层厚重的雾笼罩着山谷。

e.en: The campfire continued to {smoulder} through the night.
e.zh: 营火整夜都在缓缓燃烧着。

e.en: Old grievances {smoulder} just below the surface.
e.zh: 陈年旧怨在表面之下暗暗酝酿。

e.en: Only {smouldering} ashes remained the next morning.
e.zh: 第二天早上只剩下闷烧的灰烬。

e.en: His {smouldering} anger finally exploded at the meeting.
e.zh: 他压抑已久的怒火终于在会上爆发。

smudge.t:
n. 污渍
v. 弄脏；涂污

e.en: There's a {smudge} of ink on your sleeve.
e.zh: 你袖子上有一块墨迹污痕。

e.en: Try not to {smudge} the wet paint on the wall.
e.zh: 别把墙上还没干的漆蹭花了。

smudged.t:
adj. 有污迹的
v. 弄脏（过去式）

e.en: Her mascara had {smudged} after the long flight.
e.zh: 长途飞行后她的睫毛膏已经晕开了。

e.en: The toddler {smudged} the window with sticky fingers.
e.zh: 小朋友用黏糊糊的手指把窗户弄脏了。

smudgy.t: adj. 脏兮兮的；有污迹的

e.en: The photocopy came out faint and {smudgy}.
e.zh: 复印件出来又模糊又花。

e.en: He cleaned the {smudgy} glasses with a soft cloth.
e.zh: 他用软布擦干净了那副脏污的眼镜。

smug.t: adj. 自满的；沾沾自喜的

e.en: She wore a {smug} smile after winning the bet.
e.zh: 赢了赌局之后她带着一脸得意的笑。

e.en: His {smug} tone irritated everyone in the meeting.
e.zh: 他那副自鸣得意的语气惹恼了会上所有人。

e.en: They tried to {smuggle} phones into the prison.
e.zh: 他们试图把手机偷运进监狱。

e.en: I always {smuggle} snacks into the movie theater.
e.zh: 我总是偷偷把零食带进电影院。

e.en: Customs found rare birds {smuggled} in his luggage.
e.zh: 海关在他行李里发现了走私的珍稀鸟类。

e.en: She {smuggled} a puppy home in her jacket.
e.zh: 她把一只小狗藏在外套里偷偷带回了家。

e.en: The {smuggler} was caught at the border with cash.
e.zh: 那个走私犯在边境带着现金被抓获。

e.en: A diamond {smuggler} hid stones inside chocolate bars.
e.zh: 一名钻石走私者把宝石藏在巧克力棒里。

e.en: He was arrested for {smuggling} cigarettes across the border.
e.zh: 他因跨境走私香烟被捕。

e.en: Online {smuggling} of counterfeit goods has surged lately.
e.zh: 近期网络走私假货案件激增。

e.en: He {smugly} announced he had finished first.
e.zh: 他得意洋洋地宣布自己第一个完成了。

e.en: She smiled {smugly} when her prediction came true.
e.zh: 她的预言应验时,她得意地笑了。

e.en: His {smugness} made the loss feel even sweeter.
e.zh: 他的自鸣得意让这场失败更显大快人心。

e.en: There was a quiet {smugness} in her reply.
e.zh: 她的回答里透着一丝不动声色的自满。

smut.t: n. 淫秽内容；煤灰污迹

e.en: The magazine got banned for printing {smut}.
e.zh: 那本杂志因刊登低俗内容被禁了。

e.en: Black {smut} infected most of the wheat field.
e.zh: 黑穗病感染了大部分麦田。

e.en: He told a {smutty} joke that nobody laughed at.
e.zh: 他讲了个下流的笑话,没人笑。

e.en: The novel was full of {smutty} dialogue.
e.zh: 那本小说里满是低俗的对白。

smyrna.t: n. 士麦那（今伊兹密尔）

e.en: Ancient {Smyrna} is now the city of Izmir, Turkey.
e.zh: 古老的士麦那就是今天土耳其的伊兹密尔。

e.en: She bought a hand-knotted {Smyrna} rug at the bazaar.
e.zh: 她在集市上买了一块手工打结的士麦那地毯。

snack.t:
n. 零食
v. 吃零食

e.en: I usually grab a {snack} between meetings.
e.zh: 我通常会在会议间隙抓点零食吃。

e.en: This protein bar is my favorite afternoon {snack}.
e.zh: 这款蛋白棒是我最爱的下午零食。

e.en: The pantry is fully stocked with healthy {snacks}.
e.zh: 储物柜里塞满了健康零食。

e.en: Don't forget to bring {snacks} for the road trip.
e.zh: 别忘了带些零食路上吃。

snaffle.t:
n. 马嚼子
v. 顺走，偷拿

e.en: Try to {snaffle} a few cookies before they're all gone.
e.zh: 趁饼干还没被吃光,赶紧抢几块。

e.en: She managed to {snaffle} the last seat on the train.
e.zh: 她抢到了火车上最后一个座位。

e.en: A scheduling {snafu} delayed the entire conference.
e.zh: 日程安排上的混乱让整个会议都延期了。

e.en: The launch hit a major {snafu} at the last minute.
e.zh: 发布会在最后一刻遇上了大乱子。

snag.t:
n. 意外障碍
v. 钩住；抢到

e.en: We hit a small {snag} with the visa application.
e.zh: 我们的签证申请遇到了一点小麻烦。

e.en: Try to {snag} a good seat before the show starts.
e.zh: 演出开始前赶紧抢个好位子。

snagged.t: v. 被钩住；抢到了（snag 过去式）

e.en: She {snagged} the last pair of shoes on sale.
e.zh: 她抢到了最后一双打折的鞋。

e.en: My sweater {snagged} on a nail by the door.
e.zh: 我的毛衣被门边的钉子勾住了。

e.en: A tiny {snail} crawled slowly across the leaf.
e.zh: 一只小蜗牛慢慢地爬过叶子。

e.en: The internet here moves at a {snail}'s pace.
e.zh: 这里的网速慢得像蜗牛。

e.en: French restaurants often serve {snails} with garlic butter.
e.zh: 法国餐厅常用蒜蓉黄油烹制蜗牛。

e.en: The garden was overrun with {snails} after the rain.
e.zh: 雨后花园里到处都是蜗牛。

snake.t:
n. 蛇
v. 蜿蜒前行

e.en: A small green {snake} slithered into the bushes.
e.zh: 一条小绿蛇溜进了灌木丛。

e.en: The hiking trail began to {snake} up the mountain.
e.zh: 登山小径开始沿着山势蜿蜒而上。

e.en: Hikers should know basic first aid for a {snakebite}.
e.zh: 登山者应了解蛇咬伤的基本急救知识。

e.en: The hospital keeps antivenom ready for any {snakebite} emergency.
e.zh: 医院备有抗蛇毒血清以应对蛇咬伤紧急情况。

snakehead.t: n. 乌鳢；（偷渡组织者）蛇头

e.en: The {snakehead} fish has invaded several lakes in Maryland.
e.zh: 乌鳢入侵了马里兰州的几个湖泊。

e.en: A {snakehead} smuggler was arrested at the border last week.
e.zh: 上周一名蛇头在边境被捕。

e.en: Most {snakes} in this region are completely harmless to humans.
e.zh: 这个地区的大多数蛇对人类完全无害。

e.en: The hiking trail {snakes} through dense pine forest.
e.zh: 这条登山小道蜿蜒穿过茂密的松林。

e.en: She bought a {snakeskin} handbag at the vintage market.
e.zh: 她在复古市场买了一个蛇皮手提包。

e.en: The cowboy wore expensive {snakeskin} boots to the dance.
e.zh: 那位牛仔穿着昂贵的蛇皮靴去跳舞。

snaking.t:
v. 蜿蜒延伸
adj. 曲折的

e.en: A long line was {snaking} around the concert venue.
e.zh: 长长的队伍蜿蜒地绕着音乐会场地排开。

e.en: The river kept {snaking} through the valley below us.
e.zh: 河流在我们下方的山谷中蜿蜒流淌。

e.en: The road takes a {snaky} path up the mountainside.
e.zh: 这条路沿着山坡蜿蜒而上。

e.en: Her {snaky} smile made everyone feel uneasy.
e.zh: 她那阴险的笑容让每个人都感到不安。

snap.t:
v. 啪地折断；拍照
n. 快照

e.en: Don't {snap} at me just because you had a bad day.
e.zh: 不要因为你今天不顺心就对我发火。

e.en: I'll {snap} a quick photo before we leave the park.
e.zh: 我们离开公园前我会快速拍张照片。

e.en: The {snapdragon} flowers add bright color to her garden.
e.zh: 金鱼草为她的花园增添了鲜艳的色彩。

e.en: Children love squeezing the {snapdragon} blossoms to make them open.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢捏金鱼草花让它们张开。

snape.t: n. 斯内普（《哈利·波特》人物名）

e.en: Professor {Snape} is one of the most complex characters in Harry Potter.
e.zh: 斯内普教授是《哈利·波特》中最复杂的角色之一。

e.en: Many fans cried when {Snape}'s true loyalty was finally revealed.
e.zh: 当斯内普真正的忠诚被揭示时,许多粉丝都哭了。

snapped.t: v. 啪地断了；拍了照（snap 过去式）

e.en: The branch {snapped} under the weight of the heavy snow.
e.zh: 树枝在厚重积雪的重压下折断了。

e.en: She finally {snapped} after months of unfair treatment at work.
e.zh: 经过几个月不公平的对待后,她终于爆发了。

e.en: We grilled fresh {snapper} with lemon and herbs for dinner.
e.zh: 我们用柠檬和香草烤了新鲜的鲷鱼当晚餐。

e.en: The {snapper} caught the football and ran for a touchdown.
e.zh: 那名中锋接到橄榄球后跑去达阵得分。

e.en: He answered the reporter's question {snappily} and walked away.
e.zh: 他没好气地回答了记者的问题就走开了。

e.en: She dressed {snappily} for the important business meeting.
e.zh: 她为重要的商务会议穿得十分时髦。

e.en: Stop {snapping} at the kids; they're just being curious.
e.zh: 别对孩子们厉声呵斥,他们只是好奇而已。

e.en: Tourists were {snapping} pictures of the famous landmark.
e.zh: 游客们正在拍摄那个著名地标的照片。

e.en: He becomes {snappish} when he hasn't had enough sleep.
e.zh: 他睡眠不足时会变得脾气暴躁。

e.en: Her {snappish} reply surprised everyone in the meeting.
e.zh: 她尖刻的回答让会议上的所有人都感到惊讶。

e.en: The advertisement uses a {snappy} slogan to grab attention.
e.zh: 这则广告用一句简洁有力的口号来吸引注意。

e.en: Make it {snappy} — we're already running late.
e.zh: 快一点,我们已经迟到了。

snaps.t:
n. 快照（复数）
v. 啪地断

e.en: He always {snaps} at his coworkers when deadlines approach.
e.zh: 截止日期临近时他总会对同事发火。

e.en: She took several {snaps} of the sunset at the beach.
e.zh: 她在海滩上拍了好几张日落的快照。

snapshot.t: n. 快照；（数据）瞬时状态

e.en: This report gives a {snapshot} of the company's current finances.
e.zh: 这份报告概览了公司当前的财务状况。

e.en: I found an old {snapshot} of my grandparents in the album.
e.zh: 我在相册里找到一张祖父母的老照片。

snare.t:
n. 陷阱；小军鼓
v. 诱捕

e.en: The hunter set a {snare} to catch rabbits in the woods.
e.zh: 猎人在树林里设了一个陷阱来抓兔子。

e.en: The drummer hit the {snare} with perfect timing throughout the song.
e.zh: 鼓手在整首歌中精准地敲击着小军鼓。

e.en: Her {snarky} comments on social media often go viral online.
e.zh: 她在社交媒体上尖酸的评论经常在网上爆红。

e.en: He made a {snarky} remark about my outfit at the party.
e.zh: 他在派对上对我的着装做了个讽刺的评论。

snarl.t:
v. 咆哮；缠结
n. 怒吼

e.en: The dog let out a low {snarl} at the stranger.
e.zh: 那只狗对陌生人发出低沉的咆哮声。

e.en: Heavy rain caused a major traffic {snarl} on the highway.
e.zh: 暴雨造成高速公路上严重的交通堵塞。

snarled.t: v. 咆哮；缠作一团（过去式）

e.en: The angry dog {snarled} and showed its sharp teeth.
e.zh: 那只愤怒的狗咆哮着露出锋利的牙齿。

e.en: Traffic was completely {snarled} after the accident on Main Street.
e.zh: 主街发生事故后交通完全堵塞了。

e.en: A {snarling} wolf appeared at the edge of the campsite.
e.zh: 一只咆哮的狼出现在营地边缘。

e.en: He gave a {snarling} response when asked about the scandal.
e.zh: 被问及丑闻时他咆哮着回应。

e.en: My hair gets really {snarly} after swimming in the ocean.
e.zh: 我在海里游完泳后头发变得非常打结。

e.en: He's been {snarly} all morning because of the bad news.
e.zh: 因为坏消息他整个上午都很暴躁。

snatch.t:
v. 一把抓住，抢走
n. 片段

e.en: Thieves tried to {snatch} her purse on the crowded subway.
e.zh: 小偷试图在拥挤的地铁里抢走她的钱包。

e.en: I managed to {snatch} a few hours of sleep before the flight.
e.zh: 我在航班前设法睡了几个小时。

snatched.t: v. 抢走，一把抓过（过去式）

e.en: A seagull {snatched} the sandwich right out of my hand.
e.zh: 一只海鸥从我手里抢走了三明治。

e.en: She {snatched} victory in the final seconds of the match.
e.zh: 她在比赛最后几秒钟夺得了胜利。

e.en: Police arrested the purse {snatcher} after a brief chase downtown.
e.zh: 警方在市中心短暂追捕后逮捕了那个抢包贼。

e.en: The body {snatcher} was a popular villain in old horror films.
e.zh: 盗尸者是老式恐怖电影中很受欢迎的反派。

e.en: Phone {snatching} has become common in busy tourist areas.
e.zh: 在繁忙的旅游区抢手机已经变得很常见。

e.en: The eagle came swooping down, {snatching} fish from the lake.
e.zh: 老鹰俯冲而下,从湖中抓起鱼。

snazzy.t: adj. 时髦炫目，花哨好看

e.en: He showed up to the party in a {snazzy} new suit.
e.zh: 他穿着一套时髦的新西装来参加派对。

e.en: The app has a {snazzy} interface that users really love.
e.zh: 这款应用有一个用户非常喜爱的炫酷界面。

sneak.t:
v. 偷偷行动
n. 鬼祟的人

e.en: Let me {sneak} out of the meeting to take this call.
e.zh: 让我偷偷溜出会议室接这个电话。

e.en: The trailer offers a {sneak} peek at the upcoming season.
e.zh: 预告片提前展示了即将到来的新一季。

e.en: The kids {sneaked} into the kitchen to grab some cookies.
e.zh: 孩子们偷偷溜进厨房拿了些饼干。

e.en: He {sneaked} a glance at his phone during the lecture.
e.zh: 他在讲座期间偷偷瞥了一眼手机。

e.en: He bought a limited edition {sneaker} for over a thousand dollars.
e.zh: 他花一千多美元买了一双限量版运动鞋。

e.en: The {sneaker} community lined up overnight for the new release.
e.zh: 球鞋圈的人为了新品发售连夜排队。

e.en: A group of {sneakered} teens hung out in front of the mall.
e.zh: 一群穿着运动鞋的青少年在商场前闲逛。

e.en: Her {sneakered} feet padded quietly across the gym floor.
e.zh: 她穿着运动鞋的双脚轻轻地走过体育馆的地板。

e.en: My new {sneakers} are perfect for long morning runs.
e.zh: 我的新运动鞋非常适合长距离的晨跑。

e.en: He collects rare {sneakers} from the 1990s as an investment.
e.zh: 他收藏九十年代的稀有球鞋作为投资。

e.en: The cat {sneakily} stole food from my dinner plate.
e.zh: 那只猫偷偷地从我的餐盘里偷吃东西。

e.en: He {sneakily} added extra charges to the final invoice.
e.zh: 他偷偷地在最终发票上加了额外费用。

sneaking.t:
adj. 暗自的
v. 偷偷溜

e.en: I have a {sneaking} suspicion that he's lying to us.
e.zh: 我隐约怀疑他在对我们撒谎。

e.en: She caught him {sneaking} cookies from the jar before dinner.
e.zh: 她抓到他在晚饭前偷偷从罐子里拿饼干。

sneaks.t: v. 偷偷溜（第三人称单数）

e.en: He always {sneaks} out of work fifteen minutes early.
e.zh: 他总是提前十五分钟偷偷溜出工作岗位。

e.en: The cat {sneaks} into my bedroom every single night.
e.zh: 那只猫每晚都偷偷溜进我的卧室。

sneaky.t: adj. 鬼鬼祟祟的；暗藏心机的

e.en: That's a {sneaky} trick to get more clicks on the article.
e.zh: 那是个让文章获得更多点击的狡猾伎俩。

e.en: My {sneaky} dog stole the steak right off the counter.
e.zh: 我那只狡猾的狗从台面上偷走了牛排。

sneer.t:
v. 嘲笑，讥讽
n. 冷笑

e.en: Critics tend to {sneer} at superhero movies despite their popularity.
e.zh: 尽管超级英雄电影很受欢迎,影评人却往往嗤之以鼻。

e.en: He gave her a cold {sneer} and walked out of the room.
e.zh: 他对她冷冷地嘲笑一下就走出了房间。

sneering.t:
adj. 嘲讽的
v. 冷笑

e.en: His {sneering} tone made everyone at the table uncomfortable.
e.zh: 他嘲讽的语气让餐桌上的每个人都感到不舒服。

e.en: She walked past him, ignoring his {sneering} expression completely.
e.zh: 她从他身边走过,完全无视他嘲讽的表情。

e.en: He {sneeringly} dismissed her ideas as unrealistic and naive.
e.zh: 他嘲讽地把她的想法贬为不切实际和幼稚。

e.en: The villain laughed {sneeringly} at the hero's failed attempt.
e.zh: 反派嘲讽地嘲笑英雄失败的尝试。

sneers.t:
v. 讥笑，冷笑
n. 嘲笑的表情

e.en: He always {sneers} whenever someone mentions his rival's success.
e.zh: 每当有人提到他对手的成功他总是冷笑。

e.en: Her sarcastic {sneers} have made her unpopular at the office.
e.zh: 她讽刺的冷笑让她在办公室不受欢迎。

sneeze.t:
v. 打喷嚏
n. 喷嚏

e.en: Spring pollen always makes me {sneeze} repeatedly all morning long.
e.zh: 春天的花粉总让我整个上午不停地打喷嚏。

e.en: A million dollar prize is nothing to {sneeze} at.
e.zh: 一百万美元的奖金可不是小数目。

e.en: She {sneezed} loudly during the quiet exam.
e.zh: 她在安静的考场上大声打了个喷嚏。

e.en: The cat {sneezed} after sniffing the pepper shaker.
e.zh: 那只猫闻了胡椒瓶后打了个喷嚏。

sneezes.t:
v. 打喷嚏
n. 喷嚏

e.en: He {sneezes} every spring because of pollen allergies.
e.zh: 他每年春天都会因为花粉过敏而打喷嚏。

e.en: Cover your mouth when one of those big {sneezes} hits.
e.zh: 打那种大喷嚏的时候要捂住嘴。

e.en: I've been {sneezing} all morning thanks to the dusty room.
e.zh: 因为房间太多灰,我整个早上都在打喷嚏。

e.en: Constant {sneezing} can be a sign of seasonal allergies.
e.zh: 不停地打喷嚏可能是季节性过敏的征兆。

e.en: The fisherman tied a fresh {snell} onto his hook.
e.zh: 渔夫在鱼钩上绑了一段新的钩绳。

e.en: A short {snell} works best for fast-flowing trout streams.
e.zh: 短钩绳最适合用在水流湍急的鳟鱼溪流里。

e.en: My grandfather taught me {snelling} hooks for trout fishing.
e.zh: 我爷爷教过我钓鳟鱼时给鱼钩绑钩绳的方法。

e.en: Proper {snelling} keeps the bait aligned along the hook shank.
e.zh: 正确的钩绳绑法能让鱼饵沿着钩柄对齐。

snick.t:
v. 轻切，剪一小口
n. 小切口

e.en: I heard the {snick} of the door latch closing softly.
e.zh: 我听见门闩轻轻合上的咔哒声。

e.en: The batsman managed only a faint {snick} to the keeper.
e.zh: 击球员只是轻轻擦了一下球,被守门员接住了。

snicker.t:
v. 偷笑，窃笑
n. 窃笑声

e.en: The students tried to hide a {snicker} during the speech.
e.zh: 演讲时学生们努力憋住偷笑。

e.en: Don't {snicker} when someone mispronounces a word.
e.zh: 别人念错单词的时候不要窃笑。

e.en: The kids were {snickering} behind the substitute teacher's back.
e.zh: 孩子们在代课老师背后偷偷地笑。

e.en: Stop {snickering} and pay attention to the lecture.
e.zh: 别再窃笑了,认真听讲。

e.en: His {snide} comment about her outfit hurt her feelings.
e.zh: 他对她衣着的那句讥讽伤了她的心。

e.en: The reviewer made several {snide} remarks about the director.
e.zh: 那位影评人对导演说了好几句尖酸刻薄的话。

e.en: She {snidely} suggested that he try reading the manual.
e.zh: 她讽刺地建议他不如去看看说明书。

e.en: He {snidely} congratulated his rival on a lucky win.
e.zh: 他冷嘲热讽地祝贺对手赢得了运气好的胜利。

sniff.t:
v. 嗅，闻；抽鼻子
n. 吸气声

e.en: Let the dog {sniff} your hand before you pet him.
e.zh: 摸狗之前先让它闻一闻你的手。

e.en: I caught a {sniff} of fresh bread from the bakery.
e.zh: 我闻到了一丝面包房飘来的新鲜面包香。

e.en: She {sniffed} the milk to check if it had spoiled.
e.zh: 她闻了闻牛奶看有没有变质。

e.en: The detective dog {sniffed} every suitcase in the terminal.
e.zh: 缉毒犬把航站楼里每只行李箱都嗅了一遍。

sniffer.t:
n. 嗅探器（网络监听工具）
n. 嗅闻者

e.en: Airport security uses a {sniffer} dog to detect drugs.
e.zh: 机场安检用嗅探犬来查毒品。

e.en: Engineers ran a packet {sniffer} to debug the network.
e.zh: 工程师用抓包嗅探器来排查网络问题。

sniffing.t:
v. 嗅探；抽鼻子
n. 嗅探（网络监听）

e.en: The puppy kept {sniffing} around the kitchen door.
e.zh: 小狗一直在厨房门口闻来闻去。

e.en: Hackers were {sniffing} traffic on the public Wi-Fi.
e.zh: 黑客在公共Wi-Fi上嗅探流量。

sniffle.t:
v. 抽鼻涕
n. 抽鼻子声

e.en: I have a slight {sniffle} but no fever.
e.zh: 我有点鼻塞,但没发烧。

e.en: Children {sniffle} when they catch a mild cold.
e.zh: 孩子轻微感冒时会抽鼻子。

e.en: She was {sniffling} quietly during the sad movie.
e.zh: 她看那部悲伤电影时一直在小声抽泣。

e.en: Stop {sniffling} and use a tissue, please.
e.zh: 别再抽鼻子了,用张纸巾吧。

sniffs.t:
v. 嗅，闻
n. 吸气声

e.en: The dog {sniffs} every lamppost on our walk.
e.zh: 散步时狗会闻每一根路灯杆。

e.en: He {sniffs} the milk to check if it's spoiled.
e.zh: 他闻一闻牛奶看看有没有变质。

e.en: The waiter was a bit {sniffy} about my order.
e.zh: 那位服务员对我的点单有点不屑一顾。

e.en: Critics were {sniffy} about the new pop album.
e.zh: 评论家对这张新流行专辑颇为不屑。

e.en: He swirled brandy in a wide {snifter} by the fire.
e.zh: 他在炉火旁用宽口酒杯摇晃着白兰地。

e.en: The bartender served cognac in a crystal {snifter}.
e.zh: 调酒师用水晶白兰地杯端上干邑。

snigger.t:
v. 暗笑，偷笑
n. 窃笑

e.en: Students began to {snigger} at the teacher's typo.
e.zh: 学生们开始为老师的错别字偷偷窃笑。

e.en: I heard a {snigger} from the back of the room.
e.zh: 我听到房间后面传来一阵窃笑。

snip.t:
v. 剪断
n. 剪一下；小片

e.en: Use scissors to {snip} the loose thread off the shirt.
e.zh: 用剪刀把衬衫上的线头剪掉。

e.en: This jacket is a real {snip} at half price.
e.zh: 这件夹克半价真是太划算了。

snipe.t:
v. 狙击；暗讽
n. 鹬（鸟）

e.en: Politicians {snipe} at each other on social media daily.
e.zh: 政客们每天在社交媒体上互相攻击。

e.en: A hidden {snipe} took out the enemy commander.
e.zh: 一名隐藏的狙击手干掉了敌方指挥官。

e.en: A {sniper} was hidden on the rooftop across the street.
e.zh: 一名狙击手藏在街对面的屋顶上。

e.en: He won the auction with a last-second {sniper} bid.
e.zh: 他靠最后一秒的狙击出价赢得了拍卖。

snippet.t: n. 片段（代码、文本的小段）

e.en: She shared a {snippet} of code on Stack Overflow.
e.zh: 她在Stack Overflow上分享了一段代码片段。

e.en: I caught a {snippet} of their conversation in the hallway.
e.zh: 我在走廊里听到他们对话的一小段。

e.en: VS Code lets you save reusable {snippets} for any language.
e.zh: VS Code允许你为任何语言保存可复用的代码片段。

e.en: The trailer shows only brief {snippets} of the new film.
e.zh: 预告片只展示了新电影的几个简短片段。

e.en: Don't get {snippy} with me just because you're tired.
e.zh: 别因为你累了就对我没好气。

e.en: Her {snippy} reply ended the conversation abruptly.
e.zh: 她那句没好气的回答让对话戛然而止。

e.en: He's in a {snit} because no one liked his post.
e.zh: 他正闹脾气,因为没人给他的帖子点赞。

e.en: She got into a {snit} over a tiny misunderstanding.
e.zh: 她为一点小误会就生起了闷气。

snitch.t:
v. 告密；偷拿
n. 告密者

e.en: Nobody likes a {snitch} who tells the boss everything.
e.zh: 没人喜欢什么事都告诉老板的告密者。

e.en: Don't {snitch} on your classmates to the teacher.
e.zh: 别向老师告同学的状。

e.en: Stop {snivel} about the rain and grab an umbrella.
e.zh: 别为下雨发牢骚了,拿把伞吧。

e.en: He began to {snivel} when his phone got confiscated.
e.zh: 手机被没收时他开始抽抽搭搭地哭。

e.en: The {sniveling} child finally calmed down with a hug.
e.zh: 那个抽泣的孩子在拥抱中终于平静下来。

e.en: Stop {sniveling} and tell me what actually happened.
e.zh: 别抽抽搭搭的了,告诉我到底发生了什么。

snivelling.t: v. 哭哭啼啼（英式拼写）

e.en: He sat in the corner, {snivelling} about his lost game.
e.zh: 他坐在角落里,为输掉的比赛抽泣不已。

e.en: The {snivelling} tone of his email annoyed everyone.
e.zh: 他邮件里那种哭哭啼啼的语气让大家都很烦。

snmp.t: n. 简单网络管理协议（Simple Network Management Protocol）

e.en: We monitor router uptime using {snmp} polling every minute.
e.zh: 我们每分钟通过SNMP轮询监控路由器的运行状态。

e.en: The network admin enabled {snmp} traps for critical alerts.
e.zh: 网管启用了SNMP陷阱来发送关键告警。

e.en: He's a total wine {snob} who refuses anything cheap.
e.zh: 他是个十足的红酒势利眼,看不上任何便宜货。

e.en: Don't be such a {snob} about indie movies.
e.zh: 别对独立电影那么傲慢挑剔。

e.en: The novel exposes the petty {snobberies} of small-town life.
e.zh: 这部小说揭露了小镇生活中种种琐碎的势利做派。

e.en: Modern {snobberies} have shifted from class to taste.
e.zh: 现代的势利已从阶级转向品味之争。

e.en: Wine {snobbery} keeps many beginners from enjoying the hobby.
e.zh: 红酒圈的势利让很多新手不敢入门。

e.en: There's a lot of {snobbery} in the art world.
e.zh: 艺术圈里充斥着不少势利眼。

e.en: The waiter gave us a {snobbish} look when we ordered tap water.
e.zh: 我们点自来水时,服务员投来一副势利的眼神。

e.en: Don't be {snobbish} about people's accents.
e.zh: 别因为别人的口音就摆出傲慢的样子。

e.en: Her {snobbishness} about brands turns customers away.
e.zh: 她对品牌的势利态度让顾客望而却步。

e.en: There's a streak of {snobbishness} in his food reviews.
e.zh: 他的美食评论里透着一股势利劲儿。

e.en: That café has a really {snobby} vibe and rude staff.
e.zh: 那家咖啡馆氛围很势利,店员也不礼貌。

e.en: Don't be {snobby} just because you went to a top school.
e.zh: 别因为上了名校就摆出势利的样子。

e.en: They had a quick {snog} before catching the train.
e.zh: 他们赶火车前匆匆亲热了一下。

e.en: Teenagers like to {snog} at the back of the cinema.
e.zh: 青少年喜欢在电影院后排亲热。

e.en: He cocked a {snook} at the rules and quit on the spot.
e.zh: 他对规矩嗤之以鼻,当场就辞职了。

e.en: Anglers love catching {snook} in the Florida mangroves.
e.zh: 钓鱼爱好者喜欢在佛罗里达红树林里钓海鲈。

snooker.t:
n. 斯诺克台球
v. 使陷入困境

e.en: He plays {snooker} every Friday at the local club.
e.zh: 他每周五都在当地俱乐部打斯诺克。

e.en: Don't let the salesman {snooker} you into a bad contract.
e.zh: 别让推销员把你忽悠进一份糟糕的合同。

snoop.t:
v. 窥探，打探
n. 爱窥探的人

e.en: Don't {snoop} through my phone without asking.
e.zh: 别没经过我同意就翻我的手机。

e.en: A nosy neighbor likes to {snoop} on the new family.
e.zh: 一个爱打听的邻居总爱窥探那户新搬来的人家。

e.en: That {snooper} reads everyone's mail in the office.
e.zh: 那个爱打听的家伙偷看办公室里所有人的邮件。

e.en: Install a firewall to keep {snooper} apps off your phone.
e.zh: 装个防火墙,挡住那些窥探你手机的应用。

e.en: I caught my brother {snooping} around in my room.
e.zh: 我抓到弟弟在我房间里偷偷翻东西。

e.en: Government {snooping} on private chats raises privacy concerns.
e.zh: 政府窥探私人聊天引发了隐私担忧。

snoopy.t:
adj. 爱打听的
n. 史努比（卡通名）

e.en: Don't be so {snoopy} about your coworker's salary.
e.zh: 别这么爱打听同事的工资。

e.en: My {snoopy} aunt always asks when I'll get married.
e.zh: 我那爱打听的姨妈总问我什么时候结婚。

snoot.t:
n. 鼻子（俚语）
n. 势利的人

e.en: She turned up her {snoot} at the budget hotel.
e.zh: 她对那家经济型酒店嗤之以鼻。

e.en: Photographers use a {snoot} to focus light on a subject.
e.zh: 摄影师用束光筒把光线聚焦到拍摄对象上。

e.en: The {snooty} hostess barely glanced at our reservation.
e.zh: 那位势利的迎宾员几乎没看我们的预订单一眼。

e.en: It's a {snooty} restaurant with a strict dress code.
e.zh: 那是家高傲的餐厅,着装要求很严格。

snooze.t:
v. 小睡；打盹
n. 打盹（闹钟贪睡）

e.en: I hit {snooze} on my alarm three times this morning.
e.zh: 今早我把闹钟的小睡键按了三次。

e.en: Grandpa likes to {snooze} on the couch after lunch.
e.zh: 爷爷喜欢午饭后在沙发上打个盹。

snoozed.t: v. snooze 的过去式；打了个盹

e.en: I {snoozed} the meeting reminder and almost missed it.
e.zh: 我把会议提醒延后了,差点错过开会。

e.en: She {snoozed} for ten minutes on the train home.
e.zh: 她在回家的火车上打了十分钟的盹。

e.en: My cat {snoozes} on the windowsill every afternoon.
e.zh: 我的猫每天下午都在窗台上打盹。

e.en: He hits the alarm and {snoozes} for ten more minutes.
e.zh: 他按掉闹钟又多睡了十分钟。

snoozing.t: v. snooze 的进行式；正在打盹

e.en: The dog was {snoozing} peacefully by the fireplace.
e.zh: 狗在壁炉边安静地打着盹。

e.en: Stop {snoozing} your alarm and get out of bed!
e.zh: 别再按贪睡键了,快起床!

snore.t:
v. 打呼噜
n. 鼾声

e.en: My roommate {snores} so loudly I had to buy earplugs.
e.zh: 我室友打鼾太响,我只好买了耳塞。

e.en: The lecture was such a {snore} that half the class dozed off.
e.zh: 这堂课无聊得半个班都打瞌睡了。

snored.t: v. snore 的过去式；打了呼噜

e.en: He {snored} loudly throughout the entire flight.
e.zh: 整个飞行过程中他都在大声打鼾。

e.en: The old dog {snored} softly at her feet.
e.zh: 那只老狗在她脚边轻轻打着鼾。

e.en: My husband is such a heavy {snorer} that I sleep elsewhere.
e.zh: 我丈夫鼾声实在太大,我只好去别的房间睡。

e.en: As a chronic {snorer}, he finally tried a sleep clinic.
e.zh: 他长期打鼾,最终去了睡眠诊所就诊。

snores.t:
v. snore 的三单
n. 鼾声（复数）

e.en: His loud {snores} kept everyone in the cabin awake.
e.zh: 他响亮的鼾声让木屋里的所有人都睡不着。

e.en: Grandpa {snores} whenever he falls asleep on the couch.
e.zh: 爷爷在沙发上睡着时总会打鼾。

snoring.t:
n. 打呼噜
v. 正在打呼

e.en: Her {snoring} can be heard from the next room.
e.zh: 她的鼾声在隔壁房间都能听到。

e.en: A nasal strip can help reduce {snoring} at night.
e.zh: 鼻贴有助于减轻夜间打鼾。

snorkel.t:
n. 浮潜呼吸管
v. 浮潜

e.en: We rented a mask and {snorkel} to explore the reef.
e.zh: 我们租了潜水面镜和呼吸管去探索珊瑚礁。

e.en: You can {snorkel} right off the beach at this resort.
e.zh: 在这家度假村可以直接从沙滩下海浮潜。

e.en: An experienced {snorkeler} spotted a sea turtle near the rocks.
e.zh: 一位经验丰富的浮潜者在岩石附近发现了一只海龟。

e.en: Every {snorkeler} on the boat received a safety briefing.
e.zh: 船上每位浮潜者都听了安全须知。

e.en: We went {snorkeling} in the clear waters of Hawaii.
e.zh: 我们在夏威夷清澈的海水里浮潜。

e.en: {Snorkeling} is a great way to see tropical fish up close.
e.zh: 浮潜是近距离观察热带鱼的好方法。

snort.t:
v. 喷鼻息；嗤之以鼻
n. 哼声

e.en: She let out a loud {snort} when she heard the joke.
e.zh: 听到那个笑话时她大笑出声打了个响鼻。

e.en: The horses {snort} and stamp their hooves in the cold morning.
e.zh: 马儿在寒冷的清晨打着响鼻、跺着蹄子。

snorting.t: v. 正在喷鼻息；哼鼻子

e.en: He kept {snorting} with laughter throughout the comedy show.
e.zh: 整场喜剧表演里他一直笑得直喷气。

e.en: The bull was {snorting} angrily behind the fence.
e.zh: 那头公牛在围栏后愤怒地喷着粗气。

snot.t:
n. 鼻涕
n. 讨厌的人（俚）

e.en: The toddler wiped {snot} on his sleeve again.
e.zh: 那个小孩又把鼻涕擦在了袖子上。

e.en: That rich {snot} thinks he's better than everyone else.
e.zh: 那个有钱的傲慢小子觉得自己高人一等。

snotty.t:
adj. 傲慢无礼的
adj. 流鼻涕的

e.en: The waiter gave us a {snotty} look when we asked for tap water.
e.zh: 我们要白开水时服务员给了我们一个鄙夷的眼神。

e.en: She handed me a {snotty} tissue to throw away.
e.zh: 她把一张沾着鼻涕的纸巾递给我让我扔掉。

snout.t: n. (动物的) 口鼻部；猪嘴

e.en: The pig pushed its {snout} into the mud looking for food.
e.zh: 那头猪把鼻子拱进泥里找食物。

e.en: A curious dog poked its {snout} through the fence.
e.zh: 一只好奇的狗把鼻子从栅栏缝里探出来。

e.en: Heavy {snow} closed the schools for two days.
e.zh: 大雪让学校停课了两天。

e.en: The kids ran outside to play in the fresh {snow}.
e.zh: 孩子们跑到外面在新雪里玩耍。

snowball.t:
n. 雪球
v. 滚雪球般增长

e.en: He threw a {snowball} that hit the lamppost.
e.zh: 他扔了一个雪球,正好打中路灯杆。

e.en: Small problems can quickly {snowball} into a crisis.
e.zh: 小问题可能迅速演变成一场危机。

snowballing.t: v. 滚雪球式扩大；迅速增长

e.en: Complaints about the app are {snowballing} on social media.
e.zh: 对这款应用的投诉在社交媒体上越滚越大。

e.en: The kids spent the afternoon {snowballing} in the park.
e.zh: 孩子们整个下午都在公园里打雪仗。

snowballs.t:
n. 雪球（复数）
v. snowball 的三单

e.en: The children packed tight {snowballs} to throw at each other.
e.zh: 孩子们捏紧雪球相互投掷。

e.en: Online outrage {snowballs} faster than any newsroom can react.
e.zh: 网络愤怒比任何新闻编辑室反应都快地滚雪球般扩散。

e.en: The car skidded off the road into a {snowbank}.
e.zh: 汽车打滑冲出路面,撞进了一堆雪堆。

e.en: She sat down on the {snowbank} to catch her breath.
e.zh: 她坐在雪堆上喘了口气。

snowbird.t:
n. 冬季南迁避寒者
n. 雪鹀

e.en: My grandmother is a {snowbird} who winters in Florida.
e.zh: 我外婆是个候鸟族,冬天都去佛罗里达过。

e.en: Many Canadian {snowbird} retirees own homes in Arizona.
e.zh: 许多加拿大候鸟式退休者在亚利桑那有房子。

e.en: He cleared the driveway with his new {snowblower}.
e.zh: 他用新买的扫雪机清理了车道。

e.en: The {snowblower} broke down halfway through the storm.
e.zh: 扫雪机在暴风雪中途坏掉了。

snowboard.t:
n. 单板滑雪板
v. 玩单板滑雪

e.en: She strapped on her {snowboard} and headed down the slope.
e.zh: 她系好滑雪板,顺着斜坡滑了下去。

e.en: I learned to {snowboard} when I was twelve.
e.zh: 我十二岁时学会了滑单板。

e.en: The {snowboarder} landed a perfect jump off the ramp.
e.zh: 那位单板滑雪手从跳台上完成了一次完美跳跃。

e.en: Every {snowboarder} on the mountain wore a helmet today.
e.zh: 山上每位单板滑雪手今天都戴着头盔。

e.en: We went {snowboarding} in the Alps last winter.
e.zh: 去年冬天我们去阿尔卑斯山滑单板。

e.en: {Snowboarding} became an Olympic sport in 1998.
e.zh: 单板滑雪在1998年成为奥运项目。

snowboardings.t: n. snowboarding 的复数形式（罕用）

e.en: The resort offers different styles of {snowboardings}, from freestyle to alpine.
e.zh: 度假村提供不同风格的单板滑雪,从自由式到高山式。

e.en: Various {snowboardings} have evolved into distinct competitive disciplines.
e.zh: 各种单板滑雪已发展成不同的竞赛项目。

e.en: The shop rents {snowboards} by the day or week.
e.zh: 这家店按天或按周出租单板滑雪板。

e.en: Modern {snowboards} are lighter and more responsive than ever.
e.zh: 现代单板比以往更轻、反应更灵敏。

snowbound.t: adj. 被大雪困住的；雪阻的

e.en: The village was {snowbound} for nearly a week.
e.zh: 那个村子被大雪困了将近一周。

e.en: Travelers were left {snowbound} at the mountain inn.
e.zh: 旅客们被困在山间客栈里出不来。

e.en: A {snowcat} groomed the slopes before sunrise.
e.zh: 一辆雪地车在日出前压平了雪道。

e.en: Guests rode the {snowcat} up to the backcountry lodge.
e.zh: 客人们乘坐雪地车上到野外小屋。

snowdon.t: n. 斯诺登峰（威尔士最高峰）

e.en: We hiked to the summit of {Snowdon} last summer.
e.zh: 去年夏天我们徒步登上了斯诺登峰。

e.en: {Snowdon} is the highest mountain in Wales.
e.zh: 斯诺登峰是威尔士最高的山。

snowdonia.t: n. 斯诺多尼亚（威尔士国家公园）

e.en: {Snowdonia} National Park attracts thousands of climbers each year.
e.zh: 斯诺多尼亚国家公园每年吸引成千上万的登山者。

e.en: We spent the weekend exploring trails in {Snowdonia}.
e.zh: 我们整个周末都在斯诺多尼亚探索步道。

e.en: A huge {snowdrift} blocked the front door overnight.
e.zh: 一夜之间,一个巨大的雪堆挡住了前门。

e.en: The wind piled the snow into a {snowdrift} along the fence.
e.zh: 风把雪沿着栅栏堆成了雪堆。

e.en: The first {snowdrop} of the year bloomed in the garden.
e.zh: 今年第一朵雪滴花在花园里绽放了。

e.en: A delicate {snowdrop} pushed through the frozen soil.
e.zh: 一朵娇嫩的雪滴花从冻土中探出头来。

snowed.t: v. snow 的过去式；下过雪

e.en: It {snowed} all night, covering the streets in white.
e.zh: 雪下了一整夜,把街道染成一片白。

e.en: I'm completely {snowed} under with work this week.
e.zh: 我这周被工作压得喘不过气来。

e.en: The region had record {snowfall} this winter.
e.zh: 该地区今年冬天的降雪量创下纪录。

e.en: A light {snowfall} dusted the rooftops at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时一场小雪在屋顶上铺了一层薄白。

snowfield.t: n. 雪原；长年积雪地带

e.en: The climbers crossed a vast {snowfield} before the final ascent.
e.zh: 登山者在最后冲顶前穿越了一片广阔的雪原。

e.en: Sunlight glittered across the untouched {snowfield}.
e.zh: 阳光在未被踏足的雪原上闪闪发光。

snowflake.t:
n. 雪花
n. 玻璃心的人（俚）

e.en: Each {snowflake} has a unique six-sided pattern.
e.zh: 每一片雪花都有独一无二的六角图案。

e.en: He caught a {snowflake} on his glove and examined it.
e.zh: 他用手套接住一片雪花,仔细端详。

e.en: It's been {snowing} since early this morning.
e.zh: 从今天一大早就开始下雪了。

e.en: Look outside — it's {snowing} again!
e.zh: 看看外面,又下雪了!

e.en: Resorts struggled during the unusually {snowless} winter.
e.zh: 在这个异常无雪的冬天,度假村经营艰难。

e.en: Climate change has led to more {snowless} December days.
e.zh: 气候变化导致越来越多的十二月没有雪。

e.en: Modern {snowmaking} machines keep the slopes open year-round.
e.zh: 现代造雪机让雪道全年都能开放。

e.en: The resort invested millions in new {snowmaking} equipment.
e.zh: 度假村斥资数百万购置新的造雪设备。

e.en: The kids built a {snowman} with a carrot nose.
e.zh: 孩子们堆了一个胡萝卜鼻子的雪人。

e.en: Our {snowman} had a scarf and an old top hat.
e.zh: 我们的雪人围着围巾,戴着旧礼帽。

e.en: Spring {snowmelt} swelled the river to dangerous levels.
e.zh: 春季融雪使河水上涨到危险水位。

e.en: Farmers depend on {snowmelt} to irrigate their fields.
e.zh: 农民依靠融雪水来灌溉田地。

e.en: They rented a {snowmobile} to explore the frozen lake.
e.zh: 他们租了一辆雪地摩托去探索结冰的湖面。

e.en: A loud {snowmobile} roared past the cabin at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时一辆嘈杂的雪地摩托呼啸着冲过小屋。

e.en: This year's {snowpack} is well below the average.
e.zh: 今年的积雪量远低于平均水平。

e.en: Scientists measure the {snowpack} to predict water supply.
e.zh: 科学家测量积雪量来预测供水状况。

e.en: A {snowplow} cleared the highway just before rush hour.
e.zh: 一辆扫雪车在高峰时间前清理完了高速路。

e.en: We waited for the {snowplow} before driving to work.
e.zh: 我们等扫雪车过去后才开车去上班。

snows.t:
v. 下雪
n. 雪（snow 的复数）

e.en: It rarely {snows} in this part of the country.
e.zh: 这一带很少下雪。

e.en: The deep {snows} of January made travel impossible.
e.zh: 一月份的深雪使出行变得不可能。

snowshoe.t: n. 雪鞋（防陷入雪中的宽鞋）

e.en: You'll need a {snowshoe} on each foot to cross that meadow.
e.zh: 你得在每只脚上绑一只雪鞋才能穿过那片草地。

e.en: We hired a guide to {snowshoe} through the forest.
e.zh: 我们请了向导带我们穿雪鞋徒步穿越森林。

e.en: A massive {snowstorm} shut down the airport for hours.
e.zh: 一场大暴风雪让机场停运了好几个小时。

e.en: The {snowstorm} left twelve inches on the ground.
e.zh: 那场暴风雪在地上积了十二英寸厚的雪。

e.en: Two back-to-back {snowstorms} paralyzed the city last week.
e.zh: 上周接连两场暴风雪让整座城市陷入瘫痪。

e.en: Winter {snowstorms} are becoming more intense in the region.
e.zh: 该地区冬季暴风雪正变得越来越猛烈。

e.en: She zipped her toddler into a thick {snowsuit}.
e.zh: 她把蹒跚学步的孩子塞进厚厚的连体雪衣里。

e.en: His red {snowsuit} stood out against the white field.
e.zh: 他的红色连体雪衣在白茫茫的雪地里格外醒目。

e.en: We curled up by the fire on a {snowy} evening.
e.zh: 在一个雪夜里,我们蜷缩在炉火旁。

e.en: The mountains looked stunning under the {snowy} sky.
e.zh: 群山在雪色苍穹下显得格外壮观。

snp.t: n. 单核苷酸多态性（遗传学缩写）

snub.t:
v. 冷落；怠慢
n. 冷遇

e.en: She felt the {snub} when no one returned her greeting.
e.zh: 没人回应她的问候,她感到被冷落了。

e.en: Critics say the award committee chose to {snub} younger directors.
e.zh: 批评者称评奖委员会有意冷落年轻导演。

snuck.t: v. 偷偷地走（sneak 的过去式）

e.en: He {snuck} out the back door without saying goodbye.
e.zh: 他没说再见就从后门溜了出去。

e.en: The cat {snuck} into the kitchen and stole some chicken.
e.zh: 那只猫偷偷溜进厨房,叼走了一些鸡肉。

snuff.t:
v. 掐灭（蜡烛）
n. 鼻烟

e.en: A single gust was enough to {snuff} the candle out.
e.zh: 一阵风就足以把蜡烛吹灭。

e.en: The mayor's promise to {snuff} out corruption fell flat.
e.zh: 市长扑灭腐败的承诺没能兑现。

e.en: He kept a silver {snuffbox} in his waistcoat pocket.
e.zh: 他在马甲口袋里放着一个银制鼻烟盒。

e.en: The antique {snuffbox} sold for thousands at auction.
e.zh: 那个古董鼻烟盒在拍卖会上卖了数千元。

e.en: The puppy began to {snuffle} around the new toy.
e.zh: 小狗开始绕着新玩具嗅来嗅去。

e.en: I could hear her {snuffle} quietly into her handkerchief.
e.zh: 我能听到她轻轻对着手帕抽鼻子。

snug.t: adj. 温暖舒适的；贴身的

e.en: The baby looked {snug} wrapped in the wool blanket.
e.zh: 婴儿裹在羊毛毯里看起来暖暖的、很舒服。

e.en: These jeans feel a little too {snug} around the waist.
e.zh: 这条牛仔裤腰部感觉有点太紧了。

e.en: The kids love to {snuggle} under the blanket and watch movies.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢窝在毯子里看电影。

e.en: My dog will always {snuggle} up to me on cold nights.
e.zh: 寒冷的夜里,我的狗总会紧紧靠在我身边。

e.en: The lid fits {snugly} on the jar so nothing spills.
e.zh: 盖子严丝合缝地扣在罐子上,什么都不会洒出来。

e.en: She tucked the baby {snugly} into the crib.
e.zh: 她把婴儿紧紧地塞进婴儿床里。

e.en: His {so-called} friends abandoned him when things got hard.
e.zh: 那些所谓的朋友在他遇到困难时弃他而去。

e.en: The {so-called} smart home barely responds to voice commands.
e.zh: 这个所谓的智能家居几乎听不懂语音指令。

e.en: Let the beans {soak} overnight before cooking.
e.zh: 煮之前让豆子泡一晚上。

e.en: A long hot {soak} in the tub helps me unwind.
e.zh: 在浴缸里泡个热水澡能帮我放松下来。

e.en: I got caught in the rain and was completely {soaked}.
e.zh: 我被雨淋了个透,浑身湿透了。

e.en: She {soaked} the stained shirt in cold water overnight.
e.zh: 她把那件有污渍的衬衫在冷水里泡了一夜。

e.en: That afternoon storm turned out to be a real {soaker}.
e.zh: 那场午后的暴雨真是把人浇了个透。

e.en: The kids ran around the yard with a water {soaker}.
e.zh: 孩子们拿着水枪在院子里到处乱跑。

soaking.t:
adj. 湿透的
n. 浸泡

e.en: Come inside — you're {soaking} wet from the rain!
e.zh: 快进来——你都被雨淋透了!

e.en: {Soaking} the pan overnight makes the burnt food easy to scrub.
e.zh: 把锅泡一晚上,烧焦的食物就很容易刷掉。

e.en: She {soaks} the dried beans overnight before cooking.
e.zh: 她在烹饪前会把干豆子泡一晚上。

e.en: This sponge {soaks} up spills almost instantly.
e.zh: 这种海绵几乎能瞬间吸收洒出的液体。

soap.t:
n. 肥皂
v. 用肥皂洗

e.en: Wash your hands with {soap} for at least twenty seconds.
e.zh: 用肥皂洗手至少二十秒。

e.en: My grandmother loves watching that afternoon {soap} opera.
e.zh: 我奶奶很爱看那部下午播的肥皂剧。

soapbox.t: n. 临时讲台；街头演说场合

e.en: He climbed onto his {soapbox} about climate change again.
e.zh: 他又开始大谈气候变化的高论了。

e.en: Twitter has become a global {soapbox} for every opinion.
e.zh: 推特已成了各种观点的全球演讲台。

e.en: The kitchen counters are made of polished {soapstone}.
e.zh: 厨房台面是用抛光的皂石做的。

e.en: Artisans carve small figurines from {soapstone} blocks.
e.zh: 工匠们用皂石块雕刻小人偶。

e.en: The kids splashed happily in the {soapsuds}.
e.zh: 孩子们在肥皂泡里开心地拍水玩。

e.en: Rinse all the {soapsuds} off the car before drying.
e.zh: 擦干前先把车上的肥皂泡都冲干净。

soapy.t: adj. 含肥皂的；肥皂似的

e.en: Wipe the screen with a slightly {soapy} cloth.
e.zh: 用稍微带点肥皂水的布擦屏幕。

e.en: The plot felt {soapy} and predictable by episode three.
e.zh: 剧情到第三集就显得很狗血、很套路了。

e.en: Stock prices are expected to {soar} after the announcement.
e.zh: 消息公布后,股价预计将大幅飙升。

e.en: Eagles {soar} effortlessly above the canyon walls.
e.zh: 老鹰在峡谷上空毫不费力地翱翔。

soaraway.t: adj. 飞涨的；一路领先的

e.en: The startup posted another {soaraway} quarter of revenue growth.
e.zh: 这家初创公司又交出了一份营收狂飙的季报。

e.en: Fans were thrilled by the team's {soaraway} success this year.
e.zh: 球迷们为球队今年一飞冲天的成绩兴奋不已。

e.en: Downloads {soared} after the app went viral on TikTok.
e.zh: 这款应用在抖音上爆红后下载量暴涨。

e.en: The drone {soared} high above the treetops.
e.zh: 无人机高高飞过了树梢。

e.en: Families are struggling with {soaring} grocery prices.
e.zh: 家庭正在被飞涨的食品价格压得喘不过气。

e.en: We watched hawks {soaring} on the warm afternoon air.
e.zh: 我们看着鹰在午后的暖气流中翱翔。

e.en: Demand for electric cars {soars} every summer.
e.zh: 每年夏天电动车的需求都会大幅飙升。

e.en: The melody {soars} beautifully in the second verse.
e.zh: 旋律在第二段唱出时显得格外高亢动人。

sob.t:
v. 啜泣
n. 抽噎声

e.en: We ordered cold {soba} noodles with dipping sauce.
e.zh: 我们点了配蘸酱的冷荞麦面。

e.en: This shop makes fresh {soba} from buckwheat every morning.
e.zh: 这家店每天早上用荞麦现做面。

e.en: She {sobbed} quietly after reading the final message.
e.zh: 读完那条最后的信息,她小声啜泣起来。

e.en: The toddler {sobbed} until his mother picked him up.
e.zh: 小娃娃一直抽泣到妈妈把他抱起来。

sobbing.t:
v. 啜泣（进行时）
n. 抽噎

e.en: I could hear someone {sobbing} in the next room.
e.zh: 我能听到隔壁房间有人在抽泣。

e.en: She arrived at the hospital {sobbing} uncontrollably.
e.zh: 她到医院时已经哭得无法自控。

sober.t: adj. 清醒的；未醉的；严肃的

e.en: He has stayed {sober} for three years now.
e.zh: 他到现在已经戒酒三年了。

e.en: The report paints a {sober} picture of the economy.
e.zh: 这份报告描绘了一幅冷峻的经济图景。

sobering.t: adj. 令人警醒的；发人深省的

e.en: The accident statistics make for {sobering} reading.
e.zh: 那些事故数据读来让人警醒。

e.en: Losing the contract was a {sobering} reminder to diversify.
e.zh: 丢掉这份合同是一记让人清醒的警钟,提醒要多元化。

e.en: She dressed {soberly} for the funeral.
e.zh: 她穿得素净庄重去参加葬礼。

e.en: The CEO spoke {soberly} about the layoffs ahead.
e.zh: CEO语气凝重地谈到了即将到来的裁员。

e.en: He celebrated five years of {sobriety} last weekend.
e.zh: 他上周末庆祝了戒酒五周年。

e.en: Drivers were stopped for a roadside {sobriety} check.
e.zh: 司机被拦下做路边的酒驾检查。

e.en: "The Iron Lady" was Thatcher's famous {sobriquet}.
e.zh: “铁娘子”是撒切尔夫人著名的绰号。

e.en: New York earned the {sobriquet} "the Big Apple."
e.zh: 纽约得到了“大苹果”这个外号。

sobs.t:
v. 啜泣（三单）
n. 抽噎声（复数）

e.en: Her quiet {sobs} could be heard through the wall.
e.zh: 她压抑的啜泣声透过墙壁都能听见。

e.en: He {sobs} whenever that old song comes on.
e.zh: 每次那首老歌响起,他都会哭出声。

soc.t: n. 片上系统（SoC）；社团（society 缩写）

socal.t: n. 南加利福尼亚（Southern California）

e.en: We're flying down to {SoCal} for spring break.
e.zh: 春假我们要飞去南加州。

e.en: The {SoCal} beaches were packed all weekend.
e.zh: 整个周末南加州的海滩都挤满了人。

e.en: My daughter plays {soccer} every Saturday morning.
e.zh: 我女儿每个周六早上都去踢足球。

e.en: The {soccer} World Cup final drew a billion viewers.
e.zh: 足球世界杯决赛吸引了十亿观众。

soccers.t: n. 足球（soccer 的非标准复数）

e.en: The shop sells two different brands of {soccers} for kids.
e.zh: 这家店卖两个牌子的儿童足球。

e.en: He grabbed a couple of {soccers} from the equipment shed.
e.zh: 他从器材棚里拿了几个足球。

e.en: Dogs are prized for their loyalty and {sociability}.
e.zh: 狗因其忠诚和合群而受到喜爱。

e.en: Remote work has dampened the {sociability} of many offices.
e.zh: 远程办公让许多办公室的社交氛围淡了下来。

e.en: My roommate is friendly and very {sociable}.
e.zh: 我室友很友好,也非常爱交际。

e.en: Cats can be more {sociable} than people assume.
e.zh: 猫其实可以比人们想的更爱与人互动。

social.t:
adj. 社交的；社会的
n. 联谊活动

e.en: Teens spend hours scrolling through {social} media each day.
e.zh: 青少年每天要花好几个小时刷社交媒体。

e.en: The company hosts a {social} event every Friday.
e.zh: 公司每周五都会办一次联谊活动。

socialisation.t: n. 社会化（socialization 英式拼写）

e.en: Early {socialisation} helps puppies grow into calm dogs.
e.zh: 早期的社会化训练有助于小狗长成性格沉稳的狗。

e.en: School plays a key role in children's {socialisation}.
e.zh: 学校在孩子的社会化过程中起着关键作用。

socialise.t: v. 社交；使社会化（英式拼写）

e.en: I rarely {socialise} with coworkers outside the office.
e.zh: 我很少在下班后跟同事来往。

e.en: Dogs need to {socialise} with other animals when young.
e.zh: 小狗在年幼时需要和其他动物多接触相处。

socialised.t: v. socialise 的过去式（英式）

e.en: The rescue puppy was poorly {socialised} as a baby.
e.zh: 这只救助的小狗幼年时社会化做得不够好。

e.en: We {socialised} with the neighbours over a long dinner.
e.zh: 我们和邻居一起吃了顿很久的晚饭聊天。

socialises.t: v. socialise 的第三人称单数（英式）

e.en: He rarely {socialises} outside of work meetings.
e.zh: 他除了工作会议很少出去交际。

e.en: Our cat {socialises} surprisingly well with strangers.
e.zh: 我们家猫跟陌生人相处得出奇地好。

socialising.t: v. socialise 的现在分词（英式）

e.en: After a long week, I'm not in the mood for {socialising}.
e.zh: 忙了一周,我没什么心情去应酬。

e.en: The conference is great for {socialising} with peers.
e.zh: 这次大会很适合跟同行交流社交。

e.en: The candidate's views on {socialism} sparked heated debate.
e.zh: 这位候选人对社会主义的看法引发了激烈辩论。

e.en: Several Nordic countries blend capitalism with elements of {socialism}.
e.zh: 一些北欧国家把资本主义和社会主义元素融合在一起。

socialist.t:
n. 社会主义者
adj. 社会主义的

e.en: He votes for the {socialist} party in every election.
e.zh: 他每次选举都投票给社会主义政党。

e.en: The country adopted {socialist} healthcare in the 1970s.
e.zh: 这个国家在1970年代采用了社会主义医疗制度。

socialistic.t: adj. 带社会主义色彩的

e.en: Critics called the new tax plan {socialistic} and unrealistic.
e.zh: 批评者称这项新税收计划带有社会主义色彩,不切实际。

e.en: The country has many {socialistic} welfare programs.
e.zh: 这个国家有许多带有社会主义色彩的福利项目。

e.en: The {socialite} hosted a charity gala at her mansion.
e.zh: 那位名媛在她的豪宅举办了一场慈善晚宴。

e.en: She's a famous {socialite} often featured in fashion magazines.
e.zh: 她是位常出现在时尚杂志上的知名社交名媛。

e.en: Bees are known for their high level of {sociality}.
e.zh: 蜜蜂以高度的群居性而著称。

e.en: Human {sociality} shapes how cities are designed.
e.zh: 人类的社交性影响着城市的设计方式。

socialization.t: n. 社会化（习得社会规范的过程）

e.en: Early childhood {socialization} shapes how kids handle conflict.
e.zh: 幼年时期的社会化塑造了孩子处理冲突的方式。

e.en: Puppy classes are great for {socialization} with other dogs.
e.zh: 幼犬课堂非常有助于让小狗与其他狗社交。

e.en: Different {socializations} produce very different cultural attitudes.
e.zh: 不同的社会化过程造就了截然不同的文化态度。

e.en: The study compared {socializations} across three generations.
e.zh: 该研究比较了三代人之间的社会化过程。

e.en: I try to {socialize} with coworkers at least once a week.
e.zh: 我尽量每周至少和同事社交一次。

e.en: It's important to {socialize} a puppy before twelve weeks old.
e.zh: 在小狗十二周龄前让它社交化非常重要。

socialized.t:
v. socialize 的过去式
adj. 公有化的

e.en: We {socialized} over coffee after the conference ended.
e.zh: 会议结束后我们一起喝咖啡聊天。

e.en: A well-{socialized} dog rarely shows aggression toward strangers.
e.zh: 社交良好的狗很少对陌生人表现出攻击性。

socializes.t: v. socialize 的第三人称单数

e.en: She rarely {socializes} outside of work hours.
e.zh: 她很少在工作时间之外参加社交活动。

e.en: The app {socializes} fitness by letting friends share workouts.
e.zh: 这款应用让朋友们分享健身记录,把运动社交化。

e.en: I'm tired tonight and not in the mood for {socializing}.
e.zh: 我今晚很累,没心情社交。

e.en: Remote workers miss the casual {socializing} of an office.
e.zh: 远程工作者会怀念办公室里随意的社交时光。

socially.t: adv. 社交上；在社会层面

e.en: He's brilliant at coding but a bit awkward {socially}.
e.zh: 他编程很厉害,但在社交上有点笨拙。

e.en: Smoking has become {socially} unacceptable in most workplaces.
e.zh: 在大多数职场,吸烟已变得不为社会所接受。

societal.t: adj. 社会的；关乎社会的

e.en: Social media has caused major {societal} changes worldwide.
e.zh: 社交媒体在全球引发了重大的社会变革。

e.en: Climate change is a {societal} problem, not just an environmental one.
e.zh: 气候变化是社会问题,而不仅仅是环境问题。

societe.t: n. 公司、社团（法语 société）

e.en: The bank {Societe} Generale is one of France's largest.
e.zh: 法国兴业银行是法国最大的银行之一。

e.en: In French, {societe} simply means society or company.
e.zh: 在法语中,societe就是社会或公司的意思。

e.en: Ancient {societies} often built temples to honor their gods.
e.zh: 古代社会常常建造神庙来敬奉神明。

e.en: Many honor {societies} on campus host weekly study groups.
e.zh: 校园里许多荣誉学会每周举办学习小组。

society.t:
n. 社会
n. 社团；协会

e.en: Modern {society} relies heavily on smartphones and the internet.
e.zh: 现代社会高度依赖智能手机和互联网。

e.en: She joined a local poetry {society} after college.
e.zh: 大学毕业后她加入了当地的诗歌协会。

e.en: He offered a {sociobiological} explanation for cooperative behavior.
e.zh: 他对合作行为给出了社会生物学的解释。

e.en: The lecture covered {sociobiological} theories of altruism in animals.
e.zh: 讲座讨论了动物利他行为的社会生物学理论。

e.en: The {sociobiologist} studies how genes influence social behavior.
e.zh: 这位社会生物学家研究基因如何影响社会行为。

e.en: Wilson, a famous {sociobiologist}, wrote extensively about ants.
e.zh: 著名社会生物学家威尔逊写了大量关于蚂蚁的著作。

e.en: {Sociobiology} examines the biological basis of social behavior.
e.zh: 社会生物学研究社会行为的生物学基础。

e.en: She took a class in {sociobiology} last semester.
e.zh: 上学期她选修了一门社会生物学课程。

e.en: The film explores {sociocultural} differences between rural and urban life.
e.zh: 这部电影探讨了城乡之间的社会文化差异。

e.en: Language learning involves many {sociocultural} factors beyond grammar.
e.zh: 语言学习涉及许多语法之外的社会文化因素。

e.en: The survey collected {sociodemographic} data from over a thousand respondents.
e.zh: 这项调查收集了一千多位受访者的社会人口统计数据。

e.en: Researchers analyzed {sociodemographic} trends in major cities.
e.zh: 研究人员分析了主要城市的社会人口趋势。

e.en: Education outcomes often reflect {socioeconomic} background.
e.zh: 教育成果往往反映出社会经济背景。

e.en: The policy aims to reduce {socioeconomic} inequality.
e.zh: 该政策旨在缩小社会经济不平等。

e.en: The neighborhood is {socioeconomically} diverse and vibrant.
e.zh: 这个社区在社会经济层面多元且充满活力。

e.en: Children from {socioeconomically} disadvantaged families need extra support.
e.zh: 来自社会经济弱势家庭的孩子需要额外的支持。

e.en: The {sociolinguist} studies how teenagers use slang online.
e.zh: 这位社会语言学家研究青少年如何在网上使用俚语。

e.en: As a {sociolinguist}, she records dialects across the country.
e.zh: 作为一名社会语言学家,她在全国各地记录方言。

e.en: The book offers a {sociolinguistic} analysis of bilingual communities.
e.zh: 这本书对双语社区进行了社会语言学分析。

e.en: Code-switching is a fascinating {sociolinguistic} phenomenon.
e.zh: 语码转换是一种引人入胜的社会语言学现象。

e.en: The study takes a {sociological} approach to internet addiction.
e.zh: 这项研究从社会学角度切入网瘾问题。

e.en: Her {sociological} research focuses on urban families.
e.zh: 她的社会学研究聚焦于城市家庭。

e.en: {Sociologically}, the rise of remote work has changed cities.
e.zh: 从社会学角度看,远程办公的兴起改变了城市。

e.en: The trend is interesting both economically and {sociologically}.
e.zh: 这一趋势在经济和社会学层面都很有意思。

e.en: The {sociologist} interviewed factory workers about their daily routines.
e.zh: 这位社会学家采访了工厂工人的日常生活。

e.en: As a {sociologist}, he examines how social media shapes friendships.
e.zh: 作为社会学家,他研究社交媒体如何塑造友谊。

e.en: She majored in {sociology} and now works for a think tank.
e.zh: 她主修社会学,现在在一家智库工作。

e.en: {Sociology} helps us understand patterns in human behavior.
e.zh: 社会学帮助我们理解人类行为的规律。

e.en: Teachers use {sociometric} surveys to map classroom friendships.
e.zh: 老师使用社会测量调查来描绘班级友谊关系。

e.en: The {sociometric} data revealed who the popular kids were.
e.zh: 社会测量数据揭示了哪些孩子最受欢迎。

e.en: The villain in the movie is portrayed as a charming {sociopath}.
e.zh: 电影中的反派被塑造成一个迷人的反社会人格者。

e.en: Experts warn against casually labeling someone a {sociopath}.
e.zh: 专家警告不要随意给人贴上反社会人格的标签。

e.en: His {sociopathic} behavior alarmed his coworkers for years.
e.zh: 他反社会的行为多年来让同事们感到不安。

e.en: The thriller features a charming but {sociopathic} CEO.
e.zh: 这部惊悚片描绘了一位迷人却有反社会倾向的总裁。

e.en: The novel reflects the {sociopolitical} climate of the 1960s.
e.zh: 这部小说反映了上世纪六十年代的社会政治氛围。

e.en: Protests erupted amid rising {sociopolitical} tensions.
e.zh: 在社会政治紧张加剧之际,抗议活动爆发。

e.en: The festival has deep {socioreligious} significance for the village.
e.zh: 这个节日对村庄具有深厚的社会宗教意义。

e.en: He studies {socioreligious} movements in South Asia.
e.zh: 他研究南亚的社会宗教运动。

sock.t:
n. 袜子
v. 猛击

e.en: I can never find a matching {sock} after laundry day.
e.zh: 洗完衣服后我总是找不到配对的袜子。

e.en: He pulled a twenty-dollar bill from his {sock}.
e.zh: 他从袜子里掏出一张二十美元的钞票。

socked.t: v. sock 的过去式；猛击

e.en: The boxer {socked} his opponent right in the jaw.
e.zh: 拳手一拳正中对手的下巴。

e.en: She has a few thousand dollars {socked} away for emergencies.
e.zh: 她攒了几千美元以备急需。

socket.t:
n. 插座；插口
n. 套接字（网络编程）

e.en: Plug the charger into the wall {socket} near the desk.
e.zh: 把充电器插到书桌旁的墙上插座里。

e.en: The dentist cleaned the empty tooth {socket} carefully.
e.zh: 牙医小心地清理了空牙槽。

e.en: Wild {sockeye} salmon turn bright red during spawning season.
e.zh: 野生红鲑在产卵季节会变成鲜红色。

e.en: We grilled fresh {sockeye} for dinner last night.
e.zh: 昨晚我们烤了新鲜的红鲑做晚餐。

e.en: He bought three pairs of wool {socks} for the hike.
e.zh: 他为徒步旅行买了三双羊毛袜。

e.en: Her new album really {socks} you with emotion.
e.zh: 她的新专辑情感冲击力十足。

e.en: The statue rests on a marble {socle} in the courtyard.
e.zh: 雕像立在庭院里的一座大理石底座上。

e.en: The architect designed a low stone {socle} for the column.
e.zh: 建筑师为这根柱子设计了一个低矮的石质基座。

socrates.t: n. 苏格拉底（古希腊哲学家）

e.en: {Socrates} taught philosophy by asking endless questions.
e.zh: 苏格拉底通过不断提问来教授哲学。

e.en: The professor often quoted {Socrates} during lectures.
e.zh: 教授在讲课时经常引用苏格拉底的话。

socratic.t: adj. 苏格拉底式的（以提问启发思考）

e.en: The professor uses the {Socratic} method to challenge students.
e.zh: 教授用苏格拉底式问答法来启发学生。

e.en: Their conversation turned into a {Socratic} dialogue about ethics.
e.zh: 他们的谈话变成了一场关于伦理的苏格拉底式对话。

sod.t:
n. 草皮；草地
n. (英俚) 讨厌的家伙

soda.t:
n. 苏打水；汽水
n. 苏打（碳酸钠）

e.en: Can I get a diet {soda} with my burger?
e.zh: 我汉堡能配一杯无糖汽水吗?

e.en: Mix baking {soda} with vinegar for a fun science experiment.
e.zh: 把小苏打和醋混合可以做一个有趣的科学实验。

e.en: He joined a Catholic {sodality} dedicated to charitable work.
e.zh: 他加入了一个致力于慈善工作的天主教联谊会。

e.en: A strong {sodality} formed among the long-time volunteers.
e.zh: 长期志愿者之间形成了深厚的同伴情谊。

sodas.t: n. 苏打水、汽水（soda 复数）

e.en: The kids ordered three {sodas} and a large pizza.
e.zh: 孩子们点了三杯汽水和一个大披萨。

e.en: Diet {sodas} contain artificial sweeteners instead of sugar.
e.zh: 无糖汽水用人工甜味剂代替糖。

e.en: My shoes were {sodden} after walking through the rainstorm.
e.zh: 在暴雨中走了一路,我的鞋子湿透了。

e.en: The {sodden} ground squelched under our boots.
e.zh: 湿透的地面在我们的靴子下发出咕叽声。

sodding.t: adj. (英俚) 该死的；讨厌的

e.en: Where did I put my {sodding} keys this time?
e.zh: 这次我又把那该死的钥匙放哪儿了?

e.en: The crew finished {sodding} the new lawn yesterday.
e.zh: 工人昨天铺完了新草坪的草皮。

e.en: Doctors recommend cutting down on {sodium} for heart health.
e.zh: 医生建议为了心脏健康减少钠的摄入。

e.en: This soup is surprisingly low in {sodium}.
e.zh: 这款汤的钠含量出奇地低。

sodom.t: n. 所多玛（圣经中的罪恶之城）

e.en: The Bible describes the destruction of {Sodom} by fire.
e.zh: 《圣经》描述了所多玛被烈火毁灭的故事。

e.en: Critics compared the lawless city to ancient {Sodom}.
e.zh: 评论者把这座无法无天的城市比作古代的所多玛。

e.en: The medieval text used {sodomite} as a harsh insult.
e.zh: 那部中世纪文献用“所多玛人”作为严厉的辱骂。

e.en: Historians study how the term {sodomite} shifted meaning over centuries.
e.zh: 历史学家研究“所多玛人”一词数百年间含义的变化。

e.en: The court sentenced the attacker who tried to {sodomize} the victim.
e.zh: 法庭判处了那个试图对受害人实施鸡奸的施暴者。

e.en: Laws against any attempt to {sodomize} a minor are strictly enforced.
e.zh: 任何企图对未成年人实施鸡奸的行为都受到严厉惩处。

e.en: Old laws criminalising {sodomy} have been repealed in many states.
e.zh: 许多州已经废除了将鸡奸入罪的旧法律。

e.en: The historian wrote about how attitudes toward {sodomy} changed.
e.zh: 那位历史学家写到了人们对鸡奸看法的变化。

e.en: We curled up on the {sofa} to watch a movie.
e.zh: 我们窝在沙发上看了部电影。

e.en: The new leather {sofa} barely fit through the door.
e.zh: 新买的皮沙发差点搬不进门。

e.en: The showroom had dozens of {sofas} in every color.
e.zh: 展厅里有几十款各种颜色的沙发。

e.en: Modular {sofas} are popular in small apartments.
e.zh: 模块化沙发在小户型公寓里很受欢迎。

soffit.t: n. (建筑) 拱腹；檐底；底面

e.en: Birds had built a nest under the {soffit}.
e.zh: 鸟在屋檐底板下面筑了个窝。

e.en: We painted the {soffit} a soft cream to brighten the porch.
e.zh: 我们把屋檐底板刷成淡奶油色,让门廊显得更亮。

sofia.t: n. 索非亚（保加利亚首都）；女性名

e.en: We spent three days exploring {Sofia}, the Bulgarian capital.
e.zh: 我们花了三天在保加利亚首都索非亚游览。

e.en: Flights from London to {Sofia} are surprisingly cheap.
e.zh: 从伦敦飞索非亚的机票便宜得让人意外。

soft.t:
adj. 柔软的；轻柔的
adj. 软弱的；温和的

e.en: This pillow is incredibly {soft} and supportive.
e.zh: 这个枕头超级柔软,而且很有支撑力。

e.en: She spoke in a {soft} voice so the baby wouldn't wake.
e.zh: 她轻声说话,生怕吵醒宝宝。

e.en: My sister plays {softball} on a city league team.
e.zh: 我姐姐在市里的联盟队打垒球。

e.en: The interviewer only asked the candidate {softball} questions.
e.zh: 采访者只问了候选人一些不痛不痒的问题。

softcover.t:
n. 平装本
adj. 平装的

e.en: I prefer the {softcover} edition because it's lighter.
e.zh: 我更喜欢平装版,因为更轻便。

e.en: The {softcover} comes out three months after the hardback.
e.zh: 平装本会在精装本之后三个月发售。

e.en: Let the butter {soften} at room temperature first.
e.zh: 先让黄油在常温下软化。

e.en: He tried to {soften} the bad news with a joke.
e.zh: 他想用一个玩笑来缓和那个坏消息。

softened.t: v. 已软化（soften 过去式/分词）

e.en: Her expression {softened} when she saw the puppy.
e.zh: 她一看到那只小狗,神情就柔和下来。

e.en: The lawyer {softened} the contract language after pushback.
e.zh: 在对方反对后,律师把合同措辞改得缓和了一些。

e.en: Add a capful of fabric {softener} to the rinse cycle.
e.zh: 在漂洗时加一瓶盖的衣物柔顺剂。

e.en: Hard water taught us to install a whole-house {softener}.
e.zh: 硬水问题让我们装了一套全屋软水机。

softening.t:
n. 软化；变柔和
v. soften 现在分词

e.en: There are signs of the housing market {softening} this quarter.
e.zh: 本季度房地产市场出现了走弱的迹象。

e.en: A long soak is great for {softening} tough skin on heels.
e.zh: 长时间泡脚能很好地软化脚跟的硬皮。

softie.t: n. 心软的人；多愁善感的人

e.en: Don't let his tough look fool you—he's a real {softie}.
e.zh: 别被他凶巴巴的样子骗了,他其实心很软。

e.en: My dad is a total {softie} when it comes to puppies.
e.zh: 一遇到小狗,我爸就完全是个心软的人。

e.en: She closed the bedroom door {softly} behind her.
e.zh: 她轻轻地把卧室门带上。

e.en: He spoke {softly} so the baby wouldn't wake up.
e.zh: 他轻声说话,以免吵醒宝宝。

e.en: I love the {softness} of these bamboo sheets.
e.zh: 我特别喜欢这套竹纤维床单的柔软触感。

e.en: There was a surprising {softness} in his usually stern voice.
e.zh: 他一向严厉的声音里出现了一丝意外的温柔。

e.en: The fabric samples showed many subtle {softnesses} side by side.
e.zh: 这些布料样品展示了多种细微不同的柔软质感。

e.en: Reviewers compared the {softnesses} of three different cashmere blends.
e.zh: 测评人员对比了三种羊绒混纺面料的柔软程度。

e.en: Remember to update your antivirus {software} regularly.
e.zh: 记得定期更新你的杀毒软件。

e.en: She works as a {software} engineer at a fintech startup.
e.zh: 她在一家金融科技初创公司当软件工程师。

e.en: Pine is a {softwood} commonly used for cheap furniture.
e.zh: 松木是一种常用于廉价家具的软木。

e.en: The cabin walls were built from {softwood} planks.
e.zh: 小木屋的墙壁是用软木板搭建的。

e.en: Don't be such a {softy} when training the puppy.
e.zh: 训练小狗时别那么心软。

e.en: He acts tough but he's a real {softy} inside.
e.zh: 他装得很强硬，其实内心是个软心肠的人。

e.en: My cereal got {soggy} while I checked my phone.
e.zh: 我看手机的工夫，麦片就泡软了。

e.en: The hikers trudged through {soggy} grass after the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨过后，徒步者踩着湿漉漉的草地前行。

soho.t: n. 苏豪区（伦敦/纽约街区名）

e.en: We grabbed brunch at a trendy cafe in {Soho}.
e.zh: 我们在苏豪区一家时髦的咖啡馆吃了早午餐。

e.en: London's {Soho} is famous for its nightlife and theaters.
e.zh: 伦敦的苏豪区以夜生活和剧院闻名。

soil.t:
n. 土壤；泥土
v. 弄脏

e.en: This rich {soil} is perfect for growing tomatoes.
e.zh: 这种肥沃的土壤非常适合种番茄。

e.en: Try not to {soil} your shirt at the picnic.
e.zh: 野餐时尽量别把衬衫弄脏了。

e.en: She tossed her {soiled} clothes into the laundry basket.
e.zh: 她把脏衣服扔进了洗衣篮。

e.en: The toddler {soiled} the carpet with muddy footprints.
e.zh: 小孩在地毯上留下了泥脚印，把它弄脏了。

soiling.t: v. 弄脏（soil 现在分词）

e.en: The fabric resists {soiling} and is easy to clean.
e.zh: 这种布料不易弄脏，容易清洁。

e.en: He apologized for {soiling} the borrowed jacket.
e.zh: 他为弄脏借来的外套道了歉。

soils.t:
n. 土壤（复数）
v. 弄脏（第三人称单数）

e.en: Sandy {soils} drain water faster than clay ones.
e.zh: 沙质土壤排水比黏土快得多。

e.en: Spilled wine often {soils} a white tablecloth permanently.
e.zh: 洒出的酒常常会把白桌布永久弄脏。

e.en: They hosted an elegant {soiree} at their penthouse.
e.zh: 他们在顶楼公寓举办了一场优雅的晚会。

e.en: The ambassador's {soiree} attracted celebrities and diplomats.
e.zh: 大使的晚宴吸引了名流和外交官。

e.en: The town of {Soisson} sits in northern France.
e.zh: 苏瓦松镇位于法国北部。

e.en: Historians studied the medieval battles fought near {Soisson}.
e.zh: 历史学家研究了苏瓦松附近的中世纪战役。

sojourn.t:
v. 短暂停留；旅居
n. 逗留

e.en: Her brief {sojourn} in Paris inspired her novel.
e.zh: 她在巴黎的短暂逗留激发了她的小说灵感。

e.en: They plan to {sojourn} in Kyoto for a month.
e.zh: 他们打算在京都逗留一个月。

sojourner.t: n. 旅居者；短期逗留者

e.en: Every {sojourner} at the hostel signed the guestbook.
e.zh: 每位在旅馆短暂停留的旅客都在留言簿上签了名。

e.en: The novel follows a lonely {sojourner} crossing rural India.
e.zh: 小说讲述了一位孤独旅人穿越印度乡村的故事。

sol.t:
n. 太阳；Sol（拉丁语）
n. 音阶第五音 sol

solace.t:
n. 慰藉；安慰
v. 抚慰

e.en: She found {solace} in long walks by the river.
e.zh: 她在沿河漫步中找到了慰藉。

e.en: Music can {solace} a grieving heart.
e.zh: 音乐能抚慰一颗悲伤的心。

solana.t: n. Solana（加密货币公链）；姓氏

e.en: Developers are building NFT projects on the {Solana} blockchain.
e.zh: 开发者正在 Solana 区块链上构建 NFT 项目。

e.en: He moved his savings into {Solana} last summer.
e.zh: 去年夏天他把积蓄换成了 Solana 币。

e.en: They installed {solar} panels on the garage roof.
e.zh: 他们在车库屋顶上装了太阳能板。

e.en: Astronomers tracked a massive {solar} flare yesterday.
e.zh: 天文学家昨天追踪到一次巨大的太阳耀斑。

solaris.t: n. Solaris（Sun/Oracle 的 Unix 操作系统）

e.en: Old servers at the bank still run {Solaris}.
e.zh: 银行的旧服务器仍在运行 Solaris 系统。

e.en: Tarkovsky's film {Solaris} explores memory and grief.
e.zh: 塔可夫斯基的电影《飞向太空》探讨了记忆与悲伤。

solarium.t: n. 日光浴室；日晒沙龙

e.en: The hotel's rooftop {solarium} offers panoramic city views.
e.zh: 酒店的屋顶日光浴室可俯瞰城市全景。

e.en: She read her novel in the sunny {solarium}.
e.zh: 她在阳光明媚的日光浴室里读小说。

solarization.t: n. (摄影) 日光过曝；曝晒作用

e.en: Farmers use {solarization} to kill weeds without chemicals.
e.zh: 农民利用日光消毒法在不使用化学药剂的情况下除草。

e.en: The photographer experimented with {solarization} in the darkroom.
e.zh: 摄影师在暗房里尝试了曝光过度的太阳化效果。

sold.t:
v. 卖出（sell 过去式/分词）
adj. 已售出的

e.en: She {sold} her old laptop on Facebook Marketplace.
e.zh: 她在 Facebook 市集上卖掉了旧笔记本电脑。

e.en: The concert tickets {sold} out within ten minutes.
e.zh: 演唱会门票在十分钟内就售罄了。

solder.t:
n. 焊锡
v. 焊接

e.en: You need flux to make the {solder} flow smoothly.
e.zh: 你需要助焊剂才能让焊锡顺畅流动。

e.en: He learned to {solder} circuit boards in high school.
e.zh: 他在高中时学会了焊接电路板。

soldered.t:
v. 焊接（solder 的过去式）
adj. 已焊好的

e.en: She carefully {soldered} the wires onto the tiny chip.
e.zh: 她小心地把电线焊到那块小芯片上。

e.en: The technician {soldered} a loose connection inside the radio.
e.zh: 技师焊好了收音机内部一个松动的接点。

soldering.t:
n. 焊接（作业）
v. 正在焊接

e.en: Always wear goggles when {soldering} small electronic components.
e.zh: 焊接小型电子元件时一定要戴护目镜。

e.en: The {soldering} iron heats up in about thirty seconds.
e.zh: 这把电烙铁大约三十秒就能加热。

e.en: The young {soldier} wrote letters home every week.
e.zh: 那位年轻士兵每周都写信回家。

e.en: She decided to {soldier} on despite the bad weather.
e.zh: 尽管天气恶劣，她还是决定坚持下去。

e.en: He spent ten years {soldiering} in remote outposts.
e.zh: 他花了十年在偏远哨所里当兵。

e.en: Despite the flu, she kept {soldiering} through her presentation.
e.zh: 尽管得了流感，她还是坚持完成了演讲。

e.en: He carried himself with a {soldierly} bearing at the ceremony.
e.zh: 他在仪式上举止保持着军人般的风度。

e.en: Her {soldierly} discipline impressed even the toughest coaches.
e.zh: 她那军人般的自律连最严苛的教练都为之折服。

e.en: The {soldiers} marched silently through the foggy valley.
e.zh: 士兵们在雾蒙蒙的山谷中悄无声息地行进。

e.en: Several {soldiers} returned home after the ceasefire was announced.
e.zh: 停火宣布后，几名士兵返回了家乡。

e.en: The king relied heavily on his loyal {soldiery}.
e.zh: 国王十分倚仗他忠诚的军队。

e.en: Ancient records describe the harsh life of common {soldiery}.
e.zh: 古代文献描述了普通士兵的艰苦生活。

sole.t:
adj. 唯一的，独有的
n. 鞋底；脚掌

e.en: She is the {sole} owner of the small bakery.
e.zh: 她是这家小面包店的唯一所有者。

e.en: The {sole} of my sneaker is starting to peel off.
e.zh: 我运动鞋的鞋底开始脱胶了。

solecism.t: n. 语法错误；失礼行为

e.en: Wearing sneakers to the gala was a social {solecism}.
e.zh: 穿运动鞋去庆典是一种失礼的行为。

e.en: Editors quickly caught the grammatical {solecism} in his draft.
e.zh: 编辑很快发现了他草稿中的语法错误。

soleil.t: n. 太阳（法语词，常见于品牌名）

e.en: Cirque du {Soleil} performed to a sold-out crowd.
e.zh: 太阳马戏团向座无虚席的观众献上了表演。

e.en: The cafe was named Cafe {Soleil} after the French word.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆以法语词阳光命名为 Cafe Soleil。

e.en: This decision rests {solely} on the manager's shoulders.
e.zh: 这个决定完全由经理一人承担。

e.en: The fund relies {solely} on donations from local businesses.
e.zh: 该基金完全依靠本地企业的捐款。

e.en: He made a {solemn} promise to support the family.
e.zh: 他郑重承诺会支持这个家庭。

e.en: The funeral was a quiet, {solemn} affair.
e.zh: 葬礼是一场安静而庄严的仪式。

e.en: The judge spoke with great {solemnity} during sentencing.
e.zh: 法官在宣判时神情十分庄重。

e.en: A sudden laugh broke the {solemnity} of the room.
e.zh: 突然的一声笑打破了房间里的庄严气氛。

e.en: A registered officiant can {solemnize} marriages in this state.
e.zh: 在本州，注册主礼人可以主持婚礼。

e.en: They chose a small chapel to {solemnize} their vows.
e.zh: 他们选了一座小教堂来庄严地宣读誓言。

e.en: He {solemnly} swore to tell the truth in court.
e.zh: 他在法庭上郑重宣誓要讲真话。

e.en: The children {solemnly} placed flowers on the memorial.
e.zh: 孩子们庄重地把鲜花摆在纪念碑上。

e.en: The faulty {solenoid} prevented the engine from starting.
e.zh: 故障的电磁阀导致引擎无法启动。

e.en: Engineers tested the {solenoid} valve under high pressure.
e.zh: 工程师在高压下测试了电磁阀。

e.en: Sailboats raced across the {Solent} on a windy afternoon.
e.zh: 在多风的下午，帆船在索伦特海峡上比赛。

e.en: Ferries cross the {Solent} between Portsmouth and the island.
e.zh: 渡轮往返于朴茨茅斯与小岛之间穿越索伦特海峡。

soleus.t: n. 比目鱼肌（小腿肌肉）

e.en: Calf raises strengthen the {soleus} muscle effectively.
e.zh: 提踵动作能有效锻炼比目鱼肌。

e.en: Runners often strain the {soleus} during long downhill stretches.
e.zh: 跑者在长下坡路段常常拉伤比目鱼肌。

solicit.t: v. 征求，请求（意见、资金等）

e.en: The charity will {solicit} donations from local businesses.
e.zh: 慈善机构将向本地企业募捐。

e.en: Researchers {solicit} feedback through an online survey.
e.zh: 研究人员通过在线问卷征集反馈意见。

e.en: Door-to-door {solicitation} is banned in this neighborhood.
e.zh: 这个社区禁止挨家挨户上门推销。

e.en: The email was flagged as a phishing {solicitation}.
e.zh: 这封邮件被标记为钓鱼诈骗信息。

solicited.t: v. 征求（solicit 的过去式）

e.en: The startup {solicited} feedback from its earliest customers.
e.zh: 这家初创公司向最早的客户征求了反馈。

e.en: She {solicited} advice before quitting her stable job.
e.zh: 在辞掉稳定工作之前，她征询了不少建议。

soliciting.t: v. 征求，招揽（solicit 的现在分词）

e.en: The platform bans accounts {soliciting} personal information from users.
e.zh: 该平台禁止向用户索取个人信息的账号。

e.en: Volunteers stood outside the mall {soliciting} signatures for the petition.
e.zh: 志愿者站在商场外为请愿书征集签名。

solicitor.t: n. 事务律师（英）；推销员（美）

e.en: Her {solicitor} drafted the contract within two days.
e.zh: 她的律师在两天内起草好了合同。

e.en: A {solicitor} knocked at the door selling magazine subscriptions.
e.zh: 一名推销员上门兜售杂志订阅。

e.en: A sign on the gate read "No {solicitors} please."
e.zh: 大门上挂着一块牌子，写着"谢绝推销"。

e.en: The firm employs over fifty {solicitors} across three offices.
e.zh: 该律所在三个办公室共雇用了五十多名律师。

e.en: The nurse was {solicitous} about her elderly patient's comfort.
e.zh: 护士对老年病人的舒适非常关心。

e.en: He gave her a {solicitous} look across the dinner table.
e.zh: 他在餐桌对面投来一个关切的眼神。

e.en: She {solicitously} adjusted the blanket around her sleeping child.
e.zh: 她体贴地为熟睡的孩子掖好毯子。

e.en: The waiter {solicitously} asked if everything was to our liking.
e.zh: 服务员关切地询问我们是否一切满意。

solicits.t: v. 征求（solicit 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Our app regularly {solicits} ratings after a successful order.
e.zh: 我们的应用在订单成功后会定期请求用户评分。

e.en: The professor {solicits} questions at the end of every lecture.
e.zh: 教授在每堂课结束时都会邀请学生提问。

e.en: His mother showed great {solicitude} during his illness.
e.zh: 他生病期间，母亲表现出极大的关切。

e.en: She thanked the strangers for their unexpected {solicitude}.
e.zh: 她感谢陌生人意想不到的关怀。

solid.t:
adj. 固体的；结实的；可靠的
n. 固体

e.en: The team delivered a {solid} performance in the finals.
e.zh: 球队在决赛中表现得十分稳健。

e.en: Water turns into a {solid} when it freezes.
e.zh: 水结冰后会变成固体。

e.en: New {solidarities} formed among workers across different industries.
e.zh: 不同行业的工人之间形成了新的团结纽带。

e.en: The movement built {solidarities} between local and global activists.
e.zh: 该运动在本地与全球活动人士之间建立了团结关系。

e.en: Workers showed {solidarity} by joining the strike together.
e.zh: 工人们团结一致加入了罢工。

e.en: The post expressed {solidarity} with the protesters online.
e.zh: 那条帖子在网上声援抗议者。

solider.t: adj. 更结实的（solid 的比较级）

e.en: The new bridge feels {solider} than the old wooden one.
e.zh: 新桥感觉比那座旧木桥更结实。

e.en: We need {solider} evidence before publishing the report.
e.zh: 在发布报告前我们需要更扎实的证据。

e.en: The {solidification} of lava forms new volcanic rock.
e.zh: 熔岩的凝固形成新的火山岩。

e.en: Cooling speeds up the {solidification} of melted chocolate.
e.zh: 冷却加快了融化巧克力的凝固。

solidified.t: v. 凝固（solidify 的过去式）

e.en: The wax {solidified} quickly after I poured it.
e.zh: 蜡倒出来后很快就凝固了。

e.en: Her win {solidified} her reputation as the best player.
e.zh: 这场胜利巩固了她最佳球员的声誉。

e.en: Cold weather will {solidify} the gravy in minutes.
e.zh: 寒冷的天气会让肉汁几分钟内凝固。

e.en: The team trained hard to {solidify} their lead.
e.zh: 球队刻苦训练以巩固他们的领先优势。

e.en: The engineer compared the {solidities} of various concrete mixes.
e.zh: 工程师比较了各种混凝土配方的坚固程度。

e.en: Different metals show very different {solidities} under heat.
e.zh: 不同金属在高温下表现出非常不同的坚固性。

e.en: The wall's {solidity} surprised the inspectors during testing.
e.zh: 这堵墙的坚固程度让检查员在测试中感到惊讶。

e.en: Investors valued the company's financial {solidity}.
e.zh: 投资者看重该公司的财务稳健性。

e.en: The shelf is {solidly} built and holds heavy books.
e.zh: 这个书架做工结实,能放重书。

e.en: The town voted {solidly} for the new mayor.
e.zh: 全镇一致投票支持新市长。

e.en: I admire the {solidness} of this old oak table.
e.zh: 我喜欢这张旧橡木桌的厚重感。

e.en: The argument's {solidness} convinced even the skeptics.
e.zh: 这个论点的扎实性连怀疑者都信服了。

e.en: The baby just started eating {solids} this week.
e.zh: 宝宝这周刚开始吃固体食物。

e.en: Filter the {solids} out before drinking the broth.
e.zh: 喝汤前先把固体物滤掉。

e.en: Use a {solidus} to separate the day and month.
e.zh: 用斜杠把日和月分开。

e.en: The fraction is written with a {solidus} between numbers.
e.zh: 分数用斜杠在两数之间表示。

solihull.t: n. 索利哈尔（英国城镇）

e.en: She grew up in {Solihull}, near Birmingham.
e.zh: 她在伯明翰附近的索利哈尔长大。

e.en: The new office opened in {Solihull} last month.
e.zh: 新办公室上个月在索利哈尔开业。

e.en: Hamlet's {soliloquies} reveal his deepest doubts and fears.
e.zh: 哈姆雷特的独白揭示了他最深的疑虑与恐惧。

e.en: The actor practiced his {soliloquies} alone in the theater.
e.zh: 演员独自在剧院里练习他的独白。

e.en: He likes to {soliloquize} while walking alone at night.
e.zh: 他喜欢在夜里独自散步时自言自语。

e.en: The character begins to {soliloquize} about lost love.
e.zh: 这个角色开始独白讲述失去的爱情。

e.en: She {soliloquized} for ten minutes before the audience clapped.
e.zh: 她独白了十分钟,观众才鼓掌。

e.en: The lonely traveler {soliloquized} beside the dying fire.
e.zh: 孤独的旅人在快熄灭的火堆旁自言自语。

soliloquizes.t: v. 自言自语（第三人称单数）

e.en: The hero {soliloquizes} about fate in the third act.
e.zh: 主角在第三幕中就命运进行独白。

e.en: He often {soliloquizes} when no one is around.
e.zh: 周围没人时他常常自言自语。

soliloquizing.t: v. 自言自语（现在分词）

e.en: She caught him {soliloquizing} in front of the mirror.
e.zh: 她撞见他正对着镜子自言自语。

e.en: The actor was {soliloquizing} dramatically on the empty stage.
e.zh: 演员在空荡的舞台上戏剧性地独白。

e.en: Her famous {soliloquy} moved the audience to tears.
e.zh: 她那段著名的独白让观众感动落泪。

e.en: The play opens with a long {soliloquy} by the king.
e.zh: 该剧以国王长长的独白开场。

e.en: His {solipsism} made it hard to discuss other viewpoints.
e.zh: 他的唯我论让人很难和他讨论其他观点。

e.en: Philosophy class debated {solipsism} for two whole hours.
e.zh: 哲学课就唯我论讨论了整整两个小时。

e.en: The essay critiqued various {solipsisms} found in modern art.
e.zh: 文章批评了现代艺术中各种唯我主义倾向。

e.en: Different {solipsisms} appear throughout twentieth century philosophy.
e.zh: 二十世纪哲学中出现了各种形式的唯我论。

e.en: His {solipsistic} blog only ever talks about himself.
e.zh: 他那个自我中心的博客永远只谈他自己。

e.en: The novel takes a {solipsistic} view of reality.
e.zh: 这部小说采用唯我主义的现实观。

solitaire.t:
n. 单人纸牌游戏
n. 单颗宝石

e.en: Grandma plays {solitaire} on her tablet every evening.
e.zh: 奶奶每天晚上都在平板上玩纸牌接龙。

e.en: She wore a diamond {solitaire} ring to the party.
e.zh: 她戴着一枚单颗钻石戒指参加派对。

e.en: The monastery housed several {solitaries} who rarely spoke.
e.zh: 修道院里住着几位很少说话的隐修者。

e.en: Old hermits and {solitaries} once lived in these caves.
e.zh: 昔日的隐士和独居者曾住在这些洞穴里。

e.en: She enjoyed the {solitariness} of her morning walks.
e.zh: 她享受清晨散步时的那份独处。

e.en: The cabin's {solitariness} helped him focus on writing.
e.zh: 小屋的清静帮助他专心写作。

e.en: The poet explored different {solitarinesses} in her latest collection.
e.zh: 诗人在最新诗集中探讨了不同形式的孤独。

e.en: Various {solitarinesses} shape the lives of remote villagers.
e.zh: 各种形式的独处塑造着偏远村民的生活。

solitary.t:
adj. 孤独的；单独的
n. 独居者

e.en: He took a {solitary} walk along the empty beach.
e.zh: 他独自一人沿着空旷的海滩散步。

e.en: A {solitary} tree stood in the middle of the field.
e.zh: 一棵孤零零的树立在田野中央。

e.en: She finds peace in the {solitude} of the mountains.
e.zh: 她在山中的独处中找到内心的平静。

e.en: After a busy week, he craves a little {solitude}.
e.zh: 忙碌一周后,他渴望片刻独处。

e.en: The artist painted the vast {solitudes} of the desert.
e.zh: 画家描绘了沙漠中那一片片辽阔的孤寂。

e.en: Long {solitudes} at sea shaped the captain's character.
e.zh: 海上漫长的独处塑造了船长的性格。

solo.t:
n. 独奏；独唱
adj. 单独的

e.en: She sang a beautiful {solo} at the concert.
e.zh: 她在音乐会上唱了一段优美的独唱。

e.en: He flew {solo} across the Atlantic for the first time.
e.zh: 他首次独自飞越大西洋。

e.en: The {soloist} received a standing ovation after her performance.
e.zh: 演奏结束后,独奏家获得全场起立鼓掌。

e.en: A guest {soloist} will join the orchestra tonight.
e.zh: 今晚一位客座独奏家将与乐团合作演出。

e.en: King {Solomon} was famous for his great wisdom.
e.zh: 所罗门王以其卓越的智慧而闻名。

e.en: The judge made a {Solomon}-like decision in the case.
e.zh: 法官在这个案件中作出了所罗门式的明智裁决。

solomonic.t: adj. 所罗门式的；睿智的

e.en: She offered a {Solomonic} compromise that satisfied both sides.
e.zh: 她提出了一个让双方都满意的所罗门式折衷方案。

e.en: The mayor's {Solomonic} ruling ended the long dispute.
e.zh: 市长所罗门式的裁决结束了这场长期争端。

e.en: The {Solomons} are a beautiful island chain in the Pacific.
e.zh: 所罗门群岛是太平洋上一条美丽的岛链。

e.en: We sailed through the {Solomons} on our research trip.
e.zh: 我们在科研旅行中航行穿过所罗门群岛。

solon.t:
n. 梭伦（古希腊立法者）
n. 贤明议员

e.en: The senator was hailed as a modern {solon} by reporters.
e.zh: 这位参议员被记者誉为当代的贤明立法者。

e.en: The ancient {Solon} reformed the laws of Athens.
e.zh: 古代的梭伦改革了雅典的法律。

e.en: The guitarist's wild {solos} thrilled the entire audience.
e.zh: 吉他手疯狂的独奏让全场观众激动不已。

e.en: She prefers to fly {solos} rather than with co-pilots.
e.zh: 她更喜欢单飞而不是和副驾驶一起飞。

e.en: People gather at Stonehenge for the summer {solstice}.
e.zh: 人们聚集在巨石阵庆祝夏至。

e.en: The winter {solstice} is the shortest day of the year.
e.zh: 冬至是一年中白昼最短的一天。

e.en: Sugar's high {solubility} makes it dissolve fast in tea.
e.zh: 糖的高溶解度使它能在茶中迅速溶解。

e.en: Temperature greatly affects the {solubility} of most salts.
e.zh: 温度对大多数盐类的溶解度有很大影响。

soluble.t:
adj. 可溶的
adj. 可解决的

e.en: Salt is highly {soluble} in warm water.
e.zh: 盐在温水中极易溶解。

e.en: The vitamin tablets are {soluble} and dissolve in juice.
e.zh: 这些维生素片是可溶的,能在果汁中化开。

e.en: In saltwater, salt is the {solute} and water the solvent.
e.zh: 在盐水中,盐是溶质,水是溶剂。

e.en: Stir until the {solute} fully dissolves in the liquid.
e.zh: 搅拌直到溶质在液体中完全溶解。

solution.t:
n. 解决方案
n. 溶液

e.en: We finally found a {solution} to the login bug.
e.zh: 我们终于找到了登录漏洞的解决方案。

e.en: Pour the cleaning {solution} into a spray bottle.
e.zh: 把清洁溶液倒进喷雾瓶里。

e.en: The team brainstormed several {solutions} during the meeting.
e.zh: 团队在会议中头脑风暴出了几种解决方案。

e.en: Different cleaning {solutions} work better on different surfaces.
e.zh: 不同的清洁溶液对不同表面效果各异。

e.en: This puzzle looks hard but is actually quite {solvable}.
e.zh: 这道谜题看起来难,其实很容易解决。

e.en: Most coding bugs are {solvable} with enough patience.
e.zh: 大多数代码漏洞只要有耐心都能解决。

e.en: Can you help me {solve} this math problem?
e.zh: 你能帮我解开这道数学题吗?

e.en: The new app helps users {solve} scheduling conflicts quickly.
e.zh: 这款新应用帮助用户快速解决日程冲突。

e.en: The detective {solved} the case in just three days.
e.zh: 侦探只用三天就破了这个案子。

e.en: She {solved} the puzzle faster than everyone else.
e.zh: 她比其他人更快地解开了谜题。

e.en: The bank's {solvency} reassured worried customers and investors.
e.zh: 银行的偿付能力让担忧的客户和投资者放心。

e.en: Auditors checked the company's {solvency} before approving the loan.
e.zh: 审计员在批准贷款前核查了公司的偿付能力。

solvent.t:
n. 溶剂
adj. 有偿付能力的

e.en: The company remains {solvent} despite the difficult market.
e.zh: 尽管市场艰难,公司仍保持有偿付能力。

e.en: Use a strong {solvent} to remove the old paint.
e.zh: 用强力溶剂去除旧漆。

e.en: Industrial {solvents} can damage the environment if spilled.
e.zh: 工业溶剂泄漏会破坏环境。

e.en: The lab keeps various {solvents} in labeled glass bottles.
e.zh: 实验室把各种溶剂存放在贴标签的玻璃瓶里。

e.en: She is a great problem {solver} on the team.
e.zh: 她是团队里出色的问题解决者。

e.en: The app uses an AI {solver} to crack sudoku puzzles.
e.zh: 这款应用用人工智能求解器破解数独谜题。

solves.t: v. 解决（第三人称单数）

e.en: This update {solves} the crash issue many users reported.
e.zh: 这次更新解决了许多用户反映的崩溃问题。

e.en: He {solves} crossword puzzles every morning with coffee.
e.zh: 他每天早上一边喝咖啡一边解填字游戏。

e.en: She enjoys {solving} tricky logic puzzles in her free time.
e.zh: 她喜欢在空闲时解决棘手的逻辑谜题。

e.en: The team spent hours {solving} the production bug.
e.zh: 团队花了几个小时解决生产环境的漏洞。

som.t: n. 索姆（中亚货币单位）

e.en: The {soma} of a neuron contains the cell nucleus.
e.zh: 神经元的胞体含有细胞核。

e.en: Yoga teachers often discuss the link between mind and {soma}.
e.zh: 瑜伽老师常谈论心灵与身体之间的联系。

somali.t:
adj. 索马里的
n. 索马里人

e.en: She speaks fluent {Somali} and English at home.
e.zh: 她在家里能流利地说索马里语和英语。

e.en: The restaurant serves traditional {Somali} dishes like sambusa.
e.zh: 这家餐厅供应像三角酥这样的传统索马里菜。

e.en: {Somalia} lies on the eastern coast of Africa.
e.zh: 索马里位于非洲东海岸。

e.en: The journalist spent three years reporting from {Somalia}.
e.zh: 那名记者在索马里报道了三年。

e.en: The festival celebrated {Somalian} music and poetry.
e.zh: 这个节日庆祝索马里的音乐和诗歌。

e.en: Her grandmother taught her several {Somalian} folk tales.
e.zh: 她奶奶教过她好几个索马里民间故事。

e.en: Anxiety often produces {somatic} symptoms like headaches.
e.zh: 焦虑常常会引发头痛等躯体症状。

e.en: The therapist uses {somatic} exercises to release stored tension.
e.zh: 治疗师用身体疗愈练习释放积累的紧张感。

e.en: {Somatostatin} inhibits the release of growth hormone.
e.zh: 生长抑素会抑制生长激素的释放。

e.en: Doctors prescribed a {somatostatin} analog to control the tumor.
e.zh: 医生开了生长抑素类似物来控制肿瘤。

e.en: The room fell into a {somber} silence after the news.
e.zh: 听到消息后,房间陷入一片沉重的寂静。

e.en: He wore a {somber} grey suit to the funeral.
e.zh: 他穿着一身肃穆的灰色西装去参加葬礼。

e.en: She nodded {somberly} as the verdict was read.
e.zh: 宣读判决时,她神情凝重地点了点头。

e.en: The pianist played {somberly}, hushing the entire hall.
e.zh: 钢琴家演奏得低沉肃穆,让整个大厅安静下来。

e.en: A strange {somberness} hung over the empty office.
e.zh: 一种奇怪的阴郁笼罩着空荡荡的办公室。

e.en: The film's {somberness} stayed with me for days.
e.zh: 这部电影的沉重感让我好几天都难以释怀。

sombre.t: adj. 阴沉的；忧郁的（英式拼写）

e.en: The painting uses {sombre} tones of brown and grey.
e.zh: 这幅画用了暗沉的棕色和灰色调。

e.en: His voice grew {sombre} as he described the accident.
e.zh: 他描述那场事故时,声音变得低沉沉重。

e.en: The crowd waited {sombrely} outside the hospital gates.
e.zh: 人群神情凝重地等候在医院门口。

e.en: He spoke {sombrely} about the company's layoffs.
e.zh: 他语气沉重地谈起公司的裁员。

e.en: The dancer wore a wide-brimmed {sombrero} on stage.
e.zh: 那位舞者戴着一顶宽边墨西哥帽登台。

e.en: Tourists love taking photos in colorful {sombreros}.
e.zh: 游客们喜欢戴着彩色的墨西哥帽拍照。

some.t:
det. 一些；某些
adj. 某个

e.en: Could you grab {some} milk on your way home?
e.zh: 你回家路上能顺便买点牛奶吗?

e.en: {Some} people prefer working late at night.
e.zh: 有些人更喜欢深夜工作。

somebody.t:
pron. 某人
n. 大人物

e.en: {Somebody} left their umbrella by the door.
e.zh: 有人把伞落在门边了。

e.en: She wants to be {somebody} important in the industry.
e.zh: 她想成为业内有头有脸的人物。

someday.t: adv. 有朝一日；将来某天

e.en: I hope to visit Japan {someday} soon.
e.zh: 我希望有朝一日能去日本看看。

e.en: {Someday} you'll look back and laugh at this.
e.zh: 总有一天你回头看会觉得好笑。

somehow.t: adv. 不知怎么地；以某种方式

e.en: {Somehow} the cat opened the fridge by itself.
e.zh: 不知怎么的,猫自己把冰箱打开了。

e.en: We need to finish the project {somehow} before Friday.
e.zh: 我们得想办法在周五前完成这个项目。

e.en: {Someone} is knocking at the front door.
e.zh: 有人在敲前门。

e.en: She's waiting for {someone} to call her back.
e.zh: 她在等某个人回电话。

e.en: Let's go {someplace} quiet for dinner tonight.
e.zh: 今晚我们找个安静的地方吃晚餐吧。

e.en: I left my keys {someplace} in the kitchen.
e.zh: 我把钥匙落在厨房的某个地方了。

somersault.t:
n. 翻筋斗
v. 翻跟头

e.en: The gymnast did a perfect {somersault} on the mat.
e.zh: 那位体操运动员在垫子上完成了一个完美的前空翻。

e.en: My stomach did a {somersault} when I saw the bill.
e.zh: 看到账单时,我的胃一下子翻腾起来。

somersaulted.t: v. 翻了筋斗（somersault 的过去式）

e.en: The skateboarder {somersaulted} off the ramp gracefully.
e.zh: 那位滑板手优雅地从坡道上翻了一个跟头。

e.en: The car {somersaulted} twice before landing in the ditch.
e.zh: 那辆车翻滚了两圈才掉进沟里。

e.en: The acrobats kept {somersaulting} across the stage.
e.zh: 杂技演员们不停地在舞台上翻着跟头。

e.en: Dolphins were {somersaulting} playfully beside the boat.
e.zh: 海豚在船边欢快地翻着筋斗。

e.en: The toddler does {somersaults} on the living room rug.
e.zh: 小朋友在客厅地毯上翻跟头。

e.en: My heart turned {somersaults} when she said yes.
e.zh: 她答应的那一刻,我的心激动得翻腾起来。

somerset.t: n. 萨默塞特（英国郡名）

e.en: We spent the weekend hiking through rural {Somerset}.
e.zh: 我们整个周末都在萨默塞特乡间徒步。

e.en: {Somerset} is famous for its cider and cheddar cheese.
e.zh: 萨默塞特郡以苹果酒和切达奶酪闻名。

e.en: The train stops briefly at {Somerton} station.
e.zh: 火车在萨默顿车站短暂停靠。

e.en: She grew up in a quiet village near {Somerton}.
e.zh: 她在萨默顿附近一个安静的村子里长大。

somerville.t: n. 萨默维尔（地名/人名）

e.en: {Somerville} sits just north of Boston, Massachusetts.
e.zh: 萨默维尔位于马萨诸塞州波士顿的北边。

e.en: The coffee shops in {Somerville} are popular with students.
e.zh: 萨默维尔的咖啡馆很受学生欢迎。

e.en: There's {something} stuck in my shoe.
e.zh: 有东西卡在我鞋子里了。

e.en: She said {something} funny that made everyone laugh.
e.zh: 她说了句好笑的话,把大家都逗乐了。

sometime.t:
adv. 某个时候
adj. 以前的

e.en: Let's grab coffee {sometime} next week.
e.zh: 我们下周找个时间一起喝咖啡吧。

e.en: He arrived {sometime} after midnight last night.
e.zh: 他昨晚是在午夜后某个时候到的。

e.en: I {sometimes} skip breakfast when I'm running late.
e.zh: 我赶时间的时候有时会不吃早饭。

e.en: {Sometimes} the simplest answer is the right one.
e.zh: 有时候最简单的答案就是正确的答案。

e.en: The new menu is {somewhat} more expensive than before.
e.zh: 新菜单比以前稍微贵了一些。

e.en: I was {somewhat} surprised by her sudden resignation.
e.zh: 她突然辞职让我有些意外。

e.en: My phone is charging {somewhere} in the bedroom.
e.zh: 我的手机在卧室里某个地方充着电。

e.en: Let's drive {somewhere} new this weekend.
e.zh: 这周末我们开车去个新地方吧。

somewheres.t: adv. 某处（somewhere 的方言形式）

e.en: He must have dropped his wallet {somewheres} on the road.
e.zh: 他肯定把钱包丢在路上的某个地方了。

e.en: She said she'd seen that face {somewheres} before.
e.zh: 她说她以前在哪儿见过那张脸。

somme.t: n. 索姆河（法国河流，一战战场）

e.en: The Battle of the {Somme} cost over a million casualties.
e.zh: 索姆河战役造成了上百万人伤亡。

e.en: The river {Somme} flows through northern France.
e.zh: 索姆河流经法国北部。

e.en: The {sommelier} recommended a crisp white wine with the fish.
e.zh: 侍酒师推荐了一款清爽的白葡萄酒搭配鱼料理。

e.en: She trained for years to become a certified {sommelier}.
e.zh: 她经过多年训练才成为持证侍酒师。

e.en: A pleasant {somnolence} settled over the afternoon classroom.
e.zh: 午后的教室里弥漫着一种惬意的困倦感。

e.en: The medication's main side effect is {somnolence}.
e.zh: 这种药物的主要副作用是嗜睡。

somnolent.t: adj. 困倦的；催人入睡的

e.en: The {somnolent} hum of the heater nearly put me to sleep.
e.zh: 暖气催人入眠的嗡嗡声差点让我睡着。

e.en: After lunch the whole village felt {somnolent}.
e.zh: 午饭后整个村子都昏昏欲睡。

e.en: My {son-in-law} cooks the best pasta in the family.
e.zh: 我女婿做的意面是全家最好吃的。

e.en: She introduced her new {son-in-law} to the neighbors.
e.zh: 她把新女婿介绍给了邻居们。

sonar.t: n. 声纳（水下探测系统）

e.en: The submarine uses {sonar} to map the ocean floor.
e.zh: 潜艇使用声呐来绘制海底地图。

e.en: Dolphins navigate using a natural form of {sonar}.
e.zh: 海豚利用一种天然的声呐来辨别方向。

e.en: She practiced the Beethoven {sonata} every morning.
e.zh: 她每天早上都练习贝多芬的奏鸣曲。

e.en: The recital opened with a gentle piano {sonata}.
e.zh: 独奏会以一首柔和的钢琴奏鸣曲开场。

e.en: That {song} has been stuck in my head all day.
e.zh: 那首歌一整天都在我脑子里循环。

e.en: She wrote a {song} about her grandmother's garden.
e.zh: 她写了一首关于奶奶花园的歌。

e.en: A small {songbird} landed on the windowsill at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时分,一只小鸣禽落在了窗台上。

e.en: The singer was hailed as the {songbird} of her generation.
e.zh: 那位歌手被誉为她那一代的歌坛百灵。

e.en: She flipped through the old church {songbook} for a hymn.
e.zh: 她翻着那本旧教堂歌本找一首赞美诗。

e.en: His latest album revisits the classic American {songbook}.
e.zh: 他最新的专辑重新演绎了经典的美国歌曲集。

e.en: The playlist has over a hundred indie {songs}.
e.zh: 这个播放列表里有上百首独立音乐。

e.en: She sings traditional folk {songs} at the festival.
e.zh: 她在节日上演唱传统民谣。

e.en: The local {songster} entertained guests at the wedding.
e.zh: 那位本地歌手在婚礼上助兴。

e.en: That tiny {songster} fills the garden with melody each spring.
e.zh: 那只小鸣鸟每年春天都用歌声充满花园。

e.en: The jazz {songstress} captivated the audience for two hours.
e.zh: 那位爵士女歌手让观众沉醉了两个小时。

e.en: Critics call her the finest {songstress} of the decade.
e.zh: 评论家称她为这十年来最出色的女歌手。

e.en: She works as a {songwriter} for several pop artists.
e.zh: 她为好几位流行歌手担任词曲作者。

e.en: The award honored him as best new {songwriter}.
e.zh: 这个奖项表彰他为最佳新人词曲作者。

songwriting.t: n. 歌曲创作；词曲创作
