e.en: The doctor pressed gently on each {spinous} process of the spine.
e.zh: 医生轻轻按压脊柱上每个棘突。

e.en: This plant has {spinous} leaves that deter grazing animals.
e.zh: 这种植物长着带刺的叶子，可阻止动物啃食。

spinoza.t: n. 斯宾诺莎（荷兰哲学家）

e.en: Many philosophers still debate {Spinoza}'s views on God and nature.
e.zh: 许多哲学家至今仍在讨论斯宾诺莎关于神与自然的观点。

e.en: She wrote her thesis on {Spinoza}'s ethics.
e.zh: 她的论文写的是斯宾诺莎的伦理学。

spins.t:
v. 旋转；纺（spin 的三单）
n. 旋转；说法

e.en: The dancer {spins} gracefully across the stage.
e.zh: 那位舞者优雅地在舞台上旋转。

e.en: The press secretary often {spins} bad news into something positive.
e.zh: 新闻秘书常把坏消息粉饰成正面消息。

e.en: The old novel describes her as a lonely village {spinster}.
e.zh: 那本旧小说把她描绘成一位孤独的乡村老处女。

e.en: Modern women reject the outdated label of {spinster}.
e.zh: 现代女性拒绝接受“老处女”这一过时标签。

e.en: In that era, {spinsterhood} was viewed with unfair pity.
e.zh: 在那个年代，未婚单身女性常被不公平地怜悯看待。

e.en: She embraced {spinsterhood} as a path to independence.
e.zh: 她将单身生活视为通往独立的道路。

e.en: Be careful — that cactus has very {spiny} edges.
e.zh: 小心——那株仙人掌边缘布满尖刺。

e.en: The {spiny} anteater curled up to protect itself.
e.zh: 那只针鼹蜷成一团保护自己。

spiral.t:
n. 螺旋
adj. 螺旋形的

e.en: House prices began to {spiral} out of control last year.
e.zh: 去年房价开始失控般飙升。

e.en: She drew a perfect {spiral} in her notebook.
e.zh: 她在笔记本上画了一个完美的螺旋。

spiraling.t: v. 螺旋式变化；急剧上升

e.en: Costs are {spiraling} upward faster than the budget allows.
e.zh: 成本上升的速度比预算允许的还要快。

e.en: The hawk kept {spiraling} higher into the bright sky.
e.zh: 那只鹰盘旋着越飞越高，进入明亮的天空。

spiralling.t: v. 螺旋式变化（英式拼写）

e.en: The country faces {spiralling} inflation and rising unemployment.
e.zh: 该国面临通胀飙升和失业上升的困境。

e.en: Smoke was {spiralling} up from the chimney into the cold air.
e.zh: 烟从烟囱里盘旋而上，飘入寒冷的空气中。

e.en: The church {spire} is visible from miles away.
e.zh: 教堂的尖塔从几英里外就能看到。

e.en: Lightning struck the cathedral {spire} during the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨中闪电击中了大教堂的尖顶。

e.en: The white {spirea} blooms beautifully every spring.
e.zh: 白色的绣线菊每年春天都开得很美。

e.en: She planted a row of {spirea} along the fence.
e.zh: 她沿着篱笆种了一排绣线菊。

e.en: Oxford is famous for its dreaming {spires} and old colleges.
e.zh: 牛津以其梦幻般的尖塔和古老学院而闻名。

e.en: The cathedral's twin {spires} dominated the city skyline.
e.zh: 大教堂的双尖塔主宰着城市的天际线。

e.en: She tackled the challenge with an unbreakable {spirit}.
e.zh: 她以不屈的精神迎接挑战。

e.en: The team showed great {spirit} despite losing the game.
e.zh: 尽管输了比赛，球队仍展现出极佳的斗志。

e.en: They had a {spirited} debate about climate policy.
e.zh: 他们就气候政策展开了一场激烈的辩论。

e.en: She gave a {spirited} performance that wowed the audience.
e.zh: 她的精彩表演令观众叹为观止。

e.en: The children sang {spiritedly} during the school assembly.
e.zh: 孩子们在学校集会上朝气蓬勃地唱着歌。

e.en: She defended her thesis {spiritedly} against tough questions.
e.zh: 面对尖锐的提问，她精神抖擞地为自己的论文辩护。

e.en: Her {spiritedness} made her stand out in any room.
e.zh: 她的活力让她在任何场合都格外出众。

e.en: The puppy's {spiritedness} kept the whole family entertained.
e.zh: 那只小狗的活泼劲儿逗乐了全家人。

e.en: After the loss, the team played a {spiritless} second half.
e.zh: 失利后，球队下半场打得毫无斗志。

e.en: His {spiritless} reply showed he had given up.
e.zh: 他无精打采的回答表明他已经放弃了。

spirits.t:
n. 情绪；烈酒
n. 精神（复数）

e.en: A walk in the park lifted my {spirits} immediately.
e.zh: 在公园里走一走，我的心情立刻好起来。

e.en: The shop sells fine wines and imported {spirits}.
e.zh: 这家店出售优质葡萄酒和进口烈酒。

e.en: Meditation is an important part of her {spiritual} practice.
e.zh: 冥想是她精神修行的重要部分。

e.en: He went on a {spiritual} retreat to find inner peace.
e.zh: 他参加了一次心灵静修，以寻求内心的平静。

e.en: {Spiritualism} became popular in the nineteenth century.
e.zh: 招魂论在十九世纪盛行一时。

e.en: She studies {spiritualism} and its influence on modern wellness.
e.zh: 她研究灵性主义及其对现代健康观念的影响。

spiritualist.t: n. 招魂论者；唯灵论者

e.en: The {spiritualist} claimed to communicate with the dead.
e.zh: 那位通灵者声称能与逝者沟通。

e.en: She visited a {spiritualist} hoping for a message from her mother.
e.zh: 她去找一位通灵者，希望能收到母亲传来的讯息。

e.en: She explored Eastern {spirituality} after her trip to India.
e.zh: 她去印度旅行后开始探索东方灵性。

e.en: The book explores {spirituality} in modern urban life.
e.zh: 这本书探讨现代都市生活中的灵性。

e.en: Yoga helps me feel {spiritually} grounded each morning.
e.zh: 瑜伽让我每天清晨在精神上感到踏实。

e.en: They are very different but {spiritually} connected.
e.zh: 他们差异很大,但在精神上彼此相连。

spiro.t: 前缀. 表示"螺旋、呼吸"

e.en: Doctors used a {spiro} test to check her lung capacity.
e.zh: 医生用肺活量测试检查她的肺功能。

e.en: The clinic ordered a {spiro} machine for breathing assessments.
e.zh: 诊所订购了一台呼吸评估用的肺量计。

e.en: Lyme disease is caused by a tick-borne {spirochete}.
e.zh: 莱姆病是由蜱虫携带的螺旋体引起的。

e.en: The lab identified a {spirochete} under the microscope.
e.zh: 实验室在显微镜下识别出一种螺旋体。

spit.t:
v. 吐（唾沫）
n. 唾液

e.en: Don't {spit} on the sidewalk—it's gross and illegal.
e.zh: 别在人行道上吐痰,既恶心又违法。

e.en: The chef roasted the lamb on a {spit} over coals.
e.zh: 厨师把羊肉串在烤叉上用炭火烤。

spitball.t: n. 嚼成团的纸团；粗略想法

e.en: Let's {spitball} some ideas before the formal pitch.
e.zh: 我们在正式提案前先随便聊聊一些想法。

e.en: A kid threw a {spitball} across the classroom.
e.zh: 一个孩子在教室里扔了一个纸团。

spite.t:
n. 恶意；怨恨
phr. in spite of 尽管

e.en: She showed up {spite} the heavy rain outside.
e.zh: 尽管外面下着大雨,她还是来了。

e.en: He deleted the file out of pure {spite}.
e.zh: 他纯粹出于怨恨删除了那个文件。

e.en: Her {spiteful} comment ruined the whole dinner.
e.zh: 她那句恶毒的话毁了整顿晚餐。

e.en: Don't be {spiteful}—just let the argument go.
e.zh: 别那么记仇了,这场争论就放下吧。

e.en: He {spitefully} unfollowed her on every platform.
e.zh: 他怀着报复心在每个平台上都取关了她。

e.en: She slammed the door {spitefully} after the fight.
e.zh: 吵完架后她怀着怨气狠狠摔上了门。

e.en: He {spites} his rival by leaking the news first.
e.zh: 他抢先泄露消息来报复对手。

e.en: She often {spites} her neighbor with loud music.
e.zh: 她经常用大声放音乐来气她的邻居。

spitfire.t: n. 暴躁的人；喷火战机

e.en: Their toddler is a tiny {spitfire} with strong opinions.
e.zh: 他们家小孩是个倔强又有主见的小辣椒。

e.en: The {spitfire} coach pushed the team to the finals.
e.zh: 那位火爆的教练把球队带进了决赛。

e.en: Old maps mark several {spittals} along the pilgrim road.
e.zh: 古地图在朝圣路上标出了几处旧时的医护所。

e.en: Medieval {spittals} cared for travelers and the sick.
e.zh: 中世纪的医护所照料旅人和病患。

spitter.t: n. 吐唾沫的人；口水球投手

e.en: That pitcher is a notorious {spitter} on the mound.
e.zh: 那位投手在投手丘上是出了名的吐口水的人。

e.en: The llama turned out to be a serious {spitter}.
e.zh: 那只羊驼原来是个超爱吐口水的家伙。

e.en: The cat was {spitting} and arching its back angrily.
e.zh: 那只猫炸毛拱背,愤怒地嘶嘶叫着。

e.en: She's the {spitting} image of her grandmother.
e.zh: 她和她奶奶简直一模一样。

e.en: Tiny drops of {spittle} flew as he shouted.
e.zh: 他大喊时,几滴口水飞溅了出来。

e.en: The dentist wiped the {spittle} from the patient's chin.
e.zh: 牙医擦掉了病人下巴上的口水。

e.en: An old brass {spittoon} stood beside the saloon door.
e.zh: 酒馆门旁立着一个旧黄铜痰盂。

e.en: Cowboys aimed tobacco juice at the corner {spittoon}.
e.zh: 牛仔们把烟草汁往角落的痰盂里吐。

spiv.t: n. 游手好闲者；投机倒把者

e.en: That flashy {spiv} tried to sell me a fake watch.
e.zh: 那个花哨的小骗子想卖我一块假表。

e.en: In old British films, the {spiv} always wore loud suits.
e.zh: 在老式英国电影里,那种小混混总穿着花哨的西装。

splash.t:
v. 溅；泼洒
n. 水花

e.en: The kids love to {splash} in the pool all afternoon.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢整个下午在泳池里泼水嬉戏。

e.en: Her new album made a huge {splash} online.
e.zh: 她的新专辑在网上引起了巨大轰动。

e.en: The capsule's {splashdown} in the Pacific went smoothly.
e.zh: 飞船舱在太平洋的溅落非常顺利。

e.en: Crowds watched the live {splashdown} of the SpaceX mission.
e.zh: 人们观看了SpaceX任务溅落返回的直播。

e.en: A passing truck {splashed} muddy water onto my jeans.
e.zh: 一辆经过的卡车把泥水溅到了我的牛仔裤上。

e.en: The headline was {splashed} across every front page.
e.zh: 那条头条登上了每一份报纸的头版。

splashes.t:
n. 水花；飞溅
v. 溅起（三单）

e.en: The painting has bold {splashes} of red and yellow.
e.zh: 这幅画上有大胆的红色和黄色泼点。

e.en: He {splashes} cold water on his face every morning.
e.zh: 他每天早上都用冷水拍脸。

splashing.t: v. 飞溅；泼水（现在分词）

e.en: The dog kept {splashing} water out of its bowl.
e.zh: 那只狗一直把水从碗里溅出来。

e.en: Kids were {splashing} happily in the shallow end.
e.zh: 孩子们在浅水区开心地玩水。

splashy.t: adj. 引人注目的；华丽的

e.en: The startup launched with a {splashy} marketing campaign.
e.zh: 那家初创公司以一场轰动的营销活动开张。

e.en: She wore a {splashy} dress covered in bright flowers.
e.zh: 她穿了一条满是鲜艳花朵的抢眼连衣裙。

splat.t:
n. 啪嗒声
v. 啪嗒落下

e.en: The tomato hit the wall with a wet {splat}.
e.zh: 番茄啪的一声湿漉漉地砸在了墙上。

e.en: His pancake landed on the floor with a {splat}.
e.zh: 他的薄煎饼啪嗒一声掉在了地上。

splatter.t:
v. 溅洒
n. 飞溅物

e.en: Be careful not to {splatter} oil on the stove.
e.zh: 小心别把油溅到炉灶上。

e.en: Red paint left a {splatter} across the white canvas.
e.zh: 红颜料在白色画布上留下了一片飞溅。

e.en: His shirt was {splattered} with sauce after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后他的衬衫上溅满了酱汁。

e.en: Mud {splattered} the windshield as we drove off-road.
e.zh: 我们越野行驶时泥点溅满了挡风玻璃。

e.en: Stop {splattering} ketchup all over the counter, please.
e.zh: 请别再把番茄酱溅得满台面都是。

e.en: The {splattering} sound came from the leaking pipe.
e.zh: 啪嗒啪嗒的声音来自那根漏水的管子。

splatters.t:
v. 飞溅（三单）
n. 飞溅物

e.en: Tiny {splatters} of ink dotted the artist's apron.
e.zh: 艺术家的围裙上点缀着小小的墨点。

e.en: She {splatters} paint on the canvas in wild bursts.
e.zh: 她随性地把颜料泼洒在画布上。

e.en: Don't {splay} your fingers when typing on the keyboard.
e.zh: 打字的时候不要把手指张得太开。

e.en: The puppy's legs {splay} out when it sleeps.
e.zh: 小狗睡觉时会把腿摊开。

e.en: He sat with his legs {splayed} across the couch.
e.zh: 他坐在沙发上,腿叉得开开的。

e.en: The book lay {splayed} open on the table.
e.zh: 那本书摊开着躺在桌上。

spelled.t: v. 拼写（spell 的过去式）

e.en: She {spelled} her name slowly so the receptionist could write it.
e.zh: 她慢慢地拼出名字让前台记下来。

e.en: The slow sales {spelled} trouble for the small bookstore.
e.zh: 销售低迷意味着这家小书店麻烦不小。

e.en: He's a terrible {speller} but a great writer overall.
e.zh: 他拼写很糟，但总体上是个出色的作家。

e.en: The app works like a digital {speller} for kids.
e.zh: 这款应用就像给孩子用的数字拼字训练器。

spelling.t:
n. 拼写；拼法
v. 拼写（现在分词）

e.en: My {spelling} has improved since I started reading more.
e.zh: 自从我多读书以后，我的拼写水平提高了。

e.en: The teacher marked every {spelling} mistake in red.
e.zh: 老师用红笔标出了每一个拼写错误。

e.en: British and American {spellings} differ for many common words.
e.zh: 许多常见单词的英式和美式拼写方式不同。

e.en: The dictionary lists both {spellings} as acceptable.
e.zh: 字典将两种拼写都列为可接受的形式。

spells.t:
v. 拼写（第三人称单数）
n. 一段时间；咒语

e.en: The wizard cast powerful {spells} to defeat the dragon.
e.zh: 巫师施展了强大的咒语来击败那条龙。

e.en: This delay {spells} disaster for our launch schedule.
e.zh: 这次延误对我们的发布计划意味着灾难。

e.en: As a {spelunker}, she has explored caves on three continents.
e.zh: 作为一名洞穴探险者，她已在三个大洲探查过洞穴。

e.en: An experienced {spelunker} always brings backup lights underground.
e.zh: 经验丰富的洞穴探险者下到地下时总会带备用灯。

e.en: She kept jars of jam in the cool {spence} downstairs.
e.zh: 她把一罐罐果酱放在楼下阴凉的食品储藏室里。

e.en: The old farmhouse still had its original stone {spence}.
e.zh: 那座老农舍仍保留着原先的石砌储藏间。

spencer.t: n. 短款外套；人名 斯宾塞

e.en: She wore a tailored {spencer} over her long white dress.
e.zh: 她在白色长裙外套了一件剪裁合身的短外套。

e.en: The vintage {spencer} jacket suited the period drama perfectly.
e.zh: 那件复古短上衣非常适合这部时代剧。

spencerian.t: adj. 斯宾塞派的；斯宾塞式手写体的

e.en: Her wedding invitations featured elegant {spencerian} script.
e.zh: 她的婚礼请柬采用了优雅的斯宾塞体书法。

e.en: He learned {spencerian} handwriting from his grandmother.
e.zh: 他从祖母那里学会了斯宾塞体手写字。

e.en: Several embroidered {spencers} hung in the museum's costume display.
e.zh: 博物馆的服饰展中挂着几件刺绣短外套。

e.en: The dancers wore matching white {spencers} on stage.
e.zh: 舞者们在台上都穿着配套的白色短外套。

e.en: I {spend} too much money on coffee every week.
e.zh: 我每周在咖啡上花的钱太多了。

e.en: Let's {spend} the weekend hiking in the mountains.
e.zh: 我们周末去山里徒步吧。

e.en: My sister is a big {spender} when it comes to shoes.
e.zh: 我姐姐在买鞋方面是个大手大脚的人。

e.en: He's a careful {spender} who tracks every expense.
e.zh: 他花钱很谨慎，每笔开支都会记录。

spending.t:
n. 支出；开销
v. 花费（现在分词）

e.en: Government {spending} on healthcare increased significantly this year.
e.zh: 政府今年在医疗方面的支出显著增加。

e.en: I'm {spending} the holidays with my family this year.
e.zh: 今年假期我打算和家人一起过。

e.en: She tracks her monthly {spendings} in a budgeting app.
e.zh: 她用记账应用记录每月的开销。

e.en: Household {spendings} have risen sharply due to inflation.
e.zh: 由于通胀，家庭开支大幅上升。

spends.t: v. 花费（第三人称单数）

e.en: He {spends} most weekends working on his garden.
e.zh: 他大部分周末都花在打理花园上。

e.en: She {spends} hours scrolling through social media each night.
e.zh: 她每晚都花好几个小时刷社交媒体。

spendthrift.t:
n. 挥霍无度的人
adj. 挥霍的

e.en: His {spendthrift} habits left him broke by month's end.
e.zh: 他挥霍无度的习惯让他到月底就身无分文。

e.en: She married a charming but reckless {spendthrift}.
e.zh: 她嫁给了一个迷人却挥霍无度的男人。

spent.t:
v. spend 的过去式
adj. 用完的；精疲力竭的

e.en: I {spent} the whole weekend fixing bugs in the app.
e.zh: 我整个周末都在修复应用里的漏洞。

e.en: After the marathon she felt completely {spent} and exhausted.
e.zh: 跑完马拉松后她感到精疲力竭。

e.en: The clinic froze his {sperm} for future use.
e.zh: 诊所冷冻了他的精子以备将来使用。

e.en: A {sperm} whale was spotted off the coast yesterday.
e.zh: 昨天在海岸附近发现了一头抹香鲸。

e.en: The male squid transfers a {spermatophore} during mating.
e.zh: 雄性鱿鱼在交配时会传递一个精荚。

e.en: Scientists studied the {spermatophore} structure under a microscope.
e.zh: 科学家在显微镜下研究了精荚的结构。

e.en: Healthy {spermatozoa} swim quickly toward the egg.
e.zh: 健康的精子会快速游向卵子。

e.en: The lab counted {spermatozoa} in each fertility sample.
e.zh: 实验室对每份生育样本中的精子进行了计数。

e.en: She bought a condom coated with {spermicide} for extra protection.
e.zh: 她买了涂有杀精剂的避孕套以增加保护。

e.en: Some people are allergic to the chemicals in {spermicide}.
e.zh: 有些人对杀精剂中的化学成分过敏。

e.en: The volcano began to {spew} ash across nearby villages.
e.zh: 火山开始向附近的村庄喷出火山灰。

e.en: Don't let the bot {spew} spam into our chat.
e.zh: 别让那个机器人在我们的聊天里乱发垃圾信息。

e.en: He learned to {spey} cast on the river last summer.
e.zh: 他去年夏天在河边学会了双手抛投。

e.en: The {spey} rod is longer than a typical fly rod.
e.zh: 双手飞蝇竿比普通飞蝇竿要长一些。

spf.t: n. 防晒指数（Sun Protection Factor）

e.en: Gardeners mix {sphagnum} moss into soil to retain moisture.
e.zh: 园丁会把泥炭藓拌入土壤以保持湿度。

e.en: The bog floor was thick with damp {sphagnum}.
e.zh: 沼泽地面铺满了厚厚的潮湿泥炭藓。

sphenoid.t:
n. 蝶骨
adj. 楔形的

e.en: The {sphenoid} bone sits at the base of the skull.
e.zh: 蝶骨位于颅骨的底部。

e.en: Her CT scan revealed a fracture in the {sphenoid}.
e.zh: 她的CT扫描显示蝶骨有骨折。

e.en: Brain freeze involves the {sphenopalatine} nerve in your palate.
e.zh: 冰淇淋头痛与上颚处的蝶腭神经有关。

e.en: The doctor performed a {sphenopalatine} block to relieve migraines.
e.zh: 医生进行了蝶腭神经阻滞以缓解偏头痛。

e.en: The Earth is not a perfect {sphere}.
e.zh: 地球并不是一个完美的球体。

e.en: Privacy belongs to the personal {sphere}, not the workplace.
e.zh: 隐私属于个人领域,而不是职场范围。

e.en: The artist suspended glass {spheres} from the ceiling.
e.zh: 艺术家把玻璃球悬挂在天花板上。

e.en: Politics and religion are very different {spheres} of life.
e.zh: 政治和宗教是生活中非常不同的两个领域。

e.en: The lens has a {spheric} surface for cleaner imaging.
e.zh: 这枚镜片采用球面设计以获得更清晰的成像。

e.en: He drew a {spheric} diagram to explain the orbit.
e.zh: 他画了一个球面图来解释轨道。

e.en: A basketball is roughly {spherical} in shape.
e.zh: 篮球大致呈球形。

e.en: The new speaker emits sound in a {spherical} pattern.
e.zh: 这款新音箱以球形方式向四周发声。

e.en: Engineers measured the {sphericity} of each ball bearing.
e.zh: 工程师测量了每个滚珠轴承的球度。

e.en: High {sphericity} means the particle is nearly a perfect ball.
e.zh: 高球度意味着颗粒接近一个完美的球体。

e.en: The Earth is technically an oblate {spheroid}, not a sphere.
e.zh: 严格来说,地球是一个扁球体而不是正球体。

e.en: Researchers grew tumor cells into a tiny {spheroid}.
e.zh: 研究人员把肿瘤细胞培养成了微小的类球体。

e.en: The planet has a slightly {spheroidal} shape, not a perfect sphere.
e.zh: 这颗行星略呈球状,并不是完美的球体。

e.en: Engineers tested {spheroidal} bearings for the wind turbine.
e.zh: 工程师测试了风力发电机用的球状轴承。

e.en: The {sphincter} muscle controls the opening of the bladder.
e.zh: 括约肌控制着膀胱的开口。

e.en: Spicy food can irritate the lower esophageal {sphincter}.
e.zh: 辛辣食物会刺激食道下端的括约肌。

e.en: The surgeon performed a {sphincterotomy} to relieve the blockage.
e.zh: 外科医生做了括约肌切开术以缓解阻塞。

e.en: Recovery from a {sphincterotomy} usually takes a few weeks.
e.zh: 括约肌切开术的恢复通常需要几周时间。

sphinx.t: n. 狮身人面像；高深莫测的人

e.en: Tourists snapped photos of the Great {Sphinx} at sunrise.
e.zh: 游客们在日出时拍下了大狮身人面像的照片。

e.en: He sat there silent like a {sphinx} all night.
e.zh: 他像狮身人面像一样,整晚一言不发地坐着。

spic.t: n. 对西语裔的蔑称（冒犯语）

e.en: Her kitchen counters are always {spic} and span.
e.zh: 她家厨房台面总是擦得一尘不染。

e.en: The hotel room was {spic} and span when we arrived.
e.zh: 我们到达时,酒店房间打扫得干干净净。

spica.t: n. 角宿一（星名）；人字形绷带

e.en: {Spica} is the brightest star in the constellation Virgo.
e.zh: 角宿一是处女座中最亮的恒星。

e.en: The nurse applied a {spica} bandage around the hip.
e.zh: 护士在髋部缠上了人字形绷带。

spice.t:
n. 香料；情趣
v. 加香料；增添趣味

e.en: A pinch of {spice} can transform a boring soup.
e.zh: 一点点香料就能让平淡的汤变得美味。

e.en: They took a weekend trip to {spice} up their routine.
e.zh: 他们去度了个周末,给日常生活添点情趣。

spiced.t:
adj. 加了香料的
v. spice 的过去式

e.en: She served {spiced} apple cider at the holiday party.
e.zh: 她在节日聚会上端出了香料苹果酒。

e.en: The chef {spiced} the stew with cumin and paprika.
e.zh: 厨师用孜然和红椒粉给炖菜调味。

spicer.t: n. 香料商；人名 斯派塞

e.en: Mr. {Spicer} runs the small bookstore on Elm Street.
e.zh: 斯派塞先生经营着榆树街上那家小书店。

e.en: The local {spicer} blends his own curry mixes.
e.zh: 当地的香料商自己调配咖喱粉。

spices.t:
n. 香料（复数）
v. 加香料

e.en: Indian cuisine uses dozens of aromatic {spices}.
e.zh: 印度菜会用到几十种香料。

e.en: She {spices} her chai with cardamom and ginger.
e.zh: 她用小豆蔻和姜给奶茶调味。

e.en: You can adjust the {spiciness} of the curry to taste.
e.zh: 你可以根据口味调整咖喱的辣度。

e.en: I love the {spiciness} of fresh Thai chili.
e.zh: 我喜欢新鲜泰国辣椒那种火辣的味道。

spick.t: adj. 崭新的（多用于 spick and span）

e.en: His new apartment was {spick} and span on move-in day.
e.zh: 搬家那天他的新公寓打扫得一尘不染。

e.en: She kept her workshop {spick} and span at all times.
e.zh: 她始终把工作间保持得整洁干净。

e.en: Sponges are supported by tiny needle-like {spicule} structures.
e.zh: 海绵由细小针状的骨针结构支撑。

e.en: Each {spicule} on the solar surface lasts only minutes.
e.zh: 太阳表面的每根针状物只能存在几分钟。

spicy.t: adj. 辛辣的；有料的；劲爆的

e.en: This noodle bowl is way too {spicy} for me.
e.zh: 这碗面对我来说实在太辣了。

e.en: She shared some {spicy} gossip about the new manager.
e.zh: 她分享了一些关于新经理的劲爆八卦。

spong.t: n. sponge 的非标准拼写

e.en: The dialect word {spong} once meant a narrow strip of land.
e.zh: 方言词 spong 曾指一条狭长的土地。

e.en: Old maps occasionally label a small {spong} between two fields.
e.zh: 旧地图上偶尔标注两块田地之间有一小块狭地。

sponge.t:
n. 海绵
v. 用海绵擦拭

e.en: Use a damp {sponge} to wipe down the counter.
e.zh: 用湿海绵擦一下台面。

e.en: Children {sponge} up new languages incredibly fast.
e.zh: 孩子们吸收新语言的速度快得惊人。

sponger.t: n. 占便宜的人；揩油者

e.en: Don't be a {sponger} who never pays for dinner.
e.zh: 别做一个从不掏钱吃饭的揩油鬼。

e.en: His roommate is a total {sponger} living off others.
e.zh: 他的室友完全是个靠别人养活的寄生虫。

sponges.t:
n. 海绵（复数）
v. 擦拭

e.en: These kitchen {sponges} should be replaced every two weeks.
e.zh: 这些厨房海绵每两周就该换一次。

e.en: She {sponges} the wound gently with warm water.
e.zh: 她用温水轻轻擦拭伤口。

e.en: Mad cow disease is a {spongiform} brain disorder in cattle.
e.zh: 疯牛病是一种使牛脑呈海绵状的脑病。

e.en: Scientists study {spongiform} encephalopathy to develop treatments.
e.zh: 科学家研究海绵状脑病以开发治疗方法。

e.en: The cake's {sponginess} made it perfect for soaking up syrup.
e.zh: 蛋糕的松软质地让它非常适合吸糖浆。

e.en: She tested the mattress for {sponginess} before buying it.
e.zh: 她在购买前试了试床垫的弹软度。

e.en: The moss felt {spongy} and damp under our shoes.
e.zh: 苔藓在鞋底下感觉松软又潮湿。

e.en: Fresh bread has a light, {spongy} texture inside.
e.zh: 新鲜面包内部有种轻盈松软的质地。

sponsor.t:
n. 赞助商；主办方
v. 赞助

e.en: Nike agreed to {sponsor} the young marathon runner.
e.zh: 耐克同意赞助这位年轻的马拉松选手。

e.en: The event's main {sponsor} provided most of the funding.
e.zh: 活动的主要赞助商提供了大部分资金。

sponsored.t:
adj. 被赞助的；推广的
v. 赞助（过去式）

e.en: This podcast episode is {sponsored} by a meal kit company.
e.zh: 本期播客由一家食材包公司赞助播出。

e.en: The company {sponsored} a charity run last weekend.
e.zh: 公司上周末赞助了一场慈善跑步活动。

e.en: Several brands are {sponsoring} the upcoming esports tournament.
e.zh: 多家品牌正在赞助即将举行的电竞比赛。

e.en: She is {sponsoring} a child's education in rural Kenya.
e.zh: 她正资助肯尼亚农村一个孩子上学。

sponsors.t:
n. 赞助商（复数）
v. 赞助

e.en: The festival lost two major {sponsors} this year.
e.zh: 今年这个节日失去了两个主要赞助商。

e.en: He {sponsors} a youth basketball team in his hometown.
e.zh: 他赞助了家乡的一支青少年篮球队。

e.en: She landed a lucrative {sponsorship} deal with a sportswear brand.
e.zh: 她拿到了一份与运动品牌的高额赞助合约。

e.en: The team relies heavily on corporate {sponsorship} to operate.
e.zh: 该队的运营严重依赖企业赞助。

e.en: Top influencers earn millions from brand {sponsorships} each year.
e.zh: 顶级网红每年靠品牌赞助赚取数百万。

e.en: The athlete signed three new {sponsorships} after winning gold.
e.zh: 这位运动员夺金后签下了三份新赞助合约。

e.en: Their relationship thrived on small daily {spontaneities} and surprises.
e.zh: 他们的感情在日常的小惊喜与即兴之中蓬勃生长。

e.en: Travel allows for the kind of {spontaneities} routine forbids.
e.zh: 旅行让人能体验日常生活中无法实现的种种即兴时刻。

e.en: I love the {spontaneity} of a last-minute road trip.
e.zh: 我喜欢临时起意来一场公路旅行的那种随性。

e.en: Her performance lacked any sense of {spontaneity}.
e.zh: 她的表演毫无即兴自然的感觉。

e.en: They made a {spontaneous} decision to fly to Tokyo.
e.zh: 他们临时起意决定飞去东京。

e.en: The crowd broke into {spontaneous} applause after the speech.
e.zh: 演讲结束后人群自发地鼓起掌来。

e.en: The audience {spontaneously} stood up and cheered.
e.zh: 观众们不约而同地起立欢呼。

e.en: Old phones can {spontaneously} shut down when the battery degrades.
e.zh: 旧手机在电池老化后可能会自动关机。

spoof.t:
n. 恶搞；戏仿
v. 伪造（IP 等）

e.en: The video is a hilarious {spoof} of a luxury car ad.
e.zh: 这段视频是对豪车广告的搞笑恶搞。

e.en: Scammers {spoof} caller IDs to trick elderly victims.
e.zh: 骗子伪造来电显示来欺骗老年受害者。

spook.t:
n. 幽灵
v. 惊吓

e.en: Loud fireworks tend to {spook} the neighborhood dogs.
e.zh: 巨大的烟花声往往会吓到街坊的狗。

e.en: The empty hallway gave her a real {spook} at midnight.
e.zh: 午夜空荡荡的走廊把她吓得不轻。

e.en: Investors got {spooked} by the sudden drop in earnings.
e.zh: 投资者被突如其来的盈利下滑吓到了。

e.en: The horse {spooked} when a plastic bag blew across the path.
e.zh: 一只塑料袋从路上吹过,马受了惊。

e.en: The hallway was {spookily} quiet after midnight.
e.zh: 过了午夜，走廊安静得让人发毛。

e.en: Her prediction was {spookily} accurate this time.
e.zh: 她这次的预测准得令人毛骨悚然。

e.en: The old house looks really {spooky} at night.
e.zh: 那栋老房子晚上看起来很阴森。

e.en: We watched a {spooky} movie on Halloween.
e.zh: 我们在万圣节看了一部恐怖片。

spool.t:
n. 线轴；卷盘
v. 假脱机（打印缓存）

e.en: She wound the thread back onto the {spool}.
e.zh: 她把线重新绕回线轴上。

e.en: The printer needs a new {spool} of label tape.
e.zh: 打印机需要换一卷新的标签带。

spoon.t:
n. 勺子
v. 用勺舀

e.en: He stirred the soup with a wooden {spoon}.
e.zh: 他用一把木勺搅汤。

e.en: Please pass me a {spoon} for my yogurt.
e.zh: 请递给我一把勺子吃酸奶。

e.en: A pink {spoonbill} waded through the shallow marsh.
e.zh: 一只粉色琵鹭在浅滩沼泽里涉水。

e.en: The {spoonbill} uses its flat bill to filter food.
e.zh: 琵鹭用扁平的喙过滤食物。

e.en: Reverend {Spooner} was famous for mixing up his words.
e.zh: 斯普纳牧师以说话颠三倒四而闻名。

e.en: The term is named after William {Spooner}.
e.zh: 这个术语是以威廉·斯普纳的名字命名的。

e.en: "Belly jeans" instead of jelly beans is a classic {spoonerism}.
e.zh: 把jelly beans说成belly jeans是经典的首音互换。

e.en: He made a funny {spoonerism} during the speech.
e.zh: 他在演讲中说出了一个搞笑的首音互换。

e.en: Add a {spoonful} of sugar to the tea.
e.zh: 往茶里加一勺糖。

e.en: She took a {spoonful} of medicine before bed.
e.zh: 她睡前喝了一勺药。

e.en: The drawer is full of mismatched {spoons}.
e.zh: 抽屉里堆满了款式不一的勺子。

e.en: We need more {spoons} for the dessert table.
e.zh: 甜品台还需要更多勺子。

spoor.t: n. 野兽的足迹或气味

e.en: The ranger followed the lion's {spoor} through the bush.
e.zh: 护林员沿着狮子的足迹穿过灌木丛。

e.en: Fresh {spoor} suggested elephants had passed recently.
e.zh: 新鲜的足迹表明大象刚刚经过。

e.en: There were {sporadic} showers throughout the afternoon.
e.zh: 整个下午都有零星阵雨。

e.en: His attendance has been {sporadic} this semester.
e.zh: 他这学期出勤很不稳定。

e.en: The website crashes {sporadically} during peak hours.
e.zh: 网站在高峰时段会偶发崩溃。

e.en: She updates her blog {sporadically} these days.
e.zh: 她最近只是断断续续地更新博客。

e.en: Each mushroom releases millions of {spore} cells.
e.zh: 每个蘑菇都会释放数百万个孢子细胞。

e.en: The fern reproduces by scattering {spore} into the wind.
e.zh: 蕨类通过把孢子散到风中进行繁殖。

e.en: The moss {sporophyte} grows on top of the leafy plant.
e.zh: 苔藓的孢子体长在叶状植物的顶端。

e.en: In ferns, the {sporophyte} is the dominant generation.
e.zh: 在蕨类中，孢子体是主要世代。

sporran.t: n. 苏格兰裙前毛皮袋

e.en: He wore a kilt with a leather {sporran} at the wedding.
e.zh: 他在婚礼上穿苏格兰短裙，配着皮制毛皮袋。

e.en: The {sporran} hung in front of his kilt.
e.zh: 那只毛皮袋挂在他短裙的前面。

sport.t:
n. 运动；体育
v. 炫耀地穿戴

e.en: Soccer is the most popular {sport} in the world.
e.zh: 足球是世界上最受欢迎的运动。

e.en: She likes to {sport} a bright red scarf in winter.
e.zh: 她冬天喜欢戴一条鲜红色的围巾。

sportfisherman.t: n. 运动钓鱼者；钓鱼船

e.en: The {sportfisherman} reeled in a huge marlin off the coast.
e.zh: 那位海钓爱好者在近海钓上了一条大旗鱼。

e.en: He bought a sleek {sportfisherman} boat for weekend trips.
e.zh: 他买了一艘流线型的运动钓鱼艇周末出海。

e.en: The stadium hosts major {sporting} events every year.
e.zh: 这座体育场每年举办大型体育赛事。

e.en: He was {sporting} a brand-new pair of sneakers.
e.zh: 他炫耀地穿着一双全新的运动鞋。

e.en: She {sportingly} congratulated her opponent after losing.
e.zh: 她输了之后大方地向对手表示祝贺。

e.en: He {sportingly} agreed to try the spicy challenge.
e.zh: 他爽快地答应尝试那个辣味挑战。

e.en: The puppies were in a {sportive} mood that morning.
e.zh: 那天早上小狗们都很爱玩闹。

e.en: Her {sportive} remarks made everyone laugh.
e.zh: 她俏皮的话语逗得大家哈哈大笑。

sports.t:
n. 体育运动
adj. 运动型的

e.en: He watches {sports} every weekend on TV.
e.zh: 他每个周末都在电视上看体育比赛。

e.en: Our school offers many {sports} after class.
e.zh: 我们学校课后开设很多体育项目。

e.en: He saved for years to buy a red {sportscar}.
e.zh: 他攒了好几年钱才买下那辆红色跑车。

e.en: The {sportscar} accelerated smoothly onto the highway.
e.zh: 那辆跑车平稳地加速驶上高速公路。

e.en: I caught the {sportscast} right before dinner.
e.zh: 我在晚饭前正好看到了体育新闻。

e.en: Their {sportscast} covered every game of the tournament.
e.zh: 他们的体育转播报道了锦标赛的每一场比赛。

e.en: The veteran {sportscaster} called the final play perfectly.
e.zh: 那位资深体育解说员把最后一球解说得淋漓尽致。

e.en: She dreams of becoming a TV {sportscaster} someday.
e.zh: 她梦想着有一天能成为电视体育主播。

e.en: He's a true {sportsman} who respects every opponent.
e.zh: 他是真正的运动员，尊重每一位对手。

e.en: The {sportsman} trained six hours a day before the Olympics.
e.zh: 那位运动员奥运会前每天训练六小时。

e.en: Shaking hands after the match is {sportsmanlike} behavior.
e.zh: 赛后握手是有运动员风度的行为。

e.en: His {sportsmanlike} attitude impressed the entire team.
e.zh: 他的体育精神让整支球队都很敬佩。

e.en: Good {sportsmanship} matters more than winning.
e.zh: 良好的体育精神比胜利更重要。

e.en: The coach teaches {sportsmanship} to every young player.
e.zh: 教练向每位年轻球员灌输体育精神。

e.en: Different cultures express {sportsmanships} in different ways.
e.zh: 不同文化以不同方式表现体育精神。

e.en: The book compares various {sportsmanships} across history.
e.zh: 这本书比较了历史上各种各样的体育精神。

e.en: The store sells affordable {sportswear} for runners.
e.zh: 这家店出售面向跑者的平价运动服。

e.en: She launched her own {sportswear} brand last year.
e.zh: 她去年创立了自己的运动服品牌。

e.en: She was named {sportswoman} of the year in tennis.
e.zh: 她被评为年度网球女运动员。

e.en: The young {sportswoman} broke three national records.
e.zh: 那位年轻女运动员打破了三项全国纪录。

spleen.t:
n. 脾脏
n. 怨气

e.en: Doctors removed her {spleen} after the car accident.
e.zh: 车祸后医生切除了她的脾脏。

e.en: He vented his {spleen} about the new policy online.
e.zh: 他在网上发泄对新政策的不满。

e.en: We had a {splendid} time at the rooftop party.
e.zh: 我们在天台派对上玩得非常尽兴。

e.en: The view from the mountaintop was simply {splendid}.
e.zh: 从山顶望出去的景色简直美极了。

e.en: The two cats get along {splendidly} despite their differences.
e.zh: 尽管性格不同,这两只猫相处得非常好。

e.en: She performed {splendidly} at the piano recital.
e.zh: 她在钢琴独奏会上表现得非常出色。

e.en: Tourists marveled at the {splendor} of the ancient palace.
e.zh: 游客们惊叹于这座古老宫殿的辉煌。

e.en: Autumn brings the full {splendor} of color to the forest.
e.zh: 秋天为森林带来斑斓多彩的壮丽景象。

splendour.t: n. 壮丽，辉煌（splendor 英式拼写）

e.en: The cathedral's interior reveals breathtaking {splendour}.
e.zh: 大教堂的内部展现出令人惊叹的壮丽。

e.en: They dined in the {splendour} of the royal hall.
e.zh: 他们在富丽堂皇的皇家大厅里用餐。

e.en: After the injury, doctors performed an emergency {splenectomy}.
e.zh: 受伤之后,医生进行了紧急脾脏切除手术。

e.en: Patients need vaccines after a {splenectomy} to prevent infection.
e.zh: 脾切除术后患者需要接种疫苗以防感染。

e.en: The scan revealed a small {splenic} cyst that needs monitoring.
e.zh: 扫描显示有一个需要监测的小脾囊肿。

e.en: He was diagnosed with a {splenic} artery aneurysm.
e.zh: 他被诊断出患有脾动脉瘤。

splice.t:
v. 拼接，接合
n. 接头

e.en: The editor will {splice} the two video clips together seamlessly.
e.zh: 剪辑师会把这两段视频无缝拼接在一起。

e.en: You need to {splice} these wires before connecting the lamp.
e.zh: 在接灯之前你得先把这些电线接起来。

e.en: The technician used a fiber {splicer} to fix the cable.
e.zh: 技术员用光纤熔接机修好了电缆。

e.en: Old film editors relied on a tape {splicer} for cutting.
e.zh: 过去的电影剪辑师依靠胶带接片机来剪片。

e.en: He rolled a {spliff} and passed it to his friend.
e.zh: 他卷了一根大麻烟递给朋友。

e.en: Smoking a {spliff} is illegal in many countries.
e.zh: 在很多国家抽大麻烟是违法的。

e.en: The designer used a {spline} curve to smooth the path.
e.zh: 设计师用样条曲线让路径变得平滑。

e.en: You'll need a {spline} tool to install the window screen.
e.zh: 安装纱窗你得用一个压条工具。

e.en: The nurse put a {splint} on his broken finger.
e.zh: 护士给他骨折的手指上了夹板。

e.en: She wears a {splint} at night to ease wrist pain.
e.zh: 她晚上戴夹板来缓解手腕的疼痛。

splinter.t:
n. 碎片，刺
v. 裂成碎片

e.en: I got a tiny {splinter} from the wooden bench.
e.zh: 我被木长椅扎了一根小木刺。

e.en: A small group decided to {splinter} from the main party.
e.zh: 一小群人决定从主要政党中分裂出去。

e.en: The old door {splintered} when the police kicked it in.
e.zh: 警察一脚踹下去,那扇旧门就裂成了碎片。

e.en: The movement {splintered} into several rival factions.
e.zh: 这场运动分裂成了几个互相对立的派别。

splintering.t:
v. 裂成碎片
adj. 碎裂的

e.en: Sand the wood to prevent it from {splintering} further.
e.zh: 打磨一下木头,免得它继续开裂起刺。

e.en: The party is {splintering} over the new tax bill.
e.zh: 该党因新税法案而正在分裂。

e.en: Tiny {splinters} of glass covered the kitchen floor.
e.zh: 细小的玻璃碎片散落在厨房地板上。

e.en: Wear gloves so the rough wood doesn't give you {splinters}.
e.zh: 戴上手套,免得粗糙的木头扎到你。

e.en: The old fence is {splintery} and dangerous to touch.
e.zh: 那道旧栅栏满是木刺,碰一下都很危险。

e.en: Avoid walking barefoot on the {splintery} dock.
e.zh: 别光脚走在那座满是木刺的码头上。

split.t:
v. 分开，分裂
n. 分裂，裂口

e.en: Let's {split} the bill evenly among the four of us.
e.zh: 我们四个人把账单平均分一下吧。

e.en: The team {split} into two groups to finish faster.
e.zh: 团队分成两组以便更快完成工作。

splits.t:
n. 劈叉
v. 分开（第三人称）

e.en: She effortlessly does the {splits} during her warm-up.
e.zh: 她热身时轻松就能劈叉。

e.en: The app {splits} large videos into shorter clips.
e.zh: 这个应用会把大视频切分成更短的片段。

e.en: I bought an HDMI {splitter} so two TVs can share one source.
e.zh: 我买了个HDMI分配器,让两台电视共用一个信号源。

e.en: He's a real hair {splitter} when reviewing contracts.
e.zh: 他审合同时真是个吹毛求疵的人。

splitting.t:
adj. (头痛) 剧烈的
v. 分裂

e.en: I have a {splitting} headache after staring at the screen all day.
e.zh: 盯着屏幕一整天后，我头痛欲裂。

e.en: They are {splitting} the bill evenly among four friends.
e.zh: 他们四个朋友平摊了账单。

e.en: There's a {splodge} of paint on your sleeve.
e.zh: 你袖子上有一团油漆。

e.en: A dark {splodge} of ink stained the page.
e.zh: 一团深色墨水弄脏了纸面。

splosh.t:
v. 哗啦作响
n. 溅泼声

e.en: The kids {splosh} happily through every puddle on the way home.
e.zh: 孩子们一路上开心地踩遍每个水坑。

e.en: I heard a loud {splosh} as the dog jumped into the lake.
e.zh: 狗跳进湖里时，我听到一声响亮的扑通声。

e.en: A red {splotch} appeared on the white tablecloth.
e.zh: 白色桌布上出现了一块红色污渍。

e.en: He noticed a {splotch} of mud on his new shoes.
e.zh: 他发现新鞋上有一块泥污。

e.en: Her face turned {splotchy} after running in the cold.
e.zh: 她在冷天跑步后，脸上出现一块块红斑。

e.en: The old wall looked {splotchy} where the paint had peeled.
e.zh: 老墙上油漆剥落的地方斑驳不堪。

splurge.t:
v. 挥霍，乱花钱
n. 挥霍

e.en: I decided to {splurge} on a fancy dinner for my birthday.
e.zh: 我决定生日时奢侈一下，吃顿高档晚餐。

e.en: She went on a shopping {splurge} after getting her bonus.
e.zh: 她拿到奖金后大肆购物了一番。

splutter.t: v. 急促结巴地说；噼啪响

e.en: The old engine began to {splutter} and finally died.
e.zh: 那台旧引擎开始噼啪作响，最后熄火了。

e.en: He could only {splutter} in shock when he heard the news.
e.zh: 听到这个消息，他震惊得语无伦次。

spluttering.t: v. 噼啪作响；结巴地说

e.en: The candle kept {spluttering} in the draft from the window.
e.zh: 蜡烛在窗口的穿堂风中不断噼啪闪烁。

e.en: She left the room, {spluttering} angrily about the decision.
e.zh: 她气得语无伦次地嘟囔着那个决定，离开了房间。

spock.t: n. 史波克（星际迷航角色）

e.en: Fans still quote {Spock} from the original Star Trek series.
e.zh: 粉丝们至今仍引用《星际迷航》原版中史波克的台词。

e.en: He raised his hand in the famous {Spock} salute.
e.zh: 他举起手做出著名的史波克式敬礼。

spode.t: n. 斯波德瓷器（英国瓷器品牌）

e.en: Her grandmother left her a complete set of {Spode} china.
e.zh: 奶奶留给她一整套斯波德瓷器。

e.en: The antique shop displayed several pieces of blue {Spode} pottery.
e.zh: 古董店里陈列着几件蓝色斯波德陶器。

e.en: Don't {spoil} the movie by telling me the ending.
e.zh: 别告诉我结局，免得剧透。

e.en: Grandparents love to {spoil} their grandchildren with treats.
e.zh: 祖父母们总爱用零食宠溺孙辈。

e.en: Proper refrigeration helps prevent food {spoilage}.
e.zh: 妥善冷藏有助于防止食物变质。

e.en: The supermarket loses thousands annually due to {spoilage}.
e.zh: 超市每年因食品变质损失数千元。

e.en: The milk has {spoiled} and smells terrible.
e.zh: 牛奶已经变质了，闻起来很难闻。

e.en: He's a {spoiled} child who always gets his way.
e.zh: 他是个被宠坏的孩子，总能为所欲为。

e.en: Please don't post any {spoiler} for the new season.
e.zh: 请不要发布新一季的任何剧透。

e.en: The car has a sleek black {spoiler} on the back.
e.zh: 这辆车后部装有一个流线型的黑色扰流板。

e.en: The rain is {spoiling} our weekend picnic plans.
e.zh: 这场雨破坏了我们周末野餐的计划。

e.en: She accused him of {spoiling} their daughter with too many gifts.
e.zh: 她指责他用太多礼物宠坏了女儿。

e.en: The victors divided the {spoils} of war among themselves.
e.zh: 胜利者瓜分了战利品。

e.en: Leaving meat out overnight quickly {spoils} it.
e.zh: 肉放在外面过夜很快就会变质。

e.en: Don't be such a {spoilsport} and join the game.
e.zh: 别这么扫兴,一起来玩吧。

e.en: He's a real {spoilsport} who ruins every party.
e.zh: 他真是个扫兴鬼,每次聚会都被他搅黄。

spoilt.t: adj. 被宠坏的（spoiled 英式）

e.en: The milk has {spoilt}, so throw it out.
e.zh: 牛奶已经变质了,扔掉吧。

e.en: Their only child is completely {spoilt} and demanding.
e.zh: 他们的独生子被宠坏了,要求特别多。

spoke.t:
n. 车轮辐条
v. speak 的过去式

e.en: She {spoke} clearly and confidently during the interview.
e.zh: 她在面试中说话清晰自信。

e.en: A bent {spoke} can throw the whole bicycle wheel off.
e.zh: 一根弯曲的辐条会让整个自行车轮失衡。

e.en: Vintage bicycles often have elegant {spoked} wheels.
e.zh: 复古自行车通常配有优雅的辐条轮。

e.en: The carriage rolled along on tall {spoked} wheels.
e.zh: 马车靠着高大的辐条轮滚滚前行。

spoken.t:
adj. 口头的
v. speak 的过去分词

e.en: English is widely {spoken} as a second language.
e.zh: 英语作为第二语言被广泛使用。

e.en: He has {spoken} to the manager about the issue.
e.zh: 他已经就这个问题跟经理谈过了。

e.en: The carpenter used a {spokeshave} to smooth the chair leg.
e.zh: 木匠用刮刀把椅子腿刮光滑。

e.en: A sharp {spokeshave} makes shaping curved wood much easier.
e.zh: 一把锋利的刮刀让雕琢曲面木料容易得多。

e.en: The company's {spokesman} addressed the press this morning.
e.zh: 公司的发言人今早向媒体发表了讲话。

e.en: A government {spokesman} denied the allegations firmly.
e.zh: 一名政府发言人坚决否认了这些指控。

e.en: Several team {spokesmen} answered questions after the game.
e.zh: 几位球队发言人在赛后回答了问题。

e.en: The {spokesmen} from both companies confirmed the merger.
e.zh: 两家公司的发言人都证实了合并消息。

e.en: Industry {spokespeople} gathered at the conference yesterday.
e.zh: 行业发言人们昨天聚集在会议上。

e.en: The {spokespeople} declined to comment on the lawsuit.
e.zh: 几位发言人拒绝就诉讼一事发表评论。

e.en: A {spokesperson} for the airline apologized for the delays.
e.zh: 航空公司的一位发言人为延误道歉。

e.en: She serves as {spokesperson} for the climate movement.
e.zh: 她担任气候运动的发言人。

e.en: The {spokeswoman} clarified the CEO's earlier remarks.
e.zh: 女发言人澄清了首席执行官早些时候的言论。

e.en: A police {spokeswoman} confirmed two arrests had been made.
e.zh: 一位警方女发言人证实已逮捕两人。

e.en: Both party {spokeswomen} appeared on the morning talk show.
e.zh: 两党的女发言人都出席了早间脱口秀。

e.en: The {spokeswomen} jointly announced the new partnership.
e.zh: 几位女发言人共同宣布了新的合作关系。

e.en: The poet used {spondaic} rhythm to emphasize the somber mood.
e.zh: 诗人用扬扬格节奏强化了沉郁的氛围。

e.en: Greek epic poetry sometimes featured {spondaic} lines for effect.
e.zh: 希腊史诗有时会使用扬扬格诗行以增强效果。

e.en: Ankylosing {spondylitis} causes chronic back pain in young adults.
e.zh: 强直性脊柱炎会导致年轻人长期背痛。

e.en: The doctor diagnosed her with {spondylitis} after the MRI.
e.zh: 做完核磁共振后医生诊断她患有脊柱炎。

e.en: The {sportswriter} interviewed players after the championship.
e.zh: 那位体育记者在冠军赛后采访了球员。

e.en: She works as a {sportswriter} for a major newspaper.
e.zh: 她在一家大报担任体育记者。

sporty.t: adj. 运动风格的；时髦的

e.en: He drives a {sporty} little hatchback to work.
e.zh: 他开着一辆运动风格的小型两厢车上班。

e.en: She has a {sporty} style and loves outdoor activities.
e.zh: 她风格运动，喜欢户外活动。

spot.t:
n. 地点；斑点
v. 发现；认出

e.en: This café is the perfect {spot} to study.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆是学习的完美地点。

e.en: Did you {spot} the typo in the headline?
e.zh: 你发现标题里的错别字了吗？

spotless.t: adj. 一尘不染的；清白的

e.en: Her kitchen is always {spotless} after dinner.
e.zh: 她的厨房在晚饭后总是一尘不染。

e.en: The hotel rooms were absolutely {spotless}.
e.zh: 酒店房间打扫得非常干净。

spotlessly.t: adv. 一尘不染地；洁净地

e.en: The bathroom was {spotlessly} clean when we arrived.
e.zh: 我们到的时候浴室干净得一尘不染。

e.en: He keeps his car {spotlessly} polished every weekend.
e.zh: 他每个周末都把车擦得锃亮如新。

spotlight.t:
n. 聚光灯；关注焦点
v. 使受关注

e.en: The {spotlight} followed the singer across the stage.
e.zh: 聚光灯跟着歌手在舞台上移动。

e.en: This article puts a {spotlight} on small startups.
e.zh: 这篇文章重点关注小型创业公司。

spotlighted.t: v. 聚焦；突出显示（过去式）

e.en: The documentary {spotlighted} unsung healthcare workers.
e.zh: 这部纪录片重点呈现了默默付出的医护人员。

e.en: Her speech was {spotlighted} on the homepage today.
e.zh: 她的演讲今天被置于首页推荐位置。

e.en: The stage {spotlights} suddenly switched to deep blue.
e.zh: 舞台聚光灯突然切换成深蓝色。

e.en: The article {spotlights} three young inventors.
e.zh: 这篇文章着重介绍了三位年轻的发明家。

e.en: The sculpture stood {spotlit} in the dark gallery.
e.zh: 那件雕塑在昏暗的展厅中被聚光灯照亮。

e.en: A {spotlit} painting drew everyone's attention.
e.zh: 一幅被聚光灯照亮的画作吸引了所有人的目光。

spots.t:
n. 地点；斑点（复数）
v. 发现（第三人称）

e.en: The leopard's {spots} help it blend into the trees.
e.zh: 豹子身上的斑点能帮它融入树丛。

e.en: All the parking {spots} were already taken.
e.zh: 所有的停车位都已经被占了。

spotted.t:
adj. 有斑点的
v. 发现（过去式）

e.en: I {spotted} my old teacher at the airport yesterday.
e.zh: 我昨天在机场认出了以前的老师。

e.en: She wore a {spotted} dress to the garden party.
e.zh: 她穿了一条波点连衣裙去花园派对。

e.en: The gym requires a {spotter} for heavy bench presses.
e.zh: 健身房要求大重量卧推时必须有保护者。

e.en: The plane {spotter} photographed every aircraft that landed.
e.zh: 那位飞机迷拍下了每一架降落的飞机。

e.en: He's good at {spotting} fake news online.
e.zh: 他很擅长识别网上的假新闻。

e.en: Bird {spotting} is her favorite weekend hobby.
e.zh: 观鸟是她最爱的周末爱好。

spotty.t: adj. 参差不齐的；有斑点的

e.en: The Wi-Fi is {spotty} in this part of the building.
e.zh: 这栋楼这一带的Wi-Fi信号时好时坏。

e.en: His memory of that night is a bit {spotty}.
e.zh: 他对那晚的记忆有点零碎。

e.en: The company offers {spousal} health insurance benefits.
e.zh: 公司为员工配偶提供医疗保险福利。

e.en: He applied for a {spousal} visa to join her abroad.
e.zh: 他申请了配偶签证去国外与她团聚。

e.en: Please bring your {spouse} to the company dinner.
e.zh: 请带上您的配偶参加公司晚宴。

e.en: He listed his {spouse} as the emergency contact.
e.zh: 他把配偶列为紧急联系人。

e.en: Both {spouses} signed the mortgage documents.
e.zh: 夫妻双方都在按揭文件上签了字。

e.en: Many {spouses} of soldiers face long separations.
e.zh: 许多军人配偶都要面对长期分离。

spout.t:
n. 壶嘴；喷口
v. 喷出

e.en: Water poured from the kettle's {spout} into the cup.
e.zh: 水从水壶嘴注入杯子。

e.en: He likes to {spout} opinions about every news story.
e.zh: 他喜欢对每条新闻发表一通见解。

spp.t: n. 多个物种（species 的缩写）

sprain.t:
v. 扭伤
n. 扭伤

e.en: Be careful not to {sprain} your ankle on the trail.
e.zh: 小心别在山路上扭伤脚踝。

e.en: She got a bad {sprain} during yesterday's match.
e.zh: 她在昨天的比赛中严重扭伤了。

e.en: He {sprained} his wrist falling off the skateboard.
e.zh: 他从滑板上摔下来扭伤了手腕。

e.en: She's resting with a {sprained} ankle this week.
e.zh: 她这周在家休养，脚踝扭伤了。

sprang.t: v. 跳起（spring 的过去式）

e.en: The cat {sprang} onto the windowsill to chase a moth.
e.zh: 猫一跃跳上窗台去追飞蛾。

e.en: A new idea {sprang} to mind during the meeting.
e.zh: 开会时她突然想到一个新点子。

e.en: We grilled fresh {sprat} with lemon and salt.
e.zh: 我们用柠檬和盐烤了新鲜的西鲱鱼。

e.en: The fisherman pulled in a net full of {sprat}.
e.zh: 渔夫拉上来满满一网小鲱鱼。

sprawl.t:
v. 伸开四肢躺；蔓延
n. 无序扩张

e.en: Urban {sprawl} has swallowed the surrounding farmland.
e.zh: 城市的无序扩张已经吞掉了周边农田。

e.en: He likes to {sprawl} on the couch after work.
e.zh: 他下班后喜欢摊在沙发上。

sprawled.t: v. 四肢摊开；蔓延（过去式）

e.en: The dog {sprawled} across the rug in the sun.
e.zh: 狗四脚朝天地摊在阳光下的地毯上。

e.en: Books were {sprawled} all over the desk.
e.zh: 书本散乱地铺满了整张书桌。

sprawling.t: adj. 蔓延的；杂乱延伸的

e.en: They live in a {sprawling} mansion outside the city.
e.zh: 他们住在城外一座占地极广的大宅。

e.en: The novel has a {sprawling} cast of characters.
e.zh: 这部小说人物众多、规模庞大。

sprawls.t: v. 蔓延；伸展（第三人称）

e.en: The campus {sprawls} across three hundred acres.
e.zh: 校园延展占地三百英亩。

e.en: He {sprawls} on the bed scrolling his phone.
e.zh: 他摊在床上刷着手机。

spray.t:
n. 喷雾
v. 喷洒

e.en: Use this {spray} to repel mosquitoes at night.
e.zh: 晚上用这种喷雾来驱蚊。

e.en: Waves {spray} over the rocks at high tide.
e.zh: 涨潮时浪花飞溅过礁石。

e.en: She {sprayed} perfume on her wrists before leaving.
e.zh: 她出门前在手腕上喷了香水。

e.en: The artist {sprayed} graffiti across the brick wall.
e.zh: 艺术家在砖墙上喷了涂鸦。

e.en: The garden {sprayer} broke after one season of use.
e.zh: 那个园艺喷雾器用了一季就坏了。

e.en: Attach the {sprayer} to the hose for easy watering.
e.zh: 把喷头接到水管上方便浇水。

e.en: Workers are {spraying} pesticide on the orchard today.
e.zh: 工人今天在果园里喷洒农药。

e.en: The kids were {spraying} each other with water guns.
e.zh: 孩子们用水枪互相喷射。

sprays.t:
n. 喷雾（复数）
v. 喷洒（第三人称）

e.en: She {sprays} sunscreen on her shoulders before swimming.
e.zh: 她游泳前在肩膀上喷防晒霜。

e.en: The store sells various nasal {sprays} for allergies.
e.zh: 这家店出售多种过敏用鼻喷剂。

spread.t:
v. 传播；铺开
n. 范围；涂抹酱

e.en: The news {spread} quickly across social media.
e.zh: 消息在社交媒体上迅速传开。

e.en: He likes to {spread} peanut butter thickly on toast.
e.zh: 他喜欢在吐司上厚厚地涂一层花生酱。

spreadable.t: adj. 可涂抹的；易传播的

e.en: This cheese is soft and easily {spreadable} at room temperature.
e.zh: 这种奶酪在常温下柔软,很容易涂抹。

e.en: We bought a jar of {spreadable} chocolate for breakfast.
e.zh: 我们买了一罐早餐用的可涂抹巧克力酱。

e.en: He used a fertilizer {spreader} on the front lawn.
e.zh: 他用施肥撒播器处理了前院草坪。

e.en: That rumor turned him into a known gossip {spreader}.
e.zh: 那个传言让他成了出了名的八卦传播者。

e.en: The wildfire is {spreading} faster than firefighters expected.
e.zh: 野火蔓延的速度比消防员预想的更快。

e.en: She is {spreading} jam on a slice of bread.
e.zh: 她正在面包片上抹果酱。

spreads.t:
v. 传播（第三人称）
n. 传播范围（复数）

e.en: Misinformation {spreads} faster than the truth online.
e.zh: 网上的虚假信息比真相传播得更快。

e.en: The cafe offers various dips and {spreads} with bread.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆配面包提供多种蘸酱和涂酱。

e.en: I tracked the budget in a {spreadsheet} all year.
e.zh: 我整年都用电子表格记录预算。

e.en: Open the {spreadsheet} and check the sales figures.
e.zh: 打开那份电子表格查看销售数据。

e.en: She prefers {spreadsheets} over fancy project tools.
e.zh: 她比起花哨的项目工具更喜欢用电子表格。

e.en: The accountant juggles dozens of {spreadsheets} each month.
e.zh: 那位会计每月要处理几十份电子表格。

spree.t: n. 狂欢；无节制的购物消费

e.en: She went on a shopping {spree} after getting paid.
e.zh: 她发工资后疯狂购物了一番。

e.en: The team is on a winning {spree} this season.
e.zh: 这支球队本赛季正打出一波连胜。

e.en: Garnish the cocktail with a {sprig} of mint.
e.zh: 在鸡尾酒上点缀一小枝薄荷。

e.en: She tucked a {sprig} of rosemary into the roast.
e.zh: 她把一小枝迷迭香塞进烤肉里。

sprightly.t: adj. 轻快活泼的；精神饱满的

e.en: My grandmother is still {sprightly} at ninety years old.
e.zh: 我外婆九十岁了依然精神矍铄。

e.en: The orchestra played a {sprightly} tune to open the show.
e.zh: 乐团以一支轻快的曲子开场。

spring.t:
n. 春天；弹簧
v. 跳；涌出

e.en: Cherry blossoms bloom every {spring} in this park.
e.zh: 这座公园每年春天樱花盛开。

e.en: The mattress {spring} broke and now squeaks loudly.
e.zh: 床垫的弹簧坏了,现在吱吱响。

e.en: The internship served as a {springboard} for her career.
e.zh: 那次实习成了她事业的跳板。

e.en: He bounced off the {springboard} into the pool.
e.zh: 他从跳板上一跃跳进泳池。

e.en: A {springbok} leapt gracefully across the dry savanna.
e.zh: 一只跳羚优雅地跃过干燥的草原。

e.en: South Africa's national rugby team is called the {Springbok}.
e.zh: 南非国家橄榄球队被称为跳羚队。

e.en: Their {springer} spaniel loves chasing tennis balls in the yard.
e.zh: 他们家的史宾格猎犬喜欢在院子里追网球。

e.en: The {springer} bounded happily through the tall grass.
e.zh: 那只史宾格欢快地穿过高高的草丛。

springfield.t: n. 斯普林菲尔德（地名）

e.en: The Simpsons live in a town called {Springfield}.
e.zh: 辛普森一家住在一个叫春田镇的地方。

e.en: She drove to {Springfield} for a weekend conference.
e.zh: 她开车去春田市参加周末的会议。

springhouse.t: n. 泉屋（建在泉水上的冷藏小屋）

e.en: They stored milk and butter in the old {springhouse}.
e.zh: 他们把牛奶和黄油存放在古老的泉水屋里。

e.en: The stone {springhouse} kept produce cool all summer.
e.zh: 那座石砌泉水屋整个夏天都让食物保持清凉。

springing.t: v. 跳跃；涌现（spring 的现在分词）

e.en: New cafes are {springing} up all over the neighborhood.
e.zh: 新咖啡馆在这个街区里到处冒出来。

e.en: The dog kept {springing} over the low garden fence.
e.zh: 那只狗不停地跳过矮矮的花园栅栏。

springs.t:
n. 弹簧；泉水（复数）
v. 跳；涌出

e.en: Hot {springs} in the mountains attract tourists year-round.
e.zh: 山里的温泉常年吸引游客。

e.en: The old sofa {springs} poke through the cushions.
e.zh: 旧沙发的弹簧戳穿了坐垫。

springsteen.t: n. 斯普林斯汀（美国摇滚歌手 Bruce Springsteen）

e.en: Bruce {Springsteen} played a three-hour set last night.
e.zh: 昨晚布鲁斯·斯普林斯汀演出了整整三小时。

e.en: My dad has every {Springsteen} album on vinyl.
e.zh: 我爸收藏了斯普林斯汀的全部黑胶唱片。

e.en: Tokyo is breathtaking in {springtime} when the cherry trees bloom.
e.zh: 樱花盛开时的东京在春天美得令人窒息。

e.en: We always plant tomatoes in early {springtime}.
e.zh: 我们总是在初春种番茄。

e.en: This brand bottles fresh {springwater} from the Alps.
e.zh: 这个品牌灌装来自阿尔卑斯的新鲜泉水。

e.en: The coffee tastes better when brewed with cold {springwater}.
e.zh: 用冷泉水冲煮的咖啡味道更好。

springy.t: adj. 有弹性的；富弹力的

e.en: The new running shoes feel light and {springy}.
e.zh: 这双新跑鞋穿起来轻盈又有弹性。

e.en: She has thick, {springy} curls that bounce when she walks.
e.zh: 她有一头厚实弹性十足的卷发,走路时会跳动。

sprinkle.t:
v. 撒；洒；喷洒
n. 少量；细雨

e.en: {Sprinkle} a little salt on the fries before serving.
e.zh: 上桌前在薯条上撒一点盐。

e.en: A light {sprinkle} of rain started just before noon.
e.zh: 快到中午时下起了一阵小雨。

e.en: The {sprinkler} waters the lawn every morning at six.
e.zh: 洒水器每天早上六点给草坪浇水。

e.en: A faulty {sprinkler} soaked the entire office overnight.
e.zh: 一个故障的喷淋头一夜之间把整个办公室浇湿了。

sprinkling.t:
n. 少许；稀疏分布
v. 撒（sprinkle 的现在分词）

e.en: Add a {sprinkling} of cheese on top before baking.
e.zh: 烘烤前在上面撒少许奶酪。

e.en: There's a {sprinkling} of celebrities in the audience tonight.
e.zh: 今晚观众席里有零星几位名人。

sprint.t:
n. 冲刺；短跑
v. 全力奔跑；冲刺（开发迭代）

e.en: He had to {sprint} to catch the last train home.
e.zh: 他不得不冲刺去赶最后一班回家的列车。

e.en: The team finished the feature in a two-week {sprint}.
e.zh: 团队在两周的冲刺周期内完成了那个功能。

e.en: The Jamaican {sprinter} broke another world record yesterday.
e.zh: 那位牙买加短跑运动员昨天又打破了一项世界纪录。

e.en: As a {sprinter}, she trained mostly on explosive starts.
e.zh: 作为短跑选手,她主要训练爆发起跑。

sprints.t:
n. 冲刺；短跑（复数）
v. 冲刺

e.en: Our team works in two-week {sprints} to ship features.
e.zh: 我们团队按两周一个冲刺周期来发布功能。

e.en: He runs short {sprints} every morning to stay fit.
e.zh: 他每天早上跑短距离冲刺来保持体型。

sprit.t: n. 斜杠（帆船上的撑帆杆）

e.en: The sailor adjusted the {sprit} to catch the wind.
e.zh: 水手调整斜桁以借助风力。

e.en: A traditional {sprit} sail powered the small wooden boat.
e.zh: 一面传统的斜桁帆驱动着这艘小木船。

sprite.t: n. 精灵图（游戏/网页中的 2D 图像）；小精灵

e.en: The game artist drew every {sprite} pixel by pixel.
e.zh: 那位游戏美术师一像素一像素地画出每个角色精灵图。

e.en: In folklore, a forest {sprite} guards the ancient oak.
e.zh: 传说中,一只森林精灵守护着那棵古橡树。

spritz.t:
v. 喷洒；喷雾
n. 少量喷洒

e.en: Give the plants a quick {spritz} of water each morning.
e.zh: 每天早上给植物轻轻喷一下水。

e.en: She ordered an Aperol {spritz} at the rooftop bar.
e.zh: 她在屋顶酒吧点了一杯阿佩罗气泡鸡尾酒。

spritzer.t: n. 气泡酒（葡萄酒加苏打水）

e.en: I'll have a wine {spritzer} instead of a cocktail.
e.zh: 我要一杯葡萄酒苏打,不要鸡尾酒。

e.en: She mixed a refreshing {spritzer} with white wine and soda.
e.zh: 她用白葡萄酒和苏打水调了一杯清爽的气泡饮。

e.en: The bike's chain slipped off the rear {sprocket} again.
e.zh: 自行车链条又从后齿轮上脱落了。

e.en: Replace the worn {sprocket} before it damages the chain.
e.zh: 在磨损的链轮损坏链条之前把它换掉。

sprog.t: n. 小孩；新兵（英式俚语）

e.en: He's looking after the {sprog} while his wife travels.
e.zh: 妻子出差时,他在家照顾小孩。

e.en: The couple just had their first {sprog} last month.
e.zh: 这对夫妻上个月刚生下第一个小孩。

sprout.t:
v. 发芽；长出
n. 芽；嫩枝

e.en: The seeds will {sprout} within a week of planting.
e.zh: 种子种下一周内就会发芽。

e.en: I added a handful of bean {sprout} to the noodles.
e.zh: 我往面条里加了一把豆芽。

sprouted.t:
adj. 已发芽的
v. 发芽（过去式）

e.en: The avocado pit finally {sprouted} after three weeks.
e.zh: 那颗牛油果核三周后终于发芽了。

e.en: New tech startups have {sprouted} all over the city.
e.zh: 新的科技初创公司在整座城市里冒了出来。

sprouting.t: v. 发芽；萌发（sprout 的现在分词）

e.en: Tiny green leaves are {sprouting} from the cracked pavement.
e.zh: 嫩绿的叶子正从裂开的路面上冒出来。

e.en: He's {sprouting} a beard for the first time.
e.zh: 他第一次开始留胡子。

sprouts.t:
n. 豆芽；嫩芽（复数）
v. 发芽

e.en: Brussels {sprouts} taste amazing when roasted with bacon.
e.zh: 球芽甘蓝和培根一起烤味道好极了。

e.en: She tops her sandwich with alfalfa {sprouts} and avocado.
e.zh: 她在三明治上加了苜蓿芽和牛油果。

e.en: The spreadsheet column labeled {sprs} tracks weekly sponsors.
e.zh: 电子表格里标着 sprs 的那一栏记录每周的赞助商。

e.en: In the logs, {sprs} is shorthand for separate runs.
e.zh: 日志里 sprs 是 separate runs 的缩写。

spruce.t:
n. 云杉（树）
adj. 整洁的

e.en: A tall {spruce} stood at the edge of the forest.
e.zh: 一棵高大的云杉矗立在森林边缘。

e.en: He needs to {spruce} up his resume before applying.
e.zh: 他申请之前得把简历好好修饰一下。

sprung.t: v. spring 的过去分词（跳起、涌出）

e.en: Weeds have {sprung} up all over the garden.
e.zh: 院子里到处冒出了杂草。

e.en: A surprise inspection was {sprung} on the team yesterday.
e.zh: 昨天团队遭遇了一次突击检查。

spry.t: adj. 矫健的；（老人）精神抖擞的

e.en: My grandmother is still {spry} at eighty-five.
e.zh: 我奶奶八十五岁了依然身手矫健。

e.en: The {spry} old cat leapt onto the windowsill.
e.zh: 那只灵活的老猫跳上了窗台。

e.en: She analyzed the survey data using {SPSS}.
e.zh: 她使用 SPSS 软件分析了调查数据。

e.en: The lab requires students to learn {SPSS} for statistics.
e.zh: 实验室要求学生学习 SPSS 做统计分析。

e.en: He peeled a {spud} for tonight's stew.
e.zh: 他削了一个土豆准备做今晚的炖菜。

e.en: The diner serves burgers with a side of {spud}.
e.zh: 那家小餐馆的汉堡配土豆当配菜。

e.en: Sea {spume} drifted across the rocky shore.
e.zh: 海面的浪花飘过礁石密布的海岸。

e.en: The waterfall threw up clouds of white {spume}.
e.zh: 瀑布激起一团团白色的水沫。

spumoni.t: n. 斯普莫尼（意式分层冰淇淋）

e.en: We ordered {spumoni} for dessert at the Italian restaurant.
e.zh: 我们在意大利餐厅点了意式三色冰淇淋当甜点。

e.en: The {spumoni} layered pistachio, cherry, and chocolate flavors.
e.zh: 这款意式冰淇淋分层有开心果、樱桃和巧克力口味。

spun.t: v. spin 的过去式/过去分词（旋转、纺）

e.en: The dancer {spun} gracefully across the stage.
e.zh: 舞者在舞台上优雅地旋转。

e.en: The PR team {spun} the bad news into a positive story.
e.zh: 公关团队把坏消息包装成了正面故事。

e.en: The little kid showed real {spunk} during the match.
e.zh: 那个小孩在比赛中表现得很有胆量。

e.en: I admire her {spunk} when facing tough critics.
e.zh: 我很佩服她面对严厉批评时的勇气。

e.en: She's a {spunky} reporter who never backs down.
e.zh: 她是个从不退缩的勇敢记者。

e.en: Their {spunky} puppy chased every leaf in the yard.
e.zh: 他们家活泼的小狗在院子里追每一片叶子。

spur.t:
n. 刺激；马刺
v. 激励；促使

e.en: Low interest rates can {spur} consumer spending.
e.zh: 低利率能刺激消费者支出。

e.en: He bought the ticket on the {spur} of the moment.
e.zh: 他一时冲动就买了那张票。

e.en: Don't touch the {spurge}; its sap irritates skin.
e.zh: 别碰大戟,它的汁液会刺激皮肤。

e.en: Gardeners use {spurge} as drought-resistant ground cover.
e.zh: 园丁用大戟作为耐旱的地被植物。

e.en: The article was based on {spurious} statistics.
e.zh: 那篇文章建立在虚假的统计数据上。

e.en: He made a {spurious} claim about owning the patent.
e.zh: 他对拥有该专利提出了不实的主张。

e.en: The website {spuriously} claims to be officially endorsed.
e.zh: 那家网站虚假地声称获得了官方认可。

e.en: Some products are {spuriously} marketed as scientifically proven.
e.zh: 有些产品被虚假地标榜为有科学依据。

e.en: She chose to {spurn} his apology and walked away.
e.zh: 她选择拒绝他的道歉,转身离开了。

e.en: Investors {spurn} companies with poor governance records.
e.zh: 投资者排斥治理记录不佳的公司。

spurned.t: v. 拒绝；唾弃（spurn 的过去式）

e.en: The candidate {spurned} offers from several rival firms.
e.zh: 那位应聘者拒绝了几家竞争对手公司的邀请。

e.en: A {spurned} ex-employee leaked the internal documents.
e.zh: 一位被弃用的前员工泄露了内部文件。

spurs.t: n. 马刺；刺激（复数）；马刺队

e.en: The cowboy fastened his {spurs} before mounting the horse.
e.zh: 那位牛仔上马前系好了马刺。

e.en: Competition {spurs} startups to ship features faster.
e.zh: 竞争促使初创公司更快地推出新功能。

spurt.t:
v. 喷出；冲刺
n. 喷涌；一阵猛劲

e.en: Sales saw a sudden {spurt} after the viral ad.
e.zh: 那则广告火了之后,销量突然激增。

e.en: Water began to {spurt} from the cracked pipe.
e.zh: 水开始从裂开的管道里喷出来。

sputnik.t: n. 人造卫星（苏联 Sputnik 卫星）

e.en: The launch of {Sputnik} kicked off the space race.
e.zh: 斯普特尼克卫星的发射拉开了太空竞赛的序幕。

e.en: Museums still display replicas of the original {Sputnik}.
e.zh: 博物馆里至今还展示着最初的斯普特尼克卫星复制品。

sputter.t: v. 噼啪作响；结结巴巴地说

e.en: The old engine began to {sputter} on the highway.
e.zh: 那台老引擎在高速公路上开始噗噗作响。

e.en: He could only {sputter} when caught in the lie.
e.zh: 被当场戳穿谎言时,他只能结结巴巴。

sputtered.t: v. 噼啪作响（sputter 的过去式）

e.en: The candle {sputtered} once and went out.
e.zh: 蜡烛劈啪一声就熄灭了。

e.en: She {sputtered} an apology before bursting into tears.
e.zh: 她结结巴巴地道了歉,然后哭了起来。

sputtering.t:
n. 溅射（镀膜工艺）
v. 噼啪作响

e.en: The economy is {sputtering} despite repeated stimulus packages.
e.zh: 尽管多次出台刺激方案,经济依然举步维艰。

e.en: Bacon was {sputtering} loudly in the hot pan.
e.zh: 培根在热锅里噼啪作响。

e.en: The doctor sent a {sputum} sample to the lab.
e.zh: 医生把一份痰样送去化验。

e.en: Persistent bloody {sputum} should be checked immediately.
e.zh: 持续带血的痰应立即就医检查。

spy.t:
n. 间谍
v. 侦察；暗中监视

e.en: The captain raised his {spyglass} to scan the horizon.
e.zh: 船长举起望远镜眺望地平线。

e.en: A brass {spyglass} sat on the antique desk.
e.zh: 那张古董书桌上摆着一只黄铜望远镜。

e.en: She peeked through the {spyhole} before opening the door.
e.zh: 她先从猫眼往外看了一下才开门。

e.en: The hotel suite door has a wide-angle {spyhole}.
e.zh: 酒店套房的门上有一个广角猫眼。

spying.t:
n. 间谍活动
v. 暗中监视

e.en: He was accused of {spying} on his neighbors.
e.zh: 他被指控偷窥邻居。

e.en: The app was caught {spying} on user activity.
e.zh: 那款应用被发现暗中监视用户的活动。

e.en: The novel's {spymaster} controls agents across three continents.
e.zh: 小说中的间谍头目掌控着三大洲的特工。

e.en: A retired {spymaster} published his controversial memoir.
e.zh: 一位退休的间谍头目出版了他那本颇具争议的回忆录。

e.en: His phone was infected with sophisticated {spyware}.
e.zh: 他的手机被植入了高级的间谍软件。

e.en: Always update your antivirus to block new {spyware}.
e.zh: 务必更新杀毒软件以拦截新的间谍软件。

sql.t: n. 结构化查询语言（数据库）

e.en: The chef roasted a {squab} with herbs and butter.
e.zh: 主厨用香草和黄油烤制了一只乳鸽。

e.en: Roasted {squab} is considered a delicacy in fine dining.
e.zh: 烤乳鸽在高级料理中被视为美味佳肴。

squabble.t:
v. 为小事争吵
n. 口角

e.en: The siblings {squabble} over the TV remote every night.
e.zh: 那对兄妹每晚都为电视遥控器争吵。

e.en: A petty {squabble} delayed the meeting by an hour.
e.zh: 一场琐碎的争吵让会议推迟了一小时。

e.en: The kids were {squabbling} in the back seat again.
e.zh: 孩子们又在后座上吵起来了。

e.en: Endless {squabbling} between departments slowed down the project.
e.zh: 各部门之间没完没了的争吵拖慢了项目进度。

squad.t: n. 小队；班组；警察分队

e.en: The coach announced the starting {squad} for Saturday's match.
e.zh: 教练公布了周六比赛的首发阵容。

e.en: A bomb {squad} cordoned off the suspicious package.
e.zh: 一支拆弹小队封锁了那个可疑包裹。

squaddie.t: n. 英式俚语，士兵、新兵

e.en: The young {squaddie} wrote home every Sunday.
e.zh: 那个年轻士兵每个周日都写信回家。

e.en: He served three years as a {squaddie} in Germany.
e.zh: 他在德国当了三年小兵。

squadron.t: n. (空军) 中队；舰队编队

e.en: A fighter {squadron} took off at dawn.
e.zh: 一个战斗机中队在黎明时分起飞。

e.en: The {squadron} commander briefed pilots on the mission.
e.zh: 中队长向飞行员们交代了任务细节。

e.en: Both {squads} trained intensely before the championship.
e.zh: 两支队伍在锦标赛前都进行了高强度训练。

e.en: Police {squads} patrol the district every evening.
e.zh: 警察小队每晚在该区巡逻。

squalid.t: adj. 肮脏破败的；卑劣的

e.en: Refugees were forced into {squalid} living conditions.
e.zh: 难民被迫住在肮脏不堪的环境里。

e.en: The reporter exposed the {squalid} conditions inside the factory.
e.zh: 记者揭露了工厂内部肮脏的状况。

squall.t:
n. 暴风；飑
v. 放声大哭

e.en: A sudden {squall} caught the sailors off guard.
e.zh: 一阵突如其来的飑风让水手们措手不及。

e.en: The baby let out a piercing {squall} at midnight.
e.zh: 宝宝半夜发出一阵刺耳的尖叫。

e.en: A {squalling} infant kept the whole flight awake.
e.zh: 一个号哭不止的婴儿让全机的人都没睡好。

e.en: The {squalling} wind tore branches from the trees.
e.zh: 呼啸的狂风把树枝刮断了。

e.en: Sailors were warned of {squally} weather offshore.
e.zh: 水手们被告知近海有阵风暴雨。

e.en: The forecast predicts a {squally} weekend along the coast.
e.zh: 天气预报说沿海周末会有阵风骤雨。

e.en: The slum's residents lived in unimaginable {squalor}.
e.zh: 贫民窟的居民住在难以想象的肮脏环境中。

e.en: He grew up in {squalor} but became a renowned surgeon.
e.zh: 他在贫困肮脏中长大,后来成了知名外科医生。

e.en: The biopsy revealed {squamous} cell carcinoma.
e.zh: 活检显示是鳞状细胞癌。

e.en: Skin contains layers of {squamous} epithelial cells.
e.zh: 皮肤含有多层鳞状上皮细胞。

e.en: Don't {squander} your savings on impulse purchases.
e.zh: 别把存款挥霍在冲动消费上。

e.en: The team can't {squander} this rare opportunity.
e.zh: 这个团队不能浪费这次难得的机会。

e.en: He {squandered} his inheritance within two years.
e.zh: 他两年内就把继承的遗产挥霍一空。

e.en: The startup {squandered} its funding on lavish offices.
e.zh: 那家初创公司把融资浪费在豪华办公室上。

e.en: Critics accused the mayor of {squandering} taxpayer money.
e.zh: 批评人士指责市长挥霍纳税人的钱。

e.en: Stop {squandering} time on apps that drain your focus.
e.zh: 别再把时间浪费在消耗注意力的应用上了。

squanders.t: v. squander 的第三人称单数

e.en: He routinely {squanders} bonuses on luxury gadgets.
e.zh: 他总是把奖金挥霍在奢侈电子产品上。

e.en: A team that {squanders} chances rarely wins championships.
e.zh: 一个总是浪费机会的球队很难赢得冠军。

square.t:
n. 正方形；广场
adj. 方形的；公平的

e.en: Draw a {square} with four equal sides.
e.zh: 画一个四边相等的正方形。

e.en: Let's meet in the town {square} at noon.
e.zh: 我们中午在城镇广场见面吧。

squared.t:
adj. 平方的；方格的
v. 使成方形

e.en: Three {squared} equals nine.
e.zh: 三的平方等于九。

e.en: He {squared} his shoulders and walked into the interview.
e.zh: 他挺直肩膀走进了面试现场。

squarely.t: adv. 正对地；直截了当地

e.en: The blame falls {squarely} on management's shoulders.
e.zh: 责任完全落在管理层的肩上。

e.en: She looked him {squarely} in the eye and refused.
e.zh: 她直视着他的眼睛,断然拒绝。

e.en: Carpenters check the {squareness} of every corner carefully.
e.zh: 木匠会仔细检查每个角的方正度。

e.en: The frame's {squareness} matters for a clean print.
e.zh: 画框的方正度对干净的印刷效果很重要。

squares.t: n. square 的复数，正方形；广场

e.en: The chessboard has sixty-four alternating {squares}.
e.zh: 国际象棋棋盘有六十四个交替的方格。

e.en: European cities are famous for their lively {squares}.
e.zh: 欧洲城市以其热闹的广场而闻名。

e.en: The room had a {squarish} shape with rounded corners.
e.zh: 这个房间形状偏方形，带有圆角。

e.en: He sketched a {squarish} icon for the new app.
e.zh: 他为新应用画了一个近似方形的图标。

squash.t:
v. 压扁；挤进
n. 壁球；南瓜

e.en: Don't {squash} the bread when you pack the lunch.
e.zh: 装午餐时别把面包压扁了。

e.en: We grow butternut {squash} in the backyard garden.
e.zh: 我们在后院菜园种胡桃南瓜。

squashed.t:
adj. 被压扁的
v. 挤压（过去式）

e.en: The package arrived completely {squashed} by heavy boxes.
e.zh: 包裹被重箱子压得完全变形了。

e.en: Six people were {squashed} into the back of the car.
e.zh: 六个人挤在汽车后座里。

squashes.t: v. squash 的第三人称单数

e.en: He {squashes} every spider he sees in the kitchen.
e.zh: 他在厨房里见到蜘蛛就一脚踩扁。

e.en: The market sells pumpkins and other autumn {squashes}.
e.zh: 市场上卖南瓜和其他秋季瓜类。

e.en: Stop {squashing} the cushions on the new sofa.
e.zh: 别再把新沙发的靠垫压扁了。

e.en: The manager kept {squashing} every creative idea proposed.
e.zh: 经理把每一个创意点子都打压下去。

e.en: I sank into the {squashy} armchair and fell asleep.
e.zh: 我陷进软乎乎的扶手椅就睡着了。

e.en: The peaches felt {squashy} after sitting in the bag.
e.zh: 桃子在袋子里放久了，摸起来软塌塌的。

squat.t:
v. 蹲下；擅自占住
adj. 矮胖的

e.en: {Squat} down and lift the box with your legs.
e.zh: 蹲下来用腿的力量把箱子抬起来。

e.en: A {squat} stone tower stood at the edge of town.
e.zh: 一座低矮粗壮的石塔立在镇子边上。

e.en: A {squatter} had been living in the abandoned house for months.
e.zh: 有个擅自占屋者已在那栋废弃房子里住了好几个月。

e.en: Police evicted the {squatter} from the empty office building.
e.zh: 警方将擅自占用者从空置的办公楼里驱离。

e.en: She was {squatting} by the fire to warm her hands.
e.zh: 她蹲在火边暖手。

e.en: Several families were {squatting} in the abandoned warehouse.
e.zh: 几户人家在废弃的仓库里擅自居住。

squaw.t: n. (冒犯语) 北美印第安妇女

e.en: The old novel uses the offensive term {squaw} repeatedly.
e.zh: 这本旧小说反复使用了带有冒犯性的"squaw"一词。

e.en: Many places once named {squaw} have since been renamed.
e.zh: 许多曾以"squaw"命名的地方后来都改了名。

squawfish.t: n. 北美淡水鱼，柱骨鱼

e.en: Anglers caught a large {squawfish} in the Colorado River.
e.zh: 钓鱼者在科罗拉多河钓到一条大型北美鳕鲈。

e.en: The {squawfish} has been renamed pikeminnow in modern guides.
e.zh: 现代图鉴里已把这种鱼改名为狗鱼鲦。

squawk.t:
v. (鸟) 嘎嘎叫；大声抱怨
n. 怪叫声

e.en: The parrot let out a loud {squawk} from its cage.
e.zh: 鹦鹉在笼子里发出一声响亮的尖叫。

e.en: Customers always {squawk} when prices suddenly go up.
e.zh: 价格一涨，顾客总会大声抱怨。

squawking.t: v. 嘎嘎尖叫；高声抱怨

e.en: Seagulls were {squawking} above the fishing boats all morning.
e.zh: 海鸥整个上午都在渔船上方聒噪地叫。

e.en: Stop {squawking} about the bill and just pay it.
e.zh: 别再为账单大呼小叫了，付钱就是了。

squeak.t:
n. 吱吱声
v. 发出吱吱声

e.en: The old door let out a sharp {squeak} when opened.
e.zh: 那扇旧门一打开就发出尖锐的吱呀声。

e.en: The team managed to {squeak} into the playoffs by one point.
e.zh: 球队以一分之差勉强挤进了季后赛。

squeaker.t: n. 险胜；会吱叫的东西

e.en: The final game was a real {squeaker}, decided in overtime.
e.zh: 决赛是一场惊险的险胜，加时赛才分出胜负。

e.en: The puppy chewed the {squeaker} out of its toy.
e.zh: 小狗把玩具里的发声器咬了出来。

e.en: The {squeaking} hinge needs a drop of oil.
e.zh: 吱吱响的合页需要滴一点油。

e.en: Mice were {squeaking} somewhere behind the kitchen wall.
e.zh: 老鼠在厨房墙后面什么地方吱吱叫。

e.en: His new sneakers are really {squeaky} on the gym floor.
e.zh: 他的新运动鞋在体育馆地板上嘎吱响个不停。

e.en: The brand built a {squeaky} clean reputation over decades.
e.zh: 这个品牌几十年来建立了一尘不染的好名声。

squeal.t:
v. 尖声叫；告密
n. 长而尖的叫声

e.en: The kids let out a happy {squeal} at the surprise.
e.zh: 孩子们看到惊喜，发出开心的尖叫。

e.en: Police feared the suspect would {squeal} on his partners.
e.zh: 警方担心嫌犯会向警方告发同伙。

squealer.t: n. 告密者；爱尖叫的人

e.en: Nobody on the team trusted the known {squealer}.
e.zh: 队里没人信任那个出了名的告密者。

e.en: The brakes on that truck are a real {squealer}.
e.zh: 那辆卡车的刹车真是吱吱响个不停。

e.en: The car came to a stop with tires {squealing}.
e.zh: 汽车伴随着轮胎的尖啸声停了下来。

e.en: The children were {squealing} with delight on the slide.
e.zh: 孩子们在滑梯上高兴地尖叫着。

squeamish.t: adj. 易反胃的；过于讲究的

e.en: I'm too {squeamish} to watch surgery videos online.
e.zh: 我太容易反胃，看不了网上的手术视频。

e.en: Don't be {squeamish} about asking for a raise.
e.zh: 别不好意思开口要求加薪。

e.en: The meadow was designated an {SSSI} for its rare orchids.
e.zh: 这片草地因稀有兰花被列为特别科学价值地。

e.en: Building near an {SSSI} requires special environmental approval.
e.zh: 在特别科学价值地附近施工需要特别的环保审批。

e.en: Several Welsh {SSSIs} protect ancient woodland habitats.
e.zh: 威尔士有几处特别科学价值地保护着古老林地。

e.en: The agency monitors {SSSIs} to track biodiversity changes.
e.zh: 该机构监测各特别科学价值地以追踪生物多样性变化。

sst.t: n. 海表温度（sea surface temperature 缩写）

stab.t:
v. 刺，戳
n. 尝试，一下

e.en: I'll take a {stab} at solving this puzzle tonight.
e.zh: 我今晚试着解一下这个谜题。

e.en: She felt a sharp {stab} of pain in her side.
e.zh: 她侧腹突然一阵剧痛。

e.en: He {stabbed} the fork into the steak impatiently.
e.zh: 他不耐烦地把叉子戳进牛排里。

e.en: Her words {stabbed} him deeper than any insult could.
e.zh: 她的话比任何侮辱都更刺痛他。

stabbing.t:
n. 刺伤事件
adj. 剧痛的

e.en: She felt a {stabbing} pain behind her left eye.
e.zh: 她左眼后面感到一阵刺痛。

e.en: Police are investigating the {stabbing} that happened downtown.
e.zh: 警方正在调查市中心发生的持刀伤人案。

e.en: The patient required {stabilisation} before the surgery could proceed.
e.zh: 病人在手术前需要先稳定状态。

e.en: Currency {stabilisation} is the central bank's top priority.
e.zh: 稳定货币是央行的首要任务。

e.en: Doctors worked quickly to {stabilise} the patient's blood pressure.
e.zh: 医生迅速采取措施稳定病人的血压。

e.en: Adding ballast helped {stabilise} the small sailing boat.
e.zh: 加入压舱物帮助稳住了这艘小帆船。

stabilised.t: v. 使稳定（过去式，英式）

e.en: Markets {stabilised} after the central bank's announcement.
e.zh: 央行发布消息后,市场逐渐稳定下来。

e.en: Once her fever {stabilised}, she was discharged from hospital.
e.zh: 她的体温一稳定下来就出院了。

e.en: My toddler still rides with a {stabiliser} on his bike.
e.zh: 我家小朋友骑车还带着辅助轮。

e.en: This yoghurt contains a natural {stabiliser} from seaweed.
e.zh: 这款酸奶含有从海藻提取的天然稳定剂。

e.en: The new gimbal {stabilises} footage even when running.
e.zh: 这款新稳定器即使在奔跑时也能稳定画面。

e.en: Daily exercise {stabilises} blood sugar levels in most adults.
e.zh: 每天运动能让大多数成年人的血糖保持稳定。

e.en: The medication is {stabilising} her heart rate gradually.
e.zh: 这种药正在逐渐稳定她的心率。

e.en: Trees play a {stabilising} role in preventing soil erosion.
e.zh: 树木在防止水土流失方面起着稳固作用。

e.en: Engineers compared the {stabilities} of three different bridge designs.
e.zh: 工程师比较了三种不同桥梁设计的稳定性。

e.en: Different chemical {stabilities} affect how long medicines stay effective.
e.zh: 不同的化学稳定性会影响药物保持有效的时间。

e.en: This phone case offers great {stability} when filming videos.
e.zh: 这款手机壳在拍视频时能提供很好的稳定性。

e.en: Job {stability} matters more to her than a higher salary.
e.zh: 工作稳定对她来说比高薪更重要。

e.en: The drone uses gyroscopic {stabilization} for smooth aerial shots.
e.zh: 这款无人机用陀螺仪稳定来获得平滑的航拍画面。

e.en: Economic {stabilization} took years after the financial crisis.
e.zh: 金融危机后,经济花了好几年才稳定下来。

e.en: Take deep breaths to {stabilize} your heart rate before speaking.
e.zh: 发言前深呼吸,让心率稳定下来。

e.en: Engineers added steel beams to {stabilize} the old building.
e.zh: 工程师加装了钢梁来加固这座旧楼。

e.en: Her condition {stabilized} overnight in the intensive care unit.
e.zh: 她的病情在重症监护室一夜之间稳定下来。

e.en: The footage looks much smoother once {stabilized} in post-production.
e.zh: 视频在后期防抖处理后看起来流畅多了。

e.en: This camera {stabilizer} costs less than a hundred dollars.
e.zh: 这款相机稳定器售价不到一百美元。

e.en: The aircraft's tail {stabilizer} was damaged during landing.
e.zh: 飞机的尾部安定面在着陆时受损。

e.en: Yoga {stabilizes} both your mood and your core muscles.
e.zh: 瑜伽既能稳定情绪,又能锻炼核心肌群。

e.en: This compound {stabilizes} the vaccine at room temperature.
e.zh: 这种化合物能让疫苗在常温下保持稳定。

e.en: The Fed is focused on {stabilizing} prices this year.
e.zh: 美联储今年的重点是稳定物价。

e.en: She's {stabilizing} her tripod before taking the long-exposure shot.
e.zh: 她正在固定三脚架,准备拍长曝光照片。

stable.t:
adj. 稳定的
n. 马厩

e.en: His income has been {stable} for the past five years.
e.zh: 过去五年他的收入一直很稳定。

e.en: The horses returned to the {stable} after the race.
e.zh: 赛后,马匹回到了马厩。

e.en: The young {stableboy} fed the horses every morning at dawn.
e.zh: 年轻的马童每天清晨给马喂食。

e.en: He worked as a {stableboy} before becoming a famous jockey.
e.zh: 他在成为著名骑师前曾做过马童。

e.en: The {stableman} brushed the horse's mane with practiced ease.
e.zh: 马夫熟练地梳理着马的鬃毛。

e.en: An old {stableman} taught her how to saddle the pony.
e.zh: 一位年长的马夫教她如何给小马上鞍。

stablemate.t: n. 同一马厩的马；同公司出品

e.en: The new SUV is a {stablemate} of the popular sedan.
e.zh: 这款新 SUV 与那款热销轿车出自同一品牌。

e.en: Her horse trained alongside its {stablemate} every morning.
e.zh: 她的马每天早上和同厩的马一起训练。

stabling.t:
n. 马厩设施
v. 关入马厩

e.en: The farm offers {stabling} for up to twenty horses.
e.zh: 这家农场最多可为二十匹马提供马厩。

e.en: Overnight {stabling} costs forty dollars per horse.
e.zh: 过夜寄养每匹马收费四十美元。

e.en: The drone hovered {stably} despite the strong crosswinds.
e.zh: 尽管侧风很大,无人机依然稳定地悬停着。

e.en: The patient has been recovering {stably} since last week.
e.zh: 病人从上周开始稳定地恢复中。

stabs.t:
v. 刺（三单）
n. 刺戳（复数）

e.en: She {stabs} her salad with the fork while reading email.
e.zh: 她一边看邮件,一边用叉子戳着沙拉。

e.en: He made several {stabs} at fixing the broken code.
e.zh: 他几次尝试修复这段出问题的代码。

e.en: We climbed the rocky {stac} off the Scottish coast.
e.zh: 我们攀上了苏格兰海岸外那座岩柱小岛。

e.en: Seabirds nest on the isolated {stac} every spring.
e.zh: 每年春天海鸟都在这座孤立的海蚀柱上筑巢。

staccato.t: adj. 断奏的，断断续续的

e.en: Her {staccato} typing filled the otherwise silent office.
e.zh: 她断奏般的打字声充满了原本安静的办公室。

e.en: The pianist played the passage in sharp {staccato} notes.
e.zh: 钢琴家以清脆的断奏弹奏了这一段。

stack.t:
n. 堆；技术栈
v. 堆叠

e.en: There's a {stack} of unread books on my nightstand.
e.zh: 我床头柜上堆着一摞还没看的书。

e.en: Our backend {stack} runs on Node.js and PostgreSQL.
e.zh: 我们的后端技术栈用的是 Node.js 和 PostgreSQL。

stacked.t: adj. 堆叠的；配置丰富的

e.en: She {stacked} the dishes neatly in the cupboard.
e.zh: 她把碗碟整齐地摞进橱柜里。

e.en: The deck is {stacked} against small startups in this market.
e.zh: 在这个市场,小型创业公司处于明显劣势。

e.en: The warehouse uses an automated {stacker} to organize pallets.
e.zh: 仓库使用自动堆垛机来整理货盘。

e.en: He works as a shelf {stacker} at the local supermarket.
e.zh: 他在当地超市当理货员。

stacking.t:
n. 堆叠
v. 堆放中

e.en: She's {stacking} firewood neatly behind the cabin.
e.zh: 她正在小屋后面整齐地码放柴火。

e.en: The chairs are designed for easy {stacking} after events.
e.zh: 这些椅子设计成活动结束后可以方便地叠放。

stacks.t:
n. 一堆（复数）
v. 堆叠（三单）

e.en: There are {stacks} of paperwork waiting on my desk.
e.zh: 我桌上堆着一摞摞待处理的文件。

e.en: He earns {stacks} of cash from his side business.
e.zh: 他靠副业赚了一大把现金。

e.en: Several Olympic {stadia} were built specifically for the 2008 games.
e.zh: 有几座奥运体育场是专为 2008 年奥运会建造的。

e.en: Modern {stadia} now feature retractable roofs and giant screens.
e.zh: 现代体育场都配有可伸缩屋顶和巨型屏幕。

e.en: The {stadium} was packed for the World Cup final.
e.zh: 世界杯决赛当晚体育场座无虚席。

e.en: They're building a new {stadium} on the city's south side.
e.zh: 他们正在城市南边新建一座体育场。

e.en: Many old {stadiums} have been replaced with modern arenas.
e.zh: 许多旧体育场已经被现代化场馆取代。

e.en: The tour will visit ten {stadiums} across Europe this summer.
e.zh: 今年夏天巡演将走遍欧洲十座体育场。

staff.t:
n. 员工，职员
v. 配备人员

e.en: The hotel {staff} were friendly and incredibly helpful.
e.zh: 酒店员工既友好又乐于助人。

e.en: We need to {staff} the support desk during the launch.
e.zh: 产品发布期间我们需要给客服台配人手。

e.en: The clinic is {staffed} by volunteer doctors on weekends.
e.zh: 这家诊所周末由志愿医生值班。

e.en: The booth was fully {staffed} throughout the conference.
e.zh: 整个会议期间展位都安排了充足的工作人员。

e.en: A junior {staffer} leaked the memo to the press.
e.zh: 一名初级职员把这份备忘录泄露给了媒体。

e.en: She's a senior {staffer} in the senator's office.
e.zh: 她是这位参议员办公室的资深助理。

e.en: {Staffing} shortages have forced the restaurant to close earlier.
e.zh: 人手不足迫使这家餐厅提早打烊。

e.en: We use a {staffing} agency to find seasonal workers.
e.zh: 我们通过人力中介公司招聘季节性员工。

stafford.t: n. 斯塔福德（地名/姓氏）

e.en: The train to {Stafford} leaves from platform seven.
e.zh: 开往斯塔福德的火车从七号站台发车。

e.en: She grew up in {Stafford} before moving to London.
e.zh: 她在斯塔福德长大,后来才搬到伦敦。

e.en: She inherited a beautiful {Staffordshire} porcelain figurine from her grandmother.
e.zh: 她从祖母那里继承了一件精美的斯塔福德郡瓷塑像。

e.en: The football match was held in {Staffordshire} last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末那场足球比赛在斯塔福德郡举行。

e.en: Teachers gathered in the {staffroom} during their lunch break.
e.zh: 老师们在午休时聚集在教师休息室里。

e.en: The {staffroom} smelled of fresh coffee and photocopier ink.
e.zh: 教师休息室里弥漫着新鲜咖啡和复印机墨水的味道。

staffs.t:
n. 员工（复数）
v. 配员（三单）

e.en: The hospital {staffs} its emergency room around the clock.
e.zh: 这家医院的急诊室全天候配备人员。

e.en: Both {staffs} cooperated smoothly on the joint project.
e.zh: 两个团队在合作项目上配合得十分顺畅。

e.en: The old shepherd carried wooden {stafves} cut from oak branches.
e.zh: 老牧羊人带着用橡木枝削成的木杖。

e.en: Hikers leaned on their {stafves} as they climbed the steep trail.
e.zh: 徒步者们拄着拐杖攀登陡峭的山路。

stag.t:
n. 雄鹿
adj. 男士专场的

e.en: A magnificent {stag} appeared at the edge of the forest.
e.zh: 一头雄伟的雄鹿出现在森林边缘。

e.en: He went {stag} to the wedding since his date cancelled.
e.zh: 他独自一人去了婚礼,因为约会的对象取消了。

squeamishness.t: n. 易恶心；神经质的挑剔

e.en: Her {squeamishness} around blood ruled out medical school.
e.zh: 她见血就不舒服，因此放弃了学医。

e.en: Investors showed some {squeamishness} after the market drop.
e.zh: 市场下跌后，投资者显得有些畏缩不前。

squeegee.t:
n. 橡胶刮板（擦玻璃用）
v. 用刮板刮净

e.en: Use a rubber {squeegee} to dry the shower glass.
e.zh: 用橡胶刮水器把淋浴玻璃刮干。

e.en: He'll {squeegee} the windshield while you pump the gas.
e.zh: 你加油时他会顺便刮一下挡风玻璃。

squeeze.t:
v. 挤压；榨取
n. 挤压；拮据

e.en: Can you {squeeze} one more person into the elevator?
e.zh: 电梯里还能再挤进一个人吗？

e.en: Rising rent is putting a real {squeeze} on small businesses.
e.zh: 租金上涨给小企业带来了实实在在的压力。

e.en: Grandpa played a lively tune on his old {squeezebox}.
e.zh: 爷爷用他那台旧手风琴奏出一支欢快的曲子。

e.en: The street musician carried a battered {squeezebox} in his case.
e.zh: 街头艺人琴箱里装着一台破旧的手风琴。

squeezed.t:
v. 挤压（过去式）
adj. 被压榨的

e.en: She {squeezed} fresh lemon juice over the grilled fish.
e.zh: 她在烤鱼上挤了些新鲜柠檬汁。

e.en: Five of us {squeezed} into a tiny taxi.
e.zh: 我们五个人挤进了一辆小出租车。

e.en: This citrus {squeezer} gets every drop out of a lemon.
e.zh: 这个柑橘榨汁器能把柠檬榨得一滴不剩。

e.en: The wholesaler is a real price {squeezer} with suppliers.
e.zh: 这家批发商对供应商压价压得很狠。

squeezes.t:
v. 挤压（第三人称单数）
n. 挤压（复数）

e.en: He always {squeezes} my hand before a big meeting.
e.zh: 重要会议前他总会捏一下我的手。

e.en: The old engine still {squeezes} out forty miles per gallon.
e.zh: 这台旧发动机仍能勉强跑出每加仑四十英里。

e.en: She was {squeezing} toothpaste from a nearly empty tube.
e.zh: 她从一个快空了的牙膏管里挤牙膏。

e.en: Tax hikes are {squeezing} middle-class families this year.
e.zh: 今年的加税让中产家庭日子越来越紧。

squelch.t:
v. 压制；发出吧唧声
n. 噪声抑制

e.en: Management moved quickly to {squelch} the rumors.
e.zh: 管理层迅速采取行动压下了这些传言。

e.en: My boots {squelch} loudly with every step in the mud.
e.zh: 我的靴子在泥里每走一步都发出咕叽声。

squelching.t: v. 压制；踩水发声（现在分词）

e.en: We heard footsteps {squelching} through the wet grass.
e.zh: 我们听见脚步在湿草地上咕叽咕叽地走过。

e.en: The CEO is accused of {squelching} dissent inside the company.
e.zh: 这位CEO被指责在公司内部压制不同声音。

squelchy.t: adj. 踩上去吧唧作响的；湿软的

e.en: The trail got {squelchy} after three days of rain.
e.zh: 下了三天雨后，小路变得湿软泥泞。

e.en: My socks felt cold and {squelchy} inside my boots.
e.zh: 我靴子里的袜子又冷又湿黏。

e.en: The newspaper ran a short {squib} about the local festival.
e.zh: 报纸刊登了一则关于本地节日的短讯。

e.en: The big launch turned out to be a damp {squib}.
e.zh: 那场盛大发布会最终成了一场令人失望的哑炮。

e.en: We ordered grilled {squid} with lemon at the seaside restaurant.
e.zh: 我们在海边餐厅点了烤鱿鱼配柠檬。

e.en: A giant {squid} was filmed deep in the Pacific Ocean.
e.zh: 一只巨型乌贼在太平洋深处被拍到。

e.en: The chocolate cake had a deliciously {squidgy} center.
e.zh: 那块巧克力蛋糕的内里软糯香甜，特别好吃。

e.en: My toddler loves anything {squidgy} he can squeeze.
e.zh: 我家小宝宝喜欢一切能捏的软乎乎的东西。

e.en: She drew a quick {squiggle} as her signature.
e.zh: 她随手画了个弯弯曲曲的线作为签名。

e.en: Add a {squiggle} of caramel sauce on top of the ice cream.
e.zh: 在冰淇淋上面挤一道弯弯的焦糖酱。

squiggly.t: adj. 弯弯曲曲的；波浪形的

e.en: The editor underlined the typo with a {squiggly} red line.
e.zh: 编辑用一条波浪状的红线划出了拼写错误。

e.en: The toddler drew {squiggly} lines all over the wall.
e.zh: 小孩子在墙上画满了弯弯扭扭的线。

squinch.t: v. 眯起眼睛；缩成一团

e.en: Don't {squinch} your face like that for the photo.
e.zh: 拍照时别那样把脸皱成一团。

e.en: Try to {squinch} closer so we all fit in the frame.
e.zh: 再往里挤一挤，这样大家都能拍进画面。

squint.t:
v. 眯眼看
n. 斜视

e.en: I had to {squint} to read the tiny print on the label.
e.zh: 我得眯起眼睛才能看清标签上的小字。

e.en: The bright sun made everyone {squint} on the beach.
e.zh: 刺眼的阳光让海滩上的每个人都眯起了眼。

e.en: He {squinted} at the screen to read the error message.
e.zh: 他眯起眼睛看屏幕上的报错信息。

e.en: She {squinted} suspiciously when he offered an excuse.
e.zh: 他找借口时她眯眼狐疑地看着他。

e.en: You're {squinting} again — maybe it's time for glasses.
e.zh: 你又在眯着眼看东西了，也许该配眼镜了。

e.en: He stood {squinting} into the morning sun on the balcony.
e.zh: 他站在阳台上眯着眼望向晨光。

squints.t:
v. 眯眼看（第三人称单数）
n. 斜视（复数）

e.en: She always {squints} at her phone in bright sunlight.
e.zh: 在强光下她看手机时总要眯起眼睛。

e.en: The doctor checks for {squints} during the eye exam.
e.zh: 医生在眼科检查时会查看是否有斜视。

squinty.t: adj. 眯缝着眼的；斜视的

e.en: He gave me a {squinty} look across the dinner table.
e.zh: 他隔着餐桌眯着眼瞥了我一眼。

e.en: The photo caught her with a {squinty} sunny smile.
e.zh: 照片捕捉到她在阳光下眯眼微笑的样子。

squire.t:
n. 乡绅；地主
v. 陪伴（女士）

e.en: The young {squire} polished the knight's armor every morning.
e.zh: 年轻的侍从每天早上都为骑士擦亮盔甲。

e.en: The local {squire} owned most of the land around the village.
e.zh: 当地的乡绅拥有村子周围的大部分土地。

squirearchy.t: n. 乡绅阶层；地主统治

e.en: The novel mocks the country {squirearchy} of the time.
e.zh: 这部小说讽刺了当时的乡绅地主阶层。

e.en: Power in the county rested with a small rural {squirearchy}.
e.zh: 郡里的权力掌握在一小撮乡绅地主手中。

squirm.t:
v. 蠕动；局促不安
n. 蠕动

e.en: Tough interview questions made the candidate {squirm} a little.
e.zh: 尖锐的面试问题让那位候选人有点坐立不安。

e.en: The puppy began to {squirm} as soon as I picked it up.
e.zh: 我一抱起小狗，它就开始扭来扭去。

e.en: The child {squirmed} in his seat during the long sermon.
e.zh: 漫长的布道中，那孩子在座位上扭来扭去。

e.en: He {squirmed} when asked about his missing expense receipts.
e.zh: 被问到丢失的报销凭证时，他显得局促不安。

squirming.t: v. 扭动；局促不安（现在分词）

e.en: Stop {squirming} so I can tie your shoelaces properly.
e.zh: 别扭来扭去，这样我才能好好给你系鞋带。

e.en: The witness was clearly {squirming} under the lawyer's questions.
e.zh: 在律师的盘问下，证人明显坐立难安。

squirms.t: v. 扭动（第三人称单数）

e.en: My nephew {squirms} every time I try to take a photo.
e.zh: 我每次给侄子拍照，他都扭来扭去。

e.en: She {squirms} whenever conversations turn to her ex.
e.zh: 一聊到她前任，她就浑身不自在。

squirmy.t: adj. 扭来扭去的；令人不安的

e.en: The baby gets {squirmy} when she's ready for a nap.
e.zh: 宝宝想睡觉时就会变得扭来扭去坐不住。

e.en: I felt {squirmy} watching the awkward romantic scene.
e.zh: 看那段尴尬的浪漫戏让我浑身不自在。

squirrel.t:
n. 松鼠
v. 贮藏（away）

e.en: A {squirrel} buried acorns under the oak tree yesterday.
e.zh: 一只松鼠昨天把橡子埋在橡树下。

e.en: He tends to {squirrel} away snacks in his desk drawer.
e.zh: 他喜欢把零食藏在办公桌抽屉里。

squirrelly.t: adj. 古怪的；坐立不安的

e.en: The kids get {squirrelly} after eating too much sugar.
e.zh: 孩子们吃太多糖后就变得坐不住。

e.en: His {squirrelly} behavior made everyone suspicious at the meeting.
e.zh: 他古怪的举动让会议上每个人都起疑。

squirt.t:
v. 喷射；挤出
n. 喷流

e.en: Just {squirt} a little lemon juice on the salmon.
e.zh: 在三文鱼上挤一点柠檬汁就行。

e.en: The toy gun can {squirt} water up to ten feet.
e.zh: 这把玩具枪能把水喷出十英尺远。

squish.t:
v. 压扁；发出咕叽声
n. 压扁声

e.en: Don't {squish} the bread when you put it in the bag.
e.zh: 把面包放进袋子时别压扁了。

e.en: Kids love to {squish} the slime between their fingers.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢用手指捏挤这种黏液玩具。

e.en: The mochi has a soft, {squishy} texture inside.
e.zh: 麻薯里面有种柔软、Q弹的口感。

e.en: My new pillow is {squishy} and super comfortable.
e.zh: 我的新枕头软绵绵的,非常舒服。

sri.t: n. 室利（印度对男性的尊称）

srinagar.t: n. 斯利那加（印度城市）

e.en: We flew into {Srinagar} to start our Kashmir trip.
e.zh: 我们飞到斯利那加,开始克什米尔之旅。

e.en: The houseboats on Dal Lake make {Srinagar} unforgettable.
e.zh: 达尔湖上的船屋让斯利那加令人难忘。

sro.t: abbr. 单间出租公寓（single room occupancy）

srs.t: abbr. 辅助安全气囊系统（汽车）

ssa.t: abbr. 美国社会保障局（Social Security Administration）

e.en: The bank uses {SSAP} guidelines for its accounting standards.
e.zh: 该银行采用 SSAP 准则进行会计核算。

e.en: Older UK reports still reference the {SSAP} framework occasionally.
e.zh: 较早的英国报告偶尔还会引用 SSAP 框架。

ssc.t: abbr. 常见于超级计算中心或固态电容等语境

ssd.t: abbr. 固态硬盘（Solid State Drive）

ssds.t: n. 固态硬盘（SSD 的复数）

e.en: Modern laptops ship with {SSDs} instead of spinning hard drives.
e.zh: 现代笔记本电脑都配备固态硬盘,而非机械硬盘。

e.en: The data center upgraded all servers to NVMe {SSDs}.
e.zh: 数据中心把所有服务器升级成了 NVMe 固态硬盘。

sse.t: abbr. 东南偏南（方位）；流式SIMD扩展指令集

ssh.t: abbr. 安全外壳协议（远程登录）

ssp.t: abbr. 广告供应方平台（Supply-Side Platform）

ssrs.t: abbr. SQL Server 报表服务

e.en: Our finance team builds monthly reports in {SSRS}.
e.zh: 我们的财务团队用 SSRS 制作月度报表。

e.en: Microsoft is gradually replacing {SSRS} with Power BI.
e.zh: 微软正逐步用 Power BI 取代 SSRS。

stalk.t:
v. 跟踪骚扰
n. (植物的) 茎

e.en: Lions {stalk} their prey silently through tall grass.
e.zh: 狮子在高草丛中悄无声息地潜近猎物。

e.en: She trimmed the dry {stalk} off the flower.
e.zh: 她把花上干枯的茎剪掉了。

e.en: Police arrested the {stalker} outside her apartment.
e.zh: 警方在她公寓外逮捕了那名跟踪狂。

e.en: He felt like a {stalker} after refreshing her profile ten times.
e.zh: 他刷了十次她的主页,感觉自己像个跟踪狂。

e.en: The actress got a restraining order against the man {stalking} her.
e.zh: 那位女演员对跟踪她的男子申请了限制令。

e.en: A tiger was {stalking} a deer near the river.
e.zh: 一只老虎正在河边潜行接近一头鹿。

stall.t:
n. 摊位；小隔间
v. 拖延；熄火

e.en: The engine began to {stall} on the steep hill.
e.zh: 汽车在陡坡上开始熄火。

e.en: She bought fresh mangoes from a fruit {stall}.
e.zh: 她在一个水果摊买了新鲜的芒果。

stalled.t:
adj. 停滞的；熄火的
v. stall 的过去式

e.en: Negotiations have {stalled} over wages and working hours.
e.zh: 谈判因工资和工时问题陷入僵局。

e.en: My car {stalled} right in the middle of the intersection.
e.zh: 我的车正好在十字路口熄火了。

e.en: The market {stallholder} offered me a free sample.
e.zh: 市场摊主请我免费试吃了一份。

e.en: Each {stallholder} must register with the city council.
e.zh: 每位摊主都必须在市政厅登记。

e.en: Stop {stalling} and just give me a straight answer.
e.zh: 别再拖延了,直接给我一个明确的答复。

e.en: The pilot worried about the plane {stalling} at low speed.
e.zh: 飞行员担心飞机在低速时失速。

stallion.t: n. 种马（未阉割的公马）

e.en: The black {stallion} galloped across the open field.
e.zh: 那匹黑色种马在开阔的田野上奔驰。

e.en: She trains a champion {stallion} for show jumping.
e.zh: 她训练一匹冠军种马参加障碍赛。

stallone.t: n. 史泰龙（姓氏，常指演员）

e.en: Sylvester {Stallone} became famous for the Rocky films.
e.zh: 西尔维斯特·史泰龙因《洛奇》系列电影而成名。

e.en: My dad still rewatches every {Stallone} action movie.
e.zh: 我爸爸至今仍会重看每一部史泰龙的动作片。

stalls.t:
n. 摊位（复数）
n. 剧院正厅前排座位

e.en: The night market has dozens of food {stalls}.
e.zh: 夜市上有几十个小吃摊。

e.en: His old motorbike often {stalls} at red lights.
e.zh: 他那辆旧摩托车经常在红灯前熄火。

stalwart.t:
n. 忠实拥护者
adj. 坚定的

e.en: She is a {stalwart} supporter of the local library.
e.zh: 她是当地图书馆坚定的支持者。

e.en: The team's {stalwart} defender played every match this season.
e.zh: 球队那位忠实的后卫本赛季每场都出战。

e.en: The yellow {stamen} of the lily was covered in pollen.
e.zh: 百合花的黄色雄蕊上沾满了花粉。

e.en: Bees brush against the {stamen} as they collect nectar.
e.zh: 蜜蜂采蜜时会蹭到雄蕊。

e.en: She commutes from {Stamford} to Manhattan every weekday.
