e.zh: 她每个工作日都从斯坦福市通勤到曼哈顿。

e.en: The conference will be held in downtown {Stamford} next month.
e.zh: 会议将于下月在斯坦福市中心举行。

e.en: Marathon runners need incredible {stamina} to finish the race.
e.zh: 马拉松选手需要惊人的耐力才能跑完全程。

e.en: Toddlers seem to have endless {stamina} for playing.
e.zh: 幼儿玩耍时似乎有用不完的精力。

e.en: The coach compared the {staminas} of the two athletes.
e.zh: 教练比较了两位运动员的耐力水平。

e.en: Different sports demand different {staminas} from players.
e.zh: 不同的运动对运动员的耐力要求各不相同。

stammer.t:
v. 结结巴巴地说
n. 口吃

e.en: He began to {stammer} when the teacher called his name.
e.zh: 老师叫他名字时,他开始结结巴巴起来。

e.en: She has had a slight {stammer} since childhood.
e.zh: 她从小就有点口吃。

stammered.t: v. stammer 的过去式，结巴地说出

e.en: He {stammered} an apology and quickly left the room.
e.zh: 他结结巴巴地道了个歉,然后匆匆离开了房间。

e.en: She {stammered} through her speech, clearly nervous on stage.
e.zh: 她在台上明显紧张,演讲时结结巴巴。

stammering.t:
v. 结巴地说
adj. 口吃的

e.en: He kept {stammering} as he tried to ask her out.
e.zh: 他想约她出去时一直结结巴巴。

e.en: Speech therapy helped reduce his {stammering} significantly.
e.zh: 言语治疗大大减轻了他的口吃。

stammers.t: v. 结巴地说（第三人称单数）

e.en: He always {stammers} when he speaks in public.
e.zh: 他每次在公众面前讲话都会结巴。

e.en: The child's {stammers} faded after months of practice.
e.zh: 经过数月练习,这个孩子的结巴消失了。

stamp.t:
n. 邮票；印章
v. 盖章；跺脚

e.en: Don't forget to put a {stamp} on the envelope.
e.zh: 别忘了在信封上贴邮票。

e.en: Please {stamp} your passport at the immigration counter.
e.zh: 请在入境柜台给您的护照盖章。

stamped.t: v. 盖过章的；已贴邮票的

e.en: The officer {stamped} my passport without saying a word.
e.zh: 那位官员一言不发地在我的护照上盖了章。

e.en: She {stamped} her foot in frustration.
e.zh: 她沮丧地跺了跺脚。

stampede.t:
n. 踩踏事件；蜂拥
v. 蜂拥奔逃

e.en: A sudden noise caused the cattle to {stampede}.
e.zh: 突如其来的噪声让牛群惊慌奔逃。

e.en: There was a {stampede} for tickets when sales opened.
e.zh: 开售时人们蜂拥而上抢票。

e.en: A herd of buffalo came {stampeding} across the plains.
e.zh: 一群水牛在平原上狂奔而来。

e.en: Shoppers were {stampeding} into the store on Black Friday.
e.zh: 黑色星期五,购物者蜂拥涌入商店。

stamping.t:
v. 盖章；跺脚
n. 冲压件

e.en: The children were {stamping} in puddles after the rain.
e.zh: 雨后孩子们在水坑里使劲跺脚玩。

e.en: She was {stamping} envelopes for the morning mail.
e.zh: 她正在给早班邮件的信封盖邮戳。

stamps.t:
n. 邮票（复数）
v. 盖章（单三）

e.en: He collects rare {stamps} from around the world.
e.zh: 他收藏世界各地的珍稀邮票。

e.en: The clerk {stamps} every form before filing it away.
e.zh: 那位职员在归档前会给每份表格盖章。

stan.t:
n. 狂热粉丝
v. 狂热追捧

e.en: She's a total {stan} of that K-pop group.
e.zh: 她是那个韩团的狂热粉丝。

e.en: Don't {stan} celebrities you don't actually know.
e.zh: 别盲目追捧你其实并不了解的明星。

e.en: The company softened its {stance} on remote work.
e.zh: 公司对远程办公的立场有所软化。

e.en: The boxer adjusted his {stance} before the next round.
e.zh: 拳击手在下一回合前调整了站姿。

e.en: The two parties hold opposing {stances} on the issue.
e.zh: 两党在这个问题上立场对立。

e.en: Yoga teaches a variety of balanced {stances}.
e.zh: 瑜伽教授各种平衡的站姿。

stanch.t:
v. 止住（血流）
adj. 坚定的

e.en: The nurse used gauze to {stanch} the bleeding.
e.zh: 护士用纱布止住了出血。

e.en: New regulations aim to {stanch} the flow of fake reviews.
e.zh: 新规定旨在遏制虚假评论的泛滥。

e.en: A steel {stanchion} supports the upper deck of the bridge.
e.zh: 一根钢柱支撑着桥的上层。

e.en: Velvet ropes hung between each {stanchion} at the entrance.
e.zh: 入口处每根立柱之间挂着天鹅绒绳。

stand.t:
v. 站立；忍受
n. 立场；看台

e.en: Please {stand} when the judge enters the courtroom.
e.zh: 法官进入法庭时请起立。

e.en: I can't {stand} the smell of durian.
e.zh: 我受不了榴莲的味道。

standalone.t: adj. 独立运行的（软件、设备）

e.en: The app works as a {standalone} product without a subscription.
e.zh: 这款应用无需订阅,可作为独立产品使用。

e.en: This movie is a {standalone} story, not part of a series.
e.zh: 这部电影是独立故事,不属于任何系列。

standard.t:
n. 标准
adj. 标准的；普通的

e.en: This phone meets the new safety {standard}.
e.zh: 这款手机符合新的安全标准。

e.en: The {standard} delivery time is three to five days.
e.zh: 标准送货时间是三到五天。

e.en: The {standardisation} of charging ports has helped consumers.
e.zh: 充电口的标准化让消费者受益。

e.en: Industry leaders are pushing for the {standardisation} of safety tests.
e.zh: 行业领头者正推动安全测试的标准化。

standardise.t: v. 使标准化（英式拼写）

e.en: The EU plans to {standardise} all phone chargers next year.
e.zh: 欧盟计划明年统一所有手机充电器的标准。

e.en: Schools want to {standardise} how they grade essays.
e.zh: 学校希望统一作文评分的标准。

standardised.t: adj. 已标准化的（英式拼写）

e.en: All schools follow a {standardised} test for college entry.
e.zh: 所有学校都采用统一的高考标准化考试。

e.en: The factory uses {standardised} parts to cut costs.
e.zh: 工厂使用标准化零件以降低成本。

e.en: The {standardization} of USB-C made cables interchangeable.
e.zh: USB-C的标准化让数据线可以通用。

e.en: {Standardization} across teams reduced bugs in our software.
e.zh: 各团队间的标准化减少了我们软件中的漏洞。

standardize.t: v. 使标准化；统一规格

e.en: We need to {standardize} our coding style across the team.
e.zh: 我们需要在团队中统一代码风格。

e.en: The hospital plans to {standardize} patient intake forms.
e.zh: 医院计划统一病人入院登记表格。

standardized.t: adj. 已标准化的；统一的

e.en: Many colleges no longer require {standardized} test scores.
e.zh: 许多大学不再要求标准化考试成绩。

e.en: The team {standardized} their workflow to save time.
e.zh: 团队统一了工作流程以节省时间。

e.en: Her parents have very high {standards} for grades.
e.zh: 她的父母对成绩要求非常高。

e.en: The factory failed to meet basic safety {standards}.
e.zh: 工厂未能达到基本的安全标准。

standby.t:
n. 待机状态
adj. 备用的

e.en: The TV uses very little power in {standby} mode.
e.zh: 电视在待机模式下耗电极少。

e.en: We were on {standby} for the next available flight.
e.zh: 我们在等候下一班空位航班。

standee.t: n. 站立的乘客或观众

e.en: A cardboard {standee} of the superhero greeted us in the lobby.
e.zh: 大堂里一个纸板做的超级英雄立牌迎接我们。

e.en: The bus was full, so I rode as a {standee}.
e.zh: 公交车满了,所以我只能站着乘车。

e.en: As a regular {stander} on the subway, she rarely gets a seat.
e.zh: 作为地铁的常站客,她很少能找到座位。

e.en: The therapist used a {stander} to help the child stay upright.
e.zh: 治疗师用一台站立架帮助孩子保持直立。

standing.t:
n. 地位；排名
adj. 长期的；站立的

e.en: She has been {standing} in line for over an hour.
e.zh: 她已经在排队站了一个多小时了。

e.en: The team improved its {standing} in the league this season.
e.zh: 球队本赛季在联赛中的排名有所提升。

e.en: Our team climbed three places in the league {standings}.
e.zh: 我们队在联赛排名榜上上升了三位。

e.en: Check the latest tournament {standings} on the official site.
e.zh: 在官网上查看最新的赛事排名。

e.en: The armed {standoff} ended peacefully after six hours.
e.zh: 持枪对峙在六小时后和平结束。

e.en: The contract talks ended in another tense {standoff}.
e.zh: 合同谈判又一次陷入紧张僵局。

e.en: New colleagues sometimes find her {standoffish} at first.
e.zh: 新同事起初有时觉得她很冷淡。

e.en: He's not rude, just a bit {standoffish} around strangers.
e.zh: 他不是无礼,只是在陌生人面前有点疏远。

standout.t:
n. 杰出者
adj. 出众的

e.en: She was the {standout} performer at last night's concert.
e.zh: 她是昨晚演唱会上最出色的表演者。

e.en: This phone has a {standout} camera in its price range.
e.zh: 这款手机在同价位中拍照特别突出。

e.en: Firefighters connected the hose to the building's {standpipe}.
e.zh: 消防员把水管接到大楼的立管上。

e.en: The city installed a {standpipe} for emergency water supply.
e.zh: 市政为应急供水安装了一根立式水管。

e.en: From a safety {standpoint}, this design needs improvement.
e.zh: 从安全角度来看,这个设计需要改进。

e.en: The author writes from the {standpoint} of a working parent.
e.zh: 作者以一个职场父母的视角写作。

stands.t:
v. 站立；位于
n. 看台；支架

e.en: The fans in the {stands} cheered loudly for the home team.
e.zh: 看台上的球迷为主队大声欢呼。

e.en: He firmly {stands} by his earlier decision.
e.zh: 他坚定地维护自己之前的决定。

e.en: Traffic came to a complete {standstill} after the accident.
e.zh: 事故发生后交通完全陷入停滞。

e.en: Negotiations have reached a {standstill} this week.
e.zh: 本周谈判已陷入僵局。

e.en: The strike caused several {standstills} in production this month.
e.zh: 罢工导致本月生产多次陷入停滞。

e.en: Frequent {standstills} on the highway frustrated commuters.
e.zh: 高速公路频繁的拥堵让通勤者很恼火。

e.en: She was admitted to {Stanford} University last spring.
e.zh: 她去年春天被斯坦福大学录取了。

e.en: Many tech founders studied at {Stanford} before starting companies.
e.zh: 许多科技创始人在创业前就读于斯坦福。

stanhope.t: n. 斯坦霍普（人名/地名）

e.en: The museum displays an antique {stanhope} carriage from the 1800s.
e.zh: 博物馆陈列着一辆十九世纪的斯坦霍普马车。

e.en: He inherited a delicate {stanhope} viewer from his grandfather.
e.zh: 他从祖父那里继承了一个精致的斯坦霍普微型镜。

stank.t: v. 发出恶臭（stink 过去式）

e.en: The fridge {stank} after the power outage last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末停电后冰箱发出难闻的气味。

e.en: His gym bag {stank} so badly we made him leave it outside.
e.zh: 他的健身包臭得我们让他放到外面去。

e.en: {Stanley} forgot his keys at the office again.
e.zh: 斯坦利又把钥匙落在办公室了。

e.en: She bought a {Stanley} cup that keeps drinks cold all day.
e.zh: 她买了一个能让饮料保冷一整天的Stanley杯。

stansted.t: n. 斯坦斯特德（英国机场）

e.en: Our flight to Rome leaves from {Stansted} Airport at six.
e.zh: 我们飞罗马的航班六点从斯坦斯特德机场起飞。

e.en: Budget airlines often operate out of London {Stansted}.
e.zh: 廉价航空公司常以伦敦斯坦斯特德为基地。

e.en: Elizabeth Cady {Stanton} fought tirelessly for women's rights.
e.zh: 伊丽莎白·卡迪·斯坦顿为女权事业奋斗不息。

e.en: Mr. {Stanton} will lead the meeting tomorrow morning.
e.zh: 斯坦顿先生明早将主持会议。

e.en: The poem's final {stanza} repeats the opening image.
e.zh: 诗的最后一节重复了开头的意象。

e.en: Each {stanza} of the song tells a different memory.
e.zh: 歌曲的每一段都讲述了一段不同的回忆。

e.en: The poet read three {stanzas} aloud at the open mic.
e.zh: 诗人在开放麦上朗读了三个诗节。

e.en: Children learned the first two {stanzas} of the anthem.
e.zh: 孩子们学了国歌的前两节。

e.en: The surgeon performed a {stapedectomy} to restore his hearing.
e.zh: 外科医生为他做了镫骨切除术以恢复听力。

e.en: Recovery from a {stapedectomy} usually takes a few weeks.
e.zh: 镫骨切除术后通常需要几周时间恢复。

e.en: A {stapedotomy} uses a tiny laser to improve hearing.
e.zh: 镫骨开窗术使用微型激光来改善听力。

e.en: Her doctor recommended a {stapedotomy} over traditional surgery.
e.zh: 她的医生建议她做镫骨开窗术而非传统手术。

e.en: The {stapes} is the smallest bone in the human body.
e.zh: 镫骨是人体最小的骨头。

e.en: Damage to the {stapes} can cause serious hearing loss.
e.zh: 镫骨受损可能导致严重的听力下降。

staph.t: n. 葡萄球菌（staphylococcus 缩写）

e.en: The cut got infected with {staph} and needed antibiotics.
e.zh: 伤口感染了葡萄球菌,需要使用抗生素。

e.en: Hospitals work hard to prevent {staph} outbreaks among patients.
e.zh: 医院努力防止患者间爆发葡萄球菌感染。

e.en: The doctor diagnosed a {staphylococcal} skin infection.
e.zh: 医生诊断为葡萄球菌皮肤感染。

e.en: {Staphylococcal} pneumonia can be serious in young children.
e.zh: 葡萄球菌肺炎对幼儿可能很严重。

e.en: Many {staphylococci} live harmlessly on human skin.
e.zh: 许多葡萄球菌无害地寄居在人体皮肤上。

e.en: Some {staphylococci} have become resistant to common antibiotics.
e.zh: 一些葡萄球菌已对常见抗生素产生耐药性。

e.en: {Staphylococcus} aureus is a common cause of food poisoning.
e.zh: 金黄色葡萄球菌是食物中毒的常见病因。

e.en: Lab tests confirmed the wound contained {staphylococcus} bacteria.
e.zh: 化验结果确认伤口里含有葡萄球菌。

staple.t:
n. 订书钉；主食
adj. 主要的

e.en: Rice is a daily {staple} in many Asian households.
e.zh: 米饭是许多亚洲家庭的日常主食。

e.en: Could you {staple} these reports together for me?
e.zh: 你能帮我把这些报告订在一起吗?

e.en: She {stapled} the receipt to the expense form.
e.zh: 她把收据订在了报销单上。

e.en: The flyers were {stapled} to telephone poles around campus.
e.zh: 传单被钉在校园周围的电线杆上。

e.en: Can I borrow your {stapler} for a second?
e.zh: 能借你的订书机用一下吗?

e.en: The office {stapler} ran out of staples again.
e.zh: 办公室的订书机又没钉子了。

staples.t: n. 订书钉（复数）；主要商品

e.en: Bread and milk are {staples} on her shopping list.
e.zh: 面包和牛奶是她购物清单上的必备品。

e.en: He pulled the {staples} out before recycling the papers.
e.zh: 他在回收文件前先拔掉了订书钉。

stapleton.t: n. 斯泰普尔顿（人名/地名）

e.en: Ms. {Stapleton} teaches biology at the local high school.
e.zh: 斯泰普尔顿女士在当地高中教生物。

e.en: The {Stapleton} neighborhood has changed a lot recently.
e.zh: 斯泰普尔顿社区最近变化很大。

star.t:
n. 星星；明星
v. 主演

e.en: She wished on a shooting {star} last night.
e.zh: 她昨晚对着一颗流星许了愿。

e.en: Don't forget to {star} important emails for later.
e.zh: 别忘了把重要邮件加星标以便稍后查看。

star-crossed.t: adj. 命运不济的；生死相隔的

e.en: The novel tells the story of two {star-crossed} lovers.
e.zh: 这部小说讲述了一对命运多舛的恋人的故事。

e.en: Their {star-crossed} romance ended tragically in the final act.
e.zh: 他们薄命的爱情在最后一幕悲剧收场。

e.en: The captain ordered a sharp turn to {starboard}.
e.zh: 船长下令向右舷急转。

e.en: You can see dolphins off the {starboard} side now.
e.zh: 现在右舷外能看到海豚。

e.en: The fireworks ended with a brilliant golden {starburst}.
e.zh: 烟花以绚丽的金色星爆结束。

e.en: The logo features a colorful {starburst} design.
e.zh: 这个标志采用了彩色星爆图案设计。

starch.t:
n. 淀粉
v. 上浆

e.en: Potatoes contain a lot of {starch} and natural sugars.
e.zh: 土豆含有大量的淀粉和天然糖分。

e.en: The dry cleaner uses {starch} to keep collars crisp.
e.zh: 干洗店用浆糊让衣领保持挺括。

e.en: He wore a freshly {starched} white shirt to the interview.
e.zh: 他穿着一件刚上过浆的白衬衫去面试。

e.en: The waiters wore crisply {starched} uniforms.
e.zh: 服务员们穿着浆得笔挺的制服。

e.en: Try to limit {starchy} foods like white bread and pasta.
e.zh: 尽量少吃白面包和意面这类淀粉类食物。

e.en: His {starchy} manner made guests feel uncomfortable.
e.zh: 他刻板的举止让客人感到不自在。

e.en: The young actress rose to {stardom} after one viral video.
e.zh: 这位年轻女演员凭一段爆红视频一举成名。

e.en: Many singers struggle with the pressures of sudden {stardom}.
e.zh: 许多歌手难以应对突然成名的压力。

e.en: Astronomers say we are all made of {stardust}.
e.zh: 天文学家说我们都是由星尘构成的。

e.en: The film has a touch of Hollywood {stardust} about it.
e.zh: 这部电影带着一丝好莱坞的明星魅力。

stare.t:
v. 凝视；盯着看
n. 凝视

e.en: Don't {stare} at strangers on the subway.
e.zh: 不要在地铁上盯着陌生人看。

e.en: She gave him a cold {stare} across the table.
e.zh: 她隔着桌子冷冷地瞪了他一眼。

e.en: The child {stared} at the puppy in amazement.
e.zh: 孩子惊奇地盯着那只小狗看。

e.en: He {stared} blankly at the screen for several minutes.
e.zh: 他茫然地盯着屏幕看了好几分钟。

stares.t:
v. 凝视（第三人称单数）
n. 凝视（复数）

e.en: She ignored the curious {stares} from passersby.
e.zh: 她无视路人好奇的目光。

e.en: He {stares} out the window whenever he's lost in thought.
e.zh: 他每次出神时都会盯着窗外看。

e.en: The pilot maneuvered his {starfighter} through the asteroid field.
e.zh: 飞行员驾驶星际战机穿过小行星带。

e.en: Kids built a Lego {starfighter} from the new movie set.
e.zh: 孩子们用新电影套装拼了一架乐高星际战机。

e.en: We found a purple {starfish} clinging to the tide pool rocks.
e.zh: 我们发现一只紫色海星紧贴在潮池的岩石上。

e.en: The aquarium lets visitors gently touch a {starfish}.
e.zh: 水族馆让游客轻轻触摸海星。

stargazer.t: n. 观星者；爱做白日梦的人

e.en: As a lifelong {stargazer}, she owns three telescopes.
e.zh: 作为一名终生的观星爱好者,她拥有三台望远镜。

e.en: The {stargazer} pointed out Saturn just above the horizon.
e.zh: 那位观星者指出地平线上方的土星。

e.en: We went {stargazing} in the desert last weekend.
e.zh: 我们上周末去沙漠里观星了。

e.en: Clear winter nights are perfect for {stargazing}.
e.zh: 晴朗的冬夜最适合观星。

staring.t:
v. 凝视（现在分词）
adj. 瞪眼的

e.en: Stop {staring} at your phone during dinner.
e.zh: 吃饭时别一直盯着手机看。

e.en: She caught him {staring} at her from across the room.
e.zh: 她发现他从房间另一头一直盯着她看。

stark.t:
adj. 鲜明的；严酷的
adv. 完全地

e.en: There is a {stark} contrast between rich and poor neighborhoods.
e.zh: 富人区和穷人区之间形成鲜明对比。

e.en: The report painted a {stark} picture of climate risks.
e.zh: 这份报告对气候风险描绘了一幅严峻的图景。

e.en: The two candidates differ {starkly} on healthcare policy.
e.zh: 两位候选人在医疗政策上存在鲜明分歧。

e.en: Her white dress stood out {starkly} against the dark wall.
e.zh: 她的白裙子在深色墙壁的衬托下格外醒目。

e.en: The {starkness} of the prison cell shocked the visitors.
e.zh: 牢房的简陋荒凉让参观者感到震惊。

e.en: He was struck by the {starkness} of the desert landscape.
e.zh: 他被沙漠景观的荒凉所震撼。

stage.t:
n. 阶段；舞台
v. 上演；举办

e.en: The actors took the {stage} to thunderous applause.
e.zh: 演员们在雷鸣般的掌声中走上舞台。

e.en: We're in the early {stage} of planning the project.
e.zh: 我们正处于项目策划的早期阶段。

e.en: The {stagecoach} rumbled across the dusty western plains.
e.zh: 驿马车隆隆驶过尘土飞扬的西部平原。

e.en: Tourists rode a vintage {stagecoach} through the historic town.
e.zh: 游客们乘坐复古驿马车穿过这座历史小镇。

stagecraft.t: n. 舞台艺术；编剧技巧

e.en: Her mastery of {stagecraft} made the production unforgettable.
e.zh: 她对舞台艺术的精湛掌握让这场演出令人难忘。

e.en: The director's {stagecraft} turned a simple set into something magical.
e.zh: 导演的舞台技艺把简单的布景变得如同魔法一般。

staged.t:
adj. 分阶段的；摆拍的
v. 上演（stage 的过去式）

e.en: The company {staged} a comeback after years of decline.
e.zh: 该公司在多年衰退后实现了东山再起。

e.en: Critics suspect the photo was {staged} for publicity.
e.zh: 评论人士怀疑这张照片是为了宣传而摆拍的。

stagehand.t: n. 舞台工作人员；后台布景工

e.en: The {stagehand} quickly moved the props between scenes.
e.zh: 舞台工作人员在场景切换间迅速移动道具。

e.en: Every successful play depends on a skilled {stagehand} behind the curtain.
e.zh: 每一场成功的戏剧都离不开幕后熟练的舞台工人。

e.en: A professional home {stager} helped sell the house quickly.
e.zh: 一位专业的房屋陈列师帮忙很快卖掉了房子。

e.en: The {stager} arranged furniture to make rooms look spacious.
e.zh: 陈列师摆放家具,让房间看起来更宽敞。

stages.t:
n. 阶段（复数）
v. 举办（第三人称单数）

e.en: The disease progresses through several distinct {stages}.
e.zh: 这种疾病会经历几个明显不同的阶段。

e.en: Festival {stages} were set up across the entire park.
e.zh: 音乐节的舞台被搭建在整个公园各处。

e.en: His {stagey} gestures made the apology seem insincere.
e.zh: 他那做作的手势让道歉显得很不真诚。

e.en: The film's dialogue felt overly {stagey} and unnatural.
e.zh: 这部电影的对白显得过于戏剧化,不够自然。

stagflation.t: n. 滞胀（经济停滞加通胀）

e.en: Economists worry that {stagflation} could return in the coming year.
e.zh: 经济学家担心明年可能再次出现滞胀。

e.en: The 1970s {stagflation} crippled household budgets across America.
e.zh: 七十年代的滞胀让美国各地的家庭预算举步维艰。

stagger.t:
v. 蹒跚；使错开
n. 摇晃；错列

e.en: He began to {stagger} home after too many drinks.
e.zh: 喝得太多后,他开始踉踉跄跄地往家走。

e.en: Companies often {stagger} employee shifts to maintain coverage.
e.zh: 公司经常错开员工的轮班时间以保持人手充足。

e.en: I was absolutely {staggered} by the size of the bill.
e.zh: 看到账单的金额,我完全惊呆了。

e.en: The school {staggered} dismissal times to ease traffic.
e.zh: 学校错开了放学时间以缓解交通压力。

staggering.t: adj. 惊人的；令人震惊的

e.en: The repair costs reached a {staggering} two million dollars.
e.zh: 维修费用高达惊人的两百万美元。

e.en: She watched the drunk man {staggering} down the street.
e.zh: 她看着那个醉汉在街上踉跄而行。

staggeringly.t: adv. 惊人地；令人震惊地

e.en: The new phone is {staggeringly} expensive for what it offers.
e.zh: 这款新手机相对它提供的功能而言贵得惊人。

e.en: Their progress has been {staggeringly} fast this quarter.
e.zh: 他们这个季度的进展快得令人咋舌。

staggers.t:
v. 蹒跚（第三人称单数）
n. 眩晕症

e.en: The runner {staggers} across the finish line, exhausted but triumphant.
e.zh: 那名跑者筋疲力尽却胜利地踉跄冲过终点线。

e.en: News of the merger {staggers} investors around the world.
e.zh: 合并的消息让全球投资者都感到震惊。

e.en: Divers admired the colorful {staghorn} coral on the reef.
e.zh: 潜水员们欣赏着礁石上色彩斑斓的鹿角珊瑚。

e.en: She hung a {staghorn} fern in the bright kitchen window.
e.zh: 她在明亮的厨房窗边挂了一盆鹿角蕨。

staging.t:
n. 舞台布置；分阶段实施
v. 举办（stage 的现在分词）

e.en: Deploy the feature to {staging} before pushing to production.
e.zh: 在推送到生产环境前,先把功能部署到预发布环境。

e.en: The {staging} of the play emphasized minimalism and lighting.
e.zh: 这部戏的舞台呈现强调简约风格和灯光效果。

e.en: Wages have remained {stagnant} for nearly a decade.
e.zh: 工资水平已经停滞将近十年了。

e.en: Mosquitoes breed quickly in pools of {stagnant} water.
e.zh: 蚊子在死水池中繁殖得很快。

e.en: Without new investment, the local economy will {stagnate}.
e.zh: 没有新的投资,当地经济将停滞不前。

e.en: Skills tend to {stagnate} when you stop practicing them.
e.zh: 如果停止练习,技能往往会逐渐退化。

stagnating.t:
adj. 停滞中的
v. 停滞（现在分词）

e.en: Sales have been {stagnating} since the new competitor arrived.
e.zh: 自从新的竞争对手出现后,销售一直停滞不前。

e.en: He felt his career was {stagnating} in the same role.
e.zh: 他觉得自己在同一个职位上的事业正陷入停滞。

e.en: Years of economic {stagnation} forced the government to act.
e.zh: 多年的经济停滞迫使政府采取行动。

e.en: Creative {stagnation} pushed her to try a new medium.
e.zh: 创作上的停滞促使她尝试一种新的艺术形式。

e.en: The villain's {stagy} laugh ruined an otherwise tense scene.
e.zh: 反派那做作的笑声毁掉了本来紧张的一幕。

e.en: Her speech sounded {stagy} rather than heartfelt.
e.zh: 她的演讲听起来很矫情,而不是发自内心。

e.en: The {staid} old bank suddenly launched a trendy mobile app.
e.zh: 那家古板的老银行突然推出了一款时髦的手机应用。

e.en: He gave a {staid} but reassuring answer to reporters.
e.zh: 他向记者给出了一个保守却令人安心的回答。

stain.t:
n. 污渍；瑕疵
v. 弄脏；染色

e.en: Coffee left a stubborn {stain} on the white shirt.
e.zh: 咖啡在白衬衫上留下了一块顽固的污渍。

e.en: The scandal was a permanent {stain} on his reputation.
e.zh: 这桩丑闻成了他名誉上抹不去的污点。

e.en: His apron was {stained} with tomato sauce after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭过后,他的围裙上沾满了番茄酱。

e.en: Beautiful {stained} glass windows lit up the cathedral.
e.zh: 漂亮的彩色玻璃窗把大教堂映照得光彩夺目。

e.en: The train to {Staines} leaves from platform four every hour.
e.zh: 开往斯坦斯的列车每小时从四号站台发车。

e.en: She grew up in {Staines}, a town just west of London.
e.zh: 她在伦敦以西的小镇斯坦斯长大。

staining.t:
n. 染色；污染
v. 弄脏（现在分词）

e.en: Red wine is notorious for {staining} carpets and tablecloths.
e.zh: 红酒以容易弄脏地毯和桌布而臭名昭著。

e.en: He spent the afternoon {staining} the wooden deck a darker color.
e.zh: 他花了一下午把木甲板染成更深的颜色。

e.en: Most modern kitchens feature {stainless} steel appliances.
e.zh: 大多数现代厨房都配备不锈钢家电。

e.en: He built a long career with a {stainless} reputation.
e.zh: 他在长期的职业生涯中始终保持着无瑕的声誉。

stains.t:
n. 污渍（复数）
v. 弄脏（第三人称单数）

e.en: This detergent removes tough {stains} in a single wash.
e.zh: 这款洗涤剂只需一次清洗就能去除顽固污渍。

e.en: Time {stains} even the brightest memories with sadness.
e.zh: 时间会让最美好的回忆也染上一丝忧伤。

e.en: Professor {Stainton} teaches philosophy of language at the university.
e.zh: 斯坦顿教授在大学里教授语言哲学。

e.en: The village of {Stainton} sits quietly in the English countryside.
e.zh: 斯坦顿村静静地坐落在英国乡间。

e.en: She tripped on the bottom {stair} and dropped her phone.
e.zh: 她在最下面一级台阶上绊了一下,把手机摔了。

e.en: A creaky {stair} betrayed his attempt to sneak in late.
e.zh: 一级吱呀作响的台阶暴露了他深夜偷偷溜回家的企图。

e.en: A grand marble {staircase} swept up to the second floor.
e.zh: 一道宏伟的大理石楼梯通向二楼。

e.en: The narrow spiral {staircase} led to the attic studio.
e.zh: 那座狭窄的螺旋楼梯通向阁楼工作室。

e.en: He runs up the {stairs} every morning instead of the elevator.
e.zh: 他每天早上都跑楼梯,而不是坐电梯。

e.en: The cat slept on the {stairs} where the sun came in.
e.zh: 那只猫睡在阳光照进来的楼梯上。

e.en: A wooden {stairway} led down to the rocky beach.
e.zh: 一道木制楼梯通向布满岩石的海滩。

e.en: Emergency lights illuminated the dark {stairway} during the blackout.
e.zh: 停电期间,应急灯照亮了漆黑的楼梯通道。

e.en: His footsteps echoed loudly in the empty {stairwell}.
e.zh: 他的脚步声在空荡荡的楼梯井里回响。

e.en: They held a quick meeting in the {stairwell} for privacy.
e.zh: 为了隐私,他们在楼梯间里开了一个简短的会。

stake.t:
n. 利害关系；赌注；木桩
v. 押注；以桩支撑

e.en: There's a lot at {stake} in tomorrow's election.
e.zh: 明天的选举关系重大。

e.en: He drove a wooden {stake} into the ground to mark the boundary.
e.zh: 他在地上钉了一根木桩来标记边界。

e.en: Every {stakeholder} should be consulted before the policy changes.
e.zh: 在政策变更前应征询每一位利益相关者的意见。

e.en: As a major {stakeholder}, she has real influence on decisions.
e.zh: 作为主要利益相关者,她对决策有实际影响力。

e.en: Detectives spent three nights on a {stakeout} outside the warehouse.
e.zh: 侦探们在仓库外蹲守了三个晚上。

e.en: The {stakeout} finally paid off when the suspect appeared.
e.zh: 当嫌疑人出现时,这次蹲点监视终于有了回报。

e.en: The {stakes} are high in this championship final.
e.zh: 这场总决赛的赌注非常高。

e.en: Gardeners drove {stakes} into the soil to support the tomato plants.
e.zh: 园丁们把木桩打进土里以支撑番茄植株。

e.en: A dripping {stalactite} hung from the cave ceiling above us.
e.zh: 一根滴着水的钟乳石从我们头顶的洞穴顶上垂下。

e.en: Each {stalactite} took thousands of years to form.
e.zh: 每一根钟乳石都要花上数千年才能形成。

e.en: A massive {stalagmite} rose from the cave floor like a tower.
e.zh: 一根巨大的石笋像塔一样从洞穴地面升起。

e.en: Tourists carefully stepped around each delicate {stalagmite}.
e.zh: 游客们小心翼翼地绕开每一根脆弱的石笋。

stale.t: adj. 不新鲜的；陈旧的；过时的

e.en: The bread had gone {stale} after sitting out all night.
e.zh: 面包放了一整晚已经变得不新鲜了。

e.en: His jokes felt {stale} after telling them at every party.
e.zh: 他在每个派对上都讲那些笑话,听起来已经索然无味。

stalemate.t:
n. 僵局；和棋
v. 使陷入僵局

e.en: Negotiations reached a {stalemate} after three days of talks.
e.zh: 经过三天的谈判,谈判陷入了僵局。

e.en: The chess game ended in a {stalemate} on move forty.
e.zh: 这盘棋在第四十步时以和棋告终。

stalemated.t: adj. 陷入僵局的；僵持的

e.en: Congress {stalemated} on the budget for the third week running.
e.zh: 国会在预算问题上已连续第三周陷入僵局。

e.en: The teams {stalemated} at zero-zero through ninety minutes.
e.zh: 两队在九十分钟内以零比零僵持不下。

e.en: The {staleness} of the office air made everyone drowsy.
e.zh: 办公室里污浊的空气让大家都昏昏欲睡。

e.en: Critics noted a {staleness} in the band's latest album.
e.zh: 乐评人指出该乐队最新专辑显得了无新意。

e.en: {Stalin} ruled the Soviet Union with brutal authority for decades.
e.zh: 斯大林以残酷的权威统治苏联长达数十年。

e.en: Historians still debate the full impact of {Stalin}'s policies.
e.zh: 史学家至今仍在争论斯大林政策的全面影响。

e.en: The battle of {Stalingrad} changed the course of the war.
e.zh: 斯大林格勒战役改变了战争的走向。

e.en: Tourists still visit memorials in {Stalingrad} every year.
e.zh: 游客每年仍会前往斯大林格勒的纪念馆参观。

e.en: The professor lectured on the horrors of {Stalinism}.
e.zh: 教授讲授了斯大林主义的恐怖历史。

e.en: Many writers fled the country to escape {Stalinism}.
e.zh: 许多作家为逃离斯大林主义而离开了那个国家。

stalinist.t:
n. 斯大林主义者
adj. 斯大林主义的

e.en: The building was a grim {Stalinist} apartment block from the 1950s.
e.zh: 那栋楼是1950年代阴森的斯大林式公寓楼。

e.en: Critics called the new policy almost {Stalinist} in tone.
e.zh: 批评者称这项新政策的口吻近乎斯大林式。

e.en: We hiked back under a cloudy, {starless} sky.
e.zh: 我们在多云无星的夜空下徒步回去。

e.en: The {starless} night made navigation by sea difficult.
e.zh: 无星的夜晚让海上导航变得困难。

starlet.t: n. 初露头角的年轻女演员

e.en: The young {starlet} attended her first red carpet event.
e.zh: 这位年轻的小明星出席了她的首次红毯活动。

e.en: Magazines once followed every move of the rising {starlet}.
e.zh: 杂志曾追踪这位崛起的小明星的一举一动。

e.en: We danced on the beach by {starlight} until midnight.
e.zh: 我们在星光下的海滩上跳舞跳到午夜。

e.en: The cabin had no lamps, just gentle {starlight} through the window.
e.zh: 小屋里没有灯,只有从窗外洒进的柔和星光。

e.en: The flower has small {starlike} petals arranged in clusters.
e.zh: 这种花有成簇排列的星状小花瓣。

e.en: Tiny {starlike} flecks sparkled in the polished marble.
e.zh: 抛光的大理石上闪烁着星星点点的光斑。

e.en: A {starling} landed on the windowsill outside my office.
e.zh: 一只椋鸟落在我办公室窗台上。

e.en: Thousands of {starling} flocks darkened the evening sky.
e.zh: 成千上万的椋鸟群把傍晚的天空染暗了。

e.en: We walked along the {starlit} beach after dinner.
e.zh: 晚餐后我们沿着星光下的海滩散步。

e.en: The couple shared a quiet kiss on the {starlit} balcony.
e.zh: 那对情侣在星光下的阳台上轻轻一吻。

starred.t:
v. 主演（star 过去式）
adj. 带星号的

e.en: She {starred} in three films released last year.
e.zh: 去年她主演了三部上映的电影。

e.en: I {starred} the message so I could find it later.
e.zh: 我给那条消息加了星标方便以后查找。

starring.t:
v. 由…主演
adj. 主演的

e.en: The new series is {starring} a relatively unknown actor.
e.zh: 这部新剧由一位相对不知名的演员主演。

e.en: He landed his first {starring} role at age twenty.
e.zh: 他在二十岁时拿到了第一个主演角色。

starry.t: adj. 布满星星的；星光灿烂的

e.en: The kids gazed up at the {starry} desert sky.
e.zh: 孩子们抬头望着沙漠中布满星星的天空。

e.en: She has {starry} eyes whenever music comes on.
e.zh: 每当音乐响起,她的眼里就闪着光。

e.en: The app shows which {stars} are visible tonight.
e.zh: 这款应用显示今晚可以看到哪些星星。

e.en: This restaurant has five {stars} on every review site.
e.zh: 这家餐厅在每个点评网站上都是五星。

e.en: SpaceX launched another {starship} prototype this morning.
e.zh: SpaceX今早又发射了一艘星舰原型机。

e.en: The crew boarded the {starship} bound for distant colonies.
e.zh: 船员们登上了驶向远方殖民地的星舰。

start.t:
v. 开始；启动
n. 开端

e.en: Click the green button to {start} the download.
e.zh: 点击绿色按钮即可开始下载。

e.en: Let's {start} dinner before the kids get hungry.
e.zh: 我们趁孩子还没饿赶紧开饭吧。

e.en: I {started} learning Python during the pandemic.
e.zh: 疫情期间我开始学习Python。

e.en: The meeting {started} ten minutes late as usual.
e.zh: 会议照例迟了十分钟才开始。

e.en: This laptop is a great {starter} machine for students.
e.zh: 这台笔记本是学生入门的不错选择。

e.en: The car's {starter} motor finally gave out yesterday.
e.zh: 那辆车的起动马达昨天终于坏了。

starting.t:
v. 开始（现在分词）
adj. 起始的

e.en: I'm {starting} a new job next Monday.
e.zh: 下周一我就要开始一份新工作了。

e.en: The {starting} salary is higher than I expected.
e.zh: 起薪比我预期的要高。

e.en: Try not to {startle} the cat while she's eating.
e.zh: 她吃东西的时候尽量别吓到她。

e.en: Loud notifications {startle} me every single morning.
e.zh: 响亮的通知声每天早上都把我吓一跳。

startled.t:
adj. 受惊的
v. 惊吓（过去式）

e.en: The sudden knock {startled} everyone in the room.
e.zh: 突然的敲门声吓到了房间里的每一个人。

e.en: She gave me a {startled} look when I appeared.
e.zh: 我出现时她吃惊地看了我一眼。

startles.t: v. 使吃惊（第三人称单数）

e.en: The doorbell always {startles} the dog awake.
e.zh: 门铃声总是把狗吓醒。

e.en: Nothing {startles} her after years of emergency room work.
e.zh: 在急诊室工作多年后,没什么能吓到她。

e.en: The report revealed some {startling} new statistics.
e.zh: 那份报告披露了一些令人吃惊的新数据。

e.en: Her resemblance to her grandmother is truly {startling}.
e.zh: 她和祖母的相似程度真的令人惊讶。

e.en: The two designs are {startlingly} similar to each other.
e.zh: 这两个设计惊人地相似。

e.en: She remained {startlingly} calm throughout the crisis.
e.zh: 在整个危机过程中她出奇地冷静。

starts.t:
v. 开始（第三人称单数）
n. 起点（复数）

e.en: The movie {starts} at seven sharp tonight.
e.zh: 电影今晚七点整开场。

e.en: He always {starts} the day with a long run.
e.zh: 他总是以长跑开始一天。

e.en: Millions face {starvation} due to the ongoing drought.
e.zh: 持续的干旱让数百万人面临饥荒。

e.en: Crash diets put your body into {starvation} mode.
e.zh: 极端节食会让身体进入饥饿模式。

e.en: History records countless {starvations} caused by failed harvests.
e.zh: 历史上记载了无数因歉收而引发的饥荒。

e.en: The region endured repeated {starvations} during the war years.
e.zh: 战争年代里那个地区经历了一次次饥荒。

e.en: Don't {starve} yourself before the marathon tomorrow.
e.zh: 明天跑马拉松,别把自己饿着。

e.en: Without funding, the project will simply {starve}.
e.zh: 没有资金,这个项目只会被活活饿死。

starved.t:
adj. 极饿的
v. 挨饿（过去式）

e.en: The rescued puppy was clearly {starved} and dehydrated.
e.zh: 获救的小狗明显饿坏了,还严重脱水。

e.en: He was {starved} for attention as a child.
e.zh: 他小时候极度渴望被关注。

starves.t: v. 挨饿（第三人称单数）

e.en: Cutting the budget {starves} the team of resources.
e.zh: 削减预算让团队资源严重匮乏。

e.en: Nobody {starves} in this neighborhood thanks to the food bank.
e.zh: 多亏了食物银行,这个社区没人会挨饿。

e.en: I'm absolutely {starving} after that long hike.
e.zh: 走完那段长路后我饿得不行。

e.en: Many {starving} families rely on weekly food deliveries.
e.zh: 许多挨饿的家庭依靠每周的食物派送过活。

stash.t:
v. 藏起；私藏
n. 私藏物

e.en: I {stash} snacks in my desk drawer at work.
e.zh: 我把零食藏在公司办公桌的抽屉里。

e.en: She found a hidden {stash} of vintage records.
e.zh: 她发现了一批藏起来的老唱片。

stasi.t: n. 前东德国家安全部

e.en: The film depicts life under constant {stasi} surveillance.
e.zh: 这部电影刻画了在斯塔西无处不在的监视下的生活。

e.en: Former {stasi} files were finally opened to the public.
e.zh: 前东德斯塔西的档案终于向公众开放。

e.en: The negotiations have been in {stasis} for months.
e.zh: 谈判已经停滞了好几个月。

e.en: The patient was placed in medical {stasis} for transport.
e.zh: 病人被置于医疗静止状态以便运送。

stat.t:
n. 统计数字（statistic 的缩写）
adv. 立刻

e.en: The doctor needs those test results {stat}.
e.zh: 医生需要那些化验结果,马上就要。

e.en: That player's shooting {stat} leads the entire league.
e.zh: 那位球员的投篮数据领跑整个联盟。

state.t:
n. 状态；国家；州
v. 陈述

e.en: Please {state} your name clearly for the recording.
e.zh: 请清楚地说出你的名字以便录音。

e.en: California is the most populous {state} in America.
e.zh: 加利福尼亚是美国人口最多的州。

statecraft.t: n. 治国之道；政治手腕

e.en: The treaty showcased her remarkable skill in {statecraft}.
e.zh: 这份条约展现了她出色的治国才能。

e.en: Modern {statecraft} relies heavily on data and diplomacy.
e.zh: 现代治国之道在很大程度上依赖数据和外交。

stated.t:
v. 陈述（过去式）
adj. 规定的

e.en: The CEO {stated} the company's goals very clearly.
e.zh: 首席执行官非常清楚地阐述了公司的目标。

e.en: The {stated} reason for the delay sounded suspicious.
e.zh: 官方给出的延误理由听起来很可疑。

statehood.t: n. 国家地位；州的身份

e.en: Hawaii achieved {statehood} in nineteen fifty-nine.
e.zh: 夏威夷在1959年获得州的地位。

e.en: Puerto Rico continues to debate the question of {statehood}.
e.zh: 波多黎各仍在就建州问题进行辩论。

e.en: Protesters gathered outside the {statehouse} all weekend.
e.zh: 抗议者整个周末聚集在州议会大厦外。

e.en: The governor delivered her speech inside the {statehouse}.
e.zh: 州长在州议会大厦里发表了讲话。

stateless.t: adj. 无国籍的；无状态的

e.en: Refugees often live as {stateless} people for decades.
e.zh: 难民常常以无国籍人士的身份生活几十年。

e.en: REST APIs are designed to be {stateless} by nature.
e.zh: REST接口本质上被设计为无状态的。

e.en: They toured a {stately} home in the English countryside.
e.zh: 他们参观了英国乡间一座庄严的宅邸。

e.en: The judge entered the courtroom at a {stately} pace.
e.zh: 法官以庄重的步伐走进法庭。

e.en: The company issued a {statement} denying the rumors.
e.zh: 公司发表声明否认那些传闻。

e.en: Check your bank {statement} for any unusual charges.
e.zh: 查看你的银行对账单,看看有没有可疑扣款。

e.en: His public {statements} contradict the internal emails.
e.zh: 他的公开声明与内部邮件相互矛盾。

e.en: Download the past three monthly {statements} as PDFs.
e.zh: 把过去三个月的月对账单下载成PDF文件。

e.en: The ferry to {staten} Island offers free skyline views.
e.zh: 开往斯塔滕岛的渡轮可以免费欣赏天际线。

e.en: She grew up in a quiet neighborhood on {staten} Island.
e.zh: 她在斯塔滕岛一个安静的社区长大。

stater.t: n. 古希腊银币；陈述者

e.en: The museum displays a rare gold {stater} from ancient Greece.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一枚罕见的古希腊金币。

e.en: Collectors prize any silver {stater} in good condition.
e.zh: 收藏家很重视任何品相良好的银币。

stateroom.t: n. 船上特等舱；专用大厅

e.en: Our cruise {stateroom} had a balcony overlooking the ocean.
e.zh: 我们邮轮上的客舱有一个能俯瞰大海的阳台。

e.en: The luxury suite {stateroom} cost more than a car.
e.zh: 那间豪华客舱的价格比一辆汽车还贵。

states.t:
n. 州；国家（复数）
v. 陈述

e.en: The contract clearly {states} the cancellation policy.
e.zh: 合同清楚地写明了取消政策。

e.en: Several {states} have legalized recreational marijuana.
e.zh: 已经有几个州将娱乐性大麻合法化。

e.en: He's flying back {stateside} after two years abroad.
e.zh: 在国外待了两年后,他要飞回美国了。

e.en: The product launches {stateside} before going global.
e.zh: 这款产品先在美国本土发布,然后再推向全球。

statesman.t: n. 政治家；国务活动家

e.en: Mandela is remembered as a great {statesman} of the century.
e.zh: 曼德拉被铭记为本世纪伟大的政治家。

e.en: He spoke not as a politician but as a {statesman}.
e.zh: 他说话不像政客,更像一位政治家。

e.en: Her response to the crisis was calm and {statesmanlike}.
e.zh: 她对危机的回应冷静而有政治家风范。

e.en: The president struck a {statesmanlike} tone in his address.
e.zh: 总统在演讲中表现出政治家的风范。

statesmanship.t: n. 政治家的才能与风度

e.en: Resolving the dispute required real {statesmanship}.
e.zh: 化解这场争端需要真正的政治家智慧。

e.en: The summit was a masterclass in international {statesmanship}.
e.zh: 这次峰会堪称国际政治家智慧的典范。

e.en: Few modern {statesmen} match the eloquence of Churchill.
e.zh: 现代很少有政治家能比得上丘吉尔的口才。

e.en: The conference brought together {statesmen} from twelve nations.
e.zh: 这次会议汇集了来自十二个国家的政治家。

statewide.t: adj. 全州范围的（美国州内）

e.en: The new law applies {statewide} starting next month.
e.zh: 这项新法律下个月起在全州范围生效。

e.en: She won the {statewide} spelling competition last spring.
e.zh: 去年春天她赢得了全州拼写比赛。

static.t:
adj. 静态的；静止的
n. 静电；（广播）杂音

e.en: The radio kept picking up annoying {static} all night.
e.zh: 收音机整晚不停地接收到恼人的静电杂音。

e.en: Our website serves mostly {static} HTML pages.
e.zh: 我们的网站主要提供静态的HTML页面。

e.en: TypeScript is {statically} typed unlike plain JavaScript.
e.zh: 和普通JavaScript不同,TypeScript是静态类型的。

e.en: The site is {statically} generated for faster loading.
e.zh: 该网站采用静态生成以加快加载速度。

statin.t: n. 他汀类药物（降血脂药）

e.en: Her doctor prescribed a daily {statin} for high cholesterol.
e.zh: 医生给她开了每天一片的他汀类药物来降胆固醇。

e.en: Many seniors take a {statin} to protect heart health.
e.zh: 许多老年人服用他汀类药物来保护心脏健康。

stating.t: v. 陈述；声明（state 的现在分词）

e.en: She sent an email {stating} her reasons for leaving.
e.zh: 她发了一封邮件,说明了她离职的原因。

e.en: He kept {stating} the obvious throughout the meeting.
e.zh: 开会期间他一直在说一些显而易见的废话。

station.t:
n. 车站；站点
v. 驻扎；安置

e.en: The train pulled into the {station} right on time.
e.zh: 火车准时驶入车站。

e.en: Soldiers were {station}ed along the border for months.
e.zh: 士兵们被派驻在边境数月。

e.en: Keep the camera {stationary} while filming the scene.
e.zh: 拍摄时请保持相机静止不动。

e.en: She rides a {stationary} bike every morning at the gym.
e.zh: 她每天早上在健身房骑动感单车。

e.en: The local {stationer} sells fountain pens and notebooks.
e.zh: 当地的文具商出售钢笔和笔记本。

e.en: I ordered wedding invitations from a fancy {stationer} downtown.
e.zh: 我在市中心一家高档文具店订了婚礼请柬。

e.en: She bought floral {stationery} to write thank-you notes.
e.zh: 她买了花卉信纸用来写感谢卡。

e.en: The office {stationery} cupboard is stocked with pens and paper.
e.zh: 办公室文具柜里备有笔和纸。

stationing.t: v. 驻扎；部署（station 的现在分词）

e.en: The army is {stationing} more troops near the capital.
e.zh: 军方正在首都附近部署更多军队。

e.en: They considered {stationing} a guard at every entrance.
e.zh: 他们考虑在每个入口都安排一名守卫。

e.en: The {stationmaster} blew his whistle as the train departed.
e.zh: 列车出发时,站长吹响了哨子。

e.en: An old {stationmaster} greeted every passenger by name.
e.zh: 老站长亲切地叫出每位乘客的名字。

stations.t:
n. 车站（复数）
v. 驻扎（第三人称单数）

e.en: Tokyo has some of the busiest train {stations} in the world.
e.zh: 东京拥有世界上最繁忙的几个火车站。

e.en: All radio {stations} broadcast the emergency alert at noon.
e.zh: 所有广播电台中午都播出了紧急警报。

statism.t: n. 国家主义；中央集权

e.en: Critics warned that the new policy edged toward {statism}.
e.zh: 批评者警告说新政策正滑向国家主义。

e.en: Her essay traces the rise of {statism} in postwar Europe.
e.zh: 她的文章追溯了战后欧洲国家主义的兴起。

statist.t:
n. 国家主义者
adj. 国家主义的

e.en: The party promotes a strongly {statist} approach to the economy.
e.zh: 该党主张对经济采取强烈的国家干预方式。

e.en: His {statist} views clashed with the libertarian audience.
e.zh: 他的国家主义观点与自由意志主义听众产生了冲突。

e.en: That {statistic} about youth unemployment is genuinely shocking.
e.zh: 那个关于青年失业率的数据着实令人震惊。

e.en: Don't let yourself become just another sad {statistic}.
e.zh: 别让自己沦为又一个可悲的数字。

e.en: The study found a {statistical} link between sleep and mood.
e.zh: 研究发现睡眠与情绪之间存在统计学关联。

e.en: He uses {statistical} models to forecast next quarter's sales.
e.zh: 他用统计模型来预测下季度的销售额。

statistically.t: adv. 统计上；在统计学意义上

e.en: The difference between the two groups is {statistically} significant.
e.zh: 两组之间的差异在统计学上是显著的。

e.en: {Statistically}, most startups fail within the first five years.
e.zh: 从统计上看,大多数初创公司在五年内倒闭。

e.en: The team hired a {statistician} to analyze the trial data.
e.zh: 团队聘请了一位统计学家来分析试验数据。

e.en: As a {statistician}, she's skeptical of viral survey results.
e.zh: 作为统计学家,她对网传的调查结果持怀疑态度。

e.en: Recent {statistics} show a sharp drop in violent crime.
e.zh: 最新数据显示暴力犯罪大幅下降。

e.en: She's majoring in {statistics} and computer science.
e.zh: 她主修统计学和计算机科学。

stative.t: adj. 状态的（语法：表示状态的动词）

e.en: Verbs like "know" and "belong" are {stative}, not active.
e.zh: "know"和"belong"这类动词是状态动词,不是动作动词。

e.en: English {stative} verbs usually don't take the progressive form.
e.zh: 英语中的状态动词通常不用进行时态。

stator.t: n. 定子（电机中静止的部分）

e.en: The motor's {stator} stays fixed while the rotor spins inside.
e.zh: 电机的定子保持不动,转子在其内部旋转。

e.en: Engineers redesigned the {stator} to improve energy efficiency.
e.zh: 工程师重新设计了定子以提高能源效率。

statuary.t: n. 雕塑（总称）；雕塑艺术

e.en: The garden is filled with marble {statuary} from the Renaissance.
e.zh: 花园里摆满了文艺复兴时期的大理石雕像。

e.en: Roman {statuary} lines the long museum corridor.
e.zh: 罗马雕塑沿着长长的博物馆走廊一字排开。

e.en: A bronze {statue} of the founder stands in the plaza.
e.zh: 广场上矗立着一尊创始人的青铜雕像。

e.en: The child stood as still as a {statue} during the game.
e.zh: 游戏中那个孩子站得像雕像一样一动不动。

e.en: Ancient Greek {statues} once gleamed with bright painted colors.
e.zh: 古希腊雕像曾经涂着鲜艳的色彩闪闪发光。

e.en: Several {statues} in the park were vandalized overnight.
e.zh: 公园里好几座雕像一夜之间被人破坏。

statuesque.t: adj. 雕像般的；高挑优美的

e.en: The model walked onto the stage looking absolutely {statuesque}.
e.zh: 那位模特走上舞台,身姿宛如雕像般优美。

e.en: She admired the {statuesque} dancer leading the ballet troupe.
e.zh: 她欣赏那位身姿挺拔的领舞演员。

e.en: He won a small bronze {statuette} at the awards ceremony.
e.zh: 他在颁奖典礼上获得了一座小铜像。

e.en: A porcelain {statuette} of a dancer sat on the mantelpiece.
e.zh: 壁炉架上摆着一尊舞者瓷像。

stature.t:
n. 身材；身高
n. 名望；地位

e.en: Despite his small {stature}, he dominated the basketball court.
e.zh: 尽管个子不高,他却称霸篮球场。

e.en: Her research gave her international {stature} in the field.
e.zh: 她的研究使她在该领域拥有了国际声望。

status.t:
n. 状态；状况
n. 身份；地位

e.en: You can check your order {status} on the tracking page.
e.zh: 你可以在跟踪页面查看订单状态。

e.en: Owning a sports car became a {status} symbol in the 1980s.
e.zh: 在八十年代,拥有跑车成了身份的象征。

e.en: The app lets you customize your online {statuses} for friends.
e.zh: 这款应用允许你为好友定制在线状态。

e.en: Different membership {statuses} unlock different perks and discounts.
e.zh: 不同的会员等级可解锁不同的福利和折扣。

e.en: A federal {statute} protects whistleblowers from retaliation.
e.zh: 一项联邦法规保护举报人免遭报复。

e.en: The lawsuit was dismissed under the {statute} of limitations.
e.zh: 该诉讼因超过时效法规而被驳回。

statutorily.t: adv. 依法定地；根据法规

e.en: Employers are {statutorily} required to provide paid sick leave.
e.zh: 雇主依法必须提供带薪病假。

e.en: The agency is {statutorily} bound to publish annual reports.
e.zh: 该机构依法必须发布年度报告。

e.en: All workers are entitled to {statutory} maternity leave benefits.
e.zh: 所有劳动者都享有法定产假福利。

e.en: The company failed to meet its {statutory} reporting deadline.
e.zh: 该公司未能赶上法定的申报截止日期。

staunch.t:
adj. 坚定的；忠诚的
v. 止（血）

e.en: She has been a {staunch} supporter of the team for decades.
e.zh: 几十年来她一直是这支球队的坚定支持者。

e.en: He remained {staunch} in his beliefs despite heavy criticism.
e.zh: 尽管饱受批评,他依然坚守自己的信念。

e.en: The senator {staunchly} defended the controversial new bill.
e.zh: 那位参议员坚定地为这项有争议的新法案辩护。

e.en: She {staunchly} refused to compromise on her core principles.
e.zh: 她坚决拒绝在核心原则上做出妥协。

e.en: Tournament chess sets follow the classic {Staunton} design.
e.zh: 比赛用国际象棋棋具采用经典的斯汤顿样式。

e.en: They drove through {Staunton}, Virginia on their road trip.
e.zh: 公路旅行中,他们路过了弗吉尼亚州的斯汤顿镇。

stavanger.t: n. 斯塔万格（挪威城市）

e.en: {Stavanger} is a coastal city in southwestern Norway.
e.zh: 斯塔万格是挪威西南部的一座沿海城市。

e.en: We took a ferry from {Stavanger} to see the famous fjords.
e.zh: 我们从斯塔万格乘渡轮去看著名的峡湾。

stave.t:
n. 桶板；（诗）节；五线谱
v. 击穿；（off）避开

e.en: Doctors urged early vaccination to {stave} off the outbreak.
e.zh: 医生敦促尽早接种疫苗以遏制疫情爆发。

e.en: He grabbed a snack to {stave} off hunger before dinner.
e.zh: 他抓了点零食吃,以缓解晚餐前的饥饿。

staveley.t: n. 斯塔夫利（英国地名）

e.en: {Staveley} is a small village near the English Lake District.
e.zh: 斯塔夫利是英格兰湖区附近的一个小村庄。

e.en: We stopped in {Staveley} for coffee on our way to Windermere.
e.zh: 去温德米尔的途中我们在斯塔夫利停下来喝了杯咖啡。

stay.t:
v. 停留；保持
n. 停留；逗留

e.en: Please {stay} home if you're feeling unwell tomorrow.
e.zh: 如果明天身体不舒服,请待在家里。

e.en: Our {stay} at the beach hotel lasted an entire week.
e.zh: 我们在海滨酒店住了整整一周。

stayed.t: v. 停留；保持（stay 的过去式）

e.en: We {stayed} up late watching old movies last night.
e.zh: 昨晚我们熬夜看了几部老电影。

e.en: She {stayed} calm despite the chaos around her.
e.zh: 尽管周围一片混乱,她仍保持镇定。

stayer.t: n. 有耐力的人；持久者

e.en: The horse is a real {stayer}, perfect for long distance races.
e.zh: 这匹马耐力极佳,非常适合长距离比赛。

e.en: She's a {stayer}—she'll see this project through to the end.
e.zh: 她很有韧劲,会把这个项目坚持做到底。

staying.t: v. 停留；保持（stay 的现在分词）

e.en: Are you {staying} for dinner or heading home early?
e.zh: 你是留下来吃晚饭,还是早点回家?

e.en: {Staying} hydrated is essential during long summer hikes.
e.zh: 在长时间夏季徒步中,补水至关重要。

stays.t:
v. 停留（第三人称单数）
n. 停留；支撑物

e.en: My phone {stays} on silent during work meetings.
e.zh: 工作会议期间我的手机始终保持静音。

e.en: She {stays} in touch with old friends through social media.
e.zh: 她通过社交媒体与老朋友保持联系。

stb.t: n. 机顶盒（Set-Top Box 的缩写）

stc.t: n. 多义缩写（如沙特电信公司等）

std.t:
n. 标准（standard 缩写）
n. 性病（sexually transmitted disease）

stead.t: n. 代替；替代（in sb's stead）

e.en: Her language skills will serve her in good {stead} abroad.
e.zh: 她的语言能力在国外会对她大有助益。

e.en: The deputy spoke at the conference in the mayor's {stead}.
e.zh: 副市长代替市长在会议上发言。

e.en: He remained {steadfast} in his support for the project.
e.zh: 他对这个项目的支持始终如一。

e.en: Her {steadfast} loyalty earned the respect of her teammates.
e.zh: 她坚定不移的忠诚赢得了队友的尊重。

e.en: She {steadfastly} refused to abandon her injured friend.
e.zh: 她坚定地拒绝抛下受伤的朋友。

e.en: The country has {steadfastly} maintained its neutral position.
e.zh: 该国一直坚定地保持中立立场。

e.en: Her {steadfastness} during the crisis inspired the entire team.
e.zh: 危机中她的坚定不移激励了整个团队。

e.en: The general praised the soldiers' {steadfastness} under fire.
e.zh: 将军赞扬了士兵们在炮火下的坚定无畏。

e.en: House prices have risen {steadily} over the past decade.
e.zh: 过去十年间房价稳步上涨。

e.en: He worked {steadily} through the pile of paperwork.
e.zh: 他不慌不忙地处理着那堆文件。

e.en: A surgeon needs incredible {steadiness} of hand and nerve.
e.zh: 外科医生需要极其稳定的双手和心理素质。

e.en: The {steadiness} of her income made budgeting much easier.
e.zh: 她收入的稳定使做预算变得容易得多。

steading.t: n. 农庄；农场附属建筑

e.en: The old {steading} included a barn, stables, and a cottage.
e.zh: 那处旧农庄包括谷仓、马厩和一间小屋。

e.en: They renovated a Scottish {steading} into a holiday home.
e.zh: 他们把一座苏格兰农舍改造成了度假屋。

steady.t:
adj. 稳定的；平稳的
v. 使稳固

e.en: Hold the ladder {steady} while I climb to the roof.
e.zh: 我爬到屋顶时,把梯子扶稳。

e.en: The economy has shown {steady} growth for three quarters.
e.zh: 经济已连续三个季度保持稳定增长。

steadying.t: v. 使稳定（steady 的现在分词）

e.en: She took a deep, {steadying} breath before her speech.
e.zh: 演讲前她深深吸了一口气以稳定情绪。

e.en: He grabbed the railing, {steadying} himself on the icy steps.
e.zh: 他抓住栏杆,在结冰的台阶上稳住了身体。

e.en: He ordered a medium-rare {steak} with mashed potatoes.
e.zh: 他点了一份五分熟的牛排配土豆泥。

e.en: This restaurant grills the best {steak} in town.
e.zh: 这家餐厅烤的牛排是城里最棒的。

e.en: We celebrated her promotion at a fancy {steakhouse} downtown.
e.zh: 我们在市中心一家高档牛排馆庆祝她升职。

e.en: The {steakhouse} is famous for its dry-aged ribeye.
e.zh: 这家牛排馆以干式熟成肋眼牛排闻名。

e.en: He grilled two thick {steaks} on the backyard barbecue.
e.zh: 他在后院烤架上烤了两块厚牛排。

e.en: The butcher cut the {steaks} fresh this morning.
e.zh: 肉贩今早现切了这些牛排。

steal.t:
v. 偷窃
n. 超值便宜货

e.en: Don't {steal} someone else's idea without giving credit.
e.zh: 不要在不署名的情况下窃取别人的创意。

e.en: At twenty dollars, this jacket is a real {steal}.
e.zh: 这件夹克才二十美元,真是超值。

e.en: That puppy is a total scene {stealer} at parties.
e.zh: 那只小狗在派对上简直是焦点小偷。

e.en: The shortstop is the team's top base {stealer}.
e.zh: 这位游击手是球队头号盗垒能手。

stealing.t:
v. 偷窃
n. 盗窃行为

e.en: He was caught {stealing} candy from the corner store.
e.zh: 他在街角小店偷糖果时被抓到了。

e.en: The cat keeps {stealing} my spot on the couch.
e.zh: 那只猫总是抢占我在沙发上的位置。

e.en: She {steals} glances at him during the meeting.
e.zh: 开会时她偷偷地瞟他几眼。

e.en: The point guard averages three {steals} per game.
e.zh: 这位控球后卫场均有三次抢断。

stealth.t:
n. 隐秘；悄悄行动
adj. 隐形（技术）

e.en: The startup launched in {stealth} mode for two years.
e.zh: 这家初创公司以隐秘模式运营了两年。

e.en: The cat approached the bird with perfect {stealth}.
e.zh: 那只猫以完美的悄无声息接近小鸟。

e.en: She crept {stealthily} down the hallway after midnight.
e.zh: 午夜过后,她悄悄地溜过走廊。

e.en: The app {stealthily} collects data without user consent.
e.zh: 这款应用在用户不知情的情况下偷偷收集数据。

stealthy.t: adj. 隐秘的；鬼鬼祟祟的

e.en: The hacker used {stealthy} techniques to avoid detection.
e.zh: 这名黑客使用隐蔽手段以躲避检测。

e.en: A {stealthy} fox slipped into the chicken coop.
e.zh: 一只悄无声息的狐狸溜进了鸡舍。

steam.t:
n. 蒸汽
v. 蒸（食物）

e.en: {Steam} rose from the hot bowl of noodles.
e.zh: 热气从那碗面里袅袅升起。

e.en: The project lost {steam} after the lead developer quit.
e.zh: 主程序员离职后,项目失去了势头。

e.en: Mark Twain piloted a {steamboat} on the Mississippi River.
e.zh: 马克·吐温曾在密西西比河上驾驶蒸汽船。

e.en: The old {steamboat} still offers tours every summer.
e.zh: 那艘老蒸汽船每年夏天仍提供观光游览。

steamed.t:
adj. 清蒸的
v. 蒸（过去式）

e.en: She {steamed} the dumplings for exactly ten minutes.
e.zh: 她把饺子蒸了整整十分钟。

e.en: He was really {steamed} about the late delivery.
e.zh: 他对送货延误感到非常恼火。

e.en: I cook broccoli in a bamboo {steamer} every week.
e.zh: 我每周都用竹蒸笼蒸西兰花。

e.en: The coastal {steamer} carried mail between the islands.
e.zh: 沿海蒸汽船在岛屿之间运送邮件。

steamiest.t: adj. 最热气腾腾的（steamy 最高级）

e.en: August is the {steamiest} month in this humid city.
e.zh: 八月是这座潮湿城市里最闷热的月份。

e.en: That novel features the {steamiest} romance of the year.
e.zh: 那本小说有今年最火辣的爱情戏。

steaming.t:
adj. 冒热气的
v. 蒸；冒汽

e.en: She handed me a {steaming} mug of coffee.
e.zh: 她递给我一杯热气腾腾的咖啡。

e.en: He was {steaming} after reading the rude email.
e.zh: 读完那封无礼的邮件后,他气得冒烟。

e.en: The CEO tried to {steamroll} the proposal through the board.
e.zh: 首席执行官试图强行让董事会通过该提案。

e.en: Don't let them {steamroll} you in the negotiation.
e.zh: 别让他们在谈判中把你压得没还手之力。

steamroller.t:
n. 压路机
v. 强行压制

e.en: A {steamroller} flattened the fresh asphalt on the road.
e.zh: 一辆压路机把路上新铺的沥青压平了。

e.en: Her debating style is a complete {steamroller}.
e.zh: 她的辩论风格简直就是一台压路机。

e.en: His grandparents arrived in America by {steamship} in 1910.
e.zh: 他的祖父母于1910年乘蒸汽轮船抵达美国。

e.en: The old {steamship} is now a floating museum.
e.zh: 那艘老蒸汽轮船如今成了一座海上博物馆。

steamy.t: adj. 蒸汽弥漫的；香艳的

e.en: The bathroom mirror was {steamy} after her hot shower.
e.zh: 她洗完热水澡后,浴室镜子全是雾气。

e.en: They share a {steamy} kiss in the final scene.
e.zh: 他们在最后一幕中热吻缠绵。

e.en: Soap makers often use {stearic} acid to harden bars.
e.zh: 制皂师常用硬脂酸来让肥皂变硬。

e.en: This candle contains {stearic} acid for a cleaner burn.
e.zh: 这种蜡烛含有硬脂酸,燃烧时更干净。

e.en: The knight mounted his loyal {steed} and rode off.
e.zh: 骑士跨上他忠诚的战马疾驰而去。

e.en: She jokingly called her old bicycle her trusty {steed}.
e.zh: 她开玩笑地把她的旧自行车叫做忠实坐骑。

steel.t:
n. 钢；钢铁
v. 使坚强

e.en: The bridge is built from reinforced {steel} beams.
e.zh: 这座桥是用加固钢梁建造的。

e.en: She had to {steel} herself before the difficult conversation.
e.zh: 她必须在那场艰难的谈话前让自己坚强起来。

e.en: Anglers come here every fall to catch {steelhead} trout.
e.zh: 每年秋天钓鱼爱好者都来这里钓虹鳟鱼。

e.en: The river is famous for its wild {steelhead} runs.
e.zh: 这条河以野生虹鳟洄游闻名。

e.en: Her {steeliness} during the crisis impressed the entire team.
e.zh: 危机中她的坚毅让整个团队印象深刻。

e.en: There was a quiet {steeliness} in his calm voice.
e.zh: 他平静的嗓音里透着一股冷峻的坚毅。

e.en: The Korean {steelmaker} announced a major expansion this year.
e.zh: 这家韩国钢铁制造商今年宣布大规模扩张。

e.en: Pittsburgh was once home to America's largest {steelmaker}.
e.zh: 匹兹堡曾是美国最大钢铁制造商的所在地。

steels.t:
n. 各种钢材
v. 使坚强

e.en: She {steels} herself for bad news before opening emails.
e.zh: 打开邮件前,她总是先做好接收坏消息的心理准备。

e.en: Modern factories produce dozens of specialty {steels}.
e.zh: 现代工厂能生产数十种特种钢材。

e.en: The bridge's intricate {steelwork} took three years to complete.
e.zh: 这座桥精巧的钢结构花了三年才完工。

e.en: Decorative {steelwork} adorns the gates of the mansion.
e.zh: 装饰性的钢艺点缀着这座豪宅的大门。

e.en: His grandfather was a {steelworker} in Cleveland for forty years.
e.zh: 他祖父在克利夫兰当了四十年钢铁工人。

e.en: The {steelworker} union called for a strike yesterday.
e.zh: 钢铁工人工会昨天号召举行罢工。

steely.t: adj. 钢铁般的；冷酷坚定的

e.en: She gave the interviewer a {steely} stare.
e.zh: 她用冷峻的眼神盯着面试官。

e.en: His {steely} determination helped him finish the marathon.
e.zh: 他钢铁般的决心帮他跑完了马拉松。

e.en: The Dutch painter Jan {Steen} captured lively tavern scenes.
e.zh: 荷兰画家扬·斯滕善于描绘生动的酒馆场景。

e.en: My friend {Steen} just moved here from Copenhagen.
e.zh: 我的朋友斯滕刚从哥本哈根搬到这里。

steep.t:
adj. 陡峭的；价格过高的
v. 浸泡

e.en: The trail became dangerously {steep} near the summit.
e.zh: 靠近山顶时小路变得陡峭得危险。

e.en: Let the tea {steep} for three minutes before drinking.
e.zh: 让茶叶浸泡三分钟后再喝。

e.en: The hill begins to {steepen} just past the bridge.
e.zh: 过了桥之后,山坡就开始变陡。

e.en: Yield curves tend to {steepen} when growth accelerates.
e.zh: 当经济增速加快时,收益率曲线往往会变陡。

e.en: The white church {steeple} towered above the village.
e.zh: 白色的教堂尖塔高耸于村庄之上。

e.en: Lightning struck the old {steeple} during the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨中闪电击中了那座古老的尖塔。

steeplechase.t: n. 障碍赛马；障碍赛跑

e.en: She trained for months to win the Olympic {steeplechase}.
e.zh: 她苦练数月,终于赢得奥运障碍赛冠军。

e.en: The horse stumbled at the final fence of the {steeplechase}.
e.zh: 那匹马在障碍赛最后一道栏前绊倒了。

steeplechaser.t: n. 障碍赛参赛者（人或马）

e.en: The Kenyan {steeplechaser} broke the world record on Sunday.
e.zh: 那位肯尼亚障碍赛选手周日打破了世界纪录。

e.en: Every {steeplechaser} must master both running and hurdling.
e.zh: 每位障碍赛运动员都必须兼顾跑步与跨栏。

steepled.t: adj. 有尖塔的；尖塔状的

e.en: He sat back and {steepled} his fingers thoughtfully.
e.zh: 他靠回椅背,沉思地把手指尖对在一起。

e.en: The {steepled} church dominated the small town's skyline.
e.zh: 带尖塔的教堂主宰着这个小镇的天际线。

e.en: Housing prices have risen {steeply} over the past decade.
e.zh: 过去十年房价急剧上涨。

e.en: The road climbs {steeply} into the mountains.
e.zh: 这条路陡峭地向山中攀升。

e.en: The {steepness} of the slope made hiking exhausting.
e.zh: 坡度的陡峭让徒步变得令人筋疲力尽。

e.en: Investors worried about the {steepness} of the price drop.
e.zh: 投资者对价格下跌的陡峭程度感到担忧。

steer.t:
v. 驾驶；引导
n. 阉公牛

e.en: Try to {steer} the conversation away from politics.
e.zh: 尽量把话题从政治上引开。

e.en: The rancher sold a young {steer} at auction.
e.zh: 那位牧场主在拍卖会上卖了一头小阉牛。

steerable.t: adj. 可驾驭的；可操控的

e.en: The new drone has a fully {steerable} camera mount.
e.zh: 这款新无人机配有可全方位转向的摄像头支架。

e.en: Modern catheters are {steerable} for precise surgical navigation.
e.zh: 现代导管可以转向操控,便于精准的手术导航。

e.en: He grabbed a {stepladder} to change the lightbulb.
e.zh: 他拿来一把折梯换灯泡。

e.en: Always lock the {stepladder} before climbing up.
e.zh: 爬梯子前一定要先把折梯锁好。

e.en: My {stepmother} bakes the best chocolate cake.
e.zh: 我继母做的巧克力蛋糕最好吃。

e.en: In the fairy tale, the wicked {stepmother} hates Snow White.
e.zh: 在童话里,那位恶毒的继母憎恨白雪公主。

e.en: Fairy tales often portray {stepmothers} as villains.
e.zh: 童话故事常把继母描绘成反派。

e.en: Modern {stepmothers} face very different challenges than before.
e.zh: 现代继母面临的挑战与以往大不相同。

stepney.t:
n. 备用轮胎（旧用法）
n. 斯特普尼（伦敦地名）

e.en: He grew up in {Stepney}, a working-class neighborhood in London.
e.zh: 他在伦敦工人阶级社区斯特普尼长大。

e.en: The market in {Stepney} is bustling on weekends.
e.zh: 斯特普尼的市场在周末熙熙攘攘。

e.en: Becoming a {stepparent} requires patience and understanding.
e.zh: 成为继父母需要耐心和理解。

e.en: The book offers advice for any new {stepparent}.
e.zh: 这本书为新晋继父母提供建议。

e.en: Wild horses still roam the Mongolian {steppe}.
e.zh: 野马至今仍在蒙古大草原上奔驰。

e.en: The vast {steppe} stretched as far as the eye could see.
e.zh: 广袤的草原一直延伸到视线尽头。

stepped.t: v. 走；踩（step 的过去式）

e.en: She {stepped} carefully over the puddle.
e.zh: 她小心地跨过了水坑。

e.en: He {stepped} down as CEO after ten years.
e.zh: 十年之后,他卸任了首席执行官。

e.en: She used a {stepper} machine for thirty minutes at the gym.
e.zh: 她在健身房用踏步机锻炼了三十分钟。

e.en: The robot is driven by a precise {stepper} motor.
e.zh: 这个机器人由精密的步进电机驱动。

stepping.t: v. 踏步；走动（step 的现在分词）

e.en: He is {stepping} into a new role next month.
e.zh: 下个月他将担任一个新的职位。

e.en: Be careful when {stepping} off the curb.
e.zh: 从路边石上下来时要小心。

steps.t:
n. 台阶；步骤
v. 走（step 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Follow these simple {steps} to set up the app.
e.zh: 按照这几个简单步骤来设置这个应用。

e.en: She climbed the stone {steps} to the temple.
e.zh: 她沿着石阶走上寺庙。

e.en: My {stepsister} and I share a bedroom on weekends.
e.zh: 我和继姐周末共用一间卧室。

e.en: Cinderella's {stepsister} was jealous of her beauty.
e.zh: 灰姑娘的继姐嫉妒她的美貌。

e.en: His {stepson} just started high school this fall.
e.zh: 他的继子今年秋天刚上高中。

e.en: She is incredibly proud of her {stepson}.
e.zh: 她对继子感到无比自豪。

steptoe.t: n. 斯特普托（人名/地名）

e.en: {Steptoe} and Son was a beloved British sitcom.
e.zh: 《斯特普托父子》是一部深受喜爱的英国情景喜剧。

e.en: The law firm {Steptoe} has offices around the world.
e.zh: 斯特普托律师事务所在全球设有办公室。

stepwise.t:
adj. 逐步的；分步的
adv. 逐步地

e.en: The tutorial explains the algorithm in a {stepwise} manner.
e.zh: 该教程以循序渐进的方式讲解算法。

e.en: We adopted a {stepwise} approach to migrating the database.
e.zh: 我们采用循序渐进的方式迁移数据库。

stereo.t:
n. 立体声；音响
adj. 立体声的

e.en: He turned up the {stereo} and started dancing.
e.zh: 他把音响开大,开始跳舞。

e.en: The car comes with a premium {stereo} system.
e.zh: 这辆车配备了高级音响系统。

e.en: Victorians loved viewing the world through a {stereograph}.
e.zh: 维多利亚时代的人喜欢通过立体照片观赏世界。

e.en: She collected antique {stereograph} cards from her grandfather.
e.zh: 她从祖父那里收集了一些古董立体照片卡。

stereographic.t: adj. 立体图的；立体投影的

e.en: Maps often use {stereographic} projection for polar regions.
e.zh: 地图常用球极平面投影来绘制极地地区。

e.en: The headset offers a true {stereographic} 3D experience.
e.zh: 这款头显提供真正的立体3D视觉体验。

e.en: Vintage records sound amazing on a {stereophonic} system.
e.zh: 老式唱片在立体声系统上听起来非常棒。

e.en: The film was released with full {stereophonic} sound.
e.zh: 这部电影以完整的立体声格式发行。

e.en: The museum displays a 19th-century {stereophotograph} of Paris.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一张19世纪巴黎的立体照片。

e.en: He digitized his grandfather's old {stereophotograph} collection.
e.zh: 他把祖父的老立体照片收藏数字化了。

e.en: The lecturer used a {stereopticon} to project images on the wall.
e.zh: 讲师用幻灯放映机将图像投到墙上。

e.en: Schools once relied on a {stereopticon} for visual lessons.
e.zh: 学校曾依靠幻灯放映机进行直观教学。

e.en: Children in the 1900s peered through a {stereoscope} for fun.
e.zh: 1900年代的孩子们喜欢通过立体镜观看图片取乐。

e.en: The antique shop sold a wooden {stereoscope} for fifty dollars.
e.zh: 那家古董店以五十美元出售一台木制立体镜。

stereoscopic.t: adj. 立体的；有立体感的

e.en: VR headsets create a {stereoscopic} sense of depth.
e.zh: VR头显能营造出立体的纵深感。

e.en: The exhibit features {stereoscopic} images from the Civil War.
e.zh: 展览展出了内战时期的立体影像。

e.en: Surgeons used {stereotactic} techniques to target the tumor.
e.zh: 外科医生采用立体定向技术精准锁定肿瘤。

e.en: {Stereotactic} radiosurgery causes minimal damage to healthy tissue.
e.zh: 立体定向放射手术对健康组织的损伤极小。

stereotype.t:
n. 刻板印象；成见
v. 对…形成成见

e.en: The film challenges every {stereotype} about small-town life.
e.zh: 这部电影挑战了所有关于小镇生活的刻板印象。

e.en: It's unfair to {stereotype} people based on their accent.
e.zh: 根据口音对人形成刻板印象是不公平的。

e.en: The character is {stereotyped} as a clueless tourist.
e.zh: 这个角色被塑造成典型的迷糊游客形象。

e.en: Older media often {stereotyped} women in narrow roles.
e.zh: 早期媒体常把女性局限在刻板的角色之中。

e.en: The film challenges old {stereotypes} about working mothers.
e.zh: 这部电影挑战了关于职场母亲的陈旧刻板印象。

e.en: Avoid relying on cultural {stereotypes} when writing characters.
e.zh: 创作角色时要避免依赖文化刻板印象。

e.en: The ad uses {stereotypic} images of suburban families.
e.zh: 这则广告使用了郊区家庭的刻板形象。

e.en: Caged animals often display {stereotypic} pacing behavior.
e.zh: 被关在笼中的动物常表现出刻板的踱步行为。

stereotypical.t: adj. 典型的；刻板印象的

e.en: He plays the {stereotypical} absent-minded professor in the sitcom.
e.zh: 他在情景喜剧中扮演那种典型的心不在焉的教授。

e.en: The novel avoids {stereotypical} portrayals of immigrants.
e.zh: 这部小说避开了对移民的刻板描写。

e.en: He's {stereotypically} British, always carrying an umbrella.
e.zh: 他典型的英国做派,总是随身带着雨伞。

e.en: The villain is {stereotypically} dressed in all black.
e.zh: 反派角色按惯例一身黑衣打扮。

stereotyping.t:
n. 形成刻板印象
v. 使定型

e.en: Racial {stereotyping} has no place in modern journalism.
e.zh: 现代新闻业容不下种族刻板印象。

e.en: The training session focused on avoiding gender {stereotyping}.
e.zh: 这次培训重点讲如何避免性别刻板印象。

e.en: Zoo elephants sometimes develop {stereotypy} from confinement stress.
e.zh: 动物园的大象有时会因圈养压力出现刻板行为。

e.en: Researchers measured {stereotypy} in mice raised in empty cages.
e.zh: 研究人员测量了空笼养殖小鼠的刻板行为。

sterile.t:
adj. 无菌的；消毒的
adj. 不育的；贫瘠的

e.en: Surgeons must wear gloves to keep the area {sterile}.
e.zh: 外科医生必须戴手套以保持手术区域无菌。

e.en: The meeting felt cold and {sterile}, with no real discussion.
e.zh: 那场会议显得冷清而僵硬,没有真正的讨论。

sterilisation.t: n. 消毒；绝育（英式拼写）

e.en: Proper {sterilisation} of equipment prevents hospital infections.
e.zh: 器械的彻底消毒可防止医院感染。

e.en: Forced {sterilisation} programs have left a dark historical legacy.
e.zh: 强制绝育项目留下了黑暗的历史遗产。

sterilise.t: v. 消毒；使绝育（英式拼写）

e.en: Boil the bottles to {sterilise} them before feeding the baby.
e.zh: 喂宝宝前要把奶瓶煮沸消毒。

e.en: Vets {sterilise} stray cats to control the population.
e.zh: 兽医为流浪猫做绝育以控制数量。

sterilised.t: adj. 已消毒的；已绝育的

e.en: The nurse {sterilised} the needle with an alcohol swab.
e.zh: 护士用酒精棉片对针头进行了消毒。

e.en: All the dental tools have been {sterilised} in the autoclave.
e.zh: 所有牙科器械都已在高压灭菌器中消毒。

steriliser.t: n. 消毒器；灭菌器（英式）

e.en: We bought a UV {steriliser} for the baby's pacifiers.
e.zh: 我们买了台紫外线消毒器给宝宝的安抚奶嘴用。

e.en: The clinic's {steriliser} broke down during the busiest hour.
e.zh: 诊所的消毒器在最忙的时段坏掉了。

e.en: The textbook compares {sterilities} caused by different infections.
e.zh: 教科书比较了不同感染所引起的各种不育情况。

e.en: Doctors discussed the {sterilities} observed across multiple patient groups.
e.zh: 医生们讨论了在多组患者中观察到的不育现象。

e.en: Maintaining {sterility} in the lab is absolutely critical.
e.zh: 在实验室里保持无菌环境至关重要。

e.en: The couple sought treatment for unexplained {sterility}.
e.zh: 这对夫妇为不明原因的不孕症寻求治疗。

e.en: Heat {sterilization} kills bacteria on surgical instruments.
e.zh: 高温灭菌可以杀死手术器械上的细菌。

e.en: Pet {sterilization} clinics offer low-cost spaying and neutering.
e.zh: 宠物绝育诊所提供低价的绝育手术。

e.en: You should {sterilize} the jars before making jam.
e.zh: 做果酱之前应该先把罐子消毒。

e.en: The shelter will {sterilize} every adopted dog at no cost.
e.zh: 收容所会免费为每只被领养的狗做绝育。

sterilized.t: adj. 已消毒的；已绝育的

e.en: The wound was cleaned with {sterilized} gauze.
e.zh: 伤口用经过消毒的纱布清理过了。

e.en: Most milk sold in stores has been {sterilized} for safety.
e.zh: 商店里出售的牛奶大多经过灭菌处理以确保安全。

e.en: The bottle {sterilizer} runs a full cycle in ten minutes.
e.zh: 这台奶瓶消毒器十分钟就能跑完一个完整周期。

e.en: Our hospital's main {sterilizer} is replaced every five years.
e.zh: 我们医院的主消毒器每五年更换一次。

sterling.t:
n. 英镑
adj. 纯正的；优秀的

e.en: She did a {sterling} job organizing the charity event.
e.zh: 她把这次慈善活动组织得非常出色。

e.en: The price tag is listed in pounds {sterling}.
e.zh: 价格标签上标的是英镑。

stern.t:
adj. 严厉的；严肃的
n. 船尾

e.en: The teacher gave us a {stern} look when we whispered.
e.zh: 我们小声说话时,老师严厉地瞪了我们一眼。

e.en: Waves crashed against the {stern} of the fishing boat.
e.zh: 海浪拍打着渔船的船尾。

e.en: The patient complained of {sternal} pain after the workout.
e.zh: 病人锻炼后抱怨胸骨部位疼痛。

e.en: Surgeons made a small {sternal} incision for the procedure.
e.zh: 外科医生在胸骨处做了一个小切口。

e.en: The judge spoke {sternly} to the defendant.
e.zh: 法官严厉地对被告说话。

e.en: Mom looked at me {sternly} when I lied about homework.
e.zh: 我谎报作业时,妈妈严厉地看着我。

e.en: There was unexpected {sternness} in the coach's voice today.
e.zh: 今天教练的声音里带着出人意料的严厉。

e.en: Her usual warmth gave way to sudden {sternness}.
e.zh: 她平日的温和突然变成了严厉。

steerage.t:
n. 统舱；三等舱
n. 操舵

e.en: Immigrants traveled in {steerage} to save on fares.
e.zh: 移民们乘坐底层统舱以节省船费。

e.en: The pilot praised the boat's responsive {steerage}.
e.zh: 舵手称赞这艘船操控灵敏。

steered.t: v. steer 的过去式：驾驶、引导

e.en: She {steered} the company through a difficult recession.
e.zh: 她带领公司渡过了一场艰难的经济衰退。

e.en: He {steered} the boat carefully into the narrow harbor.
e.zh: 他小心翼翼地把船驶入狭窄的港口。

e.en: A skilled {steerer} kept the rowing eight perfectly straight.
e.zh: 一位熟练的舵手让八人赛艇保持笔直前行。

e.en: Replace the {steerer} tube if it shows any cracks.
e.zh: 如果舵管出现任何裂纹,请立即更换。

steering.t:
n. 转向系统
v. 驾驶、引导

e.en: The car's {steering} feels loose at high speeds.
e.zh: 这辆车在高速行驶时方向盘感觉很松。

e.en: She joined the project's {steering} committee last month.
e.zh: 她上个月加入了这个项目的指导委员会。

steers.t:
v. 驾驶、引导
n. 小公牛（复数）

e.en: A good captain {steers} the team through every storm.
e.zh: 优秀的队长会带领队伍渡过每一场风暴。

e.en: The ranch raises hundreds of {steers} for beef.
e.zh: 这个牧场饲养几百头阉牛供应牛肉。

e.en: The {stegosaur} had bony plates running along its back.
e.zh: 剑龙的背上长着一排骨质板。

e.en: Children love the giant {stegosaur} model at the museum.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢博物馆里那个巨大的剑龙模型。

e.en: A {stegosaurus} skeleton stood at the center of the gallery.
e.zh: 一具剑龙骨架矗立在展厅的中央。

e.en: The {stegosaurus} used its spiked tail for defense.
e.zh: 剑龙用带刺的尾巴来防御敌人。

stein.t:
n. 大啤酒杯
n. 姓氏：斯坦因

e.en: He raised a heavy {stein} of beer at Oktoberfest.
e.zh: 他在慕尼黑啤酒节上举起一只沉甸甸的啤酒杯。

e.en: The collector displayed antique {stein} mugs on the shelf.
e.zh: 收藏家把古董啤酒杯摆在架子上展示。

steinbeck.t: n. 人名：斯坦贝克（美国作家）

e.en: John {Steinbeck} wrote vividly about Depression-era California.
e.zh: 约翰·斯坦贝克生动地描绘了大萧条时期的加州。

e.en: We read {Steinbeck} in high school English class.
e.zh: 我们高中英语课上读过斯坦贝克的作品。

e.en: The concert hall features a beautifully restored {Steinway} grand piano.
e.zh: 音乐厅里有一架修复精美的施坦威三角钢琴。

e.en: She practiced for hours on her grandmother's vintage {Steinway}.
e.zh: 她在祖母那架古董施坦威钢琴上练习了好几个小时。

e.en: Archaeologists uncovered a Mayan {stela} carved with hieroglyphs.
e.zh: 考古学家发掘出一块刻有象形文字的玛雅石碑。

e.en: The ancient {stela} commemorated a king's military victory.
e.zh: 那块古代石碑纪念着一位国王的军事胜利。

e.en: A tall stone {stele} marked the entrance to the temple.
e.zh: 一块高大的石碑标示着神庙的入口。

e.en: The museum displays a {stele} inscribed with ancient laws.
e.zh: 博物馆展出一块刻有古代法律的石碑。

stellar.t:
adj. 出色的、一流的
adj. 恒星的

e.en: She gave a {stellar} performance at last night's concert.
e.zh: 她在昨晚的音乐会上表现极其出色。

e.en: Astronomers study {stellar} formation in distant galaxies.
e.zh: 天文学家研究遥远星系中恒星的形成。

stellenbosch.t: n. 地名：斯泰伦博斯（南非）

e.en: We toured the wineries around {Stellenbosch} last summer.
e.zh: 去年夏天我们参观了斯泰伦博斯周边的酒庄。

e.en: {Stellenbosch} University is one of South Africa's oldest.
e.zh: 斯泰伦博斯大学是南非最古老的大学之一。

stem.t:
n. 茎；杆
v. 阻止；源于

e.en: Many social problems {stem} from poverty and inequality.
e.zh: 许多社会问题源于贫困和不平等。

e.en: She trimmed the {stem} of each rose before arranging them.
e.zh: 她先剪短每朵玫瑰的茎,再插花。

stemmed.t:
v. 源于；阻止（过去式）
adj. 有茎的

e.en: The argument {stemmed} from a simple misunderstanding.
e.zh: 这场争吵源于一个简单的误会。

e.en: She poured wine into the tall {stemmed} glasses.
e.zh: 她把酒倒进高脚杯中。

stemming.t:
n. 词干提取（NLP）
v. 阻止；源于

e.en: The delays are {stemming} from supply chain issues.
e.zh: 这些延误源于供应链问题。

e.en: Search engines use {stemming} to match related word forms.
e.zh: 搜索引擎使用词干提取来匹配相关词形。

stems.t:
n. 茎、杆（复数）
v. 源于；阻止

e.en: The plant has thick green {stems} and small flowers.
e.zh: 这种植物有粗壮的绿茎和小花。

e.en: His confidence {stems} from years of practice.
e.zh: 他的自信源于多年的练习。

e.en: She unpacked the crystal {stemware} for the dinner party.
e.zh: 她为晚宴拿出了水晶高脚酒杯。

e.en: Hand-wash delicate {stemware} to avoid chips and cracks.
e.zh: 精致的高脚杯应手洗,以免出现缺口和裂痕。

e.en: The senator delivered a real {stemwinder} at the rally.
e.zh: 那位参议员在集会上发表了一场激动人心的演讲。

e.en: His closing speech was a {stemwinder} that brought cheers.
e.zh: 他的结束演讲精彩绝伦,赢得了一片欢呼。

e.en: The museum displays a vintage {Sten} gun from World War II.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一把二战时期的斯登冲锋枪。

e.en: Resistance fighters often used the cheap {Sten} submachine gun.
e.zh: 抵抗战士经常使用廉价的斯登冲锋枪。

e.en: A terrible {stench} rose from the overflowing trash bin.
e.zh: 溢出的垃圾桶散发出难闻的恶臭。

e.en: The {stench} of corruption hangs over the entire administration.
e.zh: 腐败的恶臭笼罩着整个政府。

stencil.t:
n. 镂空模板
v. 用模板印刷

e.en: She used a {stencil} to paint letters on the sign.
e.zh: 她用模板在标牌上喷涂字母。

e.en: Kids love to {stencil} shapes onto their notebooks.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢用模板在笔记本上印图案。

stenciled.t: v. 用模板印制（过去式）

e.en: The artist {stenciled} a mural across the brick wall.
e.zh: 艺术家用模板在砖墙上喷绘了一幅壁画。

e.en: Each crate was {stenciled} with the company's logo.
e.zh: 每个木箱上都用模板印有公司标志。

stencilled.t: v. 用模板印制（英式过去式）

e.en: Her name was neatly {stencilled} on the locker door.
e.zh: 她的名字工整地喷印在储物柜门上。

e.en: The warning was {stencilled} in bright yellow paint.
e.zh: 那条警告用亮黄色油漆喷印而成。

stendhal.t: n. 人名：司汤达（法国作家）

e.en: {Stendhal} wrote The Red and the Black in 1830.
e.zh: 司汤达于1830年写下了《红与黑》。

e.en: Many critics consider {Stendhal} a master of psychological realism.
e.zh: 许多评论家认为司汤达是心理现实主义的大师。

e.en: She still keeps a {steno} pad on her desk.
e.zh: 她办公桌上还放着一本速记本。

e.en: The court {steno} typed every word of the testimony.
e.zh: 法庭速记员逐字记录了证词。

e.en: The {stenographer} recorded every word spoken in court.
e.zh: 速记员记录了法庭上说的每一个字。

e.en: She worked as a {stenographer} before becoming a lawyer.
e.zh: 她在成为律师之前曾做过速记员。

e.en: The doctor diagnosed him with spinal {stenosis}.
e.zh: 医生诊断他患有脊椎管狭窄症。

e.en: Aortic {stenosis} can cause chest pain and fainting.
e.zh: 主动脉瓣狭窄可能引起胸痛和昏厥。

stent.t: n. (医) 支架（如血管支架）

e.en: Doctors inserted a {stent} to keep the artery open.
e.zh: 医生植入了一个支架以保持动脉畅通。

e.en: He recovered quickly after the {stent} procedure.
e.zh: 支架手术后他恢复得很快。

e.en: The coach shouted instructions in a {stentorian} voice.
e.zh: 教练用洪亮的嗓音喊出指令。

e.en: His {stentorian} tone silenced the entire room.
e.zh: 他洪亮的嗓音让整个房间瞬间安静下来。

step.t:
n. 步骤；台阶
v. 踏步；走

e.en: Watch your {step} on the icy sidewalk.
e.zh: 在结冰的人行道上小心脚下。

e.en: Booking a flight is the first {step} of the trip.
e.zh: 订机票是这次旅行的第一步。

e.en: My {stepbrother} and I grew up in the same house.
e.zh: 我和我继兄是在同一个家里长大的。

e.en: Her {stepbrother} is two years older than she is.
e.zh: 她的继兄比她大两岁。

e.en: He treats his {stepchildren} as his own kids.
e.zh: 他把继子女当成自己的亲生孩子对待。

e.en: Holiday gatherings include all the {stepchildren} from both sides.
e.zh: 节日聚会会把双方所有的继子女都聚在一起。

e.en: His {stepdaughter} just graduated from college last weekend.
e.zh: 他的继女上周末刚从大学毕业。

e.en: She walked her {stepdaughter} down the aisle.
e.zh: 她挽着继女走过婚礼的红毯。

e.en: Her {stepfather} taught her how to ride a bike.
e.zh: 她的继父教她骑自行车。

e.en: My {stepfather} has been part of my life since I was five.
e.zh: 我五岁起,继父就一直是我生命的一部分。

e.en: Many {stepfathers} struggle to find their role in blended families.
e.zh: 许多继父在重组家庭中难以找到自己的角色。

e.en: The support group is for {stepfathers} of teenage children.
e.zh: 这个互助小组面向有青少年孩子的继父们。

e.en: Stretching the {sternocleidomastoid} can relieve neck tension.
e.zh: 拉伸胸锁乳突肌可以缓解颈部紧张。

e.en: The therapist massaged my tight {sternocleidomastoid} muscle.
e.zh: 治疗师给我按摩了僵硬的胸锁乳突肌。

e.en: CPR compressions should be applied to the lower {sternum}.
e.zh: 心肺复苏的按压点应放在胸骨下段。

e.en: He fractured his {sternum} in the cycling accident.
e.zh: 他在自行车事故中摔断了胸骨。

e.en: The doctor prescribed a {steroid} cream for the rash.
e.zh: 医生开了一支类固醇药膏来治皮疹。

e.en: The athlete tested positive for an anabolic {steroid}.
e.zh: 那名运动员的合成类固醇检测呈阳性。

e.en: Doctors prefer non-{steroidal} drugs for mild inflammation.
e.zh: 对于轻度炎症,医生更倾向使用非甾体类药物。

e.en: The cream has {steroidal} ingredients, so use it sparingly.
e.zh: 这种药膏含有类固醇成分,要少量使用。

e.en: Long-term use of {steroids} can weaken your bones.
e.zh: 长期使用类固醇会让骨骼变得脆弱。

e.en: Several players were banned for using performance-enhancing {steroids}.
e.zh: 几名球员因服用兴奋剂类固醇而被禁赛。

e.en: Plant {sterol} can help lower cholesterol levels.
e.zh: 植物甾醇有助于降低胆固醇水平。

e.en: Cholesterol is the most well-known animal {sterol}.
e.zh: 胆固醇是最为人熟知的动物甾醇。

e.en: The doctor placed the cold {stethoscope} on my chest.
e.zh: 医生把冰凉的听诊器放在我胸口上。

e.en: A nurse listens to the baby's heartbeat through a {stethoscope}.
e.zh: 护士用听诊器听着婴儿的心跳。

e.en: The cowboy tipped his {stetson} as he rode past.
e.zh: 牛仔骑马经过时轻抬了一下他的牛仔帽。

e.en: He wore a wide-brimmed {stetson} to the rodeo.
e.zh: 他戴着一顶宽边斯泰森牛仔帽去看牛仔竞技。

e.en: The {stevedore} loaded heavy crates onto the cargo ship.
e.zh: 码头工人把沉重的箱子装上货船。

e.en: His grandfather worked as a {stevedore} at the port.
e.zh: 他祖父曾在港口当装卸工。

stevenage.t: n. 斯蒂夫尼奇（英国城镇）

e.en: The new factory in {Stevenage} created hundreds of jobs.
e.zh: 史蒂夫尼奇的新工厂创造了数百个就业机会。

e.en: We caught the train from London to {Stevenage}.
e.zh: 我们坐火车从伦敦去史蒂夫尼奇。

e.en: She sweetens her coffee with {stevia} instead of sugar.
e.zh: 她用甜菊糖代替白糖来给咖啡调味。

e.en: This soda is sweetened naturally with {stevia} extract.
e.zh: 这款汽水用甜菊提取物天然加甜。

stew.t:
n. 炖菜
v. 炖，煨

e.en: Mom is making beef {stew} for dinner tonight.
e.zh: 妈妈今晚要做炖牛肉。

e.en: Don't {stew} over the bad review—move on.
e.zh: 别为那条差评生闷气了,向前看吧。

e.en: The flight {steward} brought us extra blankets.
e.zh: 乘务员给我们多拿了几条毯子。

e.en: He sees himself as a {steward} of the company's values.
e.zh: 他把自己视为公司价值观的守护者。

stewardess.t: n. 空中小姐，女乘务员

e.en: The {stewardess} demonstrated how to fasten the seatbelt.
e.zh: 空姐演示了如何系好安全带。

e.en: My aunt worked as a {stewardess} for thirty years.
e.zh: 我姑姑当了三十年的空姐。

e.en: Environmental {stewardship} is everyone's responsibility.
e.zh: 保护环境是每个人的责任。

e.en: Under her {stewardship}, the company doubled its revenue.
e.zh: 在她的管理下,公司收入翻了一番。

e.en: She served {stewed} apples with vanilla ice cream.
e.zh: 她端上炖苹果配香草冰淇淋。

e.en: He {stewed} over the rejection email all afternoon.
e.zh: 他整个下午都在为那封拒绝邮件郁闷。

e.en: A big iron {stewpot} simmered on the wood stove.
e.zh: 一只大铁炖锅在柴火炉上慢慢炖着。

e.en: She tossed the carrots into the bubbling {stewpot}.
e.zh: 她把胡萝卜扔进咕嘟冒泡的炖锅里。

stews.t:
n. 炖菜（复数）
v. 炖（第三人称）

e.en: Hearty {stews} are perfect for cold winter nights.
e.zh: 丰盛的炖菜最适合寒冷的冬夜。

e.en: He always {stews} when his ideas get rejected.
e.zh: 他的想法被否决时总会闷闷不乐。

e.en: The poet analyzed each {stich} of the ancient verse.
e.zh: 诗人分析了那首古诗的每一行诗句。

e.en: A single {stich} can carry the weight of a whole stanza.
e.zh: 一行诗句有时能承载整节诗的分量。

stick.t:
n. 棍子，棒
v. 粘贴；坚持

e.en: The dog ran off chasing a {stick} into the river.
e.zh: 那只狗追着一根木棍跑进了河里。

e.en: These rules will {stick} once everyone gets used to them.
e.zh: 等大家都习惯了,这些规则就会留下来。

e.en: Kids used to play {stickball} in the city streets.
e.zh: 以前孩子们常在城里的街道上玩棍球。

e.en: He grew up playing {stickball} with his Brooklyn neighbors.
e.zh: 他从小在布鲁克林和邻居一起玩棍球长大。

e.en: My daughter put a unicorn {sticker} on her notebook.
e.zh: 我女儿在笔记本上贴了一张独角兽贴纸。

e.en: The {sticker} on the bumper made everyone laugh.
e.zh: 保险杠上那张贴纸把大家都逗笑了。

e.en: The kids decorated their helmets with skateboard {stickers}.
e.zh: 孩子们用滑板贴纸装饰他们的头盔。

e.en: You can earn cute {stickers} for finishing daily lessons.
e.zh: 完成每日课程就能获得可爱的贴纸奖励。

e.en: The {stickiness} of the dough means you need more flour.
e.zh: 面团这么黏,说明你得再加点面粉。

e.en: App designers measure {stickiness} by how often users return.
e.zh: 应用设计师用用户回访频率来衡量黏性。

e.en: The dough keeps {sticking} to my fingers as I knead it.
e.zh: 我揉面时面团一直粘在手指上。

e.en: She's {sticking} to her diet despite the holiday temptations.
e.zh: 尽管节日里诱惑很多,她仍然坚持自己的饮食计划。

e.en: A small {stickleback} darted between the reeds in the pond.
e.zh: 一条小刺鱼在池塘的芦苇间窜来窜去。

e.en: Biologists study {stickleback} fish to understand rapid evolution.
e.zh: 生物学家研究刺鱼以了解快速进化的过程。

stickler.t: n. 坚持己见者，较真的人

e.en: My professor is a {stickler} for proper citation formatting.
e.zh: 我的教授对引用格式的规范要求极其严格。

e.en: She's a real {stickler} when it comes to punctuality.
e.zh: 在守时方面,她是个一丝不苟的人。

e.en: He wore a pearl {stickpin} on the lapel of his suit.
e.zh: 他在西装翻领上别了一枚珍珠领带别针。

e.en: The antique {stickpin} once belonged to her great-grandfather.
e.zh: 那枚古董领带别针曾经属于她的曾祖父。

sticks.t:
n. 棍子（复数）
v. 粘（第三人称）

e.en: He {sticks} to his daily workout no matter what.
e.zh: 无论怎样他都坚持每天锻炼。

e.en: The kids gathered {sticks} for the campfire.
e.zh: 孩子们捡了些树枝来生篝火。

e.en: My fingers are {sticky} from eating candy.
e.zh: 我的手指因为吃糖变得黏黏的。

e.en: That's a {sticky} situation to handle politically.
e.zh: 那在政治上是个棘手的局面。

e.en: My neck feels {stiff} after sleeping wrong.
e.zh: 我睡姿不对,脖子现在很僵硬。

e.en: The startup faces {stiff} competition from larger rivals.
e.zh: 这家初创公司面临着大公司激烈的竞争。

e.en: Regulators plan to {stiffen} rules on data privacy.
e.zh: 监管机构计划加强数据隐私的相关规定。

e.en: Add cornstarch to {stiffen} the sauce slightly.
e.zh: 加点玉米淀粉让酱汁稍微变稠。

e.en: She {stiffened} when she heard the strange noise.
e.zh: 听到奇怪的声音她身体一下子僵住了。

e.en: The government {stiffened} penalties for tax evasion.
e.zh: 政府加重了对逃税行为的处罚。

e.en: The collar uses a plastic {stiffener} to keep its shape.
e.zh: 这个领子里加了塑料硬衬来保持形状。

e.en: Engineers added a metal {stiffener} along the panel edge.
e.zh: 工程师沿面板边缘加装了一根金属加强件。

stiffening.t:
v. 变硬（进行式）
n. 加固材料

e.en: Officials are {stiffening} enforcement of the new law.
e.zh: 官员们正在加强对新法律的执行力度。

e.en: She felt her muscles {stiffening} from the cold.
e.zh: 她感到自己的肌肉因寒冷而变得僵硬。

e.en: Egg white {stiffens} when you whip it long enough.
e.zh: 蛋清打发足够久后会变硬。

e.en: His posture {stiffens} whenever the boss walks in.
e.zh: 老板一进来他的姿势就变得僵直。

e.en: He bowed {stiffly} and left the room without a word.
e.zh: 他生硬地鞠了一躬,一言不发地离开了房间。

e.en: She walked {stiffly} after the long flight.
e.zh: 长途飞行后她走起路来僵硬别扭。

e.en: Morning {stiffness} in the joints can signal arthritis.
e.zh: 关节晨僵可能是关节炎的信号。

e.en: Critics complained about the {stiffness} of his acting.
e.zh: 评论家抱怨他演技太过僵硬。

e.en: Strict rules can {stifle} creativity in the workplace.
e.zh: 过严的规定会扼杀职场上的创造力。

e.en: She tried to {stifle} a yawn during the meeting.
e.zh: 开会时她努力憋住了一个哈欠。

stifled.t:
v. 抑制（过去式）
adj. 压抑的

e.en: He {stifled} a laugh when his coworker tripped.
e.zh: 同事绊了一下,他强忍住没笑出来。

e.en: Heavy censorship {stifled} public debate for years.
e.zh: 严厉的审查多年来压制了公共讨论。

stifling.t: adj. 令人窒息的；压抑的

e.en: The {stifling} heat made it hard to concentrate.
e.zh: 闷热的天气让人很难集中注意力。

e.en: She found the office culture {stifling} and quit.
e.zh: 她觉得公司氛围令人窒息,于是辞职了。

e.en: There is still a {stigma} around mental health issues.
e.zh: 心理健康问题至今仍存在污名化。

e.en: Bankruptcy used to carry a heavy social {stigma}.
e.zh: 过去破产会带来沉重的社会污名。

e.en: The painting depicts a saint receiving the {stigmata}.
e.zh: 这幅画描绘了一位圣人显现圣痕的情景。

e.en: Some believers travel far to see the {stigmata}.
e.zh: 一些信徒不远千里前来观看圣痕。

e.en: Campaigners say the policy will {stigmatise} poor families.
e.zh: 活动人士称这项政策会让贫困家庭被污名化。

e.en: Society should not {stigmatise} people seeking therapy.
e.zh: 社会不应给寻求心理治疗的人贴上污名。

stigmatised.t:
adj. 被污名化的
v. stigmatise 的过去式

e.en: For years, single mothers were unfairly {stigmatised}.
e.zh: 多年来,单亲母亲被不公地污名化。

e.en: He felt {stigmatised} after his prison release.
e.zh: 出狱之后他觉得自己被人歧视。

stigmatization.t: n. 污名化；打上耻辱烙印

e.en: The campaign aims to reduce {stigmatization} of HIV patients.
e.zh: 该运动旨在减少对艾滋病患者的污名化。

e.en: {stigmatization} prevents many from seeking help early.
e.zh: 污名化让许多人不敢及早求助。

stigmatize.t: v. 污名化；给…扣上恶名

e.en: We shouldn't {stigmatize} workers for taking sick leave.
e.zh: 我们不应给请病假的员工贴上负面标签。

e.en: Media coverage can {stigmatize} entire neighborhoods.
e.zh: 媒体的报道可能让整片社区被污名化。

stigmatized.t:
adj. 被污名化的
v. stigmatize 的过去式

e.en: Mental illness has long been {stigmatized} in many cultures.
e.zh: 在许多文化中,精神疾病长期被污名化。

e.en: She felt {stigmatized} after declaring bankruptcy.
e.zh: 申请破产后她觉得自己被人另眼相看。

stigmatizing.t:
v. 正在污名化
adj. 带有污名的

e.en: Avoid {stigmatizing} language when reporting on addiction.
e.zh: 报道成瘾问题时要避免使用污名化的措辞。

e.en: The label is {stigmatizing} and unhelpful for patients.
e.zh: 这个标签带有污名,对病人毫无帮助。

stile.t: n. 跨墙阶梯（供人越过围栏）

e.en: We climbed the {stile} to cross into the next field.
e.zh: 我们翻过梯磴进入下一片田地。

e.en: A wooden {stile} marked the start of the hiking trail.
e.zh: 一座木制梯磴标志着登山步道的起点。

e.en: The footpath crosses several {stiles} along the way.
e.zh: 这条小径沿途要翻过好几道梯磴。

e.en: Old wooden {stiles} dot the English countryside.
e.zh: 古老的木梯磴遍布英国乡村。

e.en: She wore a black dress and bright red {stiletto} heels.
e.zh: 她穿着黑色连衣裙搭配亮红色细高跟鞋。

e.en: Walking on cobblestones in a {stiletto} is a nightmare.
e.zh: 穿细高跟鞋走鹅卵石路简直是场噩梦。

still.t:
adv. 仍然；还
adj. 静止的；安静的

e.en: He's {still} working on the report at midnight.
e.zh: 半夜了他还在赶那份报告。

e.en: Please sit {still} while I take the photo.
e.zh: 我拍照的时候请坐着别动。

e.en: The hospital offers counseling for parents after a {stillbirth}.
e.zh: 医院为经历死产的父母提供心理辅导。

e.en: Researchers study what factors increase {stillbirth} risk.
e.zh: 研究人员在研究哪些因素会增加死产风险。

stillborn.t: adj. 死产的；（计划）胎死腹中的

e.en: Their first child was sadly {stillborn}.
e.zh: 他们的第一个孩子不幸是死胎。

e.en: The reform plan was {stillborn} due to political opposition.
e.zh: 这项改革方案因政治反对而胎死腹中。

stilled.t: v. 使平静；使静止（过去式）

e.en: The conductor's gesture {stilled} the entire orchestra.
e.zh: 指挥的一个手势让整个乐团瞬间安静下来。

e.en: Her gentle voice {stilled} the crying baby.
e.zh: 她温柔的声音安抚了哭闹的婴儿。

e.en: I love the {stillness} of the lake at dawn.
e.zh: 我喜欢黎明时湖面那种宁静。

e.en: A sudden {stillness} fell over the crowd.
e.zh: 人群中突然变得一片寂静。

e.en: The beach house stands on a single concrete {stilt}.
e.zh: 这座海滨小屋立在一根混凝土支柱上。

e.en: A circus performer balanced on one {stilt}.
e.zh: 一个马戏团演员在一根高跷上保持平衡。

e.en: The dialogue in the movie sounded {stilted} and unnatural.
e.zh: 电影里的对白显得生硬不自然。

e.en: Their conversation was polite but {stilted}.
e.zh: 他们的对话礼貌但生硬别扭。

stilton.t: n. 斯蒂尔顿奶酪（英国蓝纹奶酪）

e.en: He served {stilton} with port after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后他端上了斯蒂尔顿奶酪配波特酒。

e.en: A wedge of {stilton} sat on the cheese board.
e.zh: 奶酪拼盘上摆着一块斯蒂尔顿奶酪。

e.en: Coffee is the most popular legal {stimulant} worldwide.
e.zh: 咖啡是全球最受欢迎的合法兴奋剂。

e.en: Doctors prescribed a mild {stimulant} for his fatigue.
e.zh: 医生给他开了一种温和的兴奋剂治疗疲劳。

e.en: Athletes are banned from using {stimulants} in competition.
e.zh: 运动员在比赛中禁止使用兴奋剂。

e.en: He avoids {stimulants} like coffee after lunch.
e.zh: 午饭后他会避开咖啡之类的兴奋性饮品。

e.en: Tax cuts are meant to {stimulate} consumer spending.
e.zh: 减税的目的是刺激消费支出。

e.en: Puzzles {stimulate} the brain and improve memory.
e.zh: 益智游戏能刺激大脑、增强记忆力。

stimulated.t:
adj. 受刺激的
v. stimulate 的过去式

e.en: The new exhibition {stimulated} a lot of public interest.
e.zh: 新展览引发了大众的浓厚兴趣。

e.en: She felt mentally {stimulated} after the workshop.
e.zh: 参加完工作坊后,她感到精神上很受启发。

stimulates.t: v. 刺激；促进（第三人称单数）

e.en: Sunlight {stimulates} vitamin D production in the skin.
e.zh: 阳光能促进皮肤生成维生素D。

e.en: Good design {stimulates} curiosity from the first glance.
e.zh: 好的设计能让人一眼就产生好奇。

stimulating.t: adj. 有启发的；令人振奋的

e.en: We had a {stimulating} debate about climate policy.
e.zh: 我们就气候政策进行了一场激发思考的辩论。

e.en: Reading is more {stimulating} than scrolling social media.
e.zh: 读书比刷社交媒体更能激发思维。

e.en: Babies need plenty of sensory {stimulation} to develop.
e.zh: 婴儿成长需要充足的感官刺激。

e.en: He misses the intellectual {stimulation} of his old job.
e.zh: 他怀念以前那份工作带来的脑力刺激。

e.en: The therapy uses gentle electrical {stimulations} to relax muscles.
e.zh: 这种疗法用温和的电刺激来放松肌肉。

e.en: Different {stimulations} produced different brain responses in the test.
e.zh: 测试中不同的刺激会引发不同的大脑反应。

e.en: The government announced a {stimulative} package for small businesses.
e.zh: 政府宣布了一项针对小企业的刺激性方案。

e.en: Lower interest rates have a {stimulative} effect on the economy.
e.zh: 降低利率对经济有刺激作用。

e.en: The doctor implanted a nerve {stimulator} to ease his pain.
e.zh: 医生为他植入了一个神经刺激器以缓解疼痛。

e.en: This device acts as a muscle {stimulator} during physical therapy.
e.zh: 这台设备在理疗过程中充当肌肉刺激器。

stimulatory.t: adj. 促进性的；刺激作用的

e.en: The drug has a {stimulatory} effect on the immune system.
e.zh: 这种药对免疫系统有刺激作用。

e.en: Researchers identified {stimulatory} signals between the two cell types.
e.zh: 研究人员发现了这两类细胞之间的刺激信号。

stimuli.t: n. 刺激因素（stimulus 的复数）

e.en: The brain filters thousands of {stimuli} every second.
e.zh: 大脑每秒都在过滤成千上万的刺激。

e.en: Newborns react strongly to bright visual {stimuli}.
e.zh: 新生儿对明亮的视觉刺激反应强烈。

e.en: Congress passed a major economic {stimulus} package.
e.zh: 国会通过了一项大规模的经济刺激方案。
