e.en: The loud bang served as a {stimulus} for the experiment.
e.zh: 那声巨响在实验中作为一种刺激源。

sting.t:
v. 叮；刺痛
n. 刺；蜇伤

e.en: A bee {sting} can be dangerous if you're allergic.
e.zh: 如果你过敏,被蜜蜂蜇一下可能很危险。

e.en: The criticism began to {sting} more than he expected.
e.zh: 那些批评开始比他预想的更扎心。

e.en: A bee leaves its {stinger} behind after attacking.
e.zh: 蜜蜂蜇人后会把刺留在伤口里。

e.en: The article ended with a real {stinger} of a quote.
e.zh: 那篇文章以一句很扎心的话作为结尾。

stingiest.t: adj. 最小气的（stingy 的最高级）

e.en: He's the {stingiest} person I know—he never tips.
e.zh: 他是我认识最小气的人,从不给小费。

e.en: That café offers the {stingiest} portions in town.
e.zh: 那家咖啡馆的份量是镇上最抠门的。

e.en: His {stinginess} with compliments hurt the team's morale.
e.zh: 他在表扬上的吝啬伤害了团队士气。

e.en: The hotel's {stinginess} with towels frustrated every guest.
e.zh: 酒店在毛巾上的小气让每位客人都很恼火。

e.en: She accidentally brushed against a {stinging} nettle.
e.zh: 她不小心碰到了一株会刺人的荨麻。

e.en: The critic wrote a {stinging} review of the new film.
e.zh: 那位评论家给这部新电影写了一篇尖刻的影评。

e.en: A {stingray} glided gracefully across the sandy ocean floor.
e.zh: 一条魟鱼优雅地掠过沙质海底。

e.en: The diver carefully avoided stepping on the camouflaged {stingray}.
e.zh: 潜水员小心地避开那条伪装起来的魟鱼。

e.en: My boss is too {stingy} to pay for team lunches.
e.zh: 我老板太抠门,不肯请团队吃午饭。

e.en: The app is {stingy} with free credits for new users.
e.zh: 这款应用对新用户的免费额度给得很少。

stink.t:
v. 发臭
n. 恶臭

e.en: The garbage bins {stink} after sitting in the sun.
e.zh: 垃圾桶在太阳下晒过后臭气熏天。

e.en: Customers raised a {stink} about the sudden price increase.
e.zh: 顾客对突然涨价大为不满。

e.en: That movie was a real {stinker} — total waste of money.
e.zh: 那部电影烂透了,完全是浪费钱。

e.en: The exam had a {stinker} of a question at the end.
e.zh: 考试最后有一道极其难搞的题目。

stinking.t: adj. 发臭的；糟糕透顶的

e.en: Take those {stinking} sneakers off before coming inside.
e.zh: 进屋前把那双臭烘烘的运动鞋脱掉。

e.en: He's {stinking} rich but still lives in a tiny apartment.
e.zh: 他富得流油,却还住在一间小公寓里。

stinks.t: v. 发臭（第三人称单数）

e.en: This whole situation {stinks} of corruption to me.
e.zh: 在我看来,整件事透着一股腐败的味道。

e.en: The fridge {stinks} because someone forgot the leftover fish.
e.zh: 冰箱很臭,因为有人忘了里面的剩鱼。

e.en: My dog rolled in something {stinky} at the park.
e.zh: 我家狗在公园里滚到了什么臭东西上。

e.en: She wrinkled her nose at the {stinky} blue cheese.
e.zh: 她对着那块臭味浓烈的蓝纹奶酪皱起鼻子。

stint.t:
n. 一段工作时期
v. 吝惜；节省

e.en: He did a two-year {stint} as a software engineer at Google.
e.zh: 他在谷歌做了两年的软件工程师。

e.en: Don't {stint} on sleep the night before an interview.
e.zh: 面试前一晚千万别在睡眠上吝啬时间。

e.en: PhD students receive a monthly {stipend} to cover living expenses.
e.zh: 博士生每月领取津贴用于支付生活开销。

e.en: The internship offers a modest {stipend} plus housing.
e.zh: 这个实习提供少量津贴外加住宿。

stipendiary.t:
adj. 领薪的
n. 受薪者

e.en: He worked as a {stipendiary} magistrate in the city court.
e.zh: 他在市法院担任受薪治安法官。

e.en: The role is {stipendiary}, with payment made each quarter.
e.zh: 该职位为受薪岗位,每季度发放报酬一次。

stipple.t:
v. 用点画法绘制
n. 点画

e.en: Artists often {stipple} ink to create soft shading effects.
e.zh: 艺术家常用点画法画墨水来营造柔和的阴影效果。

e.en: Use a sponge to {stipple} paint onto the textured wall.
e.zh: 用海绵把颜料点涂到有纹理的墙面上。

stippled.t: adj. 点画法的；有点状纹理的

e.en: The illustration was carefully {stippled} with thousands of tiny dots.
e.zh: 这幅插图由成千上万的小点精心点画而成。

e.en: She painted a {stippled} background for her portrait.
e.zh: 她为她的人像画了一层点画风格的背景。

e.en: The contract must {stipulate} a clear deadline for delivery.
e.zh: 合同必须明确规定交付的截止日期。

e.en: Most landlords {stipulate} that pets are not allowed.
e.zh: 大多数房东都明确规定不允许养宠物。

stipulated.t: v. 规定；约定（stipulate 的过去式）

e.en: The agreement {stipulated} a six-month probation period.
e.zh: 协议规定了六个月的试用期。

e.en: She {stipulated} that her donation be used for scholarships.
e.zh: 她明确规定她的捐款用于发放奖学金。

stipulates.t: v. 规定；约定（第三人称单数）

e.en: The policy {stipulates} that refunds must be requested within 30 days.
e.zh: 该政策规定退款必须在30天内申请。

e.en: Our lease {stipulates} no smoking inside the apartment.
e.zh: 我们的租约明确规定公寓内不准吸烟。

stipulating.t: v. 规定；约定（现在分词）

e.en: He signed the offer {stipulating} a remote-work arrangement.
e.zh: 他在签署录用函时明确约定可以远程办公。

e.en: The clause {stipulating} late fees was buried in fine print.
e.zh: 那条规定滞纳金的条款被藏在小字说明里。

e.en: I'll lend you the car, with one {stipulation}: no eating inside.
e.zh: 我可以把车借给你,但有一个条件:车内不许吃东西。

e.en: The job offer came with the {stipulation} of relocating to Tokyo.
e.zh: 这份工作邀约附有一个条件,就是必须搬到东京。

e.en: Read the {stipulations} carefully before signing the rental agreement.
e.zh: 在签租房合同之前仔细阅读各项条款。

e.en: The grant has several {stipulations} about how funds can be used.
e.zh: 这笔拨款对资金的使用方式有几项规定。

stir.t:
v. 搅拌；搅动
v. 激起（情绪）

e.en: {Stir} the soup gently so it doesn't burn at the bottom.
e.zh: 轻轻搅拌汤,免得锅底糊掉。

e.en: Her surprising resignation caused quite a {stir} online.
e.zh: 她意外辞职在网上引起了不小的轰动。

stirling.t: n. 斯特灵（英国苏格兰地名/人名）

e.en: We took a weekend train trip up to {Stirling} in central Scotland.
e.zh: 我们周末坐火车去了苏格兰中部的斯特林。

e.en: The castle at {Stirling} sits on a dramatic volcanic crag.
e.zh: 斯特林的城堡坐落在一块险峻的火山岩上。

stirlingshire.t: n. 斯特灵郡（苏格兰旧郡）

e.en: He grew up on a small farm in {Stirlingshire}, Scotland.
e.zh: 他在苏格兰斯特林郡的一个小农场长大。

e.en: The hills of {Stirlingshire} are popular with weekend hikers.
e.zh: 斯特林郡的山丘很受周末徒步者欢迎。

e.en: She {stirred} sugar into her coffee absentmindedly.
e.zh: 她心不在焉地把糖搅进咖啡里。

e.en: The speech {stirred} strong emotions among the audience.
e.zh: 那场演讲在听众中激起了强烈的情绪。

e.en: Use a magnetic {stirrer} to mix the chemicals evenly.
e.zh: 用磁力搅拌器把化学品均匀混合起来。

e.en: He's a real {stirrer} who loves causing drama at meetings.
e.zh: 他真是个搅事精,特别爱在会上挑起是非。

stirring.t:
adj. 激动人心的
v. 搅拌（现在分词）

e.en: The coach gave a {stirring} speech before the final match.
e.zh: 教练在决赛前发表了一段振奋人心的演讲。

e.en: Keep {stirring} the sauce until it thickens slightly.
e.zh: 持续搅拌酱汁,直到它稍微变稠。

e.en: She placed her boot in the {stirrup} and swung onto the horse.
e.zh: 她把靴子踩进马镫,翻身上了马。

e.en: The leather {stirrup} had worn smooth from years of riding.
e.zh: 皮制的马镫因多年骑马已被磨得光滑。

stirs.t: v. 搅拌；激起（第三人称单数）

e.en: The smell of fresh bread {stirs} memories of my grandmother's kitchen.
e.zh: 新鲜面包的香味勾起了我对外婆厨房的回忆。

e.en: He {stirs} his tea slowly while reading the morning news.
e.zh: 他一边看晨报,一边慢慢搅着茶。

stitch.t:
n. 针脚；一针
v. 缝；缝合

e.en: Can you {stitch} this button back onto my shirt?
e.zh: 你能把这颗扣子重新缝回我衬衫上吗?

e.en: I got a sharp {stitch} in my side while running.
e.zh: 我跑步时侧腰一阵刺痛。

e.en: She carefully {stitched} the torn seam back together.
e.zh: 她小心地把撕裂的接缝重新缝好。

e.en: The doctor {stitched} the cut and bandaged his hand.
e.zh: 医生缝合了伤口并给他的手包扎好。

e.en: She works as a skilled {stitcher} at a leather goods workshop.
e.zh: 她在一家皮具工坊里当熟练的缝纫工。

e.en: This automatic {stitcher} can sew a hundred pages per minute.
e.zh: 这台自动装订机每分钟能装订一百页。

e.en: Her wedding dress featured exquisite hand {stitchery} along the hem.
e.zh: 她的婚纱裙摆处有一圈精美的手工刺绣。

e.en: The museum displayed antique {stitchery} from the 18th century.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了18世纪的古董刺绣作品。

stitches.t:
n. 针脚（复数）
v. 缝合（第三人称单数）

e.en: The doctor said the {stitches} can come out next week.
e.zh: 医生说下周就可以拆线了。

e.en: His jokes had us all in {stitches} during dinner.
e.zh: 他的笑话让我们晚餐时笑得前仰后合。

stitching.t:
n. 缝线；针脚
v. 缝合（现在分词）

e.en: The {stitching} on these designer jeans is starting to come loose.
e.zh: 这条名牌牛仔裤的针脚开始有点松线了。

e.en: She spent the afternoon {stitching} a quilt for her daughter.
e.zh: 她整个下午都在为女儿缝制一床被子。

e.en: A {stoat} darted across the path, its tail tipped with black.
e.zh: 一只白鼬窜过小路,尾巴尖是黑色的。

e.en: In winter, the {stoat} turns pure white except for its tail.
e.zh: 到了冬天,白鼬除了尾巴外通体变得纯白。

e.en: The model uses a {stochastic} process to simulate stock prices.
e.zh: 该模型使用随机过程来模拟股票价格。

e.en: Neural networks are trained with {stochastic} gradient descent.
e.zh: 神经网络通过随机梯度下降进行训练。

stock.t:
n. 股票；库存
v. 储备；进货

e.en: The store ran out of {stock} during the holiday rush.
e.zh: 商店在假日抢购潮中卖到断货了。

e.en: She bought {stock} in several tech companies last year.
e.zh: 她去年买入了几家科技公司的股票。

e.en: The settlers built a wooden {stockade} around the village for protection.
e.zh: 定居者们在村子周围建起一道木栅栏作为防御。

e.en: Prisoners of war were held inside the {stockade} for months.
e.zh: 战俘在木栅围场里被关押了好几个月。

e.en: My uncle works as a {stockbroker} on Wall Street.
e.zh: 我叔叔在华尔街当股票经纪人。

e.en: A good {stockbroker} can save you from costly mistakes.
e.zh: 一个好的股票经纪人能帮你避免代价高昂的错误。

e.en: He left {stockbroking} to start his own fintech startup.
e.zh: 他离开了证券经纪行业,自己创办了一家金融科技公司。

e.en: The {stockbroking} firm announced major layoffs this morning.
e.zh: 那家证券经纪公司今天上午宣布了大规模裁员。

e.en: The fridge is fully {stocked} for the weekend party.
e.zh: 冰箱已经为周末派对备足了食物。

e.en: This bookstore is well {stocked} with rare first editions.
e.zh: 这家书店里收藏了不少珍贵的初版书籍。

e.en: He works as a night {stocker} at the local supermarket.
e.zh: 他在当地超市做夜班理货员。

e.en: The {stocker} restocked the shelves before the store opened.
e.zh: 理货员在商店开门前把货架重新补满了。

e.en: Every {stockholder} received a dividend payment last quarter.
e.zh: 每位股东上个季度都领到了分红。

e.en: As a {stockholder}, she has the right to vote at meetings.
e.zh: 作为股东,她有权在会议上投票。

e.en: He sold his {stockholding} in the company before retiring.
e.zh: 他在退休前卖掉了自己在公司的全部股份。

e.en: Her {stockholding} grew significantly during the bull market.
e.zh: 她的持股在牛市期间大幅增值。

stockholm.t: n. 斯德哥尔摩（瑞典首都）

e.en: We spent a lovely week exploring the islands of {Stockholm}.
e.zh: 我们用一周愉快的时间游览了斯德哥尔摩的群岛。

e.en: {Stockholm} hosts the annual Nobel Prize ceremony every December.
e.zh: 每年12月,斯德哥尔摩都会举办诺贝尔奖颁奖典礼。

e.en: She hung a red Christmas {stocking} above the fireplace.
e.zh: 她在壁炉上方挂了一只红色的圣诞袜。

e.en: The store is busy {stocking} shelves before opening time.
e.zh: 商店正忙着在开门前往货架上补货。

e.en: He padded across the floor in his {stockinged} feet.
e.zh: 他穿着袜子轻轻地走过地板。

e.en: Please leave shoes at the door and walk in {stockinged} feet.
e.zh: 请把鞋子放在门口,只穿袜子进屋。

stockist.t: n. 经销商；特约零售商

e.en: This boutique is the only {stockist} of that brand in town.
e.zh: 这家精品店是镇上唯一一家销售那个品牌的店铺。

e.en: Check the website to find a {stockist} near you.
e.zh: 上网站查一下离你最近的经销商在哪里。

stocklist.t: n. 库存清单；股票行情表

e.en: The manager updated the {stocklist} after every delivery.
e.zh: 经理每次进货后都会更新库存清单。

e.en: Print the latest {stocklist} before the morning audit.
e.zh: 早上盘点前请打印最新的存货清单。

e.en: The {stockman} rounded up the cattle before sunset.
e.zh: 牧人在日落前把牛群赶拢了。

e.en: As a young {stockman}, he learned to ride and rope skillfully.
e.zh: 年轻时当牧场工人，他学会了娴熟的骑马和套绳技巧。

e.en: The {stockmarket} dropped sharply after the surprise rate hike.
e.zh: 出乎意料的加息消息后，股市大幅下跌。

e.en: Beginners should research before investing in the {stockmarket}.
e.zh: 新手在投资股市之前应该做好研究。

stockpile.t:
v. 囤积；储备
n. 储备物资

e.en: Many families {stockpile} canned goods in case of emergencies.
e.zh: 许多家庭会囤积罐头食品以备不时之需。

e.en: The country maintains a strategic {stockpile} of crude oil.
e.zh: 该国保有一份战略石油储备。

e.en: The country {stockpiled} medical supplies before the pandemic peaked.
e.zh: 该国在疫情高峰前囤积了大量医疗物资。

e.en: He {stockpiled} canned food in the basement just in case.
e.zh: 他在地下室囤了不少罐头以防万一。

stockpiles.t:
n. 储备（复数）
v. 囤积（第三人称单数）

e.en: The government maintains huge {stockpiles} of grain for emergencies.
e.zh: 政府储备了大量粮食以应对紧急情况。

e.en: She {stockpiles} skincare products whenever they go on sale.
e.zh: 每逢促销她就囤护肤品。

stockpiling.t: v. 囤积；储备（现在分词）

e.en: Shoppers started {stockpiling} toilet paper after the news broke.
e.zh: 消息一出,购物者就开始囤厕纸。

e.en: The company is {stockpiling} chips ahead of the shortage.
e.zh: 公司正在芯片短缺前提前囤货。

stockport.t: n. 斯托克波特（英国城镇）

e.en: She grew up in {Stockport}, just south of Manchester.
e.zh: 她在曼彻斯特南边的斯托克波特长大。

e.en: The train from {Stockport} to London takes about two hours.
e.zh: 从斯托克波特到伦敦的火车约需两小时。

e.en: He simmered the bones all afternoon in a large {stockpot}.
e.zh: 他用一只大汤锅把骨头炖了一下午。

e.en: Every good kitchen needs a heavy {stockpot} for soups.
e.zh: 每个好厨房都需要一只厚实的汤锅煮汤。

e.en: The clerk went to the {stockroom} to check for more sizes.
e.zh: 店员去库房查看是否还有其他尺码。

e.en: Boxes of new inventory filled the small {stockroom}.
e.zh: 成箱的新货堆满了狭小的库房。

e.en: Tech {stocks} fell sharply after the earnings report.
e.zh: 财报公布后科技股大幅下跌。

e.en: The store is running low on {stocks} of bottled water.
e.zh: 这家店的瓶装水库存快用完了。

e.en: The shop is closed today for annual {stocktaking}.
e.zh: 店铺今天关门进行年度盘点。

e.en: After the year ends, some {stocktaking} of priorities helps.
e.zh: 年底过后,盘点一下优先事项很有帮助。

e.en: He drove through {Stockton} on his way to San Francisco.
e.zh: 他在去旧金山的路上经过了斯托克顿。

e.en: The team plays its home games in {Stockton}, California.
e.zh: 球队在加州斯托克顿打主场比赛。

stockwell.t: n. 斯托克韦尔（伦敦地名）

e.en: She caught the Northern line at {Stockwell} station.
e.zh: 她在斯托克韦尔站搭乘北线地铁。

e.en: Their flat in {Stockwell} is just a short walk from Brixton.
e.zh: 他们在斯托克韦尔的公寓离布里克斯顿不远。

e.en: A {stocky} man in a uniform guarded the entrance.
e.zh: 一个身材敦实的制服男子守在入口处。

e.en: The bulldog was short, {stocky}, and surprisingly fast.
e.zh: 那只斗牛犬矮壮敦实,却出奇地敏捷。

e.en: Cattle were herded into the {stockyard} before auction.
e.zh: 拍卖前,牛群被赶进牲畜围场。

e.en: The old {stockyard} has been converted into a shopping district.
e.zh: 老牲畜围场已被改造成购物区。

stodge.t: n. 油腻难消化的食物

e.en: School lunches were heavy {stodge} that left us sleepy.
e.zh: 学校午餐是顶饱的厚重食物,吃完让人犯困。

e.en: The novel turned out to be Victorian {stodge} I couldn't finish.
e.zh: 这本小说原来是难以读完的维多利亚式沉闷之作。

stodgy.t:
adj. 乏味守旧的
adj. (食物) 油腻难消化的

e.en: The pudding was thick and {stodgy}, but very filling.
e.zh: 那布丁又稠又厚实,但非常顶饱。

e.en: His writing style is a bit {stodgy} for younger readers.
e.zh: 他的文风对年轻读者来说有点沉闷老派。

e.en: The old man lit a fat {stogie} on the porch.
e.zh: 老人在门廊上点燃了一支粗雪茄。

e.en: He puffed on a cheap {stogie} while reading the paper.
e.zh: 他一边看报一边抽着廉价雪茄。

stoic.t:
adj. 坚忍克己的
n. 禁欲主义者

e.en: She remained {stoic} throughout the painful procedure.
e.zh: 整个痛苦的过程中她都默默忍受。

e.en: His {stoic} expression never changed, even at the bad news.
e.zh: 即便听到坏消息,他面无表情依旧。

e.en: He bore the criticism with a {stoical} calm.
e.zh: 他以泰然自若的态度接受了批评。

e.en: Her {stoical} response surprised everyone in the room.
e.zh: 她隐忍淡定的反应令在场所有人吃惊。

e.en: The patient endured the long wait {stoically}.
e.zh: 病人默默地忍受着漫长的等待。

e.en: He {stoically} accepted the verdict without complaint.
e.zh: 他不动声色地接受了裁决,没有抱怨。

e.en: We learned {stoichiometry} to balance chemical equations in class.
e.zh: 我们在课上学化学计量来配平化学方程式。

e.en: Correct {stoichiometry} is essential for predicting reaction yields.
e.zh: 准确的化学计量对预测反应产率至关重要。

stoicism.t: n. 斯多葛哲学；坚忍克己

e.en: Many programmers find {stoicism} useful for handling daily setbacks.
e.zh: 许多程序员觉得斯多葛主义有助于应对日常挫折。

e.en: She faced the diagnosis with quiet {stoicism}.
e.zh: 她以沉静坚忍的态度面对诊断结果。

e.en: Different cultures developed their own forms of {stoicisms} over centuries.
e.zh: 几个世纪以来,各文化形成了各自的隐忍哲学。

e.en: His essay compared the {stoicisms} of East and West.
e.zh: 他的文章对比了东西方的隐忍哲学。

e.en: We trekked from {Stok} village toward the high mountain pass.
e.zh: 我们从斯托克村出发,向高山垭口徒步。

e.en: The {Stok} Range offers stunning views in Ladakh.
e.zh: 斯托克山脉在拉达克地区景色壮丽。

stoke.t:
v. 给（炉子）添燃料
v. 煽动、激起（情绪）

e.en: The ad campaign was designed to {stoke} demand for the phone.
e.zh: 这场广告活动旨在激起人们对这款手机的需求。

e.en: He added more wood to {stoke} the campfire.
e.zh: 他添了些柴来让篝火烧得更旺。

stoked.t:
adj. 非常兴奋的（俚语）
v. stoke 的过去式

e.en: I'm so {stoked} about the concert this weekend.
e.zh: 我对这周末的演唱会兴奋极了。

e.en: The viral video {stoked} fresh debate online.
e.zh: 这段爆红视频在网上引发了新一轮热议。

stoker.t: n. 司炉工；自动加煤机

e.en: The ship's {stoker} shoveled coal deep below deck.
e.zh: 船上的司炉工在甲板深处铲煤。

e.en: Bram {Stoker} wrote the novel Dracula in 1897.
e.zh: 布拉姆·斯托克于1897年创作了小说《德古拉》。

stokes.t: n. 斯托克斯（姓氏/黏度单位）

e.en: Constant negative coverage {stokes} public anxiety about the economy.
e.zh: 持续的负面报道加剧了公众对经济的焦虑。

e.en: The coach's pep talk {stokes} the team before every game.
e.zh: 教练每场比赛前的动员都让队伍士气大振。

stoking.t: v. 添加燃料；煽动情绪

e.en: The politician was accused of {stoking} fears about immigration.
e.zh: 这位政客被指控煽动公众对移民的恐惧。

e.en: She kept {stoking} the fire to keep the cabin warm.
e.zh: 她不停地添柴让小屋保持温暖。

stole.t:
v. steal 的过去式
n. 女式披肩

e.en: Someone {stole} my bike from the rack outside.
e.zh: 有人把我停在外面架子上的自行车偷走了。

e.en: She wore a silk {stole} over her evening gown.
e.zh: 她在晚礼服外搭了一条丝质披肩。

stolen.t: v. steal 的过去分词；被偷的

e.en: The police recovered the {stolen} laptop within a week.
e.zh: 警方一周内就找回了被盗的笔记本电脑。

e.en: He admitted he had {stolen} the answers from her notebook.
e.zh: 他承认从她的笔记本上偷抄了答案。

stolid.t: adj. 神情呆板的；不动声色的

e.en: The guard's {stolid} face revealed nothing about his thoughts.
e.zh: 警卫面无表情,看不出他的想法。

e.en: She gave a {stolid} reply and walked away calmly.
e.zh: 她不动声色地回了一句,平静地走开了。

e.en: His {stolidity} during the crisis impressed his colleagues.
e.zh: 危机中他的沉着不动让同事们刮目相看。

e.en: The horse's {stolidity} made it perfect for nervous riders.
e.zh: 这匹马性格沉稳,非常适合紧张的骑手。

e.en: She {stolidly} continued working despite the noise around her.
e.zh: 尽管周围吵闹,她仍不动声色地继续工作。

e.en: He {stolidly} refused to comment on the rumors.
e.zh: 他不为所动地拒绝就传闻发表评论。

stoma.t:
n. (植物叶片) 气孔
n. (医学) 造口

e.en: After surgery, the patient learned to care for the {stoma}.
e.zh: 术后,病人学会了护理人工造口。

e.en: Each leaf {stoma} opens to allow gas exchange in plants.
e.zh: 植物的每个气孔都会张开以进行气体交换。

stomach.t:
n. 胃；肚子
v. 忍受、容忍

e.en: My {stomach} growled loudly during the meeting.
e.zh: 开会时我的肚子咕咕叫得很响。

e.en: I can't {stomach} another episode of that boring show.
e.zh: 我实在受不了那部无聊剧再看一集。

e.en: I got a bad {stomachache} after eating too much cake.
e.zh: 我吃太多蛋糕后肚子疼得厉害。

e.en: The kids complained of a {stomachache} after the long bus ride.
e.zh: 孩子们坐了长途车后抱怨肚子疼。

e.en: Spicy food often gives him terrible {stomachaches}.
e.zh: 辛辣食物常常让他肚子疼得厉害。

e.en: She gets frequent {stomachaches} when she's stressed at work.
e.zh: 她工作压力大时常常胃痛。

stomaches.t: n. stomach 的复数形式（非标准拼法）

e.en: Their {stomaches} were rumbling by the time dinner arrived.
e.zh: 等晚餐上桌时,他们的肚子都在咕咕叫了。

e.en: Nobody {stomaches} that kind of rude behavior for long.
e.zh: 没人能长期忍受那种无礼的举动。

e.en: Drought triggers {stomatal} closure to reduce water loss.
e.zh: 干旱会引发气孔关闭以减少水分流失。

e.en: Researchers measured {stomatal} density on the underside of leaves.
e.zh: 研究者测量了叶背面的气孔密度。

e.en: Don't {stomp} up the stairs—the baby is sleeping.
e.zh: 别噔噔噔地上楼,宝宝在睡觉。

e.en: She watched the toddler {stomp} angrily out of the room.
e.zh: 她看着那小孩气呼呼地跺着脚走出房间。

e.en: He came {stomping} into the kitchen, clearly furious.
e.zh: 他重重地跺进厨房,显然怒气冲天。

e.en: The fans were {stomping} their feet to the beat.
e.zh: 歌迷们随着节拍跺着脚。

e.en: The village of {Ston} is famous for its salt pans and walls.
e.zh: 斯通村以盐田和城墙闻名。

e.en: We stopped in {Ston} for fresh oysters by the sea.
e.zh: 我们在斯通停下来吃了海边的新鲜生蚝。

stone.t:
n. 石头；宝石
v. 向…扔石头

e.en: The path was paved with smooth, gray {stone}.
e.zh: 小路铺着光滑的灰色石头。

e.en: He skipped a flat {stone} across the calm lake.
e.zh: 他往平静的湖面打了一个水漂。

stonebridge.t: n. 斯通布里奇（地名/姓氏）

e.en: They moved into a new flat near {Stonebridge} Park station.
e.zh: 他们搬进了石桥公园站附近的新公寓。

e.en: The {Stonebridge} development includes shops, homes, and a school.
e.zh: 石桥开发区包括商店、住宅和一所学校。

e.en: His grandfather worked as a {stonecutter} in the marble quarries.
e.zh: 他祖父曾在大理石采石场当石匠。

e.en: The skilled {stonecutter} carved intricate patterns into the granite.
e.zh: 这位技艺娴熟的石匠在花岗岩上雕出精细的图案。

stoned.t: adj. 嗑药/吸毒嗨了的；醉的

e.en: He was completely {stoned} after sharing the brownies.
e.zh: 分了那盘大麻布朗尼后,他彻底嗨了。

e.en: The angry crowd {stoned} the carriage as it passed.
e.zh: 愤怒的人群朝经过的马车投掷石块。

e.en: The angler tied a {stonefly} pattern to match the hatch.
e.zh: 渔夫绑了一只石蝇拟饵以契合羽化期。

e.en: A {stonefly} nymph clung to the rock under the stream.
e.zh: 一只石蝇若虫趴在溪流下的岩石上。

stonehaven.t: n. 斯通黑文（苏格兰地名）

e.en: We had fish and chips by the harbor in {Stonehaven}.
e.zh: 我们在斯通黑文的港口边吃了炸鱼薯条。

e.en: {Stonehaven} hosts a famous fireball festival every Hogmanay.
e.zh: 斯通黑文每年除夕都会举办著名的火球节。

stonehenge.t: n. 巨石阵（英国史前遗迹）

e.en: Tourists flock to {Stonehenge} during the summer solstice.
e.zh: 游客们在夏至时蜂拥前往巨石阵。

e.en: Archaeologists still debate how {Stonehenge} was actually built.
e.zh: 考古学家至今仍在争论巨石阵究竟是如何建造的。

stonehouse.t: n. 斯通豪斯（地名/姓氏）

e.en: They restored an old {stonehouse} on the edge of town.
e.zh: 他们修复了镇边一栋古老的石屋。

e.en: {Stonehouse} village sits quietly in the Cotswolds countryside.
e.zh: 斯通豪斯村静静坐落在科茨沃尔德乡间。

e.en: A skilled {stonemason} carved the church's intricate facade.
e.zh: 一位技艺高超的石匠雕刻了教堂精美的外立面。

e.en: Her grandfather worked as a {stonemason} for forty years.
e.zh: 她祖父当了四十年的石匠。

e.en: His roommate is a chill {stoner} who plays guitar all day.
e.zh: 他的室友是个爱抽大麻的随性家伙，整天弹吉他。

e.en: The movie became a cult classic among {stoner} comedy fans.
e.zh: 这部电影成了大麻喜剧迷心中的经典邪典片。

stones.t:
n. stone 的复数
v. stone 第三人称单数

e.en: Kids skipped flat {stones} across the calm lake surface.
e.zh: 孩子们在平静的湖面上打水漂。

e.en: The ring features three small {stones} set in gold.
e.zh: 这枚戒指镶有三颗小宝石，底座为黄金。

stonewall.t:
v. 拖延阻挠；拒不配合
n. 石墙

e.en: Officials continue to {stonewall} reporters asking about the leaked emails.
e.zh: 官员们继续敷衍记者关于泄露邮件的提问。

e.en: The witness tried to {stonewall} every question from the prosecutor.
e.zh: 证人试图对检察官的每个问题都避而不答。

stonewalling.t: v. 故意拖延、拒不回应

e.en: The CEO was accused of {stonewalling} the investigation for months.
e.zh: 该首席执行官被指控数月来一直阻挠调查。

e.en: Her constant {stonewalling} during arguments damaged the relationship.
e.zh: 她在争吵中一贯的冷处理伤害了这段感情。

e.en: She collects handmade {stoneware} mugs from local potters.
e.zh: 她收藏当地陶艺家手工制作的炻器马克杯。

e.en: This {stoneware} bowl is dishwasher and microwave safe.
e.zh: 这只炻器碗可放入洗碗机和微波炉使用。

e.en: The cathedral's ancient {stonework} has weathered eight centuries.
e.zh: 这座大教堂古老的石雕历经了八个世纪的风雨。

e.en: Skilled masons restored the crumbling {stonework} on the bridge.
e.zh: 熟练的石匠修复了桥上破损的石砌结构。

e.en: The old {stoneworks} outside town now operate as a museum.
e.zh: 城外的旧石材厂如今作为博物馆运营。

e.en: Intricate {stoneworks} decorate the entrance of the temple.
e.zh: 精巧的石雕装饰着寺庙的入口。

stoney.t: adj. 多石的（stony 的异体）

e.en: She gave him a {stoney} look that ended the conversation.
e.zh: 她冷冷地瞪了他一眼，谈话就此结束。

e.en: The path grew {stoney} as we climbed higher up the hill.
e.zh: 我们越往山上爬，路变得越是布满石块。

stonily.t: adv. 冷漠地；面无表情地

e.en: He stared {stonily} ahead, refusing to acknowledge her apology.
e.zh: 他冷漠地直视前方，对她的道歉置之不理。

e.en: The judge listened {stonily} as the defendant pleaded for mercy.
e.zh: 法官面无表情地听着被告求情。

stoning.t: v. 用石头砸（stone 的现在分词）

e.en: Human rights groups condemn {stoning} as a form of punishment.
e.zh: 人权组织谴责把石刑作为一种惩罚方式。

e.en: {Stoning} olives before cooking removes the bitter pits.
e.zh: 烹饪前给橄榄去核可以去除苦味的果核。

stony.t:
adj. 多石的
adj. 冷漠的、无情的

e.en: She met his apology with {stony} silence and folded arms.
e.zh: 她对他的道歉报以冷冰冰的沉默和抱臂相对。

e.en: The trail turned narrow and {stony} near the summit.
e.zh: 靠近山顶时，小径变得狭窄且布满石头。

stood.t: v. 站立（stand 的过去式/过去分词）

e.en: She {stood} patiently in line for over an hour.
e.zh: 她耐心地在队伍里站了一个多小时。

e.en: The old lighthouse {stood} alone on the rocky cliff.
e.zh: 那座古老的灯塔孤零零地伫立在岩石峭壁上。

e.en: Critics called the new minister a {stooge} of the corporate lobby.
e.zh: 评论人士称这位新部长是企业游说团体的傀儡。

e.en: He felt like a {stooge} taking the blame for his boss.
e.zh: 他觉得自己像个替罪羊，替老板背了黑锅。

e.en: Farmers stacked the wheat into a tall {stook} to dry.
e.zh: 农民把麦子堆成高高的禾捆晾晒。

e.en: Each {stook} in the field held about a dozen sheaves.
e.zh: 田里每一堆禾束大约由十几把麦捆组成。

e.en: He pulled up a wooden {stool} and sat at the bar.
e.zh: 他拉过一张木凳，在吧台前坐下。

e.en: The doctor ordered a {stool} sample to check for infection.
e.zh: 医生要求做粪便检查以排查感染。

e.en: The kitchen island has four matching leather {stools}.
e.zh: 厨房岛台配有四把相同款式的皮凳。

e.en: Customers perched on tall {stools} along the cocktail counter.
e.zh: 客人们坐在鸡尾酒吧台旁的高脚凳上。

stoop.t:
v. 弯腰；俯身
n. 驼背

e.en: You'll have to {stoop} to get through this low doorway.
e.zh: 你得弯腰才能穿过这扇矮门。

e.en: I refuse to {stoop} to his level of name-calling.
e.zh: 我拒绝堕落到他那种人身攻击的水平。

stooped.t:
v. 弯腰（过去式）
adj. 驼背的

e.en: She {stooped} down to tie her child's shoelaces.
e.zh: 她弯下身去帮孩子系鞋带。

e.en: The {stooped} old man shuffled slowly along the sidewalk.
e.zh: 那个驼背的老人沿着人行道缓慢地挪着步子。

stop.t:
v. 停止；停下
n. 车站；停留

e.en: Please {stop} texting and pay attention to the road.
e.zh: 请别再发短信了，注意看路。

e.en: The next bus {stop} is right outside the library.
e.zh: 下一站公交车站就在图书馆门口。

e.en: Miners worked dangerous {stopes} deep beneath the mountain.
e.zh: 矿工们在山体深处危险的采掘场作业。

e.en: The collapsed {stopes} trapped several workers underground.
e.zh: 塌陷的采矿场把几名工人困在了地下。

stopgap.t: n. 权宜之计；临时替代品

e.en: Congress passed a {stopgap} bill to keep the government open.
e.zh: 国会通过了一项临时拨款法案以维持政府运转。

e.en: This patch is just a {stopgap} until the full update ships.
e.zh: 这个补丁只是权宜之计，等完整更新发布前用一下。

e.en: Turn left at the second {stoplight} after the bridge.
e.zh: 过桥后在第二个红绿灯左转。

e.en: The {stoplight} flashed red, warning drivers to slow down.
e.zh: 红绿灯闪着红光，提醒司机减速。

e.en: Our flight has a six-hour {stopover} in Tokyo.
e.zh: 我们的航班要在东京中转停留六小时。

e.en: We made a brief {stopover} in Paris before continuing to Rome.
e.zh: 我们在巴黎短暂停留后继续前往罗马。

e.en: Cheaper tickets often come with multiple {stopovers}.
e.zh: 便宜的机票往往要经过多次中转停留。

e.en: Long {stopovers} let travelers explore connecting cities for free.
e.zh: 长时间的经停让旅客可以免费游览中转城市。

e.en: The factory faced a week-long {stoppage} due to the strike.
e.zh: 由于罢工，工厂停工了一个星期。

e.en: A power {stoppage} disrupted trading on the exchange this morning.
e.zh: 今早一次断电中断了交易所的交易。

stopped.t: v. 停止（stop 的过去式）

e.en: She {stopped} working out after her knee injury last year.
e.zh: 去年膝盖受伤后她就停止了健身。

e.en: The taxi {stopped} right in front of the hotel entrance.
e.zh: 出租车正好停在了酒店门口。

stopper.t:
n. 瓶塞；终结者
v. 塞住

e.en: Push the cork {stopper} firmly back into the wine bottle.
e.zh: 把软木塞用力塞回葡萄酒瓶里。

e.en: That dress is a real show {stopper} at any party.
e.zh: 那条裙子在任何派对上都绝对吸睛。

stopping.t:
v. 停止（stop 的现在分词）
n. 停顿；填充物

e.en: There's no {stopping} her once she sets her mind to something.
e.zh: 她一旦下定决心，谁也拦不住。

e.en: We're {stopping} for coffee before heading to the airport.
e.zh: 我们去机场之前要先停下来喝杯咖啡。

stops.t:
v. 停止（第三人称单数）
n. 车站（复数）

e.en: This express train only {stops} at major stations.
e.zh: 这趟特快列车只停靠主要车站。

e.en: She pulled out all the {stops} to impress her new boss.
e.zh: 她使出了浑身解数想让新老板刮目相看。

e.en: The coach timed every sprint with his trusty {stopwatch}.
e.zh: 教练用他那只信赖的秒表给每次冲刺计时。

e.en: My phone has a {stopwatch} app I use during workouts.
e.zh: 我手机上有个秒表应用，健身时会用到。

e.en: The judges held identical {stopwatches} to verify the race time.
e.zh: 裁判们手持相同的秒表来核对比赛成绩。

e.en: Digital {stopwatches} have largely replaced mechanical ones in sports.
e.zh: 在体育运动中，数字秒表已基本取代了机械秒表。

storable.t: adj. 可储存的；可保存的

e.en: This folding chair is lightweight and easily {storable} in a closet.
e.zh: 这把折叠椅轻便，可以轻松收纳在衣柜里。

e.en: We need {storable} food supplies for the camping trip.
e.zh: 我们需要为这次露营准备便于储存的食物。

e.en: My phone ran out of {storage} after I downloaded the game.
e.zh: 下载那个游戏后，我手机的存储空间满了。

e.en: We rented a small {storage} unit for our extra furniture.
e.zh: 我们租了一个小型仓储单元来放多余的家具。

e.en: The company operates several cold {storages} for frozen goods.
e.zh: 该公司经营几座专门存放冷冻食品的冷库。

e.en: Cloud {storages} like Dropbox and iCloud sync files across devices.
e.zh: 像Dropbox和iCloud这样的云存储可在多设备间同步文件。

store.t:
n. 商店；应用商店
v. 储存

e.en: The corner {store} sells fresh bread every morning at six.
e.zh: 街角那家小店每天早上六点出售新鲜面包。

e.en: You can {store} leftovers in the fridge for three days.
e.zh: 剩菜可以在冰箱里存放三天。

stored.t:
v. 储存（store 的过去式）
adj. 已存储的

e.en: All her photos are {stored} safely in the cloud.
e.zh: 她所有的照片都安全地保存在云端。

e.en: We {stored} the Christmas decorations in the attic last week.
e.zh: 上周我们把圣诞装饰品收到了阁楼里。

e.en: The bakery's charming {storefront} attracts tourists all day long.
e.zh: 这家面包店迷人的店面整天都吸引着游客。

e.en: Many small businesses now run an online {storefront} on Shopify.
e.zh: 许多小企业现在都在Shopify上经营网店。

e.en: The library is a {storehouse} of knowledge about local history.
e.zh: 这座图书馆是关于当地历史的知识宝库。

e.en: Workers loaded grain sacks into the wooden {storehouse}.
e.zh: 工人们把一袋袋粮食搬进木制仓库。

e.en: The friendly {storekeeper} remembered every customer by name.
e.zh: 那位热情的店主能叫出每位顾客的名字。

e.en: My grandfather worked as a {storekeeper} in a small village.
e.zh: 我祖父曾在一个小村庄当店主。

e.en: The {storeman} checked each delivery against the warehouse inventory.
e.zh: 仓管员将每批送货与仓库库存逐一核对。

e.en: He worked night shifts as a {storeman} at the depot.
e.zh: 他在物流仓库上夜班，担任仓管员。

e.en: The chef keeps spare ingredients locked in the back {storeroom}.
e.zh: 厨师把备用食材锁在后面的储藏室里。

e.en: Old files filled every shelf in the office {storeroom}.
e.zh: 办公室储藏室的每个架子上都堆满了旧档案。

stores.t:
n. 商店（复数）
v. 储存（第三人称单数）

e.en: Most {stores} downtown close by nine on weeknights.
e.zh: 市中心大多数商店在工作日晚上九点前关门。

e.en: This app {stores} your passwords behind strong encryption.
e.zh: 这款应用会用强加密保存你的密码。

storey.t: n. 楼层（英式拼写，同 story）

e.en: They live in a charming two-{storey} house near the park.
e.zh: 他们住在公园附近一栋迷人的两层小楼里。

e.en: The fire started on the third {storey} of the building.
e.zh: 火灾从大楼的三层开始燃起。

storied.t: adj. 著名的；有传奇色彩的

e.en: Harvard has a {storied} history of producing world leaders.
e.zh: 哈佛在培养世界领袖方面有着辉煌的历史。

e.en: The {storied} stadium has hosted countless legendary matches.
e.zh: 这座著名的球场举办过无数场传奇比赛。

stories.t: n. 故事；动态（如 IG 限时动态）

e.en: Grandma told us spooky {stories} around the campfire.
e.zh: 奶奶在篝火旁给我们讲恐怖故事。

e.en: The skyscraper rises an impressive sixty {stories} into the sky.
e.zh: 这座摩天大楼高耸入云，足有令人惊叹的六十层。

storing.t: v. 储存（store 的现在分词）

e.en: I'm {storing} my winter coats in vacuum bags this summer.
e.zh: 今年夏天我用真空袋来收纳冬装大衣。

e.en: The app keeps {storing} cookies even after I delete them.
e.zh: 这个应用即使在我删除后还是会一直保存cookie。

e.en: A {stork} built its nest on top of the chimney.
e.zh: 一只鹳在烟囱顶上筑了巢。

e.en: In folklore, a {stork} delivers babies to new parents.
e.zh: 在民间传说中,鹳会把婴儿送给新生儿父母。

storm.t:
n. 风暴；暴风雨
v. 猛攻；闯入

e.en: A huge {storm} knocked out power across the city.
e.zh: 一场强烈的风暴让全城都断了电。

e.en: Her speech took social media by {storm}.
e.zh: 她的演讲在社交媒体上引起了轰动。

stormer.t: n. 猛攻者；出色的事物（罕用）

e.en: Their new album is an absolute {stormer}.
e.zh: 他们的新专辑简直棒极了。

e.en: That last match was a real {stormer}.
e.zh: 上一场比赛真是精彩绝伦。

storming.t:
v. 猛攻（storm 的现在分词）
adj. 迅猛的

e.en: He came {storming} into the office demanding answers.
e.zh: 他怒气冲冲地冲进办公室要个说法。

e.en: The team is having a {storming} season so far.
e.zh: 这支球队本赛季到目前为止势如破竹。

stormont.t: n. 斯托蒙特（北爱尔兰议会所在地）

e.en: Talks resumed at {Stormont} after months of political deadlock.
e.zh: 经过数月的政治僵局后，斯托蒙特恢复了会谈。

e.en: The new bill was debated inside {Stormont} yesterday afternoon.
e.zh: 昨天下午，新法案在斯托蒙特进行了辩论。

storms.t:
n. 风暴（复数）
v. 猛攻（第三人称单数）

e.en: Tropical {storms} are becoming more frequent along the coast.
e.zh: 沿海地区的热带风暴越来越频繁。

e.en: She {storms} out of the meeting whenever criticized.
e.zh: 每当受到批评，她就怒气冲冲地离开会议。

e.en: The city upgraded its {stormwater} drainage system last summer.
e.zh: 该市去年夏天升级了雨水排放系统。

e.en: Heavy rain overwhelmed the old {stormwater} pipes downtown.
e.zh: 暴雨让市中心老旧的雨水管道不堪重负。

e.en: They had a {stormy} relationship that ended badly.
e.zh: 他们的感情风风雨雨，最后不欢而散。

e.en: The flight was canceled due to {stormy} weather.
e.zh: 由于天气恶劣，航班被取消了。

stornoway.t: n. 斯托诺韦（苏格兰地名）

e.en: The ferry to {Stornoway} runs twice daily in summer.
e.zh: 夏天去斯托诺韦的渡轮每天两班。

e.en: She grew up in {Stornoway} on the Isle of Lewis.
e.zh: 她在刘易斯岛的斯托诺韦长大。

storr.t: n. 斯托尔（地名/人名，如 Old Man of Storr）

e.en: Hikers climbed the Old Man of {Storr} at sunrise.
e.zh: 徒步者在日出时攀登了斯托尔老人岩。

e.en: The {Storr} is one of Skye's most photographed landmarks.
e.zh: 斯托尔岩是斯凯岛最常被拍摄的地标之一。

story.t:
n. 故事；报道
n. 楼层

e.en: Grandma told us a bedtime {story} every night.
e.zh: 奶奶每晚都给我们讲一个睡前故事。

e.en: The journalist broke the {story} on social media first.
e.zh: 那位记者先在社交媒体上披露了这条新闻。

e.en: The director sketched a quick {storyboard} for the chase scene.
e.zh: 导演为追逐戏快速画了一份分镜脚本。

e.en: We use Figma to {storyboard} new app features.
e.zh: 我们用 Figma 为新功能制作分镜。

storybook.t:
n. 故事书
adj. 童话般的

e.en: Their wedding felt like a {storybook} fairy tale.
e.zh: 他们的婚礼宛如童话故事一般。

e.en: She read the children a colorful {storybook} before nap.
e.zh: 她在午睡前给孩子们读了一本彩色童话书。

storyline.t: n. 故事情节；剧情主线

e.en: The game's {storyline} branches based on your choices.
e.zh: 这款游戏的剧情会根据你的选择产生分支。

e.en: Critics praised the show's tight, suspenseful {storyline}.
e.zh: 评论家称赞这部剧情紧凑、扣人心弦。

storyteller.t: n. 讲故事的人；说书人

e.en: My uncle is a gifted {storyteller} at family dinners.
e.zh: 我叔叔在家庭聚餐时是个很会讲故事的人。

e.en: The brand hired a {storyteller} to humanize its marketing.
e.zh: 品牌聘请了一位故事讲述者，让营销更有人情味。

e.en: Indigenous {storytellers} preserve history through oral tradition.
e.zh: 原住民的故事讲述者通过口述传统保存历史。

e.en: Great {storytellers} make even data sound exciting.
e.zh: 优秀的故事讲述者能让枯燥的数据也变得引人入胜。

e.en: Good {storytelling} is essential for memorable brand campaigns.
e.zh: 好的故事讲述对令人难忘的品牌活动至关重要。

e.en: The workshop teaches {storytelling} techniques for product designers.
e.zh: 该工作坊教授面向产品设计师的故事叙述技巧。

e.en: He commutes from {Stoughton} into Boston every morning.
e.zh: 他每天早上从斯托顿通勤到波士顿。

e.en: {Stoughton} hosts a small farmers' market on weekends.
e.zh: 斯托顿周末有一个小型农贸市场。

e.en: Worshippers dipped their fingers in the holy water {stoup}.
e.zh: 信徒们将手指浸入圣水钵中。

e.en: A marble {stoup} stood near the church entrance.
e.zh: 教堂入口附近放着一个大理石圣水钵。

stour.t: n. 斯陶尔河（英国河名）

e.en: The river {Stour} winds gently through the English countryside.
e.zh: 斯陶尔河蜿蜒流经英格兰乡间。

e.en: Anglers love fishing along the {Stour} in summer.
e.zh: 垂钓者夏天喜欢在斯陶尔河边钓鱼。

stourbridge.t: n. 斯陶尔布里奇（英国地名）

e.en: {Stourbridge} was once famous for its glassmaking industry.
e.zh: 斯陶尔布里奇曾以玻璃制造业闻名。

e.en: We took the train from Birmingham to {Stourbridge}.
e.zh: 我们从伯明翰乘火车到斯陶尔布里奇。

stout.t:
adj. 结实的；矮胖的
n. 烈性黑啤

e.en: He poured himself a pint of creamy Irish {stout}.
e.zh: 他给自己倒了一品脱顺滑的爱尔兰黑啤。

e.en: The hiker wore {stout} boots for the rocky trail.
e.zh: 徒步者穿着结实的靴子走崎岖的小径。

e.en: Only the {stouthearted} dared cross the frozen pass.
e.zh: 只有勇敢无畏的人才敢翻越那冰封的山口。

e.en: She gave a {stouthearted} speech defending her team.
e.zh: 她发表了一番坚定有力的演讲，为团队辩护。

e.en: He {stoutly} denied any involvement in the scandal.
e.zh: 他坚决否认与该丑闻有任何关联。

e.en: The company {stoutly} defended its pricing decisions.
e.zh: 公司坚定地为自己的定价决策辩护。

e.en: Don't leave the {stove} on when you go out.
e.zh: 出门时别让炉子开着。

e.en: I'm shopping for an induction {stove} for the kitchen.
e.zh: 我正在为厨房选购一台电磁炉。

e.en: Smoke rose from the rusty {stovepipe} on the cabin roof.
e.zh: 小屋屋顶生锈的烟囱管冒着烟。

e.en: He wore a tall {stovepipe} hat to the costume party.
e.zh: 他戴着一顶高高的烟囱礼帽参加变装派对。

e.en: Farmers feed corn {stover} to cattle during winter.
e.zh: 农民冬天用玉米秸秆喂牛。

e.en: Baled {stover} sat at the edge of the harvested field.
e.zh: 打捆好的秸秆堆在收割完的田地边上。

e.en: Modern induction {stoves} heat pans much faster than gas.
e.zh: 现代电磁炉加热锅具比燃气灶快得多。

e.en: Camping {stoves} make cooking outdoors much easier.
e.zh: 露营炉让户外做饭方便多了。

e.en: Please {stow} your luggage in the overhead bin.
e.zh: 请将行李放入头顶的行李架内。

e.en: Sailors learn to {stow} ropes neatly on deck.
e.zh: 水手们学会把绳索整齐地收放在甲板上。

e.en: The cabin offers plenty of {stowage} for carry-on bags.
e.zh: 机舱内有充足的空间存放随身行李。

e.en: Proper cargo {stowage} keeps the ship balanced at sea.
e.zh: 妥善的货物配载能让船在海上保持平衡。

e.en: A {stowaway} was discovered hiding in the cargo hold.
e.zh: 一名偷渡者被发现藏在货舱里。

e.en: The young {stowaway} hoped to reach America by ship.
e.zh: 那个年轻的偷渡者希望乘船到达美国。

e.en: Harriet Beecher {Stowe} wrote Uncle Tom's Cabin in 1852.
e.zh: 哈里特·比彻·斯托于1852年写了《汤姆叔叔的小屋》。

e.en: We spent the weekend skiing in {Stowe}, Vermont.
e.zh: 我们在佛蒙特州的斯托度过了滑雪的周末。

e.en: The pediatrician diagnosed mild {strabismus} in the toddler.
e.zh: 儿科医生诊断这名幼儿有轻度斜视。

e.en: Surgery can correct {strabismus} in most young patients.
e.zh: 手术可以矫正大多数小患者的斜视。

e.en: We strolled down a narrow {strada} in old Rome.
e.zh: 我们在古罗马的一条窄巷里漫步。

e.en: The cafe sits on a quiet {strada} near the cathedral.
e.zh: 那家咖啡馆位于大教堂附近的一条幽静小街上。

straddle.t:
v. 跨立；横跨
n. 跨式期权

e.en: The bridge {straddles} the river between two countries.
e.zh: 那座桥横跨两国之间的河流。

e.en: Many startups {straddle} both consumer and enterprise markets.
e.zh: 许多初创公司同时跨足消费者和企业市场。

stradivarius.t: n. 斯特拉迪瓦里名琴

e.en: The soloist played a priceless {Stradivarius} violin.
e.zh: 独奏者演奏了一把无价的斯特拉迪瓦里小提琴。

e.en: Only a few hundred genuine {Stradivarius} instruments still exist.
e.zh: 如今真正的斯特拉迪瓦里乐器仅存几百件。

e.en: Fighter jets would {strafe} enemy positions at dawn.
e.zh: 战斗机会在黎明时低空扫射敌方阵地。

e.en: The pilot was ordered to {strafe} the supply convoy.
e.zh: 飞行员奉命对补给车队进行扫射。

strafford.t: n. 斯特拉福德（姓氏/地名）

e.en: The Earl of {Strafford} was executed in 1641.
e.zh: 斯特拉福德伯爵于1641年被处决。

e.en: {Strafford} County is in southeastern New Hampshire.
e.zh: 斯特拉福德县位于新罕布什尔州东南部。

e.en: Tired hikers began to {straggle} behind the main group.
e.zh: 疲惫的徒步者开始落在大队伍后面。

e.en: A few protesters continued to {straggle} along the avenue.
e.zh: 几个抗议者仍三三两两地走在大街上。

e.en: The teacher waited for the last {straggler} to arrive.
e.zh: 老师等着最后一个掉队的学生到来。

e.en: One {straggler} from the marathon crossed at sunset.
e.zh: 马拉松中一名落后者在日落时才冲过终点。

e.en: A few {straggling} customers entered just before closing.
e.zh: 几个零零散散的顾客在关门前才进来。

e.en: His {straggling} beard made him look untidy.
e.zh: 他那稀疏散乱的胡子让他显得邋遢。

e.en: The puppy had {straggly} fur after playing in the rain.
e.zh: 小狗在雨中玩耍后毛变得乱糟糟的。

e.en: He brushed his {straggly} hair out of his eyes.
e.zh: 他把凌乱的头发从眼前拨开。

straight.t:
adj. 笔直的；直接的
adv. 直接；径直

e.en: Just go {straight} down this road for two blocks.
e.zh: 沿着这条路直走两个街区。

e.en: Tell me the {straight} truth about what happened.
e.zh: 把发生的事直截了当地告诉我。

straightaway.t:
adv. 立即
n. 直道

e.en: I'll send the report over {straightaway} after lunch.
e.zh: 午饭后我马上把报告发过去。

e.en: The car accelerated down the long {straightaway}.
e.zh: 汽车在长长的直道上加速行驶。

e.en: Use a {straightedge} when cutting along that line.
e.zh: 沿那条线裁切时请用直尺。

e.en: The carpenter checked the board with a metal {straightedge}.
e.zh: 木匠用金属直尺检查木板。

e.en: Let me {straighten} the picture frame on the wall.
e.zh: 让我把墙上的相框摆正。

e.en: You should {straighten} your back while sitting at the desk.
e.zh: 坐在桌前时你应该挺直背部。

e.en: She {straightened} her tie before the interview began.
e.zh: 面试开始前，她整理了一下领带。

e.en: He {straightened} up when the manager walked in.
e.zh: 经理走进来时，他立刻挺直了身子。

e.en: She's {straightening} her hair before the wedding ceremony.
e.zh: 她在婚礼前把头发拉直。

e.en: He spent the morning {straightening} up his messy desk.
e.zh: 他花了一上午整理凌乱的办公桌。

straightens.t: v. 弄直（第三人称单数）

e.en: The road {straightens} out once you pass the bridge.
e.zh: 过了桥之后，路就变直了。

e.en: She always {straightens} her desk before leaving the office.
e.zh: 她下班前总会把办公桌整理好。

straightforward.t: adj. 直截了当的；简单明了的

e.en: The setup process is pretty {straightforward}, even for beginners.
e.zh: 设置过程相当简单，新手也能上手。

e.en: I appreciate her {straightforward} feedback during reviews.
e.zh: 我很欣赏她在评审时直率的反馈。

e.en: She answered the reporter's question {straightforwardly} and honestly.
e.zh: 她直截了当、诚实地回答了记者的问题。

e.en: The instructions explain the setup process {straightforwardly}.
e.zh: 说明书把安装过程讲得清清楚楚。

e.en: I appreciated her {straightforwardness} during the difficult conversation.
e.zh: 我很欣赏她在那场艰难谈话中的直率。

e.en: His {straightforwardness} sometimes comes across as blunt to strangers.
e.zh: 他的直率有时让陌生人觉得过于直接。

e.en: Strict regulations can be a {straightjacket} for small startups.
e.zh: 严苛的监管对小型创业公司来说可能是束缚。

e.en: The patient was placed in a {straightjacket} for safety.
e.zh: 出于安全考虑,病人被穿上了束身衣。

e.en: Carpenters check the {straightness} of each board before cutting.
e.zh: 木匠在锯切前会检查每块木板是否平直。

e.en: The {straightness} of the road made it perfect for cycling.
e.zh: 这条路笔直,非常适合骑行。

e.en: She {straightway} apologized after realizing her mistake.
e.zh: 意识到错误后她立刻道歉了。

e.en: He went {straightway} to the manager with the complaint.
e.zh: 他径直去找经理投诉。

strain.t:
n. 压力；拉力
v. 拉紧；劳损

e.en: The long hours put a {strain} on his marriage.
e.zh: 长时间的工作给他的婚姻带来了压力。

e.en: Don't {strain} your eyes by reading in dim light.
e.zh: 别在昏暗的光线下读书伤眼睛。

e.en: Their relationship has been {strained} since the argument.
e.zh: 那次争吵后他们的关系一直很紧张。

e.en: She gave a {strained} smile when asked about work.
e.zh: 被问起工作时她勉强地笑了笑。

e.en: Pour the pasta through a {strainer} to drain the water.
e.zh: 把意面倒进滤网里把水沥干。

e.en: I bought a small {strainer} for loose-leaf tea.
e.zh: 我买了个小滤网用来泡散装茶叶。

straining.t: v. 拉紧；过滤（strain 的现在分词）

e.en: The dog was {straining} at the leash to chase the cat.
e.zh: 那只狗使劲拽着绳子想追猫。

e.en: He sat {straining} to hear the quiet conversation.
e.zh: 他坐着竭力想听清那段轻声的对话。

strains.t:
n. 压力（复数）
v. 拉紧（第三人称单数）

e.en: The new project {strains} our limited resources.
e.zh: 这个新项目让我们有限的资源更加紧张。

e.en: Faint {strains} of music drifted from the next room.
e.zh: 隔壁房间飘来微弱的音乐声。

strait.t:
n. 海峡
adj. 困难的

e.en: Ships pass through the {strait} between the two islands.
e.zh: 船只从两座岛之间的海峡穿过。

e.en: The Bering {strait} separates Russia from Alaska.
e.zh: 白令海峡将俄罗斯与阿拉斯加分隔开。

e.en: The family lived in {straitened} circumstances after the layoff.
e.zh: 裁员后这家人生活变得拮据。

e.en: Many retirees face {straitened} finances in old age.
e.zh: 许多退休者晚年都面临经济困窘。

e.en: The patient was put in a {straitjacket} for his safety.
e.zh: 为了安全起见,病人被套上了束身衣。

e.en: Strict rules can be a {straitjacket} on creativity.
e.zh: 严苛的规定会成为束缚创造力的枷锁。

e.en: The company is in dire {straits} after losing its biggest client.
e.zh: 失去最大客户后,公司陷入了困境。

e.en: Many small businesses found themselves in financial {straits}.
e.zh: 许多小企业发现自己陷入了财务困境。

e.en: The boat's lower {strake} was damaged after hitting the rocks.
e.zh: 船底的一条壳板撞到礁石后损坏了。

e.en: Workers replaced a rotten {strake} on the wooden hull.
e.zh: 工人们更换了木船体上一块腐烂的壳板。

strand.t:
n. 一股；一缕
v. 使搁浅

e.en: A {strand} of hair fell across her forehead.
e.zh: 一缕头发垂落在她的额前。

e.en: We walked along the {strand} at sunset.
e.zh: 我们在日落时分沿着海滩漫步。

e.en: Hundreds of passengers were {stranded} at the airport overnight.
e.zh: 数百名旅客被困在机场过了一夜。

e.en: The car broke down and left us {stranded} on the highway.
e.zh: 汽车抛锚把我们困在了高速公路上。

stranding.t: v. 使搁浅（strand 的现在分词）

e.en: The storm caused the {stranding} of dozens of whales.
e.zh: 风暴导致数十头鲸鱼搁浅。

e.en: Flight cancellations are {stranding} travelers across Europe.
e.zh: 航班取消使欧洲各地的旅客滞留。

e.en: She tied several {strands} of beads around her neck.
e.zh: 她在脖子上戴了好几串珠子。

e.en: The novel weaves together three different {strands} of plot.
e.zh: 这部小说把三条不同的情节线交织在一起。

e.en: I had a {strange} dream about flying last night.
e.zh: 我昨晚做了个关于飞翔的奇怪梦。

e.en: It feels {strange} to be back in my old school.
e.zh: 回到母校感觉有点不真实。

strangelove.t: n. 奇爱博士（电影人名）

e.en: Kubrick's Dr. {Strangelove} is a classic Cold War satire.
e.zh: 库布里克的《奇爱博士》是一部冷战时期的经典讽刺片。

e.en: He quoted Dr. {Strangelove} during the political debate.
e.zh: 他在政治辩论中引用了《奇爱博士》。

e.en: The cat has been acting {strangely} since we moved.
e.zh: 自从搬家后那只猫举止就很怪。

e.en: {Strangely}, no one remembered her birthday this year.
e.zh: 奇怪的是,今年没人记得她的生日。

e.en: There was a certain {strangeness} about the empty house.
e.zh: 那栋空房子里透着一种说不出的诡异感。

e.en: I love the {strangeness} of his short stories.
e.zh: 我喜欢他短篇小说里那种奇异的味道。

e.en: Don't accept rides from a {stranger}.
e.zh: 别接受陌生人搭的便车。

e.en: A friendly {stranger} helped me find the train station.
e.zh: 一位友善的陌生人帮我找到了火车站。

e.en: The two {strangers} struck up a conversation on the plane.
e.zh: 两个陌生人在飞机上聊了起来。

e.en: Online, we often share secrets with complete {strangers}.
e.zh: 在网上,我们常常会向完全陌生的人吐露秘密。

strangford.t: n. 斯特兰福德（北爱尔兰地名）

e.en: {Strangford} Lough is a beautiful inlet in Northern Ireland.
e.zh: 斯特兰福德湖是北爱尔兰一处美丽的海湾。

e.en: We took a ferry across {Strangford} Lough yesterday.
e.zh: 昨天我们乘渡船穿过了斯特兰福德湖。

e.en: The vines threatened to {strangle} the young tree.
e.zh: 那些藤蔓眼看就要把小树缠死。

e.en: Heavy taxes can {strangle} small businesses.
e.zh: 沉重的税负会扼杀小企业。

strangled.t: v. 被勒死（strangle 的过去式）

e.en: He let out a {strangled} cry of frustration.
e.zh: 他发出一声压抑的沮丧叫喊。

e.en: Red tape has {strangled} innovation in the industry.
e.zh: 繁琐的官僚程序扼杀了这个行业的创新。

e.en: The company has a {stranglehold} on the local market.
e.zh: 这家公司对当地市场形成了垄断式的控制。

e.en: Political corruption maintained a {stranglehold} on the country.
e.zh: 政治腐败牢牢掌控着这个国家。

e.en: Police are searching for the {strangler} who attacked two women.
e.zh: 警方正在追查袭击两名女子的勒颈者。

e.en: The {strangler} fig grows around and kills its host tree.
e.zh: 绞杀榕会缠绕宿主树并将其杀死。

strangles.t: n. 马腺疫（马的传染病）

e.en: Excessive regulation often {strangles} startup growth.
e.zh: 过度的监管常常会扼杀初创企业的发展。

e.en: The vet diagnosed the horse with {strangles}.
e.zh: 兽医诊断那匹马患了马腺疫。

e.en: High rents are {strangling} small shops downtown.
e.zh: 高昂的租金正在扼杀市中心的小店铺。

e.en: He loosened the tie that was {strangling} him.
e.zh: 他松开了勒得他喘不过气的领带。

e.en: A {strangulated} hernia requires emergency surgery.
e.zh: 嵌顿性疝气需要紧急手术。

e.en: She spoke in a {strangulated} voice through her tears.
e.zh: 她哽咽着用嘶哑的声音说话。

e.en: The autopsy revealed death by {strangulation}.
e.zh: 尸检显示死因是窒息。

e.en: Excessive regulation led to economic {strangulation}.
e.zh: 过度的监管导致了经济的窒息。

strap.t:
n. 带子；皮带
v. 捆绑

e.en: The {strap} of my bag broke on the way home.
e.zh: 我包的肩带在回家路上断了。

e.en: Please {strap} the child into the car seat.
e.zh: 请把孩子用安全带固定在儿童座椅上。

e.en: She wore a {strapless} black dress to the gala.
e.zh: 她穿了一件无肩带的黑色礼服去参加晚会。

e.en: The bride chose an elegant {strapless} gown.
e.zh: 新娘选了一件优雅的无肩带礼服。

strapped.t:
adj. 手头紧的
v. 捆绑

e.en: I'm a bit {strapped} for cash this month.
e.zh: 我这个月手头有点紧。

e.en: He {strapped} the surfboard to the roof of the car.
e.zh: 他把冲浪板绑在了车顶上。

strapping.t:
adj. 强壮的
n. 绑带

e.en: Their son grew into a {strapping} young man.
e.zh: 他们的儿子长成了一个高大健壮的小伙子。

e.en: She was {strapping} the luggage onto the bike rack.
e.zh: 她正把行李捆在自行车货架上。

e.en: She wore {strappy} sandals with her summer dress.
e.zh: 她搭配夏裙穿了一双细带凉鞋。

e.en: The {strappy} top is perfect for hot weather.
e.zh: 这件细带上衣很适合热天穿。

e.en: Adjust the {straps} on your backpack for comfort.
e.zh: 调整一下背包的肩带会更舒服。

e.en: The watch comes with two interchangeable {straps}.
e.zh: 这块手表配有两条可更换的表带。

strasbourg.t: n. 斯特拉斯堡（法国城市）

e.en: The European Parliament meets in {Strasbourg} each month.
e.zh: 欧洲议会每月都在斯特拉斯堡开会。

e.en: We spent the weekend visiting {Strasbourg}'s Christmas market.
e.zh: 我们周末去逛了斯特拉斯堡的圣诞集市。

e.en: Their apartment is on a quiet {strasse} in Berlin.
e.zh: 他们的公寓位于柏林一条安静的街道上。

e.en: The famous Friedrich{strasse} runs through central Berlin.
e.zh: 著名的腓特烈大街贯穿柏林市中心。

strat.t: n. 芬达 Strat 吉他；策略缩写

e.en: He plays a vintage Fender {Strat} in his band.
e.zh: 他在乐队里弹一把老款的芬达Strat吉他。

e.en: The {Strat} is one of the most iconic electric guitars.
e.zh: Strat是最具代表性的电吉他之一。

strata.t: n. 地层；阶层（stratum 复数）

e.en: Geologists studied the rock {strata} in the canyon walls.
e.zh: 地质学家研究了峡谷壁上的岩层。

e.en: The survey covers all social {strata} of the city.
e.zh: 这项调查涵盖了城市的所有社会阶层。

e.en: The general devised a clever {stratagem} to defeat the enemy.
e.zh: 将军设计了一个巧妙的计策来击败敌人。

e.en: Her {stratagem} for getting promoted finally worked.
e.zh: 她为升职想出的计策终于奏效了。

e.en: The company made a {strategic} decision to enter Asia.
e.zh: 公司做出了进军亚洲的战略决定。

e.en: Singapore is in a {strategic} location for trade.
e.zh: 新加坡处于贸易的战略要地。

e.en: He took a {strategical} approach to negotiating his salary.
e.zh: 他用一种讲究策略的方式来谈薪水。

e.en: The general weighed every {strategical} option carefully.
e.zh: 将军仔细权衡了每一个战略选择。

e.en: The shop is {strategically} located near the train station.
e.zh: 这家店选址很有策略,就在火车站附近。

e.en: She {strategically} placed her resume on top of the pile.
e.zh: 她有策略地把简历放在了最上面。

e.en: We need new marketing {strategies} to reach younger users.
e.zh: 我们需要新的营销策略来吸引年轻用户。

e.en: Teachers shared coping {strategies} for online learning.
e.zh: 老师们分享了应对在线学习的策略。

e.en: She's a brilliant political {strategist} for the campaign.
e.zh: 她是这次竞选活动中一位出色的政治策略家。

e.en: The CEO hired a digital marketing {strategist}.
e.zh: 首席执行官聘请了一位数字营销策略师。

e.en: Let's meet tomorrow to {strategize} about the launch.
e.zh: 我们明天碰面商量一下产品发布的策略吧。

e.en: The team gathered to {strategize} their next move.
e.zh: 团队聚在一起谋划下一步行动。

e.en: Our long-term {strategy} focuses on customer retention.
e.zh: 我们的长期战略重点是留住客户。

e.en: What's your {strategy} for studying for the exam?
e.zh: 你备考的策略是什么?

stratford.t: n. 斯特拉特福（英国地名）

e.en: Shakespeare was born in {Stratford}-upon-Avon.
e.zh: 莎士比亚出生于埃文河畔的斯特拉特福。

e.en: We took a day trip to {Stratford} to see a play.
e.zh: 我们去斯特拉特福一日游看了一场戏。

strath.t: n. 宽阔的河谷（苏格兰）

e.en: The cottage sits in a wide Scottish {strath}.
e.zh: 那间小屋坐落在苏格兰一片开阔的河谷里。

e.en: Sheep grazed peacefully across the green {strath}.
e.zh: 羊群在绿色的河谷里安静地吃草。

strathallan.t: n. 斯特拉萨兰（苏格兰地名）

e.en: He grew up near {Strathallan} in central Scotland.
e.zh: 他在苏格兰中部斯特拉萨兰附近长大。

e.en: The {Strathallan} estate hosts an annual airshow each summer.
e.zh: 斯特拉萨兰庄园每年夏天举办航空展。

strathclyde.t: n. 斯特拉斯克莱德（苏格兰地区）

e.en: She studies engineering at the University of {Strathclyde}.
e.zh: 她在斯特拉斯克莱德大学读工程专业。

e.en: {Strathclyde} was once a major industrial region of Scotland.
e.zh: 斯特拉斯克莱德曾是苏格兰重要的工业区。

strathmore.t: n. 斯特拉斯莫尔（苏格兰地名）

e.en: The town of {Strathmore} sits in a fertile farming valley.
e.zh: 斯特拉斯莫尔镇坐落在一片肥沃的农业山谷中。

e.en: Artists love {Strathmore} paper for its smooth texture.
e.zh: 画家们喜爱斯特拉斯莫尔纸张细腻的质地。

strathspey.t: n. 斯特拉斯佩（苏格兰舞曲）

e.en: The band played a lively {strathspey} after dinner.
e.zh: 乐队在晚餐后演奏了一支欢快的斯特拉斯佩舞曲。

e.en: A {strathspey} is slower than a reel but equally Scottish.
e.zh: 斯特拉斯佩舞比里尔舞慢,但同样具有苏格兰风情。

e.en: Social {stratification} remains a major issue in modern cities.
e.zh: 社会分层仍是现代城市的一大问题。

e.en: The lake shows clear thermal {stratification} in summer.
e.zh: 这片湖泊在夏季呈现出明显的温度分层。

stratified.t: adj. 分层的；按阶层划分的

e.en: Researchers used a {stratified} sample to ensure fair representation.
e.zh: 研究人员采用分层抽样以确保代表性公平。

e.en: The cliff revealed beautifully {stratified} layers of ancient rock.
e.zh: 悬崖上露出层次分明的古老岩石。

stratify.t: v. 使分层；使形成阶层

e.en: The study aims to {stratify} patients by risk level.
e.zh: 该研究旨在按风险等级对患者进行分层。

e.en: Cold winters can {stratify} the water in deep lakes.
e.zh: 寒冷的冬天会使深湖的水形成分层。

e.en: Geologists made a detailed {stratigraphic} map of the canyon.
e.zh: 地质学家绘制了峡谷详细的地层图。

e.en: The fossils were dated using {stratigraphic} analysis.
e.zh: 这些化石通过地层分析进行了年代测定。

e.en: The team published a {stratigraphical} survey of the basin.
e.zh: 团队发表了该盆地的地层学调查报告。

e.en: Each rock layer has its own {stratigraphical} significance.
e.zh: 每一层岩石都有其独特的地层学意义。

e.en: {Stratigraphy} helps scientists understand Earth's geological history.
e.zh: 地层学帮助科学家了解地球的地质历史。

e.en: Archaeologists use {stratigraphy} to date ancient settlement layers.
e.zh: 考古学家利用地层学来确定古代聚落各层的年代。

e.en: Ozone in the {stratosphere} protects us from harmful UV rays.
e.zh: 平流层中的臭氧保护我们免受有害紫外线伤害。

e.en: Her startup's valuation has shot into the {stratosphere}.
e.zh: 她创业公司的估值已经飙升到天上去了。

e.en: Different planets have very different {stratospheres} from Earth's.
e.zh: 不同行星的平流层与地球的差异极大。

e.en: Salaries in tech reach {stratospheres} ordinary workers can't imagine.
e.zh: 科技行业的薪水高得普通打工人难以想象。

e.en: Housing prices in the city have reached {stratospheric} levels.
e.zh: 这座城市的房价已经高得离谱。

e.en: Scientists monitor {stratospheric} ozone levels using satellites.
e.zh: 科学家利用卫星监测平流层的臭氧水平。

stratton.t: n. 斯特拉顿（人名/地名）

e.en: {Stratton} is a popular ski resort in southern Vermont.
e.zh: 斯特拉顿是佛蒙特州南部一个热门的滑雪胜地。

e.en: Mr. {Stratton} has taught at this school for thirty years.
e.zh: 斯特拉顿先生在这所学校任教已经三十年。

e.en: This rock {stratum} dates back over a million years.
e.zh: 这层岩层可以追溯到一百多万年前。

e.en: The policy targets a specific economic {stratum} of society.
e.zh: 该政策针对的是社会中特定的经济阶层。

e.en: A thick {stratus} cloud covered the sky all morning.
e.zh: 一层厚厚的层云笼罩了整个上午的天空。

e.en: Low {stratus} often brings light drizzle in coastal areas.
e.zh: 低层的层云常给沿海地区带来毛毛雨。

e.en: She sipped her smoothie through a paper {straw}.
e.zh: 她用纸吸管喝着冰沙。

e.en: The horses slept on a thick bed of {straw}.
e.zh: 马儿睡在厚厚的稻草堆上。

e.en: We picked fresh {strawberries} at the farm last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末我们在农场摘了新鲜的草莓。

e.en: These {strawberries} are sweeter than the ones from yesterday.
e.zh: 这些草莓比昨天的更甜。

e.en: I ordered a {strawberry} milkshake with extra whipped cream.
e.zh: 我点了一杯加奶油的草莓奶昔。

e.en: A single {strawberry} sat on top of the cheesecake.
e.zh: 芝士蛋糕上放着一颗草莓。

e.en: Many cafes have switched from plastic to bamboo {straws}.
e.zh: 许多咖啡店已从塑料吸管换成了竹制吸管。

e.en: He's just grasping at {straws} to defend his argument.
e.zh: 他只是在抓救命稻草来为自己的观点辩护。

stray.t:
v. 走失；偏离
adj. 走失的；零星的

e.en: A {stray} cat has been sleeping on our porch.
e.zh: 有一只流浪猫一直睡在我们家门廊上。

e.en: Try not to let your mind {stray} during the meeting.
e.zh: 开会时尽量别让自己走神。

e.en: The hikers {strayed} from the trail and got lost.
e.zh: 徒步者偏离了小径,结果迷了路。

e.en: His attention {strayed} as the lecture grew tedious.
e.zh: 讲座变得乏味,他的注意力开始游离。

e.en: The teacher noticed students {straying} from the assigned topic.
e.zh: 老师注意到学生们偏离了指定的主题。

e.en: Keep the dog leashed to prevent it from {straying}.
e.zh: 把狗拴好,免得它走丢。

strays.t:
n. 流浪动物
v. 走失（第三人称）

e.en: The shelter takes in dozens of {strays} every month.
e.zh: 这家收容所每月会收留数十只流浪动物。

e.en: Her mind often {strays} during long video calls.
e.zh: 开长时间的视频会议时,她常常走神。

streak.t:
n. 条纹；连胜/连败
v. 飞奔

e.en: The team is on a six-game winning {streak}.
e.zh: 这支球队正处于六连胜的势头中。

e.en: A {streak} of paint ran down the freshly painted wall.
e.zh: 一道油漆痕迹顺着刚刷好的墙壁流了下来。

streaked.t:
adj. 有条纹的
v. 飞奔（过去式）

e.en: Tears {streaked} down her face during the goodbye.
e.zh: 告别时,泪水从她脸颊上滑落。

e.en: The sky was {streaked} with pink and orange at sunset.
e.zh: 日落时分,天空被染上了粉色和橙色的条纹。

e.en: Lightning kept {streaking} across the dark stormy sky.
e.zh: 闪电不停地划过黑暗的暴风雨天空。

e.en: Rain was {streaking} the windows of the speeding train.
e.zh: 雨水在飞驰的列车窗户上划出道道水痕。

streaky.t: adj. 有条纹的；不均匀的

e.en: The window cleaner left a {streaky} finish on the glass.
e.zh: 擦窗工人把玻璃擦得满是水痕。

e.en: He fried up some crispy {streaky} bacon for breakfast.
e.zh: 他煎了一些香脆的五花培根当早餐。

stream.t:
n. 小溪；数据流
v. 流媒体播放

e.en: Millions of fans {stream} the show on opening night.
e.zh: 数百万粉丝在首播之夜在线观看这部剧。

e.en: A small {stream} runs through the back of the garden.
e.zh: 花园后面有一条小溪流过。

e.en: The drought left the {streambed} completely dry and cracked.
e.zh: 干旱使河床彻底干涸开裂。

e.en: Smooth pebbles lined the shallow {streambed} below the bridge.
e.zh: 桥下浅浅的河床上铺满了光滑的鹅卵石。

streamed.t: v. 流媒体播放（过去式）

e.en: The concert was {streamed} live to fans worldwide.
e.zh: 这场演唱会向全球粉丝进行了直播。

e.en: Sunlight {streamed} through the cracks in the curtains.
e.zh: 阳光从窗帘的缝隙间倾泻而入。

e.en: The {streamer} has over a million followers on Twitch.
e.zh: 这位主播在 Twitch 上拥有超过一百万粉丝。

e.en: A red paper {streamer} hung above the birthday table.
e.zh: 生日餐桌上方挂着一条红色的纸彩带。

e.en: Most families now subscribe to several {streaming} services.
e.zh: 如今大多数家庭都订阅了好几家流媒体服务。

e.en: Tears were {streaming} down her cheeks during the speech.
e.zh: 演讲时,泪水顺着她的脸颊不停地流下。

e.en: The new software helps {streamline} our checkout process.
e.zh: 新软件帮助简化了我们的结账流程。

e.en: Managers want to {streamline} approvals to save everyone time.
e.zh: 管理层希望简化审批流程,为大家节省时间。

e.en: The app has a {streamlined} interface that's easy to use.
e.zh: 这款应用界面简洁,使用起来很方便。

e.en: They {streamlined} operations and cut delivery times in half.
e.zh: 他们精简了运营流程,把送货时间缩短了一半。

e.en: The vintage {streamliner} train is now a museum exhibit.
e.zh: 这辆复古流线型列车如今成了博物馆的展品。

e.en: Passengers admired the silver {streamliner} pulling into the station.
e.zh: 乘客们赞叹着那辆驶入车站的银色流线型列车。

e.en: The company is {streamlining} its workflow to reduce costs.
e.zh: 公司正在精简工作流程以降低成本。

e.en: {Streamlining} the onboarding process boosted new-hire satisfaction significantly.
e.zh: 简化入职流程后,新员工的满意度显著提升。

e.en: She {streams} her cooking videos every Sunday evening.
e.zh: 她每周日晚上直播自己的烹饪视频。

e.en: Several mountain {streams} feed into the main river.
e.zh: 几条山间小溪汇入主河道。

streatham.t: n. 斯特里特姆（伦敦地名）

e.en: My cousin lives in {Streatham}, just south of central London.
e.zh: 我表哥住在伦敦市中心以南的斯特里特姆。

e.en: The ice rink in {Streatham} is popular with local families.
e.zh: 斯特里特姆的溜冰场很受当地家庭的欢迎。

e.en: There's a great coffee shop on the next {street}.
e.zh: 下一条街上有一家不错的咖啡店。

e.en: Children were playing safely on the quiet residential {street}.
e.zh: 孩子们在安静的住宅街上安全地玩耍。

e.en: We rode the {streetcar} all the way down to the harbor.
e.zh: 我们乘有轨电车一路坐到了港口。

e.en: San Francisco's historic {streetcar} line is a tourist favorite.
e.zh: 旧金山的老式有轨电车线路深受游客喜爱。

e.en: A moth circled the old {streetlamp} on the corner.
e.zh: 一只飞蛾绕着街角那盏老路灯打转。

e.en: The {streetlamp} flickered and finally went out around midnight.
e.zh: 那盏路灯闪烁了几下,最后在午夜前后熄灭了。

e.en: The {streetlight} outside my window keeps me awake at night.
e.zh: 窗外的路灯让我夜里睡不着。

e.en: They waited under the {streetlight} for their ride home.
e.zh: 他们在路灯下等着搭车回家。

e.en: The {streets} were packed with people celebrating the victory.
e.zh: 街道上挤满了庆祝胜利的人群。

e.en: Snow blanketed the empty {streets} early Sunday morning.
e.zh: 周日清晨,白雪覆盖了空荡荡的街道。

e.en: The renovation completely transformed the historic {streetscape}.
e.zh: 这次翻修彻底改变了这片历史街景。

e.en: Tree-lined sidewalks create a much more pleasant {streetscape}.
e.zh: 林荫人行道营造出更加宜人的街景。

e.en: The novel's main character was a {streetwalker} in 1920s Paris.
e.zh: 这部小说的主角是1920年代巴黎的一名街头妓女。

e.en: Police reform efforts often overlook the dangers facing every {streetwalker}.
e.zh: 警方的改革举措常常忽视街头妓女所面临的危险。

streetwise.t: adj. 有街头智慧的；老练精明的

e.en: He's {streetwise} enough to spot a scam instantly.
e.zh: 他够老练,一眼就能识破骗局。

e.en: The detective relied on her {streetwise} instincts to solve cases.
e.zh: 这位侦探靠着街头练就的直觉破案。

strength.t:
n. 力量；强度
n. 优势、长处

e.en: Her greatest {strength} is staying calm under pressure.
e.zh: 她最大的优点就是在压力下能保持冷静。

e.en: He's been training to build upper-body {strength} this year.
e.zh: 他今年一直在训练以增强上肢力量。

strengthen.t: v. 加强；增强；使更稳固

e.en: Daily exercise can {strengthen} both your body and mind.
e.zh: 每天锻炼能强健身心。

e.en: This agreement will {strengthen} ties between the two countries.
e.zh: 这项协议将加强两国之间的关系。

strengthened.t: v. 加强（strengthen 的过去式/过去分词）

e.en: The crisis only {strengthened} their friendship over time.
e.zh: 这场危机反而让他们的友谊随时间愈发深厚。

e.en: Engineers {strengthened} the bridge after the earthquake damage.
e.zh: 工程师在地震损毁后加固了这座桥。

e.en: This exercise is a great {strengthener} for your core muscles.
e.zh: 这个动作能很好地强化你的核心肌群。

e.en: Vitamin C acts as an immune {strengthener} during cold season.
e.zh: 维生素C在感冒季节有助于增强免疫力。

e.en: The gym offers classes focused on {strengthening} the back.
e.zh: 这家健身房开设了专门强化背部的课程。

e.en: They are {strengthening} ties between the two countries.
e.zh: 两国正在加强彼此之间的关系。

strengthens.t: v. 加强（strengthen 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Regular reading {strengthens} a child's vocabulary over time.
e.zh: 经常阅读能逐步丰富孩子的词汇量。

e.en: This update {strengthens} the app's password security.
e.zh: 这次更新增强了应用的密码安全性。

strengths.t: n. 力量、优势（strength 的复数）

e.en: List your top three {strengths} on your résumé.
e.zh: 在简历上列出你最突出的三项优势。

e.en: The team's main {strengths} are speed and teamwork.
e.zh: 这支队伍的主要优势是速度和团队协作。

strenuous.t: adj. 费力的；剧烈的；艰苦的

e.en: Avoid {strenuous} exercise for a week after surgery.
e.zh: 术后一周内应避免剧烈运动。

e.en: She made a {strenuous} effort to finish the report on time.
e.zh: 她费了很大力气按时完成报告。

e.en: He {strenuously} denied any involvement in the scandal.
e.zh: 他极力否认与这起丑闻有任何牵连。

e.en: The hikers worked {strenuously} to reach the summit before dark.
e.zh: 登山者在天黑前奋力登顶。

strep.t: n. 链球菌（streptococcus 的缩写）

e.en: The doctor confirmed she has {strep} throat.
e.zh: 医生确认她得了链球菌性咽喉炎。

e.en: Kids often pass {strep} around at school.
e.zh: 小孩在学校里经常互相传染链球菌。

streptococcal.t: adj. 链球菌的；由链球菌引起的

e.en: The patient was treated for a {streptococcal} infection.
e.zh: 病人正在接受链球菌感染的治疗。

e.en: Antibiotics quickly cleared the {streptococcal} sore throat.
e.zh: 抗生素很快治好了这次链球菌引起的咽喉痛。

streptococci.t: n. 链球菌（streptococcus 的复数）

e.en: The lab identified {streptococci} in the throat sample.
e.zh: 实验室在咽拭子样本中检出了链球菌。

e.en: Some {streptococci} live harmlessly on the skin.
e.zh: 某些链球菌可以无害地寄生在皮肤上。

e.en: {Streptococcus} bacteria can cause a range of infections.
e.zh: 链球菌可引起多种类型的感染。

e.en: Penicillin is effective against most {streptococcus} strains.
e.zh: 青霉素对大多数链球菌菌株都有效。

streptokinase.t: n. 链激酶（一种溶栓药物）

e.en: Doctors gave him {streptokinase} to dissolve the blood clot.
e.zh: 医生给他注射链激酶以溶解血栓。

e.en: {Streptokinase} is used in emergency heart attack treatment.
e.zh: 链激酶用于心脏病发作的紧急救治。

e.en: {Streptomycin} was once the main drug used to treat tuberculosis.
e.zh: 链霉素曾是治疗结核病的主要药物。

e.en: The vet prescribed {streptomycin} for the infection.
e.zh: 兽医为这次感染开了链霉素。

stress.t:
n. 压力；紧张
v. 强调

e.en: Work {stress} has been keeping me up at night.
e.zh: 工作压力让我最近经常失眠。

e.en: I want to {stress} how important this deadline is.
e.zh: 我想强调这个截止日期有多重要。

stressed.t:
adj. 有压力的；焦虑的
v. 强调（过去式）

e.en: She felt completely {stressed} before her final exam.
e.zh: 期末考试前她感到压力极大。

e.en: The teacher {stressed} the need for honest answers.
e.zh: 老师强调要如实作答。

stresses.t:
n. 压力（复数）
v. 强调（第三人称单数）

e.en: Daily life {stresses} can affect your mental health.
e.zh: 日常生活的种种压力会影响心理健康。

e.en: The coach {stresses} discipline above all else.
e.zh: 这位教练最强调的是纪律。

stressful.t: adj. 压力大的；令人紧张的

e.en: Moving to a new city can be really {stressful}.
e.zh: 搬到一个新城市真的很令人焦虑。

e.en: She quit her {stressful} job to travel.
e.zh: 她辞掉了那份压力大的工作去旅行。

stressfully.t: adv. 充满压力地；紧张地

e.en: He spoke {stressfully} about the upcoming layoffs.
e.zh: 他焦虑地谈起即将到来的裁员。

e.en: The team worked {stressfully} to meet the deadline.
e.zh: 团队顶着巨大压力赶在截止日前完成。

stressing.t: v. 强调；使紧张（进行时）

e.en: Stop {stressing} about things you can't control.
e.zh: 别再为无法控制的事情焦虑了。

e.en: The professor kept {stressing} the importance of citations.
e.zh: 教授一再强调引用的重要性。

e.en: Money is the biggest {stressor} for many young couples.
e.zh: 金钱是许多年轻夫妻最大的压力源。

e.en: Identifying your main {stressor} is the first step to coping.
e.zh: 找出主要的压力来源是应对压力的第一步。

stretch.t:
v. 伸展；拉伸
n. 一段（时间、距离）

e.en: Remember to {stretch} before going for a run.
e.zh: 跑步前记得做拉伸。

e.en: This road has a long {stretch} with no gas stations.
e.zh: 这条路有很长一段都没有加油站。

stretchable.t: adj. 可拉伸的；有弹性的

e.en: The pants are made from a soft, {stretchable} fabric.
e.zh: 这条裤子由柔软有弹性的面料制成。

e.en: Look for a {stretchable} phone case that fits snugly.
e.zh: 挑一个有弹性、能贴合手机的保护壳。

e.en: She {stretched} her arms after the long flight.
e.zh: 长途飞行后她伸了伸胳膊。

e.en: Our budget is already {stretched} too thin.
e.zh: 我们的预算已经捉襟见肘了。

e.en: Paramedics carried the injured man on a {stretcher}.
e.zh: 急救人员用担架抬走了伤者。

e.en: They lifted the patient onto the {stretcher} carefully.
e.zh: 他们小心地把病人抬上担架。

stretches.t:
v. 伸展（第三人称单数）
n. 一段（复数）

e.en: The beach {stretches} for miles along the coast.
e.zh: 这片海滩沿着海岸线绵延数英里。

e.en: Do a few simple {stretches} every morning.
e.zh: 每天早上做几个简单的伸展动作。

e.en: Daily {stretching} can improve your flexibility.
e.zh: 每天拉伸可以提升身体的柔韧性。

e.en: The cat is {stretching} lazily on the sofa.
e.zh: 那只猫懒洋洋地在沙发上伸懒腰。

stretchings.t: n. 拉伸动作（复数，罕用）

e.en: The yoga book describes various {stretchings} for beginners.
e.zh: 这本瑜伽书介绍了多种适合初学者的拉伸动作。

e.en: Different {stretchings} target different muscle groups.
e.zh: 不同的拉伸方式针对不同的肌群。

stretchy.t: adj. 有弹性的；可拉伸的

e.en: These leggings are super {stretchy} and comfortable.
e.zh: 这条打底裤非常有弹性,穿着很舒服。

e.en: Kids love {stretchy} toys they can pull and twist.
e.zh: 小孩子很喜欢那种可以拉扯扭动的弹力玩具。

stretford.t: n. 斯特雷特福（英国地名）

e.en: He grew up in {Stretford}, just outside Manchester.
e.zh: 他在曼彻斯特郊外的斯特雷特福长大。

e.en: The team plays its home games near {Stretford}.
e.zh: 这支球队的主场就在斯特雷特福附近。

streusel.t: n. 酥粒（洒在糕点上的碎屑配料）

e.en: She topped the muffins with cinnamon {streusel}.
e.zh: 她在玛芬蛋糕上撒了一层肉桂酥粒。

e.en: Apple pie tastes amazing with a buttery {streusel} crust.
e.zh: 加一层黄油酥粒的苹果派特别美味。

e.en: Flower girls {strew} petals down the aisle.
e.zh: 花童把花瓣撒在婚礼通道上。

e.en: Don't {strew} your toys all over the living room.
e.zh: 别把玩具撒得满客厅都是。

strewth.t: int. 天啊（澳/英俚语，表惊讶）

e.en: "{Strewth}, that traffic was unbelievable!" he said.
e.zh: 他说:“天哪,那交通真是难以置信!”

e.en: "{Strewth}, look at the size of that spider!"
e.zh: “老天爷,你看那蜘蛛多大只!”

striate.t:
adj. 有条纹的
v. 使起条纹

e.en: Erosion can {striate} the surface of soft rock.
e.zh: 侵蚀作用会在软岩表面留下条纹。

e.en: The artist used a comb to {striate} the wet paint.
e.zh: 艺术家用梳子在湿颜料上划出条纹。

striated.t: adj. 有条纹的；有纹路的

e.en: Skeletal muscle has a {striated} appearance under the microscope.
e.zh: 骨骼肌在显微镜下呈现出条纹状。

e.en: The cliff showed beautifully {striated} layers of rock.
e.zh: 那道悬崖呈现出美丽的岩层条纹。

e.en: Each {striation} in the rock marks a different era.
e.zh: 岩石上的每一道条纹都代表着一个不同的年代。

e.en: You can see fine {striation} on the polished marble.
e.zh: 在打磨过的大理石上能看到细密的纹路。

stricken.t: adj. 受打击的；受困扰的

e.en: The town was {stricken} by a sudden flood.
e.zh: 那座小镇遭遇了一场突如其来的洪灾。

e.en: She looked {stricken} when she heard the news.
e.zh: 听到这个消息时,她神情沮丧。

e.en: My parents were very {strict} about bedtime.
e.zh: 我父母对睡觉时间管得很严。

e.en: The school has a {strict} no-phone policy.
e.zh: 这所学校实行严格的禁用手机规定。

e.en: This information is {strictly} confidential.
e.zh: 这些信息是严格保密的。

e.en: {Strictly} speaking, that's not quite accurate.
e.zh: 严格来说,那并不完全准确。

e.en: The teacher's {strictness} actually helped us focus.
e.zh: 老师的严格其实让我们更加专注。

e.en: He resented the {strictness} of the new dress code.
e.zh: 他对新的着装规定的严苛感到不满。

stricture.t:
n. 严厉批评
n. （医）狭窄

e.en: The report contained harsh {stricture} of management.
e.zh: 这份报告对管理层提出了严厉批评。

e.en: Surgery was needed to repair the urethral {stricture}.
e.zh: 需要手术来修复尿道狭窄。

stridden.t: v. 大步走（stride 的过去分词）

e.en: She had {stridden} into the room before anyone noticed.
e.zh: 她大步走进房间时还没人察觉。

e.en: He had {stridden} across the stage with confidence.
e.zh: 他自信地大步走过舞台。

stride.t:
v. 大步走
n. 步伐；进展

e.en: He took a long {stride} over the puddle.
e.zh: 他迈了一大步跨过水坑。

e.en: The runner began to {stride} confidently toward the finish.
e.zh: 那名选手自信地大步冲向终点。

e.en: The {stridency} of his voice startled everyone.
e.zh: 他刺耳的嗓音把大家都吓了一跳。

e.en: Critics noted the growing {stridency} of online debates.
e.zh: 评论员注意到网络辩论的语气越来越激烈。

e.en: She became a {strident} critic of the new law.
e.zh: 她成了这部新法律的强烈批评者。

e.en: The alarm gave a {strident} beep every few seconds.
e.zh: 警报器每隔几秒就发出刺耳的鸣叫。

e.en: He {stridently} opposed any cuts to the budget.
e.zh: 他强烈反对任何预算削减。

e.en: The activists protested {stridently} outside city hall.
e.zh: 抗议者在市政厅外大声抗议。

strider.t: n. 大步行走的人；长腿水黾

e.en: A water {strider} skated across the pond's surface.
e.zh: 一只水黾在池塘水面上滑行。

e.en: She's a fast {strider} and easily outpaces her friends.
e.zh: 她步伐很快,轻松就把朋友们甩在后面。

strides.t:
n. 大步；进展
v. 大步走（stride 的第三人称单数）

e.en: The company has made huge {strides} in clean energy.
e.zh: 这家公司在清洁能源方面取得了长足进步。

e.en: He {strides} into meetings like he owns the place.
e.zh: 他走进会议室时一副大老板的架势。

striding.t: v. 大步走（stride 的现在分词）

e.en: She came {striding} down the hall, late as usual.
e.zh: 她大步走过走廊,跟往常一样迟到了。

e.en: The CEO was {striding} confidently toward the podium.
e.zh: 首席执行官自信地大步走向讲台。

e.en: The child's noisy {stridor} alarmed the doctor.
e.zh: 孩子刺耳的喘鸣声让医生很担心。

e.en: {Stridor} can indicate a blocked airway in infants.
e.zh: 喘鸣声可能提示婴儿气道阻塞。

e.en: The country has suffered years of political {strife}.
e.zh: 这个国家多年来一直饱受政治纷争之苦。

e.en: Money issues caused constant {strife} between them.
e.zh: 金钱问题让他们之间不断起冲突。

strike.t:
n./v. 罢工
v. 打击；击中

e.en: Workers plan to {strike} for better wages next week.
e.zh: 工人们计划下周罢工以争取更高的工资。

e.en: Lightning can {strike} the same place twice.
e.zh: 闪电是可以两次击中同一个地方的。

strikebreaker.t: n. 破坏罢工的人；工贼

e.en: The company hired a {strikebreaker} to keep the factory running.
e.zh: 公司雇了一名破坏罢工者来维持工厂运转。

e.en: Union members shouted at every {strikebreaker} crossing the picket line.
e.zh: 工会成员对每个越过纠察线的破坏罢工者大声斥责。

e.en: The pitcher recorded his tenth {strikeout} of the game.
e.zh: 投手拿下了本场比赛的第十次三振。

e.en: His final {strikeout} ended the inning dramatically.
e.zh: 他最后那次三振戏剧性地结束了这一局。

e.en: The team's young {striker} scored twice in the final.
e.zh: 球队年轻的前锋在决赛中梅开二度。

e.en: Each {striker} held a sign demanding fair wages.
e.zh: 每位罢工者都举着要求公平工资的牌子。

strikes.t:
n. 罢工（复数）
v. 打击（第三人称单数）

e.en: Lightning rarely {strikes} the same place twice.
e.zh: 闪电很少在同一个地方击中两次。

e.en: A wave of {strikes} disrupted public transport last week.
e.zh: 上周一连串的罢工扰乱了公共交通。

striking.t: adj. 引人注目的；显著的

e.en: She wore a {striking} red dress to the gala.
e.zh: 她穿了一条引人注目的红裙子参加晚会。

e.en: The {striking} workers gathered outside the factory gates.
e.zh: 罢工的工人们聚集在工厂门口。

e.en: The twins look {strikingly} similar despite their different styles.
e.zh: 尽管风格不同,这对双胞胎长得惊人地相似。

e.en: Her new album is {strikingly} different from her earlier work.
e.zh: 她的新专辑与早期作品有显著不同。

string.t:
n. 字符串（编程）；绳子
v. 串起

e.en: Tie the package with a piece of {string}.
e.zh: 用一根绳子把包裹捆好。

e.en: He had a {string} of bad luck this month.
e.zh: 这个月他接连遭遇不顺。

e.en: The violin is the most popular {stringed} instrument.
e.zh: 小提琴是最受欢迎的弦乐器。

e.en: She plays several {stringed} instruments in the orchestra.
e.zh: 她在管弦乐团演奏多种弦乐器。

e.en: The {stringency} of the new rules surprised many employees.
e.zh: 新规定的严格程度让许多员工感到意外。

e.en: Auditors questioned the {stringency} of the safety checks.
e.zh: 审计人员质疑安全检查的严格性。

e.en: Airports enforce {stringent} security checks for every passenger.
e.zh: 机场对每位乘客执行严格的安检。

e.en: The lab follows {stringent} hygiene standards at all times.
e.zh: 实验室始终遵循严格的卫生标准。

e.en: Food safety laws are {stringently} enforced in this country.
e.zh: 这个国家严格执行食品安全法律。

e.en: The contract terms were {stringently} reviewed before signing.
e.zh: 合同条款在签署前经过了严格审查。

e.en: She works as a {stringer} for a major news agency.
e.zh: 她为一家大型新闻机构当特约记者。

e.en: The aircraft's wing is reinforced by a steel {stringer}.
e.zh: 飞机的机翼由一根钢制纵梁加固。

strings.t: n. 字符串（复数）；弦乐器

e.en: He plucked the guitar {strings} gently.
e.zh: 他轻轻地拨动吉他的琴弦。

e.en: The job came with no {strings} attached.
e.zh: 这份工作没有任何附加条件。

e.en: The overcooked beef was tough and {stringy}.
e.zh: 煮过头的牛肉又老又有筋。

e.en: He brushed his {stringy} wet hair from his eyes.
e.zh: 他把湿漉漉的乱发从眼前拨开。

strip.t:
n. 长条
v. 剥去；脱衣

e.en: Please {strip} the bed before checking out.
e.zh: 请在退房前把床单被罩取下来。

e.en: A narrow {strip} of land separates the two countries.
e.zh: 一条狭长的土地将两国分开。

e.en: The flag has a single red {stripe} across the middle.
e.zh: 旗帜中间有一条红色条纹。

e.en: Painters added a yellow {stripe} down the road.
e.zh: 工人在路面中央画了一条黄线。

e.en: He wore a {striped} shirt to the office today.
e.zh: 他今天穿了一件条纹衬衫去办公室。

e.en: The cat curled up on the {striped} blanket.
e.zh: 猫蜷缩在那条条纹毯子上。

striper.t: n. 条纹鲈鱼；佩条纹肩章者

e.en: The angler caught a huge {striper} off the coast.
e.zh: 那位钓客在海边钓到一条大条纹鲈。

e.en: Every summer, fishermen hunt for {striper} in the bay.
e.zh: 每年夏天,渔民都会在海湾捕捞条纹鲈。

e.en: Zebras are easily recognized by their black {stripes}.
e.zh: 斑马因其黑色条纹而很容易辨认。

e.en: The referee's shirt has bold black {stripes}.
e.zh: 裁判的衬衫有醒目的黑色条纹。

e.en: He was just a {stripling} when he joined the navy.
e.zh: 他参军入海军时还是个毛头小子。

e.en: The shop was run by a tall, awkward {stripling}.
e.zh: 那家店由一个又高又笨拙的小伙子打理。

stripped.t:
adj. 被剥去的
v. 剥去（strip 的过去式）

e.en: They {stripped} the old wallpaper before painting the room.
e.zh: 他们在粉刷房间前把旧墙纸剥掉了。

e.en: The court {stripped} him of his medals after the scandal.
e.zh: 丑闻后,法庭剥夺了他的奖牌。

e.en: Use a paint {stripper} to remove the old finish.
e.zh: 用脱漆剂去除旧的漆层。

e.en: The {stripper} performed under dim purple lights.
e.zh: 那位脱衣舞者在昏暗的紫色灯光下表演。

e.en: He spent the weekend {stripping} paint from the cabinets.
e.zh: 他整个周末都在给橱柜剥漆。

e.en: The new law prevents companies from {stripping} workers' rights.
e.zh: 新法律阻止公司剥夺工人的权利。

strips.t:
n. 长条（复数）
v. 剥去（第三人称单数）

e.en: Cut the chicken into thin {strips} before frying.
e.zh: 把鸡肉切成细条再煎。

e.en: She {strips} the bed every Sunday morning.
e.zh: 她每周日早上都会把床单换下来。

e.en: The club is famous for its late-night {striptease} shows.
e.zh: 那家俱乐部以深夜的脱衣舞表演而闻名。

e.en: He performed a comedic {striptease} at the bachelor party.
e.zh: 他在单身派对上表演了一段搞笑脱衣秀。

e.en: My niece loves her {stripy} pink and white socks.
e.zh: 我侄女很喜欢她那双粉白条纹袜。

e.en: He bought a {stripy} umbrella for the rainy season.
e.zh: 他买了一把条纹雨伞应付雨季。

e.en: We {strive} to deliver the best service possible.
e.zh: 我们努力提供最好的服务。

e.en: Athletes {strive} for perfection in every training session.
e.zh: 运动员在每次训练中都力求完美。

strived.t: v. 努力（strive 的过去式）

e.en: She {strived} to finish the marathon despite the injury.
e.zh: 尽管受伤,她仍努力完成了马拉松。

e.en: He has always {strived} to support his family.
e.zh: 他一直努力地养家。

striven.t: v. 努力（strive 的过去分词）

e.en: They have {striven} for years to reform the system.
e.zh: 他们多年来一直致力于改革这一体制。

e.en: She has {striven} to overcome every obstacle in her path.
e.zh: 她努力克服了道路上的每一个障碍。

e.en: He's a real {striver} who built his business from nothing.
e.zh: 他是个真正的奋斗者,白手起家创办了自己的公司。

e.en: The school celebrates every {striver} who beats the odds.
e.zh: 学校表彰每一位突破逆境的奋斗者。

strives.t: v. 努力（strive 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Our team {strives} to improve customer satisfaction every quarter.
e.zh: 我们团队每个季度都努力提升客户满意度。

e.en: She {strives} to balance work and family life.
e.zh: 她努力在工作和家庭生活之间取得平衡。

e.en: He's always {striving} to learn new skills.
e.zh: 他一直在努力学习新技能。

e.en: The company is {striving} to reduce its carbon footprint.
e.zh: 公司正在努力减少其碳足迹。

e.en: The {strobe} light flashed in time with the music.
e.zh: 频闪灯随着音乐节奏闪烁。

e.en: Photographers used a {strobe} to freeze the dancer's motion.
e.zh: 摄影师用闪光灯定格了舞者的动作。

strobing.t:
n. 频闪效果
v. 闪烁

e.en: The {strobing} lights gave some guests a headache.
e.zh: 频闪的灯光让一些客人感到头痛。

e.en: Makeup artists love {strobing} to highlight cheekbones.
e.zh: 化妆师喜欢用打高光的方式突出颧骨。

e.en: The {stroboscopic} effect made the wheels appear to spin backward.
e.zh: 频闪效应使车轮看起来像在倒转。

e.en: Engineers used a {stroboscopic} lamp to study the engine.
e.zh: 工程师用频闪灯来研究发动机。

strode.t: v. 大步走（stride 的过去式）

e.en: She {strode} confidently into the boardroom.
e.zh: 她自信地大步走进了会议室。

e.en: He {strode} across the field to greet his team.
e.zh: 他大步穿过球场去迎接他的队伍。

stroganoff.t: n. 俄式酸奶油烩牛肉

e.en: We had beef {stroganoff} with rice for dinner.
e.zh: 我们晚餐吃了俄式炖牛肉配米饭。

e.en: Her mushroom {stroganoff} is a family favorite.
e.zh: 她做的蘑菇炖肉是家里最受欢迎的菜。

stroke.t:
n. 中风；一击；笔画
v. 抚摸

e.en: He suffered a mild {stroke} but recovered quickly.
e.zh: 他中过一次轻度中风,但很快就康复了。

e.en: With one {stroke} of the brush, she finished the painting.
e.zh: 她一笔下去就完成了那幅画。

stroked.t: v. 抚摸（stroke 的过去式）

e.en: She gently {stroked} the cat's soft fur.
e.zh: 她轻轻抚摸着猫柔软的毛。

e.en: He {stroked} his beard while thinking about the question.
e.zh: 他一边思考问题一边捋着胡须。

strokes.t:
n. 中风（复数）；笔画
v. 抚摸（第三人称单数）

e.en: The painter applied bold {strokes} of color to the canvas.
e.zh: 画家在画布上挥洒大胆的笔触。

e.en: He swims fifty {strokes} every morning.
e.zh: 他每天早上游五十下。

stroking.t: v. 抚摸（stroke 的现在分词）

e.en: She sat on the porch {stroking} her old dog.
e.zh: 她坐在门廊上抚摸着她的老狗。

e.en: He kept {stroking} his chin as he considered the offer.
e.zh: 他考虑这个提议时一直摸着下巴。

e.en: Let's take a {stroll} along the river after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后我们沿着河边散散步吧。

e.en: They like to {stroll} through the park on Sundays.
e.zh: 他们喜欢周日在公园里散步。

e.en: She pushed the baby's {stroller} along the sidewalk.
e.zh: 她推着婴儿车沿人行道走。

e.en: This {stroller} folds up small enough to fit in the trunk.
e.zh: 这辆婴儿车折叠后小到可以放进后备箱。

strolling.t: v. 散步（stroll 的现在分词）

e.en: Couples were {strolling} hand in hand through the garden.
e.zh: 情侣们手牵手在花园里漫步。

e.en: We spent the afternoon {strolling} around the old town.
e.zh: 我们整个下午都在老城区漫步。

stroma.t: n. (生物) 基质；支架组织

e.en: The {stroma} provides structural support to the organ tissue.
e.zh: 基质为器官组织提供结构支撑。

e.en: Photosynthesis reactions occur within the chloroplast {stroma}.
e.zh: 光合作用反应发生在叶绿体的基质中。

e.en: Researchers studied the {stromal} cells around the tumor.
e.zh: 研究人员研究了肿瘤周围的基质细胞。

e.en: The {stromal} tissue plays a key role in healing.
e.zh: 基质组织在愈合过程中起关键作用。

stromatolite.t: n. 叠层石（古生物沉积岩）

e.en: A {stromatolite} fossil can reveal Earth's earliest life forms.
e.zh: 叠层石化石能揭示地球最早的生命形式。

e.en: Scientists discovered a living {stromatolite} colony in the lagoon.
e.zh: 科学家在泻湖中发现了活的叠层石群落。

stromness.t: n. 斯特罗姆内斯（苏格兰地名）

e.en: Our ferry docked at {Stromness} just before sunset.
e.zh: 我们的渡轮在日落前停靠在斯特罗姆内斯。

e.en: The town of {Stromness} has charming stone-paved streets.
e.zh: 斯特罗姆内斯小镇有迷人的石板街道。

strong.t:
adj. 强壮的；强大的
adj. 浓的（茶、酒等）

e.en: She has a {strong} sense of responsibility at work.
e.zh: 她在工作中有强烈的责任感。

e.en: This coffee is too {strong} for me in the morning.
e.zh: 这杯咖啡早上喝对我来说太浓了。

strongbox.t: n. 保险箱；贵重物品箱

e.en: He kept the documents locked in a heavy {strongbox}.
e.zh: 他把文件锁在一个沉重的保险箱里。

e.en: The hotel offers a {strongbox} for valuable items.
e.zh: 酒店为贵重物品提供保险箱。

stronger.t: adj. 更强的；更强壮的（strong 的比较级）

e.en: Coffee makes me feel {stronger} in the morning.
e.zh: 咖啡让我早上感觉更有精神。

e.en: The new bridge is {stronger} than the old one.
e.zh: 新桥比旧桥更坚固。

e.en: This city was once a {stronghold} of the rebels.
e.zh: 这座城市曾是叛军的据点。

e.en: The region remains a {stronghold} of traditional values.
e.zh: 该地区仍是传统价值观的堡垒。

e.en: I {strongly} recommend reading this book.
e.zh: 我强烈推荐阅读这本书。

e.en: She feels {strongly} about protecting the environment.
e.zh: 她对保护环境有强烈的感受。

e.en: The country is ruled by a military {strongman}.
e.zh: 这个国家由一位军事强人统治。

e.en: A {strongman} at the circus lifted the heavy barbell easily.
e.zh: 马戏团的大力士轻松举起了重杠铃。

e.en: Patience is not really my {strongpoint}.
e.zh: 耐心其实不是我的强项。

e.en: The army defended the hilltop {strongpoint} for weeks.
e.zh: 军队坚守了山顶据点数周。

e.en: The bank keeps gold bars in its {strongroom}.
e.zh: 银行把金条存放在金库里。

e.en: Only the manager has the key to the {strongroom}.
e.zh: 只有经理才有金库的钥匙。

e.en: Fireworks use {strontium} to produce a bright red color.
e.zh: 烟花用锶来产生鲜艳的红色。

e.en: Radioactive {strontium} can contaminate milk after nuclear accidents.
e.zh: 放射性锶在核事故后可能污染牛奶。

strop.t:
n. 磨刀皮带
v. 在皮带上磨（刀）

e.en: The barber sharpened the razor on a leather {strop}.
e.zh: 理发师在皮带上磨剃刀。

e.en: My little brother got in a {strop} over the toy.
e.zh: 我弟弟为了那个玩具大发脾气。

e.en: The poem opens with a haunting four-line {strophe}.
e.zh: 这首诗以一段令人难忘的四行诗节开场。

e.en: Each {strophe} of the ode follows the same rhythm.
e.zh: 颂诗的每一节都遵循相同的节奏。

e.en: The waiter got {stroppy} when we asked for the bill.
e.zh: 我们要账单时,服务员变得很不耐烦。

e.en: Teenagers can be {stroppy} in the morning before school.
e.zh: 青少年早上上学前可能脾气暴躁。

stroud.t: n. 斯特劳德（英国地名/姓氏）

e.en: Traders once sold coarse {stroud} cloth to Native Americans.
e.zh: 商人曾把粗糙的斯特劳德毛呢卖给印第安人。

e.en: The museum displays a red {stroud} blanket from the 1800s.
e.zh: 博物馆展出一条十九世纪的红色斯特劳德毛毯。

strove.t: v. 努力；奋斗（strive 的过去式）

e.en: She {strove} to finish the marathon despite the pain.
e.zh: 她忍着疼痛努力跑完马拉松。

e.en: The author {strove} for clarity in every sentence.
e.zh: 作者努力让每一句话都清晰明了。

struck.t: v. 击中；打动（strike 的过去式）

e.en: Lightning {struck} the old oak tree last night.
e.zh: 昨晚闪电击中了那棵老橡树。

e.en: I was {struck} by how kind the strangers were.
e.zh: 陌生人的善良让我深受感动。

e.en: The building has serious {structural} damage after the earthquake.
e.zh: 地震后这栋建筑有严重的结构性损坏。

e.en: We need {structural} changes to fix the company's culture.
e.zh: 我们需要结构性的改革来修正公司文化。

structuralism.t: n. 结构主义（哲学、语言学流派）

e.en: {Structuralism} shaped how scholars analyze myths and language.
e.zh: 结构主义影响了学者分析神话与语言的方式。

e.en: Her thesis applies {structuralism} to modern film criticism.
e.zh: 她的论文将结构主义应用于现代电影批评。

structuralist.t:
n. 结构主义者
adj. 结构主义的

e.en: The professor offered a {structuralist} reading of the novel.
e.zh: 教授对这部小说进行了结构主义解读。

e.en: He is a leading {structuralist} in the field of anthropology.
e.zh: 他是人类学领域著名的结构主义学者。

structurally.t: adv. 结构上；在结构方面

e.en: The bridge is {structurally} sound after the recent repairs.
e.zh: 经过最近的维修,这座桥结构上很安全。

e.en: The two essays are {structurally} similar but argue different points.
e.zh: 这两篇文章结构相似,但论点不同。

structure.t:
n. 结构；构造
v. 组织；构建

e.en: The {structure} of the report is clear and logical.
e.zh: 这份报告的结构清晰且有条理。

e.en: Workers built a wooden {structure} beside the river.
e.zh: 工人们在河边搭建了一座木质建筑。

structured.t: adj. 结构化的；有条理的

e.en: She gave a well-{structured} presentation to the board.
e.zh: 她向董事会做了一场结构清晰的报告。

e.en: Children often thrive with a {structured} daily routine.
e.zh: 孩子们通常在有规律的日常作息中成长得更好。

structures.t:
n. 结构（复数）
v. 构建（第三人称单数）

e.en: Ancient stone {structures} still stand on the hilltop.
e.zh: 古老的石质建筑仍矗立在山顶上。

e.en: The company {structures} its teams around small projects.
e.zh: 公司围绕小型项目来组建团队。

structuring.t: v. 组织；构建（structure 的现在分词）

e.en: She is {structuring} the essay around three main themes.
e.zh: 她正围绕三个主要主题来构思这篇文章。

e.en: {Structuring} a startup well saves a lot of headaches later.
e.zh: 把初创公司的架构搭好,以后能省很多麻烦。

strudel.t: n. 果馅卷（一种奥地利点心）

e.en: We had warm apple {strudel} with vanilla ice cream.
e.zh: 我们吃了热苹果卷配香草冰淇淋。
