e.en: A {scalpriform} tool lay beside the bones.
e.zh: 骨头旁放着一件似刀形的工具。

e.en: The surgeon lifted the {scalprum} carefully.
e.zh: 外科医生小心地拿起解剖刀。

e.en: An ancient {scalprum} was found in the kit.
e.zh: 工具箱里发现了一把古代小刀。

e.en: The boys began to {scamble} for the coins.
e.zh: 男孩们开始争抢那些硬币。

e.en: We had to {scamble} a meal from leftovers.
e.zh: 我们只好用剩菜勉强凑出一顿饭。

e.en: The architect noted a missing {scamillus} under the column.
e.zh: 建筑师注意到柱子下面少了一块柱基小垫块。

e.en: A stone {scamillus} helped level the base.
e.zh: 一块石制柱基小垫块帮助找平了底座。

e.en: The old herbal text mentioned {scammonia} as a purgative plant.
e.zh: 那本旧草药书提到药旋花属植物可作泻药。

e.en: Botanists classified the specimen as {scammonia}.
e.zh: 植物学家把这个标本归为药旋花属植物。

e.en: The pharmacist rejected the {scammoniate} mixture.
e.zh: 药剂师拒收了那种含泻根树脂的混合物。

e.en: A {scammoniate} preparation appeared in the old formulary.
e.zh: 旧处方集中出现了一种含泻根树脂的制剂。

e.en: The analysis detected {scammonin} in the sample.
e.zh: 分析在样品中检测到泻根树脂成分。

e.en: Old medicines sometimes relied on {scammonin}.
e.zh: 旧式药物有时依赖泻根树脂成分。

e.en: The healer used {scammony} as a strong purgative.
e.zh: 那位医者把泻根树脂用作强效泻药。

e.en: A jar of {scammony} sat on the apothecary shelf.
e.zh: 药剂师的架子上放着一罐泻根树脂。

e.en: His {scampish} grin made everyone laugh.
e.zh: 他顽皮的咧嘴笑让大家都笑了。

e.en: The letter had a {scampish} disregard for rules.
e.zh: 那封信带着一种无赖似的蔑视规则。

e.en: The {scamster} promised impossible returns.
e.zh: 那个骗子承诺了不可能实现的高回报。

e.en: Police traced the online {scamster} through bank records.
e.zh: 警方通过银行记录追踪到那名网络诈骗者。

e.en: The lab repaired its old {scanatron} yesterday.
e.zh: 实验室昨天修好了那台旧电子扫描装置。

e.en: A {scanatron} converted the image into signals.
e.zh: 电子扫描装置把图像转换成了信号。

e.en: The {scandal-ridden} company lost investor confidence.
e.zh: 这家丑闻缠身的公司失去了投资者信心。

e.en: Voters rejected the {scandal-ridden} administration.
e.zh: 选民否决了这个丑闻缠身的政府。

e.en: The fossil showed a {scalariform} pattern under the lens.
e.zh: 化石在镜头下呈现梯状纹理。

e.en: Botanists noted the plant's {scalariform} vessels.
e.zh: 植物学家注意到这种植物的梯纹导管。

e.en: The cells were arranged {scalariformly} along the stem.
e.zh: 这些细胞沿着茎呈梯状排列。

e.en: The markings ran {scalariformly} across the old shell.
e.zh: 这些纹路以梯纹方式横贯旧壳。

e.en: That old {scalawag} cheated everyone at cards.
e.zh: 那个老无赖打牌时骗了所有人。

e.en: Come here, you little {scalawag}, and wash your hands.
e.zh: 过来，你这个小调皮，去洗手。

e.en: The fisherman recognized the {scaldfish} at once.
e.zh: 渔夫一眼就认出了那条scaldfish比目鱼。

e.en: A {scaldfish} lay flat against the sandy bottom.
e.zh: 一条scaldfish贴着沙质海底平躺着。

e.en: The lecture focused on {scaldic} poetry from medieval Iceland.
e.zh: 讲座聚焦于中世纪冰岛的北欧吟游诗。

e.en: Her translation preserved the harsh {scaldic} rhythm.
e.zh: 她的译文保留了那种粗粝的北欧吟游诗节奏。

e.en: The company will {scale-down} production next month.
e.zh: 公司下个月将缩小生产规模。

e.en: Use this option to {scale-down} the image before printing.
e.zh: 打印前可用这个选项按比例缩小图片。

e.en: The startup needs funding to {scale-up} quickly.
e.zh: 这家初创公司需要资金来迅速扩大规模。

e.en: You can {scale-up} the drawing without losing detail.
e.zh: 你可以放大这幅图而不损失细节。

e.en: The armor was covered with delicate {scale-work}.
e.zh: 这副盔甲覆有精细的鳞片装饰。

e.en: She studied medieval {scale-work} on metal shields.
e.zh: 她研究中世纪金属盾牌上的鳞纹工艺。

e.en: A loose {scaleboard} rattled in the old wall.
e.zh: 旧墙里一块松动的薄木板咯咯作响。

e.en: The carpenter replaced each damaged {scaleboard} carefully.
e.zh: 木匠小心更换了每块受损的薄板。

e.en: They presented a {scaled-down} version of the proposal.
e.zh: 他们提交了一个缩小版的方案。

e.en: The museum displayed a {scaled-down} model of the bridge.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一座桥的缩小模型。

scaled-work.t: 鳞片装饰工艺；鳞状作品

e.en: The helmet's {scaled-work} caught the torchlight.
e.zh: 头盔上的鳞片装饰映着火把的光。

e.en: Restorers cleaned the ancient {scaled-work} by hand.
e.zh: 修复人员手工清理了古老的鳞状工艺品。

e.en: A tiny {scaledwing} rested on the window frame.
e.zh: 一只小鳞翅昆虫停在窗框上。

e.en: The guide identified the moth as a {scaledwing}.
e.zh: 向导把那只蛾认定为鳞翅类昆虫。

e.en: The {scaleless} fish looked smooth and pale.
e.zh: 这条无鳞鱼看起来光滑而苍白。

e.en: Some snakes have nearly {scaleless} patches of skin.
e.zh: 有些蛇的皮肤上有几乎无鳞的斑块。

e.en: The mineral formed {scalelike} layers on the rock.
e.zh: 这种矿物在岩石上形成鳞片状层。

e.en: Her costume had {scalelike} panels across the shoulders.
e.zh: 她的服装肩部有类似鳞片的拼片。

e.en: A {scalene} triangle has three unequal sides.
e.zh: 不等边三角形有三条不相等的边。

e.en: The therapist checked the tight {scalene} muscle in his neck.
e.zh: 治疗师检查了他颈部紧绷的斜角肌。

e.en: The surgeon discussed {scalenotomy} as a possible treatment.
e.zh: 外科医生讨论了斜角肌切开术作为可能的治疗方案。

e.en: Recovery after {scalenotomy} required careful neck exercises.
e.zh: 斜角肌切开术后的恢复需要谨慎做颈部练习。

e.en: The anterior {scalenus} can affect nerves in the neck.
e.zh: 前斜角肌可能影响颈部神经。

e.en: He felt pain near the right {scalenus} after lifting boxes.
e.zh: 搬箱子后，他右侧斜角肌附近感到疼痛。

e.en: She placed the coins on the left {scalepan}.
e.zh: 她把硬币放在左边的天平盘上。

e.en: The empty {scalepan} swung gently in the draft.
e.zh: 空秤盘在气流中轻轻晃动。

e.en: The biologist photographed a rare {scaletail} in the forest.
e.zh: 生物学家在森林里拍到一种罕见的鳞尾动物。

e.en: A {scaletail} uses its rough tail for climbing.
e.zh: 鳞尾动物会用粗糙的尾巴攀爬。

e.en: The old book called the butterfly a {scalewing}.
e.zh: 那本旧书把蝴蝶称作鳞翅昆虫。

e.en: Each {scalewing} was pinned carefully in the collection.
e.zh: 收藏中的每只鳞翅昆虫都被小心钉好。

e.en: This lizard is {scalier} than the green one.
e.zh: 这只蜥蜴比那只绿色的鳞片更多。

e.en: The bark felt {scalier} near the base of the tree.
e.zh: 树干底部附近的树皮摸起来更粗糙像鳞片。

e.en: The oldest fish had the {scaliest} skin.
e.zh: 最老的那条鱼皮肤鳞片最多。

e.en: That was the {scaliest} patch of bark on the trunk.
e.zh: 那是树干上最粗糙、最像鳞片的一块树皮。

scandalmonger.t: 散布丑闻者；造谣生事者

e.en: The columnist was dismissed as a {scandalmonger} by the mayor.
e.zh: 市长把那位专栏作家斥为散布丑闻的人。

e.en: No one trusted the old {scandalmonger} at the club.
e.zh: 俱乐部里没人信任那个爱搬弄是非的老家伙。

e.en: The paper was accused of {scandalmongering} during the trial.
e.zh: 那家报纸被指在审判期间散布丑闻。

e.en: Her speech avoided policy and slipped into {scandalmongering}.
e.zh: 她的演讲避开政策，转而搬弄是非。

e.en: The actor refused to answer the {scandalmongers} outside the hotel.
e.zh: 那位演员拒绝回应酒店外那些散布丑闻的人。

e.en: Online {scandalmongers} spread rumors before the facts were known.
e.zh: 事实还未查清，网上的造谣者就开始传播流言。

e.en: The botanist noted the plant's {scandent} stems.
e.zh: 植物学家注意到这种植物有攀缘茎。

e.en: A {scandent} vine covered the old stone wall.
e.zh: 一株攀缘藤蔓覆盖了那面旧石墙。

e.en: The ceramic contains a small amount of {scandia}.
e.zh: 这种陶瓷含有少量氧化钪。

e.en: Researchers tested {scandia} in high-temperature fuel cells.
e.zh: 研究人员在高温燃料电池中测试了氧化钪。

e.en: The chemist measured the {scandic} compound carefully.
e.zh: 化学家仔细测量了这种钪化合物。

e.en: A faint line indicated a {scandic} impurity in the sample.
e.zh: 一条微弱谱线表明样品中有含钪杂质。

scanistor.t: 扫描电阻器；扫描管器件

e.en: The engineer replaced a faulty {scanistor} in the old display unit.
e.zh: 工程师更换了旧显示装置里一个故障的扫描电阻器。

e.en: Few students had ever seen a working {scanistor}.
e.zh: 几乎没有学生见过还能工作的扫描管器件。

e.en: Make the receipt {scannable} by printing a clear barcode.
e.zh: 打印清晰的条形码，让收据可以扫描。

e.en: Short headings make the report more {scannable}.
e.zh: 简短标题让这份报告更便于快速浏览。

e.en: Woodpeckers have {scansorial} feet suited to tree trunks.
e.zh: 啄木鸟有适合攀附树干的攀爬型脚。

e.en: The fossil suggests a partly {scansorial} lifestyle.
e.zh: 这块化石表明它可能部分以攀爬方式生活。

e.en: The second report offered {scantier} evidence than the first.
e.zh: 第二份报告提供的证据比第一份更少。

e.en: As winter deepened, food became {scantier}.
e.zh: 随着冬天加深，食物变得更加匮乏。

e.en: The {scantiness} of the evidence worried the judge.
e.zh: 证据的不足让法官感到担忧。

e.en: Readers noticed the {scantiness} of detail in the memoir.
e.zh: 读者注意到这本回忆录细节贫乏。

e.en: The crew had to {scantle} their food during the voyage.
e.zh: 船员们在航行中不得不节省食物。

e.en: Old builders would {scantle} the timber before cutting it.
e.zh: 旧时工匠会先把木料分量规划好再切割。

e.en: The carpenter chose a straight {scantling} for the frame.
e.zh: 木匠选了一根笔直的小木料做框架。

e.en: The ship's plans specified every {scantling}.
e.zh: 船舶图纸标明了每个构件的尺寸。

e.en: The report criticized the company's culture of {scapegoatism}.
e.zh: 报告批评了公司把责任推给他人的文化。

e.en: Political {scapegoatism} can distract voters from real failures.
e.zh: 政治上的替罪羊做法会让选民忽视真正的失误。

e.en: The young {scapegrace} spent his inheritance in a year.
e.zh: 那个年轻败家子一年内花光了遗产。

e.en: In the novel, the charming {scapegrace} finally reforms.
e.zh: 小说中那个迷人的浪子最终改过自新。

e.en: The watchmaker cleaned the {scapement} with a fine brush.
e.zh: 钟表匠用细刷清理了擒纵机构。

e.en: A damaged {scapement} made the clock run unevenly.
e.zh: 擒纵机构受损导致时钟走时不均。

e.en: The insect's {scaphium} was visible under the microscope.
e.zh: 在显微镜下可以看到这只昆虫的舟状结构。

e.en: The old anatomy text labeled the part as a {scaphium}.
e.zh: 那本旧解剖书把这个部位标作小舟形器官。

e.en: The infant was diagnosed with {scaphocephaly} after imaging tests.
e.zh: 影像检查后，婴儿被诊断为舟状头畸形。

e.en: Surgery can sometimes correct severe {scaphocephaly}.
e.zh: 手术有时可以矫正严重的舟状头畸形。

e.en: The shrimp's {scaphocerite} helps protect the antenna.
e.zh: 虾的鳞片状触角附肢有助于保护触角。

e.en: She sketched the {scaphocerite} while describing the specimen.
e.zh: 她一边描述标本，一边画下鳞片状触角附肢。

e.en: He fractured his {scaphoid} during the fall.
e.zh: 他摔倒时造成舟骨骨折。

e.en: The surgeon examined the {scaphoid} shape on the scan.
e.zh: 外科医生在扫描图上检查了舟状形态。

e.en: The museum displayed a tiny {scaphopod} shell.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一枚小小的掘足类贝壳。

e.en: A {scaphopod} lives partly buried in marine sediment.
e.zh: 掘足类软体动物部分埋在海底沉积物中生活。

scareheadline.t: 耸人听闻的标题；恐吓式标题

e.en: The editor rejected the {scareheadline} as misleading.
e.zh: 编辑认为那个耸人听闻的标题有误导性，便退了回去。

e.en: A {scareheadline} can drive clicks but damage trust.
e.zh: 恐吓式标题能带来点击量，却会损害信任。

e.en: The ad opened with a familiar {scareline} about crime.
e.zh: 那则广告一开头就是一句关于犯罪的常见恐吓台词。

e.en: Workers painted a red {scareline} around the unsafe floor.
e.zh: 工人在危险地面周围画了一条红色警戒线。

e.en: The old house looked {scarey} after dark.
e.zh: 天黑后那座老房子看起来很吓人。

e.en: She laughed at the {scarey} mask in the shop.
e.zh: 她看到店里那个吓人的面具，忍不住笑了。

e.en: She fastened the silk scarf with a silver {scarf-ring}.
e.zh: 她用一个银色丝巾扣固定住那条丝巾。

e.en: A simple {scarf-ring} can change the whole outfit.
e.zh: 一个简单的围巾环就能改变整套穿搭的感觉。

e.en: The villagers called the stranger {scarface} behind his back.
e.zh: 村民们在背后叫那个陌生人为疤脸。

e.en: In the old novel, {scarface} was feared by everyone.
e.zh: 在那本旧小说里，那个疤脸人让所有人都害怕。

e.en: The carpenter used a {scarfjoint} to lengthen the beam.
e.zh: 木匠用斜接榫把横梁接长。

e.en: A well-cut {scarfjoint} makes the repair almost invisible.
e.zh: 切得好的嵌接接头会让修补处几乎看不出来。

e.en: He wore a pearl {scarfpin} with his evening clothes.
e.zh: 他穿晚礼服时戴了一枚珍珠领巾针。

e.en: The {scarfpin} kept her scarf from slipping in the wind.
e.zh: 那枚围巾别针让她的围巾在风中不再滑落。

e.en: The fruit had a dry {scarfskin} after weeks in storage.
e.zh: 那水果存放数周后，表面形成了一层干薄外皮。

e.en: He peeled away the {scarfskin} before examining the wound.
e.zh: 他先剥开表层皮，再检查伤口。

e.en: The pipe was strengthened with a careful {scarfweld}.
e.zh: 管道通过一道细致的斜接焊缝得到加固。

e.en: A poor {scarfweld} may crack under pressure.
e.zh: 质量差的搭接焊在受压时可能开裂。

e.en: The old doctor cleaned the {scaricator} before use.
e.zh: 那位老医生在使用前清洁了划痕器。

e.en: A {scaricator} was once used to make small cuts in the skin.
e.zh: 过去人们曾用浅切器在皮肤上划出小口。

e.en: Seed {scarification} helps water enter the hard shell.
e.zh: 种子划痕处理有助于水分进入坚硬外壳。

e.en: In some cultures, {scarification} marks identity or status.
e.zh: 在一些文化中，刻痕纹身象征身份或地位。

e.en: The museum displayed a brass {scarificator} from the nineteenth century.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一件十九世纪的黄铜放血划痕器。

e.en: A {scarificator} made several tiny cuts at once.
e.zh: 这种浅切器能一次划出好几道小口。

e.en: The gardener used a {scarifier} to clear moss from the lawn.
e.zh: 园丁用松土机清除草坪上的苔藓。

e.en: A small {scarifier} can scratch seeds before planting.
e.zh: 小型划痕器可以在播种前刮破种皮。

e.en: Stop {scarin} the little kids with that story.
e.zh: 别再用那个故事吓唬小孩子了。

e.en: He was only {scarin} us for a laugh.
e.zh: 他只是为了逗乐才吓唬我们。

e.en: The botanist noted the flower's {scariose} bracts.
e.zh: 植物学家注意到那朵花有干膜质苞片。

e.en: A {scariose} edge made the leaf feel papery.
e.zh: 干膜质的边缘让叶片摸起来像纸一样。

scarious.t: 干膜质的；纸质薄膜状的

e.en: The plant has {scarious} margins on its leaves.
e.zh: 这种植物的叶缘呈干膜质。

e.en: Herbarium notes described the petals as thin and {scarious}.
e.zh: 标本记录把花瓣描述为又薄又呈纸质膜状。

e.en: The child recovered from {scarlatina} after several weeks.
e.zh: 那个孩子几周后从猩红热中康复。

e.en: Doctors once feared outbreaks of {scarlatina} in crowded schools.
e.zh: 过去医生很担心拥挤学校里暴发猩红热。

e.en: The patient developed a {scarlatiniform} rash overnight.
e.zh: 病人一夜之间出现了猩红热样皮疹。

e.en: A {scarlatiniform} eruption does not always mean scarlet fever.
e.zh: 猩红热样发疹并不一定表示患了猩红热。

e.en: The surgery left her skin almost {scarless}.
e.zh: 手术后她的皮肤几乎没有留下疤痕。

e.en: The company advertised a {scarless} treatment for minor cuts.
e.zh: 公司宣传一种针对小伤口的不留疤治疗。

scaroid.t: 鹦嘴鱼样的；似鹦嘴鱼的

e.en: The diver noticed a {scaroid} fish near the reef.
e.zh: 潜水员注意到礁石附近有一条像鹦嘴鱼的鱼。

e.en: Its beaklike mouth gave it a {scaroid} appearance.
e.zh: 它那像喙一样的嘴让它显得像鹦嘴鱼。

e.en: The surgeon recommended {scarpectomy} after other treatments failed.
e.zh: 其他治疗失败后，外科医生建议进行腕骨切除术。

e.en: Recovery from {scarpectomy} can require careful hand therapy.
e.zh: 腕骨切除术后的恢复可能需要细致的手部康复治疗。

e.en: The fossil has a {scapiform} plate near the edge.
e.zh: 这块化石边缘附近有一片匙形板。

e.en: Botanists described the leaf base as {scapiform}.
e.zh: 植物学家把叶基描述为肩胛状。

e.en: The collector identified the pale crystal as {scapolite}.
e.zh: 收藏者认出那块浅色晶体是方柱石。

e.en: Some {scapolite} glows under ultraviolet light.
e.zh: 有些方柱石在紫外线下会发光。

e.en: The specimen was {scapped}, with flowers rising above the leaves.
e.zh: 这个标本有花葶，花高出叶片。

e.en: A {scapped} plant may look almost leafless at first.
e.zh: 有花葶的植物乍看可能几乎没有叶子。

e.en: The mason used a hammer to {scapple} the block.
e.zh: 石匠用锤子粗凿那块石料。

e.en: Fresh {scapple} marks covered the old wall stone.
e.zh: 旧墙石上布满新近粗修的凿痕。

e.en: The X-ray showed both {scapulae} clearly.
e.zh: X光片清楚显示了两侧肩胛骨。

e.en: Bird {scapulae} are long and narrow compared with ours.
e.zh: 鸟类的肩胛骨和人类相比又长又窄。

e.en: The monk wore a dark {scapulary} over his robe.
e.zh: 那位修士在长袍外披着深色肩衣。

e.en: The report noted pain in the {scapulary} region.
e.zh: 报告记录了肩胛区域的疼痛。

e.en: A small {scapulet} hung from the pilgrim's neck.
e.zh: 朝圣者脖子上挂着一件小肩衣。

e.en: The uniform had a decorative {scapulet} on each shoulder.
e.zh: 制服每个肩头都有一枚装饰性小肩章。

e.en: The flower rose on a thin {scapulus}.
e.zh: 那朵花长在一根细长花葶上。

e.en: She measured the {scapulus} before pressing the plant.
e.zh: 她在压制植物标本前量了花葶。

e.en: A {scar-faced} guard watched the gate in silence.
e.zh: 一个脸上有疤的守卫默默看着大门。

e.en: The novel's {scar-faced} hero rarely spoke about the war.
e.zh: 小说里那位脸上有疤的英雄很少谈起战争。

e.en: The museum displayed a {scarabaean} amulet from Egypt.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一枚埃及圣甲虫护身符。

e.en: The beetle's {scarabaean} shape made it easy to classify.
e.zh: 这只甲虫的金龟子形态使分类变得容易。

e.en: Ancient artists carved {scarabaei} from blue stone.
e.zh: 古代工匠用蓝色石料雕刻圣甲虫。

e.en: Several {scarabaei} were pinned in the insect drawer.
e.zh: 昆虫抽屉里钉着几只金龟子。

e.en: The larva belonged to a common {scarabaeid}.
e.zh: 这条幼虫属于一种常见金龟子科甲虫。

e.en: A large {scarabaeid} crawled under the porch light.
e.zh: 一只大型金龟子科甲虫爬到门廊灯下。

scarabaeoid.t: 似圣甲虫的；金龟子总科的

e.en: The jewel had a {scarabaeoid} form and a flat base.
e.zh: 这件珠宝呈圣甲虫状，底部平坦。

e.en: Researchers compared several {scarabaeoid} beetle families.
e.zh: 研究人员比较了几个金龟子总科甲虫科。

e.en: The {scarabaeus} was sacred in ancient Egyptian art.
e.zh: 圣甲虫在古埃及艺术中具有神圣意义。

e.en: A black {scarabaeus} rolled dung across the path.
e.zh: 一只黑色蜣螂把粪球滚过小路。

e.en: The pendant was {scaraboid}, with tiny carved legs.
e.zh: 吊坠呈甲虫形，还刻有细小的腿。

e.en: They found a {scaraboid} insect near the compost heap.
e.zh: 他们在堆肥旁发现了一只像金龟子的昆虫。

e.en: The play's {scaramouch} bragged loudly and ran away first.
e.zh: 剧中的吹牛小丑叫得最响，却第一个逃跑。

e.en: He dismissed the loud politician as a {scaramouch}.
e.zh: 他把那个吵闹的政客斥为滑稽的吹牛人。

scaramouche.t: 意式喜剧丑角；吹牛胆小鬼

e.en: The actor entered as {scaramouche} with a swaggering bow.
e.zh: 演员扮成意式喜剧丑角，趾高气扬地鞠躬登场。

e.en: Behind his threats, he was only a {scaramouche}.
e.zh: 他的威胁背后，不过是个吹牛胆小鬼。

e.en: The geologist found {scarbroite} in the clay deposit.
e.zh: 地质学家在黏土矿层中发现了斯卡布罗石。

e.en: Pure {scarbroite} is a rare hydrated aluminum carbonate.
e.zh: 纯斯卡布罗石是一种罕见的含水碳酸铝矿物。

e.en: Rain collected on the narrow {scarcement} of the tower.
e.zh: 雨水积在塔身狭窄的墙面退台上。

e.en: The old wall shows a clear {scarcement} above the foundation.
e.zh: 旧墙在地基上方有明显的收分台阶。

e.en: The editor rejected the {scare-head} as too misleading.
e.zh: 编辑认为那个耸人听闻的标题太误导人，便拒用了。

e.en: A bold {scare-head} made the minor story seem urgent.
e.zh: 一个醒目的惊悚标题让小新闻显得很紧急。

scarecrowish.t: 稻草人似的；瘦削破烂的

e.en: He looked {scarecrowish} in the oversized coat.
e.zh: 他穿着过大的外套，看起来像稻草人一样瘦削。

e.en: The garden had a {scarecrowish} figure by the beans.
e.zh: 菜园豆架旁有个稻草人似的身影。

e.en: Don't be a {scaredy-cat}; the movie is not that scary.
e.zh: 别当胆小鬼，这部电影没那么吓人。

e.en: As a child, I was a {scaredy-cat} around dogs.
e.zh: 小时候我见到狗就很胆小。

e.en: The newspaper printed a huge {scarehead} above the story.
e.zh: 报纸在那篇报道上方印了一个巨大的耸动标题。

e.en: Online ads often use a {scarehead} to win clicks.
e.zh: 网络广告常用惊吓式标题来骗取点击。

scareheading.t: 制作耸动标题；标题恐吓手法

e.en: The editor accused the site of {scareheading} public health news.
e.zh: 编辑指责该网站给公共卫生新闻做耸动标题。

e.en: Good reporting should avoid {scareheading} complex risks.
e.zh: 好的报道应避免用标题恐吓来处理复杂风险。

scarphed.t: 有陡峭岩坡的；似峭壁的

e.en: The {scarphed} hillside rose sharply above the road.
e.zh: 那片有陡峭岩坡的山坡在路边高高耸起。

e.en: They crossed a {scarphed} coast after the storm.
e.zh: 风暴过后，他们穿过了峭壁般的海岸。

e.en: His {scarry} hands showed years of hard work.
e.zh: 他满是伤痕的双手显示出多年辛劳。

e.en: The old table had a {scarry} surface.
e.zh: 那张旧桌子的表面布满划痕。

e.en: The branch left a {scart} on his cheek.
e.zh: 树枝在他的脸颊上留下一道划痕。

e.en: Try not to {scart} the polished wood.
e.zh: 尽量不要刮伤这块抛光木材。

e.en: The {scatback} slipped through the defensive line.
e.zh: 那名小而敏捷的跑卫从防线中钻了过去。

e.en: Their offense depends on a fast {scatback}.
e.zh: 他们的进攻依赖一名速度很快的小个跑卫。

scatheless.t: 未受伤害的；安然无恙的

e.en: She escaped the crash {scatheless}.
e.zh: 她在那场撞车事故中安然无恙地逃了出来。

e.en: The old bridge stood {scatheless} after the flood.
e.zh: 洪水过后，那座老桥仍未受损。

e.en: The chemist identified {scatol} in the sample.
e.zh: 化学家在样本中检测出了粪臭素。

e.en: Tiny amounts of {scatol} can affect a perfume.
e.zh: 微量粪臭素也可能影响香水的气味。

e.en: The lecture discussed {scatology} in medieval medicine.
e.zh: 讲座讨论了中世纪医学中的粪便学。

e.en: His comedy relied too much on {scatology}.
e.zh: 他的喜剧太依赖屎尿笑话了。

e.en: The scan revealed a {scatoma} in the colon.
e.zh: 扫描显示结肠内有一块粪石。

e.en: Doctors removed the painful {scatoma} carefully.
e.zh: 医生小心取出了那块令人疼痛的硬粪块。

e.en: Some beetles are {scatophagous} as larvae.
e.zh: 有些甲虫在幼虫阶段以粪便为食。

e.en: The study focused on {scatophagous} insects.
e.zh: 这项研究关注食粪昆虫。

e.en: The doctor ordered {scatoscopy} after the symptoms worsened.
e.zh: 症状加重后，医生要求进行粪便检查。

e.en: Ancient physicians sometimes used {scatoscopy} for diagnosis.
e.zh: 古代医师有时用验粪来辅助诊断。

e.en: The singer began to {scatt} over the bass line.
e.zh: 歌手开始随着低音线即兴拟声演唱。

e.en: Her playful {scatt} delighted the jazz crowd.
e.zh: 她俏皮的即兴拟声演唱让爵士乐听众很开心。

e.en: He kept a {scatter-gun} behind the farmhouse door.
e.zh: 他把一支霰弹枪放在农舍门后。

e.en: The report took a {scatter-gun} approach to policy.
e.zh: 这份报告对政策采取了漫无重点的做法。

e.en: The instrument measured light {scatterance} in the water.
e.zh: 仪器测量了水中的光散射程度。

e.en: Higher {scatterance} made the image look cloudy.
e.zh: 更高的散射量使图像显得浑浊。

e.en: The radar display showed a wide {scatterband}.
e.zh: 雷达显示屏上出现了一条很宽的散射带。

e.en: Engineers adjusted the receiver for the {scatterband}.
e.zh: 工程师针对散布频带调整了接收器。

e.en: I am such a {scatterbrain} before deadlines.
e.zh: 截止日期前我真是个糊涂虫。

e.en: The lovable {scatterbrain} forgot his own address.
e.zh: 那个可爱的健忘鬼连自己的地址都忘了。

e.en: Those {scatterbrains} left the tickets at home.
e.zh: 那些糊涂虫把票落在家里了。

e.en: The team of {scatterbrains} still solved the problem.
e.zh: 这群健忘的人最后还是解决了问题。

e.en: The old novel mocked a cheerful {scattergood}.
e.zh: 那本老小说嘲笑了一个乐天的挥霍者。

e.en: He lived like a {scattergood} until his money vanished.
e.zh: 他像个败家子一样生活，直到钱花光。

e.en: The analyst drew a {scattergram} of sales and price.
e.zh: 分析师绘制了销售额和价格的散点图。

e.en: A {scattergram} can reveal unusual data points.
e.zh: 散点图能显示异常的数据点。

e.en: The {scattergraph} showed no clear relationship.
e.zh: 这张散点图没有显示出明确关系。

e.en: She used a {scattergraph} to compare the results.
e.zh: 她用散布图来比较这些结果。

e.en: The farmer carried a {scattergun} through the field.
e.zh: 农夫带着一支霰弹枪穿过田地。

e.en: Their campaign used a {scattergun} strategy online.
e.zh: 他们的线上宣传采用了漫无重点的策略。

e.en: The museum displayed antique {scatterguns} from the frontier.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了边疆时期的古董霰弹枪。

e.en: Management {scatterguns} resources across too many projects.
e.zh: 管理层把资源广撒到太多项目上。

e.en: The satellite used a {scatterometer} to estimate wind speed.
e.zh: 卫星用散射计估算风速。

e.en: A broken {scatterometer} delayed the ocean survey.
e.zh: 一台损坏的散射测量仪耽误了海洋调查。

e.en: She placed a {scatterrug} beside the bed.
e.zh: 她在床边放了一块小地毯。

e.en: The bright {scatterrug} warmed the hallway.
e.zh: 那块鲜艳的装饰小毯让走廊显得更温暖。

scattershot.t: 漫无目标的；胡乱的；零散的

e.en: The report took a {scattershot} approach to the problem.
e.zh: 这份报告用一种零散随意的方式处理这个问题。

e.en: His {scattershot} comments confused the whole team.
e.zh: 他东一句西一句的评论让整个团队都糊涂了。

scattier.t: 更糊涂的；更心不在焉的

e.en: She became {scattier} as the deadline approached.
e.zh: 截止日期越近，她就越心不在焉。

e.en: This draft is even {scattier} than the last one.
e.zh: 这份草稿比上一版还要杂乱无章。

scattiest.t: 最糊涂的；最心不在焉的

e.en: He is the {scattiest} person in the office.
e.zh: 他是办公室里最迷糊的人。

e.en: The {scattiest} parts of the lecture came near the end.
e.zh: 讲座最散乱的部分出现在接近结尾时。

scattily.t: 糊涂地；心不在焉地；散乱地

e.en: She packed {scattily} and forgot her passport.
e.zh: 她收拾东西时心不在焉，结果忘了护照。

e.en: The ideas were presented {scattily} throughout the essay.
e.zh: 这些观点在整篇文章里呈现得很散乱。

e.en: The valley was {scaturient} with hidden springs.
e.zh: 山谷里暗泉涌动，水源不断。

e.en: Her mind seemed {scaturient} with new ideas.
e.zh: 她的脑子里似乎不断涌出新想法。

e.en: The path ended below a dark {scaur}.
e.zh: 小路在一处阴暗的峭壁下结束。

e.en: Sheep grazed near the rocky {scaur}.
e.zh: 羊群在岩石陡坡附近吃草。

scazon.t: 跛脚抑扬格；古希腊讽刺诗格

e.en: The poem ends with a deliberate {scazon}.
e.zh: 这首诗以一个有意安排的跛脚抑扬格结尾。

e.en: He analyzed the {scazon} in the Greek verse.
e.zh: 他分析了那段希腊诗中的跛脚诗格。

scedasticity.t: 离散性；统计中的方差特性

e.en: The model assumes constant {scedasticity} across observations.
e.zh: 这个模型假定各个观测值具有恒定的方差特性。

e.en: Uneven {scedasticity} can distort the regression results.
e.zh: 不均匀的离散性可能扭曲回归结果。

e.en: The old drama presents him as a {scelerat}.
e.zh: 这部老戏把他塑造成一个恶棍。

e.en: Only a {scelerat} would betray them so coldly.
e.zh: 只有罪大恶极的人才会如此冷酷地背叛他们。

e.en: The judge condemned his {sceleratine} scheme.
e.zh: 法官谴责了他邪恶的阴谋。

e.en: A {sceleratine} mood hangs over the tragedy.
e.zh: 一种罪恶阴森的气氛笼罩着这出悲剧。

scena.t: 歌剧中的独唱场景；戏剧场面

e.en: The soprano's {scena} stopped the opera cold.
e.zh: 女高音的独唱场景让整部歌剧瞬间凝住。

e.en: He wrote a tense {scena} for the final act.
e.zh: 他为最后一幕写了一个紧张的戏剧场面。

e.en: The {scenarist} revised the ending overnight.
e.zh: 电影编剧连夜修改了结尾。

e.en: A skilled {scenarist} can shape a loose idea into drama.
e.zh: 熟练的剧本作者能把松散的想法塑造成戏剧。

e.en: They plan to {scenarize} the novel for television.
e.zh: 他们计划把这部小说改编成电视剧本。

e.en: The team tried to {scenarize} several disaster responses.
e.zh: 团队试着设想几种灾害应对情景。

scend.t: 随浪升起；船体随浪纵摇

e.en: The boat began to {scend} over the swell.
e.zh: 小船开始随着涌浪上下起伏。

e.en: Sailors watched the bow {scend} in the heavy sea.
e.zh: 水手们看着船头在大浪中上扬。

e.en: The {scending} vessel made everyone uneasy.
e.zh: 船身随浪纵摇，让所有人都不安。

e.en: We felt the deck {scending} under our feet.
e.zh: 我们感到甲板在脚下随浪起伏。

e.en: The dinghy {scends} sharply after each wave.
e.zh: 每道浪过后，小艇都会猛地上扬。

e.en: A heavy ship {scends} more slowly in rough water.
e.zh: 重船在汹涌海面上随浪起伏得更慢。

e.en: Police sealed off the {scene-of-crime} area.
e.zh: 警方封锁了犯罪现场区域。

e.en: Photographs from the {scene-of-crime} report were missing.
e.zh: 犯罪现场报告中的照片不见了。

scene-shifter.t: 舞台换景工；改变局面者

e.en: A {scene-shifter} moved the walls between acts.
e.zh: 一名舞台换景工在幕间移动布景墙。

e.en: That early goal was the real {scene-shifter}.
e.zh: 那个早早的进球才是真正改变局面的因素。

scene-stealer.t: 抢戏的人；特别吸引眼球者

e.en: The child actor was a natural {scene-stealer}.
e.zh: 那个童星天生就很抢戏。

e.en: Her red coat became the {scene-stealer} of the photo.
e.zh: 她的红外套成了照片里最吸引眼球的东西。

scenedock.t: 舞台布景存放区；布景码头

e.en: The flats were stored in the {scenedock}.
e.zh: 那些平面布景被存放在舞台布景库里。

e.en: Workers carried the old set through the {scenedock}.
e.zh: 工人们把旧布景从布景存放区搬过去。

e.en: The {sceneman} repaired the painted backdrop.
e.zh: 舞台布景工修好了那块彩绘背景布。

e.en: A veteran {sceneman} knew every rope backstage.
e.zh: 一位老布景师熟悉后台的每一根绳索。

e.en: The {scenemen} changed the set in darkness.
e.zh: 布景工们在黑暗中更换了舞台布景。

e.en: Experienced {scenemen} kept the production running smoothly.
e.zh: 经验丰富的布景师们让演出顺利进行。

scenepainter.t: 舞台布景画师；布景绘制者

e.en: The {scenepainter} added depth with pale blue shadows.
e.zh: 舞台布景画师用淡蓝色阴影增加了纵深感。

e.en: A good {scenepainter} can suggest a city with a few strokes.
e.zh: 优秀的布景绘制者几笔就能勾出一座城市的感觉。

scenepainting.t: 舞台布景绘画；景片绘制

e.en: The old theatre still teaches {scenepainting} by hand.
e.zh: 那家老剧院仍然教授手工舞台布景绘画。

e.en: Her {scenepainting} made the small stage look deep.
e.zh: 她的景片绘制让小舞台显得很有纵深。

e.en: A {sceneshifter} moved the painted wall between acts.
e.zh: 一名换景工在两幕之间移走了彩绘墙。

e.en: He worked backstage as a {sceneshifter} during college.
e.zh: 他大学时在后台做过搬景人员。

scenester.t: 小圈子潮人；场景圈中人

e.en: Every local {scenester} seemed to know the new band.
e.zh: 当地小圈子里的潮人似乎都认识那支新乐队。

e.en: The cafe became a meeting place for art {scenesters}.
e.zh: 那家咖啡馆成了艺术圈中人聚会的地方。

scenical.t: 风景优美的；舞台布景的

e.en: They chose a {scenical} route through the hills.
e.zh: 他们选择了一条穿过群山的风景优美路线。

e.en: The director praised the play's {scenical} effects.
e.zh: 导演称赞了这出戏的舞台布景效果。

scenograph.t: 舞台布景图；透视场景图

e.en: The designer pinned a {scenograph} beside the model.
e.zh: 设计师把一张舞台布景图钉在模型旁边。

e.en: His {scenograph} showed how the square would appear from above.
e.zh: 他的透视场景图展示了广场从上方看去的样子。

scenographer.t: 舞台美术设计师；布景师

e.en: The {scenographer} built a city from sheets of metal.
e.zh: 舞台美术设计师用金属板搭出了一座城市。

e.en: As a {scenographer}, she thinks first about light and space.
e.zh: 作为布景师，她首先考虑光线和空间。

scenographical.t: 舞台美术的；布景设计的

e.en: The museum displayed his {scenographical} sketches for opera.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了他为歌剧所作的舞台美术草图。

e.en: Their {scenographical} choices made the room feel unreal.
e.zh: 他们的布景设计选择让这个房间显得不真实。

e.en: Modern {scenography} often uses video and moving light.
e.zh: 现代舞台美术常常使用视频和流动灯光。

e.en: The film's {scenography} borrowed heavily from old factories.
e.zh: 这部电影的布景设计大量借鉴了旧工厂的样貌。

e.en: She found a silver {scent-bottle} in the drawer.
e.zh: 她在抽屉里发现了一个银制香水瓶。

e.en: The antique {scent-bottle} still smelled faintly of roses.
e.zh: 那个古董香料小瓶仍隐约有玫瑰香。

e.en: The garden was {scentful} after the evening rain.
e.zh: 傍晚雨后，花园里芳香四溢。

e.en: She opened a {scentful} packet of dried lavender.
e.zh: 她打开了一包香气浓郁的干薰衣草。

e.en: The lab used a {scentometer} to compare the samples.
e.zh: 实验室用气味计比较这些样品。

e.en: A portable {scentometer} measured odors near the plant.
e.zh: 一台便携式嗅觉测量仪测量了工厂附近的气味。

e.en: Her {scepsis} made every easy answer sound doubtful.
e.zh: 她的怀疑态度让每个简单答案都显得可疑。

e.en: Ancient {scepsis} questioned whether certainty was possible.
e.zh: 古代怀疑论质疑确定性是否可能存在。

e.en: The statue showed a {scepterless} king with empty hands.
e.zh: 那座雕像刻画了一位两手空空、没有权杖的国王。

e.en: He called himself a {scepterless} ruler of a broken court.
e.zh: 他称自己是破败宫廷里无王权的统治者。

scepticize.t: 使怀疑；以怀疑态度看待

e.en: The scandal helped {scepticize} voters about official promises.
e.zh: 那起丑闻让选民对官方承诺产生怀疑。

e.en: Reading philosophy can {scepticize} even confident students.
e.zh: 阅读哲学会让即使很自信的学生也学会怀疑。

e.en: The crown and {sceptral} emblems filled the hall.
e.zh: 王冠和权杖象征物布满了大厅。

e.en: A {sceptral} ornament was carved above the throne.
e.zh: 王座上方雕着一个权杖式装饰。

e.en: The priest lifted the golden {sceptron} before the crowd.
e.zh: 祭司在人群面前举起金色权杖。

e.en: In the poem, the {sceptron} stands for fragile power.
e.zh: 在这首诗中，王权杖象征脆弱的权力。

e.en: The collector labeled the dark crystal as {schafarzikite}.
e.zh: 收藏者把那块深色晶体标为锑铁矿。

e.en: Rare {schafarzikite} was found in the old manganese deposit.
e.zh: 旧锰矿床中发现了罕见的沙法尔齐克石。

schairerite.t: 硫酸氟钠钾矿；沙伊勒石

e.en: The mineral sample contained tiny grains of {schairerite}.
e.zh: 这份矿物样品含有细小的硫酸氟钠钾矿颗粒。

e.en: Geologists identified {schairerite} in the saline deposit.
e.zh: 地质学家在盐类沉积物中鉴定出了沙伊勒石。

schamotte.t: 耐火熟料；耐火黏土砖料

e.en: The furnace lining was made with {schamotte}.
e.zh: 炉衬是用耐火熟料制成的。

e.en: Potters mix {schamotte} into clay for stronger vessels.
e.zh: 陶工把耐火黏土砖料掺进陶土中，使器皿更结实。

e.en: The mill produced fine {schappe} from silk waste.
e.zh: 这家纺织厂用废丝生产精细的绢纺纱。

e.en: Her scarf was woven with soft {schappe}.
e.zh: 她的围巾是用柔软的废丝纺纱织成的。

schedular.t: 调度程序；日程安排工具

e.en: The {schedular} assigns each task to an available processor.
e.zh: 这个调度程序把每个任务分配给可用的处理器。

e.en: A shared {schedular} helps the team avoid meeting conflicts.
e.zh: 共享的日程安排工具帮助团队避免会议冲突。

e.en: The geologist found {scheelite} in the old mine.
e.zh: 地质学家在那座旧矿井里发现了白钨矿。

e.en: Under ultraviolet light, {scheelite} often glows brightly.
e.zh: 在紫外线下，白钨矿常常会发出明亮的光。

e.en: She keeps a tall {schefflera} beside the window.
e.zh: 她在窗边养了一株高高的鹅掌柴。

e.en: The office {schefflera} needs less water in winter.
e.zh: 办公室里的伞树冬天需要少浇水。

e.en: The teacher asked students to {schematise} the argument.
e.zh: 老师要求学生把这个论证图式化。

e.en: Researchers often {schematise} complex behavior before modeling it.
e.zh: 研究人员常先系统整理复杂行为，再进行建模。

e.en: His theory depends on a rigid {schematism} of social roles.
e.zh: 他的理论依赖一种僵硬的社会角色图式体系。

e.en: Kant's {schematism} remains difficult for many philosophy students.
e.zh: 康德的先验图式论对许多哲学学生来说仍很难。

e.en: The report included a {schematogram} of the machine.
e.zh: 报告中包含了一张机器的示意图。

e.en: Doctors reviewed the {schematogram} before planning treatment.
e.zh: 医生在制定治疗方案前查看了这份图式记录。

schematograph.t: 绘制示意图的装置或方法

e.en: The engineer used a {schematograph} to map the circuit.
e.zh: 工程师用绘制示意图的装置来标出电路。

e.en: An early {schematograph} simplified complex mechanical drawings.
e.zh: 早期的示意图绘制方法简化了复杂的机械图纸。

e.en: The meeting became a complete {schemozzle} after lunch.
e.zh: 午饭后会议彻底变成了一团糟。

e.en: Their travel plans ended in a costly {schemozzle}.
e.zh: 他们的旅行计划最后变成了一场代价不小的混乱。

e.en: The specialist diagnosed a small {scheroma} near the cornea.
e.zh: 专科医生诊断出角膜附近有一小块干燥性硬斑。

e.en: Untreated dryness may lead to a painful {scheroma}.
e.zh: 干燥若不治疗，可能会形成疼痛的眼部硬斑。

e.en: The pianist played the passage {scherzando}.
e.zh: 钢琴家以诙谐活泼的方式演奏了这一段。

e.en: A {scherzando} mood lightens the final movement.
e.zh: 诙谐戏谑的情绪让最后一个乐章变得轻快。

e.en: The album includes two lively {scherzi} by Chopin.
e.zh: 这张专辑收录了肖邦的两首活泼谐谑曲。

e.en: Several {scherzi} in the concert demanded great speed.
e.zh: 音乐会中的几首谐谑曲都要求极快的速度。

e.en: The philosopher used {schesis} to describe relation rather than substance.
e.zh: 那位哲学家用schesis来描述关系，而不是实体。

e.en: In old rhetoric, {schesis} could mean a connected arrangement of ideas.
e.zh: 在古典修辞中，schesis可指思想之间的连贯安排。

e.en: The dress was finished with delicate {schiffli} embroidery.
e.zh: 这条裙子用精致的梭式机器刺绣收边。

e.en: Factories use {schiffli} machines for large lace patterns.
e.zh: 工厂用梭式刺绣机制作大幅蕾丝图案。

e.en: Geologists discussed {schillerization} in the altered feldspar sample.
e.zh: 地质学家讨论了这块蚀变长石样本中的闪彩作用。

e.en: The stone's sheen resulted from {schillerization} during its formation.
e.zh: 这块石头的光泽来自形成过程中的闪彩化作用。

e.en: Tiny inclusions can {schillerize} an otherwise plain mineral.
e.zh: 微小包裹体能让原本普通的矿物呈现闪彩。

e.en: Heat treatment may {schillerize} the surface of the specimen.
e.zh: 热处理可能使标本表面产生闪彩光泽。

e.en: Their {schipperke} barked whenever someone approached the gate.
e.zh: 每当有人靠近大门，他们的比利时小黑犬就会叫。

e.en: A {schipperke} is small, alert, and usually black.
e.zh: 比利时小黑犬体型小、警觉，通常是黑色的。

e.en: The bishop condemned the group's {schismatical} teachings.
e.zh: 主教谴责了该团体分裂教会的教义。

e.en: His {schismatical} tone alarmed the older members.
e.zh: 他那种带有分裂意味的语气让老成员感到不安。

e.en: The faction acted {schismatically} after rejecting church authority.
e.zh: 该派别拒绝教会权威后，以分裂教派的方式行事。

e.en: He spoke {schismatically}, urging followers to leave the congregation.
e.zh: 他说话带有分裂倾向，敦促追随者离开会众。

schismatist.t: 宗教分裂者；分裂派成员

e.en: The pamphlet accused him of being a {schismatist}.
e.zh: 那本小册子指控他是宗教分裂者。

e.en: A {schismatist} may reject the authority of the established church.
e.zh: 宗教分裂者可能拒绝既有教会的权威。

e.en: The dispute threatened to {schismatize} the small congregation.
e.zh: 这场争端可能使这个小会众发生分裂。

e.en: Leaders feared the doctrine would {schismatize} the movement.
e.zh: 领导者担心该教义会使这场运动分裂。

e.en: The church had {schismatized} after years of bitter argument.
e.zh: 多年激烈争论后，教会已经分裂。

e.en: A {schismatized} community often struggles to rebuild trust.
e.zh: 一个已经分裂的群体往往难以重建信任。

e.en: His {schismatizing} sermons divided the parish.
e.zh: 他那些造成分裂的布道使教区产生分歧。

e.en: They warned against {schismatizing} over minor rituals.
e.zh: 他们警告不要因小小的礼仪问题而制造分裂。

e.en: The reformers hoped for a {schismless} church.
e.zh: 改革者希望教会没有分裂、保持统一。

e.en: A {schismless} community can still contain sharp disagreement.
e.zh: 一个未分裂的共同体仍可能存在尖锐分歧。

e.en: The atlas listed {schistocormus} among rare congenital malformations.
e.zh: 图谱把躯干裂畸形列为罕见先天畸形之一。

e.en: Doctors used {schistocormus} to describe the severe body-wall defect.
e.zh: 医生用schistocormus描述这种严重的体壁缺损。

e.en: The blood smear showed more than one {schistocyte}.
e.zh: 血涂片显示不止一个裂红细胞。

e.en: A {schistocyte} can suggest mechanical damage to red blood cells.
e.zh: 裂红细胞可能提示红细胞受到机械性损伤。

e.en: The lab report noted mild {schistocytosis}.
e.zh: 实验室报告记录了轻度裂红细胞增多症。

e.en: Severe {schistocytosis} may accompany microangiopathic hemolysis.
e.zh: 严重裂红细胞增多症可能伴随微血管性溶血。

e.en: The newborn was examined for {schistoglossia}.
e.zh: 医生检查这名新生儿是否有舌裂畸形。

e.en: Rare cases of {schistoglossia} appear in older medical reports.
e.zh: 较早的医学报告中可见罕见的舌裂畸形病例。

e.en: The outcrop had a {schistoid} texture.
e.zh: 这处露头具有片岩状结构。

e.en: A {schistoid} rock splits along thin, shiny layers.
e.zh: 片岩状岩石会沿着薄而发亮的层面裂开。

e.en: The specimen was classified as {schistomelus} in the old catalogue.
e.zh: 这个标本在旧目录中被归为肢体裂畸胎。

e.en: Medical historians found the term {schistomelus} in a nineteenth-century text.
e.zh: 医学史研究者在一部十九世纪文本中发现了schistomelus一词。

e.en: The diagnosis mentioned {schistoprosopia} and other facial defects.
e.zh: 诊断提到面裂畸形以及其他面部缺损。

e.en: Surgeons rarely use {schistoprosopia} in modern clinical notes.
e.zh: 外科医生在现代临床记录中很少使用schistoprosopia一词。

e.en: The old report described {schistorachis} in the newborn.
e.zh: 那份旧报告描述了新生儿的脊柱裂畸形。

e.en: Severe {schistorachis} may expose the spinal cord.
e.zh: 严重的脊柱裂可能使脊髓外露。

e.en: The surgeon noted {schistorrhachis} during the examination.
e.zh: 外科医生在检查中注意到脊柱裂畸形。

e.en: Prenatal imaging can reveal {schistorrhachis} before birth.
e.zh: 产前影像检查可以在出生前发现脊柱裂。

e.en: The hillside was made of {schistose} rock.
e.zh: 那片山坡由片岩状岩石构成。

e.en: A {schistose} texture lets the stone split easily.
e.zh: 片岩状结构使这种石头容易劈开。

e.en: The clinic treated several cases of {schistosis}.
e.zh: 这家诊所治疗了几例血吸虫病。

e.en: Untreated {schistosis} can damage internal organs.
e.zh: 未经治疗的血吸虫病可能损害内脏器官。

e.en: The geologist measured the angle of {schistosity}.
e.zh: 地质学家测量了片理的角度。

e.en: Strong {schistosity} made the rock break into sheets.
e.zh: 明显的片理使岩石裂成薄片。

e.en: A {schistosome} can live in human blood vessels.
e.zh: 血吸虫可以寄生在人类血管中。

e.en: The drug targets the adult {schistosome}.
e.zh: 这种药物针对成虫阶段的血吸虫。

e.en: The village reported more {schistosomia} after the floods.
e.zh: 洪水过后，村里报告了更多血吸虫感染病例。

e.en: Doctors suspected {schistosomia} because of the patient's history.
e.zh: 医生因患者的接触史而怀疑血吸虫病。

schistosomicide.t: 杀血吸虫药；灭血吸虫剂

e.en: The trial compared a new {schistosomicide} with praziquantel.
e.zh: 这项试验把一种新的杀血吸虫药与吡喹酮作比较。

e.en: An effective {schistosomicide} reduces parasite numbers quickly.
e.zh: 有效的灭血吸虫剂能迅速减少寄生虫数量。

e.en: The larva becomes a {schistosomulum} after entering the skin.
e.zh: 幼虫进入皮肤后会变成血吸虫童虫。

e.en: Researchers tracked each {schistosomulum} through the bloodstream.
e.zh: 研究人员追踪每个血吸虫幼体在血流中的移动。

e.en: The infant was diagnosed with {schistosternia}.
e.zh: 这名婴儿被诊断为胸骨裂畸形。

e.en: Rare {schistosternia} may require early surgery.
e.zh: 罕见的胸骨裂畸形可能需要早期手术。

e.en: The valley exposed layers of {schistous} stone.
e.zh: 山谷露出了层层片岩状石头。

e.en: Miners avoided the {schistous} section because it crumbled.
e.zh: 矿工避开那段片岩状区域，因为它容易碎裂。

schitz.t: 精神分裂症患者的贬称

e.en: He regretted calling her a {schitz} in anger.
e.zh: 他后悔自己一时气愤骂她是精神分裂症患者。

e.en: The slur {schitz} is offensive and should be avoided.
e.zh: schitz 这个贬称带有冒犯性，应避免使用。

schiz.t: 精神分裂症患者的贬称

e.en: The character was cruelly labeled a {schiz}.
e.zh: 那个角色被残忍地贴上精神分裂症患者的标签。

e.en: Do not use {schiz} as a casual insult.
e.zh: 不要把 schiz 当作随口骂人的话来用。

schizandrin.t: 五味子素；五味子木脂素

e.en: The extract contained measurable {schizandrin}.
e.zh: 这种提取物含有可检测量的五味子素。

e.en: Researchers studied {schizandrin} for possible liver protection.
e.zh: 研究人员研究五味子素是否可能保护肝脏。

e.en: She planted {schizanthus} along the greenhouse path.
e.zh: 她在温室小路旁种了蛾蝶花。

e.en: The petals of {schizanthus} look almost painted.
e.zh: 蛾蝶花的花瓣看起来几乎像画上去的。

schizo.t: 精神分裂症患者的贬称；分裂的

e.en: Using {schizo} as an insult is stigmatizing.
e.zh: 把 schizo 当作侮辱语会加深污名。

e.en: The review called the film's tone {schizo} and uneven.
e.zh: 影评说这部电影的调子分裂而不均衡。

e.en: A maple fruit is a type of {schizocarp}.
e.zh: 枫树的果实是一种分裂果。

e.en: The dry {schizocarp} split into separate segments.
e.zh: 干燥的分裂果裂成了几个独立小段。

e.en: The fossil showed a {schizodont} tooth pattern.
e.zh: 这块化石显示出裂齿型的牙齿排列。

e.en: Specialists debated whether the shell was {schizodont}.
e.zh: 专家们争论这个贝壳是否属于裂齿型。

e.en: The parasite reproduces by {schizogenesis} in this stage.
e.zh: 这种寄生虫在这一阶段通过裂殖繁殖。

e.en: The lecture explained {schizogenesis} in simple diagrams.
e.zh: 讲座用简单图示解释了分裂生殖。

e.en: The paper described a {schizogenetic} cavity in the tissue.
e.zh: 论文描述了组织中一个裂生腔。

e.en: A {schizogenetic} process separated the cells gradually.
e.zh: 裂生过程使这些细胞逐渐分开。

e.en: The botanist identified {schizogenic} spaces in the leaf.
e.zh: 植物学家在叶片中识别出裂生空隙。

e.en: Some lesions had a {schizogenic} origin.
e.zh: 有些病变源于组织分裂形成。

e.en: Resin collects in {schizogenous} ducts within the plant.
e.zh: 树脂聚集在植物体内的裂生管道中。

e.en: The cavity was {schizogenous}, not caused by decay.
e.zh: 这个空腔是裂生形成的，并非腐烂造成。

e.en: The bird skull showed clear {schizognathism}.
e.zh: 这只鸟的头骨显示出明显的裂腭型结构。

e.en: Ornithologists once used {schizognathism} in classification.
e.zh: 鸟类学家过去曾用裂腭型来进行分类。

e.en: Malaria parasites undergo {schizogony} inside red blood cells.
e.zh: 疟原虫会在红细胞内进行裂殖生殖。

e.en: The textbook illustrates {schizogony} step by step.
e.zh: 教材一步步图解裂殖生殖。

schizoidia.t: 精神分裂样状态；分裂样人格

e.en: The psychiatrist used {schizoidia} in an old case note.
e.zh: 精神科医生在一份旧病例记录中使用了 schizoidia。

e.en: Modern texts rarely use {schizoidia} as a diagnosis.
e.zh: 现代文献很少把 schizoidia 作为诊断用语。

e.en: I had to {schlepp} the boxes upstairs alone.
e.zh: 我只好一个人把那些箱子费力搬上楼。

e.en: She hated to {schlepp} across town for one meeting.
e.zh: 她讨厌为了一个会议大老远跑到城另一头。

e.en: The candle produced visible {schlieren} in the warm air.
e.zh: 蜡烛在暖空气中产生了可见的纹影。

e.en: Scientists photographed {schlieren} around the speeding projectile.
e.zh: 科学家拍下了高速弹体周围的流体条纹。

e.en: Poor Leo is a {schlimazel} who always misses the train.
e.zh: 可怜的利奥是个倒霉蛋，总是赶不上火车。

e.en: The comedy centers on a lovable {schlimazel} in New York.
e.zh: 这部喜剧围绕纽约一个讨人喜欢的倒霉鬼展开。

schlockmeister.t: 粗制滥造作品的制作者

e.en: The director was dismissed as a {schlockmeister} by critics.
e.zh: 评论家把这位导演贬为粗制滥造作品的制造者。

e.en: That {schlockmeister} still knows how to sell a cheap thriller.
e.zh: 那个烂片高手仍然懂得怎样卖出廉价惊悚片。

e.en: He arrived looking like a tired {schlub}.
e.zh: 他到场时看起来像个疲惫邋遢的窝囊人。

e.en: The film turns an ordinary {schlub} into an unlikely hero.
e.zh: 电影把一个普通窝囊废变成了意想不到的英雄。

e.en: Don't sit there like a {schlump} all afternoon.
e.zh: 别整个下午都像个懒散笨人一样坐在那里。

e.en: He would {schlump} into the office after lunch.
e.zh: 他午饭后总会拖拖拉拉地走进办公室。

e.en: She wore a {schlumpy} sweater to the rehearsal.
e.zh: 她穿着一件邋遢臃肿的毛衣去排练。

e.en: His {schlumpy} posture made him look older.
e.zh: 他懒散的姿势让他显得更老。

e.en: The ending was pure {schmalz}, but everyone cried.
e.zh: 结尾完全是俗套煽情，但大家都哭了。

e.en: She spread onion {schmalz} on warm bread.
e.zh: 她把洋葱鸡油抹在热面包上。

e.en: He wiped the counter with an old {schmatte}.
e.zh: 他用一块旧破布擦柜台。

e.en: That boutique sells overpriced {schmatte} to tourists.
e.zh: 那家精品店把廉价衣服高价卖给游客。

e.en: I'll take a bagel with a {schmear} of cream cheese.
e.zh: 我要一个百吉饼，上面抹一点奶油奶酪。

e.en: There was a dark {schmear} of grease on the door.
e.zh: 门上有一片黑乎乎的油污。

e.en: The bagel came with a generous {schmeer} of cheese.
e.zh: 这个百吉饼配了厚厚一层奶酪酱。

e.en: The contractor offered a {schmeer} to speed approval.
e.zh: 承包商送了一笔贿赂来加快审批。

e.en: Some poor {schmoe} got blamed for the mistake.
e.zh: 某个倒霉的无名小卒被拿来为错误背锅。

e.en: He is not just another {schmoe} in the crowd.
e.zh: 他可不是人群里随便一个普通人。

e.en: They stayed after dinner to {schmoose} with the guests.
e.zh: 他们晚饭后留下来和客人闲聊。

e.en: He can {schmoose} investors without sounding desperate.
e.zh: 他能和投资人套近乎，又不显得急切。

e.en: You have some {schmutz} on your glasses.
e.zh: 你的眼镜上有点脏东西。

e.en: The mechanic wiped the {schmutz} from his hands.
e.zh: 修理工擦掉手上的污垢。

e.en: They drank peach {schnaps} after the meal.
e.zh: 他们饭后喝了桃味烈酒。

e.en: A bottle of {schnaps} sat behind the bar.
e.zh: 吧台后面放着一瓶烈酒。

e.en: The bakery sold warm {schnecken} every Sunday morning.
e.zh: 那家面包店每周日早晨出售热乎的螺旋甜面包。

e.en: She packed sticky {schnecken} for the family picnic.
e.zh: 她为家庭野餐装了黏甜的螺旋面包。

e.en: The team finally got off the {schneid} with a win.
e.zh: 球队终于用一场胜利摆脱了连败低潮。

e.en: After weeks on the {schneid}, he sold a painting.
e.zh: 倒霉了几周后，他终于卖出了一幅画。

e.en: The old textbook classified the organism as a {schizomycete}.
e.zh: 那本旧教材把这种生物归为裂殖菌。

e.en: A {schizomycete} was once broadly understood as a bacterium.
e.zh: 裂殖菌一词过去常被宽泛地理解为细菌。

schizomycosis.t: 裂殖菌病；细菌性真菌样感染

e.en: The doctor noted {schizomycosis} in the historical case report.
e.zh: 医生在那份历史病例报告中记录了裂殖菌病。

e.en: Modern writers rarely use {schizomycosis} outside specialist medicine.
e.zh: 现代作者很少在专科医学之外使用裂殖菌病这个词。

schizont.t: 裂殖体；疟原虫裂殖阶段

e.en: The parasite formed a mature {schizont} inside the blood cell.
e.zh: 寄生虫在血细胞内形成了成熟的裂殖体。

e.en: Researchers counted each {schizont} under the microscope.
e.zh: 研究人员在显微镜下逐个计数裂殖体。

e.en: The new drug acts as a blood {schizonticide}.
e.zh: 这种新药可作为血液期杀裂殖体药。

e.en: A strong {schizonticide} can quickly reduce malaria symptoms.
e.zh: 强效杀裂殖体药能迅速减轻疟疾症状。

e.en: The paper used {schizophrene} as an outdated clinical noun.
e.zh: 论文把精神分裂症患者一词用作过时的临床名词。

e.en: Calling someone a {schizophrene} can sound stigmatizing today.
e.zh: 如今称某人为精神分裂症患者可能带有污名化色彩。

schizophrenese.t: 精神分裂式言语；混乱话语

e.en: The critic dismissed the manifesto as political {schizophrenese}.
e.zh: 评论家把那份宣言贬称为政治上的混乱话语。

e.en: Clinicians avoided the term {schizophrenese} in formal reports.
e.zh: 临床医生在正式报告中避免使用精神分裂式言语这个说法。

schizophrenically.t: 以精神分裂症方式；矛盾地

e.en: The patient was described, clumsily, as behaving {schizophrenically}.
e.zh: 病人的行为被笨拙地描述为呈精神分裂症式表现。

e.en: The policy moved {schizophrenically} between caution and panic.
e.zh: 这项政策在谨慎和恐慌之间矛盾地摇摆。

e.en: She was diagnosed with a {schizophreniform} disorder after evaluation.
e.zh: 评估后，她被诊断为类精神分裂症障碍。

e.en: The episode had {schizophreniform} features but lasted only briefly.
e.zh: 这次发作具有类精神分裂症特征，但持续时间很短。

e.en: The old theory blamed a {schizophrenogenic} family environment.
e.zh: 旧理论把原因归咎于致精神分裂症的家庭环境。

e.en: Most psychiatrists now reject the idea of a {schizophrenogenic} mother.
e.zh: 多数精神科医生如今否定所谓致精神分裂症母亲的观念。

e.en: The sample contained several {schizophyceous} organisms from the pond.
e.zh: 样本中含有几种来自池塘的裂殖藻类生物。

e.en: Older botanists used {schizophyceous} for certain blue-green algae.
e.zh: 早期植物学家用裂殖藻类的来指某些蓝绿藻。

schizophyte.t: 裂殖植物；低等分裂生物

e.en: The manual listed the bacterium as a {schizophyte}.
e.zh: 手册把这种细菌列为裂殖植物。

e.en: A {schizophyte} reproduces chiefly by simple division.
e.zh: 裂殖植物主要通过简单分裂繁殖。

e.en: The lichenologist identified a {schizoplectosiroderm} in the cortex.
e.zh: 地衣学家在皮层中识别出分裂缠丝状菌皮结构。

e.en: A {schizoplectosiroderm} is a highly specialized anatomical term.
e.zh: 分裂缠丝状菌皮结构是一个高度专业的解剖术语。

e.en: The fish fed on a tiny {schizopod} drifting near the surface.
e.zh: 那条鱼以漂在水面附近的小型裂足类甲壳动物为食。

e.en: Early zoologists grouped this shrimp-like animal as a {schizopod}.
e.zh: 早期动物学家把这种像虾的动物归为裂足类甲壳动物。

e.en: The lecture mentioned {schizothemia} as an obsolete psychiatric term.
e.zh: 讲座提到情感分裂是一个过时的精神病学术语。

e.en: His notes distinguished {schizothemia} from ordinary moodiness.
e.zh: 他的笔记把情感分裂同普通情绪化区分开来。

schizothyme.t: 分裂气质者；孤僻内向者

e.en: Kretschmer described the {schizothyme} as reserved and sensitive.
e.zh: 克雷奇默把分裂气质者描述为内向而敏感。

e.en: In older psychology, a {schizothyme} was not necessarily ill.
e.zh: 在早期心理学中，分裂气质者不一定是病人。

schizothymia.t: 分裂气质；孤僻内向性格

e.en: The article discussed {schizothymia} in early personality theory.
e.zh: 文章讨论了早期人格理论中的分裂气质。

e.en: His reserve was interpreted as {schizothymia}, not simple shyness.
e.zh: 他的拘谨被解释为分裂气质，而不只是害羞。

schizothymic.t: 分裂气质的；孤僻内向的

e.en: The psychiatrist used {schizothymic} language in the old case notes.
e.zh: 精神科医生在旧病例记录中使用了分裂气质的说法。

e.en: Her {schizothymic} temperament made social gatherings exhausting.
e.zh: 她孤僻内向的气质让社交聚会变得很耗神。

e.en: The rural clinic treated several cases of {schizotrypanosis}.
e.zh: 乡村诊所治疗了几例锥虫病。

e.en: Chagas disease is also known historically as {schizotrypanosis}.
e.zh: 查加斯病在历史上也称为锥虫病。

e.en: The study measured traits associated with the {schizotype}.
e.zh: 这项研究测量了与分裂型人格类型相关的特质。

e.en: A {schizotype} may show unusual beliefs without full psychosis.
e.zh: 分裂型人格类型者可能有异常信念，但未必达到精神病状态。

e.en: Each {schizozoite} emerged after the parasite divided repeatedly.
e.zh: 寄生虫反复分裂后产生了每个裂殖子。

e.en: The diagram labeled the motile stage as a {schizozoite}.
e.zh: 图示把这个能运动的阶段标为裂殖子。

schizy.t: 精神分裂症的；怪异混乱的

e.en: The reviewer called the film's editing {schizy} and disorienting.
e.zh: 评论者称这部电影的剪辑怪异混乱、令人迷失。

e.en: Using {schizy} as an insult is offensive to many people.
e.zh: 把精神分裂症的用作辱骂会冒犯很多人。

schizzo.t: 疯子；精神病人的冒犯说法

e.en: He regretted calling the stranger a {schizzo}.
e.zh: 他后悔把那个陌生人骂作疯子。

e.en: The novel uses {schizzo} to show the speaker's cruelty.
e.zh: 小说用疯子这个冒犯说法来表现说话者的刻薄。

schizzy.t: 精神分裂症的；疯癫的冒犯说法

e.en: The comedian removed the {schizzy} joke from his routine.
e.zh: 那位喜剧演员删掉了节目中关于疯癫的冒犯笑话。

e.en: Her thoughts felt {schizzy} after two nights without sleep.
e.zh: 两夜没睡后，她觉得自己的思绪混乱得近乎疯癫。

e.en: He came home completely {schnockered} after the party.
e.zh: 聚会后他回到家时已经醉得很厉害。

e.en: I was too {schnockered} to remember the joke.
e.zh: 我当时醉得太厉害，已经记不起那个笑话了。

e.en: Don't be a {schnook} and pay twice.
e.zh: 别当傻瓜付两次钱。

e.en: The poor {schnook} believed every word they said.
e.zh: 那个可怜的老实人把他们说的话全信了。

e.en: He tried to {schnorr} a free meal from us.
e.zh: 他想厚着脸皮向我们讨一顿免费饭。

e.en: She would {schnorr} rides from friends all week.
e.zh: 她整周都会向朋友蹭车。

e.en: The old {schnorrer} asked everyone for spare change.
e.zh: 那个老乞讨者向每个人要零钱。

e.en: He was known as a {schnorrer} who never paid.
e.zh: 大家都知道他是个从不付钱、爱占便宜的人。

e.en: He broke his {schnoz} playing basketball.
e.zh: 他打篮球时撞坏了鼻子。

e.en: That comedian always joked about his big {schnoz}.
e.zh: 那个喜剧演员总拿自己的大鼻子开玩笑。

e.en: The clown wore a huge red {schnozzle}.
e.zh: 小丑戴着一个巨大的红鼻子。

e.en: Mind your {schnozzle} near that hot pan.
e.zh: 靠近那个热锅时小心你的鼻子。

e.en: A {scholar-bureaucrat} advised the emperor on taxation.
e.zh: 一位士大夫向皇帝进言税制问题。

e.en: The novel portrays the lonely life of a {scholar-bureaucrat}.
e.zh: 这部小说描写了一名学者官僚的孤独生活。

e.en: The essay describes him as a {scholar-tyrant}.
e.zh: 这篇文章把他描写成一位学者型暴君。

e.en: A {scholar-tyrant} may use learning to justify cruelty.
e.zh: 学者型暴君可能用学问来为残酷辩护。

scholarch.t: 学园领袖；古代学派掌门

e.en: The {scholarch} guided debates in the ancient school.
e.zh: 这位学派掌门主持古代学院里的辩论。

e.en: After Plato, each {scholarch} shaped the Academy differently.
e.zh: 柏拉图之后，每位学园领袖都以不同方式塑造学院。

e.en: His prose suffers from excessive {scholarism}.
e.zh: 他的散文带有过重的学究气。

e.en: The movement valued public action over narrow {scholarism}.
e.zh: 这场运动重视公共行动，而不是狭隘的学者作风。

e.en: Her calm {scholarliness} impressed the committee.
e.zh: 她沉稳的学者风范给委员会留下了深刻印象。

e.en: The book has clarity as well as {scholarliness}.
e.zh: 这本书既清晰易懂，又有学术气质。

e.en: The argument sounded too {scholastical} for the audience.
e.zh: 这个论证对听众来说显得太学究式了。

e.en: He wrote in a dense, {scholastical} style.
e.zh: 他的写作风格艰深，带有经院哲学色彩。

scholasticate.t: 神学院修学阶段；修学院

e.en: He entered the {scholasticate} after two years of training.
e.zh: 经过两年训练后，他进入了神学院修学阶段。

e.en: The old {scholasticate} stood beside the monastery.
e.zh: 那所旧修学院坐落在修道院旁边。

e.en: The manuscript contains {scholia} in the margins.
e.zh: 这份手稿页边写有古注。

e.en: Modern editors often compare ancient {scholia} carefully.
e.zh: 现代编者常会仔细比较古代旁注。

e.en: A medieval {scholiast} explained the difficult line.
e.zh: 一位中世纪注释者解释了这句难懂的诗行。

e.en: The {scholiast} added historical notes to the poem.
e.zh: 这位评注家给诗加上了历史注释。

e.en: The edition includes extensive {scholiastic} material.
e.zh: 这个版本收录了大量评注材料。

e.en: His {scholiastic} habit made every page crowded.
e.zh: 他爱写旁注的习惯让每一页都显得拥挤。

e.en: A brief {scholium} explains the obscure reference.
e.zh: 一条简短旁注解释了这个晦涩的典故。

e.en: The theorem is followed by a useful {scholium}.
e.zh: 这个定理后面附有一段有用的评注。

e.en: Several {scholiums} appear after the main proof.
e.zh: 主要证明后面出现了几条评注。

e.en: The translator omitted many marginal {scholiums}.
e.zh: 译者省略了许多页边旁注。

e.en: The museum displayed a pale crystal of {scholzite}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一块浅色的磷锌钙石晶体。

e.en: Collectors prize {scholzite} for its delicate crystal sprays.
e.zh: 收藏者珍视磷锌钙石细致的放射状晶簇。

schoolmasterish.t: 像校长般严厉古板；训导式

e.en: His {schoolmasterish} tone made everyone sit up straight.
e.zh: 他那种训导式的口吻让大家都坐直了。

e.en: She gave a {schoolmasterish} lecture about punctuality.
e.zh: 她像严厉校长一样训了一通准时的重要性。

schoolmen.t: 经院哲学家；中世纪神学学者

e.en: The medieval {schoolmen} debated faith and reason.
e.zh: 中世纪经院哲学家争论信仰与理性。

e.en: His prose echoes the arguments of the {schoolmen}.
e.zh: 他的散文带有经院学者论辩的影子。

schoolmiss.t: 女学生；稚气的年轻姑娘

e.en: She blushed like a shy {schoolmiss}.
e.zh: 她像害羞的女学生一样脸红了。

e.en: The word {schoolmiss} now sounds distinctly old-fashioned.
e.zh: schoolmiss 这个词如今听起来很老派。

schoolmistressy.t: 像女教师般严厉古板的

e.en: Her {schoolmistressy} manner annoyed the committee.
e.zh: 她那种女教师般严厉古板的态度惹恼了委员会。

e.en: He disliked the editor's {schoolmistressy} corrections.
e.zh: 他不喜欢编辑那种训导式的修改。

e.en: The cadets lived aboard the {schoolship} for six months.
e.zh: 学员们在训练船上住了六个月。

e.en: An old frigate was converted into a {schoolship}.
e.zh: 一艘旧护卫舰被改造成了海事训练船。

e.en: She returned to {schoolteaching} after raising her children.
e.zh: 她抚养孩子后又回到学校任教。

e.en: Modern {schoolteaching} often uses digital tools.
e.zh: 现代学校教学常常使用数字工具。

e.en: Phones must be switched off during {schooltime}.
e.zh: 上课时间必须关掉手机。

e.en: He still remembers his {schooltime} friends.
e.zh: 他仍然记得学生时代的朋友。

e.en: The new {schoolyear} starts in September.
e.zh: 新学年在九月开始。

e.en: She improved a lot during the {schoolyear}.
e.zh: 她在这一学年里进步很大。

schooner-rigged.t: 装成纵帆式的；纵帆船式

e.en: The vessel was {schooner-rigged} for coastal trade.
e.zh: 这艘船为沿海贸易装成纵帆式。

e.en: A {schooner-rigged} yacht entered the harbor.
e.zh: 一艘纵帆式游艇驶入港口。

e.en: The rock contained dark crystals of {schorl}.
e.zh: 这块岩石里含有黑色的黑电气石晶体。

e.en: Collectors prize well-formed {schorl} specimens.
e.zh: 收藏者珍视形状完好的黑电气石标本。

schorlaceous.t: 似黑电气石的；含黑电气石的

e.en: The geologist described the vein as {schorlaceous}.
e.zh: 地质学家把这条矿脉描述为含黑电气石的。

e.en: A {schorlaceous} texture darkened the granite.
e.zh: 类似黑电气石的质地使花岗岩显得更深。

e.en: The band played a lively {schottische}.
e.zh: 乐队演奏了一首欢快的肖蒂什舞曲。

e.en: They learned the {schottische} at the folk dance class.
e.zh: 他们在民间舞蹈课上学了肖蒂什舞。

schottish.t: 肖蒂什舞的；类似肖蒂什的

e.en: The tune has a {schottish} rhythm.
e.zh: 这支曲子带有肖蒂什舞的节奏。

e.en: They practiced a {schottish} step before the performance.
e.zh: 演出前他们练习了肖蒂什式舞步。

e.en: The report identified {schradan} in the old pesticide store.
e.zh: 报告在旧农药库中检出了施拉丹。

e.en: Use of {schradan} is tightly controlled because it is toxic.
e.zh: 施拉丹有毒，因此使用受到严格管制。

e.en: The cook used {schrod} for the chowder.
e.zh: 厨师用切碎的鱼肉做杂烩汤。

e.en: Fresh {schrod} was sold at the harbor market.
e.zh: 港口市场出售新鲜的碎鱼肉。

e.en: The clinic offers free checks for {school-age} children.
e.zh: 这家诊所为学龄儿童提供免费检查。

e.en: Many {school-age} students still need help reading.
e.zh: 许多上学年龄的学生仍需要阅读帮助。

e.en: The program pairs each {school-ager} with a reading mentor.
e.zh: 这个项目为每个学龄儿童配一名阅读导师。

e.en: A tired {school-ager} may struggle to focus after lunch.
e.zh: 疲惫的学龄孩子午饭后可能难以集中注意力。

e.en: The {school-board} voted to reopen the library.
e.zh: 教育委员会投票决定重新开放图书馆。

e.en: Parents addressed the {school-board} about bus safety.
e.zh: 家长就校车安全问题向校董会发言。

e.en: The {school-boy} carried a heavy backpack.
e.zh: 那个男学生背着一个沉重的书包。

e.en: He kept a {school-boy} enthusiasm for science.
e.zh: 他一直保持着小男生般的科学热情。

e.en: A typical {school-day} starts at eight.
e.zh: 普通的上学日从八点开始。

e.en: She packed lunch for the next {school-day}.
e.zh: 她为第二天上学准备了午餐。

e.en: He often talks about his {school-days}.
e.zh: 他常常谈起自己的学生时代。

e.en: During her {school-days}, she learned three languages.
e.zh: 在上学的那些年里，她学了三门语言。

e.en: An old {school-fellow} recognized him at once.
e.zh: 一位老同学立刻认出了他。

e.en: She wrote to a {school-fellow} from her village.
e.zh: 她写信给村里的一位校友。

school-friend.t: 学校里的朋友；同窗好友

e.en: My {school-friend} still sends me birthday cards.
e.zh: 我的同窗好友至今还会寄生日卡给我。

e.en: She met a former {school-friend} on the train.
e.zh: 她在火车上遇到了一位以前的学校朋友。

e.en: The {school-girl} waited outside the classroom.
e.zh: 那个女学生在教室外等着。

e.en: She laughed with {school-girl} excitement.
e.zh: 她带着小女生般的兴奋笑了起来。

school-leaver.t: 毕业离校者；中学毕业生

e.en: The company hired a young {school-leaver}.
e.zh: 公司雇用了一名年轻的中学毕业生。

e.en: Every {school-leaver} received advice about apprenticeships.
e.zh: 每位毕业离校者都得到了有关学徒岗位的建议。

school-leavers.t: 毕业离校者；中学毕业生

e.en: Many {school-leavers} apply for college in July.
e.zh: 许多中学毕业生在七月申请大学。

e.en: Employers offered training places to local {school-leavers}.
e.zh: 雇主向当地毕业离校者提供培训名额。

e.en: He failed his {school-leaving} exam twice.
e.zh: 他的毕业考试两次没有通过。

e.en: The {school-leaving} age was raised by law.
e.zh: 法定离校年龄被提高了。

e.en: I shared a desk with my {school-mate}.
e.zh: 我和我的同学共用一张课桌。

e.en: A former {school-mate} invited her to dinner.
e.zh: 一位昔日同窗邀请她共进晚餐。

e.en: The old {school-room} had wooden desks.
e.zh: 那间旧教室里摆着木课桌。

e.en: Their lessons took place in a single {school-room}.
e.zh: 他们的课都在同一间校舍教室里上。

e.en: He gave a {schoolboyish} grin after the joke.
e.zh: 听完笑话后，他露出男学生气的笑容。

e.en: The prank had a {schoolboyish} sense of humor.
e.zh: 这个恶作剧带着孩子气的幽默感。

e.en: Good {schoolcraft} helps new teachers manage noise.
e.zh: 良好的教学技巧能帮助新教师控制课堂噪声。

e.en: Her book treats {schoolcraft} as a practical art.
e.zh: 她的书把学校管理术视为一门实用技艺。

e.en: He recognized an old {schoolfellow} at the station.
e.zh: 他在车站认出了一位老同学。

e.en: A {schoolfellow} later became her business partner.
e.zh: 一位校友后来成了她的生意伙伴。

schoolgirlish.t: 女学生气的；小女生般的

e.en: She answered with a {schoolgirlish} giggle.
e.zh: 她带着小女生般的咯咯笑作答。

e.en: The diary kept a {schoolgirlish} sweetness.
e.zh: 那本日记保留着女学生气的甜美。

e.en: A group of {schoolies} crowded the beach after exams.
e.zh: 考试结束后，一群毕业旅行学生挤满了海滩。

e.en: The cafe gives discounts to every {schoolie}.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆给每个学生打折。

e.en: The village {schoolma'am} taught children in one room.
e.zh: 村里的女教师在一间教室里教孩子们。

e.en: Her {schoolma'am} tone made the adults sit straighter.
e.zh: 她那古板女教师般的语气让成年人都坐直了。

e.en: The young {schoolmaid} hurried home with her books.
e.zh: 那个女学生抱着书匆匆回家。

e.en: A {schoolmaid} cleaned the classroom before dawn.
e.zh: 一名学校女仆在黎明前打扫了教室。

e.en: The medieval {schoolman} debated questions of faith.
e.zh: 那位中世纪经院哲学家辩论信仰问题。

e.en: He wrote like a careful {schoolman}.
e.zh: 他的写作风格像一位严谨的学者。

schoolmarmish.t: 女教师派头的；古板说教的

e.en: Her {schoolmarmish} correction embarrassed the speaker.
e.zh: 她那种女教师派头的纠正让发言者很尴尬。

e.en: The article sounded {schoolmarmish} and scolding.
e.zh: 这篇文章听起来古板又带着训斥味。

schroetterite.t: 施罗特石；一种含铝矿物

e.en: The curator labeled the pale sample as {schroetterite}.
e.zh: 馆长把这块浅色标本标为施罗特石。

e.en: Few collectors can identify {schroetterite} without a mineral guide.
e.zh: 没有矿物指南，很少有收藏者能认出施罗特石。

e.en: His comedy {schtik} still makes the audience laugh.
e.zh: 他的喜剧招牌套路仍能让观众发笑。

e.en: She dropped the sales {schtik} and spoke honestly.
e.zh: 她收起推销那套噱头，坦率地说了。

e.en: The novel hints that he {schtupped} a rival's wife.
e.zh: 小说暗示他和对手的妻子发生了关系。

e.en: That crude joke about {schtup} made everyone uncomfortable.
e.zh: 那个关于上床的粗俗笑话让大家都不自在。

e.en: My grandfather walked to {schul} every Saturday morning.
e.zh: 我祖父每周六早上步行去犹太会堂。

e.en: The children learned Hebrew at the local {schul}.
e.zh: 孩子们在当地的犹太学校学习希伯来语。

schungite.t: 舒俱来碳石；黑色含碳矿物

e.en: The bracelet was advertised as polished {schungite}.
e.zh: 这只手链被宣传为抛光的舒俱来碳石。

e.en: Some sellers claim {schungite} can purify water.
e.zh: 有些卖家声称舒俱来碳石可以净化水。

e.en: She made a fast {schuss} down the final slope.
e.zh: 她在最后一段坡道上高速直线滑下。

e.en: Beginners should not {schuss} through a crowded trail.
e.zh: 初学者不该在拥挤的雪道上直线猛冲。

e.en: The sailor repaired the cracked {schussboom} before the race.
e.zh: 水手在比赛前修好了开裂的斜桁。

e.en: A loose {schussboom} can make the sail hard to control.
e.zh: 松动的帆脚杆会让帆很难控制。

e.en: The old {schussboomer} moved steadily across the bay.
e.zh: 那艘旧斜桁帆船稳稳地穿过海湾。

e.en: He bought a small {schussboomer} for weekend sailing.
e.zh: 他买了一艘小斜桁帆船，周末出海用。

e.en: He {schussed} past the markers without slowing down.
e.zh: 他没有减速，直线滑过了那些标志。

e.en: The expert skiers {schussed} the steepest part easily.
e.zh: 那些高手轻松直线滑下最陡的一段。

e.en: A reckless {schusser} nearly hit the instructor.
e.zh: 一个鲁莽的直线滑雪者差点撞到教练。

e.en: The best {schusser} finished the run in seconds.
e.zh: 最厉害的高速直滑者几秒内就完成了滑道。

e.en: The race includes two long {schusses} near the finish.
e.zh: 这场比赛在终点附近有两段长距离直线滑降。

e.en: She {schusses} confidently when the trail opens up.
e.zh: 雪道变宽后，她会自信地直线高速滑下。

e.en: We watched him {schussing} down the mountain.
e.zh: 我们看着他从山上直线高速滑下来。

e.en: {Schussing} is thrilling but dangerous on icy slopes.
e.zh: 在结冰坡道上直线高速滑雪很刺激但危险。

e.en: The museum displayed a wartime {schutzmine} behind glass.
e.zh: 博物馆把一枚战时防步兵地雷陈列在玻璃后。

e.en: Engineers marked the suspected {schutzmine} before clearing the field.
e.zh: 工程人员先标出疑似防步兵地雷，再清理场地。

e.en: He was criticized for using the slur {schvartze}.
e.zh: 他因使用“schvartze”这个侮辱性称呼而受到批评。

e.en: The memoir quotes {schvartze} to show old prejudice.
e.zh: 回忆录引用这个辱称，是为了呈现旧时的偏见。

schwa.t: 中央元音；非重读弱元音

e.en: The final vowel in sofa is a {schwa}.
e.zh: sofa 末尾的元音是一个中央元音。

e.en: English learners often miss the {schwa} in unstressed syllables.
e.zh: 英语学习者常漏掉非重读音节里的弱元音。

e.en: The scan suggested a rare {schwannoglioma} near the spine.
e.zh: 扫描显示脊柱附近可能有罕见的神经鞘胶质瘤。

e.en: Doctors discussed whether the {schwannoglioma} required surgery.
e.zh: 医生讨论这种神经鞘胶质瘤是否需要手术。

e.en: The biopsy showed signs of {schwannosis} in the nerve tissue.
e.zh: 活检显示神经组织中有施万细胞异常增生迹象。

e.en: Researchers linked {schwannosis} with chronic nerve irritation.
e.zh: 研究人员把施万细胞异常增生与长期神经刺激联系起来。

schwartza.t: 黑人女性的冒犯性称呼

e.en: The archive kept the offensive word {schwartza} in the quotation.
e.zh: 档案在引文中保留了“schwartza”这个冒犯性词语。

e.en: She explained that {schwartza} is a racial slur.
e.zh: 她解释说“schwartza”是带有种族侮辱意味的称呼。

e.en: The phrase {schwarze} humor appeared in the German review.
e.zh: “schwarze humor”这个说法出现在那篇德语评论中。

e.en: He translated {schwarze} as black in the margin.
e.zh: 他在页边把“schwarze”译为“黑色的”。

e.en: The teacher marked the hidden {schwas} in the sentence.
e.zh: 老师标出了句子里隐藏的弱元音。

e.en: Many English {schwas} disappear in fast speech.
e.zh: 许多英语弱元音在快速讲话中会消失。

e.en: She loves old {sci-fi} movies.
e.zh: 她喜欢老科幻电影。

e.en: The novel mixes romance with {sci-fi}.
e.zh: 这本小说把爱情和科幻元素结合在一起。

e.en: The poet described a {sciad} crossing the wall.
e.zh: 诗人描写一道影子掠过墙面。

e.en: In older texts, {sciad} may simply mean a shade.
e.zh: 在较古老的文本中，sciad可能只是指阴影。

e.en: The doctor studied the {sciagram} carefully.
e.zh: 医生仔细查看那张影像图。

e.en: An early {sciagram} revealed the broken bone.
e.zh: 早期的一张影像图显示了骨折。

e.en: The old textbook included a {sciagraph} of the hand.
e.zh: 那本旧教材收录了一张手部影像图。

e.en: A clear {sciagraph} helped locate the injury.
e.zh: 清晰的影像图帮助确定了受伤位置。

e.en: Early {sciagraphy} changed medical diagnosis.
e.zh: 早期射线照相术改变了医学诊断。

e.en: The lecture covered {sciagraphy} and shadow measurement.
e.zh: 讲座介绍了射线照相术和阴影测量。

e.en: Their argument became pure {sciamachy}.
e.zh: 他们的争论变成了纯粹的徒劳争斗。

e.en: Fighting rumors can feel like {sciamachy}.
e.zh: 和谣言较劲有时像是在捕风捉影。

e.en: Ancient surveyors used {sciametry} to estimate heights.
e.zh: 古代测量员用测影法估算高度。

e.en: The lesson introduced {sciametry} through sundials.
e.zh: 这节课通过日晷介绍了阴影测量。

e.en: The pain traveled {sciatically} down his leg.
e.zh: 疼痛沿坐骨神经向他的腿部放射。

e.en: She limped {sciatically} after lifting the box.
e.zh: 她搬箱子后因坐骨神经痛一瘸一拐。

e.en: The film has a {science-fictional} setting.
e.zh: 这部电影有一个科幻背景。

e.en: Her story uses {science-fictional} ideas to discuss loneliness.
e.zh: 她的故事用科幻式构想来讨论孤独。

e.en: The essay describes humans as {scient} beings.
e.zh: 这篇文章把人类描述为有知识的存在。

e.en: A {scient} reader may notice the hidden reference.
e.zh: 有学问的读者可能会注意到隐藏的典故。

e.en: The lawyer had to prove {scienter}.
e.zh: 律师必须证明当事人是明知故犯。

e.en: The complaint alleged that he acted {scienter}.
e.zh: 诉状称他是故意这样做的。

e.en: The philosopher discussed {sciential} certainty.
e.zh: 哲学家讨论了知识上的确定性。

e.en: The book uses {sciential} language throughout.
e.zh: 这本书通篇使用偏学术的知识性语言。

e.en: His tone sounded oddly {scientifical}.
e.zh: 他的语气听起来有点奇怪地科学化。

e.en: Older writers sometimes preferred {scientifical} to scientific.
e.zh: 较早的作家有时用scientifical而不用scientific。

e.en: They tried to {scientize} the study of art.
e.zh: 他们试图把艺术研究科学化。

e.en: The reform aimed to {scientize} public administration.
e.zh: 这项改革旨在使公共管理更加科学化。

e.en: A {scientologist} defended the church publicly.
e.zh: 一名山达基教信徒公开为该教会辩护。

e.en: The article interviewed a former {scientologist}.
e.zh: 文章采访了一名前山达基教信徒。

e.en: She studies citation patterns in {scientometrics}.
e.zh: 她在科学计量学中研究引文模式。

e.en: The journal published a paper on {scientometrics}.
e.zh: 该期刊发表了一篇关于科学计量学的论文。

e.en: Only one person objected, {scilicet} the treasurer.
e.zh: 只有一个人反对，也就是司库。

e.en: The rule applies to minors, {scilicet} those under eighteen.
e.zh: 这条规则适用于未成年人，即十八岁以下的人。

e.en: The chemist identified {scillarabiose} in the sample.
e.zh: 化学家在样品中鉴定出海葱二糖。

e.en: {Scillarabiose} appears in discussions of plant glycosides.
e.zh: 海葱二糖会出现在植物糖苷的讨论中。

e.en: The extract contained {scillaren} from squill bulbs.
e.zh: 提取物含有来自海葱鳞茎的海葱苷类成分。

e.en: Older pharmacology texts mention {scillaren} as a cardiac agent.
e.zh: 较早的药理学书籍把海葱苷列为强心成分。

e.en: The enzyme {scillarenase} breaks down scillaren compounds.
e.zh: 海葱苷酶会分解海葱苷类化合物。

e.en: Researchers measured {scillarenase} activity in the extract.
e.zh: 研究人员测量了提取物中的海葱苷酶活性。

sciolistic.t: 一知半解地卖弄学问的；浅薄的学究气的

e.en: His {sciolistic} lecture impressed no real experts.
e.zh: 他那番一知半解地卖弄学问的讲座并没有打动真正的专家。

e.en: The essay had a {sciolistic} tone, full of borrowed jargon.
e.zh: 这篇文章带着浅薄的学究气，满是借来的术语。

sciolous.t: 一知半解的；卖弄浅薄知识的

e.en: A {sciolous} critic dismissed the theory after one article.
e.zh: 一个一知半解的评论者只读了一篇文章就否定了这个理论。

e.en: Her {sciolous} remarks sounded confident but lacked substance.
e.zh: 她那些卖弄浅薄知识的话听起来很自信，却没有实质内容。

sciomachy.t: 与假想敌争斗；捕风捉影的争论

e.en: The debate became pure {sciomachy} over threats nobody had made.
e.zh: 这场辩论变成了针对无人提出的威胁的捕风捉影争论。

e.en: He wasted years in {sciomachy}, fighting enemies of his own invention.
e.zh: 他多年都耗在与自己想象出来的敌人争斗上。

e.en: The villagers feared her alleged practice of {sciomancy}.
e.zh: 村民害怕她所谓用亡灵问卜的做法。

e.en: In the old tale, {sciomancy} revealed the murdered king's secret.
e.zh: 在那个古老故事里，招魂占卜揭开了被害国王的秘密。

e.en: Many forest-floor plants are {sciophiles} adapted to dim light.
e.zh: 许多森林地表植物都是适应弱光的喜阴植物。

e.en: The guide grouped the shade-loving mosses as {sciophiles}.
e.zh: 这本指南把这些喜阴的苔藓归为喜阴生物。

sciophilic.t: 喜阴的；适于阴处生长的

e.en: The fern is strongly {sciophilic} and wilts in direct sun.
e.zh: 这种蕨类非常喜阴，在直射阳光下会枯萎。

e.en: They planted {sciophilic} species beneath the dense canopy.
e.zh: 他们在茂密树冠下种了适于阴处生长的物种。

e.en: This {sciophilous} shrub thrives under old trees.
e.zh: 这种喜阴灌木在老树下面长得很好。

e.en: The report listed several {sciophilous} crops for shaded farms.
e.zh: 报告列出了几种适合阴地种植的作物。

e.en: A {sciophyte} can photosynthesize efficiently in low light.
e.zh: 阴生植物能在弱光下高效进行光合作用。

e.en: The botanist identified the moss as a typical {sciophyte}.
e.zh: 植物学家认定这种苔藓是典型的喜阴植物。

scioptic.t: 暗箱成像的；投影观察用的

e.en: The museum displayed an old {scioptic} ball for projecting images.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一只用于投影成像的旧暗箱球。

e.en: His {scioptic} device threw the street scene onto a wall.
e.zh: 他的暗箱成像装置把街景投到了墙上。

sciosophy.t: 影子般的知识；虚幻学问

e.en: The pamphlet promised wisdom but delivered only {sciosophy}.
e.zh: 这本小册子号称传授智慧，实际只有虚幻学问。

e.en: He mocked the doctrine as {sciosophy}, not serious philosophy.
e.zh: 他嘲笑这套学说只是影子般的知识，并非严肃哲学。

scirocco.t: 西罗科热风；来自撒哈拉的湿热南风

e.en: A hot {scirocco} blew dust across the harbor.
e.zh: 一股西罗科热风把尘土吹过港口。

e.en: The {scirocco} made the coastal town feel heavy and damp.
e.zh: 来自撒哈拉的湿热南风让这座海滨小镇闷热潮湿。

e.en: The surgeon noted several {scirrhi} in the old case report.
e.zh: 外科医生在那份旧病例报告中注意到几处硬癌肿块。

e.en: Historical texts often described hard tumors as {scirrhi}.
e.zh: 历史医学文献常把坚硬肿瘤称为硬性肿瘤。

e.en: The biopsy showed a {scirrhoid} mass near the duct.
e.zh: 活检显示导管附近有一个似硬癌的肿块。

e.en: Doctors described the tissue as {scirrhoid} but not malignant.
e.zh: 医生形容该组织呈硬结样，但不是恶性的。

e.en: The report mentioned unusual {scirrhosity} in the affected tissue.
e.zh: 报告提到受影响组织出现异常的硬癌样硬化。

e.en: Old medical writers used {scirrhosity} for a hardening of glands.
e.zh: 旧时医学作者用硬结状态来指腺体变硬。

e.en: The pathologist examined a {scirrhous} tumor sample.
e.zh: 病理学家检查了一份硬癌性肿瘤样本。

e.en: A {scirrhous} swelling can feel firm under the skin.
e.zh: 硬结肿胀在皮肤下摸起来可能很坚实。

e.en: The old diagnosis called the breast tumor a {scirrhus}.
e.zh: 旧诊断把这个乳腺肿瘤称为硬癌。

e.en: A {scirrhus} is characterized by dense fibrous tissue.
e.zh: 硬性癌肿的特点是纤维组织致密。

e.en: The archive contained drawings of several {scirrhuses}.
e.zh: 档案里有几幅多处硬性癌肿的图示。

e.en: Early surgeons often confused {scirrhuses} with benign hard swellings.
e.zh: 早期外科医生常把硬癌与良性硬肿混淆。

scissel.t: 金属冲裁边角料；造币废料

e.en: The mint collected the {scissel} left after cutting coin blanks.
e.zh: 造币厂收集冲裁币坯后留下的金属边角料。

e.en: Sheets of silver produced valuable {scissel} during stamping.
e.zh: 银片在冲压过程中产生了有价值的造币废料。

e.en: The mineral is {scissil} along its natural grain.
e.zh: 这种矿物沿着天然纹理很容易劈开。

e.en: Craftsmen preferred {scissil} stone for thin decorative panels.
e.zh: 工匠偏爱可切开的石材来制作薄装饰板。

e.en: Mica is a {scissile} mineral that splits into thin sheets.
e.zh: 云母是一种易切开的矿物，能剥成薄片。

e.en: The nucleus becomes {scissile} after absorbing a neutron.
e.zh: 原子核吸收一个中子后会变得可裂变。

e.en: She gave the cloth a clean {scissor-cut} edge.
e.zh: 她用剪刀把布边剪得很整齐。

e.en: The stylist chose a {scissor-cut} finish instead of clippers.
e.zh: 发型师选择用剪刀修剪收尾，而不是用电推剪。

e.en: The striker scored with a spectacular {scissor-kick}.
e.zh: 前锋用一记精彩的剪式踢破门得分。

e.en: Swimmers practice the {scissor-kick} to improve balance.
e.zh: 游泳者练习剪刀脚动作来提高平衡。

e.en: A {scissorbird} hovered above the dry grassland.
e.zh: 一只剪尾鸟在干燥的草地上方盘旋。

e.en: The children recognized the {scissorbird} by its forked tail.
e.zh: 孩子们凭它叉开的尾巴认出了这只叉尾鸟。

e.en: The costume gave the character gleaming {scissorhands}.
e.zh: 这套戏服给角色配上了闪亮的剪刀手。

e.en: Fans immediately recognized the lonely figure with {scissorhands}.
e.zh: 影迷立刻认出那个有剪刀手的孤独人物。

e.en: The sample showed a {sclerine} layer under the microscope.
e.zh: 显微镜下可以看到样本有一层硬质层。

e.en: Older texts describe the tissue as {sclerine}.
e.zh: 较早的文献把这种组织描述为硬质的。

e.en: The surgeon discussed {scleriritomy} as a possible treatment.
e.zh: 外科医生讨论了把巩膜虹膜切开术作为一种可能治疗。

e.en: Modern techniques have largely replaced {scleriritomy}.
e.zh: 现代技术在很大程度上已经取代巩膜虹膜切开术。

e.en: Severe eye pain may indicate {scleritis}.
e.zh: 严重眼痛可能提示患有巩膜炎。

e.en: Her {scleritis} improved after specialist treatment.
e.zh: 经过专科治疗后，她的巩膜炎有所好转。

scleroblast.t: 成骨针细胞；硬质生成细胞

e.en: A {scleroblast} helps form the sponge's tiny spicules.
e.zh: 成骨针细胞有助于形成海绵体内细小的骨针。

e.en: The researcher identified each {scleroblast} in the section.
e.zh: 研究人员在切片中辨认出每个硬质生成细胞。

e.en: The injury affected the {sclerocorneal} junction.
e.zh: 这处损伤影响了巩膜角膜交界处。

e.en: Doctors measured the {sclerocorneal} diameter carefully.
e.zh: 医生仔细测量了巩膜角膜直径。

e.en: The patient developed {sclerodactylia} after years of illness.
e.zh: 多年患病后，这名患者出现了硬指症。

e.en: Early {sclerodactylia} can make buttons difficult to fasten.
e.zh: 早期硬指症会让扣纽扣变得困难。

e.en: The biopsy supported a diagnosis of {sclerodermatitis}.
e.zh: 活检结果支持硬皮性皮炎的诊断。

e.en: Chronic {sclerodermatitis} may leave the skin tight and shiny.
e.zh: 慢性硬皮性皮炎可能使皮肤紧绷发亮。

sclerodermatous.t: 硬皮病样的；皮肤硬化的

e.en: The doctor noted {sclerodermatous} changes on her hands.
e.zh: 医生注意到她手上有硬皮病样改变。

e.en: A {sclerodermatous} patch appeared near the scar.
e.zh: 疤痕附近出现了一块皮肤硬化斑。

e.en: Older medical books often call scleroderma {sclerodermia}.
e.zh: 较早的医学书常把硬皮病称为sclerodermia。

e.en: Her {sclerodermia} caused stiffness in the fingers.
e.zh: 她的硬皮病导致手指僵硬。

sclerogenous.t: 生成硬组织的；致硬化的

e.en: The organism has {sclerogenous} cells that build spicules.
e.zh: 这种生物有能形成骨针的硬组织生成细胞。

e.en: A {sclerogenous} process slowly hardened the tissue.
e.zh: 一种致硬化过程逐渐使组织变硬。

e.en: The pathologist described the nodule as {scleroid}.
e.zh: 病理学家把这个结节描述为硬化样。

e.en: A {scleroid} texture made the seed coat tough.
e.zh: 近似硬质的质地使种皮很坚韧。

e.en: The redness was later diagnosed as {scleroiritis}.
e.zh: 这种眼部发红后来被诊断为巩膜虹膜炎。

e.en: Untreated {scleroiritis} can threaten vision.
e.zh: 未经治疗的巩膜虹膜炎可能危及视力。

e.en: The nasal swelling was identified as a {scleroma}.
e.zh: 鼻部肿胀被确认为硬结病灶。

e.en: A firm {scleroma} formed in the affected tissue.
e.zh: 受影响组织中形成了一个坚硬的硬化性肿块。

e.en: The technician tested the alloy with a {sclerometer}.
e.zh: 技术员用硬度计测试了这种合金。

e.en: A {sclerometer} can compare the hardness of minerals.
e.zh: 硬度计可以比较矿物的硬度。

e.en: The rare rash was diagnosed as {scleromyxoedema}.
e.zh: 这种罕见皮疹被诊断为硬化性黏液水肿。

e.en: Patients with {scleromyxoedema} often need specialist care.
e.zh: 硬化性黏液水肿患者通常需要专科护理。

e.en: Many Australian shrubs are {sclerophyllous}.
e.zh: 许多澳大利亚灌木都有厚硬叶片。

e.en: The {sclerophyllous} leaves help the plant survive drought.
e.zh: 硬叶有助于这种植物在干旱中存活。

sclerophyte.t: 硬叶植物；耐旱硬叶植物

e.en: A {sclerophyte} often has small, leathery leaves.
e.zh: 硬叶植物通常有小而革质的叶片。

e.en: The hillside was covered with {sclerophyte} shrubs.
e.zh: 山坡上长满了硬叶灌木植物。

scleroprotein.t: 硬蛋白；纤维状结构蛋白

e.en: Keratin is a common {scleroprotein} in hair and nails.
e.zh: 角蛋白是头发和指甲中常见的硬蛋白。

e.en: Collagen was once classified as a {scleroprotein}.
e.zh: 胶原蛋白曾被归类为纤维状结构蛋白。

e.en: The doctor injected a {sclerosant} into the vein.
e.zh: 医生向静脉内注射了一种硬化剂。

e.en: Each {sclerosant} must be chosen for the vessel treated.
e.zh: 每种硬化剂都必须根据所治疗的血管来选择。

e.en: The engineer measured steel hardness with a {scleroscope}.
e.zh: 工程师用回跳硬度计测量钢材硬度。

e.en: A {scleroscope} estimates hardness from rebound height.
e.zh: 回跳硬度计通过回弹高度估算硬度。

e.en: The fungus survived winter as a {sclerote}.
e.zh: 这种真菌以菌核形式越冬。

e.en: Each {sclerote} was removed from the infected stem.
e.zh: 每个硬化体都从受感染的茎上取出。

e.en: The seed's {sclerotesta} protects the embryo inside.
e.zh: 种子的硬种皮保护内部的胚。

e.en: A thick {sclerotesta} can delay germination.
e.zh: 厚硬种皮可能延缓发芽。

e.en: The {sclerotica} forms the white outer coat of the eye.
e.zh: 巩膜构成眼球白色的外层。

e.en: Yellowing of the {sclerotica} may signal liver disease.
e.zh: 巩膜发黄可能提示肝脏疾病。

e.en: Insect cuticle becomes tough when it contains {sclerotin}.
e.zh: 昆虫表皮含有硬化素时会变得坚韧。

e.en: The study measured {sclerotin} in the beetle shell.
e.zh: 这项研究测量了甲虫外壳中的昆虫硬化素。

e.en: The coal sample contained visible {sclerotinite}.
e.zh: 这份煤样中含有可见的丝炭质组分。

e.en: Petrologists classify {sclerotinite} as an inertinite maceral.
e.zh: 岩相学家把丝炭质组分归为惰质组煤岩显微组分。

scissors-and-paste.t: 剪贴式拼凑写作；剪贴法

e.en: The report felt like {scissors-and-paste} work from old articles.
e.zh: 这份报告像是从旧文章里剪贴拼凑出来的。

e.en: His {scissors-and-paste} editing left several awkward gaps.
e.zh: 他那种剪贴式编辑留下了几处别扭的断裂。

e.en: A {scissorsbill} skimmed low over the river at dusk.
e.zh: 黄昏时，一只剪嘴鸟贴着河面低低掠过。

e.en: The guide pointed out the {scissorsbill} by its unusual beak.
e.zh: 向导凭那只鸟奇特的喙认出了剪嘴鸟。

e.en: The {scissorsbird} flashed its forked tail above the field.
e.zh: 那只叉尾鸟在田野上方亮出分叉的尾巴。

e.en: Local children called the long-tailed flycatcher a {scissorsbird}.
e.zh: 当地孩子把那种长尾捕蝇鸟叫作剪尾鸟。

e.en: A {scissorstail} perched on the fence after the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨后，一只剪刀尾鸟停在篱笆上。

e.en: The old field guide used {scissorstail} for several fork-tailed birds.
e.zh: 那本旧鸟类图鉴把好几种叉尾鸟都称作剪刀尾鸟。

e.en: The {scissortail} opened its long tail like blades in flight.
e.zh: 那只剪刀尾鸟飞行时把长尾展开，像两片刀刃。

e.en: We saw a {scissortail} hunting insects above the road.
e.zh: 我们看见一只叉尾鸟在路面上方捕食昆虫。

e.en: Water seeped through a narrow {scissure} in the rock.
e.zh: 水从岩石上一道狭窄的裂缝里渗出来。

e.en: The surgeon examined the small {scissure} in the tissue.
e.zh: 外科医生检查了组织上的那处小裂开处。

e.en: The fossil belonged to an early {sciurid} from the region.
e.zh: 这块化石属于该地区一种早期松鼠科动物。

e.en: A chipmunk is a small {sciurid} with striped fur.
e.zh: 花栗鼠是一种有条纹皮毛的小型松鼠科动物。

e.en: The animal made quick, {sciurine} movements among the branches.
e.zh: 那只动物在树枝间动作敏捷，很像松鼠。

e.en: Her notes described the skull as clearly {sciurine}.
e.zh: 她的笔记把这个头骨描述为明显具有松鼠特征。

e.en: The extinct mammal had a {sciuroid} shape and long claws.
e.zh: 这种已灭绝哺乳动物体形像松鼠，爪子很长。

e.en: Researchers compared the specimen with other {sciuroid} rodents.
e.zh: 研究人员把这个标本同其他松鼠类啮齿动物作比较。

e.en: She was treated like a {scivvy} in her first job.
e.zh: 她第一份工作里被人当成干粗活的仆人使唤。

e.en: The young {scivvy} carried coal up three flights of stairs.
e.zh: 那个年轻女仆把煤搬上三层楼梯。

e.en: He managed to {sclaff} the ball only a few yards.
e.zh: 他擦地打了一下球，结果只飞出几码远。

e.en: A nervous player may {sclaff} a shot from the tee.
e.zh: 紧张的球员可能会在发球台上笨拙地击球。

e.en: She {sclaffed} the golf ball into the rough.
e.zh: 她笨拙地一击，把高尔夫球打进了长草区。

e.en: He {sclaffed} at the stone with his boot.
e.zh: 他用靴子胡乱踢了一下那块石头。

sclaffer.t: 常擦地击球的人；笨拙击球者

e.en: The coach called him a hopeless {sclaffer} after practice.
e.zh: 训练后，教练说他是个没救的笨拙击球者。

e.en: Even a {sclaffer} can improve with patient lessons.
e.zh: 就算是常常擦地击球的人，耐心学习后也能进步。

e.en: His {sclaffing} ruined an otherwise steady round of golf.
e.zh: 他的擦地击球毁掉了原本稳定的一轮高尔夫。

e.en: She kept {sclaffing} at the frozen clods with a spade.
e.zh: 她不停用铲子笨拙地砸那些冻土块。

e.en: He often {sclaffs} his first shot under pressure.
e.zh: 他一有压力，第一杆就常常擦地打坏。

e.en: The old club still shows marks from his {sclaffs}.
e.zh: 那根旧球杆上还留着他多次笨拙击打的痕迹。

e.en: The doctor checked whether the {sclera} had turned yellow.
e.zh: 医生检查他的眼白是否已经发黄。

e.en: A healthy {sclera} is usually white and firm.
e.zh: 健康的巩膜通常呈白色且较坚韧。

e.en: The scan showed a {scleratheroma} in the coronary artery.
e.zh: 扫描显示冠状动脉内有一处硬化性粥样斑块。

e.en: A large {scleratheroma} can narrow the blood vessel.
e.zh: 较大的硬化性粥样斑块会使血管变窄。

e.en: The specialist recommended {sclerectoiridectomy} for the severe glaucoma.
e.zh: 专家建议对这例严重青光眼进行巩膜虹膜切除术。

e.en: Older surgical texts describe {sclerectoiridectomy} in great detail.
e.zh: 较早的外科教材详细描述了巩膜虹膜切除术。

e.en: The patient underwent {sclerectomy} to relieve eye pressure.
e.zh: 患者接受了巩膜切除术，以降低眼压。

e.en: Partial {sclerectomy} may be used in certain eye operations.
e.zh: 某些眼科手术中可能会采用部分巩膜切除术。

e.en: The dermatologist diagnosed {scleredema} after examining his neck.
e.zh: 皮肤科医生检查他的颈部后诊断为硬肿病。

e.en: Her {scleredema} made the skin across her shoulders feel tight.
e.zh: 她的皮肤硬肿让肩部一带的皮肤发紧。

e.en: A pear's gritty texture comes partly from each {sclereid}.
e.zh: 梨子的颗粒感部分来自一个个石细胞。

e.en: The botanist identified a {sclereid} under the microscope.
e.zh: 植物学家在显微镜下识别出一个石细胞。

e.en: The newborn showed signs of {sclerema} after severe infection.
e.zh: 这个新生儿在严重感染后出现了皮肤硬化迹象。

e.en: Doctors monitored the spread of {sclerema} across the infant's back.
e.zh: 医生监测硬肿症在婴儿背部扩展的情况。

e.en: The stem is strengthened by bands of {sclerenchyma}.
e.zh: 茎部由一束束厚壁组织加强支撑。

e.en: Under the microscope, {sclerenchyma} cells have thick walls.
e.zh: 在显微镜下，厚壁组织细胞具有很厚的细胞壁。

e.en: The old diagnosis used {scleriasis} for abnormal tissue hardening.
e.zh: 旧式诊断把异常的组织硬化称为硬化症。

e.en: The report mentioned {scleriasis} in the affected skin.
e.zh: 报告提到受影响皮肤中存在硬化病变。

e.en: Minerals caused gradual {sclerification} of the surrounding tissue.
e.zh: 矿物质导致周围组织逐渐硬化。

e.en: The seed coat undergoes {sclerification} as it matures.
e.zh: 种皮在成熟过程中会发生硬化。

e.en: The culture produced {sclerotioid} bodies near the edge.
e.zh: 培养物在边缘附近产生了菌核状小体。

e.en: A {sclerotioid} texture can help identify the fungus.
e.zh: 菌核状质地有助于识别这种真菌。

e.en: The patient was treated for painful {sclerotitis}.
e.zh: 这名患者因疼痛性巩膜炎接受治疗。

e.en: Severe {sclerotitis} can threaten vision.
e.zh: 严重的巩膜炎可能威胁视力。

e.en: The fungus survived winter as a {sclerotium}.
e.zh: 这种真菌以菌核形式越冬。

e.en: Each {sclerotium} contained stored nutrients.
e.zh: 每个菌核都含有储存的养分。

e.en: Insects darken during cuticle {sclerotization}.
e.zh: 昆虫在表皮硬化过程中颜色会变深。

e.en: The study measured {sclerotization} after molting.
e.zh: 研究测量了蜕皮后的硬化程度。

e.en: The new cuticle begins to {sclerotize} quickly.
e.zh: 新的表皮很快开始硬化。

e.en: These tissues {sclerotize} as the insect matures.
e.zh: 这些组织会随着昆虫成熟而硬化。

e.en: The beetle has a heavily {sclerotized} shell.
e.zh: 这只甲虫有高度硬化的外壳。

e.en: Researchers compared soft and {sclerotized} tissues.
e.zh: 研究人员比较了柔软组织和硬化组织。

e.en: The lesion had a {sclerotoid} appearance.
e.zh: 这个病灶呈硬化样外观。

e.en: A {sclerotoid} mass formed in the culture dish.
e.zh: 培养皿中形成了一个似菌核的团块。

e.en: The vertebra develops partly from the {sclerotome}.
e.zh: 椎骨部分由生骨节发育而来。

e.en: The surgeon used a {sclerotome} for the incision.
e.zh: 外科医生用硬组织切刀进行切开。

e.en: The ophthalmologist performed a small {sclerotomy}.
e.zh: 眼科医生做了一处小的巩膜切开。

e.en: Bleeding occurred near the {sclerotomy} site.
e.zh: 巩膜切开部位附近出现了出血。

e.en: A tiny {sclerotule} appeared on the specimen.
e.zh: 标本上出现了一个小菌核。

e.en: The paper described each {sclerotule} in detail.
e.zh: 论文详细描述了每个小硬化体。

e.en: The plant developed a {sclerous} outer layer.
e.zh: 这株植物形成了坚硬的外层。

e.en: Doctors noted {sclerous} changes in the tissue.
e.zh: 医生注意到组织出现了硬化变化。

e.en: The shell showed a {scobicular} surface under magnification.
e.zh: 放大后，贝壳表面呈现锉屑状纹理。

e.en: A {scobicular} pattern covered the fossil fragment.
e.zh: 化石碎片上覆盖着锉屑状花纹。

e.en: The sample broke into {scobiform} particles.
e.zh: 样品碎成了锯屑状颗粒。

e.en: A {scobiform} deposit lined the cavity.
e.zh: 空腔内壁附着着粉屑状沉积物。

e.en: The mineral had a {scobinate} surface.
e.zh: 这种矿物表面粗糙如被锉成屑。

e.en: A {scobinate} texture distinguished the sample.
e.zh: 锉屑状粗糙质地让这个样品显得不同。

e.en: The carpenter swept the {scobs} from the bench.
e.zh: 木匠把工作台上的刨花扫掉了。

e.en: Fine {scobs} collected beneath the drill.
e.zh: 细小的锯屑聚集在钻头下面。

e.en: The old herb guide called the plant {scoke}.
e.zh: 那本旧草药指南把这种植物称为美洲商陆。

e.en: Farmers removed {scoke} from the pasture.
e.zh: 农民把牧场里的美洲商陆清除了。

e.en: The microscope revealed several {scoleces} in the sample.
e.zh: 显微镜显示样本中有几个绦虫头节。

e.en: Hooks on the {scoleces} help the parasites attach.
e.zh: 绦虫头节上的钩帮助寄生虫附着。

e.en: The veterinarian suspected {scoleciasis} after the examination.
e.zh: 检查后，兽医怀疑是蠕虫感染病。

e.en: Untreated {scoleciasis} may cause digestive problems.
e.zh: 未经治疗的蠕虫感染病可能引起消化问题。

e.en: The collector added {scolecite} to the mineral cabinet.
e.zh: 收藏者把钙沸石加入了矿物柜。

e.en: Needlelike crystals of {scolecite} filled the cavity.
e.zh: 针状钙沸石晶体填满了空洞。

e.en: The shale contained a well-preserved {scolecodont}.
e.zh: 页岩中含有保存完好的多毛类颚化石。

e.en: A {scolecodont} can reveal ancient worm diversity.
e.zh: 多毛类颚化石能揭示古代蠕虫的多样性。

e.en: The {scolex} anchors the tapeworm to the intestine.
e.zh: 绦虫头节把绦虫固定在肠道上。

e.en: Under the lens, the {scolex} had visible suckers.
e.zh: 在镜头下，绦虫头节可见吸盘。

e.en: Several {scolices} were found in the cyst.
e.zh: 囊肿中发现了几个绦虫头节。

e.en: The technician counted the {scolices} carefully.
e.zh: 技术员仔细数了这些绦虫头节。

e.en: A large {scoliid} visited the flowers.
e.zh: 一只大型土蜂科昆虫飞到花上。

e.en: The {scoliid} larva feeds on beetle grubs.
e.zh: 土蜂科幼虫以甲虫幼虫为食。

scontion.t: 小壁灯；烛台灯座；壁台灯

e.en: A brass {scontion} lit the narrow hallway.
e.zh: 一盏黄铜小壁灯照亮了狭窄的走廊。

e.en: The old inn kept a candle in each {scontion}.
e.zh: 那家老客栈在每个壁式烛台里都放着一支蜡烛。

e.en: She wore a black {scoop-neck} dress to dinner.
e.zh: 她穿了一条黑色低圆领连衣裙去吃晚餐。

e.en: The T-shirt has a soft {scoop-neck} and short sleeves.
e.zh: 这件T恤是柔和的大圆领，还有短袖。
