e.zh: 她交上了一封单倍行距的信。

e.en: Use {single-spacing} for the notes at the end.
e.zh: 末尾的注释请使用单倍行距排版。

e.zh: 编辑把文件改成了单倍行距。

e.en: The team designed a {single-stage} approval process.
e.zh: 团队设计了一个单阶段审批流程。

e.zh: 单级火箭结构更简单，但效率较低。

e.en: The app offers a {single-step} login option.
e.zh: 这个应用提供一步完成的登录选项。

e.en: Run the {single-step} test before changing the code.
e.zh: 改代码前先运行单步测试。

e.en: The virus contains {single-stranded} RNA.
e.zh: 这种病毒含有单链RNA。

e.en: She used {single-stranded} thread for the repair.
e.zh: 她用单股线来修补。

e.en: The mountain railway is mostly {single-track}.
e.zh: 这条山区铁路大多是单轨的。

e.zh: 他思路单一的做法忽略了其他可能。

e.en: The course is taught as a {single-unit} module.
e.zh: 这门课作为一个单一单元模块来教授。

e.en: They bought a {single-unit} home near the park.
e.zh: 他们在公园附近买了一套独户住宅。

e.en: This is a {single-user} license for the software.
e.zh: 这是该软件的单用户许可证。

e.en: The old database was built for {single-user} access.
e.zh: 旧数据库是为单用户访问设计的。

e.en: She sailed {singlehanded} across the Atlantic.
e.zh: 她独自驾船横渡了大西洋。

e.en: His {singlehanded} catch saved the match.
e.zh: 他单手接球挽救了这场比赛。

e.en: A {singlemasted} boat waited in the harbor.
e.zh: 一艘单桅船停在港口等候。

e.en: They restored a small {singlemasted} fishing vessel.
e.zh: 他们修复了一艘小型单桅渔船。

e.en: He learned {singlestick} at a historical fencing club.
e.zh: 他在一个历史击剑俱乐部学习单棍剑术。

e.en: The instructor handed each student a {singlestick}.
e.zh: 教练给每个学生发了一根练习棍。

e.en: The old {singlesticker} demonstrated a careful guard.
e.zh: 那位老单棍剑术练习者示范了一个谨慎的防守姿势。

e.en: A skilled {singlesticker} values footwork as much as strikes.
e.zh: 熟练的单棍剑术练习者同样重视步法和击打。

e.en: The farmer repaired the {singletree} before hitching the horse.
e.zh: 农夫套马前修好了马车横木。

e.zh: 田边孤零零地立着一棵单独的树。

e.en: Her speech shifts easily between standard English and {Singlish}.
e.zh: 她说话时能自然地在标准英语和新加坡式英语之间切换。

e.en: Some tourists find {Singlish} hard to understand at first.
e.zh: 有些游客一开始觉得新加坡式英语很难懂。

singsongy.t: 像唱歌似的；抑扬顿挫的

e.en: The guide spoke in a {singsongy} voice.
e.zh: 导游说话声音像唱歌似的。

e.en: Her {singsongy} reading made the poem feel playful.
e.zh: 她抑扬顿挫的朗读让这首诗显得很俏皮。

e.en: Mozart wrote a famous {singspiel} in German.
e.zh: 莫扎特用德语写过一部著名的德国歌唱剧。

e.en: The festival staged a comic {singspiel} with spoken dialogue.
e.zh: 音乐节上演了一部带对白的喜剧性德国歌唱剧。

e.en: The editor asked him to {singularise} the noun.
e.zh: 编辑让他把这个名词改成单数形式。

e.en: Some style guides {singularise} collective terms.
e.zh: 有些风格指南会把集合性用语改成单数形式。

e.en: The essay criticizes political {singularism}.
e.zh: 这篇文章批评政治上的单一论。

e.en: His philosophy leans toward {singularism} over universal rules.
e.zh: 他的哲学倾向于强调个体性，而不是普遍规则。

e.en: The software can {singularize} English nouns automatically.
e.zh: 这个软件能自动把英语名词变成单数形式。

e.en: Writers sometimes {singularize} a group to stress unity.
e.zh: 作者有时会把群体写成单数，以强调整体性。

e.en: The {singularized} label appears in the menu.
e.zh: 变成单数形式的标签会显示在菜单里。

e.en: A {singularized} community can seem more unified than it is.
e.zh: 被单数化描述的群体可能显得比实际更统一。

e.en: The parser {singularizes} plural nouns before matching them.
e.zh: 解析器会先把复数名词变成单数，再进行匹配。

e.en: The author {singularizes} the crowd as one angry voice.
e.zh: 作者把人群单数化，写成一个愤怒的声音。

e.en: The tool is {singularizing} each plural entry.
e.zh: 这个工具正在把每个复数条目变成单数形式。

e.en: She warned against {singularizing} a diverse culture.
e.zh: 她警告不要把多元文化单一化。

e.en: She {single-handedly} organized the entire conference.
e.zh: 她单枪匹马组织了整场会议。

e.en: The goalkeeper almost {single-handedly} saved the team from defeat.
e.zh: 守门员几乎凭一己之力让球队免于落败。

e.en: Sailing the Atlantic alone was a remarkable {single-hander}.
e.zh: 独自横渡大西洋是一次了不起的单人航行。

e.en: The small racing boat was designed as a {single-hander}.
e.zh: 这艘小型赛艇是按单人船设计的。

single-hearted.t: 一心一意的；真诚专一的

e.zh: 她一心一意的奉献打动了村里的每个人。

e.en: He gave a {single-hearted} promise to serve the public.
e.zh: 他真诚专一地承诺为公众服务。

e.en: She worked {single-heartedly} for the charity for years.
e.zh: 她多年来一心一意为这家慈善机构工作。

e.en: He {single-heartedly} supported his friend's difficult decision.
e.zh: 他真诚地支持朋友那个艰难的决定。

e.en: Her {single-heartedness} made the long campaign possible.
e.zh: 她的一心一意让这场漫长的运动得以坚持。

e.en: The poem praises the {single-heartedness} of loyal love.
e.zh: 这首诗赞美忠贞爱情中的真诚专一。

e.en: A {single-humped} camel crossed the desert track.
e.zh: 一只单峰骆驼穿过了沙漠小路。

e.en: The child drew a {single-humped} animal in the sand.
e.zh: 孩子在沙地上画了一只有一个驼峰的动物。

e.en: The botanist noted the plant's {single-leaf} pattern.
e.zh: 植物学家注意到这种植物的单叶形态。

e.en: The notice was printed as a {single-leaf} handout.
e.zh: 通知被印成单张传单发放。

single-length.t: 单一长度的；同一长度的

e.zh: 她选择了同一长度的发型，方便打理。

e.en: The factory sells {single-length} boards for standard shelving.
e.zh: 工厂出售单一长度的木板，用于标准货架。

e.zh: 他买了一台简单的单镜头相机用于旅行。

e.en: The experiment used a {single-lens} optical system.
e.zh: 这个实验使用了单透镜光学系统。

e.en: My father still prefers a {single-lens-reflex} camera.
e.zh: 我父亲仍然偏爱单镜头反光相机。

e.en: The course explains how {single-lens-reflex} focusing works.
e.zh: 这门课程讲解单镜头反光对焦的工作原理。

e.en: Please write a {single-line} answer below.
e.zh: 请在下面写一个单行答案。

e.en: The artist used a {single-line} drawing style.
e.zh: 这位艺术家采用了一笔线条式的画法。

single-loader.t: 单发装填枪；单次装载器

e.en: The museum displayed an old {single-loader} rifle.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一支老式单发装填步枪。

e.en: This machine works as a {single-loader} for test samples.
e.zh: 这台机器作为测试样品的单次装载器使用。

single-minded.t: 专心致志的；目标坚定的

e.en: Her {single-minded} focus helped her finish the novel.
e.zh: 她专心致志的投入帮助她完成了那部小说。

e.en: He was {single-minded} about winning the contract.
e.zh: 他一心只想着拿下这份合同。

single-mindedly.t: 专心致志地；一心一意地

e.zh: 他们专心致志地工作，以赶上最后期限。

e.en: She pursued the title {single-mindedly} for five years.
e.zh: 她五年来一心一意追逐这个冠军头衔。

e.en: His {single-mindedness} can be inspiring and exhausting.
e.zh: 他的专心执着既能鼓舞人，也会让人疲惫。

e.en: The project required unusual {single-mindedness} from the team.
e.zh: 这个项目需要团队表现出非同寻常的目标坚定。

e.en: She grew up in a {single-parent} household.
e.zh: 她在一个单亲家庭中长大。

e.en: The school offers support for every {single-parent}.
e.zh: 学校为每位单亲家长提供支持。

e.zh: 这个软件会对文件进行一次通过式扫描。

e.zh: 单遍过滤器清除了大部分灰尘。

e.zh: 这套公寓使用单相电源。

e.zh: 他们认为单阶段计划风险太高而否决了它。

e.en: The engineer recommended a {single-point} connection.
e.zh: 工程师建议采用单点连接。

e.en: Her talk had a clear {single-point} message.
e.zh: 她的演讲有一个清晰集中的核心信息。

e.en: The program stores coordinates in {single-precision} format.
e.zh: 该程序以单精度格式存储坐标。

e.en: Using {single-precision} arithmetic made the model faster.
e.zh: 使用单精度运算让这个模型运行得更快。

e.en: The ferry had a {single-screw} propulsion system.
e.zh: 这艘渡轮采用单螺旋桨推进系统。

e.en: A {single-screw} extruder shaped the plastic tube.
e.zh: 一台单螺杆挤出机成型了这根塑料管。

single-seat.t: 单座的；只有一个座位的

e.zh: 他试驾了一辆单座赛车。

e.en: The company designed a {single-seat} workstation for operators.
e.zh: 公司为操作员设计了一个单座工作台。

e.en: The driver climbed into the {single-seater} before the race.
e.zh: 比赛前，车手爬进了那辆单座赛车。

e.en: The old {single-seater} was restored for air shows.
e.zh: 那架老式单座飞机被修复后用于航空表演。

single-seeded.t: 单籽的；只有一粒种子的

e.zh: 这种果实完全成熟时通常只有一粒种子。

e.en: She compared {single-seeded} berries with multi-seeded ones.
e.zh: 她把单籽浆果和多籽浆果进行了比较。

e.en: He attended a {single-sex} school in London.
e.zh: 他在伦敦上过一所单性别学校。

e.zh: 这家健身房周五提供男女分开的游泳时段。

e.zh: 这种方言用单数化词形来指一粒谷物。

e.en: In linguistics, a {singulative} contrasts with a collective noun.
e.zh: 在语言学中，个体词与集合名词相对。

e.en: The patient's {singultation} continued through the night.
e.zh: 病人的呃逆持续了一整夜。

e.en: Her speech broke into {singultation} after the bad news.
e.zh: 听到坏消息后，她说话变成一阵阵抽噎。

e.en: Persistent {singultus} can disturb sleep and eating.
e.zh: 持续性呃逆会影响睡眠和进食。

e.zh: 医生把打嗝记为主要症状。

e.zh: 宝石学家把那颗黄色石头鉴定为硼铝镁石。

e.zh: 高品质的锡兰石有时会被切割后供收藏者购买。

e.en: The empire tried to {sinicize} the border communities.
e.zh: 帝国试图使边境社群汉化。

e.zh: 有些外来词经过中国化处理后更容易使用。

e.zh: 这个家族采用了一个汉化后的姓氏形式。

e.zh: 在帝国统治下，当地习俗逐渐被汉化。

e.zh: 这项政策使该地区的学校仪式汉化。

e.zh: 译者常会为年长读者把名字中国化。

e.en: Officials were accused of {sinicizing} minority education.
e.zh: 官员被指在使少数族群教育汉化。

e.en: The editor favored {sinicizing} foreign names in the article.
e.zh: 编辑倾向于在文章中把外国名字中国化。

e.en: Mustard seeds contain {sinigrin}, which gives them sharpness.
e.zh: 芥菜籽含有黑芥子苷，因此带有辛辣味。

e.en: Researchers measured {sinigrin} levels in several cabbage varieties.
e.zh: 研究人员测量了几种甘蓝中的黑芥子苷含量。

e.en: The nerve fibers curve {sinistrad} before entering the ganglion.
e.zh: 这些神经纤维在进入神经节前向左弯曲。

e.en: The diagram shows the organ shifting {sinistrad} during development.
e.zh: 图示显示该器官在发育过程中朝左移位。

e.en: The snail has a rare {sinistral} shell.
e.zh: 这只蜗牛有罕见的左旋壳。

e.en: A {sinistral} fault moves the opposite block to the left.
e.zh: 左旋断层会使对侧岩块向左移动。

e.en: The study compared {sinistrality} and right-handedness in children.
e.zh: 这项研究比较了儿童的左利性和右利手现象。

e.en: Shell {sinistrality} is uncommon in this species.
e.zh: 这种物种的贝壳左旋性并不常见。

e.en: The shell coils {sinistrally} from the apex.
e.zh: 这枚壳从顶端开始向左旋卷。

e.en: The line bends {sinistrally} near the base of the drawing.
e.zh: 这条线在图的底部附近向左弯曲。

e.en: The surgeon noted slight {sinistration} of the organ.
e.zh: 外科医生注意到该器官有轻微左偏。

e.en: Old medical texts used {sinistration} for movement toward the left.
e.zh: 旧医学文献用这个词表示向左侧的移动。

e.en: Doctors used {sinistrin} to estimate kidney filtration.
e.zh: 医生使用菊粉样多糖来估算肾脏滤过功能。

e.en: The lab prepared {sinistrin} for a renal clearance test.
e.zh: 实验室为肾清除率测试制备了左旋糖苷。

e.en: A {sinistrocular} shooter may aim better with the left eye.
e.zh: 左眼优势的射手用左眼瞄准可能更准。

e.en: The exam showed a strongly {sinistrocular} pattern.
e.zh: 检查显示出明显的左眼优势模式。

e.en: The script developed a {sinistrodextral} writing direction.
e.zh: 这种文字发展出了由左向右的书写方向。

e.en: Readers found the {sinistrodextral} layout easier to follow.
e.zh: 读者觉得由左向右的版式更容易阅读。

e.en: The experiment measured {sinistrogyration} in the crystal sample.
e.zh: 实验测量了晶体样本的左旋现象。

e.en: Botanists described the vine's {sinistrogyration} around the pole.
e.zh: 植物学家描述了藤蔓绕杆向左旋转的情况。

e.en: The plant has a {sinistrorse} climbing stem.
e.zh: 这种植物有向左缠绕的攀援茎。

e.en: A {sinistrorse} spiral appears on the shell surface.
e.zh: 贝壳表面出现一条左旋螺纹。

e.en: The herb grew with a {sinistrous} twist around the stake.
e.zh: 这株草绕着木桩向左扭转生长。

e.en: The tale gave the stranger a {sinistrous} air.
e.zh: 这个故事让那位陌生人显得带有不祥气息。

e.en: The vine curled {sinistrously} around the branch.
e.zh: 藤蔓向左缠绕在树枝上。

e.en: The clouds gathered {sinistrously} over the empty road.
e.zh: 乌云不祥地聚集在空荡的道路上方。

e.en: The boat was old but not easily {sinkable}.
e.zh: 这条船很旧，但并不容易沉没。

e.en: Designers tested whether the damaged model was {sinkable}.
e.zh: 设计人员测试受损模型是否会下沉。

e.en: Engineers measured soil {sinkage} after the heavy rain.
e.zh: 大雨过后，工程师测量了土壤沉陷量。

e.en: Tire {sinkage} affects how vehicles move on soft ground.
e.zh: 轮胎下陷会影响车辆在软地上的行驶。

e.en: She washed a {sinkful} of dishes after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后她洗了一满水槽的盘子。

e.en: A {sinkful} of cold water cooled the bottles quickly.
e.zh: 一满水槽的冷水很快把那些瓶子降温了。

e.en: The plumber sealed the crack near the {sinkhead}.
e.zh: 水管工封住了水槽顶部附近的裂缝。

e.en: Old stains had gathered around the {sinkhead}.
e.zh: 水槽头部周围积了一圈旧污渍。

e.en: The note said {sinlge-space}, but she meant single-space.
e.zh: 便条上写的是误拼的“sinlge-space”，但她想说的是单倍行距。

e.en: He left {sinlge-space} unchanged in the draft by mistake.
e.zh: 他误把草稿里的“sinlge-space”这个拼写保留了下来。

e.en: The collector labeled the tiny crystal as {sinnerite}.
e.zh: 收藏者把这小块晶体标为辛纳石。

e.en: Geologists found traces of {sinnerite} in the sample.
e.zh: 地质学家在样本中发现了辛纳石的痕迹。

e.en: The sailor made a strong {sinnet} from old rope.
e.zh: 水手用旧绳编成了一条结实的扁绳。

e.en: Her bracelet used a flat {sinnet} pattern.
e.zh: 她的手链采用了扁辫状的编绳花样。

e.en: The report focused on {Sino} trade relations.
e.zh: 这份报告关注中国相关的贸易关系。

e.en: She studies {Sino} cultural influence in Southeast Asia.
e.zh: 她研究中国文化在东南亚的影响。

e.en: The summit addressed {Sino-American} trade tensions.
e.zh: 这次峰会讨论了中美贸易紧张关系。

e.en: Her novel follows a {Sino-American} family in California.
e.zh: 她的小说讲述了加州一个华裔美国家庭的故事。

e.en: Analysts watched {Sino-US} talks closely.
e.zh: 分析人士密切关注中美会谈。

e.en: The article reviewed recent {Sino-US} policy disputes.
e.zh: 这篇文章回顾了近期的中美政策争议。

e.en: The paper measured {sinoacutine} in the plant extract.
e.zh: 论文测定了植物提取物中的青藤碱类生物碱含量。

e.en: Researchers compared {sinoacutine} with related alkaloids.
e.zh: 研究人员把青藤碱类生物碱与相关生物碱作了比较。

sinoatrial.t: 窦房的，心脏起搏部位的

e.en: The {sinoatrial} node controls the heart's rhythm.
e.zh: 窦房结控制着心脏的节律。

e.en: Doctors found a problem with her {sinoatrial} function.
e.zh: 医生发现她的窦房功能有问题。

sinography.t: 汉字书写；汉学文字研究

e.en: Her thesis examines {sinography} in early Japanese texts.
e.zh: 她的论文研究早期日本文献中的汉字书写。

e.en: The museum displayed tools used in traditional {sinography}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了传统汉字书写所用的工具。

e.en: The meteorite contained tiny grains of {sinoite}.
e.zh: 这块陨石含有细小的硅氮石颗粒。

e.en: Mineralogists identified {sinoite} under the microscope.
e.zh: 矿物学家在显微镜下鉴定出了硅氮石。

sinomenine.t: 青藤碱，一种植物生物碱

e.en: The study tested {sinomenine} for anti-inflammatory effects.
e.zh: 这项研究测试了青藤碱的抗炎作用。

e.en: Some medicines derive {sinomenine} from a climbing plant.
e.zh: 有些药物从一种攀缘植物中提取青藤碱。

e.en: The artist mixed {sinopia} with other earth pigments.
e.zh: 画家把赭红颜料同其他土色颜料混合。

e.en: Restorers uncovered the {sinopia} beneath the fresco.
e.zh: 修复人员在湿壁画下面发现了赭红底稿。

e.en: Ancient painters used {sinopis} for warm shadows.
e.zh: 古代画家用赭红颜料表现温暖的阴影。

e.en: The manuscript describes {sinopis} as a red earth.
e.zh: 手稿把赭红颜料描述为一种红色土。

e.en: The sample of {sinopite} left a reddish streak.
e.zh: 这块赭红石样本留下了一道红色条痕。

e.en: Painters once ground {sinopite} into pigment.
e.zh: 画家过去会把赭红石磨成颜料。

e.en: The shield was described as {sinople} in the old blazon.
e.zh: 旧纹章说明中把盾牌描述为绿色。

e.en: In heraldry, {sinople} can mean the color green.
e.zh: 在纹章学中，sinople 可指绿色。

e.en: The fresco's {sinopsis} revealed the painter's first plan.
e.zh: 壁画的赭红底稿显露出画家的最初构思。

e.en: Art historians studied the {sinopsis} under the plaster.
e.zh: 艺术史学家研究了灰泥层下的赭红底稿。

e.en: Police seized several bags of {sinsemilla} from the car.
e.zh: 警方从车里查获了几袋无籽大麻花。

e.en: The article described how {sinsemilla} is cultivated.
e.zh: 文章描述了无籽大麻花的种植方式。

e.en: The factory uses heat to {sinter} the metal powder.
e.zh: 工厂用高温把金属粉末烧结起来。

e.en: Mineral-rich water left {sinter} around the spring.
e.zh: 富含矿物质的水在泉边留下了烧结沉积物。

e.en: A {sirenian} grazed slowly in the warm bay.
e.zh: 一只海牛目动物在温暖的海湾里慢慢吃草。

e.en: The museum displayed a {sirenian} skull beside whale bones.
e.zh: 博物馆把一个海牛类头骨陈列在鲸骨旁边。

e.en: The soldiers feared {siriasis} during the desert march.
e.zh: 士兵们在沙漠行军时担心发生日射病。

e.en: Old medical books described {siriasis} as a dangerous fever.
e.zh: 旧医学书把日射病描述为一种危险的发热病。

e.en: The astronomer mentioned a {siriometer} in his lecture.
e.zh: 那位天文学家在讲座中提到了天狼星距离单位。

e.en: A {siriometer} was once used for vast stellar distances.
e.zh: 天狼星距离单位曾被用来表示巨大的恒星距离。

e.en: A hot {sirocco} blew dust across the harbor.
e.zh: 一阵炽热的西洛可风把尘土吹过港口。

e.en: The paintings cracked after days of {sirocco}.
e.zh: 连续几天的干热南风过后，画作出现了裂纹。

e.en: Spring {siroccos} often made the town feel airless.
e.zh: 春季的西洛可热风常让小镇闷得透不过气。

e.en: Sailors learned to recognize {siroccos} before they arrived.
e.zh: 水手们学会了在西洛可风到来前辨认它们。

e.en: Come here, {sirra}, and answer me plainly.
e.zh: 过来，小子，老老实实回答我。

e.en: The old play used {sirra} as a sharp address.
e.zh: 那出古戏用先生这个词作尖刻的称呼。

e.en: Stand still, {sirrah}, while I speak.
e.zh: 站住，小子，听我说话。

e.en: In Shakespeare, {sirrah} often sounds scolding or superior.
e.zh: 在莎士比亚作品中，sirrah常带有斥责或居高临下的口气。

e.en: They danced the {sirtaki} after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后他们跳起了希腊西塔基舞。

e.en: The music quickened as the {sirtaki} reached its end.
e.zh: 西塔基舞接近尾声时，音乐节奏加快了。

e.en: The recipe called for {sirup} instead of honey.
e.zh: 这份食谱要求用糖浆而不是蜂蜜。

e.en: Old labels sometimes spell syrup as {sirup}.
e.zh: 旧标签有时把syrup拼作sirup。

e.en: She was {siruping} the fruit for dessert.
e.zh: 她正在给做甜点的水果浇糖浆。

e.en: The factory began {siruping} the mixture before bottling it.
e.zh: 工厂在装瓶前开始把混合物加工成糖浆状。

e.en: The sauce was too {sirupy} for my taste.
e.zh: 这酱对我来说太像糖浆一样甜腻了。

e.en: His {sirupy} speech made the audience uneasy.
e.zh: 他甜腻做作的讲话让听众感到不自在。

e.en: The troubadour composed a {sirvente} against the corrupt lord.
e.zh: 那位行吟诗人写了一首中世纪讽刺诗抨击腐败领主。

e.en: A {sirvente} could mix politics with sharp personal attack.
e.zh: 中世纪讽刺诗可以把政治议题和尖锐的人身攻击混在一起。

e.en: Several {sirventes} survive in old Occitan manuscripts.
e.zh: 几首中世纪讽刺诗保存在古奥克语手稿中。

e.en: The lecture compared love songs with political {sirventes}.
e.zh: 讲座把爱情歌曲和政治讽刺诗作了比较。

e.en: The biologist measured a {siscowet} from Lake Superior.
e.zh: 生物学家测量了一条来自苏必利尔湖的肥湖鳟。

e.en: A {siscowet} has more fat than many lake trout.
e.zh: 肥湖鳟比许多湖鳟含有更多脂肪。

e.en: The {sismogram} showed a sharp tremor at dawn.
e.zh: 地震记录图显示黎明时有一次强烈震动。

e.en: Researchers compared each {sismogram} with reports from nearby towns.
e.zh: 研究人员把每张地震记录图同附近城镇的报告进行比较。

e.en: The old {sismograph} still recorded small earthquakes.
e.zh: 那台旧地震仪仍能记录小地震。

e.en: A digital {sismograph} can send readings in real time.
e.zh: 数字地震仪可以实时发送读数。

e.en: The old diagram labels this tube as a {siphonium}.
e.zh: 那张旧图把这根管子标为虹吸管状结构。

e.en: A damaged {siphonium} can affect the creature's feeding.
e.zh: 受损的虹吸管状器官会影响这种生物进食。

e.en: Researchers isolated {siphonochalynol} from a marine sponge.
e.zh: 研究人员从一种海绵中分离出虹吸查林醇。

e.en: The paper discusses whether {siphonochalynol} blocks cell growth.
e.zh: 论文讨论虹吸查林醇是否会抑制细胞生长。

e.en: The fern stem contains a clear {siphonostele}.
e.zh: 这根蕨类茎中有清晰的管状中柱。

e.en: A {siphonostele} surrounds the central pith of the plant.
e.zh: 管状中柱围绕着植物中央的髓部。

e.en: The fossil shell was clearly {siphuncled}.
e.zh: 这枚化石贝壳明显带有体管。

e.en: A {siphuncled} chamber helped identify the ancient cephalopod.
e.zh: 一个带体管的腔室帮助确认了这种古代头足类。

e.en: The specimen has a {siphunculate} internal structure.
e.zh: 这个标本具有带小管的内部结构。

e.en: A {siphunculate} shell appears in many technical descriptions.
e.zh: 带体管的贝壳常出现在许多专业描述中。

e.en: The curator noted the {siphunculated} fossil in the drawer.
e.zh: 馆员注意到抽屉里那件有体管的化石。

e.en: Several {siphunculated} shells were found in the limestone layer.
e.zh: 石灰岩层中发现了几枚有体管的贝壳。

e.en: The {siphunculus} runs through the chambers of the shell.
e.zh: 体管贯穿贝壳内部的各个腔室。

e.en: Damage to the {siphunculus} changed how the fossil was classified.
e.zh: 体管受损改变了这件化石的分类判断。

e.en: The broth was mild but pleasantly {sipid}.
e.zh: 这碗汤味道清淡，但还算鲜美可口。

e.en: Critics found his prose more {sipid} than profound.
e.zh: 评论家觉得他的散文有些趣味，却谈不上深刻。

e.en: The cabinet was made from dark {sipo}.
e.zh: 这个柜子是用深色西波木做成的。

e.en: Builders chose {sipo} for its strength outdoors.
e.zh: 建筑工人因西波木适合户外且结实而选用了它。

e.en: She floated a crisp {sippet} on the soup.
e.zh: 她把一小片脆面包放在汤面上。

e.en: The old recipe calls for a buttered {sippet}.
e.zh: 这道老菜谱要求用一小片涂黄油的面包。

e.en: The biologist found a {sipunculan} in the sand.
e.zh: 生物学家在沙中发现了一只星虫。

e.en: A {sipunculan} can retract its front end quickly.
e.zh: 星虫能迅速缩回身体前端。

e.en: The mud sample contained one small {sipunculid}.
e.zh: 泥样里有一只小星虫。

e.en: A {sipunculid} worm lives hidden under the seabed.
e.zh: 星虫通常隐藏在海床下面生活。

e.en: A faded {siquis} hung near the church door.
e.zh: 教堂门边挂着一张褪色的启事。

e.en: He posted a {siquis} after losing his horse.
e.zh: 他丢了马以后贴出了一张失物启事。

e.en: The comic used {sir-reverence} as a polite old euphemism.
e.zh: 那位喜剧演员把sir-reverence当作旧式委婉说法来用。

e.en: In the old text, {sir-reverence} simply means excrement.
e.zh: 在那篇旧文本里，sir-reverence只是指粪便。

e.en: Farmers planted {siratro} to improve the pasture.
e.zh: 农民种植锡拉草来改良牧场。

e.en: {Siratro} grows well in warm, wet regions.
e.zh: 锡拉草在温暖潮湿地区生长良好。

e.en: The estate {sircar} kept all the accounts.
e.zh: 庄园的管事负责保存所有账目。

e.en: A local {sircar} helped the merchant with taxes.
e.zh: 当地一名官员帮助商人处理税务。

e.en: The {sirdar} led the troops across the river.
e.zh: 那名军官率领部队渡过河流。

e.en: A mine {sirdar} checked the workers at dawn.
e.zh: 矿上的工头清晨检查了工人。

e.en: No {siree}, I will not sell the farm.
e.zh: 不，先生，我绝不会卖掉农场。

e.en: Yes {siree}, that was a fine meal.
e.zh: 是啊，先生，那顿饭真不错。

e.en: The lab preserved old {sismographic} charts from the earthquake.
e.zh: 实验室保存了那次地震的旧地震记录图。

e.en: Engineers checked the {sismographic} equipment before dawn.
e.zh: 工程师们在黎明前检查了地震仪设备。

e.en: The boys cruelly called him a {sissie} for crying.
e.zh: 那些男孩因为他哭了，就刻薄地叫他胆小鬼。

e.en: She rejected the old insult {sissie} as childish and mean.
e.zh: 她认为“娘娘腔”这种老套骂法幼稚又刻薄。

sissified.t: 被说成娘娘腔的；柔弱化的

e.en: The critic mocked the hero as {sissified} and unconvincing.
e.zh: 评论家嘲笑这个英雄像个娘娘腔，毫无说服力。

e.en: He hated being {sissified} by relatives for liking dance.
e.zh: 他讨厌亲戚因为他喜欢舞蹈就把他说得柔弱。

e.en: He worried the pink scarf looked {sissyish} to his teammates.
e.zh: 他担心那条粉色围巾在队友眼里显得有点娘娘腔。

e.en: The coach dismissed their fear as {sissyish}, which was unfair.
e.zh: 教练把他们的害怕说成怯懦，这并不公平。

sistah.t: 黑人英语中的姐妹；姐们儿

e.en: She greeted her friend with a warm, joking {sistah}.
e.zh: 她用一句亲切又带玩笑意味的“姐们儿”问候朋友。

e.en: The song celebrates every strong {sistah} in the neighborhood.
e.zh: 这首歌赞美社区里每一位坚强的姐妹。

e.en: In the old will, Mary was named his {sister-german}.
e.zh: 在那份旧遗嘱中，玛丽被称为他的同父同母亲姐妹。

e.en: A {sister-german} had stronger inheritance rights in that wording.
e.zh: 按那种措辞，同父同母的亲姐妹拥有更强的继承权。

e.en: As a {sisterless} child, he envied his cousins' noisy house.
e.zh: 作为没有姐妹的孩子，他羡慕表亲家热闹的屋子。

e.en: The story follows a {sisterless} queen seeking female allies.
e.zh: 故事讲述一位没有姐妹的女王寻找女性盟友。

sisterlike.t: 像姐妹般的；亲如姐妹的

e.en: Her {sisterlike} concern made the newcomer feel safe.
e.zh: 她像姐妹般的关心让新来的人感到安心。

e.en: They developed a {sisterlike} bond during the long campaign.
e.zh: 在漫长的活动中，她们建立了亲如姐妹的情谊。

e.en: Rainwater collected in a stone {sistern} behind the house.
e.zh: 雨水积存在屋后一个石砌蓄水池里。

e.en: The old {sistern} supplied water during dry months.
e.zh: 那个旧贮水槽在干旱月份提供用水。

e.en: Her two {sisters-in-law} helped prepare the wedding dinner.
e.zh: 她的两位嫂子帮忙准备婚宴。

e.en: The {sisters-in-law} disagreed about selling the family shop.
e.zh: 几个妯娌在是否出售家族店铺上意见不合。

e.en: The novel explores {sistership} beyond blood ties.
e.zh: 这部小说探讨了超越血缘的姐妹情谊。

e.en: Their colleges formed a formal {sistership} in 1920.
e.zh: 两所学院在1920年建立了正式的姊妹关系。

e.en: The museum labeled the bronze {sistra} as a ritual object.
e.zh: 博物馆把那件青铜叉形针标为仪式用品。

e.en: A small {sistra} was found beside the ancient beads.
e.zh: 一枚小叉形针在古代珠饰旁被发现。

e.en: The writer described the two towns as {sistroid} communities.
e.zh: 作者把这两座城镇描写成姊妹般的社区。

e.en: A {sistroid} resemblance linked the paired figures in the painting.
e.zh: 画中成对人物之间有一种姐妹般的相似。

e.en: The priestess shook a silver {sistrum} during the ceremony.
e.zh: 女祭司在仪式中摇动一只银制叉铃。

e.en: A painted {sistrum} appears beside the goddess in the tomb.
e.zh: 墓中女神旁边画着一件古埃及摇铃。

e.en: We had a serious {sit-down} with the manager.
e.zh: 我们和经理进行了一次严肃的会谈。

e.en: Workers began a {sit-down} protest inside the factory.
e.zh: 工人们在工厂内开始静坐抗议。

e.en: Each {sit-downer} refused to leave the lunch counter.
e.zh: 每个静坐抗议者都拒绝离开午餐柜台。

e.en: The tired {sit-downer} finally rose when the bell rang.
e.zh: 那个坐着休息的人听到铃声后终于站了起来。

e.en: The union scheduled three {sit-downs} with company leaders.
e.zh: 工会安排了三次与公司领导的会谈。

e.en: Student {sit-downs} spread to campuses across the state.
e.zh: 学生静坐抗议蔓延到全州各校园。

e.en: Students organized a {sit-in} at the administration building.
e.zh: 学生们在行政楼组织了一场静坐抗议。

e.en: I was allowed to {sit-in} on the advanced seminar.
e.zh: 我获准旁听那门高级研讨课。

e.en: One {sit-inner} read demands aloud to the reporters.
e.zh: 一名静坐抗议者向记者大声宣读诉求。

e.en: As a quiet {sit-inner}, she took notes but never spoke.
e.zh: 作为安静的旁听者，她做了笔记但从未发言。

e.en: The civil rights movement used {sit-ins} to challenge segregation.
e.zh: 民权运动用静坐抗议来挑战种族隔离。

e.en: The professor welcomed student {sit-ins} during open lectures.
e.zh: 教授欢迎学生在公开课上旁听。

e.en: She does fifty {sit-ups} before breakfast.
e.zh: 她早餐前做五十个仰卧起坐。

e.en: The child tried to {sit-up} when he heard music.
e.zh: 孩子听到音乐时试着坐直起来。

e.en: Grandmother carried a folded {sit-upon} to the picnic.
e.zh: 祖母带了一块折叠坐垫去野餐。

e.en: The scout made a waterproof {sit-upon} from newspaper and plastic.
e.zh: 童子军用报纸和塑料做了一个防水坐垫。

e.en: The {sitarist} tuned his instrument before the concert.
e.zh: 那位锡塔琴演奏者在音乐会前给乐器调音。

e.en: She became a respected {sitarist} in the classical tradition.
e.zh: 她成了古典传统中受尊敬的锡塔琴演奏者。

e.en: The old {sitcome} still makes my parents laugh.
e.zh: 那部老情景喜剧仍然能把我父母逗笑。

e.en: He wrote jokes for a weekly {sitcome}.
e.zh: 他为一档每周播出的情景喜剧写笑料。

e.en: One {sitdowner} refused to leave the factory gates.
e.zh: 一名静坐抗议者拒绝离开工厂大门。

e.en: The police interviewed each {sitdowner} after the protest.
e.zh: 抗议结束后，警方询问了每一名静坐者。

e.en: The students began a {sitfast} outside the ministry.
e.zh: 学生们在部委外开始了绝食静坐抗议。

e.en: Her {sitfast} drew attention to prison conditions.
e.zh: 她的绝食静坐让人们关注监狱环境。

e.en: He had not returned {sith} the winter storm.
e.zh: 自那场冬季暴风雪以来，他一直没有回来。

e.en: Many years have passed {sith} we first met.
e.zh: 自从我们初次见面，已经过去许多年。

e.en: She {sithed} softly at the bad news.
e.zh: 听到坏消息时，她轻轻叹了一口气。

e.en: The old man {sithed} and closed the letter.
e.zh: 老人叹息一声，把信合上了。

e.en: The workers organized a {sitin} at the factory.
e.zh: 工人们在工厂里组织了一场静坐抗议。

e.en: Students held a peaceful {sitin} in the library.
e.zh: 学生们在图书馆举行了和平的静坐抗议。

e.en: The lecture introduced {sitology} as the study of diet.
e.zh: 这场讲座把饮食学介绍为研究饮食的学科。

e.en: Few modern courses use the term {sitology} today.
e.zh: 如今很少有现代课程使用“饮食学”这个术语。

e.en: The doctor described his {sitomania} as unusually intense hunger.
e.zh: 医生把他的食欲亢进描述为异常强烈的饥饿感。

e.en: Older medical texts sometimes mention {sitomania}.
e.zh: 较早的医学文献有时会提到贪食症。

e.en: Her {sitophobia} made every meal stressful.
e.zh: 她的恐食症让每顿饭都变得很有压力。

e.en: The clinic treated {sitophobia} with gradual exposure.
e.zh: 诊所通过逐步接触疗法治疗恐食症。

e.en: The supplement contains {sitosterol} from plant oils.
e.zh: 这种补充剂含有来自植物油的谷甾醇。

e.en: Researchers measured {sitosterol} levels in the sample.
e.zh: 研究人员测量了样本中的谷甾醇水平。

e.en: The physician recommended {sitotherapy} for recovery.
e.zh: 医生建议用饮食疗法来帮助康复。

e.en: Ancient manuals discussed {sitotherapy} in detail.
e.zh: 古代手册详细讨论过饮食疗法。

e.en: The suspected {sitotoxin} caused severe stomach pain.
e.zh: 疑似食物毒素引起了严重胃痛。

e.en: Scientists isolated a {sitotoxin} from the spoiled grain.
e.zh: 科学家从变质谷物中分离出一种食物毒素。

e.en: The outbreak was diagnosed as {sitotoxism}.
e.zh: 这次暴发被诊断为食物中毒。

e.en: Old reports used {sitotoxism} for poisoning by food.
e.zh: 早期报告用“食物中毒”来指由食物引起的中毒。

e.en: The commander requested a {sitrep} before dawn.
e.zh: 指挥官要求天亮前提交一份情况报告。

e.en: Send me a quick {sitrep} after the meeting.
e.zh: 会议结束后给我发一份简短情况报告。

e.en: The bench looked barely {sittable} after the rain.
e.zh: 雨后那条长椅看起来几乎不能坐。

e.en: We need a {sittable} chair for the waiting room.
e.zh: 我们需要一把适合候诊室使用、能坐的椅子。

e.en: The guests were already {sitten} at the long table.
e.zh: 客人们已经在长桌旁坐下了。

e.en: In old verse, a {sitten} knight watched the gate.
e.zh: 在古诗中，一位坐着的骑士守望着大门。

e.en: A {sitter-in} blocked the office doorway.
e.zh: 一名静坐抗议者挡住了办公室门口。

e.en: Each {sitter-in} carried a sign demanding talks.
e.zh: 每名静坐抗议者都举着要求谈判的标语。

e.en: The sculpture was preserved in {situ}.
e.zh: 这座雕塑被保存在原处。

e.en: The cells were examined in {situ} under the microscope.
e.zh: 这些细胞在原位状态下用显微镜检查。

e.en: The seminar debated {situationethics} and moral rules.
e.zh: 研讨会辩论了情境伦理学与道德规则。

e.en: Critics said {situationethics} made decisions too flexible.
e.zh: 批评者说情境伦理学让决策过于灵活。

e.en: His essay defended {situationism} in social psychology.
e.zh: 他的文章为社会心理学中的情境主义辩护。

e.en: Artists associated {situationism} with radical urban critique.
e.zh: 艺术家们把情境主义同激进的城市批判联系起来。

e.en: The museum displayed a bronze {situla} from Italy.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一件来自意大利的青铜古提桶形容器。

e.en: Archaeologists found a decorated {situla} in the tomb.
e.zh: 考古学家在墓中发现了一件有装饰的古代提桶形容器。

e.en: She does fifty {situps} every morning before breakfast.
e.zh: 她每天早饭前做五十个仰卧起坐。

e.en: The coach counted each {situp} during the fitness test.
e.zh: 体能测试时，教练数着每一个仰卧起坐。

e.en: The lawyer discussed the {situs} of the trust assets.
e.zh: 律师讨论了信托资产的所在地。

e.en: Doctors noted the unusual {situs} of the organ.
e.zh: 医生注意到该器官的位置异常。

e.en: The nurse prepared a warm {sitz} bath for the patient.
e.zh: 护士为病人准备了温热的坐浴。

e.en: They held a short {sitz} to settle the details.
e.zh: 他们开了个简短会谈来敲定细节。

e.en: Reporters mocked the quiet front as a {sitzkrieg}.
e.zh: 记者把这条沉寂的战线讥讽为静坐战。

e.en: The negotiations became a political {sitzkrieg} with no movement.
e.zh: 谈判变成了一场毫无进展的政治僵持。

e.en: He left a deep {sitzmark} after falling on the slope.
e.zh: 他在斜坡上摔倒后留下了深深的雪地臀印。

e.en: Fresh {sitzmarks} showed where beginners had lost balance.
e.zh: 新留下的雪地坐痕显示初学者曾在那里失去平衡。

e.en: Several {sitzmarks} dotted the icy beginner slope.
e.zh: 结冰的初学者雪道上散布着几个雪地臀印。

e.en: The guide laughed at the {sitzmarks} beside the trail.
e.zh: 向导看到小道旁的坐痕笑了起来。

e.en: He wore an old {siwash} sweater by the fire.
e.zh: 他在火炉旁穿着一件旧式厚羊毛衫。

e.en: The word {Siwash} is now offensive in many contexts.
e.zh: 在许多语境中，Siwash这个词现在带有冒犯性。

e.en: The carpenter ordered a {six-by} for the frame.
e.zh: 木匠订了一根六英尺宽的木料做框架。

e.en: A warped {six-by} made the wall uneven.
e.zh: 一根弯曲的六英尺木料让墙面不平。

six-by-four.t: 六乘四木料；六乘四车辆

e.en: They used a {six-by-four} beam under the porch.
e.zh: 他们在门廊下面用了一根六乘四的木梁。

e.en: The farm bought a {six-by-four} truck for muddy roads.
e.zh: 农场买了一辆六乘四卡车来跑泥路。

e.en: A {six-by-six} post supported the heavy gate.
e.zh: 一根六乘六木柱支撑着沉重的大门。

e.en: The army drove a {six-by-six} through the snow.
e.zh: 军队开着六轮驱动车穿过雪地。

e.en: Sales showed a {six-fold} increase after the campaign.
e.zh: 活动之后，销售额增长了六倍。

e.en: The plan has a {six-fold} purpose, not just profit.
e.zh: 这个计划有六重目的，并不只是盈利。

e.en: The new guard is a strong {six-footer}.
e.zh: 新来的警卫是个强壮的六英尺高个子。

e.en: They installed a {six-footer} fence around the yard.
e.zh: 他们在院子周围装了一道六英尺高的围栏。

e.en: The cowboy carried a polished {six-gun} at his side.
e.zh: 牛仔腰间佩着一把擦得发亮的六发左轮手枪。

e.en: Old western films often featured a hero with a {six-gun}.
e.zh: 老西部片里常有带着六发手枪的英雄。

e.en: Doctors once used {six-o-six} to treat syphilis.
e.zh: 医生曾用六〇六药治疗梅毒。

e.en: The history text described {six-o-six} as an early chemotherapy drug.
e.zh: 历史教材把六〇六描述为早期化疗药物。

e.en: He brought a {six-pack} of soda to the picnic.
e.zh: 他带了一组六罐装汽水去野餐。

e.en: Months of training gave her a visible {six-pack}.
e.zh: 几个月的训练让她练出了明显的六块腹肌。

e.en: The sheriff placed his {six-shooter} on the desk.
e.zh: 治安官把他的六发左轮手枪放在桌上。

e.en: A rusty {six-shooter} hung above the bar.
e.zh: 吧台上方挂着一把生锈的六发左轮手枪。

e.en: The country adopted a {six-three-three} school system.
e.zh: 这个国家采用了六三三学制。

e.en: Reformers praised the {six-three-three} model for secondary education.
e.zh: 改革者称赞六三三模式有利于中等教育。

e.en: The quarry used a heavy {six-wheeler} for hauling stone.
e.zh: 采石场用一辆重型六轮车运石料。

e.en: A {six-wheeler} blocked the narrow country road.
e.zh: 一辆六轮车堵住了狭窄的乡间道路。

e.en: The poem ends with a graceful {sixain}.
e.zh: 这首诗以一个优美的六行诗节收尾。

e.en: She revised the {sixain} to improve its rhyme.
e.zh: 她修改了那个六行诗节，使押韵更好。

e.en: The batter hit a {sixer} over the boundary.
e.zh: 击球手把球打过边界，得了六分球。

e.en: The shop sells eggs in a {sixer}.
e.zh: 这家店按六个一组出售鸡蛋。

e.en: The engineer tested the powder's {sinterability} before production.
e.zh: 工程师在投产前测试了这种粉末的可烧结性。

e.en: High {sinterability} helps ceramics become dense at lower temperatures.
e.zh: 较高的烧结能力有助于陶瓷在较低温度下变得致密。

e.en: The {sintered} metal part was strong but slightly porous.
e.zh: 这个烧结金属零件很坚固，但略有孔隙。

e.en: Dentists sometimes use {sintered} ceramic blocks for crowns.
e.zh: 牙医有时会用烧结陶瓷块制作牙冠。

e.en: {Sintering} bonds the powder particles without fully melting them.
e.zh: 烧结会把粉末颗粒结合起来，但不会使其完全熔化。

e.en: The factory adjusted the {sintering} temperature to reduce defects.
e.zh: 工厂调整了烧结温度以减少缺陷。

e.en: The furnace {sinters} the powder into a solid shape.
e.zh: 炉子把粉末烧结成固体形状。

e.en: Porous {sinters} can filter hot gases in industrial systems.
e.zh: 多孔烧结物可以在工业系统中过滤热气体。

e.en: The river followed a {sinuate} path through the valley.
e.zh: 那条河沿着蜿蜒的路线穿过山谷。

e.en: The leaf has a {sinuate} margin with shallow curves.
e.zh: 这片叶子的边缘呈浅浅的波状弯曲。

e.en: A {sinuated} coastline made the old map hard to copy.
e.zh: 曲折蜿蜒的海岸线让那张旧地图很难临摹。

e.en: The fossil showed a {sinuated} shell edge.
e.zh: 这块化石显示出波状弯曲的贝壳边缘。

e.en: The path was {sinuating} between the trees.
e.zh: 小路在树林之间蜿蜒延伸。

e.en: A {sinuating} line decorated the rim of the vase.
e.zh: 一条波状曲线装饰着花瓶的边缘。

e.en: The artist drew each {sinuation} of the coastline carefully.
e.zh: 画家仔细描绘了海岸线的每一处蜿蜒。

e.en: The leaf's {sinuation} helps botanists describe its shape.
e.zh: 叶片的波状弯曲有助于植物学家描述它的形状。

e.en: The {sinuatrial} node helps set the heart's rhythm.
e.zh: 窦房结有助于决定心脏的节律。

e.en: Doctors monitored his {sinuatrial} function after surgery.
e.zh: 医生在手术后监测他的窦房功能。

e.en: The graph showed a {sinuidal} curve across the screen.
e.zh: 屏幕上的图表显示出一条正弦样曲线。

e.en: A {sinuidal} channel carried fluid through the tissue.
e.zh: 一条窦状通道让液体穿过组织。

e.en: A {sinuose} road climbed slowly up the hill.
e.zh: 一条弯弯曲曲的道路缓慢爬上山坡。

e.en: The dancer moved with {sinuose} grace across the stage.
e.zh: 舞者以柔美蜿蜒的姿态穿过舞台。

e.en: The map records the river's many {sinuosities}.
e.zh: 地图记录了这条河许多蜿蜒曲折之处。

e.en: Her prose follows the {sinuosities} of memory and regret.
e.zh: 她的散文顺着记忆与悔意的曲折变化展开。

e.en: Engineers measured the {sinuosity} of the river channel.
e.zh: 工程师测量了河道的蜿蜒度。

e.en: The novel's {sinuosity} makes its plot hard to summarize.
e.zh: 这部小说情节曲折，很难概括。

e.en: The old report spelled syphilis as {siphilis}.
e.zh: 那份旧报告把 syphilis 拼成了 siphilis。

e.en: A search for {siphilis} may still find pages about syphilis.
e.zh: 搜索 siphilis 仍可能找到关于梅毒的网页。

siphonaceous.t: 管状的；具虹吸管状结构的

e.en: Some algae have a {siphonaceous} body with few internal walls.
e.zh: 有些藻类具有管状体，内部隔壁很少。

e.en: The biologist described the organism as {siphonaceous}.
e.zh: 生物学家把这种生物描述为具管状结构。

e.en: Poor venting can cause {siphonage} in a drain trap.
e.zh: 通气不良可能导致排水存水弯发生虹吸作用。

e.en: The plumber checked for {siphonage} after installing the sink.
e.zh: 水管工装好水槽后检查是否有虹吸排水现象。

e.en: The mollusk extended its {siphonal} tube into the water.
e.zh: 软体动物把它的虹吸管伸进水中。

e.en: A {siphonal} current carries food particles toward the animal.
e.zh: 虹吸管水流把食物颗粒带向这种动物。

siphonate.t: 用虹吸管吸出；具虹吸管的

e.en: They used a hose to {siphonate} water from the tank.
e.zh: 他们用软管把水从水箱里虹吸出来。

e.en: A {siphonate} shell has a channel for the animal's siphon.
e.zh: 具虹吸管的贝壳有一条供动物虹吸管通过的沟槽。

siphonaxanthin.t: 管藻黄素；一种类胡萝卜素

e.en: Green algae can contain {siphonaxanthin} as an accessory pigment.
e.zh: 绿藻可能含有管藻黄素作为辅助色素。

e.en: Researchers measured {siphonaxanthin} in several marine samples.
e.zh: 研究人员测量了几份海洋样本中的管藻黄素。

e.en: The sample contained {siphonein} along with other pigments.
e.zh: 样本中含有管藻素以及其他色素。

e.en: Few general dictionaries list {siphonein} as a common word.
e.zh: 很少有普通词典把管藻素列为常用词。

e.en: The insect larva breathes through a tiny {siphonet}.
e.zh: 这种昆虫幼虫通过一个很小的管状器官呼吸。

e.en: A glass {siphonet} moved liquid between the two vessels.
e.zh: 一根小玻璃虹吸管在两个容器之间转移液体。

e.en: The toilet uses a {siphonic} action to clear the bowl.
e.zh: 这种马桶利用虹吸作用清空便池。

e.en: A {siphonic} drainage system can move rainwater quickly.
e.zh: 虹吸式排水系统可以快速排走雨水。

sixern.t: 六人一组的；六个一套的

e.en: The old game used a {sixern} arrangement of counters.
e.zh: 这个老游戏采用六枚棋子一组的摆法。

e.en: Collectors call this rare {sixern} set complete.
e.zh: 收藏者称这套罕见的六件套是完整的。

e.en: She rolled two {sixes} in a row.
e.zh: 她连续掷出了两个六点。

e.en: The shirts marked {sixes} are on the lower shelf.
e.zh: 标着六号的衬衫在下面的架子上。

e.en: The library kept the {sixmo} volume in a glass case.
e.zh: 图书馆把那本六开本书放在玻璃柜里。

e.en: Printers described the booklet as {sixmo} in the catalogue.
e.zh: 印刷商在目录中把这本小册子标为六开本。

e.en: He bought a {sixpennyworth} of sweets from the stall.
e.zh: 他从摊位上买了价值六便士的糖果。

e.en: The phrase once meant only a {sixpennyworth} of goods.
e.zh: 这个说法从前只指价值六便士的货物。

e.en: The chronicle counted {sixscore} riders at the gate.
e.zh: 编年史记载城门前有一百二十名骑手。

e.en: He lived to nearly {sixscore} years, according to legend.
e.zh: 据传说，他几乎活到了一百二十岁。

e.en: A {sixsome} of players met every Friday night.
e.zh: 一组六名玩家每周五晚上碰面。

e.en: The dance began with a lively {sixsome}.
e.zh: 舞会以一场热闹的六人舞开场。

e.en: The manuscript uses {sixte} where modern English says sixth.
e.zh: 这份手稿用古词sixte表示现代英语的第六。

e.en: The singer practiced the {sixte} between the two notes.
e.zh: 歌手练习了这两个音之间的六度音程。

e.en: The pocket prayer book was printed as a {sixteenmo}.
e.zh: 这本袖珍祈祷书印成了十六开本。

e.en: A {sixteenmo} fits more easily into a coat pocket.
e.zh: 十六开本更容易放进外套口袋。

e.en: The sale included several Victorian {sixteenmos}.
e.zh: 这场拍卖包括几本维多利亚时期的十六开本。

e.en: Small {sixteenmos} were popular with travelers.
e.zh: 小型十六开本曾很受旅行者欢迎。

e.en: The tiny almanac was issued in {sixty-fourmo}.
e.zh: 这本小年历以六十四开本发行。

e.en: A {sixty-fourmo} edition can be difficult to read.
e.zh: 六十四开本的版本可能很难阅读。

sixty-nine.t: 六十九；一种互相口交姿势

e.en: The bus route number is {sixty-nine}.
e.zh: 这条公交线路的号码是六十九。

e.en: They joked awkwardly about {sixty-nine} at dinner.
e.zh: 他们吃饭时尴尬地拿六九式开玩笑。

e.en: My grandfather turned {sixty-six} last month.
e.zh: 我祖父上个月满六十六岁。

e.en: The recipe makes {sixty-six} small cookies.
e.zh: 这个配方能做六十六块小饼干。

e.en: The village saw a {sixtyfold} increase in visitors.
e.zh: 这个村子的游客数量增加了六十倍。

e.en: The crop yielded {sixtyfold} in the old parable.
e.zh: 在那个古老寓言中，庄稼结出了六十倍的收成。

e.en: The budget grew {sizably} after the merger.
e.zh: 合并后预算显著增加。

e.en: Her confidence improved {sizably} over the summer.
e.zh: 整个夏天她的信心有了相当大的提升。

e.en: He entered Cambridge as a poor {sizar}.
e.zh: 他以贫困资助生的身份进入剑桥。

e.en: The novel follows a {sizar} struggling for respect.
e.zh: 这部小说讲述一名受资助学生努力争取尊重的故事。

e.en: The college awarded him a {sizarship} for his studies.
e.zh: 学院授予他资助生资格来支持学业。

e.en: Her {sizarship} covered meals but not books.
e.zh: 她的助学金包括餐费，但不包括书费。

e.en: The factory uses {size-grading} for every batch of fruit.
e.zh: 工厂会对每批水果按尺寸分级。

e.en: Good {size-grading} keeps clothing patterns consistent.
e.zh: 良好的尺码分档能保持服装纸样一致。

e.en: She paused to {size-up} the competition.
e.zh: 她停下来评估竞争对手。

e.en: His quick {size-up} of the room proved accurate.
e.zh: 他对房间的快速判断后来证明很准确。

e.en: The programmer used {sizeof} to check the structure's memory use.
e.zh: 程序员用sizeof检查这个结构体占用的内存。

e.en: In C, {sizeof} returns a value measured in bytes.
e.zh: 在C语言中，sizeof返回以字节计量的值。

e.en: The painter disliked the {siziness} of the old glue.
e.zh: 画家不喜欢旧胶水的黏稠感。

e.en: Too much starch gave the cloth an unpleasant {siziness}.
e.zh: 淀粉太多让布料有一种令人不快的胶黏感。

e.en: The paper felt {sizy} after the coating dried.
e.zh: 涂层干后，纸摸起来有胶料感。

e.en: A {sizy} liquid clung to the brush.
e.zh: 一种黏稠的液体粘在刷子上。

e.en: The bacon began to {sizz} in the hot pan.
e.zh: 培根开始在热锅里嘶嘶作响。

e.en: We heard a sharp {sizz} from the loose wire.
e.zh: 我们听到松动电线发出刺耳的嘶嘶声。

e.en: Yesterday was a real {sizzard} in the city.
e.zh: 昨天城里真是酷热难当。

e.en: On a {sizzard} like this, the fields shimmer.
e.zh: 在这样的酷热天里，田野都热得发亮。

e.en: The guard carried a heavy {sjambok} at his side.
e.zh: 守卫腰间带着一根沉重的南非皮鞭。

e.en: Police were accused of using a {sjambok} on protesters.
e.zh: 警方被指控用皮鞭抽打抗议者。

e.en: The police found {skag} hidden in the car.
e.zh: 警方在车里发现了藏着的海洛因。

e.en: Calling someone {skag} is crude and offensive.
e.zh: 把别人叫作丑女人既粗俗又冒犯。

e.en: The scholar studied {skaldic} poems from medieval Iceland.
e.zh: 那位学者研究中世纪冰岛的古北欧吟唱诗。

e.en: His lecture explained the dense style of {skaldic} verse.
e.zh: 他的讲座解释了古北欧吟唱诗歌的繁复风格。

e.en: They played {skat} after dinner.
e.zh: 他们晚饭后玩了斯卡特牌戏。

e.en: A good {skat} player must count cards carefully.
e.zh: 优秀的斯卡特牌手必须仔细记牌。

e.en: The gardener pushed a {skatebarrow} across the yard.
e.zh: 园丁推着一辆带轮搬运车穿过院子。

e.en: A {skatebarrow} can move heavy loads on smooth floors.
e.zh: 带轮搬运车能在平整地面上搬运重物。

e.en: The child rode a homemade {skatemobile} down the path.
e.zh: 孩子骑着自制的滑轮小车沿小路滑下去。

e.en: Early inventors built a {skatemobile} from boards and skate wheels.
e.zh: 早期发明者用木板和滑轮做成滑板车。

e.en: The new {skatepark} opened near the river.
e.zh: 新的滑板公园在河边开放了。

e.en: Teenagers practice tricks at the {skatepark} after school.
e.zh: 青少年放学后在滑板公园练习动作。

e.en: Chemists detected {skatol} in the sample.
e.zh: 化学家在样品中检测到了粪臭素。

e.en: A tiny amount of {skatol} can affect a perfume's smell.
e.zh: 极少量粪臭素也会影响香水的气味。

e.en: The odor came partly from {skatole}.
e.zh: 这种气味部分来自粪臭素。

e.en: Researchers measured {skatole} levels in the laboratory.
e.zh: 研究人员在实验室测量了粪臭素含量。

e.en: The paper mentioned {skatoxyl} during the chemical analysis.
e.zh: 论文在化学分析中提到了粪臭素衍生物。

e.en: Few students had heard of {skatoxyl} before the lecture.
e.zh: 讲座前很少有学生听说过粪臭素衍生物。

e.en: The warrior carried a {skean} at his belt.
e.zh: 那名武士腰间佩着一把短刀。

e.en: A Scottish {skean} was displayed in the museum case.
e.zh: 一把苏格兰短刀陈列在博物馆展柜里。

e.en: They went to {skee} on the frozen hill.
e.zh: 他们去结冰的山坡上滑雪。

e.en: Old guidebooks sometimes spell ski as {skee}.
e.zh: 旧指南书有时把ski拼作skee。

e.en: He {skeed} down the slope before sunset.
e.zh: 日落前他滑下了山坡。

e.en: The sled {skeed} over the hard snow.
e.zh: 雪橇在坚硬的雪面上滑行过去。

e.en: The young {skeeler} moved gracefully across the ice.
e.zh: 那位年轻滑冰者优雅地滑过冰面。

e.en: Every {skeeler} wore thick gloves in the cold rink.
e.zh: 寒冷的冰场里每个滑冰者都戴着厚手套。

e.en: The old man called the thief a {skeesicks}.
e.zh: 老人把那个小偷骂作无赖。

e.en: In that dialect, {skeesicks} means a worthless fellow.
e.zh: 在那种方言里，skeesicks指没用的家伙。

e.en: They joined a {skeetshoot} at the country club.
e.zh: 他们参加了乡村俱乐部的飞碟射击活动。

e.en: The annual {skeetshoot} attracted many experienced marksmen.
e.zh: 年度飞碟射击赛吸引了许多经验丰富的射手。

e.en: He wore a stiff {skeffington} to the costume party.
e.zh: 他穿着一件高领硬领服装去参加化装舞会。

e.en: The tailor described the antique {skeffington} in detail.
e.zh: 裁缝详细描述了那件古式高领硬领服装。

e.en: The fisherman found a {skegger} under the stone.
e.zh: 渔夫在石头下面发现了一只小龙虾。

e.en: Local children used {skegger} as bait for larger fish.
e.zh: 当地孩子用小虾当作钓大鱼的饵。

e.en: The {skeigh} nobleman ignored the villagers.
e.zh: 那个傲慢的贵族不理会村民。

e.en: Her tone sounded {skeigh}, though she meant no insult.
e.zh: 她的语气听起来很高傲，虽然她并无冒犯之意。

e.en: The old text spelled skeleton as {skelecton}.
e.zh: 那本旧书把skeleton拼作skelecton。

e.en: A complete {skelecton} stood in the anatomy room.
e.zh: 解剖室里立着一具完整的骨架。

e.en: The study examined {skeletogenous} tissue in young fish.
e.zh: 这项研究检查了幼鱼体内生成骨骼的组织。

e.en: Doctors discussed the {skeletogenous} cells involved in repair.
e.zh: 医生讨论了参与修复的成骨细胞。

e.en: The lecture covered {skeletogeny} in vertebrate embryos.
e.zh: 讲座讲解了脊椎动物胚胎中的骨骼发生。

e.en: Abnormal {skeletogeny} can affect the shape of limbs.
e.zh: 异常的成骨过程会影响四肢形态。

e.en: We tried {skibobbing} on the lower slope.
e.zh: 我们在较低的雪坡上试了滑雪自行车运动。

e.en: {Skibobbing} combines skiing with cycling balance.
e.zh: 滑雪自行车运动结合了滑雪和骑车的平衡感。

e.en: The old table had a tiny {skice}.
e.zh: 那张旧桌子上有一道很细的划痕。

e.en: He gave the wall a quick {skice} with sandpaper.
e.zh: 他用砂纸很快地轻擦了一下墙面。

e.en: He clipped on his {skid-lid} before starting the bike.
e.zh: 发动摩托车前，他扣好了头盔。

e.en: That cracked {skid-lid} should be replaced immediately.
e.zh: 那个裂开的摩托车头盔应该马上换掉。

e.en: The bathroom floor has a {skid-proof} surface.
e.zh: 浴室地面有防滑表面。

e.en: They fitted {skid-proof} tires for winter driving.
e.zh: 他们装上了适合冬季驾驶的防打滑轮胎。

e.en: When the police arrived, the boys {skiddooed}.
e.zh: 警察一到，那些男孩就赶紧溜走了。

e.en: You had better {skiddoo} before the boss sees you.
e.zh: 你最好在老板看见你之前赶快离开。

e.en: The crowd {skiddooed} when the rain began.
e.zh: 雨一下起来，人群就迅速散开了。

e.en: He {skiddooed} from town after the scandal.
e.zh: 丑闻之后，他从镇上溜走了。

e.en: They were {skiddooing} before anyone could question them.
e.zh: 还没人来得及盘问，他们就正在溜走。

e.en: Stop {skiddooing} every time work gets difficult.
e.zh: 别每次工作一难就赶紧开溜。

e.en: The road felt {skiddy} after the first frost.
e.zh: 第一场霜后，道路感觉很容易打滑。

e.en: Her bike became {skiddy} on the wet leaves.
e.zh: 她的自行车在湿树叶上变得不太稳。

e.en: A long {skidmark} crossed the road.
e.zh: 一条长长的刹车痕横过路面。

e.en: The joke about a {skidmark} embarrassed him.
e.zh: 那个关于内裤污痕的笑话让他很尴尬。

e.en: When trouble started, he decided to {skidoo}.
e.zh: 麻烦一出现，他就决定赶快离开。

e.en: They crossed the frozen lake on a {skidoo}.
e.zh: 他们骑着雪地摩托穿过结冰的湖面。

e.en: Several {skidoos} waited outside the lodge.
e.zh: 几辆雪地摩托停在小屋外面。

e.en: She always {skidoos} when chores begin.
e.zh: 一开始干杂活，她总是赶紧溜走。

e.en: New drivers practised braking on the {skidpan}.
e.zh: 新司机在防滑训练场上练习刹车。

e.en: The {skidpan} teaches control on slippery roads.
e.zh: 防滑驾驶训练场教人如何在湿滑路面上控制车辆。

e.en: These boots have {skidproof} soles.
e.zh: 这双靴子的鞋底是防滑的。

e.en: The ramp needs a {skidproof} coating.
e.zh: 这段坡道需要一层防滑涂层。

e.en: Logs slid down the muddy {skidway}.
e.zh: 原木顺着泥泞的运木滑道滑下去。

e.en: Workers repaired the {skidway} before hauling timber.
e.zh: 工人们在运木材前修好了滑道。

e.en: A pale, {skiey} light filled the room.
e.zh: 一种淡淡的天蓝色光线充满了房间。

e.en: Her scarf was a soft {skiey} blue.
e.zh: 她的围巾是柔和的天空蓝。

e.en: They learned {skijoring} with a trained dog.
e.zh: 他们跟着一只训练有素的狗学习牵引滑雪。

e.en: {Skijoring} is popular in some snowy regions.
e.zh: 牵引滑雪运动在一些多雪地区很受欢迎。

e.en: His {skill-lessness} showed in every repair attempt.
e.zh: 他每次尝试修理时都显出缺乏技能。

e.en: The review mocked the actor's apparent {skill-lessness}.
e.zh: 那篇评论嘲笑了演员明显的笨拙。

e.en: The team's {skillessness} cost them the match.
e.zh: 队伍缺乏技术，结果输掉了比赛。

e.en: She hid her {skillessness} behind confident talk.
e.zh: 她用自信的言辞掩饰自己的无能。

e.en: The prisoners were given bowls of {skilley}.
e.zh: 囚犯们领到一碗碗稀粥。

e.en: For supper, the poor family shared thin {skilley}.
e.zh: 晚饭时，贫穷的一家人分着喝稀薄的汤粥。

e.en: The sailors complained about the watery {skilligalee}.
e.zh: 水手们抱怨那种稀得像水的粥。

e.en: No one wanted another plate of {skilligalee}.
e.zh: 没人想再吃一盘那种劣质食物。

e.en: The shed had a simple {skillion} roof.
e.zh: 那间棚屋有一个简单的单坡屋顶。

e.en: They added a {skillion} to the back of the house.
e.zh: 他们在房子后面加建了一间偏厦。

e.en: The workhouse served {skilly} every morning.
e.zh: 济贫院每天早上供应稀粥。

e.en: He remembered the tasteless {skilly} of his childhood.
e.zh: 他还记得童年时那种没味道的稀粥。

e.en: I {skim-read} the report before the meeting.
e.zh: 开会前我快速浏览了那份报告。

e.en: Students often {skim-read} articles for key points.
e.zh: 学生常常略读文章来抓住要点。

e.en: His {skimble-scamble} speech confused the audience.
e.zh: 他那番杂乱无章的讲话让听众很困惑。

e.en: The letter was full of {skimble-scamble} excuses.
e.zh: 那封信里全是乱七八糟的借口。

e.en: The {sketchiness} of his story made everyone suspicious.
e.zh: 他那番话的可疑之处让大家都起了疑心。

e.en: The map's {sketchiness} forced us to ask locals for directions.
e.zh: 地图画得太粗略，我们只好向当地人问路。

e.en: The monks lived quietly in a remote {skete}.
e.zh: 那些僧侣住在一座偏远的小修道院里，生活清静。

e.en: Pilgrims climbed the hill to visit the ancient {skete}.
e.zh: 朝圣者爬上山去参观那座古老的隐修院。

e.en: The old portrait showed a {skew-eyed} sailor.
e.zh: 那幅旧画像里画着一个斜视的水手。

e.en: He gave me a {skew-eyed} look across the table.
e.zh: 他隔着桌子斜着眼看了我一眼。

e.en: The picture was hanging {skew-whiff} above the fireplace.
e.zh: 那幅画歪歪地挂在壁炉上方。

e.en: Something felt {skew-whiff} about the whole arrangement.
e.zh: 整个安排总让人觉得有点不对劲。

e.en: The mason replaced the cracked {skewback} under the arch.
e.zh: 石匠更换了拱门下开裂的拱脚斜石。

e.en: A worn {skewback} can weaken the whole bridge arch.
e.zh: 磨损的拱座可能削弱整座桥拱。

e.en: A {skewbald} pony waited by the gate.
e.zh: 一匹黑白以外花斑的小马在门边等着。

e.en: She preferred the {skewbald} horse with brown and white patches.
e.zh: 她更喜欢那匹棕白相间的花斑马。

e.en: His tie was {skewwhiff} after the windy walk.
e.zh: 一路迎风走来后，他的领带歪了。

e.en: The deal sounded slightly {skewwhiff} from the beginning.
e.zh: 这笔交易从一开始听起来就有点不对劲。

e.en: The {ski-lift} carried us to the top of the slope.
e.zh: 滑雪缆车把我们送到了雪坡顶端。

e.en: They closed the {ski-lift} because of strong winds.
e.zh: 因为风太大，他们关闭了滑雪缆车。

e.en: She wore a {ski-mask} to keep her face warm.
e.zh: 她戴着滑雪面罩给脸保暖。

e.en: The robber was identified despite his {ski-mask}.
e.zh: 尽管劫匪戴着头套，还是被认了出来。

e.en: A {ski-plane} landed safely on the frozen lake.
e.zh: 一架雪橇式飞机安全降落在结冰的湖面上。

e.en: The research team used a {ski-plane} to reach the glacier.
e.zh: 研究队乘雪橇式飞机抵达冰川。

e.en: Only the upper slopes are {skiable} this week.
e.zh: 这周只有上部雪坡适合滑雪。

e.en: Fresh snow made the narrow trail {skiable} again.
e.zh: 新雪让那条狭窄的小道又能滑雪了。

e.en: The doctor examined the {skiagram} for signs of a fracture.
e.zh: 医生查看那张X光照片，寻找骨折迹象。

e.en: An old {skiagram} was filed with her hospital records.
e.zh: 一张旧X光片被归入她的医院病历中。

e.en: The surgeon requested a new {skiagraph} before operating.
e.zh: 外科医生要求术前再拍一张X光片。

e.en: The museum displayed an early medical {skiagraph}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一张早期医学射线照片。

e.en: Early {skiagraphy} transformed the diagnosis of broken bones.
e.zh: 早期X光摄影术改变了骨折诊断方式。

e.en: The lecture traced the history of medical {skiagraphy}.
e.zh: 讲座回顾了医学X光摄影术的发展史。

e.en: Their argument became a {skiamachy} over imagined insults.
e.zh: 他们的争吵变成了围绕臆想冒犯的无谓争斗。

e.en: The essay mocked politics as endless {skiamachy}.
e.zh: 那篇文章嘲讽政治不过是没完没了的捕风捉影之争。

e.en: The optometrist adjusted the {skiameter} before the eye test.
e.zh: 验光师在视力检查前调好了检影镜。

e.en: An antique {skiameter} stood in the medical display case.
e.zh: 一个古董影度计摆在医学展柜里。

e.en: The clinic still teaches {skiametry} to trainee optometrists.
e.zh: 这家诊所仍向见习验光师教授检影验光法。

e.en: Accurate {skiametry} requires careful control of light.
e.zh: 准确的检影验光需要仔细控制光线。

e.en: She held the {skiascope} close to the patient's eye.
e.zh: 她把视网膜检影镜靠近病人的眼睛。

e.en: The old {skiascope} was replaced by modern equipment.
e.zh: 旧的视网膜检影镜被现代设备取代了。

e.en: The optician used {skiascopy} to estimate the prescription.
e.zh: 配镜师用视网膜检影法估算度数。

e.en: Students practiced {skiascopy} under dim clinic lights.
e.zh: 学生们在诊室昏暗的灯光下练习视网膜检影法。

e.en: The engineer described how a {skiatron} stored an image.
e.zh: 工程师讲解了早期显像管如何存储图像。

e.en: A rare {skiatron} appeared in the electronics collection.
e.zh: 电子藏品中出现了一只罕见的早期显像管。

e.en: He arrived in a {skibby} coat with torn cuffs.
e.zh: 他穿着一件袖口破了的邋遢外套来了。

e.en: The room looked {skibby} after weeks of neglect.
e.zh: 几周没人打理后，房间显得破旧邋遢。

e.en: He rode a {skibob} down the beginner slope.
e.zh: 他骑着滑雪自行车从初级雪坡滑下。

e.en: The resort rents a {skibob} to visitors who dislike skis.
e.zh: 度假村向不喜欢滑雪板的游客出租滑雪自行车。

e.en: The {skibobber} leaned hard into the icy turn.
e.zh: 那名滑雪自行车手用力倾身转过结冰的弯道。

e.en: A skilled {skibobber} can control speed with subtle movements.
e.zh: 熟练的滑雪自行车手能用细微动作控制速度。

e.en: The drawing showed a {skeletonic} frame beneath the skin.
e.zh: 这幅图显示皮肤下面有一个像骨架的结构。

e.en: The old tower had a {skeletonic} outline against the sky.
e.zh: 那座旧塔在天空下呈现出骨架般的轮廓。

e.en: The insects can {skeletonise} a leaf in hours.
e.zh: 这些昆虫能在几小时内把叶子啃得只剩叶脉。

e.en: The artist chose to {skeletonise} the figure with thin black lines.
e.zh: 艺术家用细黑线把人物处理成骨架状。

e.en: The larvae can {skeletonize} the leaves very quickly.
e.zh: 幼虫能很快把叶子啃得只剩叶脉。

e.en: The software will {skeletonize} the shape into simple lines.
e.zh: 这个软件会把形状简化成简单的线条骨架。

skeletonized.t: 骨架化的；被剔成骨架状的

e.en: We found {skeletonized} leaves under the damaged tree.
e.zh: 我们在受损的树下发现了只剩叶脉的叶子。

e.en: The diagram used a {skeletonized} model of the hand.
e.zh: 这张图使用了手部的骨架化模型。

skeletonizer.t: 骨架化工具；剔成骨架者

e.en: The image {skeletonizer} reduced each letter to a thin line.
e.zh: 这个图像骨架化工具把每个字母都简化成细线。

e.en: A leaf {skeletonizer} insect had eaten most of the soft tissue.
e.zh: 一种啃叶成骨架的昆虫吃掉了大部分柔软组织。

e.en: The team is {skeletonizing} the scanned shapes for analysis.
e.zh: 团队正在把扫描形状骨架化以便分析。

e.en: Several caterpillars were {skeletonizing} the rose leaves.
e.zh: 几条毛虫正在把玫瑰叶啃得只剩叶脉。

e.en: The costume looked oddly {skeletonless} without its wire frame.
e.zh: 没有金属框架后，这套服装看起来怪怪的，像没有骨架。

e.en: Jellyfish are {skeletonless} animals with soft bodies.
e.zh: 水母是没有骨骼、身体柔软的动物。

e.en: The stray dog looked thin and {skeletony}.
e.zh: 那只流浪狗看起来很瘦，瘦得像只剩骨头。

e.en: Bare branches made a {skeletony} pattern on the wall.
e.zh: 光秃的树枝在墙上投下骨架般的图案。

e.en: The villagers called him a cheating {skellum}.
e.zh: 村民们说他是个骗人耍滑的无赖。

e.en: In the old tale, the {skellum} finally gets caught.
e.zh: 在那个古老故事里，那个恶棍最后被抓住了。

e.en: No one trusted the {skelm} at the market.
e.zh: 市场上没人信任那个无赖。

e.en: The play turns the charming {skelm} into a comic villain.
e.zh: 这出戏把那个迷人的流氓写成了滑稽反派。

e.en: She gave the table a sharp {skelp} with her hand.
e.zh: 她用手猛地拍了一下桌子。

e.en: He threatened to {skelp} the boy for lying.
e.zh: 他威胁说要因那男孩撒谎而揍他一顿。

e.en: The boxer was known as a powerful {skelper}.
e.zh: 那名拳击手以出拳有力、打击凶狠出名。

e.en: That last wave was a real {skelper}.
e.zh: 最后那道浪真是狠狠的一下。

e.en: Children began to {skelter} across the yard.
e.zh: 孩子们开始匆匆穿过院子乱跑。

e.en: The papers flew in a {skelter} of wind and noise.
e.zh: 文件在风声和喧闹中乱纷纷地飞了起来。

e.en: The old warrior carried a small {sken} at his belt.
e.zh: 那位老战士腰间带着一把小短刀。

e.en: A decorated {sken} lay inside the museum case.
e.zh: 一把装饰精美的匕首放在博物馆展柜里。

e.en: Actors entered from the {skene} during the ancient play.
e.zh: 在那出古代戏剧中，演员从舞台建筑处入场。

e.en: The ruins still show where the {skene} once stood.
e.zh: 遗址仍能看出昔日舞台建筑所在的位置。

e.en: The beekeeper kept an old {skep} in the shed.
e.zh: 养蜂人在棚屋里保存着一个旧草编蜂箱。

e.en: She carried apples in a wide {skep}.
e.zh: 她用一个宽大的篮子装着苹果。

e.en: His {skepsis} made the committee examine every claim.
e.zh: 他的怀疑态度促使委员会审查每一项说法。

e.en: Ancient {skepsis} questioned whether certain knowledge was possible.
e.zh: 古代怀疑论质疑确定知识是否可能存在。

skepticize.t: 使怀疑；以怀疑态度看待

e.en: The scandal seemed to {skepticize} even loyal supporters.
e.zh: 这场丑闻似乎连忠实支持者也变得怀疑起来。

e.en: Students learn to {skepticize} claims without rejecting evidence.
e.zh: 学生学会以怀疑态度看待说法，但不拒绝证据。

e.en: There was not a {skerrick} of food left.
e.zh: 一点食物也没剩下。

e.en: I cannot find a {skerrick} of proof for that story.
e.zh: 我找不到一丁点证据来支持那个说法。

e.en: He was criticized for calling her a {sket}.
e.zh: 他因骂她是荡妇而受到批评。

e.en: The word {sket} is offensive street slang in Britain.
e.zh: sket 这个词在英国街头俚语中带有冒犯性。

e.en: She opened her {sketch-block} and drew the bridge.
e.zh: 她打开素描本，画下了那座桥。

e.en: A small {sketch-block} fits easily in his coat pocket.
e.zh: 一本小速写簿很容易放进他的外套口袋。

e.en: He filled his {sketch-book} with faces from the train.
e.zh: 他在速写簿里画满了火车上乘客的脸。

e.en: Her travel {sketch-book} became a record of the trip.
e.zh: 她的旅行素描本成了这趟旅程的记录。

skimble-skamble.t: 胡言乱语的；杂乱无章的；无意义的言辞

e.en: The witness gave a {skimble-skamble} account of the accident.
e.zh: 证人对事故的描述杂乱无章。

e.en: His speech sounded like {skimble-skamble} to the tired audience.
e.zh: 在疲惫的听众听来，他的演讲像一通胡言乱语。

e.en: She carried her {skimboard} down to the wet sand.
e.zh: 她把浅水滑板带到湿沙滩上。

e.en: They learned to {skimboard} along the edge of the waves.
e.zh: 他们学着在浪边玩浅水滑板。

e.en: The old {skimeister} still raced with surprising speed.
e.zh: 那位老滑雪高手比赛时速度仍然惊人。

e.en: Reporters called her a {skimeister} after her third title.
e.zh: 她第三次夺冠后，记者称她为滑雪冠军。

e.en: The ranger used a {skimobile} to reach the cabin.
e.zh: 护林员开雪地摩托赶到小屋。

e.en: Guests can {skimobile} across the frozen lake in winter.
e.zh: 冬天游客可以乘雪地车穿过结冰的湖面。

e.en: The new costume was {skimpier} than the old one.
e.zh: 新服装比旧服装更暴露。

e.en: This year's budget is {skimpier} than we expected.
e.zh: 今年的预算比我们预期的更少。

e.en: The dancers were {skimpily} dressed for the beach show.
e.zh: 舞者们为了海滩表演穿得很暴露。

e.en: The report was {skimpily} documented and hard to trust.
e.zh: 这份报告资料不足，很难让人信服。

e.en: Parents complained about the {skimpiness} of the costumes.
e.zh: 家长们抱怨那些服装太暴露。

e.en: The {skimpiness} of the evidence weakened the case.
e.zh: 证据不足削弱了这个案子的说服力。

e.en: The charity was funded {skimpingly} for many years.
e.zh: 多年来这个慈善机构得到的资金很少。

e.en: He praised the staff only {skimpingly} after their success.
e.zh: 他们成功后，他只是很吝啬地夸了员工几句。

skin-bound.t: 皮面装订的；皮肤紧绷的

e.en: The library kept a {skin-bound} volume behind glass.
e.zh: 图书馆把一本皮面装订的书放在玻璃柜后。

e.en: The burn left his hand stiff and {skin-bound}.
e.zh: 烧伤让他的手僵硬，皮肤紧绷。

e.en: Her confidence was only {skin-deep} at first.
e.zh: 起初她的自信只是表面上的。

e.en: The cut looked serious but was merely {skin-deep}.
e.zh: 伤口看起来严重，但其实只是皮外伤。

skin-dive.t: 徒手潜水；进行轻装潜水

e.en: We planned a {skin-dive} near the coral reef.
e.zh: 我们计划在珊瑚礁附近徒手潜水。

e.en: Tourists can {skin-dive} in the clear bay.
e.zh: 游客可以在清澈的海湾里轻装潜水。

skin-diver.t: 轻装潜水者；徒手潜水员

e.en: A {skin-diver} found the lost camera underwater.
e.zh: 一名轻装潜水者在水下找到了丢失的相机。

e.en: The experienced {skin-diver} avoided the strong current.
e.zh: 那位经验丰富的徒手潜水员避开了急流。

skin-divers.t: 轻装潜水者；徒手潜水员

e.en: Several {skin-divers} explored the shallow wreck.
e.zh: 几名轻装潜水者探索了浅水中的沉船。

e.en: The guide warned the {skin-divers} about sharp rocks.
e.zh: 向导提醒徒手潜水员注意锋利的岩石。

e.en: We tried {skin-diving} during our island holiday.
e.zh: 我们在海岛度假时尝试了轻装潜水。

e.en: Good weather makes {skin-diving} much safer.
e.zh: 天气好会让徒手潜水安全得多。

e.en: The patient needed {skin-grafting} after the burn healed.
e.zh: 烧伤愈合后，病人需要植皮。

e.en: Modern {skin-grafting} can reduce severe scarring.
e.zh: 现代皮肤移植可以减轻严重疤痕。

e.en: The clinic treated a {skin-popper} with an infected arm.
e.zh: 诊所治疗了一名手臂感染的皮下注射毒品者。

e.en: Police reports used {skin-popper} as slang for certain drug users.
e.zh: 警方报告用这个俚语指某些注射毒品者。

e.en: He wore a {skin-tight} cycling jersey.
e.zh: 他穿着一件紧身骑行衫。

e.en: The actor appeared in a {skin-tight} silver suit.
e.zh: 那名演员穿着一套贴身的银色服装亮相。

skinbound.t: 皮面装订的；皮肤紧绷的

e.en: The collector owned a rare {skinbound} manuscript.
e.zh: 收藏家有一本罕见的皮面装订手稿。

e.en: The healed scar felt hard and {skinbound}.
e.zh: 愈合后的疤痕摸起来坚硬且皮肤紧绷。

e.en: Do not {skinch} the children on warm clothes.
e.zh: 别在孩子的保暖衣物上克扣。

e.en: The landlord tried to {skinch} repairs after the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨过后，房东想在维修上省钱克扣。

skinched.t: 少给了；克扣了；吝啬供给了

e.en: They felt the company had {skinched} their holiday pay.
e.zh: 他们觉得公司克扣了他们的假日工资。

e.en: The recipe failed because I {skinched} the butter.
e.zh: 这道菜失败了，因为我黄油放得太少。

e.en: He was accused of {skinching} wages from seasonal workers.
e.zh: 他被指控克扣季节工的工资。

e.en: Stop {skinching} on paint if you want a smooth wall.
e.zh: 如果想让墙面平整，就别在油漆上省得太狠。

e.en: The nurse measured the baby's {skinfold} carefully.
e.zh: 护士仔细测量了婴儿的皮褶厚度。

e.en: A {skinfold} test can estimate body fat.
e.zh: 皮褶测试可以估算体脂。

skyless.t: 没有天空的；不见天日的

e.en: The prisoners lived in a {skyless} room underground.
e.zh: 囚犯们住在地下一个不见天日的房间里。

e.en: A {skyless} gray dawn made the city feel unreal.
e.zh: 没有天空感的灰色黎明让这座城市显得不真实。

e.en: The old {skyman} told stories about early balloon flights.
e.zh: 那位老飞行员讲起早期气球飞行的故事。

e.en: In the poem, a lonely {skyman} watches the earth below.
e.zh: 在诗中，一个孤独的空中人俯望着大地。

e.en: The museum displayed a painted {skyphos} from ancient Greece.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一只古希腊彩绘双耳深酒杯。

e.en: She identified the vessel as a {skyphos}, not a bowl.
e.zh: 她认出这个器皿是双耳深酒杯，而不是碗。

skyport.t: 空中交通港；飞行器港口

e.en: The company plans to build a rooftop {skyport} for air taxis.
e.zh: 公司计划在屋顶建一个供空中出租车使用的飞行器港口。

e.en: Passengers waited at the {skyport} above the railway station.
e.zh: 乘客们在火车站上方的空中交通港等候。

e.en: The cargo ship tested a giant {skysail} to save fuel.
e.zh: 那艘货船测试了一张巨大的风筝式船帆来节省燃料。

e.en: Engineers adjusted the {skysail} as the wind changed.
e.zh: 风向变化时，工程师调整了高空帆。

e.en: New glass towers {skyscrape} above the old market streets.
e.zh: 新的玻璃高塔在老市场街道上方直入云天。

e.en: The cliffs seemed to {skyscrape} in the evening light.
e.zh: 那些悬崖在暮光中仿佛高耸入云。

e.en: They admired the {skyscraping} towers along the harbor.
e.zh: 他们欣赏着港湾边那些高耸入云的塔楼。

e.en: A {skyscraping} ambition drove the young architect forward.
e.zh: 一种冲天般的雄心推动着这位年轻建筑师前进。

skysurfing.t: 空中冲浪；高空滑翔运动

e.en: He learned {skysurfing} after years of ordinary skydiving.
e.zh: 他练了多年普通跳伞后开始学习空中冲浪。

e.en: The video shows {skysurfing} with a board strapped to the feet.
e.zh: 视频展示了脚上绑着板子的空中冲浪。

e.en: The {skytrooper} landed behind enemy lines at dawn.
e.zh: 那名空降兵在黎明时降落到敌后。

e.en: In the game, each {skytrooper} carries a jet pack.
e.zh: 在游戏里，每个空中士兵都背着喷气背包。

e.en: The commander sent {skytroops} to secure the bridge.
e.zh: 指挥官派空降部队去控制那座桥。

e.en: Futuristic {skytroops} patrol the city in the novel.
e.zh: 小说中，未来感十足的空中部队在城市上空巡逻。

e.en: Volunteers joined the night {skywatch} during the meteor shower.
e.zh: 流星雨期间，志愿者参加了夜间观天活动。

e.en: The airport maintains a constant {skywatch} for storm clouds.
e.zh: 机场持续监测天空中的暴风云。

e.en: The pilot will {skywrite} a message above the beach.
e.zh: 飞行员将在海滩上空用飞机写出一条信息。

e.en: Companies used to {skywrite} advertisements over crowded cities.
e.zh: 过去公司常在拥挤城市上空用飞机写广告。

e.en: His sudden {skinniness} worried his parents.
e.zh: 他突然变得瘦削，让父母很担心。

e.en: The designer liked the chair's elegant {skinniness}.
e.zh: 设计师喜欢这把椅子纤细优雅的样子。

e.en: They decided to {skinny-dip} after midnight.
e.zh: 他们决定午夜后去裸泳。

e.en: I would never {skinny-dip} in a public lake.
e.zh: 我绝不会在公共湖里裸泳。

e.en: They {skinny-dipped} in the cold river.
e.zh: 他们在冰冷的河里裸泳过。

e.en: She admitted she had {skinny-dipped} once at camp.
e.zh: 她承认自己在营地时裸泳过一次。

e.en: A {skinny-dipper} ran back to the beach towels.
e.zh: 一个裸泳者跑回了沙滩毛巾旁。

e.en: The sign warned every {skinny-dipper} about cameras nearby.
e.zh: 告示提醒每个裸泳者附近有摄像头。

e.en: {Skinny-dipping} is illegal on that beach.
e.zh: 在那片海滩裸泳是违法的。

e.en: They joked about {skinny-dipping} after the party.
e.zh: 他们开玩笑说派对后去裸泳。

e.en: He sometimes {skinny-dips} in his private pool.
e.zh: 他有时会在自家泳池里裸泳。

e.en: Their secret {skinny-dips} became local gossip.
e.zh: 他们秘密裸泳的事成了当地闲话。

e.en: The clinic treated infections caused by {skinpopping}.
e.zh: 诊所治疗因皮下注射毒品引起的感染。

e.en: The report described {skinpopping} as a risky practice.
e.zh: 报告把皮下注射毒品称为一种危险做法。

e.en: The novel describes {skinwalkers} as terrifying shapeshifters.

e.zh: 她的围巾并不是蓝色，只是有点像天空的颜色。

e.zh: 罪犯计划劫持一架客机。

e.zh: 恐怖分子在飞机起飞后不久劫持了它。

e.zh: 被劫持航班上的乘客保持了冷静。

e.zh: 村庄坐落在一座冒烟的炉渣堆旁。

e.en: Don't {slag-off} your colleagues in public.
e.zh: 不要当众说同事的坏话。

e.en: Fans began to {slag-off} the referee online.
e.zh: 球迷开始在网上贬损那名裁判。

e.en: Workers {slag-out} the furnace after each shift.
e.zh: 工人每班结束后都清理炉内炉渣。

e.en: The plant must {slag-out} impurities during smelting.
e.zh: 工厂在冶炼过程中必须排出杂质炉渣。

e.en: The road was covered with {slaggy} gravel.
e.zh: 路面铺着含有矿渣的碎石。

e.en: A {slaggy} crust formed on the molten metal.
e.zh: 熔融金属表面形成了一层炉渣状硬壳。

e.en: Children played near the black {slagheap}.
e.zh: 孩子们在黑色矿渣堆附近玩耍。

e.en: The abandoned {slagheap} scarred the valley.
e.zh: 废弃的炉渣堆破坏了山谷的景观。

e.en: He raised his glass and said {slainte}.
e.zh: 他举起酒杯说了声祝健康。

e.en: The guests shouted {slainte} at midnight.
e.zh: 客人们在午夜高喊干杯。

e.en: Don't {slaister} paint over the clean wood.
e.zh: 别把油漆胡乱涂到干净的木头上。

e.en: He tends to {slaister} through every small repair.
e.zh: 他做每个小修理都常常邋里邋遢地糊弄过去。

slakeless.t: 无法满足的；不能熄灭的

e.en: She felt a {slakeless} thirst for knowledge.
e.zh: 她有一种无法满足的求知欲。

e.en: The poem speaks of {slakeless} fire.
e.zh: 这首诗写到无法熄灭的火焰。

slaky.t: 像熟石灰的；易碎的石灰质的

e.en: The old mortar felt {slaky} after the rain.
e.zh: 雨后，旧砂浆摸起来像熟石灰一样松散。

e.en: A {slaky} powder coated the broken stones.
e.zh: 破碎的石头上覆盖着一层石灰质粉末。

e.en: The door shut {slam-bang} behind us.
e.zh: 门在我们身后砰的一声关上了。

e.en: They opened with a {slam-bang} action scene.
e.zh: 他们用一场热闹猛烈的动作戏开场。

e.en: She finished the fast break with a {slam-dunk}.
e.zh: 她在快攻最后完成了一记扣篮。

e.en: With that evidence, the case is a {slam-dunk}.
e.zh: 有了那项证据，这个案子几乎十拿九稳。

e.en: He laid the boards {slanchwise} across the ditch.
e.zh: 他把木板斜着架在沟上。

e.en: The rain drove {slanchwise} against the window.
e.zh: 雨斜斜地打在窗户上。

slanderella.t: 爱诽谤的女人；恶毒造谣者

e.en: The columnist was dismissed as a {slanderella} by her rivals.
e.zh: 那位专栏作家被对手讥为恶毒造谣的女人。

e.en: Nobody trusted the office {slanderella} for long.
e.zh: 办公室里那个爱诽谤的人很快就没人信了。

e.en: This translation sounds {slangier} than the original.
e.zh: 这个译本听起来比原文更俚俗。

e.en: His later songs became {slangier} and sharper.
e.zh: 他后来的歌俚语更多，也更尖锐。

e.en: That was the {slangiest} speech in the whole film.
e.zh: 那是整部电影里俚语最多的一段台词。

e.en: She chose the {slangiest} phrase to sound local.
e.zh: 她选了最俚俗的说法，好显得像本地人。

e.en: He spoke {slangily} to impress the younger crowd.
e.zh: 他故意用俚语说话，想给年轻人留下印象。

e.en: The review describes the hero {slangily} as a hustler.
e.zh: 那篇评论用俚俗的说法把男主角称作混混。

e.en: The editor reduced the {slanginess} of the dialogue.
e.zh: 编辑降低了对白中的俚语味。

e.en: Its {slanginess} made the novel feel immediate.
e.zh: 它的俚俗感让这部小说显得很有现场感。

slangster.t: 常用俚语的人；俚语作家

e.en: A young {slangster} explained the phrase to the tourists.
e.zh: 一个爱用俚语的年轻人向游客解释了这个短语。

e.en: The old magazine hired a {slangster} for punchier captions.
e.zh: 那本老杂志请了一位俚语写手来写更有劲的图片说明。

e.en: Teen {slanguage} changes faster than dictionaries can follow.
e.zh: 青少年的俚语化语言变化得比词典更新还快。

e.en: The manual was full of programmer {slanguage}.
e.zh: 那本手册里满是程序员行话。

e.en: The cat {slank} under the porch at dusk.
e.zh: 黄昏时，那只猫偷偷钻到门廊下面。

e.en: He {slank} away before anyone could question him.
e.zh: 还没等别人盘问，他就偷偷溜走了。

e.en: The novel describes one sailor with a {slant-eye}.
e.zh: 小说描写了一名水手长着一只斜眼。

e.en: He was suspended for using {slant-eye} as an insult.
e.zh: 他因使用辱称亚洲人的词而被停职。

e.en: A {slant-eyed} cat watched from the wall.
e.zh: 一只斜眼的猫从墙头看着。

e.en: The film removed a {slant-eyed} caricature from the scene.
e.zh: 影片删掉了场景中带种族冒犯的斜眼丑化形象。

e.en: The carpenter cut a {slantendicular} notch in the beam.
e.zh: 木匠在梁上切出一个斜向的凹口。

e.en: A {slantendicular} path climbed behind the barn.
e.zh: 一条歪斜的小路从谷仓后面往上延伸。

e.en: The fence ran {slantindicular} to the road.
e.zh: 篱笆斜斜地朝着道路延伸。

e.en: He made a {slantindicular} mark across the page.
e.zh: 他在纸页上画了一道斜向的记号。

e.en: A {slantingdicular} shadow crossed the kitchen floor.
e.zh: 一道斜斜的影子横过厨房地板。

e.en: The hikers followed a {slantingdicular} trail uphill.
e.zh: 徒步者沿着一条倾斜的小径上山。

e.en: She placed the ladder {slantingways} against the shed.
e.zh: 她把梯子斜着靠在棚屋上。

e.en: The snow blew {slantingways} across the street.
e.zh: 雪斜斜地吹过街面。

e.en: Turn the couch {slantways} to get it through.
e.zh: 把沙发斜着转一下，才能搬过去。

e.en: The cut runs {slantways} across the fabric.
e.zh: 那道剪口斜着穿过布料。

e.en: The shop sits {slap-bang} in the town center.
e.zh: 那家店正好位于镇中心。

e.en: The ball hit {slap-bang} against the garage door.
e.zh: 球砰的一下撞在车库门上。

slap-happy.t: 糊里糊涂的；轻率快活的

e.en: After two sleepless nights, we were {slap-happy}.
e.zh: 两晚没睡之后，我们都变得糊里糊涂。

e.en: The team made a {slap-happy} decision under pressure.
e.zh: 团队在压力下做了一个轻率的决定。

e.en: They served a {slap-up} dinner after the match.
e.zh: 比赛后他们端上了一顿丰盛的晚餐。

e.en: We found a {slap-up} little hotel near the station.
e.zh: 我们在车站附近找到一家很不错的小旅馆。

e.en: The sign stood {slapdab} in the middle of the path.
e.zh: 那块牌子正好立在小路中央。

e.en: He landed {slapdab} on the wet pavement.
e.zh: 他猛地一下摔在湿漉漉的人行道上。

e.en: The report's {slapdashery} annoyed the whole committee.
e.zh: 这份报告的草率让整个委员会都很恼火。

e.en: Her early paintings show energy, not mere {slapdashery}.
e.zh: 她早期的画显出活力，并不只是马虎涂抹。

slaphappier.t: 更糊涂的；更轻率快活的

e.en: By midnight, the exhausted crew grew {slaphappier}.
e.zh: 到了午夜，疲惫的工作人员变得更糊涂了。

e.en: The sequel feels {slaphappier} than the original comedy.
e.zh: 这部续集感觉比原来的喜剧更轻率快活。

e.en: The old novel calls the kitchen maid a {slavey}.
e.zh: 那本旧小说把厨房女佣称作苦役般的女仆。

e.en: He felt like a {slavey} doing everyone's errands.
e.zh: 他替所有人跑腿，觉得自己像个苦工。

e.en: A powerful {slavocracy} dominated the plantation economy.
e.zh: 强大的奴隶主统治阶层支配着种植园经济。

e.en: The reformers attacked the {slavocracy} in their speeches.
e.zh: 改革者在演讲中抨击奴隶主统治集团。

e.en: The rain seemed to {sleak} the dark stones.
e.zh: 雨水似乎把那些黑石头冲得光滑发亮。

e.en: Her hair began to {sleak} down in the mist.
e.zh: 雾气中，她的头发开始贴顺下来。

e.en: The worker had to {sleave} the silk by hand.
e.zh: 工人得用手把丝线一缕缕分开。

e.en: Old ropes can {sleave} into loose fibers.
e.zh: 旧绳子会散成松松的纤维。

e.en: She examined the {sleaved} silk before spinning it.
e.zh: 她在纺线前检查已经分成丝缕的蚕丝。

e.en: The {sleaved} fibers clung to his gloves.
e.zh: 那些散开的纤维粘在他的手套上。

e.en: The apprentice learned {sleaving} from an old silk worker.
e.zh: 学徒向一位老丝工学习分丝。

e.en: The cable was {sleaving} at the broken end.
e.zh: 那根缆线在断口处正散成纤维。

e.en: Everyone knew he was a {sleazebag} who cheated clients.
e.zh: 大家都知道他是个欺骗客户的卑鄙小人。

e.en: Don't let that {sleazebag} talk you into signing anything.
e.zh: 别让那个下流家伙哄你签任何东西。

e.en: The reporter exposed the {sleazeball} behind the scam.
e.zh: 记者揭露了骗局背后的那个卑鄙家伙。

e.en: She called him a {sleazeball} after his crude joke.
e.zh: 他讲了粗俗笑话后，她骂他是下流胚。

e.en: He {sleazily} hinted that money could change the result.
e.zh: 他下流地暗示钱可以改变结果。

e.en: The motel was {sleazily} lit by a broken neon sign.
e.zh: 那家汽车旅馆被坏掉的霓虹灯照得寒酸肮脏。

e.en: The film captures the {sleaziness} of the old nightclub.
e.zh: 这部电影捕捉到了那家老夜总会的肮脏下流感。

e.en: Voters were tired of the {sleaziness} around the campaign.
e.zh: 选民厌倦了竞选中那种卑劣肮脏的风气。

e.en: That {sleazo} kept bothering people at the party.
e.zh: 那个猥琐家伙在派对上不停骚扰别人。

e.en: The movie villain is a charming but dangerous {sleazo}.
e.zh: 电影里的反派是个有魅力却危险的下流人物。

e.en: They used a {sledge-hammer} to break the concrete.
e.zh: 他们用大锤砸碎混凝土。

e.en: The policy would {sledge-hammer} small firms with new costs.
e.zh: 这项政策会用新增成本重压小企业。

e.en: The engineer tested a {sledgemeter} on the icy track.
e.zh: 工程师在冰道上测试了一台雪橇计量器。

e.en: A broken {sledgemeter} gave the team unreliable readings.
e.zh: 坏掉的雪橇计量器给团队提供了不可靠的读数。

e.en: The stylist used oil to {sleeken} her hair.
e.zh: 发型师用油让她的头发变得光滑亮泽。

e.en: Rain can {sleeken} the surface of old stone.
e.zh: 雨水能让旧石面的表面变得光滑。

e.en: I need a {sleep-in} after working late all week.
e.zh: 我整周加班到很晚，真需要睡个懒觉。

e.en: The nurse accepted a {sleep-in} shift at the care home.
e.zh: 护士接受了养老院的住家夜班。

e.en: The children planned a {sleep-out} in the garden.
e.zh: 孩子们计划在花园里露宿一晚。

e.en: Some staff prefer a {sleep-out} arrangement to living on site.
e.zh: 有些员工更喜欢在外住宿，而不是住在工作地点。

e.en: She wrapped a warm {sleepcoat} around her shoulders.
e.zh: 她把一件暖和的睡袍披在肩上。

e.en: The vintage {sleepcoat} was trimmed with faded lace.
e.zh: 那件复古睡衣外套镶着褪色的蕾丝。

e.en: She booked a {sleeperette} for the overnight train.
e.zh: 她为夜班火车订了一个简易卧铺座。

e.en: The airline advertised a reclining {sleeperette} for long flights.
e.zh: 航空公司宣传长途航班上的可躺式小卧铺座。

e.en: A {sleepful} calm settled over the warm room.
e.zh: 温暖的房间里弥漫着一种令人昏昏欲睡的宁静。

e.en: After the meal, he felt heavy and {sleepful}.
e.zh: 饭后他觉得身体沉沉的，很想睡觉。

slaphappy.t: 被打昏的；糊里糊涂的；鲁莽乐观的

e.en: After the long shift, he looked {slaphappy} and confused.
e.zh: 漫长班次后，他看起来昏昏沉沉、糊里糊涂。

e.en: Their {slaphappy} optimism ignored every warning sign.
e.zh: 他们那种鲁莽乐观无视了所有警告信号。

e.en: The comedian called himself a cheerful {slaphead}.
e.zh: 那位喜剧演员自称是个乐呵呵的秃头。

e.en: Calling someone a {slaphead} can sound rude.
e.zh: 叫别人秃子可能听起来很粗鲁。

e.en: The children played {slapjack} after dinner.
e.zh: 孩子们晚饭后玩拍纸牌游戏。

e.en: He ordered a plate of {slapjacks} with syrup.
e.zh: 他点了一盘浇糖浆的薄煎饼。

e.en: She scored with a powerful {slapshot}.
e.zh: 她用一记有力的大力击球得分。

e.en: The goalie blocked the {slapshot} with his glove.
e.zh: 守门员用手套挡住了那记大力击球。

slash-and-burn.t: 刀耕火种的；激烈削减的

e.en: Some communities still use {slash-and-burn} farming.
e.zh: 一些社区仍然采用刀耕火种的农业方式。

e.en: The company announced a {slash-and-burn} cost plan.
e.zh: 公司宣布了一项大刀阔斧削减成本的计划。

e.en: We worked during every {slatch} of clear weather.
e.zh: 每逢天气短暂放晴，我们就抓紧干活。

e.en: A brief {slatch} in the wind let us launch the boat.
e.zh: 风势片刻平息，让我们得以把船放下水。

e.en: The roof was painted {slate-black}.
e.zh: 屋顶被漆成了石板般的深灰黑色。

e.en: Clouds turned {slate-black} before the storm arrived.
e.zh: 暴风雨来临前，云层变成了深灰黑色。

e.en: She wore a {slate-coloured} wool coat.
e.zh: 她穿着一件石板色的羊毛大衣。

e.en: The sea looked {slate-coloured} under the winter sky.
e.zh: 冬日天空下，大海显得蓝灰沉暗。

e.en: He chose a {slate-grey} suit for the interview.
e.zh: 他为面试选了一套石板灰色西装。

e.en: The lake was {slate-grey} in the morning light.
e.zh: 晨光中，湖面呈现出蓝灰色。

e.en: The mineral breaks into thin {slatelike} sheets.
e.zh: 这种矿物会裂成薄薄的石板状片层。

e.en: Her voice had a flat, {slatelike} coldness.
e.zh: 她的声音带着一种平板而冰冷的感觉。

e.en: The carpenter replaced a broken {slath}.
e.zh: 木匠更换了一根断裂的屋顶板条。

e.en: Rain leaked through the old {slaths} above the shed.
e.zh: 雨水从棚顶老旧的板条间漏了下来。

e.en: The room's {slatternliness} shocked the landlord.
e.zh: 房间的邋遢程度让房东很震惊。

e.en: She mistook poverty for {slatternliness} and judged them harshly.
e.zh: 她把贫穷误当成邋遢，对他们作了苛刻评价。

e.en: The {slaughterman} worked at the town abattoir.
e.zh: 那名屠宰工在镇上的屠宰场工作。

e.en: A skilled {slaughterman} must follow strict hygiene rules.
e.zh: 熟练的屠宰工必须遵守严格的卫生规定。

e.en: The {slaughtermen} started before dawn.
e.zh: 屠宰工们天亮前就开始工作。

e.en: New regulations changed how {slaughtermen} handled livestock.
e.zh: 新规定改变了屠宰工处理牲畜的方式。

e.en: The poem describes a {slaughterous} battle.
e.zh: 这首诗描写了一场血腥凶残的战斗。

e.en: His {slaughterous} rage terrified the villagers.
e.zh: 他那种嗜血般的狂怒吓坏了村民。

slaughterously.t: 血腥凶残地；大肆屠杀地

e.en: The army advanced {slaughterously} through the valley.
e.zh: 军队血腥凶残地穿过山谷推进。

e.en: The villain laughed {slaughterously} in the old melodrama.
e.zh: 那部老情节剧里的反派发出凶残的笑声。

slave-born.t: 生为奴隶的；奴隶出身的

e.en: The novel follows a {slave-born} woman seeking freedom.
e.zh: 这部小说讲述一位生为奴隶的女子追求自由。

e.en: A {slave-born} artisan could still become highly skilled.
e.zh: 奴隶出身的工匠仍可能拥有高超技艺。

slave-drive.t: 严酷驱使；像奴隶般逼迫工作

e.en: The manager tried to {slave-drive} the staff through weekends.
e.zh: 经理试图逼员工周末也像奴隶一样干活。

e.en: You cannot {slave-drive} volunteers and expect loyalty.
e.zh: 你不能严酷驱使志愿者还指望他们忠诚。

e.en: The overseer was feared as a brutal {slave-driver}.
e.zh: 那个监工因残暴而被视为可怕的奴隶监工。

e.en: Her boss is a {slave-driver} during tax season.
e.zh: 报税季时，她的老板是个苛刻的督工。

e.en: The law protected {slaveholding} families in the colony.
e.zh: 这项法律保护殖民地里的蓄奴家庭。

e.en: He inherited a {slaveholding} estate in the south.
e.zh: 他继承了南方一处拥有奴隶的庄园。

e.en: The farm was unusually {slaveless} for that region.
e.zh: 在那个地区，这座农场罕见地没有奴隶。

e.en: They imagined a {slaveless} society after the war.
e.zh: 他们设想战后会出现一个无奴隶的社会。

e.en: The prisoners endured {slavelike} conditions in the camp.
e.zh: 囚犯们在营地里忍受着奴隶般的处境。

e.en: He hated the {slavelike} obedience demanded by the regime.
e.zh: 他痛恨那个政权要求的奴性顺从。

slaveocracy.t: 蓄奴阶层统治；奴隶主集团

e.en: A wealthy {slaveocracy} controlled much of the legislature.
e.zh: 富有的奴隶主集团控制了立法机构的大部分权力。

e.en: Abolitionists denounced the {slaveocracy} in public speeches.
e.zh: 废奴主义者在公开演说中谴责奴隶主统治集团。

e.en: She was the {sleepiest} person in the car.
e.zh: 她是车里最困的人。

e.en: I feel {sleepiest} just before dawn.
e.zh: 我在黎明前最想睡觉。

e.en: He packed a {sleeping-bag} for the camping trip.
e.zh: 他为露营旅行打包了一个睡袋。

e.en: The old {sleeping-bag} was still warm inside.
e.zh: 那个旧睡袋里面仍然很暖和。

e.en: We booked beds in a {sleeping-car}.
e.zh: 我们订了卧铺车厢里的床位。

e.en: The {sleeping-car} was quiet after midnight.
e.zh: 午夜过后，卧铺车厢里很安静。

e.en: A {sleeplike} calm settled over the village.
e.zh: 一种睡眠般的宁静笼罩了村庄。

e.en: He lay in a {sleeplike} trance for hours.

e.en: There was a strange {slinkiness} in his movements.
e.zh: 他的动作里有一种奇怪的鬼祟劲儿。

e.en: He approached {slinkingly} from the side door.
e.zh: 他从侧门偷偷摸摸地靠近。

e.en: The dog crept {slinkingly} back after stealing food.
e.zh: 那条狗偷吃后又鬼祟地溜了回来。

e.en: The gloves were made from rare {slinkskin}.
e.zh: 这副手套是用稀有的早产小牛皮制成的。

e.en: Old dealers valued {slinkskin} for its soft texture.
e.zh: 老皮货商看重这种薄软皮革的柔软质地。

e.en: The engineer checked the estimate with a {slipstick}.
e.zh: 工程师用计算尺核对了估算结果。

e.en: Before calculators, students often carried a {slipstick}.
e.zh: 在计算器普及以前，学生常常随身带着计算尺。

e.en: He sharpened the blade on a small {slipstone}.
e.zh: 他在一块小磨石上把刀刃磨利。

e.en: The jeweler used a {slipstone} for the narrow groove.
e.zh: 珠宝匠用细磨石打磨那道窄槽。

e.en: The old poem says the moon had {slipt} away.
e.zh: 那首古诗写道月亮已经悄然滑走。

e.en: In dialect writing, he had {slipt} through the gate.
e.zh: 在方言体文字里，他已经溜过了大门。

e.en: One {slipup} delayed the whole shipment.
e.zh: 一个小差错耽误了整批货物的运输。

e.en: She apologized for the {slipup} in the report.
e.zh: 她为报告中的疏忽道了歉。

e.en: The museum displayed English {slipware} from the seventeenth century.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了十七世纪的英国泥浆装饰陶器。

e.en: Her bowl imitates traditional {slipware} patterns.
e.zh: 她做的碗仿照了传统泥浆装饰陶器的纹样。

e.en: The {slit-eyed} cat watched from the wall.
e.zh: 那只眯着眼的猫在墙上盯着看。

e.en: He gave me a {slit-eyed} look of suspicion.
e.zh: 他眯起眼睛，怀疑地看了我一眼。

e.en: The {slitless} envelope had to be torn open.
e.zh: 那个没有开口缝的信封只能撕开。

e.en: She chose a {slitless} skirt for the formal dinner.
e.zh: 她为正式晚宴选了一条不开衩的裙子。

e.en: The villain was drawn as a {slitty-eyed} figure.
e.zh: 那个反派被画成眯缝眼的形象。

e.en: Avoid calling someone {slitty-eyed}; it sounds insulting.
e.zh: 不要说别人眼睛眯缝缝的，这听起来很冒犯。

e.en: The broken shell had a {slivery} edge.
e.zh: 破壳的边缘像薄片一样锋利。

e.en: She added {slivery} strips of almond to the cake.
e.zh: 她往蛋糕上加了细薄的杏仁片。

e.en: They served {slivovitz} after the heavy meal.
e.zh: 他们在丰盛的一餐后端上了李子白兰地。

e.en: A small glass of {slivovitz} warmed his throat.
e.zh: 一小杯李子白兰地让他的喉咙暖了起来。

e.en: The goal looked dramatic in {slo-mo}.
e.zh: 那个进球用慢动作看起来很有戏剧感。

e.en: She replayed the fall in {slo-mo}.
e.zh: 她用慢动作回放了摔倒的画面。

e.en: Our office team plays {slo-pitch} every Thursday.
e.zh: 我们办公室的队伍每周四打慢投垒球。

e.en: The park has a league for {slo-pitch}.
e.zh: 这个公园有一个慢投垒球联赛。

e.en: His {slobbish} habits annoyed his roommates.
e.zh: 他邋遢懒散的习惯让室友很恼火。

e.en: The apartment looked {slobbish} after the party.
e.zh: 聚会过后，公寓显得乱糟糟又邋遢。

e.en: The novel describes a {sloe-eyed} singer at the bar.
e.zh: 小说描写了一位在酒吧里的深色大眼歌手。

e.en: A {sloe-eyed} child stared quietly at the camera.
e.zh: 一个深色大眼的孩子静静地望着镜头。

e.en: She mixed {sloe-gin} with tonic water.
e.zh: 她把黑刺李杜松子酒和汤力水调在一起。

e.en: The homemade {sloe-gin} tasted sweet and sharp.
e.zh: 自制的黑刺李杜松子酒尝起来甜中带烈。

e.en: A {sloeworm} slid through the wet grass.
e.zh: 一条无足蜥从湿草中滑了过去。

e.en: Many people mistake a {sloeworm} for a snake.
e.zh: 许多人会把无足蜥误认成蛇。

e.en: The campaign tried to {sloganise} a complex issue.
e.zh: 这场运动试图把复杂问题口号化。

e.en: Politicians often {sloganise} instead of explaining policy.
e.zh: 政客常常喊口号，而不是解释政策。

e.en: The ad agency wanted to {sloganize} the new product.
e.zh: 广告公司想把这个新产品包装成一句口号。

e.en: It is easy to {sloganize} fear during an election.
e.zh: 在选举期间，把恐惧变成口号很容易。

e.en: The school taught {sloid} to improve manual skill.
e.zh: 学校教授斯洛伊德手工训练法来提高手工能力。

e.en: Old education manuals praised {sloid} for careful craftsmanship.
e.zh: 旧教育手册称赞斯洛伊德训练有助于培养精细手艺。

e.en: Fishermen gathered {sloke} from the rocks at low tide.
e.zh: 渔民在退潮时从岩石上采集可食海藻。

e.en: The soup was flavored with dried {sloke}.
e.zh: 这道汤用晒干的紫菜类海藻调味。

e.en: He began to {sloom} beside the warm fire.
e.zh: 他在温暖的炉火旁开始打盹。

e.en: A heavy {sloom} settled over the quiet room.
e.zh: 一种沉沉的睡意笼罩了安静的房间。

e.en: The rainwater drained into a narrow {sloot} beside the field.
e.zh: 雨水流进田边一条狭窄的排水沟。

e.en: An old {sloot} marked the edge of the farm.
e.zh: 一条旧沟渠标出了农场的边界。

e.en: We stopped at the {slopehead} to look down into the valley.
e.zh: 我们在坡顶停下，俯看山谷。

e.en: Loose stones gathered near the {slopehead} after the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨后，松动的石块堆在斜坡上端附近。

e.en: The geologist found fresh {slopewash} below the rocky hillside.
e.zh: 地质学家在岩石山坡下发现了新的坡面冲积物。

e.en: Heavy rain left a fan of {slopewash} across the track.
e.zh: 大雨在小路上冲出一片扇形的坡洗沉积。

e.en: The sailor bought a rough jacket from a {slopseller}.
e.zh: 水手从一个廉价成衣商那里买了件粗糙夹克。

e.en: The pamphlet mocked him as a {slopseller} of cheap ideas.
e.zh: 那本小册子嘲笑他是贩卖廉价观点的劣货贩子。

e.en: He found work shirts in a crowded {slopshop} near the docks.
e.zh: 他在码头附近一家拥挤的廉价成衣店买到工作衬衫。

e.en: Critics called the theatre a {slopshop} for lazy entertainment.
e.zh: 评论家把那家剧院称作贩卖懒散娱乐的低档小店。

e.en: The editor rejected the article as careless {slopwork}.
e.zh: 编辑认为那篇文章粗制滥造，便退了稿。

e.en: Cheap {slopwork} can ruin a building in a few years.
e.zh: 粗劣施工几年内就可能毁掉一栋楼。

e.en: The path was too {slopy} for the old cart.
e.zh: 这条路坡度太大，旧手推车不好走。

e.en: She chose flat shoes for the {slopy} garden.
e.zh: 花园地面倾斜，她便选了平底鞋。

e.en: The field was {sloshy} after three days of rain.
e.zh: 连下三天雨后，田地湿漉漉的。

e.en: He carried a {sloshy} bucket across the kitchen.
e.zh: 他拎着一只水晃来晃去的桶穿过厨房。

e.en: Use a {slot-drill} to cut the narrow channel cleanly.
e.zh: 用槽钻可以把那条窄槽切得很干净。

e.en: The machinist replaced the worn {slot-drill} before starting.
e.zh: 机械工开工前换掉了磨损的开槽钻头。

e.en: The {slotback} caught a quick pass over the middle.
e.zh: 槽位跑卫在中路接到了一记快速传球。

e.en: Their fastest receiver often lines up as a {slotback}.
e.zh: 他们最快的接球手常常站在内侧接球手的位置。

e.en: The hunter followed the deer {slote} through the mud.
e.zh: 猎人沿着泥地里的鹿蹄印追踪。

e.en: Fresh {slote} showed that cattle had crossed the lane.
e.zh: 新鲜的蹄印表明牛群刚穿过小路。

e.en: He walked {slouchily} into the meeting room.
e.zh: 他没精打采地走进会议室。

e.en: She leaned {slouchily} against the wall and yawned.
e.zh: 她懒散地靠在墙上打了个哈欠。

e.en: His {slouchiness} made him look less confident.
e.zh: 他那副弯腰驼背的样子让他显得不太自信。

e.en: The coach criticized the team's {slouchiness} during warm-up.
e.zh: 教练批评队员热身时太懒散。

e.en: The trail became {sloughy} near the river bend.
e.zh: 小路到河湾附近变得像沼泽一样泥泞。

e.en: The nurse cleaned the {sloughy} wound carefully.
e.zh: 护士仔细清理了有腐肉的伤口。

e.en: The old fabric {slove} apart under the strain.
e.zh: 旧布料受力后裂开了。

e.en: A sudden crack {slove} the silence of the hall.
e.zh: 一声突响划破了大厅的寂静。

e.en: The manager would not tolerate {slovenry} in the kitchen.
e.zh: 经理不能容忍厨房里的邋遢作风。

e.en: His notes showed a habit of intellectual {slovenry}.
e.zh: 他的笔记显示出思维上马虎敷衍的习气。

e.en: The doctor prescribed a {slow-acting} medicine for steady relief.
e.zh: 医生开了一种起效较慢但能稳定缓解症状的药。

e.en: This is a {slow-acting} poison, not an instant one.
