e.zh: 这是一种慢性毒药，不是立即发作的那种。

e.en: The panel uses a {slow-actingrelay} to delay shutdown.
e.zh: 控制面板使用延时继电器来推迟关机。

e.en: A faulty {slow-actingrelay} kept the motor running too long.
e.zh: 一个故障的延时继电器让电机运转过久。

e.en: A sharp {slow-down} followed the warning sign.
e.zh: 警示牌之后车辆明显减速。

e.en: The factory faced a {slow-down} in new orders.
e.zh: 工厂的新订单增长放慢了。

e.en: The {slow-footed} defender could not catch the winger.
e.zh: 那个脚步慢的后卫追不上边锋。

e.en: A {slow-footed} response cost the company several clients.
e.zh: 反应迟缓让公司失去了几个客户。

e.en: The goal looked spectacular in {slow-mo}.
e.zh: 那个进球用慢镜头看起来很精彩。

e.en: She replayed the crash in {slow-mo} to see what happened.
e.zh: 她用慢动作重放撞车画面，想看清发生了什么。

e.en: The film shows the explosion in {slow-motion}.
e.zh: 影片用慢动作展示了爆炸场面。

e.en: He gave a {slow-motion} demonstration of the tennis serve.
e.zh: 他用慢动作演示了网球发球。

e.en: A {slow-moving} truck blocked the narrow road.
e.zh: 一辆行驶缓慢的卡车堵住了窄路。

e.en: The committee is a {slow-moving} part of the process.
e.zh: 委员会是这个流程中进展很慢的一环。

e.en: The film is {slow-paced} but beautifully acted.
e.zh: 这部电影节奏缓慢，但表演很出色。

e.en: She prefers a {slow-paced} village life.
e.zh: 她更喜欢节奏缓慢的乡村生活。

e.en: Hurry up, you {slow-poke}, or we will miss the bus.
e.zh: 快点，你这个慢吞吞的家伙，不然我们会错过公交车。

e.en: My brother is a {slow-poke} at breakfast.
e.zh: 我弟弟吃早饭总是慢吞吞的。

e.en: The doctor prescribed {slow-release} tablets for the pain.
e.zh: 医生开了缓释片来止痛。

e.en: Use a {slow-release} fertilizer in early spring.
e.zh: 早春时使用缓释肥料。

e.en: The {slow-spoken} teacher made every point clear.
e.zh: 那位说话缓慢的老师把每个要点都讲清楚了。

e.en: He sounded calm and {slow-spoken} during the interview.
e.zh: 面试中他听起来镇定而语速缓慢。

e.en: Distance runners often develop strong {slow-twitch} muscles.
e.zh: 长跑运动员通常会练出强健的慢肌纤维。

e.en: {Slow-twitch} fibers help with endurance rather than speed.
e.zh: 慢肌纤维有助于耐力，而不是速度。

e.en: Roadworks may {slow-up} traffic all morning.
e.zh: 道路施工可能让整个上午的交通都变慢。

e.en: A lack of parts will {slow-up} production.
e.zh: 零件短缺会拖慢生产。

e.en: The joke was cruel because it mocked a {slow-witted} boy.
e.zh: 这个笑话很刻薄，因为它嘲笑了一个反应迟钝的男孩。

e.en: He is not {slow-witted}; he just needs time to think.
e.zh: 他并不迟钝，只是需要时间思考。

e.en: Her silence was mistaken for {slow-wittedness}.
e.zh: 她的沉默被误认为是迟钝。

e.en: The novel treats his {slow-wittedness} with unusual kindness.
e.zh: 这部小说以少见的温和态度描写他的迟钝。

e.en: A {slow-worm} was hiding under the warm stone.
e.zh: 一条无足蜥藏在温暖的石头下面。

e.en: People often mistake a {slow-worm} for a snake.
e.zh: 人们常把无足蜥误认为蛇。

e.en: Come on, {slowcoach}, the train leaves soon.
e.zh: 快点，慢吞吞的家伙，火车快开了。

e.en: I was a {slowcoach} compared with the other runners.
e.zh: 和其他跑步者相比，我慢得像个慢吞吞的人。

e.en: The {slowcoaches} at the back delayed the whole group.
e.zh: 后面那些慢吞吞的人拖慢了整个队伍。

e.en: Stop waiting for the {slowcoaches}; we need to start.
e.zh: 别再等那些慢吞吞的人了，我们得开始了。

e.en: The research was {slowgoing} at first.
e.zh: 这项研究一开始进展缓慢。

e.en: Reading the old manuscript proved {slowgoing}.
e.zh: 阅读那份旧手稿事实证明很费时。

e.en: The old {slowhound} followed the scent patiently.
e.zh: 那条老猎犬耐心地循着气味追踪。

e.en: He called himself a {slowhound} when climbing hills.
e.zh: 爬山时他自嘲自己动作慢得像只慢猎犬。

e.en: The service was {slowish} but friendly.
e.zh: 服务有点慢，但态度友好。

e.en: We took a {slowish} walk after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后我们慢悠悠地散了个步。

e.en: The book is {slowpaced} in the opening chapters.
e.zh: 这本书开头几章节奏缓慢。

e.en: He enjoys {slowpaced} games with careful strategy.
e.zh: 他喜欢节奏较慢、讲究策略的游戏。

e.en: There was a sudden {slowup} near the bridge.
e.zh: 桥附近突然出现了车速放慢的情况。

e.en: The factory noticed a {slowup} in orders.
e.zh: 工厂注意到订单增长放慢了。

e.en: The child found a {slowworm} in the garden.
e.zh: 孩子在花园里发现了一条无足蜥。

e.en: A {slowworm} is a lizard, not a snake.
e.zh: 无足蜥是蜥蜴，不是蛇。

e.en: {Slowworms} often live in compost heaps.
e.zh: 无足蜥常生活在堆肥堆里。

e.en: Gardeners sometimes protect {slowworms} because they eat pests.
e.zh: 园丁有时会保护无足蜥，因为它们吃害虫。

e.en: The school introduced {sloyd} to teach practical skills.
e.zh: 学校引入手工木工教育法来教授实用技能。

e.en: He studied {sloyd} as part of teacher training.
e.zh: 他在教师培训中学习了手工木工教育法。

e.en: The linen had a small {slub} in the weave.
e.zh: 这块亚麻布的织纹里有一个小粗节。

e.en: Designers sometimes add {slub} for a handmade texture.
e.zh: 设计师有时会加入纱线粗节来营造手工质感。

e.en: She bought a {slubbed} cotton shirt.
e.zh: 她买了一件带纱线粗节的棉衬衫。

e.en: The fabric looked intentionally {slubbed} and rustic.
e.zh: 这种布料看起来是有意做出粗节，风格朴素。

e.en: A {slubber} prepared the wool before final spinning.
e.zh: 粗纺工在最后纺纱前处理羊毛。

e.en: Do not be a {slubber} with important documents.
e.zh: 处理重要文件时别粗心马虎。

e.en: The old comedy called him a {slubberdegullion} in mock anger.
e.zh: 那出老喜剧假装生气地骂他是个肮脏懒散的人。

e.en: No one wanted the {slubberdegullion} near the clean kitchen.
e.zh: 没人愿意让那个邋遢懒散的人靠近干净的厨房。

e.en: He {slubbered} the page with ink.
e.zh: 他把那页纸用墨水弄得一塌糊涂。

e.en: The apprentice {slubbered} the repair badly.
e.zh: 学徒把这次修理做得十分草率。

e.en: Stop {slubbering} paint over the edges.
e.zh: 别再把油漆胡乱涂到边缘外面了。

e.en: His {slubbering} work angered the master.
e.zh: 他敷衍草率的活儿惹恼了师傅。

e.en: He wrote {slubberingly} across the damp paper.
e.zh: 他在潮湿的纸上潦草地写着。

e.en: The task was done {slubberingly} and late.
e.zh: 这项任务做得草率，而且还拖晚了。

e.en: The mill added a new {slubbing} machine.
e.zh: 工厂添置了一台新的粗纺机器。

e.en: Uneven {slubbing} made the yarn weak.
e.zh: 粗纱不均匀使纱线变得脆弱。

e.en: A {sludgeworm} wriggled in the ditch mud.
e.zh: 一条污泥蠕虫在沟里的泥中扭动。

e.en: The biologist counted each {sludgeworm} sample.
e.zh: 生物学家清点了每份污泥蠕虫样本。

e.en: The old cowboy walked like a {sluefoot}.
e.zh: 那个老牛仔走路像个外八字脚的人。

e.en: His {sluefoot} stance slowed his skating.
e.zh: 他外撇脚的站姿拖慢了滑冰速度。

e.en: Wake up, you lazy {slugabed}.
e.zh: 醒醒吧，你这个贪睡的懒家伙。

e.en: The poem mocks every morning {slugabed}.
e.zh: 这首诗嘲笑每个早晨赖床的人。

e.en: They opened the {sluice-gate} after rain.
e.zh: 雨后他们打开了水闸门。

e.en: A rusty {sluice-gate} controlled the canal.
e.zh: 一道生锈的水闸控制着运河水流。

e.en: The {sluicegate} jammed during the flood.
e.zh: 洪水期间那道水闸门卡住了。

e.en: Workers repaired the old {sluicegate} today.
e.zh: 工人们今天修好了那座旧水闸。

e.en: Water roared down the narrow {sluiceway}.
e.zh: 水沿着狭窄的泄水道轰鸣而下。

e.en: The mine used a wooden {sluiceway}.
e.zh: 那座矿场使用一条木制洗矿水槽。

e.en: A {sluicy} rush filled the tunnel.
e.zh: 一阵像泄洪般的水流灌满了隧道。

e.en: The poet loved the river's {sluicy} sound.
e.zh: 诗人喜爱河水那种奔泻的声音。

e.en: Rainwater gathered in the roadside {sluit}.
e.zh: 雨水积在路边的小排水沟里。

e.en: The wagon crossed a dry {sluit}.
e.zh: 马车穿过了一条干涸的南非小沟。

e.en: She packed soft {slumber-wear} for the trip.
e.zh: 她为旅行打包了柔软的睡衣。

e.en: The shop sells children's {slumber-wear}.
e.zh: 这家店出售儿童睡衣。

slumbercoach.t: 卧铺客车；经济卧铺车厢

e.en: They booked a {slumbercoach} to Chicago.
e.zh: 他们订了一节去芝加哥的卧铺车厢。

e.en: The old {slumbercoach} offered tiny private rooms.
e.zh: 那种老式卧铺客车提供小型私人卧室。

e.en: The child drifted into {slumberland} quickly.
e.zh: 孩子很快进入了梦乡。

e.en: The lullaby carried her toward {slumberland}.
e.zh: 摇篮曲把她慢慢带入睡梦之中。

e.en: He spent a {slumberless} night worrying.
e.zh: 他忧心忡忡地度过了一个无眠之夜。

e.en: The city felt {slumberless} under neon lights.
e.zh: 霓虹灯下，这座城市显得彻夜不眠。

e.en: A {slumberous} heat settled over the village.
e.zh: 令人昏昏欲睡的热气笼罩了村庄。

e.en: Her voice had a {slumberous} softness.
e.zh: 她的声音带着一种催人入睡的柔和。

e.en: The room felt warm and {slumbery}.
e.zh: 房间里温暖得让人昏昏欲睡。

e.en: He gave a {slumbery} smile at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时他露出一个困倦的微笑。

e.en: The {slumbrous} afternoon slowed every thought.
e.zh: 这个令人困倦的下午让每个念头都慢了下来。

e.en: She listened with {slumbrous} half-closed eyes.
e.zh: 她半闭着睡意朦胧的眼睛听着。

e.en: Each {slumdweller} faced rising rents nearby.
e.zh: 每个贫民窟居民都面临周边租金上涨。

e.en: The report interviewed a young {slumdweller}.
e.zh: 这份报告采访了一位年轻的贫民窟居民。

e.en: The campers cooked {slumgullion} over the fire.
e.zh: 露营者在火上煮了一锅杂烩炖菜。

e.en: His notes became a {slumgullion} of ideas.
e.zh: 他的笔记变成了一堆杂乱的想法。

e.en: The beekeeper scraped {slumgum} from the press.
e.zh: 养蜂人从压蜡机上刮下蜂蜡渣。

e.en: Old {slumgum} still smelled faintly of honey.
e.zh: 旧蜂蜡渣仍隐约有蜂蜜的气味。

slumism.t: 贫民窟现象；贫民区习气

e.en: The essay attacked urban {slumism}.
e.zh: 这篇文章抨击了城市贫民窟现象。

e.en: Reformers blamed {slumism} on bad housing.
e.zh: 改革者把贫民区问题归咎于恶劣住房。

e.en: Factories bordered the city's {slumland}.
e.zh: 工厂紧邻城市的贫民窟地带。

e.en: The novel begins in Victorian {slumland}.
e.zh: 这部小说开篇写的是维多利亚时代的贫民区。

e.en: This block looks {slummier} after dark.
e.zh: 天黑后这个街区显得更像破旧贫民窟。

e.en: They moved to a {slummier} part of town.
e.zh: 他们搬到了城里更破败的地段。

small-animal.t: 小动物的；小型动物相关的

e.en: The clinic has a {small-animal} surgery room.
e.zh: 这家诊所有一间小动物手术室。

e.en: She chose {small-animal} medicine after graduation.
e.zh: 她毕业后选择从事小动物医学。

small-beer.t: 微不足道的事物；淡啤酒

e.en: Compared with the scandal, this mistake is {small-beer}.
e.zh: 和那桩丑闻相比，这个错误微不足道。

e.en: Workers once drank {small-beer} because it was safer than water.
e.zh: 工人过去喝淡啤酒，因为它比水更安全。

e.en: He practised with a {small-bore} rifle.
e.zh: 他用小口径步枪练习射击。

e.en: The debate became {small-bore} and technical.
e.zh: 这场辩论变得狭窄又技术化。

e.en: The designer set the subtitle in {small-caps}.
e.zh: 设计师把副标题排成小型大写字母。

e.en: The fund invests mainly in {small-caps}.
e.zh: 这只基金主要投资小盘股。

e.en: A {small-eared} dog slept by the fire.
e.zh: 一只小耳朵的狗睡在炉火旁。

e.en: The guide pointed out a {small-eared} desert fox.
e.zh: 向导指出了一只小耳朵的沙漠狐。

e.en: The police arrested the {small-fry} but missed the leaders.
e.zh: 警方抓住了小人物，却漏掉了头目。

e.en: That contract is {small-fry} for such a large company.
e.zh: 对这么大的公司来说，那份合同只是小事。

e.en: The potter preferred {small-grained} clay for fine work.
e.zh: 陶工做精细作品时更喜欢细粒黏土。

e.en: This {small-grained} sand feels smooth underfoot.
e.zh: 这种细粒沙踩在脚下很柔滑。

e.en: It was {small-minded} to mock her accent.
e.zh: 嘲笑她的口音显得心胸狭窄。

e.en: The policy reflected a {small-minded} fear of outsiders.
e.zh: 这项政策反映出对外来者的小气恐惧。

e.en: He {small-mindedly} refused to share credit.
e.zh: 他小气地拒绝分享功劳。

e.en: They {small-mindedly} opposed every new idea.
e.zh: 他们心胸狭窄地反对每一个新想法。

e.en: A {small-number} of voters changed the result.
e.zh: 少数选民改变了结果。

e.en: The study used a {small-number} sample.
e.zh: 这项研究使用了小数量样本。

e.en: They began with a {small-scale} trial.
e.zh: 他们从一次小规模试验开始。

e.en: The village supports {small-scale} farming.
e.zh: 这个村庄支持小规模农业。

e.en: She became a {small-screen} star in the 1990s.
e.zh: 她在二十世纪九十年代成了电视明星。

e.en: The app works well on {small-screen} devices.
e.zh: 这个应用在小屏幕设备上运行良好。

e.en: We made {small-talk} while waiting for coffee.
e.zh: 等咖啡时我们闲聊了几句。

e.en: He hates forced {small-talk} at office parties.
e.zh: 他讨厌办公室聚会上勉强的寒暄。

e.en: He was a {small-time} dealer in stolen phones.
e.zh: 他是个倒卖被盗手机的小贩。

e.en: The magazine treated him like a {small-time} actor.
e.zh: 那本杂志把他当成不重要的演员看待。

e.en: The crime boss used a {small-timer} as a courier.
e.zh: 犯罪头目让一个小角色当信使。

e.en: She refused to think like a {small-timer}.
e.zh: 她拒绝用小人物的心态思考。

e.en: He grew up with {small-town} values.
e.zh: 他在小城镇的价值观中长大。

e.en: The film captures {small-town} gossip perfectly.
e.zh: 这部电影把小镇流言表现得很到位。

e.en: The old recipe calls for chopped {smallage}.
e.zh: 这份老食谱需要切碎的野芹菜。

e.en: Gardeners once grew {smallage} for its strong flavor.
e.zh: 园丁过去种野芹菜，取其浓烈风味。

e.en: A {smallboy} ran across the yard.
e.zh: 一个小男孩跑过院子。

e.en: The tale begins with a lonely {smallboy}.
e.zh: 这个故事从一个孤独的小男孩开始。

e.en: He folded his {smallclothes} into the trunk.
e.zh: 他把贴身内衣叠进箱子里。

e.en: The portrait shows a gentleman in eighteenth-century {smallclothes}.
e.zh: 这幅肖像画中是一位穿着十八世纪短裤的绅士。

e.en: The team ran a {smallscale} test first.
e.zh: 团队先做了一次小规模测试。

e.en: Many {smallscale} producers sell directly online.
e.zh: 许多小规模生产者直接在网上销售。

e.en: He was only a {smallshot} in the organization.
e.zh: 他在组织里只是个小人物。

e.en: The reporter ignored the {smallshot} candidates.
e.zh: 记者忽略了那些不重要的候选人。

e.en: The officer wore a silver {smallsword}.
e.zh: 那名军官佩着一把银色细剑。

e.en: Fencing masters taught nobles to use the {smallsword}.
e.zh: 击剑师教贵族使用轻便细剑。

e.en: Her {smalltalk} helped guests relax.
e.zh: 她的闲聊让客人放松下来。

e.en: I am terrible at {smalltalk} with strangers.
e.zh: 我很不擅长和陌生人寒暄。

e.en: The gang stayed {smalltime} for years.
e.zh: 这个帮派多年来一直只是小规模活动。

e.en: He hated being treated as a {smalltime} performer.
e.zh: 他讨厌被当成小角色演员对待。

slummiest.t: 最像贫民窟的；最破败的

e.en: That alley was the {slummiest} part of the district.
e.zh: 那条小巷是这个街区最破败的地方。

e.en: They chose the {slummiest} hotel to save money.
e.zh: 为了省钱，他们选了最简陋脏乱的旅馆。

e.en: He called himself a {slummock} after spilling soup again.
e.zh: 他又把汤洒了，自嘲是个邋遢笨拙的人。

e.en: The old novel describes a kitchen {slummock} with cruel humor.
e.zh: 那本旧小说用刻薄的幽默描写了一个厨房里的懒散邋遢人。

slummy.t: 贫民窟般的；破旧脏乱的

e.en: The apartment felt {slummy} despite the fresh paint.
e.zh: 尽管刚刷过漆，那套公寓还是显得破旧脏乱。

e.en: She hated the {slummy} bars near the station.
e.zh: 她讨厌车站附近那些像贫民窟一样的酒吧。

slungshot.t: 绳端带重物的旧式武器

e.en: The sailor carried a {slungshot} for protection.
e.zh: 那名水手带着一件绳端带重物的武器防身。

e.en: A {slungshot} was found among the antique weapons.
e.zh: 一件旧式绳锤在古董武器中被发现。

e.en: The child began to {slup} the soup noisily.
e.zh: 那个孩子开始吧嗒作响地喝汤。

e.en: We heard the mud {slup} under our boots.
e.zh: 我们听见泥浆在靴子下发出吸吮般的声响。

slurb.t: 含糊地说；拖泥带水地说

e.en: He tried not to {slurb} his words after drinking.
e.zh: 喝酒后他尽量不把话说得含糊不清。

e.en: The tape made her voice {slurb} strangely.
e.zh: 录音带让她的声音听起来异常含混。

slushiest.t: 最泥泞的；最煽情俗套的

e.en: February left the {slushiest} streets downtown.
e.zh: 二月让市中心的街道变得最泥泞。

e.en: She saved the {slushiest} song for the wedding.
e.zh: 她把最煽情的歌留到婚礼上唱。

e.en: The pamphlet condemned what it called public {sluttery}.
e.zh: 那本小册子谴责它所谓的公开淫荡行为。

e.en: The word {sluttery} sounds archaic and insulting today.
e.zh: sluttery 这个词如今听起来古旧而带侮辱性。

e.en: The critic used a cruel, {sluttish} stereotype.
e.zh: 那位评论者用了一个残酷而带有荡妇羞辱意味的刻板印象。

e.en: In older English, {sluttish} could also mean untidy.
e.zh: 在较早的英语中，sluttish 也可以表示邋遢。

e.en: The novel says she smiled {sluttishly}, a dated insult.
e.zh: 小说说她“淫荡地”笑了笑，这是过时的侮辱说法。

e.en: He was dressed {sluttishly} in the old moralist's account.
e.zh: 在那位旧道德家的描述中，他穿得邋遢下流。

e.en: The sermon attacked supposed {sluttishness} in the city.
e.zh: 那篇布道抨击城市中所谓的淫荡风气。

e.en: Her essay analyzes the word {sluttishness} historically.
e.zh: 她的文章从历史角度分析 sluttishness 这个词。

e.en: You little {slyboots}, you hid the biscuits.
e.zh: 你这个小滑头，把饼干藏起来了。

e.en: Everyone knew the old {slyboots} had another plan.
e.zh: 大家都知道那个老滑头另有打算。

e.en: Her second excuse was {slyer} than the first.
e.zh: 她第二个借口比第一个更狡猾。

e.en: The advertisement took a {slyer} approach to persuasion.
e.zh: 这则广告用了更隐晦的说服方式。

slyest.t: 最狡猾的；最隐秘巧妙的

e.en: He was the {slyest} negotiator in the room.
e.zh: 他是房间里最狡猾的谈判者。

e.en: The {slyest} joke passed almost unnoticed.
e.zh: 那个最隐晦巧妙的笑话几乎没人注意到。

e.en: The monks crossed the {slype} in silence.
e.zh: 修士们默默穿过教堂回廊间的通道。

e.en: A narrow {slype} linked the cloister to the chapter house.
e.zh: 一条狭窄的通道连接着回廊和会议厅。

e.en: The ball landed {smack-dab} in the puddle.
e.zh: 球正好落进了水坑里。

e.en: Their house sits {smack-dab} between two busy roads.
e.zh: 他们的房子恰好夹在两条繁忙道路之间。

e.en: That repair cost me fifty {smackeroos}.
e.zh: 那次修理花了我五十美元。

e.en: She gave the baby a loud {smackeroo} on the cheek.
e.zh: 她在宝宝脸颊上响亮地亲了一下。

e.en: The film portrays him as a homeless {smackhead}.
e.zh: 电影把他描绘成一个无家可归的海洛因瘾君子。

e.en: Calling someone a {smackhead} is harsh and insulting.
e.zh: 称别人为 smackhead 很刺耳，也带有侮辱性。

e.en: The old {smacksman} knew every shoal along the coast.
e.zh: 那位老渔船水手熟悉沿岸每一处浅滩。

e.en: A {smacksman} repaired the nets before dawn.
e.zh: 一名渔船船员在黎明前修补渔网。

e.en: The dialect word {smail} appears in the old glossary.
e.zh: 方言词 smail 出现在那本旧词汇表里。

e.en: He used {smail} to mean tiny fish.
e.zh: 他用 smail 来表示小鱼。

smart-mouthed.t: 说话尖刻无礼的；顶嘴的

e.en: The teacher warned the {smart-mouthed} student after class.
e.zh: 老师课后警告了那个说话尖刻无礼的学生。

e.en: He sounded {smart-mouthed}, but he was only nervous.
e.zh: 他听起来像是在顶嘴，但其实只是紧张。

e.en: You need a {smartcard} to enter the secure office.
e.zh: 你需要一张智能卡才能进入安全办公室。

e.en: The bank issued a new {smartcard} with better protection.
e.zh: 银行发行了一张防护更好的新芯片卡。

smartdrive.t: 智能驱动器；智能驾驶系统

e.en: The {smartdrive} adjusted its speed on wet roads.
e.zh: 智能驾驶系统在湿滑路面上自动调节了速度。

e.en: The engineer tested a {smartdrive} for the factory machines.
e.zh: 工程师测试了一种用于工厂机器的智能驱动器。

smartie.t: 自作聪明的人；聪明孩子

e.en: Come on, {smartie}, tell us the answer.
e.zh: 来吧，聪明人，告诉我们答案。

e.en: Their little {smartie} learned to read at four.
e.zh: 他们家的聪明孩子四岁就学会了阅读。

e.en: It was a {smartless} plan from the beginning.
e.zh: 这个计划从一开始就很不聪明。

e.en: The old poem calls the thief {smartless} and vain.
e.zh: 那首古诗把小偷称作愚笨又虚荣的人。

e.en: {Smartweed} grew thickly along the muddy stream.
e.zh: 泥泞小溪边长满了蓼草。

e.en: The herbalist collected {smartweed} before the first frost.
e.zh: 草药师在初霜前采集了水蓼类植物。

smarty-pants.t: 自作聪明的人；小机灵鬼

e.en: Nobody likes a {smarty-pants} who corrects every sentence.
e.zh: 没人喜欢那种每句话都要纠正别人的自作聪明者。

e.en: All right, {smarty-pants}, show me how it works.
e.zh: 好吧，小机灵鬼，给我看看它怎么用。

smash-up.t: 严重撞车；混合拼贴作品

e.en: Three cars were involved in a {smash-up} on the bridge.
e.zh: 桥上发生了一起三辆车相撞的严重车祸。

e.en: The album is a wild {smash-up} of jazz and punk.
e.zh: 这张专辑是爵士和朋克的狂野混合拼贴。

smash-ups.t: 严重撞车；混合拼贴作品

e.en: The icy road caused several {smash-ups} overnight.
e.zh: 结冰的道路一夜之间造成了几起严重撞车事故。

e.en: Her videos are clever {smash-ups} of old movie scenes.
e.zh: 她的视频是旧电影场景的巧妙混剪作品。

e.en: The charity concert was a real {smasheroo}.
e.zh: 那场慈善音乐会真是大获成功。

e.en: He ended the match with a {smasheroo} down the line.
e.zh: 他用一记沿边线的精彩重击结束了比赛。

e.en: The song is a {smashup} of two pop classics.
e.zh: 这首歌是两首流行经典的混搭作品。

e.en: Police cleared the {smashup} from the highway by noon.
e.zh: 警方在中午前清理了高速路上的严重撞车现场。

e.en: The DJ became famous for energetic {smashups}.
e.zh: 这位DJ因充满活力的混搭作品而出名。

e.en: Fog led to several {smashups} near the tunnel.
e.zh: 大雾导致隧道附近发生了几起严重撞车事故。

e.en: Add a {smatch} of salt to the soup.
e.zh: 往汤里加一点点盐。

e.en: There was a {smatch} of envy in her voice.
e.zh: 她的声音里带着一丝嫉妒。

e.en: He can {smatter} a few phrases in Italian.
e.zh: 他会一点点意大利语短语。

e.en: The painter would {smatter} bright dots across the canvas.
e.zh: 画家会在画布上零星点缀亮色圆点。

e.en: She {smattered} her speech with French expressions.
e.zh: 她在演讲中夹杂了一些法语表达。

e.en: The table was {smattered} with crumbs after breakfast.
e.zh: 早餐后桌上零星散落着面包屑。

e.en: A {smatterer} of science may misuse impressive terms.
e.zh: 一个只略懂科学的人可能会误用听起来很厉害的术语。

e.en: He was no expert, only a cheerful {smatterer}.
e.zh: 他不是专家，只是个乐呵呵的浅尝辄止者。

e.en: She {smatters} in Spanish but cannot hold a conversation.
e.zh: 她略懂西班牙语，但还不能对话。

e.en: Rain {smatters} the window during the quiet evening.
e.zh: 安静的夜晚，雨点零星打在窗户上。

e.en: His {smattery} knowledge impressed nobody at the meeting.
e.zh: 他那点浅薄杂乱的知识在会上没有打动任何人。

e.en: The review was full of {smattery} references to philosophy.
e.zh: 那篇评论充满了对哲学一知半解的引用。

e.en: A brown {smaze} hung over the industrial valley.
e.zh: 一片棕色烟雾霾笼罩着工业山谷。

e.en: By afternoon, the city disappeared into {smaze}.
e.zh: 到了下午，整座城市都消失在烟雾混浊中。

e.en: Grandma spread {smearcase} on warm rye bread.
e.zh: 奶奶把软干酪抹在温热的黑麦面包上。

e.en: The old recipe calls for fresh {smearcase} and herbs.
e.zh: 这道老食谱需要新鲜农家奶酪和香草。

e.en: The sample formed a {smectic} liquid-crystal phase.
e.zh: 样品形成了近晶相液晶结构。

e.en: The geologist identified a {smectic} clay in the soil.
e.zh: 地质学家在土壤中识别出一种皂状黏土。

e.en: The material entered the {smectic-a} phase when cooled.
e.zh: 材料冷却后进入近晶A相。

e.en: Researchers measured the layers in a {smectic-a} sample.
e.zh: 研究人员测量了一个近晶A相样品中的层状结构。

e.en: The tilted molecules showed a {smectic-c} arrangement.
e.zh: 倾斜的分子显示出近晶C相排列。

e.en: Her thesis compared {smectic-c} films under different fields.
e.zh: 她的论文比较了不同场下的近晶C相薄膜。

e.en: A gray {smeech} rose from the damp fire.
e.zh: 潮湿的火堆冒起一股灰色烟尘。

e.en: The room was filled with {smeech} and soot.
e.zh: 房间里充满了烟雾和煤烟。

e.en: The peat began to {smeek} in the hearth.
e.zh: 壁炉里的泥炭开始冒烟。

e.en: A bitter {smeek} hung over the cottages.
e.zh: 一股刺鼻的烟雾笼罩着小屋。

e.en: He wiped the {smeg} from the old machine.
e.zh: 他把旧机器上的脏东西擦掉。

e.en: Oh {smeg}, I forgot the keys again.
e.zh: 该死，我又忘带钥匙了。

e.en: Poor hygiene can allow {smegma} to build up.
e.zh: 卫生不佳可能导致包皮垢堆积。

e.en: The doctor explained what {smegma} is without embarrassment.
e.zh: 医生毫不尴尬地解释了什么是阴垢。

e.en: The old satire calls him a {smell-feast}.
e.zh: 那篇旧讽刺文把他称作蹭饭的人。

e.en: A {smell-feast} praised every dinner he was not invited to.
e.zh: 那个只闻不吃的人称赞每一顿没请他的晚餐。

e.en: The cleaner is almost {smell-less} after it dries.
e.zh: 这种清洁剂干了以后几乎没有气味。

e.en: A {smell-less} patient may miss signs of danger.
e.zh: 没有嗅觉的病人可能察觉不到危险信号。

e.en: The bin gave off a strange {smellage}.
e.zh: 垃圾桶散发出一种奇怪的臭味。

e.en: There was a faint {smellage} of smoke in the hall.
e.zh: 大厅里有一股淡淡的烟味。

e.en: The mineral oil seemed {smelless} and clear.
e.zh: 这种矿物油似乎无色无味。

e.en: A {smelless} gas can still be dangerous.
e.zh: 无气味的气体仍然可能很危险。

e.en: The lab tested a {smellless} vapor in sealed jars.
e.zh: 实验室在密封罐中测试一种无气味的蒸气。

e.en: He felt strangely {smellless} after the infection.
e.zh: 感染后，他觉得自己奇怪地失去了嗅觉。

e.en: The old {smeltery} closed after the mine failed.
e.zh: 矿山停产后，那座旧冶炼厂关闭了。

e.en: Workers at the {smeltery} wore heavy masks.
e.zh: 冶炼车间的工人戴着厚重的口罩。

e.en: The fisherman sold a fresh {smergal} at dawn.
e.zh: 渔夫在清晨卖掉了一条新鲜的梅林鱼。

e.en: A {smergal} flashed silver below the pier.
e.zh: 一条小海鱼在码头下闪着银光。

e.en: There was black {smet} on his sleeves.
e.zh: 他的袖子上有黑色污渍。

e.en: She scrubbed the {smet} from the kitchen wall.
e.zh: 她把厨房墙上的脏污刷掉了。

e.en: A male {smew} floated near the reeds.
e.zh: 一只雄性白秋沙鸭漂在芦苇旁。

e.en: Birdwatchers hoped to spot a {smew} on the lake.
e.zh: 观鸟者希望在湖上看到白秋沙鸭。

e.en: The farmer found {smice} nesting in the grain.
e.zh: 农夫发现一群小鼠在谷物里筑巢。

e.en: Old stories warned that {smice} spoiled winter stores.
e.zh: 旧故事警告说鼠类会糟蹋冬季储粮。

e.en: Add a {smidgeon} of salt to the sauce.
e.zh: 往酱汁里加一点点盐。

e.en: She showed a {smidgeon} of doubt in her smile.
e.zh: 她的笑容里露出一丝怀疑。

e.en: I need a {smidgin} more time.
e.zh: 我还需要一点点时间。

e.en: The cake tastes better with a {smidgin} of lemon.
e.zh: 蛋糕加一点点柠檬味道更好。

e.en: She spread {smiercase} on dark bread.
e.zh: 她把软干酪抹在黑面包上。

e.en: The old recipe calls for fresh {smiercase}.
e.zh: 这道老食谱需要新鲜的凝乳奶酪。

e.en: The botanist described the vine as {smilacaceous}.
e.zh: 植物学家把这根藤描述为菝葜科植物。

e.en: Its {smilacaceous} leaves helped identify the specimen.
e.zh: 它的菝葜科特征叶片帮助鉴定了标本。

e.en: The extract contained traces of {smilacin}.
e.zh: 这种提取物含有微量菝葜苷。

e.en: Researchers isolated {smilacin} from the dried root.
e.zh: 研究人员从干根中分离出菝葜苷。

e.en: The florist used {smilax} to frame the bouquet.
e.zh: 花艺师用菝葜藤来衬托花束。

e.en: Wild {smilax} climbed over the fence.
e.zh: 野生菝葜爬过了篱笆。

e.en: The shop sold kitchen {smallware} beside the ovens.
e.zh: 这家店在烤箱旁边出售厨房小件器具。

e.en: Hotel buyers ordered {smallware} for every guest room.
e.zh: 酒店采购员为每间客房订购了小件用品。

e.en: The restaurant bought new {smallwares} before opening.
e.zh: 餐厅开业前买了新的小件器具。

e.en: Her stall was crowded with cheap {smallwares}.
e.zh: 她的摊位上摆满了便宜的小商品。

e.en: He smiled {smally} and changed the subject.
e.zh: 他微微一笑，换了个话题。

e.en: The child wrote her name {smally} in the corner.
e.zh: 孩子把自己的名字小小地写在角落里。

e.en: The painter mixed {smalt} into the pale sky.
e.zh: 画家把蓝色玻璃颜料调进浅色天空部分。

e.en: Old pottery often used {smalt} for a rich blue glaze.
e.zh: 旧陶器常用蓝色玻璃颜料做出浓郁的蓝釉。

e.en: The mosaic was made from thousands of {smalti}.
e.zh: 这幅马赛克由数千片彩色玻璃片拼成。

e.en: Restorers matched the missing {smalti} by hand.
e.zh: 修复人员手工配出缺失的彩色玻璃马赛克片。

e.en: The vase had a {smaltine} sheen under the lamp.
e.zh: 花瓶在灯下带着蓝玻璃颜料般的光泽。

e.en: She chose a {smaltine} pigment for the border.
e.zh: 她为边框选了一种含蓝玻璃颜料的颜料。

e.en: The museum displayed a dark sample of {smaltite}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一块深色的砷钴矿标本。

e.en: Miners once valued {smaltite} as a cobalt ore.
e.zh: 矿工过去把砷钴矿视为有价值的钴矿石。

e.en: The jeweler repaired the blue {smalto} on the brooch.
e.zh: 珠宝匠修补了胸针上的蓝色珐琅。

e.en: Italian mosaics often use bright {smalto}.
e.zh: 意大利马赛克常使用鲜亮的彩色玻璃。

e.en: The ring held a deep green {smaragd}.
e.zh: 戒指上镶着一颗深绿色的祖母绿。

e.en: Poets compared the valley to a {smaragd}.
e.zh: 诗人把山谷比作一块翡翠绿宝石。

e.en: The lake turned {smaragdine} in the morning light.
e.zh: 湖水在晨光中变成了翠绿色。

e.en: She wore a {smaragdine} silk scarf.
e.zh: 她戴着一条祖母绿般的丝巾。

e.en: The geologist identified {smaragdite} in the rock sample.
e.zh: 地质学家在岩石样本中认出了绿闪石。

e.en: A vein of {smaragdite} gave the stone a green streak.
e.zh: 一条绿闪石脉让石头带上了绿色纹路。

e.en: As a {smark}, he noticed every staged twist.
e.zh: 作为懂行的摔角迷，他注意到每个编排好的转折。

e.en: The forum was full of {smarks} debating the finish.
e.zh: 论坛里满是懂行摔角迷在争论结局安排。

e.en: His apology was coated in obvious {smarm}.
e.zh: 他的道歉里满是明显的虚情假意。

e.en: The salesman tried to {smarm} his way into the meeting.
e.zh: 那个销售想靠油腔滑调混进会议。

e.en: The second speech sounded even {smarmier} than the first.
e.zh: 第二次演讲听起来比第一次还要油腻奉承。

e.en: He became {smarmier} whenever a manager entered the room.
e.zh: 每当经理进屋，他就变得更加谄媚油滑。

e.en: That was the {smarmiest} compliment I had ever heard.
e.zh: 那是我听过最油腻虚伪的恭维。

e.en: The {smarmiest} host kept praising every guest too loudly.
e.zh: 最油滑的主持人总是过分夸张地称赞每位嘉宾。

e.en: He {smarmily} thanked everyone for their brilliant ideas.
e.zh: 他油腔滑调地感谢大家提出的高明想法。

e.en: The agent smiled {smarmily} before naming the price.
e.zh: 经纪人在报价格前谄媚地笑了笑。

e.en: Her speech had a {smarminess} that made people uneasy.
e.zh: 她的讲话带着一种油滑谄媚，让人不舒服。

e.en: The film mocks the {smarminess} of celebrity interviews.
e.zh: 这部电影嘲讽了名人访谈中的虚伪奉承。

e.en: He {smarms} around the boss every Monday morning.
e.zh: 他每周一早上都围着老板谄媚讨好。

e.en: The article attacks the {smarms} of political advertising.
e.zh: 这篇文章抨击政治广告里的油滑奉承。

e.en: Don't be a {smart-alec} during the interview.
e.zh: 面试时别表现得像个自作聪明的人。

e.en: The teacher ignored the {smart-alec} in the back row.
e.zh: 老师没有理会后排那个耍小聪明的人。

e.en: Nobody likes a {smart-aleck} who corrects every joke.
e.zh: 没人喜欢那种连笑话都要纠正的自作聪明者。

e.en: She gave a {smart-aleck} answer and lost the room.
e.zh: 她给了个自作聪明的回答，结果让全场反感。

e.en: His {smart-aleckry} annoyed the whole committee.
e.zh: 他那些自作聪明的言行惹恼了整个委员会。

e.en: The novel treats teenage {smart-aleckry} with affection.
e.zh: 这部小说以温和态度描写青少年的耍小聪明。

e.en: She made a {smart-alecky} remark about the rules.
e.zh: 她对规则说了一句自作聪明的俏皮话。

e.en: His {smart-alecky} tone did not help the discussion.
e.zh: 他那种耍嘴皮的语气对讨论毫无帮助。

e.en: Stop making {smart-assed} comments in class.
e.zh: 别在课堂上说那些自作聪明又讨嫌的话。

e.en: Her {smart-assed} reply made the officer frown.
e.zh: 她那句欠揍的机灵回答让警官皱起了眉。

e.en: His son became a {smart-mouth} at thirteen.
e.zh: 他儿子十三岁时变成了个爱顶嘴的人。

e.en: Don't {smart-mouth} your grandmother at dinner.
e.zh: 吃饭时别跟你奶奶耍嘴皮子顶嘴。

e.en: The guard gave us a {smileless} stare.
e.zh: 卫兵面无笑容地盯着我们。

e.en: Her {smileless} reply made the room quieter.
e.zh: 她冷淡的回答让房间更安静了。

e.en: She added a {smilie} to soften the message.
e.zh: 她加了一个笑脸符号，让消息显得柔和些。

e.en: That old forum used a yellow {smilie}.
e.zh: 那个老论坛使用黄色的笑脸表情。

e.en: The chat was full of {smilies} and jokes.
e.zh: 聊天里满是笑脸符号和玩笑。

e.en: Please avoid too many {smilies} in formal emails.
e.zh: 正式邮件里请避免使用太多表情符号。

e.en: A {smilodon} skeleton stood near the museum entrance.
e.zh: 一具剑齿虎骨架立在博物馆入口附近。

e.en: The child learned that {smilodon} had huge canine teeth.
e.zh: 孩子了解到剑齿虎有巨大的犬齿。

e.en: Add a {smitch} of salt to the soup.
e.zh: 往汤里加一点点盐。

e.en: There was a {smitch} of doubt in his voice.
e.zh: 他的声音里带着一丝怀疑。

e.en: He learned {smithcraft} from his grandfather.
e.zh: 他从祖父那里学会了锻造手艺。

e.en: The village valued {smithcraft} during the war.
e.zh: 战争期间，村里很看重铁匠技艺。

e.en: Several old {smitheries} still stand by the river.
e.zh: 河边仍保留着几间老铁匠铺。

e.en: The town's {smitheries} once supplied farm tools.
e.zh: 镇上的锻造作坊曾供应农具。

e.en: The {smithery} rang with hammer blows.
e.zh: 铁匠铺里回响着锤打声。

e.en: He wrote a history of local {smithery}.
e.zh: 他写了一部当地锻造业的历史。

smithite.t: 铁匠派教徒；史密斯派成员

e.en: The historian described him as a devoted {smithite}.
e.zh: 历史学家把他描述为一名忠诚的史密斯派成员。

e.en: A lone {smithite} defended the old doctrine.
e.zh: 一名铁匠派教徒独自为旧教义辩护。

e.en: The collector bought a green piece of {smithsonite}.
e.zh: 收藏者买了一块绿色的菱锌矿。

e.en: Miners found {smithsonite} in the abandoned tunnel.
e.zh: 矿工们在废弃坑道里发现了菱锌矿。

e.en: The gate showed fine {smithwork} in every hinge.
e.zh: 这扇门的每个铰链都体现出精细的锻造工艺。

e.en: Old {smithwork} filled the workshop walls.
e.zh: 作坊墙边摆满了旧铁匠制品。

e.en: The {smogbound} city canceled outdoor sports.
e.zh: 这座被雾霾困住的城市取消了户外运动。

e.en: Flights were delayed in the {smogbound} valley.
e.zh: 雾霾笼罩的山谷里，航班被延误了。

smoggier.t: 烟雾更重的；雾霾更浓的

e.en: The air became {smoggier} after rush hour.
e.zh: 高峰时段过后，空气里的雾霾更重了。

e.en: This winter feels {smoggier} than last year.
e.zh: 今年冬天感觉比去年雾霾更浓。

e.en: They dreamed of a {smogless} morning downtown.
e.zh: 他们盼望市中心能有一个无雾霾的早晨。

e.en: The island offered clear, {smogless} skies.
e.zh: 那座岛上天空清澈，没有烟雾污染。

e.en: The school announced a {smogout} before noon.
e.zh: 学校在中午前宣布因雾霾停课。

e.en: Fans hated the rare {smogout} at the stadium.
e.zh: 球迷们讨厌体育场少见的因烟雾取消比赛。

e.en: The herb is dried until it becomes {smokable}.
e.zh: 这种草药会被晾干到可以吸食。

e.en: Only certain cuts of meat are {smokable}.
e.zh: 只有某些部位的肉适合熏制。

e.en: We served {smoke-cured} ham with bread.
e.zh: 我们把烟熏腌火腿配面包端上桌。

e.en: The shop sells {smoke-cured} fish from the coast.
e.zh: 这家店出售沿海来的烟熏腌鱼。

e.en: The hikers packed {smoke-dried} meat for the trip.
e.zh: 徒步者为旅程准备了烟熏干肉。

e.en: Villagers stored {smoke-dried} peppers for winter.
e.zh: 村民们储存烟熏干辣椒过冬。

e.en: Firefighters entered the {smoke-filled} hallway carefully.
e.zh: 消防员小心进入烟雾弥漫的走廊。

e.en: They argued policy in a {smoke-filled} room.
e.zh: 他们在一间烟雾缭绕的房间里争论政策。

e.en: The hotel offers {smoke-free} rooms on every floor.
e.zh: 这家酒店每层都提供无烟客房。

e.en: The city made all restaurants {smoke-free}.
e.zh: 这座城市规定所有餐馆都禁止吸烟。

e.en: The old farm had a brick {smoke-house} behind the kitchen.
e.zh: 这座老农场的厨房后面有一间砖砌的熏制房。

e.en: They cured the ham in a small {smoke-house}.
e.zh: 他们在一间小熏制房里腌熏火腿。

e.en: Students held a {smoke-in} to protest the new ban.
e.zh: 学生们举行吸烟抗议聚会，反对新的禁令。

e.en: The newspaper described the {smoke-in} as a peaceful demonstration.
e.zh: 报纸称这场吸烟抗议聚会是一次和平示威。

e.en: The soldiers crossed the field behind a {smoke-screen}.
e.zh: 士兵们借着烟幕穿过了田野。

e.en: The charity event was a {smoke-screen} for illegal payments.
e.zh: 这场慈善活动只是掩盖非法付款的烟幕。

e.en: The dried leaves are {smokeable} but harsh.
e.zh: 这些干叶可以吸食，但味道很呛。

e.en: This fish is firm enough to be {smokeable}.
e.zh: 这种鱼肉质够紧实，适合烟熏。

e.en: Soot collected inside the engine's {smokebox}.
e.zh: 煤烟积在机车的烟箱里面。

e.en: The mechanic opened the {smokebox} for inspection.
e.zh: 机械师打开烟箱进行检查。

e.en: A {smokechaser} spotted the fire before it spread.
e.zh: 一名山火巡查员在火势蔓延前发现了火情。

e.en: The forest service hired another {smokechaser} for summer.
e.zh: 林务部门又雇了一名夏季山火巡查员。

e.en: The old kitchen still had a working {smokejack}.
e.zh: 那间老厨房里还有一台能用的烟力烤肉转架。

e.en: A {smokejack} turned the spit above the fire.
e.zh: 烟力转动装置带着烤叉在火上旋转。

e.en: A {smokelike} haze drifted over the valley.
e.zh: 一层烟雾般的薄霭飘过山谷。

e.en: The painting uses {smokelike} shadows around the figure.
e.zh: 这幅画在人物周围用了烟雾般的阴影。

e.en: The inspector checked emissions with a {smokemeter}.
e.zh: 检查员用烟尘浓度计检测排放。

e.en: A broken {smokemeter} gave unreliable readings.
e.zh: 坏掉的烟尘浓度计给出的读数不可靠。

e.en: The crew lit a {smokepot} to mark the landing zone.
e.zh: 机组点燃发烟罐来标出着陆区。

e.en: Farmers once used a {smokepot} to protect orchards from frost.
e.zh: 农民过去会用发烟罐保护果园免受霜冻。

e.en: The hotel installed {smokeproof} doors on each floor.
e.zh: 酒店在每层都安装了防烟门。

e.en: A {smokeproof} stairwell can save lives during a fire.
e.zh: 防烟楼梯间在火灾中能救命。

e.en: The salmon came from a coastal {smokery}.
e.zh: 这批三文鱼来自海边的一家熏制厂。

e.en: Guests gathered in the {smokery} after dinner.
e.zh: 晚餐后客人们聚到吸烟室里。

e.en: The laboratory tested visibility with a {smokescope}.
e.zh: 实验室用烟雾观察仪测试能见度。

e.en: A {smokescope} helped engineers compare exhaust levels.
e.zh: 烟雾观察仪帮助工程师比较废气浓度。

e.en: The report mentions {smokescopy} as an early testing method.
e.zh: 报告提到烟雾检测法是一种早期测试方法。

e.en: Few technicians still practice {smokescopy} today.
e.zh: 如今仍会使用烟雾检测法的技术员很少。

e.en: She wore a ring set with a dark {smokestone}.
e.zh: 她戴着一枚镶有深色烟晶的戒指。

e.en: The collector polished the {smokestone} carefully.
e.zh: 收藏者小心地打磨那块烟色宝石。

e.en: Fire codes require a {smoketight} seal around the door.
e.zh: 消防规范要求门周围有不透烟的密封。

e.en: The hatch must remain {smoketight} under pressure.
e.zh: 舱口在压力下也必须保持防烟密封。

e.en: He ordered an Arbroath {smokie} for lunch.
e.zh: 他午餐点了一份阿布罗斯熏鱼。

e.en: The vendor grilled a {smokie} at the street stall.
e.zh: 摊贩在街边摊烤了一根烟熏香肠。

e.en: That was the {smokiest} barbecue sauce on the menu.
e.zh: 那是菜单上烟熏味最重的烧烤酱。

e.en: The basement was the {smokiest} part of the building.
e.zh: 地下室是整栋楼里烟最浓的地方。

e.en: The candle burned {smokily} in the draft.
e.zh: 蜡烛在穿堂风里冒着烟燃烧。

e.en: She sang {smokily} in the crowded jazz club.
e.zh: 她在拥挤的爵士俱乐部里用沙哑迷离的嗓音唱歌。

e.en: They talked quietly in the hotel {smoking-room}.
e.zh: 他们在酒店吸烟室里低声交谈。

e.en: The old train had a separate {smoking-room}.
e.zh: 那列老火车有单独的吸烟室。

e.en: The builders stopped for {smoko} at ten.
e.zh: 建筑工人十点停下来工间休息。

e.en: She made tea during her morning {smoko}.
e.zh: 她在上午休息时泡了茶。

e.en: The factory installed a {smokometer} near the chimney.
e.zh: 工厂在烟囱附近安装了一台烟尘浓度计。

e.en: Readings from the {smokometer} were recorded every hour.
e.zh: 烟尘浓度计的读数每小时记录一次。

e.en: The child managed to {smole} jam across the table.
e.zh: 孩子把果酱抹得满桌都是。

e.en: Old soot seemed to {smole} the cottage walls.
e.zh: 陈年的煤烟似乎把小屋墙壁弄脏了。

e.en: He tried to {smoodge} a free ticket from his friend.
e.zh: 他想从朋友那里讨一张免费票。

e.en: She would {smoodge} around the boss before reviews.
e.zh: 考核前她总会围着老板奉承讨好。

e.en: The {smooth-faced} boy looked younger than eighteen.
e.zh: 那个脸庞光滑的男孩看起来不到十八岁。

e.en: A {smooth-faced} clerk greeted us at the desk.
e.zh: 一位无须的职员在柜台前接待了我们。

e.en: The hotel depends on a {smooth-running} reservation system.
e.zh: 这家酒店依靠运转顺畅的预订系统。

e.en: Good planning made the conference {smooth-running} from start to finish.
e.zh: 周密计划让会议从头到尾都进行得很顺畅。

e.en: He arrived {smooth-shaven} for the interview.
e.zh: 他刮净胡子来参加面试。

e.en: The actor's {smooth-shaven} face changed his whole look.
e.zh: 演员刮净胡子的脸让他的形象完全变了。

e.en: The baby was {smooth-skinned} and smiling.
e.zh: 那个婴儿皮肤光滑，正笑着。

e.en: This lizard is {smooth-skinned}, unlike the rougher desert species.
e.zh: 这种蜥蜴皮肤光滑，不像那些更粗糙的沙漠种类。

smooth-spoken.t: 说话圆滑的；温和得体的

e.en: The {smooth-spoken} lawyer calmed the nervous witness.
e.zh: 那位说话温和得体的律师安抚了紧张的证人。

e.en: A {smooth-spoken} salesman persuaded them to upgrade.
e.zh: 一个口才圆滑的销售员说服他们升级。

smooth-talking.t: 花言巧语的；能说会道的

e.en: Do not trust that {smooth-talking} stranger too quickly.
e.zh: 别太快相信那个花言巧语的陌生人。

e.en: Her {smooth-talking} style helped close the deal.
e.zh: 她能说会道的风格帮助谈成了这笔交易。

smooth-tongued.t: 油嘴滑舌的；巧言令色的

e.en: The {smooth-tongued} adviser promised easy profits.
e.zh: 那个油嘴滑舌的顾问承诺能轻松赚钱。

e.en: Even the judge distrusted his {smooth-tongued} apology.
e.zh: 连法官也不相信他那番巧言令色的道歉。

e.en: Use sandpaper to {smoothen} the wooden edge.
e.zh: 用砂纸把木头边缘磨光滑。

e.en: The mediator helped {smoothen} relations between the teams.
e.zh: 调解人帮助缓和了两个团队之间的关系。

e.en: She {smoothened} the icing with a warm knife.
e.zh: 她用热刀把糖霜抹平。

e.en: Time had {smoothened} their old disagreements.
e.zh: 时间已经缓和了他们过去的分歧。

e.en: The carpenter is {smoothening} the table surface.
e.zh: 木匠正在把桌面打磨平滑。

e.en: Better communication is {smoothening} the merger process.
e.zh: 更好的沟通正在让合并过程变得更顺畅。

e.en: This cream {smoothens} dry skin quickly.
e.zh: 这种面霜能很快让干燥皮肤变光滑。

e.en: A short break {smoothens} the transition between meetings.
e.zh: 短暂休息能让两场会议之间的衔接更顺。

e.en: Professional {smoothers} removed dents from the metal panels.
e.zh: 专业整平工去除了金属板上的凹痕。

e.en: Tax cuts acted as economic {smoothers} during the slowdown.
e.zh: 减税在经济放缓期间起到了缓冲作用。

e.en: The fisherman released a small {smoothhound} back into the sea.
e.zh: 渔夫把一条小星鲨放回了海里。

e.en: A {smoothhound} has flatter teeth for crushing shellfish.
e.zh: 星鲨有较扁的牙齿，用来压碎贝类。

e.en: We made {smores} around the campfire after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后我们围着营火做了烤棉花糖夹心饼。

e.en: The children asked for more {smores} before bedtime.
e.zh: 孩子们睡前还想再吃一些烤棉花糖夹心饼。

e.en: The final phrase should be played {smorzando}.
e.zh: 最后一个乐句应当渐弱渐慢地演奏。

e.en: Her voice faded {smorzando} at the end of the aria.
e.zh: 咏叹调结尾时，她的声音渐弱渐慢地消散。

e.en: The tiny room gave him a feeling of {smotheration}.
e.zh: 那个小房间让他有一种窒息感。

e.en: Her constant fussing felt like {smotheration} to the children.
e.zh: 她不停地操心让孩子们觉得像是过度关爱。

e.en: The attic felt {smothery} in the summer heat.
e.zh: 夏天的阁楼让人觉得闷热窒息。

e.en: His {smothery} attention made her uncomfortable.
e.zh: 他那种令人透不过气的关注让她不舒服。

e.en: He tried to {smouch} coins from the counter.
e.zh: 他试图从柜台上偷拿硬币。

e.en: The boys would {smouch} snacks from anyone nearby.
e.zh: 那些男孩会向附近的人讨要零食。

e.en: The thief tried to {smouse} a wallet in the crowd.
e.zh: 小偷想在人群中偷一个钱包。

e.en: He began to {smouse} around the pantry for sweets.
e.zh: 他开始在食品柜周围鬼鬼祟祟地找糖吃。

e.en: The photocopy looked {smudgier} than the original page.
e.zh: 这份复印件看起来比原页更模糊。

e.en: His hands grew {smudgier} as he repaired the bike.
e.zh: 他修自行车时，双手变得更脏污了。

e.en: This is the {smudgiest} copy of the report.
e.zh: 这是那份报告污迹最重的一份。

e.en: The {smudgiest} memory came back first.
e.zh: 最模糊的记忆反而最先回来了。

e.en: The ink spread {smudgily} across the page.
e.zh: 墨水在纸页上糊成一片。

e.en: Her face appeared {smudgily} in the old photograph.
e.zh: 她的脸在旧照片里显得模糊不清。

e.en: The printer left a gray {smudginess} on every page.
e.zh: 打印机在每页上都留下灰灰的污迹。

e.en: The painting's {smudginess} made the figures feel distant.
e.zh: 画面的模糊感让人物显得很遥远。

e.en: My daughter dressed as a {smurf} for the party.
e.zh: 我女儿打扮成蓝精灵去参加聚会。

e.en: Police said the {smurf} moved small cash deposits between banks.
e.zh: 警方称那名洗钱同伙在各银行之间转移小额现金存款。

e.en: Do not {smutch} the fresh paint with your sleeve.
e.zh: 别用袖子把新刷的漆弄脏。

e.en: A dark {smutch} marked the clean white wall.
e.zh: 干净的白墙上有一块黑污点。

e.en: His cuffs were {smutched} with coal dust.
e.zh: 他的袖口沾上了煤灰。

e.en: She {smutched} the paper while erasing the sketch.
e.zh: 她擦草图时把纸弄脏了。

e.en: Black {smutches} covered the mechanic's hands.
e.zh: 修理工的手上满是黑色污迹。

e.en: He {smutches} every clean sheet he touches.
e.zh: 他碰到的每张干净纸都会被他弄脏。

e.en: Stop {smutching} the glass with your fingers.
e.zh: 别再用手指把玻璃弄脏了。

e.en: The lamp was {smutching} the ceiling with smoke.
e.zh: 那盏灯正用烟把天花板熏黑。

e.en: He handed me a {smutchy} old envelope.
e.zh: 他递给我一个脏兮兮的旧信封。

e.en: The kitchen looked {smutchy} after the fire.
e.zh: 火灾后厨房看起来满是烟污。

e.en: That was the {smuttiest} joke he told all night.
e.zh: 那是他整晚讲过最下流的笑话。

e.en: The {smuttiest} window faced the busy road.
e.zh: 最脏的那扇窗正对着繁忙的马路。

e.en: He laughed {smuttily} at the crude remark.
e.zh: 他听到那句粗俗话后下流地笑了。

e.en: The candle burned {smuttily} in the corner.
e.zh: 蜡烛在角落里冒着黑烟燃烧。

e.en: The editor toned down the {smuttiness} of the script.
e.zh: 编辑把剧本里的下流内容弱化了。

e.en: The {smuttiness} of the chimney stained the bricks.
e.zh: 烟囱的煤烟污垢染黑了砖块。

e.en: The collector labeled the mineral as {smythite}.
e.zh: 收藏者把这种矿物标为菱硫铁矿。

e.en: A thin vein of {smythite} ran through the sample.
e.zh: 样本中有一条细细的菱硫铁矿脉。

e.en: The village {snab} repaired boots by the fire.
e.zh: 村里的鞋匠在火炉旁修靴子。

e.en: He worked as a {snab} before opening his own shop.
e.zh: 他开店前曾当过鞋匠学徒。

e.en: We bought sandwiches at the {snack-bar}.
e.zh: 我们在小吃店买了三明治。

e.en: The cinema {snack-bar} closes after the last show.
e.zh: 电影院的小吃柜台在最后一场结束后关门。

e.en: A new {snackery} opened near the station.
e.zh: 车站附近新开了一家小吃店。

e.en: The beach {snackery} sold coffee and fried fish.
e.zh: 海滩边的小吃铺卖咖啡和炸鱼。

e.en: Every office {snacketeer} knew where the biscuits were hidden.
e.zh: 办公室里每个爱吃零食的人都知道饼干藏在哪儿。

e.en: The cheerful {snacketeer} reviewed crisps online.
e.zh: 那位快乐的零食爱好者在网上点评薯片。

e.en: The school opened a {snacketeria} beside the library.
e.zh: 学校在图书馆旁开了一间小吃自助餐厅。

e.en: Students crowded the {snacketeria} after class.
e.zh: 下课后学生们挤满了那间小吃自助餐厅。

e.en: She packed a tiny {snackette} for the train ride.
e.zh: 她为火车旅程装了一份小点心。

e.en: The roadside {snackette} served tea and buns.
e.zh: 路边小吃摊供应茶和小面包。

e.en: The rough file will {snaggle} the edge of the metal.
e.zh: 粗锉会把金属边缘弄得参差不齐。

e.en: One {snaggle} showed when the dog lifted its lip.
e.zh: 狗掀起嘴唇时露出一颗乱牙。

e.en: A single {snaggle-tooth} gave the old dog character.
e.zh: 一颗歪牙让那只老狗显得很有特点。

e.en: He was teased for his front {snaggle-tooth}.
e.zh: 他因为门牙歪突而被取笑。

e.en: The {snaggle-toothed} grin made everyone laugh.
e.zh: 那副牙齿歪斜的笑容把大家逗笑了。

e.en: A {snaggle-toothed} old comb lay in the drawer.
e.zh: 抽屉里放着一把齿参差不齐的旧梳子。

e.en: His {snaggled} teeth made speech difficult.
e.zh: 他参差不齐的牙齿让他说话有些困难。

e.en: The fishing line was {snaggled} in the weeds.
e.zh: 钓鱼线缠在水草里了。

e.en: The vendor used a {snatchback} clause to recover the goods.
e.zh: 卖方利用一项突然收回条款取回了货物。

e.en: Her quick {snatchback} of the phone startled him.
e.zh: 她一下子把手机抢回来，吓了他一跳。

snatchy.t: 断断续续的；急促抢夺般的

e.en: The radio gave only {snatchy} reports during the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨中，收音机只断断续续传来报道。

e.en: His {snatchy} movements made the dog nervous.
e.zh: 他急促突兀的动作让那只狗紧张起来。

e.en: The old scythe needed a new {snath}.
e.zh: 那把旧长柄镰刀需要换一根柄。

e.en: He leaned on the wooden {snath} after cutting hay.
e.zh: 割完干草后，他靠在木制镰刀柄上休息。

e.en: The farmer learned to {snathe} a scythe properly.
e.zh: 农夫学会了正确地给长柄镰刀装柄。

e.en: They would {snathe} the blade before harvest began.
e.zh: 收割开始前，他们会给刀片装上长柄。

e.en: The soldiers planned a {sneak-raid} before dawn.
e.zh: 士兵们计划在黎明前发动一次偷袭。

e.en: Police made a {sneak-raid} on the hidden gambling room.
e.zh: 警方突袭搜查了那个隐蔽的赌博房间。

e.en: She found the {sneakiest} route into the garden.
e.zh: 她找到了进入花园最隐蔽的路线。

e.en: That was the {sneakiest} trick he had ever played.
e.zh: 那是他耍过的最狡猾的花招。

e.en: His {sneakiness} made everyone distrust him.
e.zh: 他的鬼祟行径让大家都不信任他。

e.en: The joke depended on a little {sneakiness}.
e.zh: 这个玩笑需要一点偷偷摸摸的安排。

e.en: The headmaster would {sneap} boys for careless work.
e.zh: 校长会因作业马虎而斥责男孩们。

e.en: A late frost can {sneap} the young shoots.
e.zh: 晚霜会抑制嫩芽的生长。

e.en: She lifted the {sneck} and opened the cottage door.
e.zh: 她抬起门闩，打开了小屋的门。

e.en: Please {sneck} the gate before you leave.
e.zh: 你离开前请把大门闩上。

e.en: They {sned} the branches from the fallen tree.
e.zh: 他们把倒下的树上的枝条削掉了。

e.en: Workers {sned} each log before hauling it away.
e.zh: 工人们把每根原木修枝后再拖走。

e.en: He gave a {sneerful} answer to the question.
e.zh: 他对这个问题给出了带讥讽的回答。

e.en: Her {sneerful} smile ended the conversation.
e.zh: 她那嘲讽的笑容让谈话结束了。

e.en: The critic wrote in a {sneery} tone.
e.zh: 那位评论家用嘲讽的语气写作。

e.en: His {sneery} friends mocked the simple plan.
e.zh: 他那些爱冷笑的朋友嘲弄了这个简单计划。

e.en: The old sailor offered him a pinch of {sneesh}.
e.zh: 老水手递给他一撮鼻烟。

e.en: A silver box of {sneesh} sat on the table.
e.zh: 桌上放着一个装鼻烟的银盒。

e.en: Yellow {sneezeweed} grew along the wet ditch.
e.zh: 黄色喷嚏草长在潮湿的沟边。

e.en: The gardener planted {sneezeweed} to attract late butterflies.
e.zh: 园丁种了喷嚏草来吸引晚季蝴蝶。

sneezy.t: 老打喷嚏的；让人打喷嚏的

e.en: I feel {sneezy} whenever the windows are opened.
e.zh: 每次窗户一打开，我就觉得想打喷嚏。

e.en: The dusty attic was a {sneezy} place to work.
e.zh: 满是灰尘的阁楼是个容易让人打喷嚏的工作地点。

snaggleteeth.t: 参差不齐的牙齿；龅牙或歪牙

e.en: The old cartoon pirate grinned with {snaggleteeth}.
e.zh: 那位老卡通海盗咧嘴一笑，露出参差不齐的牙齿。

e.en: She joked about her childhood {snaggleteeth} in the interview.
e.zh: 她在采访中拿自己童年时的歪牙开玩笑。

e.en: A single {snaggletooth} stuck out when he smiled.
e.zh: 他一笑，就露出一颗突出的歪牙。

e.en: The villain was drawn with a sharp {snaggletooth}.
e.zh: 那个反派被画成有一颗尖尖的乱牙。

snaggletoothed.t: 牙齿参差不齐的；有歪牙的

e.en: The {snaggletoothed} dog looked oddly charming.
e.zh: 那只牙齿参差不齐的狗看起来怪可爱的。

e.en: He played a {snaggletoothed} sailor in the film.
e.zh: 他在电影里扮演一个有歪牙的水手。

e.en: The trail was {snaggy} with broken branches.
e.zh: 小路上满是断枝，很容易被挂住。

e.en: This old sweater feels {snaggy} against rough wood.
e.zh: 这件旧毛衣碰到粗木头时很容易勾丝。

e.en: Progress on the road repairs was {snail-paced}.
e.zh: 道路维修的进展慢得像蜗牛一样。

e.en: She grew impatient with the {snail-paced} download.
e.zh: 下载速度慢得要命，让她很不耐烦。

e.en: The old laptop was {snail-slow} after the update.
e.zh: 更新之后，那台旧笔记本慢得像蜗牛。

e.en: Traffic moved at a {snail-slow} crawl downtown.
e.zh: 市中心的车流以极慢的速度一点点挪动。

e.en: The chef visited a {snailery} outside Lyon.
e.zh: 那位厨师参观了里昂郊外的一处养蜗牛场。

e.en: A small {snailery} supplied the restaurant each week.
e.zh: 一家小型蜗牛饲养处每周给餐厅供货。

e.en: Scientists filmed a {snailfish} near the ocean floor.
e.zh: 科学家在海底附近拍到了一条狮子鱼。

e.en: The pale {snailfish} survived intense deep-sea pressure.
e.zh: 这条苍白的狮子鱼能承受深海的巨大压力。

e.en: The robot moved in a {snaillike} glide.
e.zh: 机器人以像蜗牛般缓慢的方式滑动。

e.en: A {snaillike} creature crossed the wet stone.
e.zh: 一个像蜗牛的生物爬过潮湿的石头。

e.en: The tree had rough {snake-bark} along its trunk.
e.zh: 那棵树的树干上有粗糙的蛇纹树皮。

e.en: Craftsmen valued {snake-bark} for its striking pattern.
e.zh: 工匠看重蛇纹树皮，因为它的纹理很醒目。

e.en: A {snake-charmer} played a flute in the square.
e.zh: 一名耍蛇人在广场上吹着笛子。

e.en: The tourist watched the {snake-charmer} from a safe distance.
e.zh: 游客站在安全距离外观看那位弄蛇艺人。

e.en: {Snake-charming} is often performed for tourists.
e.zh: 耍蛇表演常常是给游客看的。

e.en: The documentary questioned myths about {snake-charming}.
e.zh: 纪录片质疑了关于弄蛇术的一些传说。

e.en: The troupe performed a slow {snake-dance}.
e.zh: 舞团表演了一段缓慢的蛇舞。

e.en: Students formed a {snake-dance} through the hallway.
e.zh: 学生们排成蜿蜒的队形穿过走廊。

e.en: The mongoose is a famous {snake-eater}.
e.zh: 獴是有名的食蛇动物。

e.en: Villagers called him a {snake-eater} after the strange feast.
e.zh: 那场奇怪的宴席之后，村民们叫他吃蛇的人。

e.en: A {snakebird} stretched its long neck above the water.
e.zh: 一只蛇鸟把长长的脖子伸出水面。

e.en: The guide pointed out a {snakebird} drying its wings.
e.zh: 向导指给大家看一只正在晾翅的蛇鸟。

e.en: A {snakefly} landed on the window screen.
e.zh: 一只蛇蛉落在了纱窗上。

e.en: The child noticed the {snakefly}'s unusually long neck.
e.zh: 孩子注意到那只蛇蛉有异常长的脖子。

e.en: The island was believed to be {snakeless}.
e.zh: 人们认为这座岛上没有蛇。

e.en: Campers preferred the {snakeless} meadow near the lake.
e.zh: 露营者更喜欢湖边那片没有蛇的草地。

e.en: A tiny {snakelet} slipped under the leaves.
e.zh: 一条小蛇钻进了叶子下面。

e.en: The keeper moved the {snakelet} to a warmer tank.
e.zh: 饲养员把幼蛇移到更暖的箱子里。

e.en: The dancer made a {snakelike} movement with her arms.
e.zh: 舞者用手臂做出像蛇一样的动作。

e.en: A {snakelike} river wound through the valley.
e.zh: 一条蜿蜒的河流穿过山谷。

snakemouth.t: 蛇口状开口；蛇口形部位

e.en: The cave had a dark {snakemouth} entrance.
e.zh: 那座洞穴有一个像蛇口般阴暗的入口。

e.en: The carving ended in a wide {snakemouth}.
e.zh: 那件雕刻的末端是一个宽大的蛇口形部位。

e.en: The zoo kept vipers in a secure {snakepit}.
e.zh: 动物园把毒蛇养在安全的蛇坑里。

e.en: The meeting turned into a political {snakepit}.
e.zh: 那场会议变成了一个政治上的混乱险地。

e.en: The herbalist dried {snakeroot} for winter remedies.
e.zh: 草药师把蛇根草晒干，留作冬天配药。

e.en: White {snakeroot} can poison grazing cattle.
e.zh: 白蛇根草可能会毒害吃草的牛。

snakestone.t: 蛇石；传说中治蛇咬的石头

e.en: The healer pressed a {snakestone} against the bite.
e.zh: 治疗者把一块蛇石按在咬伤处。

e.en: Museums sometimes display {snakestone} as folk medicine.
e.zh: 博物馆有时会把蛇石作为民间药物展出。

e.en: Yellow {snakeweed} spread across the dry pasture.
e.zh: 黄色蛇草蔓延在干燥的牧场上。

e.en: Ranchers worried that {snakeweed} would crowd out grass.
e.zh: 牧场主担心蛇草会挤占牧草的生长空间。

e.en: The bow was made from polished {snakewood}.
e.zh: 这把弓是用抛光的蛇木制成的。

e.en: Cabinetmakers prize {snakewood} for its dense grain.
e.zh: 家具木匠看重蛇木，因为它纹理致密。

e.en: The old teacher gave him a sharp {snib}.
e.zh: 那位老教师狠狠训了他一顿。

e.en: She tried to {snib} the boy for lying.
e.zh: 她想因为男孩撒谎而责骂他。

e.en: The pirate drew a {snickersnee} from his belt.
e.zh: 海盗从腰带上拔出一把大刀。

e.en: The tale ends with a comic {snickersnee}.
e.zh: 故事以一场滑稽的持刀决斗收场。

e.en: A {snickery} laugh came from the back row.
e.zh: 后排传来一阵偷偷嘲笑的笑声。

e.en: His {snickery} tone made the apology sound false.
e.zh: 他那种带着窃笑的语气让道歉显得不真诚。

e.en: We reached the market through a narrow {snicket}.
e.zh: 我们穿过一条狭窄小巷到了市场。

e.en: The children hid in the {snicket} behind the church.
e.zh: 孩子们躲在教堂后面的小通道里。

e.en: Stop {sniddling} and finish the letter.
e.zh: 别再瞎磨蹭了，把信写完。

e.en: He liked to {sniddle} with small tasks all morning.
e.zh: 他喜欢整个上午都在小事上瞎忙。

e.en: The police watched the suspected {snidesman} near the station.
e.zh: 警方在车站附近盯着那个可疑的骗子。

e.en: In the old slang, a {snidesman} passed false coins.
e.zh: 在旧时俚语里，snidesman 指使用假币的人。

e.en: That was the {snidest} remark of the evening.
e.zh: 那是今晚最刻薄的一句话。

e.en: Even his {snidest} critics admitted the plan worked.
e.zh: 即使是最尖刻的批评者也承认这个计划奏效了。

e.en: The wine was barely {sniffable} after a week open.
e.zh: 这瓶酒开了一周后几乎不值得闻了。

e.en: Keep dangerous powders away from anything {sniffable}.
e.zh: 把危险粉末远离任何可能被嗅入的东西。

e.en: The clerk grew {sniffier} when we asked for a refund.
e.zh: 我们要求退款时，店员变得更傲慢了。

e.en: This cat is {sniffier} about food than the other one.
e.zh: 这只猫对食物比另一只更挑剔。

e.en: She gave him her {sniffiest} look.
e.zh: 她用最傲慢的眼神看了他一眼。

e.en: The {sniffiest} guests complained about the coffee.
e.zh: 最挑剔的客人抱怨咖啡不好。

e.en: She answered {sniffily} and turned away.
e.zh: 她不屑地回答了一句，然后转过身去。

e.en: He {sniffily} rejected the cheaper restaurant.
e.zh: 他傲慢地拒绝了那家较便宜的餐馆。

e.en: Her {sniffiness} annoyed the whole team.
e.zh: 她那种傲慢态度惹恼了整个团队。

e.en: There was a trace of {sniffiness} in his reply.
e.zh: 他的回答里带着一丝不屑。

e.en: He sounded rather {sniffish} about their new house.
e.zh: 他说起他们的新房子时显得相当不屑。

e.en: A {sniffish} waiter ignored our table.
e.zh: 一个傲慢的服务员无视我们这桌。

e.en: She looked {sniffishly} at the muddy shoes.
e.zh: 她不屑地看着那双沾满泥的鞋。

e.en: He {sniffishly} dismissed the suggestion as childish.
e.zh: 他傲慢地把这个建议斥为幼稚。

e.en: His {sniffishness} made new students nervous.
e.zh: 他的傲慢让新学生感到紧张。

e.en: The review had an air of {sniffishness}.
e.zh: 那篇评论带着一种轻蔑的味道。

e.en: He gave a little {snift} before speaking.
e.zh: 他说话前轻轻吸了吸鼻子。

e.en: The dog began to {snift} around the doorway.
e.zh: 狗开始在门口四处嗅闻。

e.en: She {snifted} and wiped her eyes.
e.zh: 她吸了吸鼻子，擦了擦眼睛。

e.en: The horse {snifted} at the unfamiliar feed.
e.zh: 马对着陌生的饲料嗅了嗅。

e.en: That is a {snifty} little jacket.
e.zh: 那件小夹克挺漂亮时髦的。

e.en: He found a {snifty} trick for fixing the error.
e.zh: 他找到了一个很不错的修错小办法。

e.en: The fisherman caught a {snig} in the muddy stream.
e.zh: 渔夫在浑浊的小溪里抓到一条小鳗鱼。

e.en: They used to {snig} along the riverbank at night.
e.zh: 他们过去常在夜里沿河岸捕鳗鱼。

e.en: The children began to {sniggle} during the speech.
e.zh: 孩子们在演讲时开始偷偷发笑。

e.en: Old villagers would {sniggle} for eels after dark.
e.zh: 老村民们天黑后会偷偷捕鳗鱼。

e.en: She {sniggled} when he mispronounced the word.
e.zh: 他把那个词读错时，她偷偷笑了。

e.en: They {sniggled} in the reeds beside the canal.
e.zh: 他们在运河边的芦苇丛里偷偷捕鳗。

e.en: His quiet {sniggling} distracted the class.
e.zh: 他轻轻的窃笑分散了全班的注意力。

e.en: The boys spent the evening {sniggling} by the creek.
e.zh: 男孩们整个晚上都在小溪边偷偷捕鳗。

e.en: Their {snip-snap} filled the whole dinner table.
e.zh: 他们你来我往的急促争辩充满了整张餐桌。

e.en: She enjoyed the {snip-snap} of witty dialogue.
e.zh: 她喜欢那种机敏对答的对白。

e.en: The search for the missing file became a {snipehunt}.
e.zh: 寻找那份丢失文件变成了一场徒劳搜寻。

e.en: They sent the newcomer on a midnight {snipehunt}.
e.zh: 他们半夜让新来的人去参加一场恶作剧式的寻物。

snipehunter.t: 徒劳搜寻者；被骗寻物者

e.en: The intern felt like a {snipehunter} after hours of searching.
e.zh: 找了几个小时后，实习生觉得自己像个徒劳搜寻的人。

e.en: Every camp had one unlucky {snipehunter} on the first night.
e.zh: 每个营地第一晚都会有一个倒霉的被骗寻物者。

e.en: The path made a {snakey} line through the grass.
e.zh: 小路在草地里弯弯曲曲，像蛇一样延伸。

e.en: He gave me a {snakey} smile.
e.zh: 他冲我露出一种阴险狡猾的笑。

e.en: This river looks {snakier} on the map.
e.zh: 这条河在地图上看起来更蜿蜒。

e.en: His excuse sounded even {snakier} than before.
e.zh: 他的借口听起来比以前更加阴险可疑。

e.en: That was the {snakiest} road in the hills.
e.zh: 那是山里最弯弯曲曲的一条路。

e.en: She was the {snakiest} liar in the group.
e.zh: 她是这群人里最阴险狡诈的骗子。

e.en: The cable curled {snakily} across the floor.
e.zh: 电缆像蛇一样弯曲地横在地板上。

e.en: He answered {snakily}, avoiding the real question.
e.zh: 他阴险地回答，避开了真正的问题。

e.en: The dancer made a {snakish} movement with her arms.
e.zh: 舞者用手臂做出蛇一般的动作。

e.en: His {snakish} glance made everyone uncomfortable.
e.zh: 他那蛇似的目光让大家都不自在。

e.en: The old tale warned children about the {snallygaster}.
e.zh: 这个古老传说用斯纳利加斯特怪兽来吓唬孩子。

e.en: They named the festival mascot a {snallygaster}.
e.zh: 他们把节日吉祥物命名为传说中的斯纳利加斯特怪兽。

e.en: He wore a gray {snap-brim} with his suit.
e.zh: 他穿西装时戴了一顶灰色翻檐帽。

e.en: The detective tipped his {snap-brim} at the door.
e.zh: 侦探在门口轻抬了一下他的翻檐帽。

e.en: The toy has {snap-on} wheels for easy repair.
e.zh: 这个玩具有卡扣式轮子，方便维修。

e.en: She chose a {snap-on} cover for the phone.
e.zh: 她给手机选了一个扣上式保护壳。

e.en: He bought a black {snapback} at the concert.
e.zh: 他在演唱会上买了一顶黑色可调帽。

e.en: The market showed a quick {snapback} after the drop.
e.zh: 市场下跌后出现了迅速反弹。

e.en: The museum displayed a rare {snaphance} pistol.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一把罕见的燧发枪机手枪。

e.en: He wrote about the {snaphance} in early firearms.
e.zh: 他写到了早期火器中的燧发枪机。

e.en: The worker shaped the rivet with a {snaphead}.
e.zh: 工人用制圆头工具把铆钉头压成形。

e.en: A neat {snaphead} finished the metal joint.
e.zh: 一个整齐的圆铆钉头完成了金属接合。

e.en: He was a sharp {snapper-back} in every debate.
e.zh: 他在每场辩论中都是个尖锐抢话反驳的人。

e.en: The teacher warned the {snapper-back} to listen first.
e.zh: 老师提醒那个爱抢着顶嘴的人先听完。

e.en: She was a {snapper-up} of cheap antiques.
e.zh: 她是个见到便宜古董就抢购的人。

e.en: The company is a {snapper-up} of small rivals.
e.zh: 这家公司常迅速收购小竞争对手。

e.en: The slogan needs more {snappiness} and rhythm.
e.zh: 这句口号需要更多利落感和节奏感。

e.en: The app's {snappiness} impressed new users.
e.zh: 这个应用反应利索，让新用户印象很深。

e.en: Tourists often {snapshoot} every street corner.
e.zh: 游客常常把每个街角都快速拍下来。

e.en: The soldier had to {snapshoot} in poor light.
e.zh: 士兵不得不在昏暗光线下仓促射击。

e.en: A careless {snapshooter} blocked the doorway.
e.zh: 一个随手拍照的人不小心挡住了门口。

e.en: The magazine hired a street {snapshooter}.
e.zh: 杂志雇了一名街头快拍摄影者。

e.en: He tried to {snarf} the last slice of pizza.
e.zh: 他想把最后一片披萨狼吞虎咽地吃掉。

e.en: The program can {snarf} data from old files.
e.zh: 这个程序可以从旧文件里抓取数据。

e.en: Her comment was pure {snark}, not advice.
e.zh: 她那句话纯粹是尖刻挖苦，不是建议。

e.en: The review mixed humor with sharp {snark}.
e.zh: 这篇评论把幽默和尖锐讽刺混在一起。

e.en: A crash caused a huge {snarl-up} downtown.
e.zh: 一场车祸造成市中心严重交通堵塞。

e.en: The paperwork created a legal {snarl-up}.
e.zh: 这些文件引发了一场法律纠纷。

e.en: Roadworks caused several {snarl-ups} this morning.
e.zh: 道路施工今天早上造成了好几处堵塞。

e.en: Contract {snarl-ups} delayed the project again.
e.zh: 合同上的纠纷再次拖慢了项目进度。

e.en: This is the {snarliest} bug in the release.
e.zh: 这是这次发布中最棘手的漏洞。

e.en: He owned the {snarliest} dog on the block.
e.zh: 他养着街区里最凶的一条狗。

e.en: The child gave a rude {snash} to his aunt.
e.zh: 那个孩子粗鲁地顶撞了他的姨妈。

e.en: Do not {snash} at customers, even when tired.
e.zh: 即使累了，也不要对顾客粗鲁回嘴。

e.en: A {snatch-squad} arrested the suspect at dawn.
e.zh: 一支突袭抓捕小队在黎明逮捕了嫌疑人。

e.en: The protest leaders feared a police {snatch-squad}.
e.zh: 抗议领袖担心警方派出突袭抓捕小队。

e.en: She looked {snootily} around the cheap cafe.
e.zh: 她傲慢地环顾这家便宜咖啡馆。

e.en: He {snootily} refused to answer basic questions.
e.zh: 他自以为是地拒绝回答基本问题。

e.en: Her {snootiness} made new colleagues uncomfortable.
e.zh: 她的傲慢让新同事很不自在。

e.en: The restaurant's {snootiness} annoyed regular customers.
e.zh: 那家餐厅自命不凡的态度惹恼了老顾客。

e.en: The baby began to {snoozle} after lunch.
e.zh: 宝宝午饭后开始打起盹来。

e.en: The cat liked to {snoozle} against my sweater.
e.zh: 那只猫喜欢贴着我的毛衣依偎着睡。

e.en: The old dog sounded {snorty} after running.
e.zh: 那条老狗跑完后哼哧作响。

e.en: His {snorty} laugh broke the tense silence.
e.zh: 他那带着嗤笑的笑声打破了紧张的沉默。

e.en: A {snot-nosed} child waited by the door.
e.zh: 一个流着鼻涕的孩子在门边等着。

e.en: Don't let that {snot-nosed} intern bully you.
e.zh: 别让那个乳臭未干的实习生欺负你。

e.en: He pulled a {snot-rag} from his pocket.
e.zh: 他从口袋里掏出一块擦鼻涕的手帕。

e.en: Use a tissue, not your sleeve or a {snot-rag}.
e.zh: 用纸巾，别用袖子或脏手帕擦鼻涕。

e.en: Some {snotnose} was kicking the bus seat.
e.zh: 有个小屁孩一直踢公交车座位。

e.en: The nurse gently cleaned the little {snotnose}.
e.zh: 护士轻轻给那个流鼻涕的小孩擦干净。

e.en: He became even {snottier} after the promotion.
e.zh: 升职后他变得更加傲慢。

e.en: The toddler looked {snottier} by evening.
e.zh: 到傍晚时，那个幼儿鼻涕看起来更多了。

e.en: She was the {snottiest} guest at dinner.
e.zh: 她是晚宴上最傲慢的客人。

e.en: He caught the {snottiest} cold in class.
e.zh: 他在班里感冒得最厉害，鼻涕最多。

e.en: She answered {snottily} and walked away.
e.zh: 她傲慢地回了一句就走开了。

e.en: The clerk {snottily} corrected my pronunciation.
e.zh: 店员尖酸地纠正了我的发音。

e.en: His {snottiness} cost him several friends.
e.zh: 他的傲慢无礼让他失去了几个朋友。

e.en: The child's {snottiness} worried his parents.
e.zh: 孩子一直流鼻涕的状态让父母担心。

e.en: A {snotty-nosed} boy ran through the hall.
e.zh: 一个流鼻涕的男孩跑过大厅。

e.en: He dismissed me as a {snotty-nosed} beginner.
e.zh: 他把我当成乳臭未干的新手而不屑一顾。

e.en: The little {snottynose} wiped his face.
e.zh: 那个流鼻涕的小孩擦了擦脸。

e.en: Some {snottynose} scratched my car door.
e.zh: 有个小鬼划了我的车门。

e.en: The mask had a strange {snoutish} shape.
e.zh: 这个面具有一种奇怪的口鼻部形状。

e.en: His {snoutish} grin made the cartoon funnier.
e.zh: 他那猪嘴似的咧笑让漫画更滑稽。

e.en: The {snouty} fish searched the sand for food.
e.zh: 那条长吻鱼在沙里寻找食物。

e.en: The toy pig had a {snouty} pink face.
e.zh: 那只玩具猪有一张鼻子突出的粉脸。

e.en: The car slid into a {snow-bank}.
e.zh: 汽车滑进了一堆积雪里。

e.en: Children built tunnels through the {snow-bank}.
e.zh: 孩子们在雪堆里挖出了隧道。

snow-blind.t: 雪盲的；被雪光刺伤眼的

e.en: The climber became {snow-blind} without goggles.
e.zh: 那名登山者没戴护目镜，患上了雪盲。

e.en: A {snow-blind} traveler may lose direction quickly.
e.zh: 雪盲的旅行者可能很快迷失方向。

snow-blinded.t: 患雪盲的；被雪光晃花的

e.en: He was {snow-blinded} during the long crossing.
e.zh: 他在漫长穿越中被雪光晃到雪盲。

e.en: The {snow-blinded} skier needed medical help.
e.zh: 那名患雪盲的滑雪者需要医疗帮助。

e.en: Goggles help prevent {snow-blindness} on glaciers.
e.zh: 护目镜有助于在冰川上预防雪盲症。

e.en: Temporary {snow-blindness} left him in pain.
e.zh: 暂时性雪盲让他疼痛难忍。

e.en: He started the {snow-blower} before dawn.
e.zh: 他天亮前启动了除雪机。

e.en: A small {snow-blower} cleared the driveway quickly.
e.zh: 一台小型吹雪机很快清理了车道。

e.en: The road was covered in gray {snow-broth}.
e.zh: 路面覆着灰色的融雪水。

e.en: They jokingly called the thin soup {snow-broth}.
e.zh: 他们开玩笑把那碗清汤叫作雪水汤。

e.en: We photographed the {snow-capped} mountains at sunrise.
e.zh: 我们在日出时拍下了山顶积雪的群山。

e.en: A {snow-capped} volcano rose beyond the lake.
e.zh: 一座雪冠火山耸立在湖的远处。

snow-clad.t: 被雪覆盖的；银装素裹的

e.en: The {snow-clad} village looked silent and bright.
e.zh: 这个银装素裹的村庄显得安静明亮。

e.en: They crossed a {snow-clad} pass at noon.
e.zh: 他们中午翻过了一条被雪覆盖的山口。

e.en: The children played in the {snow-covered} yard.
e.zh: 孩子们在被雪覆盖的院子里玩耍。

e.en: A {snow-covered} road can be dangerous.
e.zh: 被雪覆盖的道路可能很危险。

e.en: The sheep were trapped behind a {snow-drift}.
e.zh: 羊群被困在一处风吹成的雪堆后面。

e.en: Wind piled a {snow-drift} against the door.
e.zh: 风把雪吹成一堆，堵在门边。

sniperscope.t: 狙击镜；瞄准镜零件或器具

e.en: The old rifle had a cracked {sniperscope} mounted on top.
e.zh: 那支旧步枪上装着一个裂了的狙击镜。

e.en: He adjusted the {sniperscope} before taking careful aim.
e.zh: 他在仔细瞄准前调整了瞄准镜。

e.en: Use the {snippers} to cut the loose thread.
e.zh: 用这把小剪刀把松线剪掉。

e.en: Gardeners carry sharp {snippers} for trimming roses.
e.zh: 园丁会带着锋利的剪枝剪来修剪玫瑰。

e.en: That arrogant {snippersnapper} tried to lecture the whole committee.
e.zh: 那个自以为是的年轻人竟想教训整个委员会。

e.en: The captain called him a {snippersnapper} and sent him away.
e.zh: 船长骂他是个毛头小子，然后把他打发走了。

e.en: Her notes were {snippety} and hard to follow.
e.zh: 她的笔记零零碎碎，很难看懂。

e.en: The film has a {snippety} rhythm, jumping between brief scenes.
e.zh: 这部电影节奏碎片化，在短场景之间跳来跳去。

e.en: She answered {snippily} when asked about the delay.
e.zh: 别人问起延误时，她不耐烦地尖声回答。

e.en: He {snippily} corrected every small mistake in the report.
e.zh: 他尖刻地纠正了报告里的每个小错误。

e.en: They played {snipsnapsnorum} by the fire on winter evenings.
e.zh: 冬夜里他们围着炉火玩一种叫snipsnapsnorum的旧纸牌游戏。

e.en: The diary mentions {snipsnapsnorum} as a favorite family pastime.
e.zh: 日记里提到snipsnapsnorum是家人喜爱的消遣。

e.en: His {snipy} remarks made the meeting uncomfortable.
e.zh: 他那些尖酸话让会议气氛很不舒服。

e.en: She grew {snipy} after waiting for an hour.
e.zh: 等了一个小时后，她说话变得很冲。

snivet.t: 烦躁不安；小题大作的恼火

e.en: He got into a {snivet} over the missing receipt.
e.zh: 他因为收据不见了而烦躁得小题大作。

e.en: There is no need for a {snivet} about one late email.
e.zh: 没必要为一封迟到的邮件这么恼火。

e.en: A {sno-cat} carried supplies to the mountain lodge.
e.zh: 一辆雪地履带车把物资运到山间小屋。

e.en: The rescue team used a {sno-cat} after the road disappeared under snow.
e.zh: 道路被雪埋住后，救援队使用了雪地履带车。

snobbier.t: 更势利的；更自命不凡的

e.en: The club became {snobbier} after it raised its fees.
e.zh: 俱乐部提高会费后变得更势利了。

e.en: He sounded {snobbier} than usual at the dinner party.
e.zh: 在晚宴上他说话听起来比平时更自命不凡。

snobbiest.t: 最势利的；最自命不凡的

e.en: It was the {snobbiest} restaurant in town.
e.zh: 那是城里最势利的一家餐馆。

e.en: She was voted the {snobbiest} student in the yearbook.
e.zh: 她在年鉴投票中被选为最自命不凡的学生。

e.en: His {snobbism} annoyed colleagues who worked just as hard.
e.zh: 他的势利态度惹恼了同样努力工作的同事。

e.en: The novel mocks the {snobbism} of fashionable society.
e.zh: 这部小说讽刺了时髦社交圈的自命不凡。

e.en: The young {snobling} refused to sit near ordinary customers.
e.zh: 那个小势利眼不肯坐在普通顾客旁边。

e.en: He played a comic {snobling} in the school production.
e.zh: 他在学校演出中扮演了一个滑稽的势利小辈。

e.en: The writer attacked the local {snobocracy} in a sharp essay.
e.zh: 那位作家在一篇尖锐文章中抨击当地势利阶层。

e.en: Membership was controlled by a quiet {snobocracy} of old families.
e.zh: 会员资格由一些老家族组成的隐性势利集团掌控。

e.en: By midnight, half the guests were {snockered}.
e.zh: 到午夜时，一半客人都喝醉了。

e.en: He looked {snockered} after the boxer landed a heavy punch.
e.zh: 拳手重重一击之后，他看起来被打懵了。

e.en: We grilled fresh {snoek} with lemon and herbs.
e.zh: 我们用柠檬和香草烤了新鲜的snoek鱼。

e.en: Dried {snoek} is sold in many coastal markets.
e.zh: 许多沿海市场都有出售晒干的snoek鱼。

snofari.t: 雪地观光行程；雪上游猎

e.en: The resort offers a guided {snofari} through the frozen valley.
e.zh: 度假村提供穿越冰冻山谷的雪地观光行程。

e.en: Their weekend {snofari} included sleds, hot drinks, and wildlife tracks.
e.zh: 他们周末的雪地游包括雪橇、热饮和野生动物足迹。

e.en: The columnist called the mayor a shameless {snollygoster}.
e.zh: 专栏作家称市长是个无耻的无原则政客。

e.en: Voters were tired of every smooth-talking {snollygoster} in the capital.
e.zh: 选民厌倦了首都里每个花言巧语的狡猾政客。

e.en: She tucked her hair into a black {snood}.
e.zh: 她把头发塞进一个黑色发网里。

e.en: On cold mornings he wears a wool {snood} around his neck.
e.zh: 寒冷的早晨，他会戴一条羊毛围脖。

e.en: The portrait shows a {snooded} woman in a plain dress.
e.zh: 画像中是一位戴着发网、穿素裙的女子。

e.en: Her {snooded} hair gave the costume an old-fashioned look.
e.zh: 她束在发网里的头发让这身装扮显得古典。

snooperscope.t: 窥探用观察镜；夜视窥镜

e.en: The detective raised a {snooperscope} to watch the dark warehouse.
e.zh: 侦探举起窥探镜观察黑暗的仓库。

e.en: In the fantasy story, the {snooperscope} revealed hidden creatures at night.
e.zh: 在那个奇幻故事里，夜视窥镜能在夜间显出隐藏的生物。

e.en: Her constant {snoopery} made the neighbors distrust her.
e.zh: 她总爱窥探打听，让邻居们不信任她。

e.en: The office banned casual {snoopery} into private files.
e.zh: 办公室禁止随意窥看私人文件。

e.en: He took a {snootful} of the sharp kitchen fumes.
e.zh: 他吸进了一鼻子刺鼻的厨房烟味。

e.en: After a {snootful} of whiskey, he became unusually cheerful.
e.zh: 喝下一大口威士忌后，他变得格外高兴。

e.en: The boutique felt {snootier} than the one next door.
e.zh: 这家精品店感觉比隔壁那家更傲慢势利。

e.en: He became {snootier} after moving into the wealthy district.
e.zh: 搬进富人区后，他变得更势利了。

e.en: She chose the {snootiest} hotel on the avenue.
e.zh: 她选了那条大道上最傲慢势利的酒店。

e.en: Even the {snootiest} critics praised the simple performance.
e.zh: 连最挑剔自大的评论家也称赞了这场朴素的演出。

e.en: The resort bought a new {snowmaker} for the ski slope.
e.zh: 度假村为滑雪坡买了一台新的造雪机。

e.en: A skilled {snowmaker} checked the temperature all night.
e.zh: 一名熟练的造雪工整夜检查气温。

e.en: The lost {snowmobilist} called rescuers from a frozen lake.
e.zh: 迷路的雪地摩托驾驶者在结冰的湖上呼叫救援人员。

e.en: Every {snowmobilist} must wear a helmet on this trail.
e.zh: 在这条雪道上，每个雪地摩托驾驶者都必须戴头盔。

e.en: A {snowplough} cleared the road before dawn.
e.zh: 一辆铲雪车在黎明前清理了道路。

e.en: Beginners often use the {snowplough} to slow down.
e.zh: 初学者常用犁式滑雪制动来减速。

e.en: Several {snowploughs} worked through the storm.
e.zh: 几辆铲雪车在暴风雪中持续作业。

e.en: She {snowploughs} carefully on the steep beginner slope.
e.zh: 她在陡的初级雪坡上小心地用犁式制动滑行。

e.en: The mayor joked that the {snowpocalypse} had finally ended.
e.zh: 市长开玩笑说，这场特大暴雪灾难终于结束了。

e.en: News sites called the sudden blizzard a {snowpocalypse}.
e.zh: 新闻网站把这场突如其来的暴风雪称为雪灾末日。

e.en: The cabin overlooked a silent {snowscape}.
e.zh: 小屋俯瞰着一片寂静的雪景。

e.en: Her painting turned the city into a blue-white {snowscape}.
e.zh: 她的画把城市变成了一幅蓝白色的雪景。

e.en: The train passed through a wooden {snowshed} in the mountains.
e.zh: 火车穿过山里的一座木制防雪棚。

e.en: Engineers repaired the {snowshed} before winter storms arrived.
e.zh: 工程师在冬季风暴到来前修好了防雪棚。

e.en: A small {snowslide} blocked the hiking trail.
e.zh: 一场小雪崩堵住了徒步小径。

e.en: The guide warned that a {snowslide} could start above us.
e.zh: 向导警告说，我们上方可能会发生雪崩。

e.en: A sudden {snowslip} covered the mountain road.
e.zh: 突发的雪层滑落覆盖了山路。

e.en: Climbers avoided the slope after a minor {snowslip}.
e.zh: 发生一次小型雪崩后，登山者避开了那片斜坡。

e.en: They crossed a {snowswept} field at dusk.
e.zh: 黄昏时，他们穿过一片被雪扫过的田野。

e.en: The {snowswept} village looked almost deserted.
e.zh: 那个雪覆的村庄看起来几乎空无一人。

e.en: He used a {snowthrower} to clear the driveway.
e.zh: 他用吹雪机清理车道上的积雪。

e.en: The old {snowthrower} broke during the first storm.
e.zh: 那台旧抛雪机在第一场风暴中坏了。

e.en: She wore a {snowwhite} scarf with her dark coat.
e.zh: 她穿深色外套时配了一条雪白的围巾。

e.en: The walls were painted {snowwhite} to brighten the room.
e.zh: 墙壁被刷成雪白色，让房间更明亮。

e.en: The child drew a {snub-nosed} dog with big ears.
e.zh: 孩子画了一只短鼻子、大耳朵的狗。

e.en: The detective found a {snub-nosed} revolver in the drawer.
e.zh: 侦探在抽屉里发现了一把短枪管左轮手枪。

e.en: The machine uses rubber {snubbers} to reduce vibration.
e.zh: 这台机器用橡胶缓冲器来减少振动。

e.en: The party's habitual {snubbers} ignored every newcomer.
e.zh: 聚会上那些惯于冷落别人的人无视每个新来者。

e.en: The puppy's {snubbiness} made its face look comic.
e.zh: 小狗短翘的鼻子让它的脸显得很滑稽。

e.en: Her {snubbiness} at dinner offended the guests.
e.zh: 她晚餐时的冷淡态度冒犯了客人。

e.en: He replied {snubbingly} and turned back to his phone.
e.zh: 他冷淡地回了一句，又转头看手机。

e.en: The clerk looked {snubbingly} at our muddy boots.
e.zh: 店员轻蔑地看着我们沾满泥的靴子。

e.en: The cartoon pig had a {snubby} little nose.
e.zh: 那只卡通猪有个短而翘的小鼻子。

e.en: His {snubby} answer ended the conversation quickly.
e.zh: 他冷淡的回答很快结束了谈话。

e.en: The antique {snuff-box} was made of silver.
e.zh: 那个古董鼻烟盒是银制的。

e.en: He opened a small {snuff-box} after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后，他打开了一个小鼻烟盒。

e.en: He chose a {snuff-colored} coat for the autumn wedding.
e.zh: 他为秋季婚礼选了一件黄褐色外套。

e.en: The old paper had turned {snuff-colored} with age.
e.zh: 那张旧纸随着年代久远变成了鼻烟色。

e.en: She wore {snuff-coloured} gloves with a black dress.
e.zh: 她穿黑裙子时戴了一副黄褐色手套。

e.en: The curtains were faded and {snuff-coloured}.
e.zh: 窗帘已经褪色，呈鼻烟般的黄褐色。

e.en: The old {snuff-taker} carried a silver box.
e.zh: 那位年老的吸鼻烟者带着一个银盒子。

e.en: A habitual {snuff-taker} may sneeze after each pinch.
e.zh: 习惯吸鼻烟的人每吸一撮后可能会打喷嚏。

e.en: {Snuff-taking} was common among gentlemen in that century.
e.zh: 在那个世纪，绅士中吸鼻烟很常见。

e.en: The doctor asked about his old {snuff-taking} habit.
e.zh: 医生询问了他过去吸鼻烟的习惯。

e.en: The border was planted with {snow-in-summer} and lavender.
e.zh: 花境里种了雪夏花和薰衣草。

e.en: White {snow-in-summer} softened the edge of the path.
e.zh: 白色的雪夏花柔化了小路边缘。

e.en: The garden center sells {snow-on-the-mountain} for dry borders.
e.zh: 园艺中心出售适合干燥花境的银边翠。

e.en: Be careful, because {snow-on-the-mountain} can irritate the skin.
e.zh: 要小心，银边翠可能会刺激皮肤。

e.en: A {snow-plough} cleared the road before dawn.
e.zh: 一辆扫雪车在黎明前清理了道路。

e.en: The tractor pulled a heavy {snow-plough} through the village.
e.zh: 拖拉机拉着沉重的除雪犁穿过村庄。

e.en: He kept a {snow-shovel} beside the front door.
e.zh: 他把一把雪铲放在前门旁边。

e.en: The plastic {snow-shovel} cracked in the freezing weather.
e.zh: 塑料雪铲在严寒天气里裂开了。

e.en: The airport closed during the {snow-storm}.
e.zh: 机场在暴风雪期间关闭了。

e.en: A sudden {snow-storm} trapped hikers on the ridge.
e.zh: 突如其来的雪暴把徒步者困在山脊上。

e.en: She wore a {snow-white} coat to the ceremony.
e.zh: 她穿着一件雪白的大衣参加仪式。

e.en: The sheets looked {snow-white} after washing.
e.zh: 床单洗完后看起来洁白如雪。

e.en: A {snowbell} tree bloomed beside the old gate.
e.zh: 一棵银钟树在旧大门旁开花了。

e.en: The nursery recommends {snowbell} for a small shaded garden.
e.zh: 苗圃推荐在小型阴凉花园里种雪铃花。

e.en: Buffalo lies in the American {snowbelt}.
e.zh: 布法罗位于美国的多雪地带。

e.en: Drivers in the {snowbelt} prepare early for winter.
e.zh: 雪带地区的司机会提前为冬天做准备。

e.en: The {snowberry} has white berries that birds may eat.
e.zh: 雪果结白色浆果，鸟类可能会啄食。

e.en: We planted {snowberry} along the fence for winter interest.
e.zh: 我们沿着篱笆种了雪果灌木，让冬季景观更有看头。

e.en: The Inuit guide noticed {snowblink} on the horizon.
e.zh: 因纽特向导注意到地平线上有雪映亮光。

e.en: Pilots sometimes use {snowblink} to judge distant ice fields.
e.zh: 飞行员有时利用雪光判断远处的冰原。

e.en: Farmers planted a {snowbreak} along the northern field.
e.zh: 农民在北侧田边种了一条防雪林带。

e.en: The wooden {snowbreak} kept drifts off the road.
e.zh: 木制挡雪障防止积雪吹到路面上。

e.en: Keep a {snowbrush} in the car all winter.
e.zh: 整个冬天都要在车里备一把除雪刷。

e.en: She used the {snowbrush} to clear the windshield.
e.zh: 她用扫雪刷清理挡风玻璃。

e.en: The {snowbush} brightened the tropical courtyard.
e.zh: 那株雪灌木让热带庭院显得更明亮。

e.en: Prune the {snowbush} lightly after new growth appears.
e.zh: 新芽长出后，轻轻修剪雪灌木。

e.en: The mountain's {snowcap} shone in the morning sun.
e.zh: 山顶的积雪在晨光中闪闪发亮。

e.en: Scientists measured how fast the polar {snowcap} was shrinking.
e.zh: 科学家测量了极地雪冠缩小的速度。

snowcapped.t: 顶部积雪的；雪冠覆盖的

e.en: We saw {snowcapped} peaks from the train.
e.zh: 我们从火车上看见了顶部积雪的群峰。

e.en: The postcard showed a {snowcapped} volcano above the town.
e.zh: 明信片上是一座雪冠覆盖的火山，俯瞰着小镇。

snowcraft.t: 雪地生存技能；雪地技巧

e.en: The course teaches basic {snowcraft} for winter climbers.
e.zh: 这门课程教授冬季登山者基本的雪地生存技能。

e.en: Good {snowcraft} can prevent accidents on steep slopes.
e.zh: 良好的雪地技巧能避免在陡坡上发生事故。

e.en: Engineers studied {snowcreep} above the mountain road.
e.zh: 工程师研究了山路上方雪层缓慢下滑的情况。

e.en: The fence was bent by years of {snowcreep}.
e.zh: 多年雪层缓慢下滑把围栏压弯了。

e.en: The climbers dug a {snowhole} before the storm arrived.
e.zh: 登山者在风暴来临前挖了一个雪洞。

e.en: A well-built {snowhole} can be warmer than a tent.
e.zh: 修得好的雪中避难洞可能比帐篷更暖和。

e.en: The children built a small {snowhouse} in the yard.
e.zh: 孩子们在院子里搭了一个小雪屋。

e.en: An igloo is a traditional kind of {snowhouse}.
e.zh: 冰屋是一种传统的雪屋。

e.en: This winter is {snowier} than last year.
e.zh: 今年冬天比去年雪更多。

e.en: The higher trail looked {snowier} and harder to follow.
e.zh: 更高处的小径看起来积雪更多，也更难辨认。

e.en: The peaks gleamed {snowily} under the moon.
e.zh: 群峰在月光下雪白地闪着光。

e.en: Her dress fell {snowily} around her feet.
e.zh: 她的裙摆像雪一样垂落在脚边。

e.en: The resort advertises the reliable {snowiness} of its slopes.
e.zh: 度假村宣传其雪坡积雪稳定。

e.en: The painting's {snowiness} made the room feel colder.
e.zh: 画面里的雪白感让房间显得更冷。

e.en: The climbers camped just below the {snowline}.
e.zh: 登山者在雪线下方不远处扎营。

e.en: Climate change has pushed the {snowline} higher.
e.zh: 气候变化使雪线升高了。

e.en: The mayor called the blizzard {snowmageddon} on television.
e.zh: 市长在电视上把这场暴风雪称为灾难性大暴雪。

e.en: After {snowmageddon}, schools stayed closed for a week.
e.zh: 那场灾难性大暴雪过后，学校停课了一周。

e.en: He wore a {snuffcolored} coat to the meeting.
e.zh: 他穿着一件鼻烟色外套去开会。

e.en: The old paper had turned {snuffcolored} with age.
e.zh: 那张旧纸因年代久远变成了黄褐色。

e.en: She chose a {snuffcoloured} ribbon for the hat.
e.zh: 她给帽子选了一条鼻烟色的丝带。

e.en: The walls looked {snuffcoloured} in the dim light.
e.zh: 墙壁在昏暗光线下显得黄褐。

snuffers.t: 剪烛花的剪刀；吸鼻烟者

e.en: The servant used {snuffers} to trim the candle wick.
e.zh: 仆人用剪烛花的剪刀修剪烛芯。

e.en: The tavern table was crowded with old {snuffers}.
e.zh: 酒馆桌边挤满了吸鼻烟的老人。

e.en: The club attracted a few elderly {snuffies}.
e.zh: 这个俱乐部吸引了几位年长的鼻烟爱好者。

e.en: Those {snuffies} in the drawer are old tobacco tins.
e.zh: 抽屉里那些鼻烟色的小东西是旧烟草罐。

e.en: The dog moved {snuffingly} along the garden path.
e.zh: 那只狗一路嗅着沿花园小径走。

e.en: He answered {snuffingly} through a blocked nose.
e.zh: 他鼻子不通，说话带着鼻音回答。

snuffless.t: 没有鼻烟的；无鼻烟味的

e.en: The box was strangely {snuffless} after years of use.
e.zh: 这个盒子用了多年后竟没有鼻烟味。

e.en: He felt miserable and {snuffless} during the long voyage.
e.zh: 长途航行中没有鼻烟，他觉得很难受。

e.en: The room smelled old and {snuffy}.
e.zh: 房间闻起来陈旧，还有股鼻烟味。

e.en: She sounded {snuffy} after walking in the rain.
e.zh: 她淋雨走路后说话听起来鼻塞。

e.en: The inn had several warm {snuggeries} beside the bar.
e.zh: 这家旅店在吧台旁有几间温暖舒适的小房间。

e.en: Writers rented tiny {snuggeries} for quiet winter work.
e.zh: 作家们租下小小的舒适房间，在冬天安静写作。

e.en: He read all evening in his {snuggery}.
e.zh: 他整晚都在自己的舒适小屋里读书。

e.en: The pub kept a private {snuggery} for regular guests.
e.zh: 那家酒吧为熟客留了一间私密小房间。

e.en: The children wore soft {snuggies} after their bath.
e.zh: 孩子们洗完澡后穿上柔软舒适的衣物。

e.en: She asked for {snuggies} before bedtime.
e.zh: 睡前她想要有人抱抱亲热一下。

snuggish.t: 有点舒适的；略显贴身的

e.en: The attic felt {snuggish} once the fire was lit.
e.zh: 火点起来后，阁楼有点温暖舒适。

e.en: The jacket was {snuggish} around the shoulders.
e.zh: 这件夹克肩部略微有些贴身。

snurfing.t: 早期雪板运动；雪上冲浪

e.en: He tried {snurfing} before modern snowboards became popular.
e.zh: 现代单板滑雪流行前，他试过早期雪板运动。

e.en: The resort hosted a vintage {snurfing} contest.
e.zh: 度假村举办了一场复古雪上冲浪比赛。

e.en: He kept a tin of {snus} in his jacket pocket.
e.zh: 他把一罐瑞典含服湿鼻烟放在夹克口袋里。

e.en: Some smokers switch to {snus} instead of cigarettes.
e.zh: 有些吸烟者改用瑞典含服湿鼻烟而不抽香烟。

e.en: The puppy tried to {snuzzle} into her sleeve.
e.zh: 小狗想把鼻子蹭进她的袖子里。

e.en: He would {snuzzle} closer when the room grew cold.
e.zh: 屋里变冷时，他会更贴近地依偎过来。

e.en: The canoe drifted into a quiet {snye}.
e.zh: 独木舟漂进了一条安静的河道支流。

e.en: Fishermen waited where the {snye} met the main river.
e.zh: 渔民们等在侧水道汇入主河的地方。

e.en: Just write {so-and-so} if you forget the name.
e.zh: 如果忘了名字，就写某某人好了。

e.en: That rude {so-and-so} took my parking space.
e.zh: 那个没礼貌的讨厌家伙抢了我的停车位。

e.en: The list was full of {so-and-sos} I barely knew.
e.zh: 名单上全是些我几乎不认识的某某人。

e.en: Those lazy {so-and-sos} left the work to us.
e.zh: 那些懒惰的讨厌家伙把活都留给了我们。

e.en: The food was only {so-so} tonight.
e.zh: 今晚的饭菜只能说一般般。

e.en: I feel {so-so}, not really sick.
e.zh: 我感觉马马虎虎，不算真的生病。

e.en: The wall showed clear {soakage} after the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨后，墙上明显有渗水痕迹。

e.en: Long {soakage} made the beans cook faster.
e.zh: 长时间浸泡让豆子更容易煮熟。

e.en: Rainwater drains into a {soakaway} behind the house.
e.zh: 雨水排进屋后的渗水井里。

e.en: The builder replaced the blocked {soakaway}.
e.zh: 建筑工人更换了堵塞的雨水渗排坑。

e.en: His grandfather worked as a {soap-boiler} in London.
e.zh: 他的祖父曾在伦敦做肥皂制造工。

e.en: The {soap-boiler} watched the mixture thicken slowly.
e.zh: 煮皂工看着混合物慢慢变稠。

e.en: The factory specialized in {soap-boiling} and candle making.
e.zh: 这家工厂专门从事制皂和蜡烛生产。

e.en: Old manuals describe {soap-boiling} in careful detail.
e.zh: 旧手册仔细描述了煮皂过程。

soap-operatic.t: 肥皂剧式的；情节夸张的

e.en: The argument became strangely {soap-operatic} by lunchtime.
e.zh: 到午饭时，这场争吵变得奇怪地像肥皂剧一样夸张。

e.en: Her novel avoids the {soap-operatic} twists common in melodrama.
e.zh: 她的小说避免了通俗情节剧里常见的肥皂剧式转折。

e.en: The shampoo used {soapbark} as a natural foaming agent.
e.zh: 这款洗发水用皂树皮作为天然起泡成分。

e.en: Merchants once imported dried {soapbark} for washing wool.
e.zh: 商人过去进口干皂树皮来清洗羊毛。

soapberry.t: 无患子；肥皂果植物及其果实

e.en: The villagers washed clothes with dried {soapberries}.
e.zh: 村民用晒干的无患子洗衣服。

e.en: A {soapberry} tree grew beside the old well.
e.zh: 老井旁长着一棵无患子树。

e.en: Put the wet soap back in the {soapdish}.
e.zh: 把湿肥皂放回皂碟里。

e.en: The ceramic {soapdish} matched the sink.
e.zh: 这个陶瓷肥皂盒和洗手池很配。

e.en: The old {soapery} closed after the war.
e.zh: 那家老制皂厂在战后关闭了。

e.en: She sells handmade bars from a small {soapery}.
e.zh: 她售卖一家小肥皂作坊做的手工皂。

e.en: My grandmother never missed her afternoon {soapie}.
e.zh: 我祖母从不错过下午那部肥皂剧。

e.en: The scandal sounded like a plot from a {soapie}.
e.zh: 这桩丑闻听起来像肥皂剧里的情节。

soapier.t: 更肥皂味的；更像肥皂剧的

e.en: This detergent smells {soapier} than the last one.
e.zh: 这种洗涤剂比上一种肥皂味更重。

e.en: The second season became even {soapier}.
e.zh: 第二季变得更像肥皂剧了。

e.en: That was the {soapiest} bath foam I have tried.
e.zh: 那是我用过肥皂味最重的泡泡浴液。

e.en: The finale was the {soapiest} episode of the series.
e.zh: 大结局是整部剧最煽情的一集。

e.en: The water slid {soapily} over the tiles.
e.zh: 水像带着肥皂一样滑过瓷砖。

e.en: He apologized {soapily} on the talk show.
e.zh: 他在访谈节目上煽情地道了歉。

e.en: The lotion's {soapiness} bothered my skin.
e.zh: 这款乳液的肥皂感让我的皮肤不舒服。

e.en: Critics mocked the movie's heavy {soapiness}.
e.zh: 影评人嘲笑这部电影过分的煽情感。

e.en: Use a {soapless} cleanser on sensitive skin.
e.zh: 敏感肌肤要使用无皂洁面产品。

e.en: The hikers found themselves {soapless} for three days.
e.zh: 徒步者有三天都没有肥皂可用。

e.en: She learned {soapmaking} from online videos.
e.zh: 她通过网络视频学会了制皂。

e.en: The museum offers a {soapmaking} workshop.
e.zh: 博物馆开设肥皂制作工作坊。

e.en: The guide pointed out a wild {soapolallie} bush.
e.zh: 向导指出了一丛野生的北美银莓灌木。

e.en: Indigenous families once gathered {soapolallie} berries there.
e.zh: 原住民家庭过去常在那里采集北美银莓果。

e.en: The carver shaped the soft {soaprock} carefully.
e.zh: 雕刻师小心地塑造那块柔软的皂石。

e.en: A vein of {soaprock} ran through the hillside.
e.zh: 山坡中有一条皂石矿脉。

e.en: The herb garden included pink {soapwort}.
e.zh: 香草园里种着粉色的肥皂草。

e.en: People once used {soapwort} to clean delicate cloth.
e.zh: 人们过去用皂草清洗精细布料。

e.en: The ridge created {soarable} air for gliders.
e.zh: 山脊形成了适合滑翔机高飞的气流。

e.en: Only a few thermals were {soarable} that morning.
e.zh: 那天早晨只有少数上升气流可供滑翔。

e.en: The child grew {sobby} when bedtime came.
e.zh: 到了睡觉时间，孩子变得爱哭起来。

e.en: His {sobby} speech embarrassed the audience.
e.zh: 他那番含泪煽情的讲话让观众很尴尬。

e.en: If the plan fails, {sobeit}.
e.zh: 如果计划失败，那就这样吧。

e.en: Let justice be done, and {sobeit}.
e.zh: 愿正义得到伸张，但愿如此。

e.en: We need a {sober-minded} assessment of the risks.
e.zh: 我们需要对风险作出头脑清醒的评估。

e.en: Her {sober-minded} advice calmed the team.
e.zh: 她审慎的建议让团队冷静下来。

e.en: He was the {soberest} driver after the party.
e.zh: 聚会后他是最清醒的司机。

e.en: Even her {soberest} warning sounded kind.
e.zh: 即使是她最严肃的警告也听起来很温和。

e.en: Cold water helped {soberize} the dizzy sailor.
e.zh: 冷水帮助那名头晕的水手清醒过来。

e.en: The accident seemed to {soberize} the whole town.
e.zh: 这场事故似乎让全镇都严肃起来。

e.en: A {soberminded} leader avoids dramatic promises.
e.zh: 头脑清醒的领导者会避免夸张承诺。

e.en: The report offered a {soberminded} view of growth.
e.zh: 这份报告对增长给出了审慎的看法。

sociosexual.t: 社会性行为的；性伴态度的

e.en: The survey measured {sociosexual} attitudes among students.
e.zh: 这项调查测量了学生对性伴关系的态度。

e.en: Researchers debated whether {sociosexual} behavior changes with age.
e.zh: 研究人员讨论社会性行为是否会随年龄改变。

sociotechnical.t: 社会技术的；社会与技术互动的

e.en: The team studied the platform as a {sociotechnical} system.
e.zh: 团队把这个平台作为社会技术系统来研究。

e.en: A {sociotechnical} approach considers both tools and people.
e.zh: 社会技术方法会同时考虑工具和人的因素。

sociotechnological.t: 社会技术的；社会与科技相关的

e.en: The report described broad {sociotechnological} changes after automation.
e.zh: 报告描述了自动化之后广泛的社会技术变化。

e.en: Her thesis examines {sociotechnological} risks in digital health care.
e.zh: 她的论文研究数字医疗中的社会技术风险。

e.en: The old legal text called him a trusted {socius}.
e.zh: 那份古老法律文本称他为可信赖的伙伴。

e.en: In Roman usage, a {socius} could be an ally.
e.zh: 在罗马用法中，socius 可以指盟友。

e.en: Her final argument was a real {sockdolager}.
e.zh: 她最后的论点真是决定性一击。

e.en: The verdict came as a {sockdolager} to the town.
e.zh: 这个判决对全镇来说都是惊人的消息。

e.en: The punch line landed like a {sockdologer}.
e.zh: 这个笑点像重重一击一样落下。

e.en: That discovery was a scientific {sockdologer}.
e.zh: 那项发现是科学上的惊人之事。

e.en: The boxer delivered a quick {sockerino} in the final round.
e.zh: 拳手在最后一回合打出了一记快速重击。

e.en: That joke was a {sockerino} at the dinner table.
e.zh: 那个笑话在餐桌上真是精彩一击。

e.en: The hero gave the villain a {sockeroo}.
e.zh: 英雄给了反派一记重击。

e.en: The announcement was a {sockeroo} for investors.
e.zh: 这项公告对投资者来说相当震撼。

e.en: He wore leather shoes on {sockless} feet.
e.zh: 他光脚穿着皮鞋。

e.en: The model made the {sockless} look fashionable.
e.zh: 那位模特把不穿袜子的造型穿得很时髦。

e.en: The movie ended with a {socko} finale.
e.zh: 这部电影以精彩有力的结尾收场。

e.en: He gave the bag a {socko} with his fist.
e.zh: 他用拳头重重打了一下袋子。

socman.t: 社会人类学家；社会学者

e.en: The {socman} interviewed families in the village.
e.zh: 这位社会学者采访了村里的家庭。

e.en: As a {socman}, he focused on kinship and ritual.
e.zh: 作为社会人类学家，他关注亲属关系和仪式。

socmen.t: 社会人类学家们；社会学者们

e.en: The {socmen} compared marriage customs across regions.
e.zh: 这些社会学者比较了不同地区的婚俗。

e.en: Several {socmen} attended the anthropology conference.
e.zh: 几位社会人类学家参加了那场人类学会议。

e.en: She taught {socratically}, answering questions with more questions.
e.zh: 她用苏格拉底式方法教学，用更多问题来回应提问。

e.en: The lawyer {socratically} led the witness toward contradiction.
e.zh: 律师通过层层提问引导证人走向自相矛盾。

e.en: Each {sodalist} promised to support the charitable work.
e.zh: 每位会社成员都承诺支持慈善工作。

e.en: The old chapel recorded the names of every {sodalist}.
e.zh: 那座老礼拜堂记录了每位兄弟会成员的名字。

e.en: The necklace was made with polished {sodalite}.
e.zh: 这条项链由抛光方钠石制成。

e.en: Geologists identified {sodalite} in the volcanic rock.
e.zh: 地质学家在火山岩中鉴定出方钠石。

e.en: The chemist handled {sodamide} under dry conditions.
e.zh: 化学家在干燥条件下处理氨基钠。

e.en: {Sodamide} reacts violently with water.
e.zh: 氨基钠会与水发生剧烈反应。

e.en: The {sodbuster} broke the prairie soil with a plow.
